english: Maize rolls its leaves inward as a natural defence mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation when the sun is too hot. If the soil stays dry for too long, the leaves will stay rolled up and eventually turn brown.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, strong sunlight and severe drought. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves and burrows into the leaf whorl. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your maize yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni efoɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu o-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Managing these pests early with suitable sprays prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water stays trapped in heavy or poorly drained soil, causing root rot disease. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: How do I know if my farm soil lacks nutrients before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If crops from the previous season had pale green or yellowish leaves and grew very slowly despite good rain, your soil is likely low in nutrients like nitrogen. Applying well-composted manure or NPK fertilizer helps replenish the soil.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni jɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crops are harvested and root residues decompose, they naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers around the main plantain stem causes them to compete for soil nutrients and water. Keeping only two or three healthy suckers ensures your main stem produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ abɔle ŋmeii babaoo ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ afee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when daytime heat is too intense or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet repeatedly. Mulching the soil and watering regularly helps keep soil moisture constant so fruits can set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that dries out the topsoil quickly. Waiting for steady, consistent rain ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahum ni mli edɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the season make my crop yield so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from young crop seedlings during their critical growth period. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks allows your crops to establish strong root systems without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo pɛ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have short roots that stay near the surface of the soil. When the soil surface dries out, the plant cannot absorb nitrogen and water, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and stop growing.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛ nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do rice plants require so much standing water compared to crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice naturally grows in swampy environments and needs saturated soil to feed properly and choke out weeds, while cassava has deep storage roots that allow it to hold water and survive in very dry soils.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ, ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛha jwɛi akabote ŋshɔ lɛ naa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ.

english: How can my crops manage to stay alive during the long dry season in Ghana?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Crops survive the dry season when farmers use techniques like spreading dried grass on top of the soil (mulching) to trap moisture, giving plants shade, or choosing crop varieties with deep roots that reach underground moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni okwaafoi kɛ ŋaai tamɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Ha tsei loo tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he lɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The plant wilts on purpose to shrink its leaf area and save water, usually recovering once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaa baa shi ni amɛbu nu he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops much more heavily during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, wild bushes dry up and die, so insects move into irrigated farm fields looking for food. Heat also causes insects to hatch and multiply much faster.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi. No sɛɛ lɛ, kooloi bibii fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni afɔseɔ nu yɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Dɔlɛ hu haa kooloi fɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous rice harvest give me smaller yields than certified seeds bought from authorized sellers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced in controlled environments to maintain strong yield traits and disease resistance. Seeds saved season after season naturally lose these strong qualities and can carry hidden diseases.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ feɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ. Bɔni afee ni ahiɛ yibiiwoo su ni mli wa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela lɛ mli Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout out of the soil even after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry for them to wake up, if they are buried too deep for the young shoot to reach sunlight, or if insects and fungi in the soil destroy the seed before it emerges.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etswa. aloo afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ aná hulu la loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my crop field is running out of food in the soil just by looking at my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ mitsei lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Plants show hunger through visual signs: yellowing lower leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, purplish stems or leaves point to a lack of phosphorus, and weak stems with burnt leaf edges mean low potassium.
ga: Tsei jieɔ hɔmɔ kpo kɛtsɔ okadii ni anaa lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ ashã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa.

english: What happens to my crop plants if I plant them too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, resulting in tall, weak plants with very small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tight like a cup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense response. It is usually caused by tiny sucking insects hiding under the leaf, or extreme heat causing the leaf to fold up to prevent moisture from escaping.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa. Teemɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa Ha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them creates shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ E-haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: How close together should I plant my maize seeds so that I get big cobs?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tɛŋŋ koni maná ŋmãa wuji?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Keeping rows about 75 cm apart gives each plant enough room and nutrition underground to develop full, healthy cobs.
ga: Abele dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee 75cm lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ ŋta ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why is my cassava farm growing tall green leaves but very small tubers underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai ni kɛlɛ shi eyɛ ŋmɔji bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots below. Using balanced fertilizers rich in potassium helps the plant direct nutrients down into the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How do I tell if my crops have bad roots underground if I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shishifãi gbohii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mana hu?

english: Healthy crop roots are usually light in color, firm, and spread out wide to gather food. If a plant stays stunted, wilts easily during the heat of the day, or leaves turn yellow despite regular rain, it usually means roots are rotting or blocked underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ su ni mli tse, amɛhe wa, ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he koni amɛbua niyenii naa. Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi ni egbɔjɔ Egboɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Aloo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite loo amɛmiiwo shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the leaves of my maize right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season brings pests like the Fall Armyworm, which lay eggs on new, soft maize leaves. Checking your fields early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem oil solutions into the leaf funnels stops caterpillars before they ruin the farm.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ baai lɛ amli. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: What causes my tomato plants to suddenly wilt and die when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of soil-borne fungi or bacteria that enter the stem base and block water from moving up the plant. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like maize or cassava starves these soil diseases over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ sũ mli ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ helai nɛɛ aye hɔmɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every year even though I plant the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season consumes the same specific nutrients from the soil until the ground becomes exhausted. Rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally to restore farm yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa be lɛ baabi niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baaho. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii fata he lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and feeding the plant during the flowering stage keeps the blossoms on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and brown early before the harvest season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when affected by leaf spot diseases like anthracnose or prolonged dry spells. Staking vines high off the ground improves airflow around leaves, reducing disease spread and keeping the plant green longer.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe tamɔ anthracnose loo be kakadaŋŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni no haa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa tsei feɔ eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface and struggle to anchor the heavy plant during strong windstorms, especially when carrying fruit. Heap soil around the base of the stem (earthing up) and use bamboo stakes to support trees with heavy bunches.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ tsei ni tsii amli yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli. titri lɛ kɛ́ ewo yibii Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (shwie nɔ) ni okɛ ŋmeii atsu nii ni okɛfi tsei ni ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and burn when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi koko tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their root systems are not yet strong enough to take up enough water to stay cool. Clearing all shade trees exposes seedling leaves to sunburn, causing them to dry up, turn yellow, and drop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ aná hulutsoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baagbi. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of using energy to grow thick stems and big cobs, the plants stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the light, resulting in tall, weak stalks and poor yields.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji Tsei lɛ baajie amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flooded my field for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes out all the oxygen in the soil, causing the roots to suffocate, die, and rot before they can be harvested.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves and thick stems but tiny tubers after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ efata he sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers rich in nitrogen encourage green leaves and vine growth. If too much is applied, the plant spends all its energy expanding its top leaves instead of transferring starches down to build thick underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tso lɛ daalɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ ashikishaŋ ɔ kɛ wo mi konɛ e pee tuber nɛ mi wa.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas between my rows of young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-baby corn ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. Planting cowpea alongside maize acts like a natural fertilizer, feeding nitrogen to the maize while covering the bare soil to prevent weeds.
ga: Cowpea tsei yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Amɛhaa nitrogen baa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa koni jwɛi akaje mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and insects. Planting them back-to-back on the same plot allows pests and fungal spores left in the soil from the first crop to immediately attack the new plants.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fata tsei akuu kome he, ni helai kɛ kooloi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Dumɔ ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli lɛ tutuaa tso hee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers during the hot dry season without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: High heat and dry soil cause severe stress to pepper plants. To save water and preserve their own lives, the plants drop their blossoms, as they lack the moisture needed to nourish growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Koni okɛ nu aba shi ni okɛbu bo diɛŋtsɛ owala he. Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ejaakɛ ebɛ nu ni he hiaa koni ekɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's hybrid harvest produce weaker plants than the original seeds I bought from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically created by cross-breeding distinct parent plants to achieve maximum vigor in the first generation only. The seeds collected from that harvest lose those special traits in the second generation, producing uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Abɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni anyɛ ana hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms attack my young maize leaves so aggressively as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn baai lɛ waa kɛji nugbɔ je shishi pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay eggs on fresh, tender maize leaves because young leaves are soft enough for newly hatched caterpillars to eat. The onset of the rainy season creates the warm, humid weather and fresh plant growth the caterpillars need to hatch quickly.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ehee lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa ni tsei heei hu kwɛ̃ɔ Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ afɔ oya.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and die off right when the tubers are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves act as factories that turn sunlight into food and store it in the underground tuber throughout the growing season. Once the tuber is fully mature and full of starch, the vine naturally shuts down, yellowing and drying up to signal that the crop is ready to be dug up.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii akɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ niyenii mli ni ekɛtoɔ tuber lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Wein tso lɛ baakpa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kwraa ni etsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atsa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I don't plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni miduuu plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that shield the young cocoa plants from heat, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil runs low on nitrogen. To keep growing, the maize plant pulls nutrients away from its older, lower leaves and sends them to the top leaves and growing corn ear.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. koni eya nɔ ekwɛ Abɛi tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa baa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ abɛi toi ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts have special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, creating natural food that fertilizes the ground for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lush green leaves but produce tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much leaf growth or excess nitrogen, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of sending starches down to swell the tubers below.
ga: Be mli ni cassava lɛ baa lɛ fa babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu ŋmeii kɛba shi koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam plants yield much bigger tubers when I support the vines with tall poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs ni dara kwraa beni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ fiɔ wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to trap sunlight. Sunlight powers the leaves to produce food, which travels down the vine to feed and enlarge the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ wain tso lɛ mli koni eyatao niyenii ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do I find holes in my young maize leaves with tiny droppings inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. They crawl deep into the central leaf funnel during the day to hide from the sun and heat while feeding on the soft leaf tissues.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up, shrink, and stop growing normally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the sap under the leaves. As they feed, they pass viruses into the plant that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛkɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot rapidly during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool weather. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods, where humidity allows it to grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i lɛ baaha kookoo yibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I cut cassava stems from plants with yellow, twisted leaves to plant in my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ tsei ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ mli ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. The virus lives inside the stem fluid, so planting those cuttings will transfer the disease directly into your new crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Virus lɛ hiɔ nu ni jɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã otso hee lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant during hot, dry spells without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When heat is extreme or water is scarce, tomato plants drop their flowers to save moisture and stay alive, which stops the flowers from being fertilized and turning into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo nu faaa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their root systems are still small. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that keep the soil cool and prevent the leaves from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ lɛ baa, ni ehaa baa lɛ shãaa.

english: How do I know which direction to bury my cassava stem cutting in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds along the cassava stem; they must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoot will struggle to turn itself around underground, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Ewa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's growth will help restore the leaves to a healthy dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ wo mli yɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do I need to set up tall wooden sticks next to my yam mounds after planting?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔdu wɔgbe naa lɛ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔkɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs height to spread its leaves out toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent rot and ensures the plant captures enough sunlight to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Staking baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛkafite ni eha tso lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize crop early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds inside the growing whorl of maize. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active protects the crop before they destroy the growing points.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants twisting up and turning crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Clearing nearby weeds and using neem oil or mild soaps can help clear these pests and keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ni okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant stay cool and hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many maize seeds together in one hole to get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Akɛ dumɔwui toɔ he kome yɛ bu kome mli koni ená yibii babaoo.

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the crops to fight with each other for space, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each single stem enough resources to grow thick stalks and produce large, fully filled corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná he ko, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmei agboi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do people advise planting beans or groundnuts on a field before planting corn the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them with maize enriches the soil naturally, so your next crop grows stronger with less expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara waaa nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes develop black rotten spots as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato shishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kɛji ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black rotten spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by Blossom End Rot, which happens when plants don't get a steady supply of water to transport calcium to the fruit. Watering your plants regularly and evenly prevents these spots from forming.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black spot rot ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji Blossom End Rot, ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ calcium baa amɛyibii lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ. Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ daa kɛ daa lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting drowned by excess water, which starves the roots of air. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eefo nu mli fe nine, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally feed nitrogen into the soil, acting as a free, natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛdara yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why are my crops staying tiny and stunted even though I feed them fertilizer regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Your soil may have become too acidic, which locks up nutrients so the plant roots cannot absorb them. Applying agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil lowers the acidity and frees up those nutrients for your crops.
ga: Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ato kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha acidity lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha nakai niyenii lɛ aya onibii amli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light rain because the soil underneath remains dry. Wait until a heavy rain thoroughly wets the top soil down to about 10 to 15 centimeters so the seeds have enough continuous moisture to germinate.
ga: Kaadu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo pɛ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ji sɛntimitai 10 kɛyashi 15 lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant many seeds close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to develop strong roots and produce large, full yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to multiply in the ground. It also drains the exact same nutrients every season, leaving the soil tired and weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hu hoɔ daa be mli. Ehaa etɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds when my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate and grow slowly at first. Clearing weeds early stops aggressive weeds from stealing the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your young crops desperately need to establish themselves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ waaa ni amɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Ehaa jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ waa koni amɛto amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I saved from last harvest will actually grow before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani adu?

english: Take 10 seeds and place them inside a wet cloth for three to four days. If 8 or more sprout, your seed batch is strong; if fewer than 5 sprout, the seeds are poor quality and you should source new seed.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji tsei ni shɛɛɛ 5 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ehiii kwraa. Ni esa akɛ otao dumɔwui heei.

english: How should I store my cassava stem cuttings so they do not dry out before I plant them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ koni mi-cassava niji lɛ akagbi dani madu?

english: Store cassava stems vertically in a cool, heavily shaded area with their bottom ends resting in moist soil. This keeps the stems alive and juicy for several weeks until you are ready to plant them.
ga: Kɛ sinava tsei lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Naagbee ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baajɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ otsii babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: Why do my rice seedlings grow very tall and thin instead of strong and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei daa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are sown too close together, the young plants compete heavily for sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as they can to reach light, which makes them grow tall and weak rather than developing thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii baatswa hulu la he akaŋ waa. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená tso ni mli wa ni mli wa

english: Why do young plants struggle to develop strength when there are too many growing in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ? Beni tso bibioo lɛ daa babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Plants in a crowded area must share a limited amount of soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Because no single plant gets enough food, none of them can build the strong roots and stems needed to produce a heavy yield.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la fioo ko pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni baanyɛ aná shishifãi kɛ tsei ni wa ni he hiaa koni ewo ŋmɔshi nii babaoo.

english: How does proper spacing prevent my mature rice crops from falling over during heavy rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa aaatsi ŋmãa tsei ni eda lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Giving plants enough space allows them to build deep root systems and wide, thick stems. These sturdy plants can easily support the weight of heavy rice heads and withstand strong winds and rain without falling over.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mli tse. Nɛkɛ ŋmãa tsei ni he wa nɛɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo. Ebaanyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa ni egbeee shi.

english: How does moving rice seedlings from a nursery to the main field make them healthier?
ga: Te ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛná hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Transplanting gives each seedling its own dedicated space in the main field. With room to spread its roots and leaves without competition, the seedling gains strength, branches out better, and grows healthier.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ. Kɛ gbɛ ni akɛgbɛɔ shishifãi kɛ baai ashwãa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa. Niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ hewalɛ kpakpa

english: Is it better to grow my rice in a small nursery bed first or plant seeds directly in the main field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ loo aaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery allows you to nurture delicate shoots safely. Moving the strongest seedlings to the main field with proper spacing ensures a more uniform, healthy, and high-yielding crop compared to scattering seeds directly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he titri lɛ kɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome, amɛhe wa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa tɛ̃ɛ he

english: What happens if I leave my rice seedlings in the nursery bed for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa saatso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seedlings stay trapped in a crowded nursery bed past their ideal move date, they become overcrowded, tall, and weak. Transplanting them late makes it harder for them to recover and grow strong in the main field.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baayi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi tsɔ. Tall and weak Late planting lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaatsake amɛhe ni amɛdara waa yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do rice plants that have space around them produce more grain branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ni he ko bɛ ehe lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani niji babaoo yɛ?

english: Space allows sunlight to reach the base of the rice plant, encouraging it to produce multiple side shoots called tillers. More tillers mean more heads of grain on a single plant.
ga: He lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi. Ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fãi srɔtoi ni atsɛɔ amɛ spades lɛ he hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ babaoo tsɔɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni jɛ tso kome mli.

english: Why should I spend money on labor to transplant rice instead of just scattering the seeds on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: While scattering seeds saves labor upfront, it leads to crowded, weak crops and low harvest yields. Spending money on transplanting ensures strong plants that produce much more grain, earning back your investment and turning a higher profit.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, dumɔwui lɛ agbɛshwãa lɛ haa nitsumɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ hiɛ lɛ baa. Shi ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo fioo pɛ. Shika ni afiteɔ yɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo. Enɛ haa onáa shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ ekoŋŋ ni onáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: How do I know if putting extra money into proper rice planting methods will give me a good return?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ shika babaoo ni okɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai baaba?

english: Proper methods like nursery growing and transplanting yield significantly more grain per acre. The cash you gain from selling the extra rice harvest usually far outweighs the initial expense of careful planting.
ga: Gbɛi ni sa tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔ mli ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ haa dumɔwui babaoo baa yɛ acre kome mli. Bei pii lɛ, shika ni onáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ mli lɛ fa fe shishijee shika ni okɛbaadu amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can spending a little more during planting help me afford my farming costs for the next season?
ga: Ani shika fioo ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ baaye abua mi yɛ mi okwaayeli he nyɔmɔwoo kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, investing in good planting techniques produces a larger, higher-quality crop. The extra profit from selling a bigger harvest leaves you with enough money to cover your expenses and reinvest in your farm for the following season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ shika wo ŋaai kpakpai ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi ni baajɛ nibii babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli aba lɛ baaha oná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to start growing crops without using high-cost fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture well and has plenty of decomposed plant material or earthworms is a sign of healthy soil that can feed young crop roots naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsei ahe nibii loo ŋmeii babaoo ni fiteɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe okadi.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and turn yellowish during the dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl to protect themselves from losing water during intense heat, but yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen or suffering from root stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi lɛ miipiŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers before any peppers actually start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or an imbalance of nutrients, such as having too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛ phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to one another to get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants and a lower overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do experienced farmers grow beans alongside maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in the same place allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up in the ground and drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava leaves are changing color because of a disease rather than a lack of rain?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ hela hewɔ ni ŋmeii baa lɛ miitsake amɛsu moŋ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: A lack of rain causes bottom leaves to dry and fall off slowly, whereas plant diseases usually create distorted leaves, twisted growth, or bright yellow patches across the foliage.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ haa shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi fiofio. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ tsei ahe helai haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. shweremɔ ni ejaaa loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ ahe

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even when there is enough rain for everything to grow?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have aggressive root systems that steal essential soil nutrients, block sunlight, and harbor pests that can attack your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa, ni amɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atutua onibii titrii lɛ ahiɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to water my crops during the hot season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the afternoon prevents the water from evaporating quickly in the sun, allowing the roots to absorb maximum moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu babaoo.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ dɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred and treated to resist common diseases, sprout evenly, and produce higher yields compared to saved seeds, which lose vigor over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni atsaa amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato ni hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ he

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and retaining soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for growing large tubers beneath the soil. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves up to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: How do cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil richer for the next season's crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Heavy rainfall fills all the air pockets in the ground with water, suffocating the roots and allowing soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eyi kɛ nu. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. The plant temporarily droops to shrink its surface area facing the sun to prevent water loss.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛkwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ koni nu akafite.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience drought stress. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the unpollinated blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves or transmitting viruses. The plant leaves curl up as a reaction to damage and stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ mli baa.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide deep inside the center funnel of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-corn baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the cool, moist leaf funnel during the day to protect themselves from the hot sun, birds, and chemical sprays while feeding on the soft young leaves inside.
ga: Roundworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, okpoi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe. be mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my young crops look small and weak if I delay weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, fertilizers, and sunlight faster than young crop seedlings can. Early weeding removes this competition so your crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe dumɔwui bibii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, ebaajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that dry out quickly in harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them from the sun while their roots grow deep into the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure around the plants helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea, loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo fata Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes into the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young corn leaves and stalks. Detecting them early and applying recommended neem-based sprays or bio-pesticides directly into the central plant funnel kills the pests before they destroy the entire crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii. Ni aaana amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni neem yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nubu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baagbe kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Healthy cassava stems should be selected from strong, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from diseases or insect damage. Cutting firm stems from the middle portion of the main stalk gives the best sprouting success.
ga: Esa akɛ ahala ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela loo kooloi fiteee amɛ lɛ amli. Tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and spread them out toward the sunlight. When leaves get plenty of sunlight, they make more food energy, which leads to much larger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha niyenii lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I avoid placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that burn tender stems and roots when touched directly. Placing the fertilizer in a ring or line a few inches away from the stem allows roots to absorb nutrients safely without burning.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baashã tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmei loo ŋmei mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my land for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested and root residues decompose, natural nitrogen fertilizer is left behind in the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi ni efite lɛ fite lɛ, ashiɔ Natural nitrogen fertilizer yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it better to clear weeds while my crops are still small instead of waiting until the weeds grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ agbɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops compete heavily with weeds for light, water, and plant nutrients in the soil. Removing weeds early gives young plants an uninterrupted head start, whereas waiting lets tall weeds choke the crop and steal vital nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ jwɛi yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ haa jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: What causes the bottom of my tomato fruits to turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Black rotten spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which occurs when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium into growing fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and making the fruits stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee aduawai lɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that spread viruses, or by severe heat stress. Spraying early with insecticidal soap or neem oil controls these insects and protects plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Haomɔ ni naa wa ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ shwieɔ nɔ mra Ekudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ he.

english: How does heavy land digging or mining activity near my farm affect my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsaa loo shika tsuru ni atsuɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ ni tsii lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Digging and heavy soil disruption strip away the fertile topsoil and can release toxic minerals or heavy sediment into nearby soil and water sources, making it hard for crop roots to absorb nutrients and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni atsaa waa kɛ ekpãtãmɔ lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ejie sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo sũ ni mli wa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops give a smaller harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize rapidly consumes essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture so the young cocoa survives its early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi lolo yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to capture maximum sunlight for energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground allows the plant to feed itself better, resulting in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest that targets the tender central funnel of maize plants. Checking your farm early and using biopesticides or targeted spraying keeps them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and dying off quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: This is often a sign of fungal leaf diseases or root damage. Pruning dead leaves and keeping the surrounding soil well-drained helps stop fungi from spreading to healthy parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji fungal leaf hela loo shishifãi ni efite lɛ he okadi. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when soil stays soaked in water for days. Excess water starves the tubers of oxygen, encouraging rot-causing organisms; planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli gbii babaoo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha bulb lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Ekanyaa nibii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Does my valley-bottom rice need to be submerged in deep water all the time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-jɔɔ lɛ shishi ŋmãa lɛ awo nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: Rice likes wet soil, but seedling plants can drown if completely submerged for too long. Soil needs to be kept moist or shallowly flooded, but keeping the tops of young plants above water is necessary for good growth.
ga: Omɔ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ. Shi dumɔwui baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ to nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo nu atsɔ mli fioo. Shi tso bibioo lɛ yiteŋ ni aaaha ehi nu nɔ lɛ he miihia waa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off before any tomatoes can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when air temperatures get extremely high or when the plant experiences sudden water drought during flowering, which prevents pollen from fertilizing the flower into a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. aloo beni tso lɛ naa hɔmɔ shihilɛi trukaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni pollen lɛ akawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Can I plant pepper together with cassava on the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu pepper kɛ cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping pepper with young cassava works well because pepper grows fast and can be harvested early, while cassava takes longer to mature and branch out, allowing you to maximize cash flow from one piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmeii bibii duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ mra. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ niji. Enɛ haa onáa shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from lower leaves usually means your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key food plant roots take from the soil to stay green, so when soil runs low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei shishifãi jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts on my farmland before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a special ability to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut plant dies and rots after harvest, that stored nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmei tsei gboi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If cassava stems are planted too close together, their underground roots will fight each other for water and soil nutrients. This leaves you with many small, thin roots instead of large, heavy tubers that yield a good crop.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha oná shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii ni woɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my corn plants even when the corn is already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? mi ŋmãa tso lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi momo moŋ, shi.

english: Even if your corn is taller than surrounding weeds, the weed roots under the ground are actively stealing water and soil fertilizer away from your corn's roots, which weakens the plant and reduces harvest size.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-abele lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ po, Shi jwɛi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ miiju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛmiijɛ abele lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ nɔ aba shi.
