english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall sticks or wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nine loo tso tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yam plants produce energy to grow large underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts leaves off damp soil into full sunlight, preventing fungal diseases and helping the plant make bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over after they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi lɛ? Beni ebɔi yibiiwoo sɛɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, making it difficult for the tree to support a heavy fruit bunch on its own during strong winds. Supporting the stem with sturdy wooden props helps bear the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli Tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ muji lɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because afternoon heat causes water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch the leaves or cause fungal rot.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ loo eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my young cocoa tree leaves wilting and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves wilt because direct, hot sunlight dries them out faster than their small root systems can draw water from dry ground. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kookoo baai lɛ gĩɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in young leaves are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, eating the tender leaves inside the plant funnel before they open up. Checking the funnel early helps you spot pests before they destroy the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite tso lɛ shishi.

english: How can I know if my cassava tubers are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: You can tell cassava is reaching maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem as expanding underground tubers push the soil open.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko miida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbeleɔ.

english: How can I protect my tomato plants from insects that eat the fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ aduawai lɛ ahe?

english: Pests love tender crops like tomatoes. You can protect them by applying safe chemical insecticides or natural neem oil sprays regularly, starting before you even notice major damage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ tomato. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛbaatsu nii daa loo ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛbaashwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ejeɔ shishi dani oyɔseɔ nɔ ni efite waa po.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Spray your crops early in the morning or late in the evening. Spraying when the sun is very hot can burn the leaves and cause the chemical to evaporate too quickly.
ga: Okɛ tsofa afɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã baai lɛ ni eha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my vegetable plants to turn yellow and drop off?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi?

english: Yellow leaves are often caused by pest damage, fungal diseases from high humidity, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Fungal hela ni jɛɔ hulutsoo babaoo loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen

english: How much harvest can I expect to get from a single tomato plant?
ga: Yibii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ tomato tso kome mli?

english: With good care, proper water, and pest control, one healthy tomato plant can produce between one to three kilograms of good fruits over its lifetime.
ga: kɛ nu ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ Tomato tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai kilogram kome kɛyashi etɛ yɛ ewala beaŋ.

english: What key things do my plants need so they produce large fruits instead of small ones?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titri he hiaa mitso lɛ koni ewo yibii wuji yɛ bibii najiaŋ?

english: Plants need rich nutrients from organic manure or fertilizer, consistent water (especially when flowers appear), and full sunlight to produce heavy, high-quality fruit.
ga: Tsei he miihia niyenii ni fa babaoo, humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii. nu ni yaa nɔ daa Ehe miihia hulu babaoo (titri lɛ kɛ́ eyɛ fɔfɔi amli) kɛ hulu ni eyi obɔ koni ewo yibii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant many seeds close together or give them space?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe loo maha amɛ gbɛ?

english: It is always better to space your plants properly. Crowded plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small and weak harvests.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ oookɛ otsei lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my tomato plants during transplanting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ abɔ he kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ateŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Space your tomato plants about two feet apart in rows, with three feet between each row. This allows air to flow freely and prevents leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ ato ŋwɛigbɛ aaafee ninetalɔi enyɔ, ni ŋwɛigbɛ fɛɛ ŋwɛigbɛ afee ninetalɔi etɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa baa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Can I start growing crops successfully if I only have a small amount of money?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye lɛ dumɔ kɛji miyɛ shika fioo pɛ?

english: Yes, you can start small by buying basic certified seeds and using homemade compost or organic pest solutions to keep your starting costs low.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo kɛtsɔ shishijee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ nɔ. ni okɛ shia ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii koni shishijee nyɔmɔwoo lɛ akafee nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why do my crops sometimes fail even when my neighbor's crops succeed on the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ omanye eyɛ mli akɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop success depends on consistent management. Small details like planting depth, early pest control, seed quality, and watering schedules make a huge difference in harvest outcomes.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ omanyeyeli damɔ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa nɔ. Nibii bibii tamɔ dumɔ mlibotemɔ mlibotemɔ Mra Pest Control Dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ nu be ni tsɔɔ Ehaa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa ŋmaa lɛ mli nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Should I buy certified seed packets from a store or save seeds from market tomatoes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui akui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ shwapo ko mli loo mabua dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato mli lɛ anaa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Certified seeds from agricultural stores are better because they are specially treated and bred to resist local pests and diseases, giving you a higher chance of a successful crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ hi fe no ejaakɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ babaoo ni okɛbaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green and leafy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trunk before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani eda lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess shade branches allows sunlight and air to dry the trees, which stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji babaoo ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tso lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the sap from the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from distorting the leaves and stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ he okadi. Nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ Mra nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛkaha tsei lɛ adalɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing ground fungus and rot to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Shi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbo, ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does covering the ground around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive warm days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-vegetables lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. It keeps the soil cool and slows down water evaporation so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes, which means they can capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When a plant feels thirsty or overheated, it drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ tso lɛ nu kumai he loo edɔ lɛ tsɔ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu ehe.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over when the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold up the heavy weight of a maturing bunch. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy, notched wooden pole provides the support needed until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ tsei niji ni eda lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ fĩ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ aba kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I put too many seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and branches to expand fully.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa fioo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients intended for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I make my garden beds narrow enough that my hand can reach the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee mibɔɔ mli saatso lɛ mlɛo bɔ ni sa koni minine ashɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Making garden beds narrow enough so you can easily reach the center allows you to pull out weeds and harvest crops without stepping on the soil. Stepping on the bed packs down the dirt, which damages delicate roots and makes it hard for water to sink in.
ga: Kɛ́ oha obɔɔ mli saatso lɛ fee mlɛo bɔ ni sa koni onyɛ oyashɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ogbalaa jwɛi ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ onaji shwie saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabua muji naa. Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ehaa ewaa akɛ nu baabote mli.

english: Why do I need to leave clear walking paths between my rows of crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Clear paths give you convenient access to move around your field with your tools, inspect your plants for diseases, and pull weeds without accidentally trampling on your growing crops.
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ haa onáa gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ oya he fɛɛ he. ŋmɔ mli kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ kɛji helai yɛ amɛmli. ni ogbala jwɛi ni okɛ onibii ni miida lɛ shwieee shi yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant with too little food, resulting in thin stalks and very small yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii fioo tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds right around the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing the area directly around the plant stem removes competition so the crop roots get all the water and fertilizer. It also clears away dark, damp places where harmful pests like to hide.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he ni ebɔle tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaa akaŋshii ni yaa nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ahe koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ shi. Ejieɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara yɔɔ mli lɛ hu kɛyaa.

english: Why should I pull weeds out by hand instead of using a hoe around young tender vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ minine agbala jwɛi moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmei baabɔle aduawai bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Using a heavy hoe close to young crops can easily slice or damage their delicate root systems just under the soil. Pulling weeds by hand allows you to remove the weed root cleanly without disturbing your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni tsii tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ efo loo efite shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ onine gbala jwɛi lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi lɛ shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ogbalaaa onibii amli.

english: How can I tell if weeds are stealing food from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ jwɛi miiju niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: If your crop leaves begin to look pale or yellow, grow much slower than normal, or stay small while the wild plants around them look tall and bushy, the weeds are taking the soil's nutrients away from your crop.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo babaoo fe bɔ ni eji daa loo bibii yɛ be mli ni koo mli tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi lɛ miihe niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ onibii amli.

english: Why is clearing the ground completely before I plant so important for my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo he lɛ dani madu kɛha midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Clearing the land gives your new seeds open space, direct sunlight, and exclusive access to water and soil food without having to fight established bush roots from day one.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oootsi lɛ baaha odumɔwui heei lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ shishifãi lɛ awuu kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like human babies and need shade from hot sun to survive. Leaving tall shade trees protects them from scorching heat and keeps the soil cool and moist until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni ehe miihia ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ waɔ.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering bare soil with dry grass acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and blocks sunlight so new weeds cannot sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni otsĩ hulu lɛ naa koni jwɛi heei akakwɛ̃.

english: Can I allow my sheep and goats to enter and graze on my field after harvest?
ga: Ani miŋmɛɔ mitooi kɛ mibotiai lɛ gbɛ koni amɛye miŋmɔji lɛ yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, allowing animals onto your field after harvest helps clear leftover crop waste and naturally suppresses early weeds. As the animals graze, they also drop droppings that enrich your soil with free natural manure for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oŋmɛɛ kooloi ahe kɛtee oŋmɔji amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ni ebaatsi jwɛi ni baa mra lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. be mli ni kooloi yeɔ jwɛi Amɛshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are some crop seeds red while others are white, and does the color affect how they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi yɛ tsuru ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ futafuta lɛ? Ni ani kɔla lɛ náa edalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Seed color usually identifies different varieties of the same crop species. While color itself doesn't change growth, different colored varieties often have different traits, such as how fast they mature, their taste, market demand, or resistance to diseases.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni su diɛŋtsɛ tsakeee bɔ ni mɔ lɛ daa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, sui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi, tamɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya, bɔ ni amɛ ŋɔɔ, bɔ ni jarayeli nibii taoɔ, loo bɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai.

english: Why do some crop varieties have local names like 'Aso Ntɛm', and what does that tell me about the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ gbɛi tamɔ ‘Aso Ntɛm’ ni mɛni enɛ tsɔɔ mi yɛ tso lɛ he?

english: Local names are often given by local farmers or plant breeders to describe a plant's special trait. For instance, names containing 'Ntɛm' in Twi usually mean 'fast' or 'early', telling you that the crop grows quickly and matures in a short time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋ okwaafoi loo tsei akwɛlɔi kɛ akutsoŋ gbɛi haa koni amɛkɛtsɔɔ tso ko sui krɛdɛɛi. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, gbɛi ni ‘Ntɛm’ yɔɔ mli yɛ Twi mli lɛ fɔɔ shishitsɔɔmɔ ni ji ‘oya’ loo ‘mra’, ni ekɛɔ bo akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How do I choose the right month, like July or August, to start planting my crops?
ga: Mahala nyɔŋ ni sa, tamɔ July loo August. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aje tsei akwɛmɔ shishi?

english: You choose planting months based on the rainfall patterns in your region and how long your crop takes to grow. Planting in July or August allows short-season crops to use the late rains to develop fully before dry weather arrives.
ga: Ohalaa odumɔ nyɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahe ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ July loo August mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ naagbee be lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: If you plant too late, the rains may stop before the plants finish forming seeds or fruits. This causes the crops to dry up early, resulting in small seeds, poor yields, or complete crop failure.
ga: Kɛji odu sɛɛ tsɔ Nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa dani tsei lɛ agbe dumɔwui loo aduawai akwɛmɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii baa, yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshɛɛɛ he.

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest a crop twice in one year in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, if you plant fast-growing or early-maturing crop varieties during both the major rainy season and the minor rainy season, you can successfully harvest twice in a single year.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okwɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oná ŋmaakpamɔi enyɔ ni yeɔ omanye yɛ afi kome mli.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a crop takes 65 days to mature?
ga: Beni extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heɔ gbii 65 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: It means that from the exact day you put the seed into the moist soil, it will take about 65 days (a little over two months) for the plant to grow, flower, and produce mature seeds or fruits ready to be harvested.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɛjɛ gbi ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Eheɔ aaafee gbii 65 (ni fe nyɔji enyɔ fioo) dani tso lɛ daa, ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni eda loo aduawai ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why should I buy a crop variety that matures in two months instead of one that takes four months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ mli moŋ fe nɔ ni heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ?

english: Two-month varieties are ideal if your region has short rainy seasons or unpredictable rainfall. They escape late-season droughts, allow you to harvest quickly for fast cash, and spend less time exposed to farm pests.
ga: Nɔ ni eye nyɔji enyɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku loo nugbɔshiimɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ. Amɛjoɔ hɔmɔ naa foi yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa oya koni oná shika oya. ni amɛyeɔ be fioo ni amɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpeɔ

english: How can I tell if my crop seeds are progressing well under the soil after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Good seed progress begins with quick, even germination within 4 to 7 days. Once sprouted, healthy seedlings will have strong green stems and leaves, showing steady growth each week without yellowing or wilting.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ni yaa hiɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ oyaiyeli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ po yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, amɛyɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa. Ebaaya nɔ eda daa otsi ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does using saved seeds from my previous harvest affect how fast my crop matures?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaná bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, saved seeds can lose quality over time, leading to slow or uneven growth. Certified seeds from reliable suppliers grow uniformly and are guaranteed to mature within the exact timeframe stated for that variety.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa edalɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛjɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni anáa nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni ato aha nakai dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: How do I know for sure that my crop is ready for harvest around October?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ October mli?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready for harvest, such as leaves turning yellow or drying up, stems becoming brittle, and seed pods or grains becoming firm, dry, and changing to their final mature color.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ, tamɔ baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni amɛgbiɔ. Tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmeii loo dumɔwui lɛ mli waa, amɛgbiɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛfeɔ su ni egbɔ.

english: How do I know for sure that my maize is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is mature when the silk turns dark brown, the outer leaves turn dry and straw-colored, and a small black spot appears at the tip of each kernel where it connects to the cob.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ siliki lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe feɔ jwɛi su. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ naa.

english: Can I leave my mature crops on the field for a few weeks if I am not ready to harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi miŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi kɛji mifeee klalo akɛ makpãa?

english: Leaving mature crops on the field exposes them to rain, pests, and fungal diseases, which damages the crop quality and reduces the amount you can harvest.
ga: Nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ehaa nɔ ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my corn bring in very little money during the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest and sell corn at the exact same time, the market gets overcrowded with supply, causing buyers to lower their prices.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmãa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayelihe lɛ eyi kɛ nibii. ni haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baa shi

english: How do I choose a new crop to plant if my current crop is no longer profitable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni madu? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ bɛ sɛɛnamɔ dɔŋŋ hu?

english: Look at what local markets and restaurants are buying regularly, check which crops grow well in your soil, and choose varieties that can be stored easily without spoiling fast.
ga: Kwɛmɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei kɛ niyelihei ni amɛheɔ nii yɛ daa lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ni halamɔ srɔtoi ni abaanyɛ akɛto mlɛo ni efiteee oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or suffering from water shortage, which weakens the plant and stops it from making big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii loo nu ni faaa lɛ miikpe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and woody instead of swelling big underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi agboi ni efuu lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small when the soil is too hard for them to expand, when plants are spaced too closely together, or when the land lacks essential soil nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa. Beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face heat stress, lack of water, or inadequate soil nutrition, causing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my neighbor's farm yield bigger crops than mine even though we planted the same week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ, beni wɔdu yɛ otsi kome mli lɛ?

english: Yield differences often depend on soil quality, using improved seed varieties, proper plant spacing, and timely weeding to prevent weeds from stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni jwɛi akaju tsei lɛ amli niyenii.

english: How does joining a farmers' group help me get better value for my produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe aaawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛha minibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: When you join a group, you can combine your harvested crops together to sell in bulk, giving you more bargaining power to demand higher prices from large buyers.
ga: Kɛ okɛ ohe wo kuu ko mli Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ afata he ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa onáa hewalɛ babaoo ni okɛbaahe nii koni obi jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛjɛ jarayelɔi wuji adɛŋ.

english: Why should I register my farm with the district agricultural officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋmala ŋmɔ lɛ awo kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Registering your farm makes it easier to receive subsidized fertilizers, certified high-yielding seeds, support services, and direct training from agricultural extension workers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ wo wolo nɔ lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shika mli lɛ anɔ. Dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni aŋmala he odaseyeli Fiɔ nitsumɔi kɛ tsɔsemɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ mlɛo

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees planted near them when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa ehe hulutsoo be mli ni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains act like umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until its branches grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi niji lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very slowly after I transplant them into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly when planted in poor soil or when soil pests like stem borers attack their roots. Adding rich compost and clearing pests around the base helps them start growing quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ stem borers lɛ tutua amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kompostifeemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ haa amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the stem base starts cracking as the roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves. Applying animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaves and spread viruses. Spraying neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Neem tso mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or poor nutrients. Keeping the soil continuously moist with mulching helps flowers stay on the plant and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ mulching ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ni etsɔɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small, round holes to appear all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo? ni shwieɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: These holes are caused by hungry caterpillars and beetles feeding on the soft leaves. You can protect your cabbages by spraying them with natural neem oil solutions or dusting them with clean wood ash.
ga: Hɔmɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ feɔ nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ. Obaanyɛ obu cabbage he kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni okɛbaafɔ nɔ loo tso sũ ni he tse ni okɛaafɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my farm crops if I leave them growing together in the same bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui kɛji miha amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, which starves your plants and significantly reduces the size of your final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni ehaa naagbee ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do the roots of my garden vegetables rot if I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli babaoo daa gbi lɛ?

english: Too much water pushes air out of the soil and drowns plant roots, causing harm and encouraging fungal diseases that rot the roots. Roots need moist, well-drained soil with air spaces to stay healthy.
ga: Nu babaoo tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ awuiyeli baa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa shishifãi fiteɔ lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does placing dried grass or leaves around my crop stems help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, locks moisture into the soil, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into free organic food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What short-term crops can I plant in Ghana that will be ready to harvest in about three months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli?

english: Crops like maize, cowpeas, and tomatoes mature in about 90 days (three months). Planting them gives you a quick harvest and fast income while you wait for longer-term crops to mature.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ aaafee gbii 90 (nyɔji etɛ) mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oná ŋmaa oya ni oná shika oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Can I plant my vegetables under large shade trees, or do they need direct sunlight to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ shishi? Aloo ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani enyɛ eda?

english: Most vegetables need full sunlight to produce food and grow strong. Heavy shade from big trees stops them from getting sunlight, making them slow-growing, yellow, and weak.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia aduawai babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo ni mli wa lɛ haaa amɛná hulu la, ni no haa amɛdaraa blɛoo, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Look at the leaves early in the morning; if they are wilting or curling before the sun gets hot, your plants are thirsty. Watering at the base of the stem early in the morning helps the soil hold moisture longer.
ga: Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ leebi Kɛji amɛgboi loo amɛbɔle amɛhe dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye otso lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are small insects suddenly eating the leaves of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai trukaa lɛ?

english: Young plants have tender, sweet leaves that naturally attract pests like caterpillars and aphids. Checking your field regularly allows you to catch and treat these pests early before they destroy the entire plant.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni otsa amɛ mra. dani amɛbaakpãtã tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant the exact same crop on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: When you plant the same crop repeatedly, it sucks out the exact same nutrients from the soil until the ground is depleted. Rotating different crops or adding animal manure restores energy back into the soil.
ga: Beni okɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ duɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Ebaaŋɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi sũ lɛ baaho aya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied twice: first about two weeks after planting when the roots start growing, and second at about six weeks when the plant needs extra food to make the maize cobs.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ mli beni tsei lɛ he hiaa niyenii kroko koni amɛkɛfee ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I just leave them in the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds steal the water, soil nutrients, and sunlight meant for your crops. If left unchecked, they consume the plant's food and leave your crops starved and undergrown.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ Kɛji akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaaye tsei ni amɛha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the mature plants fight for the same limited water and nutrients in the soil, leading to thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is fully ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as plant food for leaf growth, or that excessive water in the soil is preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tsei aniyenii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning dry during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to protect themselves from severe heat and water loss, but it can also be a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies have transmitted a virus to the plant.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, egbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tomato tsei amli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by prolonged drought, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attacks that damage the tiny flowers before pollination occurs.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafite amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hot temperatures make pepper plants shed their flowers as a natural defense mechanism to save water and energy so the plant itself can survive.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy soil for too long during rainy periods, causing soil fungi and bacteria to attack the wet roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi tutuaa shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: How does a seed yam sitting in my barn know when it is time to start sprouting?
ga: Te sweet potato dumɔwui ni ta mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural rest period called dormancy, and internal chemical changes trigger sprouting when temperatures and moisture signal that the rainy season is approaching.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Ni tsofai ni tsakeɔ yɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily even in light wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ po mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that are easily destroyed by pests like stem borers or tiny soil worms, leaving the heavy plant without strong support in the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers loo sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ fioo ko pɛ fiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that get scorched by direct sunlight; they need shade from taller trees to stay cool and retain moisture in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my maize crops grow thin and short even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ kuku kɛ kuku kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal light, water, and soil nutrients before your maize plants can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani o-corn tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops start showing signs of stress around November and December in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi haomɔ he okadii kpojiemɔ yɛ November kɛ December mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Around November and December, the harmattan weather begins, bringing dry, strong winds and lower humidity. This weather shift causes plants to lose moisture rapidly through their leaves, leading to temporary stress even if the weather was previously good.
ga: Aaafee November kɛ December mli lɛ, Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi eje shishi, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi eba. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa be kukuoo mli kɛji akɛ tsutsu lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ hi po.

english: How should I adjust my watering routine when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsake bɔ ni mikɛ nu woɔ nu mli yɛ Harmattan be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During the transition to the dry season, plants lose water faster due to dry winds. Water early in the morning or late in the evening to reduce evaporation, and apply mulch around the base of plants to trap soil moisture.
ga: yɛ tsakemɔ kɛmiiya hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ. Nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops when water builds up too much in the field after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: When standing water covers your crop roots for too long, it pushes out air from the soil. This prevents the roots from breathing, causing the plant to get stressed, turn yellow, or stop growing.
ga: Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akamu Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ekpa dalɛ

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually cause them stress instead of helping them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhao moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water. Without air, roots cannot absorb nutrients properly, leading to root rot and plant stress that looks similar to drought damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe haomɔ ni tamɔ hɔmɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops look weak even when there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: If soil stays completely waterlogged, the roots become deprived of oxygen and shut down. When roots cannot function properly, they fail to take up water and nutrients, making the plant look weak despite the moisture.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛbaafee amɛhe. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do strong winds that shake my crops cause them to stop growing normally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni hosoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dalɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Excessive movement and shaking from high winds create physical stress in the plant stems and can tear tiny root fibers underground, forcing the plant to spend energy repairing itself instead of growing.
ga: He ni ajieɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni hosoɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ. Ni ebaanyɛ efolɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni eha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ asaa ehe moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃.

english: How can I protect my crops from getting stressed by strong winds during storm seasons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli baa yɛ ahum be mli lɛ he?

english: Planting rows of taller trees or crops as windbreaks around your farm reduces the force of strong winds, preventing physical shaking damage and helping crops hold onto their moisture.
ga: Tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ŋwɛi koni akɛbu he ni ebɔle he lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Oŋmɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ hewalɛ aba shi. Tsi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni ekahoso ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Do crop roots really need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy?
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Koni ehiɛ hewalɛ kpakpa mli loo ehiɛɛɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ kpakpa mli?

english: Yes, plant roots need oxygen to perform normal living functions and absorb nutrients. Healthy, loose soil allows air to enter so roots can breathe properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli tse lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from environmental stress caused by bad soil air or water levels?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu ni ehiii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Stressed plants often show sudden yellowing of leaves, leaf droop, stunted growth, or early leaf dropping as they try to save energy under poor conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ jieɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa, baai ni shwieɔ shi, kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kpo. Aloo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛmiitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa amli.

english: Why do my young crops seem more easily affected by sudden weather changes than older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe oya fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young plants have smaller, weaker root systems and thinner stem tissues. They cannot store as much water or energy, making them much more sensitive to wind shaking, heavy water, or dry shifts.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛto nu loo hewalɛ babaoo amɛto. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if corn will grow well on my land before I spend money to plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mafite shika kɛdu?

english: Corn grows best in deep, well-draining soil that gets full sunlight and steady rainfall. You can check if nearby farms successfully grow corn or ask an extension officer to look at your soil texture and water retention before planting.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enaa hulutsoo be fɛɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa mli loo obi mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ hiɛɔ mli ehaa dani odu.

english: Should I focus on growing raw crops like corn or plant crops that are processed into finished products?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ nibii ni agbe naa lɛ adumɔ nɔ?

english: Raw food crops like corn give you quick food security and fast cash in local markets. Crops processed into finished products (like cocoa or oil palm) often bring higher profits, but they take longer to mature and require access to processing centers or contract buyers.
ga: Niyenii ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oná niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛ shika oya yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ nibii ni agbe naa (tamɔ kookoo loo mu) lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa, shi amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni ebiɔ ni anyɛ aya nitsumɔhei loo mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kpaŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow and dry up when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during extreme heat mean the plant is stressed from lack of water or nitrogen. When soil dries out, the roots cannot absorb nutrients properly, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow as the plant tries to save energy.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ miihao tso lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato lɛ.

english: What causes corn leaves to curl up tightly into tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural defense against heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the harsh sun, which stops moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do some of my corn plants produce large ears while others right next to them stay small and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ toi wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ji bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Uneven growth usually happens when seeds are planted too close together or at different depths. Plants that sprout first steal sunshine, soil nutrients, and water from neighboring seeds, leaving the smaller plants weak and unable to fill out their ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hei srɔtoi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ juɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo toi lɛ amli

english: How can I get reliable information on modern farming methods if my farm has poor mobile network service?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná saji ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni kɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi ahe? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ bɛ mobile network nitsumɔ ni ehiii hu?

english: You can visit community extension agents during weekly market days, listen to local agricultural radio shows, or download farming guides to your phone whenever you are in town so you can read them offline later on your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara akutso lɛ mli shweremɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔi lɛ yɛ otsi fɛɛ otsi jarayeli be lɛ mli. Bo maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he redio nɔ nifeemɔi atoi Aloo okɛ okwaayeli he gbɛtsɔɔmɔ awo otɛlifoŋ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni obaaya maŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okane yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Intanɛt lɛ nɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can weather apps on a smartphone really help me decide the exact week to plant my seeds?
ga: Ani smartphone nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he app ko baanyɛ aye abua mi diɛŋtsɛ ni makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ otsi pɔtɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu midumɔwui lɛ he?

english: Yes, mobile weather tools track regional cloud patterns and rainfall trends. They help you avoid planting during 'false rains'—brief rains that trick farmers into planting early right before a long dry spell that destroys young seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ dɛŋdade ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ kwɛɔ atatu henɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ dumɔ nii ahe yɛ ‘fake rain’, ni ji nugbɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ mli. ni lakaa okwaafoi koni amɛdu nii mra Dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni fiteɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ aba.

english: Is it better for me to plant only corn on my field or mix it with other crops like beans?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mikɛ ŋmãa krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa afutu mli?

english: Mixing corn with leguminous crops like beans (intercropping) is usually better. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps the corn grow stronger while protecting your farm income if one crop fails.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa (nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa) lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ oŋmɔ mli shika ni onáa lɛ he kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength and needs fertilizer or rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he waaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ awo mli?

english: If your crops are growing shorter than usual, showing pale green or yellow leaves, or taking longer to flower, your soil lacks essential nutrients. Planting cover crops or adding compost helps restore soil life.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ da kuku fe bɔ ni eji lɛ Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. loo eheɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni efeɔ daa lɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ wala baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do buyers in the market pay less for my harvest during the main season compared to the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ mikpamɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo yɛ be titri lɛ mli kɛ akɛtoɔ fɛ̃i be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crop prices depend on supply and demand. During the main harvest season, many farmers sell corn at the same time, forcing prices down. In the dry season, fresh corn is scarce, so buyers pay higher prices for available supply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe jara damɔ nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ. yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli Okwaafoi babaoo hɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ajara ni baa shi. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa hee baafee nɔ ni faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to build leaves and stems. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps bring back the healthy green color and improves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛma baai kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, but crops like beans and groundnuts naturally put food back into the soil through their roots. This keeps your land fertile without having to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ekɛ niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow better in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, so your plants stay hydrated even during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, otsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes inside the young leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide deep inside the center whorl of maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract early in the morning can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli leebi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is usually caused by irregular watering, which stops the plant from taking up calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the fruit develop normally without rotting at the bottom.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the tall trees off my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby gives young cocoa plants the cool shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long and drowns the roots. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why should I measure the space between my plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in weak plants and small harvests. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakpa ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why is it a good idea for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing cassava and maize reduces your risk of crop failure. Maize grows quickly and gives you food to harvest in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underneath and gives you a reliable food source long after the maize is gone.
ga: Kassava kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ baa shi. Abɛi daa oya ni ehaa bo niyenii ni obaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ, ni eji niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ efo mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tightly to trap moisture and reduce water loss through their leaves during intense heat. It is a natural sign that the plant is under heat stress and needs moisture or mulch to keep the roots cool.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi ni ehe miihia ni aná ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Is it safe to water my vegetable garden with stream water that cattle walk in and drink from?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ faa mli nu ni tsinai nyiɛɔ mli ni amɛnuɔ lɛ baafɔ mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: Using water mixed with animal waste can spread harmful bacteria like E. coli onto your crops and make people sick. It is safer to collect water from a clean well or build a small settling pond before applying it to your vegetables.
ga: Nu ni okɛ kooloi ahe jwɛi futuɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ E. coli, kɛya onibii amli. ni ebaanyɛ eha gbɔmɛi aná hela Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaabua nu kɛjɛ nubu ni mli tse mli loo afee nubu bibioo ko ni shwieɔ nu mli. Dani okɛbaatsu nii yɛ o-vegetables lɛ anɔ

english: How does covering the soil around my yam mounds with dried grass help the yams grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the soil soft and cool, allowing yam tubers to swell and grow much larger.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛfeɔ agboi babaoo.

english: What fast-growing barrier can I plant around my farm to stop roaming cattle from eating my food crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu gbɛtsii nii ko ni yaa hiɛ oya kɛbɔle ehe. miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsinai ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ akaye miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Planting thick, thorny hedge plants like acacia, bougainvillea, or bitter cassava around your field creates a living fence. Cattle dislike pushing through thorny or bitter leaves, which keeps them from entering your farm.
ga: Aduɔ tsei bibii tamɔ akasia, bougainvillea, loo yucca ni mli edɔ waa ni ebɔleɔ he. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ baafee gbogbo ni hiɛ ka. Tsinai sumɔɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ni mli edɔ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops growing along the edge of my farm field grow slower than the ones in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anaa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Edge crops suffer more because the soil there gets trampled hard by farm animals or humans walking past, compacting the dirt. Compacted soil prevents roots from spreading easily to take up water and plant food.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ naa amanehulu babaoo ejaakɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi loo adesai nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ waa aahu akɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oya koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow even when I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the roots are drowning from too much water or the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Giving plants too much water washes away nutrients and prevents roots from breathing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi babaoo ni ebote shishi. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaajie niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ mli, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akamu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers set into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cowpea plant suddenly wilt and die when the ground around it is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ lɛ? Ani efɔ lolo?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root rot or fungal disease living in the earth that clogs the plant's water pipes. Rotating your crops every season prevents these soil-borne diseases from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground space. This causes the plants to grow tall and slender above ground while producing small, skinny tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do crops planted right under large trees yield far less food than crops in open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food and form flowers or fruits. Big trees shade smaller crops from sunlight and their large root systems steal most of the water and fertilizer from the soil.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii ni amɛwo fɔfɔi loo aduawai. Tsei wuji haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ feɔ shade kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, full sunlight burns their sensitive leaves. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or shade trees alongside them protects the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni aaadu tso ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni daa oya tamɔ plantain loo umbrella tso yɛ emasɛi. Ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily whenever strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can struggle to hold up heavy fruit during storms. Staking the main stem with strong wooden poles and cutting away excess suckers helps keep the plant stable.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni baanyɛ awuu koni ekpa aduawai ni tsii yɛ ahum be mli Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ he ni afolɔ tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop fail to produce full corn cobs when the rains start late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo ŋmãa ni fa bɔ ni sa beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs consistent moisture when it forms flowering silk and ears. Delayed rains cause water stress, preventing proper pollination and keeping cobs small or unfilled.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ efee siliki kɛ fɔfɔi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa. Tsi pollination naa jogbaŋŋ ni oha ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii loo dumɔwui bɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even after staying in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ kɛ́ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin when planted in hard, packed soil or nutrient-poor land. Loosening soil into raised mounds or ridges gives roots room to expand and absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: Yes, intercropping beans with maize improves soil quality. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil to feed the maize, while maize stalks give bean vines support.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfiɔ ŋmãa wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: What is causing ragged holes and brown powder inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ pores kɛ brown powder ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?
