english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that eats the growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved controls prevents severe yield loss.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ yibiiwoo ni fiteɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ naa.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering in the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent allows tomato plants to continuously take up necessary calcium.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oooha ehi shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ daa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my food crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miniyenii tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is damp and plants have established early roots, typically 2 to 3 weeks after sprouting. Applying it during dry periods can burn root systems.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ etswa shishifãi oya, bei pii lɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back much faster than my crops every time it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants adapted to quickly soak up rainwater and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing sunlight and water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest yield less crop than certified seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mlijalɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor and disease resistance over generations. Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for higher yields, strength, and better pest resistance under Ghanaian growing conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ nɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yibiiwoo ni fa, hewalɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana shweremɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a natural defense to conserve moisture. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry periods to save water and energy. As long as the stems and top leaves remain healthy, the plant is simply protecting itself until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛkɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers before any pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa?

english: Cocoa trees drop unpollinated or weak flowers when they lack sufficient shade, moisture, or soil nutrients. Shedding extra flowers is the tree's way of managing its energy so it only feeds the pods it can support.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shi kɛji amɛbɛ hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: What basic steps can I take to protect my farm if a plant disease breaks out in a neighboring village?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji tso hela ko ba akrowa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli?

english: To protect your farm from spreading diseases, clean your tools with soap or fire after working, avoid moving soil or planting materials from affected farms, and clear away infected leaves immediately.
ga: Bɔni afee ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he Kɛ samla loo la atsumɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe kɛji ogbe nitsumɔ naa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo nibii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni ena naagbai lɛ amli lɛ he. ni ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt completely under the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho kwraa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ shishi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: Tomatoes can wilt under strong sun because heat makes water leave the leaves faster than the roots can pull it up. If they do not bounce back by evening, it may indicate root damage or a soil-borne fungal disease blocking water flow inside the stem.
ga: Tomato baanyɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu jeɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛji oku osɛɛ obaaa gbɛkɛ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ shishifãi ni efite loo sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why does heavy standing water cause my cassava roots to rot underground while the top leaves still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni tsii ni ekã shi lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shi amɛyiteŋ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the plant's roots, causing root cells to suffocate and decay underwater. The top leaves may stay green for a few days using stored nutrients before showing signs of damage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa wala yibii lɛ yashɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ nu shishi. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi eŋɔli gbii fioo komɛi kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ dani ejie okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ efite lɛ kpo.

english: How can I tell if my soil has recovered enough to support a new planting season after a bad harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ehiii sɛɛ?

english: Healthy, recovered soil feels moist and dark, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains living earthworms. If the soil is hard, pale, or dusty, it needs compost or organic manure before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ duŋ, efoɔ oya yɛ enine mli, ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ sũ lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii dani odu.

english: Why do weeds always sprout and grow much faster than my planted crop right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce tough seeds that stay dormant in the soil for months and react instantly to moisture. They grow quickly to capture sunlight and soil nutrients before your planted crops have established strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛhe hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every year when I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recharge. Rotating different crops, such as alternating maize with beans or groundnuts, rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainfall patterns keep changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi hewɔ lɛ

english: Avoid planting right after the very first light rain. Wait until the soil stays continuously moist several inches deep for three consecutive days to ensure seeds have enough water to germinate and grow roots.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛyashɛ inchii babaoo gbii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—their leaves burn easily under full sun. They need shade from taller plants like plantains to keep the air moist and protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed. If the tree drops almost all of them, it usually means the soil lacks key nutrients, the tree is thirsty, or there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ baagbee shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. tso ni kumai yeɔ lɛ Aloo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do some pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and high humidity allow a fungus to grow on the pods, causing black pod disease. Trimming excess shade leaves allows air to flow and sunlight to reach the trunk, keeping pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ black pod hela baa. Baai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce a lot of pods in certain months but very few in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli shi ekrokomɛi amli lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to rainfall cycles. Rain triggers flowering, and it takes about five to six months for those flowers to mature into full pods, creating natural main and minor harvest seasons each year.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he nii. Nugbɔ haa fɔfɔi baa. Ni fɔfɔi nɛɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli kpamɔ bei baa daa afi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is moving its nutrients to feed newer leaves or developing fruit. If too many leaves yellow at once, the soil might be low on nitrogen or water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsi niyenii mli nibii koni ekɛfee baai heei loo eewo yibii. Kɛji yellow card babaoo yɛ be kome mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ nitrogen loo nu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like large trees; their roots grow shallowly near the surface. When they carry a heavy bunch of fruit, strong winds can pull the roots out unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei wuji. Eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo yɛ nu lɛ hiɛ beni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni tsii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do new plantain shoots keep growing around the main stem after I harvest?
ga: Plantain tsei heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. Te mafee tɛŋŋ akpa tso titri lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow from an underground stem called a corm. When the main stalk dies or is cut down after fruiting, energy shifts to the small shoots (suckers) growing out of the same corm to create the next generation.
ga: Dumɔwui daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ amli. Beni tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ gbo loo afo lɛ beni ewo yibii sɛɛ. Akɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) ni daa kɛjɛɔ bulb kome mli lɛ amli koni ekɛfee yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does rice grow better when there is standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Rice plants can breathe through special tubes in their stems that bring air down to their roots underwater. Standing water protects the crop by drowning weeds that would otherwise steal light and soil nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ atsɔ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ amli amu koni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba shi kɛya nu shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju niyenii, la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my rice plants looking pale green instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse shi jeee eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves show that the rice plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding organic matter or fertilizer gives the leaves the building blocks they need to turn deep green and produce heavy grains.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Can I grow cassava or maize alongside my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside new cocoa provides temporary shade for the young cocoa seedlings while giving you food and income from the same piece of land while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo hee masɛi lɛ baaha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Heavy rains can also wash away nutrients from shallow roots, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yams produce huge green vines above the ground but only small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive shade, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leaves and vines above ground instead of storing nutrients in the tuber below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ woɔ tso nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them out in open, sunny fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves dry out easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective umbrella of shade and moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha shade kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay healthy during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that prevents heat from evaporating soil moisture, keeping the roots cool and wet for longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: The very first rain often only wet the surface while deep soil remains dry. It is best to wait until rains become consistent over several days so the seed gets continuous moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli egbi Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa gbii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and causing the whole plant to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading through the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. These pests hide inside the growing whorl of the plant to feed, and spraying early in the morning or late evening reaches them while they are active.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli kɛha niyenii. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie amɛnɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa amɛ be mli ni amɛtsuɔ nii lolo lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in flat or heavy soil without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, protecting the roots from fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, during dry spells, or when there are no insects to pollinate them, causing the plant to drop blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Shĩ tomato tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them too weak to form large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees like plantains or shade-giving forest trees to protect them, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to dry up and fall off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ebaai bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: What is eating tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaving small green droppings inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central whorl of the young maize plant during the day and eat the tender leaves, which can severely reduce your harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why does my cassava yield fewer and smaller roots when I plant it on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fioo kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants absorb a lot of nutrients from the ground to build large tubers. When you plant cassava repeatedly on the same spot without giving the soil a break or adding organic fertilizer, the soil gets tired and starves the new crops.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Beni oduɔ ŋmei shii abɔ yɛ he kome ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee shi loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei heei.

english: How do weeds hurt my maize crops if I leave them growing between the rows?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ baaye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. By taking away these essential foods from your maize plants, weeds cause the maize to grow thin, weak stalks with small cobs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi haa abele lɛ náa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too close forces your crops to fight each other for root space, water, and sunlight. Instead of producing more food, overcrowding creates weak, tall plants that produce fewer and smaller fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi, nu, kɛ hulu la mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha niyenii babaoo aba. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the stem before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant faces extreme heat stress or erratic watering. When the weather gets too hot or the ground goes completely dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe lɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetables with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves—a process called mulching—acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the dirt so the heat doesn't dry it out, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi haa nɔ - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions. Pruning low branches lets sunlight and fresh air into your farm to dry out the moisture and keep the fungus away.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, hɔɔŋ, kɛ nu ni efɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ooofolɔ Ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes nitrogen nutrients out of the ground, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts do the opposite—they put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, making the ground fertile for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii feɔ nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ nakai. Ebaaku sɛɛ ekɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to germinate after I buried them deep in dry dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a small amount of air, gentle warmth, and damp soil close to the surface to wake up. Planting them too deep buries them where water cannot easily reach them and where the young stem isn't strong enough to push through the heavy soil.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ fioo. hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ koni ekɛte shi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaafu lɛ yɛ he ko ni nu nyɛɛɛ aya jɛmɛ oya, ni ŋmeii lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen. Maize moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the newer leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei amli koni ehi shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my farm help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass help them during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which shades the soil from the harsh sun, keeps moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaaa efo oya. ni eha shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i ahi shi

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense, direct sunlight. Large shade trees act like umbrellas that protect fragile cocoa leaves from sun damage and keep the air humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni buɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into fruits when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up the pollen inside the blossoms. Without successful pollination, the flower cannot form fruit and falls off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes air out of the dirt, preventing roots from breathing. This excess moisture allows soil fungi to multiply and decay the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Plantain plants do not have a single deep taproot; instead, they have many shallow surface roots. Heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy, easily pulling the shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ bɛ shishifã kome po ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ sisifãhi fuu nɛ a mi kuɔ we. Yibii ni tsii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo. ni egbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ oya

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight enables the leaves to generate more energy, leading to larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of tough seeds that remain asleep in the dirt for years. When rain falls, these seeds quickly absorb water and sprout faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni wa ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, dumɔwui nɛɛ gbalaa nu oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms appear on my young maize leaves right after the dry spell ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall flukes jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni hulutsoo be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: The moths that lay fall armyworm eggs travel long distances on rain winds and prefer to lay their eggs on tender, fresh green shoots that sprout with the first rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ mli. Ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛwo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight overheats them and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains nearby keeps the environment cool and protects the young plants from harsh sun until they mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ fe nine ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots and heavy trunks. When the heavy fruit bunch develops, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground, which is why supporting the trees with bamboo poles or wooden stakes is essential.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa kɛ tsei ni tsii. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ afi otsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, a major food source for maize. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will help restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji ŋmãa niyenii titri lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms hiding in the center of my maize plants and eating the new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young maize shoots. Applying recommended biopesticides or safe organic mixtures like neem seed extract into the leaves early will protect the crop from severe damage.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛfutuɔ tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii. kɛbote baai lɛ amli kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout properly if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the surface, leaving the deeper soil hot and dry. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures the soil has enough moisture underground for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water fills the air pockets in heavy soil, preventing roots from breathing and encouraging fungus. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight, which feeds the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la, ni haa tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiitsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when water supply is irregular. Excessive heat stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination, so regular watering during flowering helps keep the blossoms healthy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du cowpea lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural food supply for the maize while also shielding the ground from weeds.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ bean lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry leaves and crop stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ tsei ashishifãi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, traps soil moisture, prevents weeds from growing, and decomposes over time to feed nutrients back into your farmland.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: How long does a cocoa tree take from the day I plant it until it starts producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ kookoo tso heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties recommended in Ghana usually start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years to start producing pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛba Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young seedlings usually mean they are getting too much direct sunlight, lack enough water, or need nutrients from the soil to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia koni ekwɛ̃ waa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun; plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects called midges; heavy rain, dry weather, or poor soil can also cause flowers to drop early.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hu baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo oya.

english: How often should I clear the weeds and bush around my cocoa trees?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weeding should be done about 3 to 4 times a year, especially during the rainy season, so weeds do not steal water and plant food from your cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ ejuuu nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during wet, dark, and humid weather when cocoa trees are planted too close together or surrounded by thick bush.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, duŋ, kɛ fɛ̃i be mli, kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time a cocoa pod is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A pod is ready when its skin changes color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn bright orange-yellow.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo beni hewolo lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse.

english: Why shouldn't I use a sharp cutlass to chop pods directly off the cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni mli wa tsuɔ nii? Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ kookoo lɛ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Chopping pods with a cutlass damages the flower cushion on the bark, which is the exact spot where future flowers and pods must grow for next year's harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dagger ŋmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe baahia ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ kɛha afi ni baa lɛ kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why must I cover my fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛgbi lɛ?

english: Fermenting the wet beans under plantain leaves for 5 to 6 days builds the rich chocolate flavor and changes the bean color from purple to dark brown.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ wo plantain baai ashishi gbii 5 kɛyashi 6 lɛ, ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa. ni otsake ŋmeii lɛ ahe su kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ mli

english: How do I test if my cocoa beans are fully dried and ready to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fully dried cocoa beans will crackle cleanly when squeezed in your hand, and when you cut them open, they should be brown throughout rather than purple.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa lɛ tswaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ nine mimɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ ofo lɛ Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: Cocoa trees require insects or human hand-pollination to transfer pollen between flowers. If pollination fails, the tree drops the unfertilized flowers to conserve energy for healthy pod growth.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ kooloi loo gbɔmɔ pollen koni ekɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛhe wa.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does doing it help my cocoa farm produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ ni ekɛ pods babaoo aba?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using tiny tools. This ensures a much higher percentage of flowers turn into full-sized pods compared to relying only on natural insects.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii oha mlijaa 100 ni fa babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔi ni dalɛ fa babaoo. Kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli kooloi pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and burn under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby shields young seedlings from excessive heat and provides the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni ebaaha amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This stress forces plants to grow tall searching for light rather than developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani minɔ lɛ gĩ ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda?

english: This is often due to cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree sheds excess young pods it cannot feed, or early fungal infections like black pod disease caused by too much shade and dampness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cherelle lɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei jieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. loo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some good branches from my cocoa trees when pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tso lɛ?

english: Pruning removes extra branches to allow fresh air and sunlight into the tree canopy. This reduces dampness that causes diseases and helps the tree direct more food and energy into pod production.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la abote tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce many flowers during the rainy season but drop them when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli shi amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Crops need continuous water to form and support flowers. During dry periods, water scarcity causes plants to drop flowers to protect themselves from drying out and dying.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei daa koni amɛto fɔfɔi lɛ ama shi ni amɛye amɛbua amɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be mli Nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbo koni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Are all the small insects crawling on my crop flowers harmful to my yield?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mitsei lɛ afɔfɔi anɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, many insects like tiny midges and bees are beneficial because they carry pollen from flower to flower so fruits can form. Only specific pests like capsids actually harm your crop.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli koni anyɛ awo yibii. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii komɛi, tamɔ capsids pɛ ji nɔ ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating crops like maize with legumes helps restore soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for nutrients just by looking at their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Plants show nutrient deficiency through leaf signs: light yellow leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, while purplish leaves indicate a lack of phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he okadii kɛtsɔɔ tsei ahe okadii anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or water. The plant pulls nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the growing cob, which tells you the soil needs extra fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is healthy enough to yield big tubers for making banku?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji kɛha banku?

english: Healthy cassava plants have full, bright green leaves without curling or light yellow patches. If the stems are strong and free from dark spots, the plant is successfully sending food down into the tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔleko loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ mli wa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ bɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ niyenii aya ŋmei lɛ mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why does plant sickness spread so fast from one end of my farm to the other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naagbee kɛyaa ekroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic fungi, bacteria, or viruses that travel through wind, splashing rain, or dirty tools. When infected plants touch or stand close to healthy ones, the sickness easily spreads across the field.
ga: Tse helai jɛɔ ŋmei bibii, muawai, loo muawai ni tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo nibii ni he tseee. Kɛji tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ta tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe loo amɛdamɔ amɛhe lɛ Hela gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops get tiny holes and start drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ejeɔ shishi egbiɔ?

english: Tiny insects like beetles or caterpillars chew on the leaves to feed themselves. Leaves act as the plant's food factory, so when insects destroy them, the plant cannot feed itself and slowly dries up.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars shwieɔ baai koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛye niyenii. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii feemɔ nitsumɔhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata nakai tsei lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii eha ehe ni fiofio lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year even when I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni mi hu midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground every season. If you keep planting without giving the soil a break or adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil loses its richness and becomes exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu nii ni ogbalaaa sũ lɛ mli loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, sũ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the maize I plant next season grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave that natural food behind, making the soil richer for maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Eshiɔ nakai adebɔɔ niyenii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of producing food, the plant spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach the sun.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ niyenii ni amɛbaafee lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui oya kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than farm crops. They steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants during their most critical growing stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otso lɛ yɛ edalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and look soft during the hottest time of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a plant's defense mechanism against heat. By rolling up, the leaves present a smaller surface to the sun, preventing the crop from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi bibioo kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some saved seeds fail to sprout well compared to fresh seeds bought from certified officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni ato lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or damp places lose their living power or carry diseases from the old harvest. Certified seeds are tested and treated to ensure almost every seed sprouts healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ loo amɛbaaŋɔ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa momo lɛ amli lɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ana akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plant roots need from the soil to stay green and build strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi taoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛma tsei shishifãi ni wa.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil after harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply granular fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away from the root zone into gutters and streams before the roots can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving crops hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli. dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ Efiteɔ oshika ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak and produce small yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers from my plantain tree instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo plantain tso ko mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food and water from the main mother plant, which results in smaller plantain bunches at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on tall poles instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food, while keeping the leaves away from damp ground diseases that cause rot.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhoo nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture faster than young roots can drink it, so the tree drops leaves to save water and keep its main trunk alive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and spoil quickly if I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes mature cassava tubers to soak up too much water underground, which lowers starch content and accelerates rot right after harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ fitemɔ yaa oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cup shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies that spread viruses while feeding on juice from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa be mli ni enuɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out and fail at pollination, making the plant shed the blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo amɛhe fɔfɔi lɛ. Ha tomato tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Yellow and curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects called whiteflies spreading the Cassava Mosaic Disease. Clearing weeds regularly and uprooting diseased plants early stops the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out easily under full sunshine and hot winds. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa creates living shade and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my maize crop lacks nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks nutrients like nitrogen, the leaves turn light green or yellow starting from the tips, and the plants stay short with thin stalks. Adding fertilizer early when the plants are knee-high restores their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ naa. Ni tso lɛ yɛ kuku ni eyɛ tsitsi bibioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tso lɛ mli mra beni eshɛɔ enaneshi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too closely makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leading to thin stems and small or empty cobs. Giving each seed proper spacing gives every plant enough room to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants adapted to quickly soak up water and fertilizer before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early within the first few weeks gives your crops a fair chance to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii ashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the soil becomes too dry or when daytime temperatures become excessively high. Keeping the soil consistently moist by placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plants helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni oookɛwo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller on the older plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni edara lɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it produces many young shoots called suckers that steal food from the main plant. Pruning away excess suckers and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main plant to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers, ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why are my harvested yams rotting so fast in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvesting, or if they are stored in hot, dark spaces with no airflow. Storing uninjured yams on raised bamboo racks in a well-ventilated, cool shade prevents rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni pilaaa lɛ to ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their vigor over generations, producing weaker plants and smaller yields. Certified improved seeds are specifically bred to germinate well, withstand local pests, and give higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and need protection. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist while your young cocoa trees become established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni ehe miihia ni abu he. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow. Adding compost or a nitrogen fertilizer will give the crop the nutrients it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How do cowpeas and groundnuts help improve my soil for other crops?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tsei krokomɛi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the soil, they leave behind natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rain becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the soil airy and the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ hu waa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by dry soil or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the tomato plant take up calcium from the soil properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if armyworms are attacking my young maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji parasites miitutua mi-baby corn lɛ?

english: Check the central leaves of your young corn plants for small ragged holes and dark patches of waste. Spotting these early allows you to treat the crop with neem extracts or recommended sprays before major damage occurs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ o-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli kɛji bu bibii yɛ mli. Ani egbɛ eshwa ni eyɛ sũ ni mli edɔ? Nibii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii dani fitemɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the season make my crops yield more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from young crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the resources it needs during its most critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Alternating maize with crops like beans or cassava keeps the soil balanced and reduces pests.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ebuaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: Why is it better to plant my seeds in straight lines instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives each crop enough space to get sunlight and nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa enáa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Watering regularly during hot dry periods helps the plant retain its flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ anyɛ afee.

english: Why should I separate my seeds and plant them spaced apart instead of putting many in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala dumɔwui lɛ amli ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: Crops are like people sitting at a dining table—if too many are crowded in one spot, they will fight over the same food, water, and sunlight. Spacing them out allows each plant to grow strong stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tamɔ mɛi ni eta okpɔlɔ he. Kɛji gbɔmɛi babaoo bua amɛhe naa yɛ he kome Amɛbaatswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome he. He ni tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso tsitsi mli waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize grains spoil and go moldy when I pack a large amount into big bags right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miifite ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui wuji amli babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize grains are still 'breathing' and trapping moisture. If you dump a huge amount into one big bag without drying them properly first, heat and sweat build up inside, causing mold and rot to destroy the crop.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ ‘muɔ’ lolo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji okɛ babaoo shwie kotoku agbo kome mli ni ogbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa buaa ehe naa yɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting even when I do not plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are alive even after harvest. When the rainy season approaches, the yam feels the change in humidity and naturally wakes up from its rest period to grow a new plant, using up the energy stored inside the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ po. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ, Sweet potatoes baanu tsakemɔ ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he. ni ebaate shi kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe mli koni ekwɛ tsei heei Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wither when I put a large amount of fertilizer right at the plant base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is concentrated like salt. If you dump too much at once right next to the roots, it burns them and sucks moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it. It is better to split the fertilizer into smaller amounts and place it a short distance from the stem.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋoo. Kɛji okɛ babaoo shwie shi shikome yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaashã ni ebaamu ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo fãi srɔtoi amli. ni okɛto he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow when the soil stays soaked with water for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When the ground is completely flooded, the water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing the plant to choke and its leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose to save water during dry spells. By dropping its leaves, the plant reduces water loss and puts itself to sleep until the rains return to bring new leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ewɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba ni ekɛ baai heei aba.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without producing any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant and dries out the pollen inside the flower. When it is too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed growing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Beni edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tomatoi ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my rice plant split into multiple stems after I transplant a single shoot into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ mli gbalaa ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo mli beni midu ŋmãa tso kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice naturally creates new branches called tillers from its base when it has enough space, water, and nutrients. This allows one single seedling to produce multiple heads of grain.
ga: Omɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ niji heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ niji kɛji eyɛ he ko, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa dumɔwu kome woɔ dumɔwui ayitsei babaoo.

english: Why do caterpillars eat my cabbage leaves so aggressively while leaving nearby cassava plants alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ waa, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves contain naturally bitter chemicals that protect them from pests, whereas cabbage leaves are soft, sweet, and rich in water, making them an easy favorite meal for caterpillars.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ cassava baai lɛ amli. Shi kɛlɛ, kaabeji baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni ŋmeii sumɔɔ waa.

english: Is it better to burn the bush when clearing my land or to clear it with a cutlass and leave the cut grass on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ ŋmei baashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Clearing with a cutlass and leaving the grass as mulch is better for your land. Burning destroys natural soil nutrients, kills beneficial organisms like earthworms, and leaves the soil dry, whereas decaying grass turns into natural fertilizer and keeps the soil cool and moist for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baatsu nii ni okɛshi jwɛi lɛ akɛ mulch lɛ, ehi kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.
