Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if the soil on my new farmland is rich enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Rich soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hands, holds moisture well after rain, and shows plenty of earthworms or dark leafy wild plants growing on it naturally. Pale, sandy, or hard-baked soil usually lacks the nutrients crops need to thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ o dɛ mi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo koo mli tsei ni baai diji babaoo yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ashã ni wa lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a signal that the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rain washes nutrients away or if the roots are sitting in too much stagnant water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani oooha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows under heavy shade, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ starch kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my field help my main crops grow better afterwards?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food inside the soil. When the bean plants die and rot, that food stays in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cold, and dark conditions. Clearing extra shade trees, pruning dead branches, and picking off infected pods quickly helps airflow and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei kɛha hulutsoo kroko. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebɔleɔ he fɛɛ he ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot inside the ground before I even dig them up at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ po yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Yam rot in the ground is usually caused by tiny worms called nematodes or fungal infections entering through wounds in the seed yam. It also happens when yams are planted in waterlogged soil that cannot drain properly after rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Ebaa hu kɛ́ adu sweet potatoes yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. If the weather is too dry and hot, or if there are no insects visiting to shake the pollen inside the flower, the plant drops the bloom to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni baa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is heavy rain or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. If soil insects or nematodes damage those shallow roots, or if the soil becomes too soft from standing water, the heavy weight of the plantain bunch easily pulls the whole tree down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii loo nematodes fite nakai shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bafee blɛoo tsɔ kɛjɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Plantains tsei ni tsii lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shi mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast in my field right after I clear the land with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmei efo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried quietly deep in the dirt for long periods. When you turn the soil with a hoe, you bring those hidden seeds up to the top where sunlight and air trigger them to germinate all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dioo be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aya ŋwɛi. he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikome lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep wilting when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their tender leaves burn and lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it. Planting nurse crops like plantains or cassava alongside them provides the shade and moisture needed for survival.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Adumɔ tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli. Ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ahi shi lɛ aba.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is typically caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with natural sprays like neem oil and removing infected plants stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What makes my cassava tubers rot in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess rainwater collects around the roots because the soil does not drain well. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain freely away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee nu jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is necessary for green leafy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer around the base helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts refills the soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ ayiɔ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do crops like cowpeas and groundnuts help improve my farmland's soil?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air using beneficial bacteria in their roots and store it in the soil, which feeds the next crops planted in that spot.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, he ni ekɛ niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to stay small and yield less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miifee bibioo ni ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your main crop gets all the nourishment it needs to produce well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold up heavy fruit bunches during windstorms. Supporting the plants with strong wooden or bamboo poles under the stem keeps them upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. mlɛo yɛ ahum be mli Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, poor watering, or too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding heavy fertilizer during flowering helps fruit form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves receive full sunlight to produce food. Better sunlight exposure on the leaves leads directly to larger, healthier tubers growing underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa.

english: Can I let my goats move freely around the farm where I grow my cassava and yams?
ga: Mibaanyɛ maha mitoo lɛ aya he fɛɛ he. Ani ŋmɔ ko ni miduɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee?

english: Goats will eat cassava leaves and dig up young yam shoots, which damages your yield. It is best to keep goats in a pen or tether them, then cut and carry crop waste or weeds to feed them safely.
ga: Tooi baaye cassava baai ni amɛbaafo yam yiteŋ, ni no baafite oŋmɔshi nibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaawo tooi yɛ ŋtayaai amli loo akɛ kpãa fĩ amɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, amɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo jwɛi lɛ ni amɛkɛyaa koni amɛha amɛ niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I use goat manure to help my plantains grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ too ŋmei atsu nii koni eye ebua mi plantains lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Goat manure is rich in nutrients that build healthy soil. You should collect the manure, let it sit and rot (compost) for a few weeks, and then spread it around the base of your plantain stands to feed the crop.
ga: Too ŋmei mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ fa babaoo. Esa akɛ obua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa. Ha ni egbo (compost) otsii fioo komɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛgbɛ ashwã plantain shishi lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant yams on the same piece of land every single year, will they still yield well?
ga: Kɛji odu sweet potato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Ani ebaawo yibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Yams take a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Planting yams repeatedly on the same plot weakens the soil and increases crop diseases, resulting in much smaller tubers over time unless you rotate crops or add nutrients.
ga: Atomɔ jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tsei ahe helai aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo yɛ be ni sa mli. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fata he.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crops after I have farmed it continuously for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without breaks depletes the organic matter and natural plant food in the ground. Giving the soil a rest (fallowing) or adding organic fertilizer helps restore its strength for future planting.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ (tillage) loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when there is heavy rain or strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit heads. If they are planted too shallowly or not supported with wooden stakes (props), strong winds and wet, soft soil can easily pull them down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ayitsei ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ aduɔ nii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii (Props) Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi oya.

english: When is the best time of year for me to plant plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: Plantains need plenty of water to establish strong roots. The best time to plant suckers is right at the beginning of the major rainy season so they receive constant water while young.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli koni amɛná nu daa kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do I need to put up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the vines off the wet ground, exposing leaves to light and protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha wain tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ la he ni etsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if stored in hot, unventilated spaces. Handle them carefully during harvest and store them off the ground in a cool, shady, airy barn.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Tsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: What should I do if my cassava leaves turn yellow and start curling up?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yellow, curled leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. To fix this, clear out infected plants and plant disease-resistant cassava stem varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Bɔni afee ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When too many small shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the main plant to produce larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves from drought. As long as the stem remains green and healthy, the plant will grow new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli ni ehe wa lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground, which gives them maximum sunlight and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking fiɔ wain tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ. ni etsi helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee baai ni fiteɔ

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing center of maize plants. Identifying them early lets you treat the crop with recommended sprays or neem extract before they destroy the yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ lɛ Ehaa okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he nii dani efiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight over water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block light from each other. Spacing them correctly helps every plant grow strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa tso shishi ni wa kɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Giving plants consistent water and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep flowers on the vine to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the underside of the leaves. Managing these pests early stops the leaves from twisting and ensures normal fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil organisms to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, that nitrogen naturally feeds the soil for crops planted afterward, like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Crop roots can only absorb fertilizer when it dissolves in water. Applying fertilizer to hot, dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money because the fertilizer will not work until moisture is present.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii ja eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly if I plant them right after heavy tractors work on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛji midu amɛ beni traktɔi wuji etsu nii yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Heavy machines can pack the soil down tightly, which starves crop roots of air and makes it hard for them to spread out and take up water and nutrients.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ni enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛye nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Will using mechanical tools to harvest my cassava hurt the tubers underground?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkpaa ŋmei lɛ baaye ŋmei lɛ awui?

english: Mechanical harvesters can cut or bruise tubers if they are set at the wrong depth, and those small cuts allow rot and insects to spoil the cassava quickly.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ afo loo amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ kɛji akɛ ato bɔ ni amɛmli kwɔ ha lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Enɛɛmɛi baaha egbo oya ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains start heating up and spoiling when I store them inside a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi edɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains give off moisture as they settle; without fresh air moving through the room, that trapped damp heat creates the perfect environment for mold and insects to multiply.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔɔ tsu lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fɔɔ bii.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough to bag and store without it rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli ni mikɛto ni efiteee?

english: Dry maize should feel glass-hard when you bite a kernel and produce a sharp clicking sound when dropped; soft or dented kernels still hold water that will breed fungus inside sealed bags.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ anu he akɛ ewa tamɔ glase kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ ajie lɛ shi lɛ, gbee ko ni naa wa ko yɛ. Nu yɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli lolo ni akɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to undergo fermentation and sun drying before they are ready for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii ni hulu lɛ agbi dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Raw cocoa beans contain natural bitterness and water; fermentation and drying heat up the beans to kill the germ, develop the rich brown chocolate flavor, and reduce moisture so they don't spoil.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ahoko lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsokolate ni mli tse, ni ji ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni okɛ hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do cassava tubers turn soft and watery inside if I leave them in wet soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy; when the ground remains waterlogged, the roots suffocate and begin to break down into a soft, watery rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbálaa kɛfeɔ nu mli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense heat, uneven watering, or poor soil nutrients, choosing to conserve their energy rather than feed growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhalaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and turn pale during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural crop defense against sun damage; by curling, the leaves expose less surface area to the heat to prevent precious water from evaporating.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Curling baai lɛ baa ni hulutsoo bɛ mli tsɔ koni nu ni jara wa lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture energy, which is then sent down into the soil to feed and expand the big yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ hia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni aha lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does using soil testing equipment help me grow better vegetables like tomatoes?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ aduawai tamɔ tomato jogbaŋŋ?

english: Monitoring equipment measures soil moisture and nutrient levels directly at the roots, showing you exactly when your crops need feeding or watering so you avoid diseases like root rot.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ susuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsɔɔ bo be pɔtɛɛ ni ehe baahia ni aha otsei lɛ niyenii loo nu. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle full sunlight. Direct sun burns their foliage and dries up soil moisture quickly before the plant can establish deep root networks.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya dani tso lɛ afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain suckers in the same field alongside new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade to shield young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seedlings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, causing the plants to grow thin, weak, and yield smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is suffering from a lack of nutrients, particularly nitrogen in the soil, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with lots of leaves but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into developing leafy top growth instead of storing starch in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops wilt during hot afternoons even though it rained heavily a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: Heat causes moisture to evaporate quickly from topsoil. If the soil lacks organic matter to hold water, the plant leaves lose water faster through transpiration than the roots can take it up.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha nu ahi shi lɛ Tsei laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why are my small cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark conditions with low airflow, especially during continuous heavy rainy periods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crop leaves more during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mitso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: During dry weather, plants become stressed from water shortage, making them weaker and less able to resist pests that feed on plant sap for hydration.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, nu ni faaa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the side branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage and dead branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach the inner tree while directing the tree's energy into producing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my main crops to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops, effectively starving the main plants if they are not cleared regularly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ajieee jwɛi kɛjɛɛɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant plantains or cassava around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high temperatures. Planting crops like plantains provides natural canopy shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the tender cocoa trees while they build deep roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves is a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a main food crops need to stay green. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new top leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves and center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The young worms hide inside the leaf funnel of the corn plant during the day and eat the tender leaves, which weakens the plant before it can grow corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and attract fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Is it good to put chemical fertilizer in the soil on the exact same day I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafata he yɛ gbi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is better to wait until a week or two after seeds sprout before applying fertilizer. Raw seeds rely on stored energy to grow their first roots, and placing strong fertilizer too close right away can burn the fresh roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi otsi kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ damɔɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ koni amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo mli ni bɛŋkɛ shikome tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi heei ashã.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that fix nitrogen from the air directly into the dirt. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds both the legume crop and nearby crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni haa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmeii kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ ŋmei fɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off before growing into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients. When conditions are too hot or dry, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why should I not cut up and plant seed yams that already have black rot spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii diji momo lɛ ni aduɔ?

english: Planting seed yams with rot spots carries fungal infections directly into your farm soil. These infected setts either fail to sprout or produce rotten tubers that can contaminate the rest of your harvest.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hei ni egbo lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ hela aba oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ shikpɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ nɛɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛfee ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni baanyɛ afite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry out during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is typically Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads quickly through rain splashes and heavy humidity. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees lets in air and sunlight to keep pods dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji hydrophilic fungus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward in the afternoon heat as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. It can also be a sign of tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaf, making it curl as it grows.
ga: Ha ni ekɛ ehe awo mli yɛ shwane mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi. Ebaanyɛ efee tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hu he okadi. Ha etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from the hot sun because direct sunlight can dry them out and kill them. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi ni egbe amɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems underground are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need sunlight to generate energy for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which prevents leaf diseases and increases tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa ni eha tuber lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plants face stress from extreme heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli baa lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same plot where I just harvested my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it depleted. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa efiteɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ he koni maná ŋmãa babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crop plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large, healthy cobs instead of many small, empty ones.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa. Yɛ cob bibioo ko najiaŋ lɛ, he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko babaoo

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yields so much more when the plants are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi babaoo beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small root systems and need all the sunlight, water, and nutrients available. Fast-growing weeds quickly steal these resources and shade out the young seedlings before they can establish.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nibii nɛɛ oya ni amɛhaa dumɔwui bibii anɔ dani amɛjeɔ shishi.

english: What causes the leaves on my vegetable crops to curl up and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɛɛɛ amɛhe?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hidden under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil extract or soapy water helps clear these pests before they stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the true rainy season starts. Planting too early can cause your seeds to sprout and then wither in the dry soil if rain does not fall again soon.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ mra.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color so they can produce large cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni anyɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big leaves above ground but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, it puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Adding potassium-rich fertilizer or wood ash to the soil encourages the plant to form thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Efiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ loo tso mli sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: How does planting groundnuts make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts and leave the roots to decay, that stored food remains in the soil to nourish your next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they do not receive enough water, lack soil nutrients, or suffer from insect damage like mirids. Regulating tree shade, keeping the soil moist, and controlling pests help flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen efite Tso lɛ shade nɔkwɛmɔ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting fruit when the heat gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Very hot weather damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit so they fall off. Providing light shade during peak sun hours helps protect the blossoms so fruits can set.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. ni kɛ aduawai ko baaa ni no hewɔ lɛ egbeeɔ shi Kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ agbee shi.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom of peppers happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering. Watering your farm consistently keeps calcium flowing into the growing fruit.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni calcium lɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying neem oil or soapy water under the leaves kills these pests and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai heei anaa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers turn yellow and dry up from the outer leaves inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ amli kɛmiiya mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing outer leaves on plantains often signal root damage caused by small worm pests in the soil or Panama disease. Planting clean, healthy suckers in fresh soil prevents these underground pests from destroying the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kponɔgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo Panama hela efite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi nɛɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops grow short and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow tall and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start growing shoots in the barn before planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months of storage when temperatures and humidity change. Keeping yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn on raised wooden racks delays shooting until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ beni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa tsakeɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tutswaa lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu.

english: Why should I buy certified improved seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ makwɛ nɔ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to give higher yields, grow faster, and withstand common local pests and dry spells. Seeds saved from past harvests gradually lose these strong traits, resulting in smaller harvests over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. edaa oya ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni hi shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ fiofio. Sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ elaaje. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa nɔ fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety recommended by officers will do well in my specific region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei ni onukpai lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: Agricultural officers test crop varieties across different ecological zones in Ghana. Varieties selected for your specific area are matched to your local soil type and rainfall patterns to ensure maximum growth and yields.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsulɔi kaa tsei srɔtoi amɛkwɛɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ. Akɛ tso srɔtoi ni ahala kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ he koni ekwɛ akɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the plant's main food for leaf growth, and when it is missing, plants cannot feed properly to stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Ni kɛ́ etee lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aye amɛhe niyenii jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that draw nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for crops that demand high nutrients like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on the same plot every year make my yields go down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply in your field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa Na shia ni baahi shi daa kɛha fɔmɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its own life when stress makes it too weak to feed growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala. Beni nɔnyɛɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai ni miida lɛ

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It is caused by calcium deficiency in the fruit, which usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly during fruit growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be easily destroyed underground by pests like nematodes or root rot, depriving the heavy plant of the anchor support it needs to stand firm.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ni tsii lɛ bɛ ŋshɔkei ni he hiaa lɛ koni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and cannot regulate heat under full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates temporary shade and holds soil moisture to protect the seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛdɔlɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rains stay on the field?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Excess water trapped around cassava roots starves them of oxygen and creates ideal conditions for soil rot fungi to multiply and spoil the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle Cassava shishifãi ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ faaa. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why is my corn taking so long to sprout after I put the seeds in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn seeds need adequate soil moisture, warm ground temperatures, and proper planting depth—usually about 2 to 5 centimeters—to germinate. If the soil is too dry or the seeds are buried too deep, sprouting will be significantly delayed or fail entirely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa dumɔwui. shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ ni sa (bei pii lɛ sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 5) koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, Ekwɛ̃mɔ baahe sɛɛ waa loo ebaafite kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, and when it is lacking, the plant pulls nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. Ni kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to intense heat and sunlight, which helps the plant conserve water during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baa shi lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough to harvest without spoiling during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni efiteee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown, the grain feels hard against a fingernail, and a tiny black spot appears at the tip of the kernel where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ wa kɛji akɛ okɛ nine ta he. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ naagbee.

english: If chemical fertilizers become too expensive or hard to get, what can I use to keep my crops growing well?
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ loo ewa akɛ aaana lɛ, Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can feed your soil using well-rotted animal manure, compost made from plant waste, or by planting leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas, which naturally draw nitrogen from the air into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Kompost ni akɛ tsei amli jwɛi feɔ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why does my field yield fewer bags of grain every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baagi fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season depletes specific soil nutrients and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your crops regularly helps restore balance and maintains soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ afee ekome ekoŋŋ ni eha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What should I do when small caterpillars start eating holes in the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɔi bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: These are likely fall armyworms. Checking fields early and often allows you to apply recommended pest control methods—such as spraying in the early morning or placing a pinch of dry sand mixed with wood ash into the growing tip—before they destroy the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji enɛɛmɛi. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni bei pii lɛ ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii, tamɔ ŋã ni egbi ni akɛ tso sũ fioo efutu mli lɛ ni oookɛshwie ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. dani ekpãtã tsei ahiɛ

english: How do I prevent insects from eating my harvested corn grains while I wait for a good market price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Grain must be thoroughly dried in the sun until moisture is low, cleaned of dirt, and then stored in airtight hermetic bags, which block oxygen and prevent pests from living inside.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. clean up dirt No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli, ni no tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ naa, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds when the rain pattern keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni nugbɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: It is best to plant after the soil has received a solid, deep rain that soaks at least 15 to 20 centimeters into the ground, ensuring enough continuous moisture for seeds to germinate and build initial roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni naa wa ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛntimitai 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ sɛɛ koni ena nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishijee shishifãi.

english: What fast-growing crops can a group of farm workers plant to harvest food and income within just a few months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oyayaayai ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi akuu ko baanyɛ adhu koni amɛkpa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ nyɔji fioo ko pɛ mli?

english: Short-duration crops like okra, leafy vegetables, pepper, and cowpeas mature quickly—often within 60 to 90 days—providing regular food and fast cash flow while waiting for main field crops to mature.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ okra, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, ŋmeii, kɛ tsina ŋmeii daa oya—bei pii lɛ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli—ni ehaa niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shika ni baa oya yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all weeds from my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Clearing all weeds before planting ensures your young seeds do not have to compete with wild plants for food, water, and space, giving them the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ dani odu lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni odumɔwui bibii lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaadara waa.

english: How does preparing my soil properly before planting help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Proper soil preparation loosens the earth so young roots can spread easily, removes unwanted weeds, and prepares the ground to hold nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ehiɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Can I just plant my seeds directly among the existing weeds and clear them later?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ateŋ ni majie amɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: No, your land should be completely free of weeds before planting. If weeds are present, they will steal essential nutrients and sunlight from your young crops from day one.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ jwɛi akafee nɔ ko kwraa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu nii. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ, amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What should my farm land look like right before I put my seeds into the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ afee tɛŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Your land should be well-prepared, soft, and completely clean of any weeds so that the newly planted seeds can grow without any competition.
ga: Esa akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ, ni efee bɔdɔɔ ni ehe tse ni jwɛi ko bɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ mli.

english: When is the right time for me to apply NPK fertilizer to my newly planted crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi tsei ni midu ehee lɛ amli?

english: You should apply NPK fertilizer early in the plant's life, usually around the first or second week after planting, when the young crop is ready for food.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ wala mli mra. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsi klɛŋklɛŋ loo otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha niyenii

english: Why do my young crops need fertilizer so early after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii oya yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Just like a young child needs good food early in life to grow into a healthy adult, young crops need early fertilizer to feed their initial growth spurt.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbekɛbii bibii kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ onukpa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii mra. Koni akɛha shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ oya yɛ shishijee lɛ niyenii

english: What specific good does NPK fertilizer do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi pɔtɛɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: NPK fertilizer acts as food for the plant, specifically working to make the roots grow deep and strong and keeping the main stem firm and sturdy.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei. Titri lɛ, ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ adara ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe awa. ni ehaa tso titri lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ewaa

english: What is NPK fertilizer and why is it recommended for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛni hewɔ ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: NPK fertilizer is a vital plant food containing essential nutrients that nourish young crops so they can build firm roots and strong stems.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I delay giving them NPK fertilizer until much later?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha amɛ?

english: If you wait too long, your young crops will lack early nourishment, resulting in weak stems and poor root systems that hinder their overall growth.
ga: Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ Odumɔwui lɛ niyenii bɛ amɛhe mra. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ. ni tsiɔ dalɛ fɛɛ naa lɛ.

english: How can I make sure my young crops grow strong stems so they do not fall over?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni midumɔwui lɛ aná tsei ni wa koni amɛkagbee shi?

english: Giving your crops NPK fertilizer within the first or second week after planting provides the exact nutrients required to make their stems firm and upright.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ loo otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves green so the plant can make large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn plants to look like they were shredded by insects overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii egbala amɛ? nyɔɔŋ kome

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central leafy whorl during the day and eat the soft leaves at night. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates heavy competition for water and food underground. Pruning to leave only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni eshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Does it matter which way I point cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matsɔɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the growing buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the stems to bend awkwardly to reach the light, which wastes energy and leads to small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ɔ shi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ koni la abote mli. ni fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ yitso bibioo baa

english: Why do I have to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei ahe tsɔi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food for the underground tuber. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases from spreading through the vine.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛha niyenii babaoo aha ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa wain tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet unexpectedly. When stressed by harsh conditions, the plant sheds its flowers to preserve its own energy instead of growing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa nyɛ amɛnɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ aduawai

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings fall over and rot right at the soil line after germinating?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a disease called damping-off, caused by fungi that thrive in overly wet, crowded soil. Nursery beds need good drainage and airflow so the seedling stems remain dry and strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ hela nɛɛ akɛ damping. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Esa akɛ gbekɛbii asaji lɛ aná nu ni hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I grew maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. Rotating these crops naturally restores soil fertility so your next grain crop grows better.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni odumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to leave small weeds around my crops even if they don't seem to cover the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashi jwɛi bibii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji amɛhaaa tsei lɛ ahe po lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal fertilizers, water, and space away from your crops long before you notice them blocking the light. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani oyɔseɔ akɛ amɛmiitsi la naa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa trees suddenly turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather and high humidity. It spreads through rain splashes, wind, and infected tools, destroying pods quickly if rotten ones are not removed promptly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kpatamɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny cocoa pods to turn yellow, shrivel up, and dry out before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbo ni egbi dani eda?

english: This condition is known as cherelle wilt. It is often the cocoa tree's natural way of reducing the number of pods it carries when it lacks enough nutrients or water, though pest attacks can also trigger it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Cherel’s Wilt. Bei pii lɛ, eji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa ŋmeii ni cacao tso lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ayibɔ shi kɛ́ ebɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi kɛlɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai hu baanyɛ aha cacao tsei lɛ atutua.

english: Why do my crops seem to suffer more disease and pod loss in wet months like May and June?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ helai babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli tamɔ May kɛ June lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and prolonged cloudy skies create high moisture and low sunlight. Moisture encourages fungal diseases to spread, while reduced sunlight limits the tree's ability to produce food, leading to pod rot and flower drops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ŋwɛi ni atatu ewo mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulu la fioo baa. Fɛ̃i woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni baa shi lɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under harsh daylight. They require temporary shade plants, such as plantains or cassava, to shield them until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni ebu he kɛyashi shishifã lɛ mli baawa

english: What is causing dark spots and tiny puncture marks on my cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Yɛ mi-kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ
