english: These marks are usually caused by mirids (capsids), which are sap-sucking insects. Their bites inject toxic saliva into the plant tissue, causing leaf drop, dieback of young shoots, and damaged pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ okadii nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei woɔ tso lɛ mli fãji amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ laajeɔ, ŋmeii gboiɔ kɛ pod lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my mature cocoa trees falling off rapidly even though the weather is not dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ amɛ moŋ? He ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɛɛ yɛ?

english: Sudden leaf loss outside of dry periods can indicate pest attacks, root damage, or viral infections like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. Damaged root systems prevent trees from absorbing water and nutrients properly.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ebatutua. shishifãi ni efite loo helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli tamɔ cocoa bud virus Shifãi ni efite lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but very few of them develop into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects like midges for pollination. If rain washes the flowers away, if chemical sprays kill beneficial pollinators, or if trees lack soil nutrients, flowers drop off without setting pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛfeɔ pollination. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baaje mli. Kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ gbe pollinators ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: How does leaving too many tall shade trees on my farm affect my cocoa yield?
ga: Te tsei babaoo ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mikookoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive shade blocks sunshine, which reduces the tree's energy to form pods. Deep shade also traps humidity under the canopy, creating a breeding ground for fungal pod diseases.
ga: Shade babaoo tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ pods lɛ baa shi. Shade ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi lɛ. ni feɔ he ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow tall around my cocoa trunks harm my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ji oshara kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa roots for soil water and fertilizer. They also create damp micro-climates near the base of the tree, hiding insect pests and encouraging fungal infections.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛhaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ hu baa yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow very bushy with plenty of leaves but gives me almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛbɛ ŋmeii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are unpruned, they spend most of their nutrients growing unnecessary branches and foliage instead of flowering and setting pods. Pruning redirects energy into pod development and allows sun to reach flower sites.
ga: Beni afooo kookoo tsei lɛ Amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ateŋ babaoo baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei niji kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔii ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, Pruning tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishijee mli ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Yellowing and drying leaves usually mean the young trees need temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees nearby to protect them from heat while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra branches on my cocoa trees if I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ cacao tso nɔ lɛ kɛji miitao ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that drain energy and block light. Opening up the tree leaves room for sunlight to reach lower branches, improves air flow to reduce diseases, and encourages the tree to use its energy for pod production.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni haa hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai aba shi ni owo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, high-humidity weather. Regularly harvesting ripe pods and clearing weeds allows air to circulate, lowering moisture and stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ, ehaa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do small insects like mirids attack my cocoa tree shoots especially during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids lɛ tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ayiteŋ, titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Mirids suck sap from fresh shoots and pods, and they thrive when cocoa trees are stressed by drought or too much direct sunlight. Proper shade management and timely spraying with approved insecticides help protect young shoots from these attacks.
ga: Mirids nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei kɛ ŋmeii amli. Ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hɔmɔ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ hao kookoo tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaabu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tutuamɔi nɛɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients before my cassava plants start showing poor yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli dani mi-cassava tsei lɛ aje shishi amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early signs of low soil nutrients include pale leaves, thin stems, and slow growth. Applying organic manure or compost before planting improves soil health and helps cassava tubers grow larger and stronger.
ga: Mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni tsuɔ, tsei bibii, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they compete for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks that fall easily and yield smaller corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Can I plant legumes like beans or groundnuts alongside my main farm crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii? Ani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ mi okwaayeli nibii titrii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting legumes alongside main crops improves soil health because legumes take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. They also act as ground cover to prevent soil erosion and weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to pick without ruining the beans?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ ni efiteee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A fully ripe cocoa pod changes color completely, usually turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety. Picking pods only when they fully change color ensures the beans inside are mature and ready for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ebafeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛsu lɛ etsake kwraa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmeii.

english: Why must I ferment my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves before sun-drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ woɔ plantain baai ashishi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats the beans, killing the seed germ, removing bitter flavors, and developing the chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for. Plantain leaves hold in the natural heat needed for proper fermentation.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ. Egbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa. Plantain baai lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop their flowers without forming fruits when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High heat causes heat stress, making plants drop flowers to conserve water and energy. Placing mulch around the roots retains soil moisture and keeps the roots cool during hot days.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Ha tsei ashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow. Applying a balanced fertilizer like NPK early helps the plants recover and grow strong.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa, tamɔ NPK wo tsei lɛ amli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are too shaded, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves instead of food. Avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant focus on growing larger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ehiɛ hulutsoo tsɔ Yɛ niyenii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the leaves of young maize. Spraying approved insecticides or bio-pesticides early in the morning or late evening when they feed will keep them under control.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai amli lɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and look burnt at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves, or by a lack of water and calcium. Controlling insects early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo nu kɛ calcium ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa Mra Be mli Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra young pods (a condition called pod wilt) when they lack water, nutrients, or suffer from insect damage, as the tree tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. (shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ pod wilting) kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu, niyenii, loo kooloi bibii efite amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why is it better for me to plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni mafo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each crop gets enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow bigger, while also making weeding and applying fertilizer much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I rot cleared weeds into the ground instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and natural soil nutrients. Allowing cleared grass to rot on the farm feeds the soil naturally, keeps the soil moist, and protects crops from heat.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he

english: Why are some of the crop seeds I planted failing to come out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the soil, if the soil dried out completely, or if soil insects and rot destroyed them before they could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ kpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛje kpo.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers under the soil are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely, showing that the plant has finished storing energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to clear my land before the farming season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okwaayeli be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Clearing your land shortly before the rains start prevents weeds from growing back quickly and ensures the soil is clean and ready to absorb water when planting begins.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ oya. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu kɛji akɛ aje dumɔ shishi.

english: What happens if I clear my land too early before I am ready to plant?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra tsɔ dani efee klalo akɛ abaadu nii?

english: Clearing too early leaves the soil bare and exposed to strong sun, which dries out essential nutrients and allows weeds to take over again before you plant.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa aba nɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ agbi ni eye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ aha ehe ekoŋŋ dani odu.

english: Why is it important to plant my crops at a specific time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mitsei lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Planting at the correct time ensures your crops receive enough rainfall throughout their growth stages so they can mature fully before the dry season.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be fɛɛ ni ekwɛɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ eda kwraa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Will my seeds grow well if I plant them when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to germinate, so planting in dry soil without near-term rain can cause the seeds to dry up, rot, or get eaten by pests before growing.
ga: Nu he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai aye amɛ dani adu.

english: How should I handle plant cuttings or stems before putting them in the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mitso lɛ niji loo eshishifãi lɛ anɔ dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ?

english: You must pluck and trim healthy plant parts cleanly and keep them moist so they stay alive and sprout quickly once planted.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ni ofolɔ amɛhe ni oha amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: Why do I need to prepare my planting materials before taking them to the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa dumɔ nii dani adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Preparing seedlings or cuttings beforehand ensures only strong, healthy plants are put in the soil, giving them a better chance of surviving.
ga: Kɛ́ asaa dumɔwui loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hegbɛ kpakpa ni akɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to dig holes in the ground instead of just dropping seeds on the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsa bu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni oooshɛrɛ dumɔwui ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Digging loosens the soil so plant roots can grow deep easily, absorb nutrients, and anchor the crop securely against wind and rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ oya. shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehiɛɔ tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ he.

english: How deep should I dig the ground when planting my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The depth depends on the crop, but digging deep enough to create soft, loose soil helps water collect around the roots so the plant grows strong.
ga: Bɔ ni mli kwɔ ha lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ mli kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ buaa ehe naa. shishifãi koni eha tsei lɛ adara waa

english: Where on my farm should I plant crops that need a lot of moisture?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ni he hiaa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should place water-sensitive crops in moist areas or near water sources where the ground naturally retains dampness to sustain the plants.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni nu nyɛɔ amɛhe lɛ awo he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ loo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ hulutsoo mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does heavy rainfall make my newly planted crops flourish?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ shwere?

english: Rainwater cools the soil, dissolves nutrients so plant roots can absorb them, and fuels rapid growth after planting.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii shwieɔ shi koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. ni ekanyaa shweremɔ oya yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a natural canopy that keeps the cocoa cool and retains soil moisture during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning light green and yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the primary nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer from the topsoil before the crop's roots have a chance to absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist—but not during intense rainfall—ensures the nutrients stay near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ—shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ—baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots through beneficial soil bacteria. When the plant finishes its lifecycle and decays, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, enriching it naturally for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli kɛtsɔɔ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tso ko gbe ewala shihilɛ naa ni egbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ fɔmɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged conditions. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience extreme heat or drought stress, which prevents pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay healthy and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are often caused by tiny sucking pests, such as aphids or mites, feeding on the juice of young leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide or neem oil solution clears these pests and allows normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch direct sunlight, which helps the leaves produce food for the underground tuber. Keeping the leaves off the ground also protects the plant from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to grow larger fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ daa ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and produce small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for available sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures that your main crops receive all the food and water they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight during their first few years. Planting them alongside fast-growing crops like plantains creates living shade that protects the young cocoa from harsh heat while retaining soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are people telling me to cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool during hot days, and prevents weeds from taking over your plot.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests build up. Alternating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts valuable nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of big leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes plants to put all their energy into leafy growth above ground instead of root growth below. Using balanced nutrients encourages the plant to store food in big, healthy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ wami ji. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato bulbs agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my corn seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures thick stalks and larger cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I wait for a few steady rains before sowing my maize seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu ŋmãa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Sowing after just one early rain is risky because a sudden dry spell can kill germinating seeds before roots grow deep. Waiting for reliable, continuous rain ensures seeds have steady moisture to survive.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ abote mli shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni haa amɛhiɔ shi daa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them for too long because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli bu ni etse lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended biological controls or safe treatments before they burrow deep into the crop will save your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni adu lɛ anɔ mra. Ni kɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii dani okɛ ohe awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Flower dropping happens when pepper plants experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering in the cool morning and proper feeding help flowers stay on the stem and turn into fruit.
ga: Blossom ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli kɛ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build healthy green leaves, and when the soil runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its oldest lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant maize on the same farm every season, why does my yield keep dropping?
ga: Kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year without giving the earth time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with natural bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the root zone. When the cowpea plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the overhead shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight or high heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to trap moisture and protect them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli.

english: Why do my yam vines grow much bigger tubers when I give them long sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs ni dara kwraa lɛ? Be ni mikɛ nine kakadaŋŋ aha bo Slither kɛyaa ŋwɛi?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for expanding the tuber underground. Putting up stakes lifts the vines off the floor, spreading out the leaves to catch maximum sunlight without shading each other out.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Tso ni akɛma shi lɛ baaye abua ni awo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant cassava very close together, will I harvest more cassava tubers from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ Ani makpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close forces cassava plants to fight each other for water, nutrients, and sunlight. This competition results in tall, thin stems with very small, thin roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe abɔi nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii waa yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It keeps the blazing sun off the bare soil, preventing water from evaporating quickly, keeping the roots cool, and stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Early morning is best because the soil can absorb the water before the heat causes it to evaporate, giving plants the drink they need to face the hot afternoon sun without getting stressed.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkpe shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni amɛhaomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites living on the underside of the leaf, or by a virus carried by those insects that damages the leaf cells as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ anɔ beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress during hot afternoons, lack of moisture in the soil, or a lack of insects like bees to shake and pollinate the flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hosoɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their tender leaves from intense sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Leaving some large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the seedlings cool and helps them survive their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize plants turning light yellow from the middle of the leaf down to the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shishi kɛmiiya shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the dark green color and boost crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundpeas help fix my farm soil for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the ground. When you harvest them, they leave natural fertilizer behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nodes krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil retains too much water, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for foliage growth. Staking also prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, leading to larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni baa lɛ adara. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning back excess suckers leaves only the main stem and one or two replacements, ensuring larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri lɛ pɛ kɛ nɔ kome loo enyɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ koni aná yibii babaoo.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green droppings left inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni etse yɛ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa? ni eshwɛ yɛ kɔni lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the leaf funnel of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying organic neem spray or recommended insecticides will protect your crop from damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem spray loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ baabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays prevents leaf distortion and improves fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu naa ni eye ebua ni aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too high, when water supply is irregular, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Regular watering and applying balanced compost helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts in the spaces between my cassava rows instead of leaving the land bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ he ni kã ŋmeii akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts covers the bare soil quickly, which suppresses weed growth, keeps the soil moist, prevents erosion, and feeds the soil with nitrogen, allowing both crops to perform well together.
ga: Peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya. ni tsiɔ jwɛi adalɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni ehaa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: This yellowing is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure near the root zone will help the plant recover and produce healthy ears.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots very thin and woody instead of big and full of starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee mlɛo ni amɛfee tamɔ tso lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if they are planted in hard, unploughed soil or if weeds steal nutrients during the first three months of growth. Loosening the soil before planting and keeping the farm clear of weeds early on allows the roots to expand fully.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ nii nɔ. Aloo kɛji jwɛi lɛ ju niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ dani aduɔ nii ni akwɛɔ koni jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying your crop with neem oil solution or an appropriate mild insecticide controls these pests and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ shwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark brown or black and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions during the rainy season. Pruning excess shade tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly will prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn dark brown long before the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee lɛ?

english: This early drying is caused by Yam Anthracnose, a fungal disease that attacks leaves and stems in high humidity. Staking your yam vines off the wet soil and planting disease-resistant yam varieties helps keep the leaves healthy until harvest.
ga: Anthracnose ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni egbiɔ oya nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ, ni adu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit bunch starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akui lɛ miihe afee shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because tiny worms called nematodes or stem-boring weevils have damaged the root system under the ground. Planting pest-free suckers and propping up fruiting plants with sturdy wooden stakes prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Seedlings fell because of tiny worms. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii, ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ, ni adu tsei ni woɔ yibii ni akɛ tsei ni wa wo mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or a shortage of tiny midges that pollinate the blooms. Maintaining light shade and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during peak flowering preserves pollinating insects.
ga: Cocoa trees bloom when exposed to heat stress. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo bibii ni yɔɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ aha sui lɛ afee mlɛo ni ajie tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of green leaves but producing almost no flowers or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves and few pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when tiny pests called flower thrips destroy the young buds. Avoiding nitrogen fertilizers on legumes and checking for flower pests helps crop setting.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ flower thrips lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotten while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato shishi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium woɔ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and leafy instead of forming a hard, tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads stay loose when the weather is too hot, when plants are crowded too close together, or when they don't get enough water during head formation. Spacing seedlings properly and watering regularly during dry spells ensures firm heads.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo be mli ni amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni bulb lɛ feɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛyitsei lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow healthy green leaves. This often happens in poor soil or after heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or sudden dry weather. When the plant feels it does not have enough water to support growth, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛ yaje dɔlɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛdalɛ bɛ Abaafolɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni akɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even after sitting in the ground for a full year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo yɛ be mli ni mita shikpɔŋ afi muu fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand. If the ground is too hard or compacted, the roots cannot push through the soil to swell into large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛmli alɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfu ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly before I can sell them in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes give off heat and moisture after harvest. When they are packed tightly in deep wooden crates under the hot sun, the trapped heat speeds up rotting and softens the skin.
ga: Tomato haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa hewolo lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating my stored maize after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni ato yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weevils attack maize when the grain still has moisture inside. Drying the maize thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are completely hard before storing them in airtight sacks stops the insects from breeding.
ga: Weevils tutuaa ŋmãa beni ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ afɔmɔ kpaa.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have shallow roots and large leaves that lose water very quickly in hot weather. Covering the soil around their base with dry grass holds moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji, ni nu lɛ laajeɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I build high earth mounds to plant my yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni mikɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: High mounds loosen the soil deep down, giving yam tubers space to grow long and thick while allowing heavy rainwater to drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Pii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ mli koni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming shaded branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ duŋ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are armyworms eating the leaves inside the center funnel of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay their eggs inside the central leaf funnel because the young leaves there are soft and hidden from predators. The caterpillars eat from the inside out where the tissue is easiest to chew.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ejaakɛ baa bibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Kplukai yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ, ni no ji fã ni anyɛɔ ashɛreɔ oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough power to grow good crops without chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Good, rich soil is dark in color, feels moist, and crumbles easily in your hand. If wild, dark-green weeds grow naturally and fast on that land, it shows the soil has strong natural nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hi ni ewoɔ nii, ni eyɛ su ni tsuɔ. Henumɔ ni mli edɔ ni ekumɔ oya kɛji akɛ eyɛ enine mli Kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nakai he lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni mli wa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or keeping large trees keeps the soil moist and protects the young leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ latsaa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut and plant to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: You should use the mature middle portion of healthy cassava stems cut into pieces about 20 to 25 centimeters long. Avoid using the soft top parts or the very bottom stem, as mature middle cuttings sprout faster and produce stronger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ atsu nii, ni ofo mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 25. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi loo shishigbɛ tso lɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni eda lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How do I choose the best plantain sucker from my field to plant a new crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ koni mikɛdu tsei heei?

english: Look for maiden suckers or sword suckers that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a strong, large bulb base. Avoid using suckers with wide, broad leaves because they grow slower and produce smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Taomɔ oblayei ashishifãi loo klante ashishifãi ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo agbo ni mli wa ni tamɔ bulbous. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ he ejaakɛ amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ plantains bibii.

english: What causes small green worms to eat holes in my maize leaves and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji lɛ Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa amɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks young maize. You can control them early by applying recommended insecticides, putting neem powder or clean sand into the leaf funnel, and clearing surrounding weeds where they hide.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Okɛ neem powda loo ŋã ni mli tse awo tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli. ni ojie jwɛi ni bɔle He ni amɛtee lɛ

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by extreme heat and drought. Controlling these small insects early with recommended sprays or neem liquid prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the middle of lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, an important plant food. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage helps the leaves turn green and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not during heavy rainfall. Covering the fertilizer with a light layer of soil right after putting it near the base of the plant ensures the moisture helps dissolve it into the roots rather than washing it off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeefo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop mostly because of very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of proper nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant balanced fertilizer keeps flowers attached to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ titri. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up into direct sunlight. When leaves get enough light, they produce more energy for the plant, which helps the yam tubers under the ground grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my food crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients very quickly from the soil. Removing weeds during the first four to six weeks after planting prevents them from crowding out your crops and taking their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4-6 ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni amɛkaha lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and strength to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within a few days even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root rot living in the dirt that blocks water from moving up the stem. Rotating your crops by planting corn or cassava on that bed next season starves these soil germs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria loo fungal root rot ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ saatso nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli koni hɔmɔ aye sũ mli helai.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are growing big tubers underground instead of just growing tall stems and leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tsei kɛ baai kakadaji kɛkɛ?

english: When cassava gets full sunlight and balanced nutrients without excessive nitrogen, it diverts its energy downward into the roots. Strong, thick lower stems and healthy green leaves usually show that the plant is feeding tubers underneath.
ga: Beni ŋmãa nine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ ni nitrogen babaoo bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ tsei ni mli wa ni mli tse kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers on the trunk, but most of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? lots on the trunk Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers if they suffer from drought, extreme heat, pest attack, or a lack of shade trees. Maintaining shade trees on your farm and keeping moisture in the soil helps more flowers successfully turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, loo tso lɛ bɛ hulutsoo. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsɔɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Young plantain suckers compete with the parent plant for nutrients and water in the soil. Removing excess suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main plantain stem to get maximum strength to produce a heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs missing grains or only half-filled with seeds when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo loo amɛji fã pɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Incomplete cobs happen when pollen from the top tassels fails to reach the silks during dry winds or heat stress. Planting your maize in close blocks rather than single long rows helps the wind carry pollen evenly across all silks.
ga: Cobs ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ siliki lɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo latsaa be mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ blɔkii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kakadaŋŋ mli Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aŋɔ ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ siliki lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl upward and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves. Spraying with organic neem leaf extract or recommended treatments clears the pests so new leaves grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds planted in dry soil rot after a small rainfall instead of sprouting into healthy seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ dumɔwui ni he wa

english: A light shower gives seeds just enough moisture to start sprouting, but if the soil dries up immediately, the young shoot inside dies and decomposes. Planting when rainy season rains are regular ensures seeds get continuous wet soil to emerge fully.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi trukaa lɛ Tsobii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why is my young cashew tree taking so many years to bear fruit compared to my neighbor's trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cashew trees grown directly from local seeds take three to four years to flower, whereas grafted cashew seedlings produce fruit much faster. Grafted seedlings come from branches of mature, high-yielding trees that are already ready to produce.
ga: Cashew tsei ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cashew nut dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ baawo yibii oya kwraa. Dumɔwui ni akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ aniji ebɔ he lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii.

english: Why do my young vegetable leaves burn and turn brown during the bright afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender young leaves lose moisture through their pores faster than their tiny roots can drink water from the soil under hot sun. Providing temporary shade using palm fronds and watering early in the morning protects them from heat shock.
ga: Baai bibii bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni anu nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ baaye abua ni akafee hulutsoo.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin without producing big corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When maize plants are seeded too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. This overcrowding causes them to spend all their energy growing tall to reach the light instead of spending energy on big corncobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi ni eyi fe nine nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji anɔ lɛ

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce fewer pods when the leaf canopy becomes very thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ amli etse ni eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: A canopy that is too thick blocks sunlight and traps moisture, creating a damp environment where diseases thrive. Pruning excess branches allows air to flow and sunlight to reach the inner stems, encouraging healthy flower and pod development.
ga: Kpo ni mli tse tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai srɔtoi baa mli lɛ baa. baanyɛ adara Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ pod lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why are my crops failing to grow even after I applied fertilizer to a field full of tall weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ ni jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds absorb water and plant food faster than your crops can. If weeds are left to grow out of control first, the fertilizer you add will feed the weeds instead of your crops, leaving the crops choked and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ niyenii oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Kɛji oha jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni enyɛŋ eye nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ

english: Why does spraying chemical medicine fail to save my farm when pests have already eaten most of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ? Beni ŋmeii lɛ eye baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo?

english: Leaves act as food factories for the plant using sunlight. Even if the medicine kills the pests late in the season, a plant with fully destroyed leaves can no longer feed itself or recover to produce food.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei kɛha tsei ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofa lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ moŋ, shi tsei ni amɛbaai lɛ efite kwraa lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛhe dɔŋŋ loo amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off after heavy rains cover the farm with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni ekã shi eha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water sits on the land with nowhere to drain, the roots drown and die, preventing the plant from pulling food up to its leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛgboi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbala niyenii kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does the soil around my vegetable plants dry up and harden so quickly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ ni ewaa oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare, unshaded soil loses water quickly through evaporation. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw protects the earth from direct sun heat and keeps moisture trapped near the roots longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ha onibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year yield smaller harvests each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: The same crop pulls the exact same nutrients out of the soil every year without giving the earth time to rest. Repeated planting also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ekoŋŋ lɛ hu haa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This happens when tiny organisms in the soil enter the plant's stem and block its internal water channels. Even if water is in the soil, the plant cannot pump it up to the leaves, causing it to wilt.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bote tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsi nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛre kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli. baanyɛ aha egbo

english: Why do my cassava plants stop producing large tubers as the stems get older and overgrown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji feemɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni amɛdara fe nine lɛ?

english: As a plant gets older and oversized, it uses most of its energy simply maintaining its heavy stems and foliage rather than storing extra energy in root tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛdara lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai ni tsii lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami kpa ko ngɛ tso ɔ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do pepper seeds taken straight from a freshly harvested fruit fail to sprout when I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ aduawai ni akpa ehee lɛ amli lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh seeds contain natural substances that keep them in a sleeping state while inside the wet fruit. Drying the seeds properly signals to them that it is time to wake up and germinate when planted.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ aduawai ni efɔ mli lɛ yɛ dumɔwui heei amli. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu amɛ.

english: My neighbor used a chemical to cure his farm's leaf problem, so why did the same spray destroy my tomato crops when I tried it?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ tsofai tsuɔ baa he naagba ko ni yɔɔ eŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nii. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ tsofa nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbe mi-tomato tsei lɛ beni mika lɛ mikwɛ lɛ?
