english: Different crop problems are caused by different issues like fungi, bacteria, or insects. Using a medicine meant for insects on a fungal disease will not work, and applying the wrong chemical or wrong dose can burn and kill sensitive plants like tomatoes.
ga: Naagbai srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, loo kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi baa. Tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsofa ni ejaaa loo falɛ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ tomato ni egbe amɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to buy liquid farm chemicals sold in plain bottles without any label or instructions?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe tsofai ni ji nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ tɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko mli ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ amli?

english: No, buying unlabelled chemicals is very dangerous. Without a proper label, you cannot know what chemical is inside, how much water to mix with it, or whether it will poison your crops, soil, or family.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni aheɔ ni aŋmalaaa nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ yɛ oshara waa. Kɛji akɛ wolo ko ni ja bɛ nɔ lɛ Onyɛŋ ole tsofai ni yɔɔ mli. Nu enyiɛ esa akɛ afutu? Aloo ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛha onibii, shikpɔŋ loo oweku lɛ?

english: How can I be sure I am buying the right chemical for my sick maize field at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miheɔ tsofai ni sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Always look for products with clear, official labels showing approved target crops, dosage instructions, and expiration dates. It is best to describe your crop's exact symptoms to an agricultural extension officer before buying any input.
ga: Taomɔ nibii ni aŋmala nɔ nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni tsɔɔ tsei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ tsofa lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ he kɛ gbi ni ebaagbe naa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔɔ bɔ ni onibii lɛ yɔɔ ha diɛŋtsɛ mli oha okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ dani ohé saji komɛi.

english: Why do my crops keep dying even after I spray them repeatedly with the chemical I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ tsofai ni mihe lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shii abɔ po lɛ yaa nɔ egboɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying heavily with the wrong chemical will not cure the plant and can actually toxicity-burn the crop. Also, insects and diseases can become resistant if you keep using the same chemical over and over without identifying the exact cause.
ga: Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ hereŋ tso lɛ yiwala, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa fɔŋ awo tso lɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ helai Resistance hu baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ ni kɛbaa.

english: Who can I turn to on my community to properly inspect my sick crops before I spend money on spray?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ? Dani mafite mishika yɛ spray nɔ?

english: You should contact your local ministry extension officer or qualified agricultural agent. They are trained to inspect the fields, diagnose whether the cause is a bug, fungus, or poor soil, and recommend the correct treatment.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ omaŋ mission extension officer loo okwaayeli najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko ni he esa abɔ. Atsɔɔ amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kwɛmɔ kɛji nɔ ni kɛbaa ji kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii. ni amɛtsɔɔ gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa lɛ

english: How can I tell if the spots on my pepper leaves are caused by insects or by a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ ba?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible bite marks, holes, or actual pests hiding under leaves, whereas plant diseases often create colored spots, patches, or rotting without obvious physical insects present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa ŋmeii ni anaa, bu, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ehiɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why did my young nursery plants wither and die immediately after I applied liquid medicine near their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni ji nu ewo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young plant roots are soft and easily scorched by strong chemicals. Applying undiluted or unrecommended chemical drenches can destroy the delicate root system, causing the plant to dry up and die.
ga: Tsoi bibii ashishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni tsofai ni mli wa shãa amɛ oya. Tsofai ni akɛwooo mli loo ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbi ni egbo.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and dropping off during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture during the rainy season creates ideal conditions for root rot and fungal diseases to spread quickly in wet soil, preventing the cassava plant from taking up nutrients and causing leaf yellowing.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: My crops have very green leaves, but why are they failing to produce fruits or pods?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji waa. Shi mɛni hewɔ enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to grow thick, green leaves at the expense of flowering. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to produce healthy flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná baai ni mli tse ni efite fɔfɔii. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni afee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why does a disease seem to spread so fast from one side of my vegetable garden to the other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ fã kome kɛyaa fã kroko lɛ?

english: Fungal spores and bacteria travel easily on farm tools, shoes, wind, and splashing rain. Working in sick parts of the farm and then moving to healthy plants without cleaning your tools spreads the sickness across the field.
ga: Fungal kɛ bacteria spores lɛ fãa gbɛ mlɛo yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii, tokotai, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ko ni hela mɔ lɛ he nii, ni no sɛɛ lɛ aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ ni atsumɔɛɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hela agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops close to a dam or water body?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ faa loo nu jɛɛhe masɛi?

english: Planting close to a dam ensures your crops have a continuous supply of water, especially during dry spells, which helps seeds germinate quickly and keeps plants healthy throughout the growing season.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ faa ko masɛi lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nu ni yaa nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Which side of a water dam should I choose to set up my farm plot?
ga: Mɛɛ faa lɛ fã esa akɛ mahala koni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ama shi?

english: Setting up your farm on the lower or southern side of a dam allows gravity to carry water naturally toward your farm through small channels, making irrigation easier without needing expensive water pumps.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ wo faa shishi loo yɛ faa ko kooyigbɛ lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ bibioo ko nɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni nu pɔmpii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: How does the position of my land affect how well my crops grow?
ga: Te he ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The position of your land determines how much sunlight your crops receive, how water flows through the soil, and whether strong winds or runoff from neighboring areas will damage your young crops.
ga: He ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni hulu la ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná lɛ fa ha. Te nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baafite onibii bibii lɛ?

english: What is a sluice channel, and how will it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nu homɔ gbɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: A sluice channel is a dug canal or pipe with a gate that leads water directly from a source like a dam into your farm, giving you full control over when and how much water reaches your crops.
ga: Sluice channel ji faa loo dugout ni shinaa ko yɔɔ ni kɛ nu baa tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ jɛɛhe ko tamɔ dam kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ be kɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: How can I guide water from a river or dam into my crop field without flooding the land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa loo faa mli aba miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu aaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can dig narrow channels along your farm and use small gates or earth barriers to open the water flow when the soil is dry and block it when the field has received enough water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko. Yaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ shinaa bibioo lɛ loo sũ ni tsiɔ nii anaa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbele nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli egbi. ni atsĩ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops suffer when I don't clear weeds and trash out of my water channels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwieee shi ni mikɛ jwɛi akabote nu gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Blocked channels stop water from reaching all parts of your farm evenly, leaving some crops thirsty while overflowing and causing waterlogging in other spots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni atsĩ naa lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa kumai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ be mli ni amɛhoɔ babaoo ni ehaa nu shwieɔ ekrokomɛi anɔ.

english: How do I know if my land slopes enough for water to flow to my plants naturally?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni baaha nu ajɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: If water moves slowly in a steady direction when poured on the ground without collecting into deep stagnant pools, your land has a good gentle slope for channel irrigation.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ blɛoo yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ beni eshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuaaa ehe naa kɛyaaa nubui ni mli kwɔ amli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ fioo ko ni abaanyɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ nubu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when too much water sits on the soil for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off the air they need to breathe, preventing them from taking up plant food from the soil and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I check if my crops are getting the right amount of water from the irrigation channel?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni sa kɛmiijɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Push your finger into the soil near the plant roots; if it feels damp like a wrung-out sponge, the water level is right, but if water squishes out or the ground is hard, you need to adjust your water flow.
ga: Nyɛɛ onine nɔ yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji enuɔ he akɛ edɔ tamɔ sponji ni edɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ja. Shi kɛji akɛ nu lɛ shwie shi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa Esa akɛ otsake bɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ ehaa lɛ.

english: Why should I plan where my water source is before clearing my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato he ni mi nu jɛɛhe lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ dani majie shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔ nii?

english: Planning your water source first saves you from planting crops in dry areas where seedlings will wither, and ensures you lay out your farm rows in line with the water flow.
ga: Kɛ́ oto ohe nu lɛ he gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaahere bo kɛjɛ tsei ni okɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni dumɔwui lɛ baagbo lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ ato gbɛjianɔ bɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why should I leave measured gaps between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When cassava plants are grown too close together, their roots compete under the ground for water and food. Leaving proper space gives each plant room to expand and produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. He ni sa haa tso tsu fɛɛ tsu mli lɛɛɔ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do you advise us to plant maize in straight rows with fixed gaps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ wɔdu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines with equal gaps ensures every maize plant gets the same amount of sunlight, air, and nutrients, while also making it much easier for you to weed and apply fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants bend toward the direction where the sun rises?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ ebɔle he ni hulu lɛ teɔ shi yɛ lɛ?

english: Crops naturally lean toward light because sunlight is what they use to make their food. This behavior is normal and helps the leaves capture maximum sunlight for growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kwɛɔ adebɔɔ mli la nɔ ejaakɛ hulu la ji nɔ ni amɛkɛhooɔ amɛ niyenii. Nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to yield well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni akwɔɔ koni ewo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally seek height to reach maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes keeps them away from damp soil diseases and helps the plant send more energy down into building bigger tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ he ko ni kwɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee bulbs wuji

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, too little water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and nourished helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu fioo tsɔ he. loo niyenii ni esaaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ená niyenii kpakpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or water. When the ground is too dry, roots cannot draw nutrients upward, causing leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo nu. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbala niyenii mli nibii kɛya ŋwɛi. ni haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and shrink when small insects appear under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni kooloi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Small insects like whiteflies suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses like cassava mosaic disease. This causes the leaves to curl, distort, and lose their ability to produce food for the root.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai tamɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I tell if my cowpea plants are getting too much rain in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ená nugbɔ babaoo yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli?

english: When cowpea plants get waterlogged, their roots cannot breathe. You will notice the leaves turning pale yellow, the plant wilting despite wet soil, and the roots turning soft and rotting.
ga: Beni nu eyi cowpea tsei lɛ amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Obaayɔse akɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ egbo kɛ sũ ni efɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ moŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young cocoa trees with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil around young cocoa seedlings keeps the ground cool and traps moisture, preventing the hot sun from drying out the delicate young roots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛwoɔ Young cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekagbi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why does my garden egg crop stop bearing fresh fruit if I leave all the lower leaves on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei kɛji mishi shishigbɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Lower leaves close to the soil consume plant energy and can easily catch soil-borne diseases. Pruning lower branches allows the crop to redirect its food energy into producing fresh flowers and larger fruits.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsakeɔ niyenii hewalɛ ewoɔ fɔfɔi heei kɛ aduawai wuji amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees need special fertilizer instead of just relying on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaafɔ̃ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require large amounts of nutrients, especially potassium and nitrogen, to produce thick stems and large bunches. Special plantain fertilizer replaces nutrients lost in the soil and helps the plant grow faster and yield bigger fruit.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. titri lɛ potassium kɛ nitrogen Koni ekɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ jwɛi wuji. Plantain ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko baaye niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my plantain farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is during the rainy season when the soil is moist, starting about one to two months after planting. Moist soil allows plantain roots to easily absorb the nutrients without burning the plant.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛjɛ aaafee nyɔji 1-2 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa plantain shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Which kind of plantain sucker should I plant to get the best harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain esa akɛ madu koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: You should select 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong, large base. They grow faster, resist strong winds better, and produce larger bunches than 'water suckers' with broad leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘Sword Bud’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo agbo ni mli wa. Amɛ daa oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni ekɛ kui wuji baa fe ‘tso ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant isn't getting enough water. Removing dead leaves helps the plant direct its energy toward growing new leaves and fruit.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ naaa nu bɔ ni sa. Baai ni egboi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai kɛ aduawai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem is good enough to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ko hi jogbaŋŋ ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good cassava stems should be cut from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Look for thick stems with raised, undamaged eye buds and no signs of disease or insect damage.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmei kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Taomɔ tsei ni mli tse ni amɛwo amɛhe nɔ, ni amɛfiteee. ni amɛbɛ hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe okadi ko kwraa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on raised mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmei?

english: Planting on mounds or ridges loosens the soil, giving cassava roots space to expand into big tubers. It also prevents waterlogging, which can cause the roots to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Ehaa nu hu shwieɔ shi, ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How can I get my cassava crops to give me more tubers per plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná tubers babaoo yɛ tso kome mli kɛha mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: To get a higher yield, plant healthy stem cuttings at a slight angle, keep the farm weed-free during the first three months, and ensure the soil is loose and fertile so tubers can expand.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ Dumɔ tsei niji ni wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo. Ha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready 8 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the plant cracking as the roots grow larger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli gbalaa beni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my food crops seem to grow poorly even when I clear the land and plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ he ni miduɔ yɛ be naa lɛ moŋ?

english: Soils lose their fertility over continuous farming seasons as crops draw out natural nutrients. Adding organic manure or crop fertilizers recharges the soil so your crops have the energy to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ shweremɔ bei ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ amli be mli ni tsei lɛ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Underground rot usually happens when heavy rains leave water trapped in the soil around the roots. Improving soil drainage by planting on higher ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping tubers healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni abaaha eya hiɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni eha yitso lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Why are my vegetables wilting and dying faster these days even when I water them like I used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Weather patterns are changing, bringing higher heat and drier conditions that evaporate soil water rapidly. Adapting your farming methods, such as using shade nets or mulching, helps keep the soil cool and retains the moisture your plants need to survive.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbiɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ oya. Gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ shade netting loo mulching ni okɛbaatsu nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know when it is time to change my traditional farming methods for new technology?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ matsake mi blema okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ? Eji tɛknɔlɔji hee.

english: When unpredictable rains, unexpected dry spells, or rising heat start reducing your harvest despite your hard work, it means the natural environment has shifted, and adopting modern farming methods will help protect your crops.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ ji hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ Loo latsaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ otsu nii waa moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ etsake. Ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi ni oootsɔ nɔ otsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni obu onibii ahe.

english: How can government agricultural initiatives help me get better harvest from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Agricultural initiatives bring modern training, improved seed varieties, and modern structures like greenhouses directly to local communities, giving you the tools and knowledge to farm successfully despite changing weather.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsumɔ lɛ kɛ tsɔsemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ baa Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛjianɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, baa akutso lɛ mli bii lɛ aŋɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni akɛ nibii kɛ nilee ni baaha otsu okwaayeli he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha bo.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it make crops grow better than in an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: A greenhouse is a framed structure covered with protective material that creates an ideal climate inside. It shields crops from harsh sun, heavy rainfall, and pests, allowing plants like tomatoes and peppers to grow faster and produce more fruit.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsɔne ko ni akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa emli. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ awui ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei tamɔ tomato kɛ pepper ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do tomato leaves turn yellow and rot during the heavy rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct heavy rain washes away nutrients from the soil and leaves moisture on leaves that causes fungal diseases. Growing tomatoes under a protective structure keeps rainfall off the leaves while keeping the roots properly hydrated.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa baa lɛ anɔ. Tomato ni akwɛɔ yɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ akanɛɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow fresh vegetables during the dry season when there is no rainfall?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ odu aduawai heei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, by using protected greenhouse structures combined with drip irrigation, you can control the temperature and water supply, allowing you to harvest high-value crops all year round regardless of the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋwɛitsu ni abuɔ he ni akɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, ekɔɔɔ he eko be ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the fertilizer I apply to my crop beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In open fields, intense rainfall creates surface runoff that carries away topsoil and loose fertilizer before plant roots can absorb it. Covered farming or applying fertilizer directly to the root zone through controlled drip lines prevents this waste.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ yaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Blanket okwaayeli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ drip line ni akudɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Why is drip irrigation better for my crops than pouring water with a bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hi fe ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Pouring water with a bucket splashes muddy water onto leaves, which can spread diseases, and wastes water through evaporation. Drip irrigation delivers slow, steady drops directly to the roots where the plant needs it most.
ga: Nu ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ ashwie baai lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo, ni eshwieɔ shi po kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ he ni tsei lɛ he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my pepper plants more when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Heat accelerates the breeding cycle of insects, and as open vegetation dries up, pests migrate to your green farm crops for food. Enclosing crops with insect-proof mesh net stops pests from entering without needing heavy chemicals.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa kooloi kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii oya. ni kɛ́ tso lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Pests lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli koni amɛyaye nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii awo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli ni tsofai ni tsii he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my plants drop their flowers before producing fruit when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ yibii be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and heat place high stress on plants, forcing them to drop flowers to conserve energy and water. Shading the plants lowers the temperature, allowing flowers to stay healthy and turn into full-sized fruits.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ashi amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or leaving tall shade trees shields young cocoa, keeps the soil moist, and helps the plants survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo shade tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem cutting when I push it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ otsɔɔ nɔ okɛfoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first before turning up, which wastes energy, delays growth, and reduces root yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi dani amɛdara. Enɛ baafite hewalɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ayibii baa shi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani abele lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains often wash away soil nutrients, so applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage keeps the foliage green and improves grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust looking dirt inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baa kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's growing point. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnel helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and humid weather. Clearing weeds around the tree base, pruning extra branches to improve air movement, and spraying copper-based fungicides help protect your cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ofolɔ mli babaoo koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɔɔble yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Mounds loosen the soil so root tubers can expand easily without pushback from hard dirt. Loose raised soil also improves water drainage, stopping the tubers from sitting in water and rotting.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ kɛje kpo. Looser soil also improves drainage. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ abote nu mli ni amɛgboi.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne pests and diseases build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know it is safe to plant my maize seeds after the first rainfall of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until there have been two or three steady rainfalls and the soil stays moist a few inches deep. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. And the soil was still moist a few inches down. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get moldy or full of small insects when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Be ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli?

english: Grains develop mold and attract weevils if they are not dried sufficiently before storage. Drying corn thoroughly in the sun until it is hard and using airtight storage bags protects your harvest from moisture and insect damage.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked. Keeping soil moisture consistent with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant is smart—it pulls nitrogen from its old lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young growing top leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. smart corn plant Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛbu ŋmeii bibii ni miida lolo lɛ ahe.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly feeds off the exact same nutrients year after year, exhausting the soil. It also lets pests and soil diseases that feed on maize build up in that field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu shii abɔ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl and droop in the hot afternoon even when it rained recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ enɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: When the sun is extremely strong, plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water into the air. It is a natural way for the plant to rest and survive the intense afternoon heat.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ akaje amɛdɛŋ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛjoɔ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ naa foi.

english: Why is my pepper plant producing small flowers when it is still very short and young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ kuku lolo ni eji gbekɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences stress from poor soil or lack of water, it fears it might die soon. It quickly produces flowers early to try to make seeds for the next generation before its time runs out.
ga: Kɛ tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ mishe gbeyei akɛ ekolɛ tso lɛ baagbo etsɛŋ. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya mra. Koni abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni adu dumɔwui lɛ aha yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani be lɛ ashɛ.

english: Why are some of my yam vines growing very strong while others right next to them remain weak and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida waa waa lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛji bibii.

english: Soil nutrients and moisture are not spread evenly underground, or tiny worms called nematodes may be attacking the roots of the weaker plants, preventing them from taking up food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ejaraaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi pɛpɛɛpɛ. aloo ŋmeii bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ashishifãi. ni otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When their roots decompose, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil to feed your maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I harvest more food from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani minɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aya hiɛ?

english: When crops are crowded too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small, weak plants and a lower overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air gets too hot, when water is lacking, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers. The plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ nu faaa, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and drop after heavy rains flood the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water fills the tiny air pockets in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without oxygen in the root zone, the plant cannot breathe or absorb food, causing leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and green compared to my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ akɛto tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi enɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive local conditions. They act quickly to grab water and soil food before your crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Amɛtsuɔ nii oya koni amɛmɔmɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Can I just pick any soil from my farm to fill my seedling bags?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahala shikpɔŋ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛwo mi dumɔwui kotokui lɛ amli?

english: No, random farm soil can be too compact, sandy, or contaminated with diseases. Using loose topsoil mixed with compost provides the right balance of nutrients and airflow that young roots need to grow easily.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni afee lɛ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ, nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋã, loo helai ewo mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni he hiaa shishifãi bibii lɛ koni amɛdara mlɛo lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to sift soil through a mesh before putting it into nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋ dani mikɛwo grow bag lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sifting removes big stones, sticks, and hard lumps. Soft, fine soil allows tiny seedling roots to spread freely without hitting hard barriers that slow down their growth.
ga: Filtering jieɔ tɛi wuji, tsei niji, kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ehe ni etswaaa gbɛtsii nii ni wa ni haa edalɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Can I mix animal manure directly into the soil I use for my nursery bags?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu sũ ni akɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You can, but the manure must be well-dried and fully rotted first. Fresh manure generates heat as it breaks down, which will burn and kill delicate seedling roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi esa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni egbo klɛŋklɛŋ. Manɔ hee feɔ dɔlɛ beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baashã ni efite dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Can I use empty sachet water plastic bags to grow my crop seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ plastic nu sachet kotokui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛdu mi tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, empty sachet water bags make cheap and effective nursery containers, but you must poke small holes near the bottom so excess water can escape.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu kotokui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ gbekɛbii amli ni jara waaa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni ogbu bu bibioo ko. Ebɛŋkɛ tɔ lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to cut holes at the bottom of my nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo bu yɛ grow bag lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Without drainage holes, excess water gets trapped inside the bag. Trapped water starves the roots of air and leads to root rot, which kills the young plant.
ga: Kɛji nu homɔ bu ko bɛ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baabote kotoku lɛ mli. Nu ni emɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves of my nursed seedlings turning yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni mikwɛ nɔ lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering fills up the tiny air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ, ebaakpa niyenii yeli Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do I need to put palm fronds over my nursery bed to shade the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei awo ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Shade structures protect tender leaves from heat stress and keep the soil from drying out too fast.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five seeds into one single nursery bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ grow bag kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one bag forces the seedlings to fight for the small amount of soil, water, and light available, resulting in thin, weak plants.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ kotoku kome mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la fioo. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die right after I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes root shock, especially in hot weather. Planting early in the morning or late in the afternoon helps the plant adjust smoothly without drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni egbiɛɛ.

english: How can I easily tell if the soil on my farm is good for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good farming soil is dark, crumbles easily in your hand, and stays moist without turning into heavy sticky mud. The dark color shows it is rich in organic nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ su yɛ ediŋ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa. Sui ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli.

english: Why should I keep shade trees on my land instead of cutting them all down before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as living umbrellas that shield young cocoa trees from intense sunlight and extreme heat, keeping the soil moist so the cocoa plants don't dry out and die.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni cacao tsei lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagboi.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to produce fruit bunches under heavy tree cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ aduawai akui yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ewo wu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains need plenty of direct sunlight to make food and grow strong. When tree shade is too dense, it slows down their growth and results in smaller or delayed fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ efee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha aduawai akui bibii loo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or lack of water, as the plant tries to save energy to survive heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛye dɔlɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading plant viruses, which distorts new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. which distorts the growth of new leaves

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot in the soil when I plant them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soaking wet soil starves stem cuttings of oxygen, encouraging fungal decay before root growth starts. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ni aaawo mli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baaje shishi lɛ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same farm at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving plenty of light and room for the slower cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Ha kane kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ akwɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after clearing forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni ajie koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Forest soil contains thousands of dormant weed seeds that sprout rapidly once land clearing opens the canopy, allowing direct sunlight and rain to hit the ground.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji ajie ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know when my yams are fully ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the yam vines and leaves start turning yellow and dry up naturally at the end of the season, it signals that the plant has stopped growing and the tuber is mature.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ edara.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady, deep rainfall over a few days so the ground has enough lasting moisture to germinate the seeds without them drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa gbii fioo komɛi bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbiŋ.

english: How do I know the exact best time to plant my maize seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the soil has received two or three heavy rains and is thoroughly wet about finger-deep. Planting after the very first light drizzle often leads to seeds drying out and failing to sprout if the rain pauses for several days.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ. ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ aaafee inchi kome Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ agbimɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with grass and dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? Nibii ni jwɛi gboi kɛ baai yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil—which is called mulching—acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly decays into rich natural food for your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa kɛha onibii.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crops very close together in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all of them weak and thin with small yields, whereas proper spacing lets every plant feed well and produce full harvests.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kpakpa ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer near the base of the plant helps them recover their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do all the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress, lack of nutrients, or damage from tiny sucking bugs called mirids. Keeping shade trees over your cocoa, protecting soil moisture, and controlling pests will help the flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nu mli haomɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids lɛ efite amɛ. Tso He Kwɛmɔ: Ha o-cocoo tso lɛ nɔ hulutsoo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he buu Kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji ni ekumɔ lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing tip or 'funnel' of the maize. Applying approved treatments directly into the central funnel early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi loo ‘gbɛi’ ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo center funnel lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Spraying the underside of leaves early with neem oil extract or soapy water helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo nu ni akɛ samla tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes develop black rotten spots on the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering or rainfall is irregular. Keeping the soil steadily moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents the bottom rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite.

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep, and as the fruit bunch grows, the tree becomes heavy at the top. You can prevent them from falling by propping up the stem with strong wooden poles and piling mounded soil around the base.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ni kɛ́ tso lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Obaanyɛ otsi enaa koni ekagbee shi kɛtsɔ tso ni wa ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛfi esɛɛ ni okɛ muji ato shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot so fast if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain alive underground, but if left in waterlogged soil past maturity, water gets trapped inside and rots them. Once dug out, they also spoil quickly, so it is best to harvest only what you can use or sell immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaada kwraa Nu lɛ baakpã mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba. Kɛ́ atsa lɛ, ebaagbo oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaakpa nɔ pɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make green leaves and food. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic manure helps the leaves stay green and strong so the plant can yield big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tight during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up on hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water to the sun. It is a natural defense behavior where the plant shrinks its leaf surface area to save moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni hulu lɛ akafite nu babaoo. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ ko ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo baa.

english: What is the purpose of the tassel on top of my corn plant, and why is yellow dust falling from it?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe? Ni mɛni hewɔ sũ ŋmɔŋ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: The tassel is the male part of the corn plant, and the yellow dust is pollen. The wind blows this pollen down onto the silk threads of the young cobs so seeds can form inside.
ga: Tasel ji ŋmãa tso lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ. Ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji pollen. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa nɛkɛ pollen nɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmei bibioo lɛ siliki lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui aba mli.

english: How far apart should I plant my corn seeds when sowing them in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting corn seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart in rows gives each plant enough space to spread its roots and leaves. If they are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni kɛ cob bibioo ko baa

english: Why shouldn't I just save and replant seeds from my harvested hybrid maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crop varieties lose their strong traits in the next generation, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures high yields and uniform crop behavior.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ, ni ana he odaseyeli daa be mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii asui ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal nutrients, space, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with good rainfall, your crops will struggle because the weeds are consuming the food in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Oŋmɔshi nibii po baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How does adding dry animal manure into my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure, helping it hold water longer during dry spells while slowly releasing essential plant nutrients that feed crop roots over time.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ kpo.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves deep inside the funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that target the soft, tender center leaves of young maize plants. Catching them early with appropriate bio-pesticides or recommended treatments keeps them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is completely dry and ready for final harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa ni efee klalo kɛha naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn completely brown and papery, and a tiny black spot forms at the base of the grain kernel when pulled off the cob.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛfee tamɔ wolo. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi kɛji ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce better crops when I plant groundnuts after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, restoring the nutrients that maize took away.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛ niyenii ni ŋmãa ejie lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and helps them build strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to strong heat, which keeps it from losing too much water.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa baa lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ afite fe nine.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves when water is scarce to conserve moisture in their roots under the soil, and they will sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ nu faaa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ebaatswa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are small green worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that loves to feed on young maize funnels. Early detection and applying recommended treatment prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa bibii. Nibii ni ana mra Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when the weather is extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry, as the plant saves its remaining water to keep itself alive rather than feeding fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ toɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ehi shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my yams under the ground are mature enough to harvest without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii?

english: You can tell yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ sweet potatoes efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs than the original packet seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishijee paketi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single strong generation. The seeds collected from that harvest lose their hybrid strength, leading to uneven growth and lower yields in the next planting season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome ni he wa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hybrid hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What is 'smart rice' and how is it different from the traditional rice I plant?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘smart rice’ ni te esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ blema ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Smart rice' usually refers to improved, high-yielding, or climate-resilient rice varieties developed by agricultural scientists. Unlike traditional seeds, these varieties are bred to mature faster, resist local pests better, and produce more grain per acre when properly managed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘Smart rice’ tsɔɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee lɛ. Esoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe Afɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi nɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ acre kome mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it worth spending extra money to buy improved crop seeds if my local seeds are free?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ awoɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛji akɛ mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, certified improved seeds generally yield much more grain, germinate more reliably, and resist common field diseases better than saved local seeds, which helps cover the initial purchase cost through a bigger harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo. amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni awo shishijee nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ he nyɔmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ wuji anɔ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties require different fertilizers than my local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi fe mimaŋ tsei lɛ.

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to grow faster and produce heavier harvests, which means they feed more aggressively and need specific soil nutrients at key growth stages to reach their full yield potential.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ nii waa ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi titrii amli koni amɛshɛ amɛ yibiiwoo he hewalɛ ni fa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin but produce very few grains when planted near large forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi ewoɔ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When crops are shaded by tall forest trees, they stretch upward searching for sunlight instead of putting energy into developing strong stems and healthy, full grain heads.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ koo mli tsei kakadaji lɛ ashishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛná tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna hulu la.

english: Does clearing forest land mean the soil will stay rich and fertile for my crops for many years?
ga: Ani koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa nii ni ebaaba nii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo ni baaba lɛ?

english: No, while newly cleared forest soil is rich in leaf mulch and organic matter initially, exposing the bare soil to heavy tropical rains and direct sun quickly washes away these nutrients unless organic matter or fertilizers are continuously added.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ, koo lɛ mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo moŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ oya. ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he be fɛɛ be

english: Can I plant rice inside a shady forest area, or does it need open land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ kooi ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli loo esa akɛ efee he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ?

english: Rice requires direct, full sunlight throughout the day to convert light into energy for grain production, making open fields or cleared lowlands far better than shaded forest spots.
ga: Omɔ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni ekɛtsake la lɛ ewo hewalɛ mli kɛha ŋmaa feemɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔji ni mli tse loo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe kooi amli hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my rice plants fall over flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over (called lodging) when their stems are too weak to support heavy grain heads, often caused by planting seeds too close together, using too much nitrogen fertilizer, or strong winds.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi (ni atsɛɔ amɛ shĩai) kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuɔ nii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why are my crops thriving on one side of town but struggling on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi nɔmɔ ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water retention, and shade levels can vary greatly even across short distances in the same town, directly affecting how easily crop roots can draw up water and nutrients.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli nu ni akɛhiɛɔ Ni hulutsoo be lɛ baanyɛ atsake waa yɛ gbɛ kukuji po amli. yɛ maŋ kome mli Enɛ saa bɔ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds sprout at different times even though I planted them all on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Uneven sprouting usually happens when seeds are planted at different soil depths, receive unequal soil moisture, or when uncertified seed mixes of varying quality are planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ srɔtoi anɔ. Na ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ.

english: How do I know if standing water in my rice field is helping or harming my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni damɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiye mibua loo eeye mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: Shallow, standing water helps suppress weeds and keeps rice roots moist, but if deep water completely covers the leaves for several days straight, the plants will suffocate and rot.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa ni ehaa omɔ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ nu ni mli kwɔ ha baai lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. The tree will suffocate and rot.

english: Young cocoa plants prefer partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture in their shallow root systems before they can establish.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Egbiɔ dani abaanyɛ ama.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, which lays eggs on maize and feeds inside the soft, young leaf shoots where water collects.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ ni eyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli, he ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ.

english: Excess rainwater and high moisture encourage a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly from the soil to the fruit when pods remain wet for long periods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick my cassava stems into the ground?
ga: Ekɔɔɔ he eko gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward before turning upward, which wastes plant energy and leads to very low tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ayibii lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why should I remove extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many shoots share the same root water and food, taking vital strength away from the mother plant and resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ, ni no haa plantains bibii baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow even when there is enough rain?
