ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main element crops need to produce dark green leaf material and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji nɔ titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil, giving nearby maize free plant nutrients.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni ŋmãa bɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing them to stretch tall for light instead of building fat cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛhe la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatswa ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruit during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato flowers, causing pollen to dry up before pollination occurs, which leads the plant to drop its unpollinated flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When soil stays flooded with water, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing damp fungal diseases to grow and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli ewo fɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat, sudden dry soil conditions, or when there is too much leaf-building fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ haomɔ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. Aloo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, ground space, and nutrients. They stretch upward quickly to reach light, making their stalks thin and weak.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. This makes their stems thin and weak.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my crops yield smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Without enough food and water, your crops do not have the energy to build large fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛji niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I wait to plant my seeds instead of planting on the very first day it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ koni madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry period. If you plant too early, the young seeds will sprout but then dry up and die before the regular rains return.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on sticks gives leaves maximum light and keeps them clean from ground diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ niji wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná la babaoo, ni ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe atse ehe.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my green crops more severely during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, wild grasses dry out and leave little food for insects. Pests move directly to farm crops because your crops are green, juicy, and full of water.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni eshiɔ niyenii fioo ko kɛhaa kooloi bibii. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafã kɛya okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji, amɛmli nu, ni nu eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plantain stems with dry grass help them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from evaporating water out of the ground. It keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom leaves usually means your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food that creates green leaves; when the soil runs out of it, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has left up to the new top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ fite lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa baai heei amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with small tubers when I plant them under big timber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to make food and store it underground in its roots. When planted in deep shade, the plant uses all its energy trying to grow tall to reach the sun, leaving no extra energy to swell its cassava roots.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni ehoo, ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara koni amɛná hulu la. ni efiteee hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and burn when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a living canopy that shelters the young cocoa from direct heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe waaa waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he lɛ baa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my maize stems stay weak and fall over in the wind when I put five seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni mikɛ dumɔwui 5 wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the seedlings to fight each other for the same soil food, water, and sunlight. This competition makes all of them grow thin and weak instead of developing strong, thick stems.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu amɛha niyenii, shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii ni he wa ni mli wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too stressed by dry soil or severe heat. When the weather is too dry and hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ babaoo mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why did my green pepper leaves look burnt after I placed chemical fertilizer directly against the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ewo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated mineral salts. When placed right against the stem, they pull moisture straight out of the plant tissues like salt on an open cut, causing the leaves to burn and dry up.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does cutting off the small shoots around my main plantain tree help it produce a bigger bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ebɔle mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe hewɔ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niji lɛ daraa.

english: All shoots on the same plantain stool share the same roots and soil nutrients. When you remove the extra suckers, all the food and water from the soil go directly into feeding the main tree and making its fruit bunch grow larger.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ plantain ŋmɔtɔ kome nɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ sũ mli niyenii kome. Kɛji ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ Niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni eyaha tso titri lɛ niyenii. ni oha aduawai akuu lɛ afee agbo

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli eggplant lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding on the underside of the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, causing the tender leaves to wrinkle and stop growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites, kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ nu. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni sa.

english: Why do the roots of my yam plants turn soft and rot when rainwater gathers on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air inside the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When standing water covers your field for too long, it drowns the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungal diseases to multiply.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa.

english: Why don't my saved maize seeds grow when I plant them after storing them in a warm, humid room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A seed contains a tiny living embryo that stays resting until planted. Storing seeds in a warm, moist room tricks them into using up their stored energy too early, weakening or killing the seed before it ever touches the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ fɔmɔ nii bibii ni hiɛ ka ni baakã he ahi shi kɛyashi abaadu. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ lakaa amɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ blɛoo loo amɛgboiɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ taa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees near my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Shade trees protect them from severe heat, keep the soil cool and moist, and help the young crops grow safely into healthy adult trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei haa amɛnáa hɔnɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry out and drop their leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan wind is very dry and sucks moisture out of plant leaves and soil rapidly. Trees shed leaves during this period to save water and protect themselves from dying in the extreme dry heat.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects. If the tree lacks sufficient water, soil nutrients, or insect pollinators, it naturally drops extra flowers to save energy for the pods it can support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. E pɛ ji nɔ nɛ a ma nyɛ maa pee pollen. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛjɛ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are some of the green pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in humid, rainy weather. Leaving infected pods on the tree allows the disease to spread to healthy pods nearby, so they must be removed.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie pods lɛ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees yield fewer pods now than they did a few years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees produce pods season after season, they consume nutrients from the soil. If those nutrients are not replaced through fertilizer or organic compost, the soil becomes tired and cannot support large harvests anymore.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ be kɛ bei amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I prune off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or dead branches so sunlight and air can pass freely through the tree canopy. This lowers humidity around the tree to prevent fungal diseases and helps the tree direct its strength into producing pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔjɔ loo ni egboi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ hɔɔmɔ mli oya. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ aba shi koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my cocoa trees reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mikokoo tsei lɛ ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ba shi.

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water that your cocoa trees need to grow. They also trap unwanted moisture and hide insect pests that can attack your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni he hiaa o-cocoa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo lɛ hu ni ekɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ atutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why should I leave fallen cocoa leaves on the ground instead of clearing and burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ ni mashã amɛ?

english: Fallen leaves decay over time and turn into rich organic fertilizer for your soil. They also act like a blanket over the soil, keeping it moist and cool during hot, dry weather.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii hu tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe pod changes color completely, turning from green to bright yellow or from red to orange. Harvesting only ripe pods ensures that the cocoa beans inside have fully developed sugar and oil content.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ etsuru kɛya akutu mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ sugar kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to leave harvested cocoa pods sitting on wet farm ground for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Damp ground encourages mold, fungi, and insects to penetrate the pods and spoil the beans inside. Transporting pods quickly to a dry place preserves the quality and weight of your harvest.
ga: He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii abote ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ tee he ko ni egbi oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okpamɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Is it true that crops always need as much water as possible to grow well?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be bɔ ni abaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No. Although people often say crops like water, that is not always true. Excess water can harm crops depending on how deep it gets and how long it remains on the field.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nu moŋ. Shi jeee be fɛɛ be eji anɔkwale. Nu babaoo baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii awui. Edamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɔ ha kɛ be ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Do all crops tolerate sitting in water for a long period?
ga: Ani tsei fɛɛ kpɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: No, crops do not always tolerate standing water. If a crop is planted in a place where water stays continuously for about three months, it will die.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo nu mli aaafee nyɔji etɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaagbo.

english: Why would my crops start dying after a period of prolonged flooding on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miibɔi gboimɔ yɛ nu afua ni ho yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even though crops need moisture, standing water that remains around your planted crops for up to three months or reaches too deep a level will destroy and kill them.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ Shi nu ni damɔ shi ni ehiɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔji etɛ loo eboteɔ mli tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛ ni egbe amɛ.

english: Does the depth of standing water on my field really matter to my crops?
ga: Ani bɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, water depth matters greatly. If the water level on your planted land gets too deep, it reaches a point where the crops can no longer survive and will die.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu mlibotemɔ he miihia waa. Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ Ebaashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi dɔŋŋ ni ebaagbo.

english: Should I immediately drain my field as soon as I notice water standing on it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo nu lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina nu ni damɔ shi?

english: You shouldn't just drain waterlogged land straight away or leave it as it is without assessing it. You need to consider how deep the water is getting and how long it is likely to stay.
ga: Esaaa akɛ ojieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ he ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo oshiɔ jɛmɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ. Esa akɛ osusu bɔ ni nu lɛ mli kwɔ ha kɛ be abɔ ni ebaahi shi lɛ he.

english: Is it safe for me to just leave waterlogged land alone without doing anything to it?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikome too mashi he ni nu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni mifeee nɔ ko?

english: No, simply leaving waterlogged land as it is can be dangerous because if that standing water stays pooled on your crops for up to three months, they will die.
ga: Dabi, he ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni oooshi kɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛji nakai nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ onibii amli kɛyashi nyɔji etɛ. Amɛbaagboi.

english: What will happen to my planted crops if water sits on my land for up to three months?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nu hi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji etɛ?

english: If water stays pooled in your planting area for about three months, your crops will eventually die.
ga: Kɛji nu damɔ he ni okwɛɔ lɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ nɛ. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii baagboi.

english: How do I know when standing water on my farm has become dangerous for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nu ni ekã shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Water becomes dangerous to your crops when it gets too deep or when it sits on the planted area continuously for about three months.
ga: Nu yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji eyɛ mli tsɔ loo kɛ́ ehi he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be aaafee nyɔji etɛ.

english: What is the right approach when dealing with a farm field that easily collects water?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ ŋmɔji ni nu buaa amɛhe naa oya lɛ ahe nii?

english: When managing waterlogged land, avoid making quick decisions to drain it immediately or leave it untouched. Instead, observe if the water gets too deep or stays long enough—around three months—to kill your crops.
ga: Beni ookwɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ yiŋkpɛɛ ni oookpɛ oya akɛ obaajie nu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo oshi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko akataa he lɛ he. Kadimɔ kɛji nu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ loo eshɛɛɛ jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ. (aaafee nyɔji etɛ) ni baagbe oŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Can land that stays wet for months still be used to keep crops alive?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ atsu nii lolo koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi?

english: If water stays on that land for about three months continuously, any crops planted there will die, so prolonged water retention must be carefully managed.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be aaafee nyɔji etɛ. Nibii ni adu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akwɛ nu ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant trap moisture inside and stop itself from drying out during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Can my vegetable crops keep bearing fruit during the dry season if I keep giving them water?
ga: Ani mi-aduawai lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛji miha amɛ nu?

english: Yes, crops can continue flowering and fruiting all year round as long as they get enough water and nutrients, because water allows the plant leaves to keep producing energy regardless of rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu haa tsei ahe baai yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the crop, causing it to drop flowers to save energy and water so that the main plant can stay alive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava turn yellow and fall off when the rain stops for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, the plant intentionally sheds its older lower leaves to conserve water and direct its limited moisture to the young growing tips at the top.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛshishi baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko amaje tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up water so the roots can drink before the hot midday sun causes the moisture to evaporate into the air.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do improved seed varieties yield more crop than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to resist local diseases, grow stronger root systems, and use water and soil nutrients more efficiently than seeds saved over many generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni okɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ato kɛha yinɔi babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without giving many fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, crops compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, using all their energy to grow tall toward the light instead of developing fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa kɛyaa la lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when water stays trapped on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do; when water covers the soil for too long, it drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up plant food and causing them to decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa amɛye tso lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my crops more heavily during dry periods than during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather weakens crops, making it easier for pests to pierce the leaves, while insects actively search for green crops to get the water trapped inside them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛbaabote baai lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ ekãa taoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni nu akahi mli.

english: How do deep-rooted crops like cassava survive long droughts while shallow-rooted crops like lettuce die quickly?
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ lettuce lɛ, gboi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Deep roots work like deep underground wells, pulling up water hidden far beneath the ground, while shallow roots can only reach the top soil layer which dries out quickly in the heat.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nubu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ he. ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of tiny insects when I store it in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ efite loo ŋmeii bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ be akɛto tsu lɛ mli?

english: Maize rots or attracts pests like weevils when it is stored with too much moisture inside the grains. Drying the maize thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are hard, and using airtight storage bags, keeps insects out and stops mold from destroying your harvest.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ loo egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to ŋmeii lɛ amli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okɛ vacuum storage bags atsu nii koni kooloi kɛ ŋmeii akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to make food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops roll up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, plants roll or droop their leaves to save water and prevent drying out. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ baafolɔ loo amɛbaashɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes through the leaves of my growing corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai ni miida lɛ amli?

english: These worms are caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, that hatch from eggs laid by night-flying moths. They feed on tender leaves to grow, but checking your field early and using recommended safe pest treatments can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii koni amɛdara. Shi kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava tubers turn black and soft when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain floods the field for long periods, the ground becomes waterlogged, choking the roots and causing soil fungi to make the tubers soft and rotted.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ, nu hoɔ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ. Nu baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. efoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many maize seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick stalks and produce full, heavy cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds right after the first major rains of the season start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu ni yɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting right after the first big rains ensures seeds get consistent moisture to sprout quickly and establish deep roots before any unexpected dry spell occurs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baa.

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much smaller food than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo kwraa fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm, stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures all available soil food goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ baashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot dry weather, irregular watering, or a lack of plant nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and evenly moist helps the plant keep its flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa ni egbi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ ahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli daa ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Applying fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients the plants need to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices, or by viruses they spread. Spraying with mild soapy water or recommended neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Planting maize about 25 to 30 centimeters apart in rows allows every stalk enough space to drink water, catch sunlight, and feed from the soil without fighting its neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛnuɔ nu, enáa hulu la, ni enaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu.

english: How can I tell if my land is good enough to plant tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu tomato?

english: Good tomato soil should crumble easily in your hands, allow rain water to drain through without standing in puddles, and be rich in dark organic matter like compost or decomposed leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ tomato shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ akumɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Ehaa nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli ni ebɛ nubu ko mli. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni fiteɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my groundnuts produce empty shells with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium or becomes too dry while the pods are developing underground. Adding lime or wood ash to the soil before planting provides the calcium needed to form full nuts.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo egbi tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani adu lɛ, ebaaha calcium ni he hiaa koni afee ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree before making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme dry weather, poor soil food, or attacks by bugs like capsids. Providing shade and keeping the soil moist helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water settles around them in swampy soil or after heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to run off away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ mli loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my yam leaves drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ egbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves dry up early when attacked by leaf spot diseases or when beetles damage the vines under the soil. Staking the vines off the wet ground keeps the leaves dry and healthy longer.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ leaf spot ko mɔ amɛ loo kɛji ŋmeii bote wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ tee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my watermelons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa watermelon?

english: A watermelon is ready when the small curly vine tendril closest to the fruit turns brown and dry, and the underside spot resting on the dirt changes from white to a creamy yellow color.
ga: Watermelon lɛ efee klalo beni ŋmei bibioo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Those near the fruit turn brown and dry. ni shishigbɛ hei ni kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eyɛŋ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ krim.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil still feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: Crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it when the sun is very hot. Wilting is the plant's natural way of curling up to save water until the cool evening arrives.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛji hulu lɛ miitso. Withering ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ ehe koni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi fɛ̃i be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but end up with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots to make big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo tsɔ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or lack of water cause stress to pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to save their energy and stay alive rather than producing peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa Loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell early in the season if my maize farm will give me a good yield or a poor one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli akɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai loo yibii gbohii?

english: You can judge early by checking leaf color and silk formation; if the leaves stay dark green and there is sufficient rain during the tasseling stage, the plants are healthy enough to fill the maize cobs fully.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo mra. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ su kɛ siliki feemɔ mlipɛimɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni abuaa nibii anaa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil dries out completely after planting, or if soil pests eat the seeds before they have a chance to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Plants send available food to their new top leaves first; yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the lower leaves are not getting enough sunlight.
ga: Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ majeɔ baai heei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ náaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do crops planted very close together grow thin and fall over easily in strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they race upward to steal sunlight from each other, which makes their stems long, thin, and weak instead of growing strong and thick enough to withstand wind.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Ebaajo foi kɛya ŋwɛi ni ebaaju hulu la kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, efeɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden lightly every day or give it a heavy soaking once or twice a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli nu fioo daa gbi loo oooha lɛ nu ni mli wa? Shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli

english: Heavy soaking once or twice a week is better because it forces the roots to grow deep into the ground where water lasts longer, making the plant stronger during hot dry weather.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ wo mli waa shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my land make my next crop of maize grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts capture natural food from the air and store it in the soil through their roots; when you harvest them, that trapped food stays behind in the soil to act as free fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Niyenii ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so the beans don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely from green to yellow, or red to orange; harvesting too early leaves the beans under-developed, while waiting too long causes the seeds to sprout inside the pod.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru kɛtee ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do tomato plants inside a greenhouse grow taller than the ones I grow on my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ daraa fe tomato tsei ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouse tomato plants get continuous warm temperatures, protection from heavy rain, and light shade, which allows them to spend energy growing upward without suffering from weather stress or pests.
ga: Tomato tsei ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ naa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he ni eyɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛkɛ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnaaa piŋmɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do sweet pepper leaves inside a shade structure curl up when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bell pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce surface area, helping it hold onto moisture and protect itself from extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he.

english: When temperatures get too high or the plant lacks enough water, it gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of making seeds and fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa lɛ Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ wuhi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my cucumber plants produce many blossoms but very few cucumbers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi kukumba fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Cucumber plants produce both male and female flowers; if insects like bees are not visiting the field to move pollen from male to female flowers, the fruits will not form.
ga: Kukumba tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya yei amli lɛ, Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baaa mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the soil lacks enough nitrogen; the maize plant is pulling nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei miigba nitrogen kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei ni darako lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge green leaves but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to direct all its food into leaf and stem growth instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkudɔ amɛ niyenii fɛɛ kɛya baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do the roots of my crop plants burn and dry up after I apply chemical fertilizer during a dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve; without water, the fertilizer concentrated around the roots draws water out of the plant, burning the roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni sũ lɛ mli ajɔ koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing small, thin fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving each plant with less energy to develop big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haaa tso fɛɛ tso aná hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds in my field grow much faster than my crop seedlings after rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted over time to quickly drink water and take up soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛnu nu oya ni amɛhe niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when big tree canopies completely block the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni tso ni eda lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa kwraa lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need shade, mature cocoa trees need moderate sunlight on their leaves to make the food necessary to form flowers and develop pods.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kokoo tsei bibii. Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside them protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ha loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green even after good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaf growth. Rain alone does not feed the plant; adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ pɛ haaa tsei niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings is the best way to prevent this disease from stopping your roots from growing big.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Gbalaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekaha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause tomato plants stress, making them drop their flowers to conserve energy and water. Watering regularly at the roots and putting dry grass mulch around the base of the plant helps keep the soil cool and preserves the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Okɛ nu awo shishifãi lɛ amli daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce thin, woody roots instead of big tubers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Yɛ bulbs wuji najiaŋ beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough underground space and nutrients to expand. When planted too close together, the roots compete for water and soil nutrients, resulting in many thin, unusable roots rather than large, healthy tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very leafy and tall but fail to produce many peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwereɔ ni ekwɛɔ shi enyɛɛɛ ewo pepper babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Balancing the soil food with fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set plenty of peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potassium babaoo mli lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the next season's maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and legumes have natural helpers in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant breaks down, that trapped nutrient acts as free fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ legumes yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni cowpea tso lɛ gbee shi lɛ Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmei henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cool, very wet conditions encourage Black Pod disease, which is a fungus that spreads rapidly through water drops. Pruning extra branches and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ blackpod hela baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli ŋmeii amli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do tiny caterpillars chew holes right inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which hides inside the central leaves of maize to feed on tender tissue. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the leaf funnels kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni eye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings fall over and rot right at the ground level soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called 'damping-off,' caused by soil fungi that thrive when the nursery bed is too wet and overcrowded. Giving seedlings proper spacing and avoiding over-watering keeps the soil surface dry enough to stop stem rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ mli ewo nu tsɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛbaa Dumɔwui lɛ ni oooha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava take almost two years in the soil before I can harvest big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ aaafee afii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava stores food in its underground roots slowly over time. While some early varieties mature faster, traditional varieties take up to two years to build up full starch reserves and give you maximum yield.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ henɔi lɛ Srɔtoi komɛi baakwɛ̃ oya. Shi blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ heɔ afii enyɔ dani amɛtswaa amɛ starch ni amɛto lɛ amɛma shi ni amɛshɛɔ yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the rain stops for just a short period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Maize plants need water to absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. When dry weather pauses their growth, the plant cannot take up food properly, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Abɛi tsei taoɔ nu koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, dalɛ kpaa be kukuoo ko. Tsei nyɛŋ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why should I allow my farmland to take a break and rest after planting crops on it for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous farming drains nutrients from the soil. Giving the land a break, or fallowing, allows the soil to naturally restore its richness, organic matter, and beneficial organisms for future crops.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efoɔ loo efoɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ ekɛ ehe awo ŋmɔshi nibii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to start planting when the rain begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hand without being too sticky or overly sandy, holds moisture well, and has living organisms like earthworms inside.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cocoa trees use to protect themselves from water loss during hot, dry winds. It helps the tree conserve moisture until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain suckers struggle to grow well when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need direct sunlight and plenty of nutrients to grow strong trunks. Big trees block the light and steal water and food from the soil, slowing down the plantain's growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa plantains lɛ daalɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ du cowpea lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize while keeping the ground covered and cool.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing flowers but dropping them without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi egbee shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is extreme stress from dry soil. It can also happen if there are no bees or insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly when left in the hot sun after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still living tubers that breathe and react to heat. Excess heat creates moisture buildup and damage inside the tuber, allowing decay fungi to enter and cause rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lolo ni muɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa bulb lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants slow down and stop producing new peppers after I harvest them repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛkpaa pepper heei feemɔ beni mikpa amɛ shii abɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants use a lot of energy to grow flowers and fruits. After several harvests, the plant exhausts its stored food and soil nutrients, requiring light pruning and organic compost to start producing again.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi babaoo sɛɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebiɔ ni afolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii feemɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to one another, they compete for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of putting energy into building thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛhe la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know when the rain is steady enough to start planting my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the very first rain can kill seeds if dry weather returns. It is best to wait until the rain moistens the soil down to about the depth of your hand, showing that the rainy season has truly established itself.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves up to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green bushy leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its strength growing thick leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the next crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants finish growing and rot in the soil, they leave behind natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Abaashi Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and high temperatures. Shade trees protect young cocoa from sunburn and keep the soil damp so the roots do not dry out.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without making any fruits when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from forming fruit. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to save its energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollination Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold up and turn brown along the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water quickly in the sun. When the soil is dry, the leaves curl up to reduce exposure to heat and protect the rest of the plant from losing moisture.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba dɔlɛ shi ni ebu hei krokomɛi ahe. ni ji tsei lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in cool, dark, and wet weather. Rain drops splash the fungus from the soil onto the pods, and dense leaves trap water on the trees.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni baai ni mli eyi lɛ toɔ nu yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do tiny worms appear inside the funnel of my maize leaves and chew big holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii je kpo yɛ mi-corn leaf cones lɛ amli ni amɛye buji wuji nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These worms, like fall armyworms, hatch from eggs laid by adult moths on the leaves. They crawl into the central funnel of the plant where it is dark and moist to hide while eating the tender young leaves.
ga: Taakɛ fall armyworms ji lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni amɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ amli koni amɛyatee amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Giving your plants steady moisture and applying balanced fertilizer will help the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nu haa tsei lɛ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa woɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist, such as a day after a good rain. Putting fertilizer on bone-dry soil can burn the plant roots, while applying it during heavy rain can wash all the nutrients away before the plant can drink them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ gbi lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ anu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn and dry up under direct, hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it gets older.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together reduce my overall harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them out properly gives every plant enough room and food to produce bigger stems and heavier yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps pests away.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Curled and yellow cassava leaves are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni woɔ nibii ahe adafi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomatoes rotting from the bottom end while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ naagbee be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rot at the bottom of a tomato fruit, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulching and adding lime or organic matter helps stop this rot.
ga: Rot ni yɔɔ tomato aduawai lɛ shishi Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ahaa amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ lime loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long and suffocates the roots. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers safe and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become regular and the soil is moist at least palm-deep before planting. Planting after just one light rain can trap your seeds in drying dirt if the rain stops for several weeks afterward.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni sa, ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tamɔ tso ni ji tso dani odu. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shikome pɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my crops when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje tsei ashishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil is consistently moist down to about hand-depth, usually after two or three steady rains, rather than planting after the very first light shower which can dry out quickly and destroy your seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashɛ onine mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni baanyɛ agbi oya ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops look weak and yellow when the rain comes too late after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady moisture right after germination to build strong roots and absorb nutrients. When rains are delayed, the young plants become stressed, fail to take up nitrogen from the soil, and turn yellow.
ga: Abele he miihia nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ koni ená shishifãi ni wa ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baaná haomɔ. Enyɛɛɛ ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do the roots of my vegetable crops rot after standing water stays on my field for a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from small air spaces in the soil to breathe. Standing water drowns the root system, cutting off oxygen and causing the roots to rot and the plant to wither.
