ga: Tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii amli lɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛmu Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there are no bigger shade plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa amɛhe lɛ bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow fully and yield a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does heavy rain sometimes make my crop fertilizer disappear without helping the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mitsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ ni eyeee ebuaaa tsei lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash fertilizer deep into the ground past the reach of the plant roots, or wash it off the surface entirely. Applying fertilizer in smaller split amounts during calm weather prevents this loss.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtekeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ wo mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant cassava on the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before producing any fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms as a survival tactic when exposed to extreme heat or drought stress to conserve water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa mli. Koni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa mɔ daa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss through evaporation, allowing the root to survive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi tsei titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb surface moisture and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early stops them from starving your crops of essential food and water.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be tied to tall wooden stakes while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Tying the vines to stakes lifts the leaves off the damp ground, giving them full sunlight while protecting them from rot and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha lɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are sown too close together, their roots and leaves compete heavily against each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and lose their color during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe feɔ shoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and turn yellow when the plant is stressed by intense heat or under attack by tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies. It is the plant's way of conserving water and reacting to pest pressure.
ga: Yucca baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha tso lɛ hao loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ tutua lɛ. Eji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni etsuɔ ​​he nii kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ enɔ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land has good soil for my vegetable farm before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ aduawai dani aduɔ nii?

english: Good soil is usually dark brown or black, soft, and crumbles easily in your hand while holding some moisture. Soil that is very pale, hard like clay, or pure sand lacks the natural plant food needed for good crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nine mli yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse waa lɛ wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ sũ. loo ŋã ni he tse Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to pick my pepper crop so that I get good quality to sell for a profit?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ ohala ŋmɔtɔ tsei koni amɛfee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ni ana sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Harvest peppers when they are firm and have fully reached their bright ripe color. Picking them at full maturity gives them a longer shelf life during transportation and ensures they command a higher price at the market.
ga: Kpaa ŋmeii beni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe su lɛ mli tse kwraa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ beni amɛdara kwraa lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ. Ni ehaa jara lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing plantains provides crucial shade and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei kakadaji ni damɔ shi loo odu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why does my field give me fewer tomatoes if I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tomato fioo kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Alternating tomatoes with crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Tomato ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off prematurely when the plant experiences water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate them. Regular watering and protecting helpful insects encourage fruit growth.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adara.

english: Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so the roots can safely drink it in. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil creates a harsh environment that can scorch and destroy the plant's roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops rot at the roots when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miifite kɛmiiya amɛshishifãi amli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it smothers the roots, preventing oxygen intake and causing root rot that eventually kills the plant.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting trees too closely makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller pods and making it easier for diseases to spread between branches.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ aniji ateŋ mlɛo.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, damp weather. Pruning extra branches lets in sunlight and airflow, which helps dry out the tree and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: What is the strange bush growing directly on my cocoa tree branches, and should I cut it off?
ga: Mɛni ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɛɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: That is mistletoe, a harmful parasite that steals water and food directly from your cocoa tree. You must remove it by cutting off the branch right below where the mistletoe attaches.
ga: No ji mistletoe Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ ojie kɛtsɔ tso nine ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni mistletoe lɛ ekpɛtɛ he lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers, but only a few pods end up growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Most cocoa flowers naturally fall off, but tiny beneficial insects called midges are needed to pollinate them. Poor soil nutrients, drought, or lack of pollination prevent flowers from developing into full pods.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ he miihia waa kɛha pollination. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, hɔmɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ adara kwraa ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will cutting branches off my cocoa tree hurt it or help it produce more pods?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ baaye lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning unnecessary or weak branches actually helps the tree focus its energy on producing bigger, healthier pods while allowing air and light to flow through the tree.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eeefee lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the seeds inside have properly developed high-quality beans.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs extra nutrients for my crops to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi koni mitsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield small harvests, the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, which can be restored using organic manure or fertilizers.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ daa blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ

english: Can I grow cassava on the same farm right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava grows aggressive roots that steal too much water and soil nutrients from young cocoa trees, so it is better to plant plantains or cocoyams which provide shade without choking the cocoa.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu kookoo dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni haaa kookoo lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why do I have to weed my young cocoa farm so frequently compared to my mature cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shii abɔ kɛ akɛto mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have small leaves that let sunlight reach the ground, encouraging weed growth. Older cocoa trees form a thick canopy overhead that blocks light and naturally prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii. ni haa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ daa Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse ni haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout properly if I plant them directly into soil that is very hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni wa waa ni mli edɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Hard soil makes it difficult for young roots to push downward and access oxygen. Loosening the soil before planting creates air pockets and allows roots to spread easily so the seed can take up water and sprout strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shi ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with neighboring plants for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of making big cobs, the plant uses all its energy stretching upward to fight for light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii wuji Moŋ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwuɔ eshiɔ la.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same spot season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that plant needs most. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it rich.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ lɛ daa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the young leaves on my vegetable plants turn pale yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing a lack of nutrients, especially nitrogen, or poor root drainage. Adding compost or well-rotted manure helps restore nutrients so leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shishifãi ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Kɛkɛ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die so quickly if I plant them in an open field with no shade around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily scorch and dry out under direct afternoon sun. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates living umbrellas that trap moisture and shade the seedling.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ wala mli ni mɔɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ hulutsoo lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow weak and small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and aggressively steal fertilizers, soil water, and root space away from your crops, leaving your plants starving despite good rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and look lifeless in the hot noon sun, but stand back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ni enyɛ ete shi gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves release moisture faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce heat exposure and water loss, recovering once temperatures drop.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Akɛ yiŋtoo ko shwieɔ tsei anɔ koni hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebaahe ejɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants yellow and drop off during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's survival trick to conserve water during dry periods. By shedding top leaves, the plant stops losing moisture and stays alive underground until the next rainy season.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ko ni haa ŋmei yeɔ wala koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize, and why does it stop the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ekpaa tsei adalɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the fresh, tender inner growing tip of the maize stalk. Damaging this core stops the plant from producing new leaf growth and developing corn ears.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ afite nɛkɛ shishigbɛ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee baai heei ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi afee.

english: Why do my groundnut plants turn yellow and show dark spots on the leaves during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture creates an environment where leaf spot fungi thrive on wet foliage. These spots block sunlight from hitting the leaf surface, which slows down growth and weakens the pod yield underneath.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni baa mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekatswa baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ayibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture while cocoa plants establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ damɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the old, yellowing fronds from my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mu tsei ahe baai momo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning old fronds allows more air and sunlight to reach the tree, which reduces fungal diseases, keeps pests from hiding, and makes harvesting the palm fruit bunches much easier.
ga: Fern tsei momoi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tso lɛ he. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe Ni ehaa ŋmei yibii akui ni akpaa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogging around the roots, which prevents the crop from absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are these small caterpillars chewing holes in the funnels of my maize, and how do I deal with them?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-corn cones lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ amɛ aye?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. You can control them by applying recommended insecticides early in the morning or sprinkling dry sand or wood ash into the leaf funnel.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni okɛaawo mli leebi loo ŋã ni egbi loo tso sũ ni oookɛshwie baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stems on raised mounds instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds keep the soil loose so cassava roots can easily expand into large tubers, while also allowing excess rainwater to drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun and keeps them off the wet soil, preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil drops below required moisture levels, or when there are no bees and insects to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ shishi Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying organic neem oil or suitable pesticides helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo aphids, ni miinu nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts help make my soil better for next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply granular fertilizer right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer before the plant roots can soak it up. This wastes your money and can pollute nearby streams. Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, not soaking wet.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ oshika, ni ebaanyɛ efite faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, shi jeee be mli ni edɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an important plant food for green growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava grows best in loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water easily so the roots can swell into big tubers. If heavy water stays on top of your land for days after it rains, the soil is too wet and can rot the crop.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. ni shwieɔ nu oya No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji nu afua nu lɛ hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving your seeds the recommended spacing gives each plant enough food and room to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni akɛhaa yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when they get direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that dry out and burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or shade trees next to them provides a living canopy that shelters the cocoa until it gets older and stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ kã ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry weather to save water and protect itself from dying. Once the rains return, the plant naturally grows fresh leaves and continues feeding its underground roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaya nɔ ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants blossom above the ground but form the actual nuts inside the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is fertilized, it grows a long stem called a peg that bends down and burrows into the soil. The nuts form underground where it is cool and moist, protecting them from heat while they mature.
ga: Beni awo ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii sɛɛ lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ feɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ naa be mli ni ahoɔ nii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded with water. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching helps the flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi aahu akɛ nu afua ba trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juices from the leaves and spread diseases. Spraying recommended neem solutions or mild insecticidal soaps helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem solution loo samla ni mli wa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground is often caused by water standing around the tubers or tiny pests called nematodes attacking the skin. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Yitso loo tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ nematodes ni ŋmɔɔ hewolo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How do I keep tiny insects from making holes in my stored cowpea seeds after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afo bu yɛ tsina dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Holes in stored cowpeas are caused by small beetles called weevils that eat the grain from the inside. Drying your seeds thoroughly under the hot sun and storing them in clean, sealed airtight bags stops insects from breeding.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni okɛto vacuum bag ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akabote gbalashihilɛ mli.

english: Why do seed varieties brought from outside Ghana sometimes fail to grow well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Foreign crop varieties are bred for different soils, temperatures, and rainfall patterns. When planted in Ghana, the local heat, pests, or soil conditions can stress the crop, causing low yields or disease unless the seeds are properly adapted to our local climate.
ga: Akwɛɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi kɛha shikpɔji, latsaa, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ Ghana He ni dɔlɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi loo hela. Ja dumɔwui lɛ tsake amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds every season instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for high yields and strong disease resistance. Saving seeds from hybrid crops causes the next generation to lose those strong traits, leading to uneven crop growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni abaabu he lɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ afite nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why do my maize crops produce smaller ears when there is too much heat during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ toi bibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: High temperatures dry out the silks on the maize cob, preventing pollen from fertilizing the plant properly. Without complete fertilization, the plant cannot form full, healthy kernels across the ear.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ fɔmɔ nii ni yeɔ emuu bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ toi lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers as a survival reaction to conserve water when moisture is scarce. Without enough soil water, the tree cannot support both its foliage and new pod development at the same time.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni amɛfeɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛji ŋmɔtɔ faaa. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso nyɛŋ aye abua tso lɛ yibii kɛ pod hee lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my yam vines wilt in the afternoon sun even when I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The temporary wilting is the plant's way of reducing leaf exposure to save water until the temperature drops in the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves happen if plant roots are damaged by standing water, if the soil is too dry to absorb nutrients, or if the wrong fertilizer was used. Plants need healthy roots and balanced soil moisture to drink up nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baa kɛji nu ni damɔ shi lɛ fite tso shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Tsei lɛ he miihia shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ja koni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but produce small root tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, it spends all its energy growing leaves to reach sunlight, leaving very little energy to store in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni eda lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛɔ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The warm temperatures and light rains of the minor season create ideal breeding conditions for insects, while crops experience brief water shortages that weaken their natural defenses against pests.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo. Yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, afeɔ fɔmɔ shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ahaa kooloi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ be kukuoo mli kpe. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do exotic fruit trees like temperate apples struggle to produce fruit in warm areas of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tso ko ni anaaa lɛ waa tamɔ apple ni mli edɔ waa lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Certain non-native fruit trees require a set period of cold winter temperatures to trigger flower growth. Ghana's warm climate does not give the tree that cold signal, so it continues to grow leaves without producing fruit.
ga: Yibii tsei komɛi ni jeee maŋ lɛ mli tsei lɛ biɔ fɛ̃i be mli fɛ̃i be ko koni eha fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ tsei lɛ fɛ̃i, no hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my harvested grains are dry enough so they do not rot during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbooo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Grains are dry enough when they crack cleanly between your teeth instead of denting. High moisture inside the grain allows mold and web-worms to grow, ruining the crop's value in the market.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛ́ amɛgbala amɛhe fɛfɛo yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ daa. Enɛ fiteɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: How does strong wind affect my maize plants while they are growing?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Strong winds can bend or snap maize stalks and dry out the soil quickly. Protecting them or planting sturdy varieties helps prevent the plants from falling over and losing their grain.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ abɔle loo akumɔ ŋmãa tsei ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Tsei srɔtoi ni wa lɛ ahe ni abuɔ loo aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ akagbee shi ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ akalaaje.

english: What happens to my vegetable farm when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds pull moisture out of plant leaves and soil very quickly. Adding a layer of dried leaves or grass around the base of your vegetables (mulching) helps hold water in the soil during this time.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ebɔle aduawai lɛ ashishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ahi sũ lɛ mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees catch leaf diseases when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ náa baai helai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, breeze cannot flow through them to dry off wet leaves after rain. Trapped moisture and warm air create the perfect condition for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni eha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better on the flat part of my land than on the steep hills?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ fe migɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertile topsoil and fertilizer from hillsides down to the low areas. Flat land holds onto both topsoil and rainwater much better.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ ashishi kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ nugbɔ nu fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when I plant them in the valley area during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Water gathers in low valley areas and stays there. Cassava roots need well-drained soil; sitting in flooded ground suffocates the roots and causes fungal rot.
ga: Nu lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ ni ehi jɛmɛ. Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko ta he ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Which crops are best to plant in the wet lowland areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like rice and sugarcane love lots of water and grow very well in wet lowlands, whereas crops like cassava and groundnuts prefer drier, higher ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei sumɔɔ hei ni egbi ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction I dig my crop rows on a hillside?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mikɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, digging rows across the slope (contour farming) creates small barriers that stop rainwater from washing away your soil and fertilizer down the hill.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋtayaai ni atsaa yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ. (Kontu okwaayeli) kɛ gbɛtsii nibii bibii baa. No baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ akafɔ oshikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: Should I leave big trees at the edge of my farm, or will they ruin my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa? Aloo tso lɛ baafite midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Trees on the boundary act as natural windbreaks that protect your crops from storm damage and soil drying, as long as you trim branches that block direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ ahum ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Shii abɔ ni obaafolɔ tsei niji ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ,

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my seeds when rain comes and goes unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni enɛɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Wait to plant until the soil stays wet for a few consecutive days after a heavy rain, rather than planting after the very first light shower which might be followed by a long dry spell.
ga: Mɛɛ ni odu kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii 2-3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, a duɔ mɛ ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi ɔ se, nɛ eko ɔ, hwɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ maa nyɛɛ se.

english: What can I do to keep my pepper plants upright when heavy storms hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko ni miitswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: You can tie your pepper stems to strong wooden sticks placed in the ground (staking) or pile extra soil high around the plant base to keep them supported against heavy rain and wind.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ pepper tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ (stakes) lɛ ahe loo okɛ sũ ni fa fe nine lɛ ato tso lɛ shishi koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when the soil holds too much water. Applying NPK fertilizer or compost restores nutrients and helps bring back healthy green growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji sũ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is tired and needs fertilizer or a rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he ejɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ awo mli?

english: Tired soil produces smaller crop yields, thin stems, and pale leaves even when rainfall is good. Adding animal manure, growing legumes like cowpeas, or applying mineral fertilizer restores the soil's strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛji nugbɔ kpakpa po. Koolooi ashishifãi ni akɛfataa he Ni aduɔ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo mineral fertilizers ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunshine and drying winds. Leaving controlled shade trees or intercropping with plantains provides living umbrellas that shield young cocoa until it is mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛ dumɔwui wo amɛmli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka baabu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by soil pests like nematodes or heavy winds. Supporting heavy stems with bamboo props and planting suckers in deep, rich soil keeps them standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ, ni aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting, curling up, and showing light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off the stems without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too hot, water supply is irregular, or tiny insects attack the blossoms. Mulching the soil and watering regularly helps plants retain their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Plant after two or three consecutive heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if the rain pauses.
ga: Dumɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield even when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your main crops can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting ensures your crop gets all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni akɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fresh peppers after I pick them a few times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei ni mikɛwoɔ mli shii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants pause fruit production if soil nutrients become depleted or if mature peppers are left too long on the stem. Harvesting mature fruits quickly and applying compost encourages continuous flowering.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kɛji akɛ ashi pepper ni eda lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop tiny holes and turn to powder inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔ sũ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Holes and powder in stored grain are caused by weevil pests feeding on dry seeds. Properly drying maize until it is fully hard and using airtight storage bags protects your harvest from insect damage.
ga: Bu kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli. Abele ni ooogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni okɛ vacuum storage bags tsuɔ nii lɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure around the roots will help restore their green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep dropping off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding excessive fertilizer during flowering will help the plants set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which usually happens when watering is uneven. Watering your crop regularly keeps the soil moisture stable so the plant can draw up calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and moisture to protect the seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop plants stay thin and weak when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to one another, the seedlings compete for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing seeds according to recommendations gives each plant room to develop strong stems, healthy leaves, and maximum yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsũ fɛɛ tsũ ni daa lɛ aná tsei ni wa, tsei ahe tsei ni wa, kɛ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on their leaves to produce food that feeds the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil, giving them full access to sunlight while protecting the foliage from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal applied fertilizers, root space, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot rapidly drains specific soil nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores natural nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi oya. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which target the inner funnels of young maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended crop protection products or natural solutions like neem extract can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe loo adebɔɔ mli tsabaai tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava signals maturity when its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a mostly bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the expanding tubers swell beneath the surface.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Trunk lɛ mli babaoo bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni dara lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or lack sufficient water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central funnels of maize plants. Applying neem leaf extract or sprinkling clean dry sand mixed with ash into the central leaves early on can suffocate and drive them away.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ neem baa mli nu loo okɛ ŋã ni mli tse ni egbi ni akɛ sũ efutu mli lɛ afɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. Ebaanyɛ eha mɔ agbɔjɔ ni ashwie lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of straight up in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant (about a 45-degree angle) allows the roots to spread out horizontally near the upper soil layer, making it easier for tubers to grow larger and making harvesting much less difficult.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ haa bulb wuji lɛ akwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, poor soil nutrients, or uneven watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost gives the plant the energy it needs to retain flowers and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I saved from last harvest are still good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ sa lolo akɛ adu?

english: Wrap ten random seeds in a damp cloth and keep it in a shady place for three days; if at least eight seeds sprout roots, your batch of seed is healthy and ready for full planting in the field.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui nyɔŋma ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ awo mama ni mli efɔ mli ni okɛto hulutsoo be mli gbii etɛ. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ dumɔwui kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui ni yeɔ emuu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to plant cowpeas during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas dislike excessive water; heavy rains can rot the seeds in the ground and spoil the seed pods when mature. Planting toward the end of the rains gives them enough moisture to grow while ensuring dry weather for harvest.
ga: Cowpeas sumɔɔɔ nu babaoo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efite dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of green leaves but only tiny fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai bibii pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive too much nitrogen or grow excessive side branches, they use all their food to make leaves instead of fruit. Trimming off small side shoots (suckers) forces the plant to send its energy directly into growing larger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo amɛyɛ niji babaoo lɛ, Yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ, tomato kɛ amɛ niyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai. Kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my yams under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Yams indicate maturity when the vines and leaves above ground naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing leaves and finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ eda beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my garden eggs curl inward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural self-defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce leaf area exposed to the hot sun, helping it conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Obaai ni oootsi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and maize help each other; beans pull nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil for the maize, while maize stalks give bean vines a strong structure to climb, giving you two crops from one land.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe. Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or its roots are waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps green up the leaves and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to focus on leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer tubers of cassava every year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji midu yɛ be ni sa mli po.

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients. Resting the land or rotating with leguminous crops like groundnuts restores soil natural fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe loo ni oootsake ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I pinch off the top growing tips of my pepper plants to get more pepper?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ koni maná pepper babaoo?

english: Yes, cutting or pinching the main tip of a young pepper plant forces it to grow side branches. More branches produce more flowers, leading to a higher harvest yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofo pepper tso bibioo ko naagbee titri lɛ loo okɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niji akwɛ̃. Niji babaoo woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmaa ni anáa babaoo.

english: How does sprinkling wood ash on my vegetable leaves protect them from insects?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso sũ ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ lɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe?

english: Wood ash creates a dry, irritating barrier on leaves that deters soft-bodied pests like caterpillars and beetles from eating the foliage, while also supplying minor potassium to the soil.
ga: Tso ashwishwɛ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni egbi ni haa mɔ mli fuɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye baai lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ potassium fioo ko hu baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does heavy rain cause my plantain trees to fall over so easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the topsoil. Excessive water softens the ground and heavy wind pulls down the top-heavy leaves and fruit bunches unless you prop them up with sturdy wooden sticks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu babaoo haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa baai ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui lɛ kɛbaa shi. Ja okɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack due to swelling tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa akɛni ŋmei ko ni efuu yɛ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting so quickly in my storage area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo shweremɔ oya waa yɛ he ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot in hot, damp, unventilated spaces, and they sprout when exposed to light and warmth. Storing them off the ground on raised bamboo racks in a dark, cool, airy barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves into tubes to protect themselves from losing too much water during the hottest part of the day. It acts like closing a window to trap moisture inside the plant.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa samflɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers when the hot January weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi beni January hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: High heat and dry winds cause extreme stress to pepper plants. To save energy and water needed to stay alive, the plant drops its flowers instead of spending resources to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa pepper tsei anɔ. Koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ ato. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛnibii baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants look limp and dead in the afternoon but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: During the hot day, tomatoes lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can pull from the soil. At night, leaf water loss stops and the roots catch up on drinking, making the stems firm again by morning.
ga: Yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ. ni shishifãi lɛ baaba ni amɛbanu nu. Ha tsɔne lɛ mli awa ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during dry weather to stop water from evaporating through the leaf pores. The plant rests until the rains return, surviving on nutrients stored in its tubers.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ ŋmei baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni abua naa yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ni akɛaafɔ̃ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorched at the edges in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that get burnt by direct sunlight and dry heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains grown nearby to act as natural umbrellas while their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ la ni mli egbi lɛ shãa amɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dried grass around the base of my crops help them survive the intense sun?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Dried grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil that blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the root zone cool, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly, and protects shallow roots from baking.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are my green tomato fruits developing hard, white, dry patches on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli wa, eyɛŋ, ni egbiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ?

english: This is sunscald, which happens when intense, direct sunlight overheats the exposed fruit skin and destroys the tissue underneath, similar to a sunburn on human skin.
ga: Enɛ ji hulutsoo he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kpɛ aduawai ahewolo ni edɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ. ni efiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ Etamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to pour water directly over my crop leaves in the middle of a hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Water droplets sitting on leaves under bright sunshine can trap intense heat and burn the leaf surface. Additionally, much of the water evaporates into the hot air before reaching the soil roots.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baa nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni eshã baa lɛ hiɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why did my crops burn and dry out after I applied fertilizer during a hot, dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is made of salts that require plenty of ground moisture to dissolve safely. Applied in dry soil, the fertilizer sucks water out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, causing the leaves to dry up.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni biɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ feɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni egbi

english: Why do I see far more whiteflies and small insects on my vegetables during hot dry weather than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi babaoo yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures speed up the egg-hatching cycle of insects like whiteflies, causing their numbers to grow rapidly. Furthermore, heavy rains normally wash pests off leaves, so without rain, their populations expand unchecked.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ fɔɔ amɛhe oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oyayaayai. Kɛfata he lɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ Amɛyibɔ ​​baaya hiɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni baakwɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle intense, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava grown beside them to act as natural shade umbrellas and preserve soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. It is a natural defence mechanism the plant uses to conserve moisture until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing big fruits when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii wuji kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing big fruits or tubers, they waste energy stretching upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai loo bulbs lɛ Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la.

english: If too many shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Removing excess shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Heat and drought stress prevent the flower from getting fertilized, causing the plant to drop the blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ haomɔ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows leaves to make food, which is sent down to build large, healthy tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni he wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell beneath the ground if my cassava is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?
