english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a mostly bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni shishifãi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ateŋ babaoo eshwɛ kɛ hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as a natural fertilizer for crops planted afterward.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite Nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it better to give my crops a little water every day or soak the soil deeply twice a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli?

english: Soaking the soil deeply a few times a week is better because it forces roots to grow deep into the ground where soil stays moist longer, making the crop stronger during hot dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa.

english: If I weed and prune my cocoa farm properly, does that guarantee my trees will never get sick?
ga: Kɛ mijie jwɛi ni mifolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Ani hela mɔŋ mitso lɛ?

english: Good farm management makes trees stronger and more resilient, but it cannot fully prevent diseases. Pests like mealybugs or airborne spores can still carry diseases from neighboring farms onto your well-kept land.
ga: Okwaayeli nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa haa tsei lɛ waa ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Shi enyɛŋ etsĩ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mealybugs loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ anaa kwraa. Ekã he eji nɔ ni kɛ helai jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa hei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are catching a disease even when I am looking after them well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela lɛ emɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ mli kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po?

english: Look out for early signs such as yellowing leaf veins, swollen young shoots, abnormal red leaf color, or unusual dark spots on the pods. Checking your trees regularly helps catch infections before they spread.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ baa fãji ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii ni efuu, kɛ baa su tsuru ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ. loo ŋmeii diji ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ona helai dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Can a disease spread across my whole farm if only a few of my cocoa trees are sick?
ga: Ani hela ko baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei fioo komɛi pɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases can spread rapidly across large areas of land. Insects moving between trees or shared pruning tools can carry the disease from a few infected trees to hundreds of healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã hei wuji oya. Kplukai ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ loo amɛjaa nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie hela lɛ kɛjɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya tsei ohai abɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Does planting my cocoa trees too close together make it easier for diseases to attack them?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha helai srɔtoi aba. Ani ewaaa akɛ ooobote mli ni oye mɔ awui?

english: Yes, planting trees too close blocks airflow and sunlight. This creates a dark, damp environment where fungal and viral diseases thrive and spread easily from leaf to leaf.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli woɔ duŋ ni edɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni fungal kɛ virus helai lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa mlɛo kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ.

english: How big is a hectare of land, and how many cocoa trees can I fit on it?
ga: Te hectare kome da ha tɛŋŋ? Ni kookoo tsei enyiɛ manyɛ madu?

english: One hectare is roughly the size of a standard football field (about 2.5 acres). With recommended spacing of 3 meters by 3 meters, you can plant about 1,111 cocoa trees on one hectare.
ga: Hectare kome dalɛ tamɔ bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ (aaafee acre 2.5). Kɛji akɛ atsɔɔ akɛ okɛ mitai 3 x mitai 3 teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 lɛ, obaanyɛ odu aaafee kookoo tsei 1,111 yɛ hectare 1 nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and flowers when they start getting sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree is attacked by a disease, its internal system stops transporting food and water properly. The tree drops leaves and flowers to save energy and try to stay alive.
ga: Kɛ helai batutua kookoo tsei lɛ Emli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ kpaɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni akɛyaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do some areas of Ghana suffer more cocoa farm sickness than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana hei komɛi naa helai babaoo kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli fe hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Disease outbreaks depend on factors like tree age, weather patterns, local pest populations, and how close infected neighboring farms are. High humidity and older trees make certain regions more vulnerable.
ga: Helai gbɛfaŋnɔ damɔ nibii tamɔ afii ni tso lɛ eye kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Kuu lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ emɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ haa hei komɛi feɔ oshara waa.

english: What should I do immediately if I notice a group of sick cocoa trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ akuu ko yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should report the sickness to your local extension officer immediately and avoid moving tools or plant material from the sick area to healthy parts of your farm to stop the spread.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ hela he amaniɛ otsɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni oootsi kɛjɛ hei ni helatsɛmɛi yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he koni okpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: If I cut down diseased cocoa trees, can I plant new cocoa seedlings in that exact same spot right away?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ, Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait and plant shade crops like plantains first. Replanting cocoa immediately in soil where diseased roots remain can cause the new seedlings to get infected as well.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ adu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lolo lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba dumɔwui heei anɔ hu.

english: Are there chemicals I can spray on my cocoa trees to cure them once they get swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makɛshwie cacao tsei anɔ koni mikɛtsa amɛ kɛ́ amɛwo ŋmeii ni efuu?

english: There is currently no chemical spray that can cure swollen shoot disease once a tree is infected. The only effective control is to cut down infected trees to save the surrounding healthy ones.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni efu kɛji hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ pɛ. Nɔ pɛ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ ji ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves up to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛye baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks break and fall over so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when their root systems are weak or damaged by underground pests, or when seeds were planted too close together, causing the plants to grow tall, thin, and fragile while competing for sunlight.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite amɛ. Aloo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant my maize seeds with specific spacing instead of just scattering them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Proper spacing makes sure every single maize plant gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil without competing with neighboring plants for survival.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛhi shi

english: Why does rice need so much standing water to grow well compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice roots are naturally built to survive in waterlogged soil. Keeping water in the field keeps weeds from taking over and protects the plants from high heat during sunny days.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi lɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa jwɛi akaye nɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are some of my rice grains turning out light, white, and empty instead of full of food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ mli tse, eyɛ futafuta, ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ niyenii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty rice grains happen when the crop suffers from extreme heat or lack of water during the flowering stage, preventing the plant from filling the seed heads properly.
ga: Kernels ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo edumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does growing soya beans on my land make the soil better for other crops in the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Soya beans take nitrogen gas out of the air and trap it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant is harvested, that nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Soybeans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my soya bean crop producing plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybeans lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving soya beans too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves rather than flowering and making seed pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha soybeans lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni efee dumɔwui ŋmeii

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, trapping moisture inside and stopping water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: How can chicken manure from my poultry farm help my field crops grow big and healthy?
ga: Te tsina ŋmei ni jɛ mi kooloi akwɛmɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure is rich in essential plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus, which feed the beneficial organisms in the soil and give your crops quick energy to produce bigger leaves and fruit.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi amli tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus eyi mli obɔ. ni haa niyenii kɛhaa nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ Ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai wuji kɛ aduawai oya.

english: Why are my newborn crop seedlings rotting and falling over right at the soil surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings rot at ground level when the soil is too wet, creating an environment where harmful soil fungi bloom and destroy the soft stems of young plants.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow when the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize plants usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to grow strong and stay green, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore the leaves to a healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa ni ehi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔji ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or leaves around my vegetables help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-aduawai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you do not have to water as often, and stops weeds from growing and taking water away from your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ mli bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes, which means they can pull nitrogen out of the air and store it in small knots on their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground, providing free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot weather helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown waste inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant during the day to feed. Checking your fields early and applying recommended neem-based sprays or bio-pesticides early in the morning can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ neem spray loo bio-insecticide ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying the underside of the leaves with a mild soap solution or suitable insecticide will control the insects and protect new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi. Aloo, tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye kooloi lɛ anɔ ni ebu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava nearby creates a living umbrella that shields the young cocoa until it is tough enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can tell cassava is nearing maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem. To be completely sure, carefully dig around one plant base to inspect a root to see if it has reached a good size.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ebɛŋkɛ ni ebaakwɛ̃ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. koni ona nɔmimaa Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome shishi koni okwɛ shishifãi lɛ koni ona kɛji amɛdalɛ sa.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots around my plantain stem instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Plantain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: If too many shoots grow around a single plantain tree, they will compete for water, sunlight, and food, resulting in small fruit bunches. Keeping only the main stem and one strong sucker ensures the plant has enough energy to grow heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii, ni no haa aduawai bibii baa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni mli wa pɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ ŋmei ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and leads to bigger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ eshwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Removing infected plants early helps prevent the disease from spreading to the healthy crops on your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ye obua ni hela akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to uneven soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently watered helps the plant draw up the calcium it needs.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my lowland rice plants turning yellow after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in flooded rice often means the plants are lacking nitrogen or oxygen due to standing water. Draining excess water briefly and applying nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo oxygen bɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kuku Ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: No, planting maize seeds too close together causes the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving them proper spacing ensures every plant grows strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my seed yams take such a long time to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. If planted before this resting phase ends or in soil that is too dry, sprouting will naturally be delayed.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu dani hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ shɛ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ lɛ, shweremɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees drop flowers when exposed to harsh sunlight or intense heat without enough shade. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young trees so they can hold their blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe. Koni enyɛ ekwɛ fɔfɔi anɔ

english: My pepper plants have plenty of green leaves, so why are they not producing flowers?
ga: Mi pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ amɛfɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth without flowers is usually caused by too much nitrogen fertilizer. Reducing nitrogen and adding fertilizers higher in phosphorus helps the pepper plant focus on blooming and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni daa fe nine ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ baa. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ phosphorus ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pepper tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flower drop in cowpeas is commonly caused by tiny insects called thrips feeding on the blossoms. Inspecting flowers early and using recommended organic or chemical treatments protects the blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ okwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating small holes into the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ye bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-babi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's central funnel. Checking the funnels early allows you to apply treatments before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa awo mli dani nɔ ko ni naa wa aba.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy bunches, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main trunk with strong wooden props helps hold the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to insert my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the small leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots and shoots will struggle to grow in the right direction, leading to weak plants and low yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛi Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to heap soil into large mounds before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu shikpɔŋ agbo ko naa dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and soft soil so their tubers can expand downwards without meeting hard earth. Creating mounds loosens the soil, improves drainage so roots do not rot, and gives the yam tuber enough room to grow big.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ada kɛya shi ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ he. Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. improve drainage Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite Ni enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when they experience sudden water stress, like going from very dry soil to overwatering. This is the plant's natural response to protect itself during harsh conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ ni amɛyaa kɛyaa nu ni amɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni ekɛbuɔ ehe yɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii amli.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects feed on the leaves, they distort the leaf growth and stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Beni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main plant to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so that I can get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in tall, thin, weak crops that produce smaller fruits or grains than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell under the ground if my groundnuts are ready to be dug up for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akumɔ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and dry out. You can also dig up a few test pods; if the inside lining of the shell has turned dark brown or black instead of white, the groundnuts are ripe.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ test pods fioo komɛi hu atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eho.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to spread fertilizer right before a heavy rain begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertilizer from the top of the soil before the plant roots have time to absorb it. This wastes your money and can cause the fertilizer to wash into local water streams instead of feeding your crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Nakai feemɔ baaha ofite shika, ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii atsɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and lose moisture quickly. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key plant food responsible for deep green leaves and healthy stem growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni haa ŋmeii ni wa daa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too hot or water is scarce. The plant drops the flowers to save energy and water so that the main plant can survive the heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to stop water from escaping through the foliage. The plant goes dormant to protect its underground roots, and fresh leaves will quickly sprout once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Tsei yaa wɔɔ koni amɛbu amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for the roots. Training the vines up wooden stakes exposes maximum leaf surface to the sun, leading to much larger yam tubers at harvest time.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ atsɔse wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are my ripening tomatoes cracking open on the sides before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when water supply is irregular—such as heavy rain following a dry period. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to burst.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the specific nutrients that maize feeds on and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the soil. Rotating crops lets the soil recover and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ yeɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever there is a strong wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ baa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when root support is weak. Heaping soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) encourages strong brace roots to grow, anchoring the plant firmly into the ground.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ gbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni aaabɔle tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ) lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black, soft bottoms on tomatoes indicate blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. Irregular watering prevents the plant from transporting calcium properly from the soil to the growing fruit.
ga: Tomato ni shishi yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ naagbee efite, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛkɛ calcium ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the lower leafy side-shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Removing lower, extra shoots redirects the plant's food and energy away from unnecessary leafy growth and straight into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ adalɛ he. kɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why did my maize farm produce a huge harvest last season, but this season the cobs are very small even though I planted the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ? Shi be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa, eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Crop yields change because planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil. Weather shifts, irregular rainfall, and loss of soil strength over consecutive seasons can drastically reduce cob size if nutrients are not replaced.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ ejaaa. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ bei ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei lɛ dalɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ atsakeee niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ.

english: What causes my maize plants to turn yellow and stay short instead of growing tall and green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee kuku yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaves and strong stems. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds bought from the store perform better than the seeds I saved from my own last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in a lab for high strength, uniform growth, and pest resistance in their first generation. When you replant seeds saved from a harvest, they lose those special qualities, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo. shweremɔ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo ni teɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ du ekoŋŋ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baafite nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year when I don't leave it to rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Be ni mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Soil is like a bank account; crops take out nutrients every season. Without resting the land (fallowing), rotating crops, or adding organic compost and fertilizers, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed healthy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ shikatoohe akaunt. Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ daa be mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ (tillage) bɛ lɛ, tsakemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting beans with maize is actually beneficial. Beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger without fighting for food.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii akaŋ.

english: How does a long dry spell during the flowering stage affect my maize crop?
ga: Te be kakadaŋŋ ni hɔmɔ baa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baaná mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Flowering is the most delicate time for maize because that is when the cobs form. If the plants lack water during this stage, the silks dry out, preventing proper pollination and leaving you with empty or half-filled cobs.
ga: Be ni fɔfɔi fɔɔ lɛ ji be ni ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nakai beaŋ ji be ni ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Siliki lɛ baagbi. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ni eshiɔ bo kɛ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo fã ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to protect itself from losing water through evaporation during intense heat, signaling that the soil is drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbi.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn to powder and get full of holes after just two months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This destruction is caused by insects like weevils that lay eggs inside the grain. If the maize is not fully sun-dried until hard and stored in airtight bags or treated storage containers, pests will multiply and destroy the grains.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ahako ŋmãa lɛ mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli loo ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni afee he tsofa lɛ amli lɛ, Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I know that my maize grains are dry enough to safely store without molding?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abɛi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni ŋmeii akafee amɛ?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a kernel; if it cracks cleanly with a sharp sound, it is dry. You can also mix grains in a dry glass jar with household salt; if salt sticks to the glass, there is still too much moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo kɛ gbee ni tswaa lɛ, no lɛ egbi. Obaanyɛ okɛ shia ŋmei afutu ŋmaa ni yɔɔ glase tsinsii ni egbi mli lɛ hu. Kɛji ŋoo ba glase lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ mli lolo.

english: Why do grain prices fall so low right after harvest time, and how can I protect my income?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa jara baa shi waa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shika ni mináa lɛ he?

english: Prices drop because most farmers harvest and try to sell at the exact same time, creating an oversupply in the market. Farmers who dry and safely store their grains can wait a few months until supply drops to sell at much higher prices.
ga: Jara baa shi ejaakɛ okwaafoi babaoo kpaa ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. ni kɛ nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ Okwaafoi ni gĩɔ amɛŋmaa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛmɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Keeping or planting fast-growing shade trees like plantains protects them from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa plants are mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food maize plants need to grow leaves and stalks. Adding organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji abɛi tso lɛ niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai kɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil during growth. Legumes like groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for your next main crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them because the roots cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period before the main rains settle in. If seeds sprout after the first rain and then face weeks without water, the young sprouts will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ esa akɛ amɛkɛ otsii babaoo akpee ni nu bɛ mli. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat deep into the middle shoot of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on the leaves so the hatched caterpillars can crawl into the central shoot to feed on soft growth. Catching them early or applying recommended control methods prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛwui lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli kɛya tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye nɔ ni eda ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Aloo, gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the resources it needs to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb upward so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the root underground. Staking keeps the leaves off damp ground to prevent leaf diseases and allows the yam tuber to grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akɛtsi baai helai anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo

english: Why do my pepper plants produce fewer fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, their roots fight for space and food in the soil, and their leaves shade each other from light. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to spread branches and produce more flowers and fruits.
ga: Beni pepper tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ la lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha egbɛ eshwa ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before applying fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb them safely. Applying fertilizer to completely dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do crops grow differently when I plant them on a hill compared to flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔji anɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Soil on hilly land loses water and plant food faster because rain sweeps nutrients down the slope, while flat land holds moisture longer, causing crops on slopes to need different care.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ srɔtoi.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my crops when I farm on sloped land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni mitsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops in ridges across the slope rather than up and down creates small natural dams that trap water and topsoil, keeping your crops rooted and nourished.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ŋshɔi bibii ni hiɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shishifãi amli ni amɛná niyenii.

english: Is it good practice to clear all the big trees from my land before planting my crops?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ majie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Leaving a few trees provides gentle shade for sensitive young crops, keeps the soil cooler, and breaks strong winds that can snap tender stems.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aná hulutsoo blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni efite kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my young crops seem to struggle right after I clear fresh bushland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie sũ lɛ?

english: Newly cleared ground gets exposed to harsh hot sun and direct rain, which temporarily bakes the topsoil and strips surface nutrients until the ground settles.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaná he ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shãa ni ejieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does removing big tree roots affect the soil where I want to plant crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Te tsei wuji ashishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he hiaa yɛ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing large roots loosens the earth so root crops can expand easily, but it can also temporarily dry out the upper soil layer until organic matter is built back up.
ga: Shishifãi wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi baanyɛ alɛɛ mli mlɛo. Shi ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baatswa shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to divide my large farm into smaller sections instead of planting one single crop everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ majara miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli awo fãi bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu tso henɔ kome yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he.

english: Dividing your land allows you to manage water better, track pest issues easily, and match specific crops to the patches of ground best suited for them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ mlijaa yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ nu nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai lɛ amli oya ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi ato hei ni sa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know which crops to plant on different parts of my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mihei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Observe where water naturally settles and where the ground dries fast; water-loving crops thrive in moist low spots, while drought-resistant crops do better on high, dry ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hei ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ. Tsei ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be faaa yɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni egbi.

english: What should I plant if part of my farm stays wet while another part dries out quickly?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ madu kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli ewo nu yɛ be mli ni fã kroko hu gĩɔ oya?

english: Use the wet sections for crops like rice or leafy vegetables that demand water, and reserve the drier sections for crops like yams or legumes that dislike standing water.
ga: Kɛ fã ni efɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni he hiaa nu. Ni okɛ hei ni egbi lɛ ato kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes loo legumes ni sumɔɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi.

english: Why do crops in one section of my farm grow tall while the same crops in another section stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ daa kuku lɛ?

english: Soil depth and nutrient levels vary naturally across even small farms, meaning some spots have rich topsoil while neighboring spots may be rocky or thin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hei komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. yɛ be mli ni hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee tɛi loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt so fast during the hot afternoon on open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Open land without ground cover or shade tree canopy loses soil moisture quickly to the hot sun, causing crops to lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up.
ga: Hei ni agbele ni shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize plants growing tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants stretch tall and thin when they are planted too close together or lack sufficient sunlight and nitrogen. They waste energy competing for light rather than building sturdy stalks and healthy cobs.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛmiitswa la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and heat, preventing severe water loss.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha abɛi tsei koni amɛbu nu mli. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baa amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni nu akafite waa

english: What causes small holes in my young corn leaves and leaves a powdery dust in the plant center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ sũ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the leaf funnel of young corn plants to feed on tender leaves, leaving behind chewed holes and frass that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Eshiɔ buji ni atsɔ mli kɛ tsei bibii ni tamɔ tsei ni atswa lɛ.

english: Why do my soybean leaves turn yellow even when I water the field properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Soybean leaves turn yellow primarily due to a lack of nitrogen or poor root aeration. Soybeans rely on special soil bacteria to fix their own nitrogen; without these bacteria or proper soil drainage, the crop starves and yellows.
ga: Soybean baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ loo shishifãi lɛ amli kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Soybeans kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ sũ mli helai krɛdɛɛi anɔ koni amɛsaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my harvested soybean pods pop open and drop seeds on the ground before I can gather them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybean ni mikpa lɛ gbeleɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui woɔ shikpɔŋ dani manyɛ mabua naa lɛ?

english: This behavior is called pod shattering, caused by extreme heat and low humidity drying the pods too quickly. Harvesting early in the morning when moisture is higher keeps the pods closed until threshing.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ pod mligbalamɔ. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Kpaa nii lɛ leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Ha ŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni ashɛreɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my soybean plants starting to flower while they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni amɛji kukuji waa lolo lɛ?

english: Soybeans react strongly to day length and stress. If planted during periods with shorter daylight or under severe heat stress, the plant rushes to flower early to produce seeds before it dies.
ga: Soybeans lɛ tsuɔ nii waa yɛ gbi kakadaŋŋ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ he. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli loo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi oya koni ewo dumɔwui dani egbo.

english: How does planting soybeans on the same plot with my maize help improve my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybean ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Soybeans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in root nodules. When left in the ground, these roots decay and enrich the soil naturally, providing free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the stems and leaf edges of my young corn turn dark purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ tsei kɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ miitsɔ purple ni mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves usually indicate a phosphorus deficiency. This often happens in cold or waterlogged soil, which prevents the young roots from absorbing the phosphorus necessary for healthy early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi bibii lɛ aŋɔ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa kɛha mra be mli dalɛ ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Can I feed raw harvested soybeans directly to my livestock straight from the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha kooloi soybeans ni akpa lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Raw soybeans contain natural substances called trypsin inhibitors that block digestion in animals. Soybeans must be roasted or cooked first to destroy these compounds and make the protein safe for livestock.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ trypsin inhibitor, ni tsiɔ niyenii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi amli lɛ naa lɛ yɛ soybean ni ahoko lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ashã soybeans loo ahoo lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛgbala nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ amli ni eha protein lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha kooloi.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster than my main crop right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy, wild root systems designed to absorb moisture and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops a chance to establish roots without competing for food.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni afee koni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ená shishifãi ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii akaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has to the new top growth, causing the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa tsei heei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my field before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop seedlings and will steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, leaving your crop weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: How does digging channels or bunds in my field help my crops during rainy days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔ loo ŋtayaa ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Channels and bunds capture rainwater so it stays near your crops long enough to soak deep into the soil, while also preventing heavy rains from washing away your fertile topsoil.
ga: Funnels kɛ marshes mɔɔ nugbɔ nu koni ehi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie oshikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to water my crops in the cool evening instead of during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering in the evening allows moisture to stay in the soil overnight so roots can drink deeply, whereas afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate in the hot sun before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ahi shi nyɔɔŋ kome bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu kɛya shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaf, or a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely during flowering, or when insect pollinators are absent.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ.

english: What makes my cassava tubers stay thin and small even after a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers stay thin if the soil is packed too tightly for roots to expand, if crops are planted too close together, or if weeds were left to compete with the plants during their early months.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi koni amɛkɛ tsei abɔ akaŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing lots of big green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpea plants produce excess leaves instead of pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which encourages foliage growth over flower and pod development.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ baai krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni fe fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ he hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and humidity to protect cocoa plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ mli waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ripe when its color changes completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange, and it makes a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ebaaha gbee ni mli ewo muji aba kɛji akɛ ata he fioo.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves at the bottom to support new leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has a special ability to take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring its strength for future crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have very sensitive leaves that cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight. Shade trees act as a screen, keeping the temperature cool and preserving soil moisture so the seedlings can grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam vines produce energy for the underground tuber through their leaves. By climbing up a stake, the leaves spread out to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make more food and produce bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii babaoo ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa.

english: Planting seeds too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants with very small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large and produce a full harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewoɔ eyibii fɛɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots. Without air, the cassava tubers suffocate, and soil fungi easily enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafo. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baabote mli oya ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are small green worms eating the inside leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides deep inside the growing point (whorl) of young maize. They eat the tender leaves before they unfold, which can destroy the growing center of the plant if not managed early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ (rings) lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperatures are extremely high or when they suffer from irregular watering. The heat or water stress stops the flower from pollinating properly, so the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ faaa. Dɔlɛ loo nu mli haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slow even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that consume water and fertilizer much faster than your crops can. When weeds are growing nearby, they steal the nutrients you meant for your crops, leaving the crop weak and starved.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yeɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni oyɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ mɔ.

english: This is usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key soil nutrient, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away deeper than the roots can reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni mli kwɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow well in the first year but become weak if I plant the same crop on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi egbɔjɔɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Each crop feeds on specific nutrients from the soil, so planting the same crop continuously drains those specific nutrients and leaves the soil exhausted.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aya nɔ ajɛ mli. ni ekɛ sũ lɛ fite

english: What makes my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during wet seasons when air cannot move freely between densely planted trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya tsei ni adu amɛ babaoo lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant gets too much leafy food instead of fruit-building nutrients.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni akɛ baai babaoo haa tsei yɛ niyenii ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I cut down all the big trees on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under direct, harsh sunshine; they need protective shade from larger trees or plantains to retain moisture while growing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I put many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miŋɔ dumɔwui babaoo Ato dumɔwui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, leaving no single plant strong enough to yield large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa tsei komɛi bɛ ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I still need to clear weeds around my farm when my crops are already fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ lolo lɛ? Miŋmɔ lɛ Nɛgbɛ ji he ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and soil nutrients from under the ground even when crops are tall, which reduces the final size and weight of your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara po. Enɛ haa naagbee okpamɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much standing water during heavy rains, which suffocates the roots and encourages rot fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when river water overflows onto my farmland for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ faa mli nu ho kɛbote miŋmɔshi nibii amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air underground to breathe; when standing water covers the farm for days, the roots drown and lose their ability to take up food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu dɔŋŋ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my crops grow better than planting directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ni amɛduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of clear plastic or mesh that creates a protected room for plants. It keeps away heavy rains, direct scorching sun, and insect pests, allowing crops like tomatoes and peppers to grow faster, stay healthier, and yield fruits all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo mesh ni mli tse fee ni haa tsei feɔ he ko ni buɔ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ pepper lɛ daa oya. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni ofee nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from being fertilized. When flowers cannot form seeds, the plant drops them to save energy; growing tomatoes under shade nets or inside a greenhouse helps reduce this heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui Tsei shwieɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ trellis shishi loo yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: How can I protect my cabbages from caterpillars without spraying harsh chemical pesticides on the food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cabbage lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa waa lɛ efɔɔɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ?
