english: You can protect cabbages by covering them with fine insect netting or spraying a natural extract made from soaked neem seeds. Neem acts as a natural pest repellent that stops caterpillars from eating leaves without leaving toxic chemicals on your produce.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-cabbage lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni okɛbaahã nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛ neem dumɔwui ni akɛwo nu mli lɛ fee lɛ awo mli. Neem tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii aye baai lɛ ni amɛshiuuu tsofai fɔji yɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by heat stress. Mosquito-proof netting or greenhouse mesh blocks these insects from reaching your plants in the first place.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Mosquito netting loo greenhouse netting baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ otsei lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom parts of my sweet pepper fruits turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom of the fruit is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. It usually happens when watering is irregular, so keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops better than using only chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure by helping it hold water and nutrients longer, while chemical fertilizers only feed the plant for a short time. Manure keeps the soil rich and soft over many seasons rather than leaving it hard and dry.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii be kukuoo pɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ bei babaoo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs moisture before the hot sun dries it up. Watering late at night leaves wet moisture on the leaves all night, which encourages fungal diseases and leaf rot to spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ nu dani egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a nursery tray or small bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ tsɛnsii loo saatsoi bibii amli lɛ? dani amɛfã kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Young seeds are very weak and easily destroyed by heavy rain, weeds, or insects in the open farm. A nursery lets you protect young seedlings until they grow strong roots and healthy leaves, ensuring higher survival rates when transplanted.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, jwɛi, loo kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni agbele mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli.

english: Which vegetables grow fast enough to give me quick harvests to feed my family and sell at the local market?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ oya bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkpa oya ni amɛkɛye weku ko ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ?

english: Leafy greens like amaranth (gboma), lettuce, cucumber, and spring onions grow very quickly and can be harvested within 3 to 6 weeks. They allow you to produce food and generate income continuously on small patches of land.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli tamɔ spinach (gboma), lettuce, cucumbers kɛ scallions lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli, ni ehaa onáa niyenii ni okɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa baa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ.

english: Why do some of my vegetable seeds fail to sprout when I sow them directly into dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require continuous moisture, warmth, and oxygen to wake up and germinate. If sowed too deep or in dry soil, the seeds either dry out and die or run out of stored energy before their shoots can reach sunlight above the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ loo amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down our cocoa trees when they get sick instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ cocoa tsei kɛji hela mɔ wɔ moŋ fe ni wɔɔwo wɔ tsofa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain viral diseases, like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, live inside the tree's internal vascular system where sprays cannot reach. Cutting down and removing infected trees is the only effective way to destroy the virus and save nearby healthy farms from infection.
ga: Helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli lá fãji lɛ amli he ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ amɛ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpataa hela lɛ hiɛ ni ahereɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ hela mli.

english: How can I check my cocoa trees to know if they have swollen shoot disease before it ruins the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ koni mana kɛji amɛyɛ bud swelling dani efite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Look out for swollen stems or branches, red vein patterns on young leaves, and stunted or abnormally rounded pods. Recognizing these early signs allows you to remove infected plants before insects spread the virus to healthy trees.
ga: Taomɔ tsei akutsei loo niji ni efuu. Line tsuji yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. ni ŋmeii lɛ egbɔjɔ loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oyɔse nɛkɛ mra be mli okadii nɛɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ dani kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast on my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones, and thick shade traps moisture, helping the disease grow quickly.
ga: Fungs ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Ni shade ni mli tse lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do some cocoa trees stay standing and healthy on a farm while neighboring trees die from disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ gboiɔ yɛ helai amli lɛ?

english: Different cocoa trees have different genetic traits. Some natural varieties are naturally resistant or tolerant to specific diseases, allowing them to survive and yield fruit even when weaker neighboring trees get infected.
ga: Cacao tso fɛɛ tso yɛ fɔmɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai komɛi anɔ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai komɛi anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ po ná hela.

english: What is the main difference between the old cocoa trees our grandfathers planted and the new hybrid varieties available today?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei momo ni wɔtsɛmɛi lɛ du lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees take 5 to 7 years to start fruiting and grow very tall. Hybrid varieties grow shorter, begin producing pods in just 2 to 3 years, and produce higher yields per acre when properly cared for.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi ni amɛdaraa waa. Hybrid henɔi lɛ yɛ kuku. Amɛjeɔ pods feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods now compared to when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛ akɛto cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years of age, their biological processes slow down, and their root systems become less efficient at absorbing soil nutrients, leading to reduced flower and pod production.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛmli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: If my diseased cocoa trees are cut down, how soon can I plant new crops on that same piece of land?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo mi-kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu tsei heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ oya?

english: You should clear all remaining roots, let the land rest for a few months, and first plant temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava. Once the shade canopy is ready, you can safely transplant new, healthy cocoa seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi. Ni odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ efee klalo Obaanyɛ okwɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it important to keep big forest trees scattered on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooi babaoo egbɛ eshwã mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nɛkɛ?

english: Big shade trees protect delicate cocoa leaves from extreme sun heat, reduce wind damage, keep the soil moist during dry seasons, and drop dead leaves that decompose into natural organic fertilizer.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ehaa baai ni egboi ni fiteɔ kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight for nutrients and their leaves block out sunlight. This overcrowding creates high humidity that encourages fungal diseases and leads to smaller pod yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he akaŋ ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baa.

english: Why should I prune the branches of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches, allowing sunlight and air to flow freely through the tree canopy. This lowers humidity to prevent pod diseases and redirects the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi koni ekɛtsi pod hela naa, ni etsakeɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee pods wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to build strong, green leaves for making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa tree trunk keep falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani egbeeɔ shi ni edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients, or has not been pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Keeping shade trees and moisture in the soil helps keep these beneficial insects active and reduces tree stress.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii, ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but only forming thin, tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground. Proper balanced fertilizer helps direct energy to tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa tuber lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the heavy tuber underneath. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to light while preventing fungal diseases that spread on wet ground leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni tsii ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná la ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before the fruit even gets ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant continuously carry calcium from the soil up into the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and getting wrinkled like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these sap-sucking pests early stops the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees snap or fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani yibii lɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny pests like root nematodes or weevils can weaken their underground hold. Propping the stems with bamboo poles supports the heavy fruit load and protects the weak root system from strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii. Ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ shishi tsuŋwoohe lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei fĩɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebuɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize feeds and restores the depleted soil naturally for your next crop season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable bed in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb water before the heat of the day causes fast evaporation. Afternoon watering can burn hot leaves and creates damp nighttime conditions that attract fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ ni eha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ gbɛkɛ ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Why am I finding small ragged holes in my maize leaves with powdery brown dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ powder yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Ragged leaf holes and brown frass (dirt) are signs of caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying approved bio-pesticides or neem extracts early into the leaf funnel kills the caterpillars before they ruin the cob.
ga: Baai lɛ amli buji ni etse kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ (muji) ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ahe okadi. Akpɛlɛ nɔ mra akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu awoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni akɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How long will it take for my new coconut seedlings to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-ŋmei tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Depending on the variety you plant, dwarf coconut trees usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 10 years. Good soil management and regular weeding help them reach their fruiting potential faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ damɔ tso henɔ ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 10 lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why are some of my coconut trees producing small fruits while my neighbor's trees have very big coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii bibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ ŋmei wuji waa lɛ?

english: Fruit size depends on the specific seed variety planted as well as how well the tree is nurtured with soil nutrients, water, and weed control during its growing years.
ga: Yibii lɛ dalɛ damɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni adu lɛ nɔ. kɛ agbɛnɛ bɔ ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What kind of soil and environment do my coconut trees need to produce heavy fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ shihilɛ he hiaa mi ŋmei tso lɛ koni ewo yibii ni tsii?

english: Coconut trees perform best in well-draining soil with plenty of sunlight, good moisture, and adequate space so their roots can spread out and absorb nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulu la babaoo, hulutsoo kpakpa, kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do improved seed varieties yield more harvest than the seeds I save from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are bred specifically with strong genetics that give them the potential to resist pests, absorb soil nutrients better, and produce higher yields than traditional saved seeds.
ga: Akɛ fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa fɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety for the specific type of land I have?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties thrive in different conditions; you should match the seed's requirements for water, soil type, and sun exposure with the actual conditions of your farmland.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Esa akɛ okɛ nu, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa odumɔwui lɛ ato shihilɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do crops from the same batch of seeds grow differently across different sections of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ dumɔwui akuu kome mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Even with identical seeds, crops grow differently depending on local variations in soil fertility, water retention, shade, and how well each area was cleared and weeded.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji ekome moŋ, shi Dumɔwui lɛ daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsakemɔ lɛ nɔ. Te nu ni akɛtoɔ, hulutsoo kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: How does early nurturing of a young tree seedling affect its yield when it matures?
ga: Tsei bibii akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Te enáa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa?

english: Nurturing young trees by watering them during dry spells and keeping weeds away builds strong root systems early on, allowing the mature tree to reach its full fruiting capacity later in life.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei bibii anɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni mli wa aba mra. Enɛ haa tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli sɛɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to protect my newly planted tree seedlings from dying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu tso dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Providing temporary shade using palm fronds or planting fast-growing nurse crops nearby protects delicate young seedlings from scorching until their root systems are strong enough.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei tsu nii ni akɛha hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli loo adu nurse tsei ni shwereɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is regular weeding around the base of my fruit trees so important?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your trees for water and soil nutrients, effectively stealing the food your tree needs to grow healthy and yield full fruits.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ ni ejuɔ lɛ nɔ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers tell us not to plant our tree crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaf canopies overlap and fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to produce smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ woɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do I know the right month to start planting maize when the rain patterns keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ? Beni nugbɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana have shifted, so relying strictly on traditional calendar months can be risky. Instead of planting on a specific date, wait until the soil stays consistently moist after two or three strong rains, and consider planting early-maturing seed varieties that need less time to harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ miitsake. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ kusum kalanda nyɔji Strictly tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee oshara. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi asɛɛ, ni osusu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra ni heɔ be fioo dani akpaa lɛ he.

english: If the minor rainy season starts late in my region, should I still plant my crops or wait for the major season next year?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikpokpaa lɛ je shishi nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ madu nii loo mamɛ kɛyashi afi ni baa lɛ mli be ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting late in the minor season can cause your crops to dry up before harvest if the dry season arrives early. If you decide to plant, use short-duration or drought-tolerant crop varieties like cowpeas or early-maturing maize that finish growing within two to three months.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi dani akpa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba mra. Kɛji okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaadu Okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo loo ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa, tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do some cassava varieties take up to a full year to yield while others are ready in just six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different genetic growth cycles; fast-maturing varieties focus energy on bulking roots early, while traditional varieties take up to twelve months because they spend the first few months building strong stems and leaf canopy before filling their tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ bɔ ni fɔmɔ nii lɛ dalɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ srɔtoi. Henɔi ni daa oya lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛaato shishi mra lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kusum mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ heɔ nyɔji 12 ejaakɛ amɛkɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ maa tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ baai ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ dani amɛkɛ bulbs fataa he.

english: How can I tell if my field corn is completely ready for harvest, or if I should leave it for another month?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? Aloo esa akɛ mashi kɛha nyɔŋ kroko?

english: Corn is ready for dry grain harvest when the leaves and husks turn completely brown and papery, and a black layer forms at the tip of the individual kernels when you scrape them off the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ akpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛfee tamɔ wolo lɛ. Ni ŋmei diŋ ko baa ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa kɛ́ okɛshwie ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers instead of growing into peppers during the hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high during the sunny months, pepper plants experience heat stress and shed their flowers to conserve water and energy rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and droop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop and turn yellow during prolonged dry periods as a natural survival tactic to reduce water loss through their broad leaves, signaling that the plant needs supplemental watering or mulch around its base to hold moisture.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nu kroko loo abɔle ehe. shishitoo koni ekɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly in Accra's sandy soil even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Accra shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil in coastal areas like Accra has large particles that allow water to drain away rapidly rather than holding it around the roots. Adding compost or organic manure creates a sponge-like structure in the soil that holds water longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei tamɔ Accra lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni haa nu hoɔ oya moŋ fe ni eeetsi ehe kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko tamɔ sponji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ onibii amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow fast in the first month after planting but then stop growing before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpaa dalɛ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds contain initial stored energy to shoot up quickly, but after the first month, they rely entirely on soil nutrients; if the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus, growth stalls until fertilizer or organic manure is applied.
ga: Dumɔwui eto hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishijee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus lɛ Dalɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ nitsumɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baawo mli.

english: What crops can I plant that will keep providing food for my family continuously throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ koni maná niyenii ni yaa nɔ aha miweku lɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava, plantain, and sweet potatoes are excellent choices because they can remain in the ground and be harvested gradually as needed over many months, unlike grains that must all be harvested at once.
ga: Cassava, plantains, kɛ sweet potato ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ fiofio. Kpamɔ bɔ ni asumɔɔ yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ ŋmaa ni esa akɛ akpa fɛɛ shikome lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my harvested yams from rotting during the dry, hot months?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ akafite yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: To prevent rot, store yams in a shaded, well-ventilated traditional yam barn off the bare ground, and regularly inspect and remove any tubers showing soft spots so decay does not spread to the rest.
ga: koni akafite Too sweet potato yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ. ni okwɛ bɔl ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ mli daa ni ojie. Koni fitemɔ akagbɛ ashwã gbɔmɔtso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: My maize leaves are turning yellow and curling up—is there a medicine I can spray on my farm to fix them?
ga: Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe. Ani tsofa ko yɛ ni manyɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛsaa enɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize is either missing nutrients like nitrogen or being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. An extension officer can help identify if you need nitrogen fertilizer or an approved pesticide to spray early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miitutua lɛ. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni amɛna kɛji nitrogen fertilizer loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ he miihia bo ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi.

english: How do tiny white insects under my tomato leaves cause the whole plant to stop growing?
ga: tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo yɛŋ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tomato baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ aaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃?

english: These tiny insects are whiteflies. They suck the sap out of your tomato leaves like mosquitoes suck blood, which weakens the plant and spreads viral diseases that cause the leaves to wrinkle and stunt growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ. Amɛmuɔ tomato baai lɛ amli nu lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii nuɔ lá lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the plant stems and leaves grow very big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ dara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when cassava stems are planted upside down, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to swell the roots below.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Aloo be mli ni adu ŋmei tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ nɛ tsɔ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off the plant before they turn into actual peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebafeɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the sun is too hot and soil water is low, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save water and keep themselves alive. Mulching dry grass around the base keeps the roots cool and wet.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhe ahi wala mli. Mulch ni egbi ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my tomato plants when they are growing so bushy and well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cutting off small extra side shoots (called suckers) forces the tomato plant to send all its water and food into growing large, healthy fruits instead of wasting energy on useless green leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ohaa tomato tso lɛ tsɔɔ emli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛfeɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains or shade trees next to them acts like a living umbrella, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei bibii ni daa oya loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm. Even with rain, weeds aggressively suck up soil nutrients, fertilizer, and sunlight before your main crops have a chance to feed.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ kɛ ekãa shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la dani onibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest this year to plant again next rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni akpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Using saved hybrid seeds often gives poor yields because the second generation loses its strength. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures high yields and protection against common field diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ejaakɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ahe waaa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo ni atsĩɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa.

english: Is chemical fertilizer really necessary, or can my farm perform well with just good soil and rainwater?
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo ani miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ nu pɛ?

english: Every crop harvest takes nutrients away from the soil. Over time, soil gets tired and empty, so fertilizer puts essential plant food back into the earth to maintain healthy crop yields.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so fast while stored inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when cut during harvesting or stored in hot, dark spaces with poor airflow where rot-causing fungi thrive. Storing undamaged yams in a raised, well-ventilated traditional barn prevents spoilage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji afo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmei ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ to blema ŋmɔ ko ni awo nɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water. Nitrogen is the plant food that gives leaves their dark green color and energy to grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa ehiɛ su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛdaraa.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are putting energy into growing big roots under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants focus on their underground roots when they have healthy leaves but stop growing tall too fast. Avoid adding too much nitrogen fertilizer late in the season, as that forces the plant to grow bushy leaves instead of thick cassava tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛyɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ shi amɛkpaa shweremɔ oya tsɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ akwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a few become pods because they rely on tiny insects called midges for pollination. The tree also naturally drops extra flowers it cannot support with water and food.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ejaakɛ amɛdamɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ nɔ ni akɛfeɔ pollination. Tso lɛ hu shwieɔ fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi ni nyɛɛɛ nu kɛ niyenii atsu nii.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up and twist during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tomato leaves curl when the plant is trying to save water during hot, dry days, or when tiny insects like whiteflies spread a virus to the plant. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants from insects helps keep the leaves flat.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be mli ni tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves with caterpillar dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Small holes and dirt in the leaf funnel mean destructive caterpillars, like fall armyworms, are eating the growing center of your maize. Applying targeted control methods early into the central leaf funnel protects the crop before it gets destroyed.
ga: Bu bibii kɛ muji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ, tamɔ fall fluke lɛ. O-corn ni miida lɛ tsui ni ayeɔ. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Gbɛ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani efiteɔ.

english: Does my yam crop really need tall wooden sticks to climb on, or can it just grow along the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato lɛ biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ. ŋwɛi diɛŋtsɛ Aloo ebaanyɛ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves toward the sun. When yam leaves get full sunshine off the ground, they can produce far more energy to feed and expand the big yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛdu yam ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops produce less food when I plant maize in the exact same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt every year and allows soil pests to build up. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aku sɛɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on pepper fruits happen when soil moisture fluctuates wildly or when the soil lacks calcium. Watering your garden regularly without letting the soil dry completely stops this blossom end rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ pepper aduawai anɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ calcium bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo abɔɔ lɛ mli daa ni ohaaa sũ lɛ agbi lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ akpa kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have heavy fruit bunches and wide leaves, but very shallow root systems in the topsoil. Staking heavy fruiting plants with strong poles and mounding thick earth around the base keeps them anchored in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Shi shishifã ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Yibii tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa kɛ sũ ni mli tse ni bɔleɔ amɛshishi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa amɛshishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the open dirt around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni agbele ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering dirt with dried grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the roots cool, holds moisture in the ground longer, and slowly turns into organic soil food as it rots.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings drying up and falling off during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense, direct sunlight. Without shade from plants like plantains or temporary shade trees, the hot sun causes the leaves to dry out, turn brown, and drop off to protect the plant from losing too much water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ adɛŋ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi. etsɔ blɔfo ni egbee shi koni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to its newer top leaves, causing the bottom ones to fade to yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni amɛha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What causes the central funnel of my young maize plant to look chewed with green powder inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ powda eŋɔli ewo mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the hidden center of young maize plants to eat the soft growing leaves. The green powder is the worm's waste, and catching it early stops the caterpillar before it destroys the central leaf shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ. Pauda eŋɔli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii. ni emɔ lɛ mra Etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa dani amɛfiteɔ baa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Which way should I point the buds on my cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ aha tɛŋŋ kɛya ŋmei nine lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava stems should always be planted with the raised buds or leaf scars pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the new shoots to grow downward into the soil first before bending up, which wastes energy and weakens root development.
ga: Esa akɛ adu Yucca tsei lɛ ni ŋmeii ni ewó nɔ loo baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkotoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔɔ.

english: What happens to my yam crop if I do not put stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ efɔɔɔ stake koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air on wooden stakes so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Leaving vines on the hot ground reduces leaf growth and exposes the leaves to soil moisture, which brings diseases and rots.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ tsei anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ kɛ helai kɛ gangrene baa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the young suckers keep growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only one or two leaves enough energy for the mother plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome pɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli Tso lɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni aaafolɔ ni akɛfataa he kɛ baa kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni tso nyɛ lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper roots turn soft and die when water sits on my farm after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When excess rainwater sits on top of the soil for days without draining away, it suffocates the roots and allows harmful water fungus to attack and rot the root system.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. When excess rainwater sits on the soil for several days without draining out. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. and allow harmful fungus in the water to attack and rot the root system.

english: Why is it dangerous to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated mineral salts that attract water. Placing fertilizer directly against a tender plant stem pulls moisture out of the plant skin, burning and damaging the stem tissue instead of feeding the roots softly through the soil.
ga: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated mineral salts that attract water. Applying fertilizer directly to plant stems draws moisture away from the plant's skin. Ekɛ shãa baa ni efiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Instead, it feeds the roots gently through the soil.

english: Why are my garden egg plants dropping all their flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, poor water supply, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to transfer pollen. Keeping the soil damp and allowing bees around the farm helps the flowers turn into healthy green fruits.
ga: Eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo he haomɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ ehiii. aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ baaya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ Fam lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help the soil make my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni mikɛbaakwɛ nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnut plants belong to a plant family that works with friendly bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut harvest is done, those rich roots decay and leave natural nitrogen fertilizer in the ground for the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei fata tsei aweku ko ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmei kpamɔ lɛ naa Nakai shishifãi ni woɔ yibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why should I water my young crops early in the morning instead of in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo midumɔwui lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to drink and absorb moisture before the sun gets hot. Midday sun causes water to evaporate too fast and can stress or burn hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nuɔ nu ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la. Hulu ni tsoɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. Ni ebaanyɛ eha nɔnyɛɛ loo baai ni mli edɔ lɛ ashã.

english: Can I apply strong solid fertilizer directly to my newly sprouted seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ anɔ?

english: No, newly sprouted seedlings have very tender roots that can easily burn from harsh solid fertilizers. Young plants need gentle nutrients dissolved in water or well-rotted compost until their roots mature.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã amɛ oya. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛwo nu mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why is it important to wet the soil before putting dry fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi afata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil can scorch plant roots. Wet soil helps dissolve the fertilizer gently so the roots can drink up the nutrients without getting damaged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops droop and curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants shrink or curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce surface area and cut down on water loss. As temperatures cool down in the evening, they usually perk back up.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi ni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when the farm stays flooded with water for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess standing water drowns the roots by cutting off their air supply. Without oxygen, roots cannot absorb the soil nutrients needed to keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know my nursery seedlings are ready to be transplanted into the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are ready when they have developed a sturdy stem, several full true leaves, and a strong root system that holds soil together, showing they can survive open field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛná tso ni mli wa, baai diɛŋtsɛ babaoo, kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni fiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Atsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli tse mli.

english: Why are my seedlings growing very tall and thin instead of broad and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miidara waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and grow thin when they do not receive enough direct sunlight. Moving them to a brighter spot helps them grow thick, strong stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee mlɛo kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: How do my crops take in nutrients from solid manure added to the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi tsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ mli?

english: Crops cannot chew or absorb solid manure directly. Water in the soil breaks down the manure and dissolves its nutrients so the plant roots can suck them up like liquid.
ga: Tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛye loo amɛŋɔ ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ. Nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbálaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ tamɔ nu.

english: Why shouldn't I spray liquid chemicals on my crops during midday sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Spraying liquid chemicals under direct midday heat causes rapid evaporation and can react with the sun to scald the crop's leaves. Early morning or late afternoon spraying is much safer.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hulu la lɛ afee ekome ni eha tso baai lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa.

english: Why do crops that grow well in one part of Asante Akyem perform poorly in another part of the same district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Asante Akyem kpokpaa kome nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpaa nɛɛ nɔŋŋ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Asante Akyem has two main ecological zones: the forest zone and the transitional zone. The forest area receives more rain and has cooler soil, while the transitional zone is drier and hotter, meaning crops require different planting times and care depending on where your farm is located.
ga: Asante Akyem yɛ bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe hei titrii enyɔ: koo lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ kɛ tsakemɔ he lɛ. Kooi amli hei lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo, ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ hu yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsakemɔ he lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ shweremɔ be kɛ kwɛmɔ srɔtoi. Edamɔ he ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm in the transitional zone dry out much faster than farms in the forest zone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ tsakemɔ he lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Transitional zones usually have lighter soil and fewer trees, allowing sunlight and wind to dry out the ground quickly. Forest soils have more fallen leaves and tree shade, which help trap water in the ground for much longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee kɛ tsei fioo pɛ yɔɔ hei ni tsakemɔ baa lɛ. Ehaa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Koo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ baai babaoo kɛ tsei ahe hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the minor rainy season starts around October?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ October aaafee lɛ?

english: You should plant immediately after the first steady rains begin in October. Planting early allows your crops to use all the moisture in the soil before the short rainy season ends and the intense dry season takes over.
ga: Esa akɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ October mli lɛ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ baa naagbee ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ yeɔ esɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I delay planting until late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔ lɛ to sɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee?

english: If you plant too late, the rains will stop while your crops are still young. Without enough water in the soil, the plants will struggle to grow, drop their flowers, and may die before you can harvest anything.
ga: Kɛji odu nii sɛɛ tsɔ Nugbɔ lɛ baakpa be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba akɛ ebaada. fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ egbo dani obaanyɛ okpa nɔ ko.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my farm land weeks before the rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni masaa he otsii komɛi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early ensures the very first rain sinks straight into soft, weed-free soil. If you wait to clear land after it rains, you lose valuable growing days when the soil moisture is at its best.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji omɛ ni ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Obaafite dumɔwui gbii ni jara wa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Crops roll up their leaves to expose less surface area to the hot sun, which stops water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly when the soil is dry.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli bɔni afee ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe fioo. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ ajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop producing flowers when the weather gets too dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔii feemɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences water stress from heat, it enters survival mode. It saves its limited energy and moisture to stay alive rather than spending energy on producing flowers or fruit.
ga: Kɛji tsei na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔii loo aduawai afeemɔ mli lɛ

english: Can I plant the exact same variety of maize in both forest areas and transitional areas?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa srɔtoi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ koo mli kɛ tsakemɔ hei fɛɛ?

english: It is better to use different varieties. Drier transitional areas need fast-maturing or drought-tolerant maize seeds because the rainy window is shorter, while forest areas can support varieties that take longer to mature.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ henɔi srɔtoi baatsu nii. Tsakemɔ hei ni mli egbi lɛ biɔ abele dumɔwui ni daa oya loo nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, samflɛ ni akɛnaa nugbɔ lɛ yɛ kuku. yɛ be mli ni hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa henɔi ni heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Should I leave some large trees standing when clearing my farm, or should I cut everything down?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni amɛdamɔ shi beni mijieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mafo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli?

english: Leaving a few tall trees helps shade young plants from harsh sun and reduces strong winds. This shade keeps the soil cool and slows down how fast water evaporates from your farm.
ga: tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ fioo komɛi to lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: What simple step can I take to protect my soil from losing water during a dry spell?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni mabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ he?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry leaves, straw, or farm waste (called mulching) acts like an umbrella. It blocks direct sunlight from hitting the earth and keeps the soil damp for a longer time.
ga: Akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔ mli jwɛi baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. (Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch and dry out under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural protective canopy and retains soil moisture during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow starting from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves inward along the center vein is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize requires plenty of nitrogen to build healthy green foliage, and applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore plant vigor.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa mli kɛtsɔɔ tsitsi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should the small buds face when I plant cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava stem buds must point upward toward the sky when buried at an angle. Placing them upside down causes the new sprouts to twist underground to reach sunlight, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui heei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly. Regular watering at the root zone and applying mulch keeps the roots cool and helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ ahe daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi yibii lɛ baawo.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from an old farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for maidenhead or sword suckers with narrow, needle-like leaves and a broad bulbous base. These suckers store more energy reserve than water suckers with wide leaves, allowing them to establish roots faster and produce stronger stalks.
ga: Taomɔ oblayoo bulbs loo klante ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ bulb shishi ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ suckers nɛɛ toɔ hewalɛ babaoo fe suckers ni yɔɔ wide-blade lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛ feɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛ haa tsei ni wa.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce long leaf canopy systems that need direct sunlight to produce food energy. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing the leaves to light while protecting them from rot and soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ baai ni biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa la yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and twisting like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by microscopic sucking pests like thrips or aphids hiding underneath the leaves. Controlling these tiny insects prevents virus transmission and allows new leaves to uncurl naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. small insect control Enɛɛmɛi baaye abua ni atsĩ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa ni eye ebua ni baai heei lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is my maize harvest getting smaller every year even though I plant on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? ni midu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Growing maize continuously on the same plot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your maize crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally replenishes nitrogen into the soil and restores fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ daa be. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ Ekɛ nitrogen baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ŋmãa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does lowland rice need standing water around its stem while maize roots rot in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔleɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have special air passages inside their stems that carry oxygen down to roots underwater. Maize roots lack these internal tubes and suffocate when soil stays submerged for extended periods.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bote nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the low branches touching the ground on my cashew trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ yɛ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches improves air movement around the tree trunk and prevents fungal spores in the soil from splashing onto lower leaves. It also encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing higher branches that yield more nuts.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ amɛhe lɛ yaa hiɛ. tso lɛ shishi ni etsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ewoɔ tso lɛ hu hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ aya niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and rapidly dries out root moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees around them creates a protective canopy that keeps them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ gĩɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo be kukuoo mli shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ehaa shade ni haa ohe feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ohe jɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when heavy waterlogging damages the roots. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted compost helps restore leaf color and improves overall plant growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ nu ni fa babaoo fite shishifãi lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings in the soil to get big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ tɛŋŋ koni maná ŋmeii wuji?

english: Spacing cassava cuttings about 1 meter apart gives the roots enough underground room to expand without competing with neighboring plants for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ateŋ aaafee mita kome, ni oha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: What is making small holes in my corn leaves and leaving brown dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni ashi muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, a caterpillar pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves of corn. Checking fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf center helps control them before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ amɛ dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas alongside my main crop helps my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural nodes on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer, leaving the soil richer for neighboring crops and future planting seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the wet ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for big tubers, while also protecting the foliage from fungal diseases that thrive in ground moisture.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha bulb lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, dry spells, or a lack of key nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant maintain stable temperatures to retain its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ mli. Kɛ́ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of my soil help my vegetables grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops sunlight from evaporating soil moisture quickly. It also keeps the roots cool and decays over time into rich organic matter.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo.

english: Should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces them to steal nutrients and water from the main bearing tree. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Is it safe to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until rains become regular and wet the soil deeply. The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry stretch that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds before the main rains settle in.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong direct sunlight and high heat. Keeping shade trees or intercropping with plantains protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps the soil retain moisture so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo okɛ plantains wo mli lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.
