english: Will cutting off branches from my cocoa tree reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo tso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing extra or weak branches allows sunlight and air to reach the inner parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa tree drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ gbee shi ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they lack water, nutrients, or tiny pollinating insects called midges. Keeping soil healthy and avoiding harsh chemicals that kill helpful insects will help more flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. You can reduce it by pruning branches to let in air and sunlight, and by harvesting ripe pods promptly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ oba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni oookpa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on the young maize leaves, but you can manage them by inspecting crops early and applying neem seed extract or recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Shi obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and look wilted during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves roll up to trap moisture and protect the plant from drying out in intense heat. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps keep the roots cool and wet.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu tso lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without yielding much when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong roots and yield more food.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing around my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Too many suckers growing from the same base steal food and water from the main plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishitoo kome mli lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ baawo plantain tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots develop dark lines and spoil within a few days of harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly once dug up because exposure to air causes rapid chemical breakdown. It is best to harvest cassava only when you are ready to use, sell, or process it into gari or flour.
ga: Kɛ́ atsa cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛgboi oya ejaakɛ kɛ́ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ŋmei pɛ kɛji ofee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii, okɛhɔ̃ɔ, loo okɛfee gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential food for growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure restores the green color and keeps the plants strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, prolonged dry spells, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Maintaining good shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps the flowers set into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa ba amɛnɔ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuamɔ. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting, curling up, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe, ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which can also pass viruses to the crop. Spraying with neem oil or suitable insect control early prevents the leaf damage and stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu Mra ni akɛ neem fɔ loo kooloi bibii ni sa baashwie nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite baa lɛ ni ekpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them in soaked soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain off easily, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my soil better for the next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes pull nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay in the dirt, they release this natural fertilizer, which feeds the maize and enriches the soil.
ga: Ajieɔ Nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ŋmãa niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable beds with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the roots cool, conserves soil moisture, and eventually turns into rich food for the soil as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebatsɔ niyenii ni baa nii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Does it really make a difference if I do not stake my yam vines with wood?
ga: Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mikɛ tsei etswaaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to feed and grow big tubers below ground. Leaving vines on the wet soil leads to leaf rot and much smaller harvests.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbo ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why am I advised to cut off some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots, or suckers, to grow creates competition for water and nutrients with the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers directs energy back into the mother plant, resulting in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ baa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: What is eating small holes through the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Holes in the central growing funnel of young maize are a primary sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying targeted treatments or applying clean sand or ash directly into the funnel kills the pest before it destroys the plant's growing point.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmãa lɛ he okadii titri. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ shwie nɔ loo ŋã loo sũ ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani ebaanyɛ efite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of leaves and blossoms, but no fruits are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer makes tomatoes grow thick, leafy stems at the expense of fruit development, while extreme heat can dry up pollen before flowers are fertilized. Balancing fertilizer application and keeping soil moisture consistent encourages the flowers to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato lɛ aná baai ni mli edɔ kɛ aduawai ni efite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi dani fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which acts like main food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally fertilizes your field, saving you money on chemical fertilizers while improving soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ shika toɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be kome too mli. kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry chemical fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat dry fertilizer; they can only drink nutrients dissolved in water. Placing chemical fertilizer in dry soil can scorch and burn your crop's roots instead of helping them grow.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod Disease, which spreads easily in cool, damp, shaded weather. Clearing weeds, pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight in, and applying approved fungicides help protect your cocoa harvest.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la aba Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants look like they were chewed up with powdery dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ sũ ewo amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This destruction is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the plant's central leaves during the day. Applying appropriate control measures early in the morning or late evening when the worms emerge to feed helps kill them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛbaaye nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of straight down into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanted angle allows the roots to grow near the loose topsoil layer where nutrients and moisture are easily reached. This encourages the plant to produce a larger cluster of thick tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etsilɛ lɛ he. ni yɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he mlɛo Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do we need to make high soil mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down deep into the earth as they mature. Making high, soft mounds loosens the hard soil so the tubers can expand smoothly into large, healthy roots without hitting tough ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shishifãi wuji ni mli wa lɛ amli mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During very hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can pull it from the ground, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant. As long as they recover by evening, the plants are healthy, but spreading dry grass (mulch) around the base keeps the soil cooler.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu tso lɛ he. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi lolo. Shi jwɛi ni egbi (Mulch) ni akɛbaawo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought stress. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing shade during hot afternoons helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast on my farm even after I carefully clear them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie amɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping underground for years waiting for sunlight and rain. When you clear or dig the field, you bring buried seeds to the surface where they sprout quickly, which is why covering the soil with mulch or shade crops helps suppress them.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ akã shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ. Kɛji otsi ŋmɔ mli loo otsa ŋmɔ mli lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni jwɛi loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛtsi nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my coconut trees drop their tiny green fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada?

english: Coconut trees often drop young fruits due to water stress, lack of essential soil nutrients like potassium, or sudden weather changes. Ensuring proper watering and balanced feeding helps the tree hold onto its nuts until maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Nibii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni sa baaye abua ni emɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: What is the main difference between dwarf coconut trees and the tall ones?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso bibioo kɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ teŋ?

english: Dwarf coconut trees produce fruit much earlier—usually within 3 to 4 years—and stay short for easy harvesting, while tall coconut trees take 6 to 8 years to fruit but generally live longer and tolerate poor soil better.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ baawo yibii mra kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni amɛbaakã he amɛhi shi koni akpa amɛ mlɛo. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruits are ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: An oil palm bunch is ripe when its color turns deep orange-red and a few individual ripe fruits naturally break loose and fall to the ground around the base of the palm.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli kwɔ. Ni aduawai komɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baagbala amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Leaves curl up in intense sunlight as a natural survival reaction to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which helps the plant conserve moisture and stop from drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo nɔ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he ni dɔlɛ baa lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of leafy branches but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing stems and leaves instead of flowering. Adding phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to produce blooms and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sun. They need shade trees like plantains to shelter them while their root system and canopy establish during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ maa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around the base of my crop plants help them grow better?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves—known as mulching—keeps the root zone cool, locks in soil moisture during dry spells, stops weeds from growing, and slowly decays to add rich nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, forcing them to stretch upward quickly and remain weak rather than building thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leaves on top look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ eŋɔli?

english: If the soil underground is packed too tightly or contains excessive nitrogen, the cassava plant directs its energy toward growing top foliage instead of pushing outward to swell its root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo tsi lɛ kɛ ya kpo nɔ konɛ sisifã ɔ nɛ bli.

english: What causes the lower leaves of my coconut palms to turn yellow and die off early?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-koko lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya?

english: Premature yellowing of lower palm leaves is usually a sign of nutrient deficiencies in the soil, root damage from waterlogged ground, or early symptoms of diseases like Lethal Yellowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi. loo hela lɛ he okadii ni jeɔ kpo mra, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbeɔ mɔ

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or urea early gives the crop the food it needs to turn deep green and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my rice plants staying very short and turning an orange-yellow color in the flooded field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ efee kuku ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Orange-yellow leaves and stunted growth in swampy rice fields often happen when the soil has too much iron toxic to roots, or lacks zinc. This suffocates the root system, preventing the plant from taking up water and food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dade ni gbeɔ shishifãi lɛ fa babaoo loo zinc faaa. Enɛ baaha shishifã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often dries out quickly, leaving the hot soil thirsty again within days. Seeds need continuous moisture over several days to germinate safely, so planting after rains become regular prevents the seeds from drying out and dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni kumai yeɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná nu ni mli edɔ daa gbii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and drop off when I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa mihe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially when young, cannot survive harsh direct sunlight for long periods. Big shade trees protect the cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keep the soil moist so the cocoa plant stays healthy and cool.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ kɛ́ amɛdarako lɛ, nyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni kookoo tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller and smaller every year on the same stem group?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ ŋmeii akuu kome mli lɛ?

english: A plantain plant produces too many young shoots (suckers) that fight with the main plant for food and water in the soil. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the plant to produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui woɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ ni kɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before the fruit ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes (blossom-end rot) happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering is irregular or the dry season soil dries out too quickly between rainfalls.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ Blossom tip rot (blossom end rot) baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and maintaining good watering helps the plant hold its blossoms to make fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ, ni okɛ nu kpakpa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do tiny insects swarm and destroy my cowpea flowers as soon as they open up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet scents that attract pests like thrips, which eat the inside of the flower and stop pods from forming. Protecting the farm with early organic or safe pest control right as flowers start to open ensures good pod yield.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips, ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛkpaa pod lɛ feemɔ. Akɛ mra be mli, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔji ahe loo shweshweeshwe be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ Ebaaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than their small roots can drink it from the soil. Providing shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow stronger roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni enyɛ enu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni akɛhaa tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, so adding nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves and passing on viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava stems when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the roots enough room underground to swell into large, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival instead of spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifee mitso titri lɛ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures that your main crops get all the nutrients they need to grow tall and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often cools the surface, but the soil deep down may still be dry. If a dry spell follows that initial rain, your germinated seeds will dry up and die before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Shi ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Kɛji hɔmɔ ahum ko nyiɛ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, drying up moisture and stopping the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as slow-release food for your crops and improves the soil's structure, allowing it to hold onto water longer during dry days.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ blɛoo kɛhaa onibii. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Small suckers drain water and food away from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree has enough strength to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suction cup bibioo ko jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How long does a coconut tree take from the day I plant it until it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko woɔ yibii?

english: Depending on the variety, dwarf coconut trees can start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while tall varieties usually take 6 to 10 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni amɛji srɔtoi lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when I want to plant a new coconut seedling?
ga: Kɛ́ oosumɔ ni odu ŋmei tso hee lɛ, te esa akɛ akumɔ bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Dig a hole about 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep. Mixing the topsoil with compost or well-rotted manure before placing the seedling helps the young roots spread easily and grow strong.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee ninetalɔi enyɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi enyɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ futu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that they are receiving too much or too little water. Adding well-rotted compost or fertilizer usually helps them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to put fresh animal manure directly around my plant roots to help them grow?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei baabɔle he? Ekɛ mi tsei lɛ shishifãi tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: No, fresh animal manure generates high heat and strong chemicals as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots. It is best to let manure rot and turn into cool compost before applying it to crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ tsofai ni mli wa baa kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ejɔ dani akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Plants conserve moisture during the hottest part of the day by closing tiny pores on their leaves, causing them to curl or droop. They usually bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Tsei buɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛŋaa lɛ nɔ, ni no haa amɛkpãa loo amɛshwieɔ shi. Bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔ pɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to place cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem. Plant the stem into the ground with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots grow properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ Dumɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do coconut trees need so much space between them when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ, ehe hiaa ni amɛteŋ gbɛ babaoo ahi shi lɛ?

english: Coconut trees grow very wide fronds and large root systems. Giving them 8 to 9 meters of space ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and nutrients to yield plenty of coconuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ shishifãi wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 8 kɛyashi 9 ha lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmei babaoo.

english: What causes black spots and a sticky substance on the underside of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ kɛ nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baa?

english: This is usually caused by small insects like aphids or mealybugs feeding on the plant sap. They secrete a sticky substance that attracts mold, which weakens the plant if not controlled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni gbalaa ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Do my young crop seedlings need to be watered every day during the dry season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young seedlings need moisture, but watering deeply 2 to 3 times a week is better than light daily watering. Deep watering encourages roots to grow deep into the soil where water lasts longer.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ. Shi nu ni oooha lɛ shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi lolo fe nu ni oooha lɛ fioo daa gbi. Nu ni awoɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni nu baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no trees above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tso ko bɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Without shade trees like plantain or forest trees to shield them, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it from the ground, causing them to burn and yellow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo kooi ni buɔ wɔhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the bare soil around my young plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, protects the ground from the direct hot sun. This keeps the soil cool and stops soil water from evaporating, allowing your plant roots to stay hydrated longer.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and fail to grow tall if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛɛɛ shɔŋŋ kɛji midu lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds germinate during this fake start to the rainy season, the young roots quickly dry out in the thirsty soil, causing the seedlings to turn yellow and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui kwɛ̃ yɛ amale shishijee ni yaa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kumai yeɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around a mother plantain, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves all the food for the main stem, resulting in larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cassava produce very big, bushy green leaves but small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi agboi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava spend all its energy growing leaves above ground rather than storing food in its underground tubers. Balanced soil nutrients are needed for good root growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ he miihia koni shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer burn my crops if I apply it when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve safely. When applied to dry soil, the concentrated salts pull water out of the crop's roots instead of feeding them, causing the roots and stems to burn.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shãa.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up tightly and feel sticky when I touch them?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni enuɔ he akɛ ekpɛtɛɔ he kɛji ota he?

english: Curled, sticky pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. As they feed on the leaf juice, they release a sticky waste that curls the leaf.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Amɛjieɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi. kpo, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in the middle of my maize leaves with stuff that looks like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu bibioo ko lɛ? ŋmãa baa teŋ Ani ŋmãa yɛ mli?

english: Small holes with sawdust-like waste are a clear sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the fresh growing center of the maize stem. Treating the farm early prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Buji bibii ni sũ ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni miikwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ateŋ. Okwaafoi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale even if the weeds are not tall enough to block sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, jwɛi lɛ etsɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni baatsi hulu lɛ naa.

english: Even short weeds have underground roots that spread quickly and steal water, fertilizer, and space from your crop roots long before they ever grow tall enough to block the sun.
ga: Jwɛi kukuji po yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani amɛyaa ŋwɛi bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why does burning the cleared weeds on my field before planting hurt my soil in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away organic matter that holds water and plant food. While the remaining ash gives a small short-term boost, continuous burning leaves your soil dry, hard, and lacking essential nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa nibii ni hiɛɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo moŋ, shi shãa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewaa ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Maize pulls the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it continuously on the same spot drains those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ajɛ mli kwraa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for green leaf growth. It can also mean there is too much standing water around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekamu.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Pruning extra shade branches to allow sunshine and air movement around your cocoa trees helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Inspecting leaves early and controlling these pests prevents leaf damage.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo hela ko ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water with poor drainage, the roots drown from lack of oxygen, allowing soil fungi to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ shi, ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become extremely high or when the soil gets too dry. High heat and water stress prevent successful pollination, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ nu ni fa babaoo tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions and grow aggressively. They quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients ahead of cultivated crops, which is why early weeding gives your crops the space to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni amɛdaraa waa. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani tsei lɛ daa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of smooth and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, deep soil to push downward easily. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the tuber cannot grow straight. Tiny soil worms called nematodes can also attack the root skin and stunt growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwereŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifã lɛ hewolo kɛ edalɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to put my seeds into the ground after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Planting should happen only after steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil at least two or three times. Planting after just one light early rain can cause seeds to germinate and then wither when hot, dry days follow.
ga: Esa akɛ adu nii pɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi be mli ni gbii ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the field and waterlog the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔji amli ni ekɛ nu ewo tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Flowers often drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tsei anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo beni anáa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when soil moisture fluctuates too much, which prevents the plant from taking up enough calcium while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. They wilt temporarily to conserve moisture and usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: When maize is crowded, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak, thin stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack that crop to build up in your field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my vegetables help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents soil water from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem is good enough to be cut and planted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni adu?

english: Good cassava planting stems should be taken from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Use the thick middle portion of the stem where the nodes are close together.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli tse lɛ atsu nii yɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal the essential plant food, root space, and sunlight that your crops need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: When clearing my farm, should I scrape away all the dry grass and leaves or leave them on the ground?
ga: Beni miitsumɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: It is much better to leave dry leaves and grass on the ground. They act as a protective cover that keeps your soil cool, traps moisture, and slowly breaks down into rich plant food that feeds your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly after I burn all the cleared weeds and leaves on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni mishã jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ baai ni mijie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the healthy organic matter and good living organisms in your topsoil. Without this natural plant food, the soil becomes dry and weak, making it hard for your crops to grow well.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ko bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: If I have access to a stream or water source on my farm, can I grow crops continuously throughout the year?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ faa loo nu jɛɛhe ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, having a steady water source allows you to water your crops even during the dry season. This lets you harvest during off-seasons when crop prices are higher in the market.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu jɛɛhe ni oyɔɔ daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo oŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli po. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara ni jara nɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my soil dry up so quickly after rain, and how can I keep it wet for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast because the hot sun cooks it and evaporates the moisture. Spreading a layer of dry plant leaves or crop residues over the ground shelters the soil from direct heat and traps water longer for plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hoɔ lɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Tso baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ooogbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ebaaha nu ahi tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I prepare my farm to make sure vegetable crops survive the intense heat of the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ koni aduawai anyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Besides having a water source, you should cover the soil around your crops with a thick layer of organic mulch like dry leaves or palm waste to prevent the dry season heat from baking your plant roots.
ga: Kɛfata nu jɛɛhe ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ Esa akɛ Okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ palm shavings lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatsi fɛ̃i be mli latsaa lɛ naa koni ekaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: How can spreading palm kernel waste on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ŋmei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Palm kernel waste acts as an excellent soil conditioner. It retains moisture in the ground, prevents soil erosion, and slowly decomposes to feed your crops with natural nutrients.
ga: Palm kernel jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Etsiɔ sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha onibii lɛ.

english: Chemical fertilizers are too expensive for me; what affordable local materials can I use to build soil fertility?
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ kɛha mi. Mɛɛ nibii ni jara waaa, ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ manyɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can use cheap or freely available organic materials like dry farm leaves, palm kernel cake, and cocoa husks. Adding these to your soil improves its fertility, structure, and ability to hold water without high costs.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni jara waaa loo ni aheee nɔ ko tamɔ ŋmɔ mli baai ni egbi, palm kernel keeki atsu nii. kɛ kookoo ŋmeii Kɛ́ akɛ enɛɛmɛi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni shika babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Can covering my soil with dry leaves reduce the amount of time I spend weeding my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha be ni heɔ koni akɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, applying a thick layer of dry leaves blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds in the dirt. This prevents most weeds from sprouting and saves you time and labor on clearing.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ baatsi jwɛi babaoo anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebaaha be kɛ nitsumɔ akafite yɛ jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mli.

english: How does the strong afternoon sunshine affect my soil, and how do I protect my young crops from it?
ga: Te shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ sũ lɛ he?

english: Direct afternoon heat scorches bare topsoil, kills beneficial soil microbes, and steals water quickly. Covering the soil surface around young plants with leaves or organic waste shields the root zone from heat stress.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni ejuɔ nu oya Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: When heavy rain falls on my field, my topsoil washes away easily. What simple method can stop this?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Mishikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ hoɔ oya. Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ akpa enɛ?

english: Leaving plant residues or spreading mulch across your field breaks the force of falling rain. The organic cover cushions the impact, slowing down water runoff and keeping your topsoil in place.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ aba shi. Organic nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my papaya plants are male or female before they start flowering?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mipapaya tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo dani ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: When papaya plants are young seedlings, you cannot tell their sex just by looking at them. You can only identify their sex once they mature and produce flowers: male plants grow flowers on long, hanging stems, while female plants grow larger flowers directly against the trunk.
ga: Beni papaya tso lɛ ji dumɔwu bibioo lolo lɛ Obaanyɛ oyɔse bɔ ni amɛji lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛdara ni amɛwo fɔfɔi: tsei hii fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei kakadaji ni fĩɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ, yɛ be mli ni tsei yei fɔɔ fɔfɔi wuji ni teɔ shi woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Do I need to plant both male and female plantain suckers in my farm for them to bear fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu dumɔwui hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii?

english: No, plantain trees do not need separate male and female plants to produce fruit. Each plantain stalk develops its own flower bud that forms a bunch of plantains without needing pollination from another tree.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni agbala dumɔwui lɛ amli awo tsei hii kɛ yei amli koni amɛwo yibii. Plantain tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ efɔfɔi ni feɔ plantain kuu ni ehe ehiaaa ni tsei krokomɛi aŋɔ fɔfɔi awo mli.

english: Why do my young crop plants suddenly dry up and die a few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ gĩ trukaa ni egbo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants usually die because of soil fungal diseases like damping-off, insects attacking the roots underground, or planting too shallowly where the roots dry out quickly under the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Kplukai ni tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi Aloo dumɔ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even when there is enough rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from too much trapped water in the soil, preventing them from feeding.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi lɛ amli nu efo yɛ nu babaoo ni emɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ ana niyenii

english: How do crop diseases spread from one plant to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through rain splashes, wind carrying spores, infected seeds, insect bites, or dirty farm tools like cutlasses moving from a sick plant to a healthy one.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai, kɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kplukai ni ŋmɔɔ Loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee tamɔ dade ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: When is the best time of day to apply medicine or spray my crops against insects?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo akɛshwie kooloi anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon because insects are active, temperatures are cooler so the chemical won't burn the leaves, and there is less wind to blow the spray away.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo shwane. Ejaakɛ kooloi baatsu nii Temperature lɛ mli ejɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsofai lɛ haaa baai lɛ ashã. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛyaa lɛ faaa

english: Will applying more chemical medicine than recommended help my crops recover faster?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni awieɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya?

english: No, applying too much chemical can burn the crop leaves, poison the soil, kill beneficial insects like bees, and cause more harm than good to your harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ baai lɛ. Ekɛ tsofai fɔji baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni eyeɔ onibii awui fe nɔ ni ehi.

english: Are there natural ways to protect my crops from pests if I cannot afford chemical medicine?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli gbɛi komɛi yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛ tsofa fee hu?

english: Yes, you can use homemade sprays made from neem leaf extracts or hot pepper mixed with mild soap, clear weeds regularly, and rotate your crops to disrupt insect breeding cycles.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shia ni akɛ neem baa mli nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ efutu mli lɛ atsu nii. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. ni otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni ofite bɔ ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ.

english: Why are my crops giving a smaller harvest now compared to when I first started farming this land years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe beni mije okwaayeli shishi afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming removes vital nutrients from the soil every season. Over time, the soil becomes depleted or 'tired' unless you replenish it using animal manure, compost, or fertilizers.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo loo ‘egbɔjɔ’ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Is it bad to plant the same type of crop on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Ani eji tɔmɔ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Yes, planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know when an old crop tree on my farm has reached the end of its life and needs to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ amɛsɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee ni ehe miihia ni atsake amɛ?

english: When a tree produces very few small fruits despite good rains and fertilizer, shows major trunk decay, or frequently dries up, it has reached old age and should be cut down and replanted.
ga: Beni tsei woɔ yibii bibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ mli egbo waa. loo bei pii lɛ egbiɔ Tso lɛ hu miibote onukpayeli mli ni esa akɛ afo lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What should I do to prepare my land before planting new crops where old ones have died?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu tsei heei yɛ he ni tsei momoi egboi yɛ lɛ?

english: Clear away and burn diseased plant remains, add compost or well-rotted animal manure to rebuild the soil strength, and let the soil rest or plant legumes like beans first to restore nutrients.
ga: Jiemɔ tso ni hela emɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ni oshã. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he koni ekɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo odu ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or if they are just drying up from the heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo amɛmiigbi kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli?

english: Plants suffering from heat usually wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon and recover by early morning. If leaves stay yellow, show spots, or curl permanently even after watering, the plant is likely infected by a fungus, bacteria, or virus.
ga: Tsei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ po. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei, muawai, loo hela ko emɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to prevent your crop from getting this sickness.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to rot and turn black at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifite ni etsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛ po?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or overly acidic soil, rather than a chemical disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Yɛ tsofa hela ko najiaŋ

english: When my crops catch a strange sickness, should I buy any chemical spray I find or ask an extension officer first?
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Ani esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mina lɛ loo mabi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to ask an agricultural extension officer first to diagnose the exact disease. Buying the wrong chemical wastes money, can harm your soil, and might not cure the specific sickness affecting your crop.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko klɛŋklɛŋ ni etsɔɔ hela lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni ooohe lɛ baaha ofite shika. Ekolɛ ebaaye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui ni ebaanyɛ etsaaa helai pɔtɛɛ ni saa onibii ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots before they fully develop. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them protects them during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbiɔ shishifãi lɛ dani amɛdaraa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants often shed their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when they lack sufficient water. Giving them consistent water at the base and light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛmli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many thick, leafy vines but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing green leaves instead of flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii mli Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ he nii yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ashishifãi najiaŋ.

english: Yam tubers twist and struggle to grow large when the soil is hard, compact, or filled with stones. Making high, soft soil mounds allows the tubers to expand freely underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi agbo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi amɛhaa amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize stalks break easily and fall over before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks often break because stem-borer insects eat the inside of the stems, or because the soil lacks potassium, which gives plants the strong structure they need to stand tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa ejaakɛ kooloi yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mligbɛ. aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium hewɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ he wa ni ekɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I plant at the right time during the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Soil loses its nutrients over time when the same crop is planted year after year without adding compost, manure, or rotating with crops like beans that naturally put nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ kɛji adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps bring the green color and growth back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia otso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get all the fertilizer and water you give them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni okɛhaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when heavy rainwater sits on the farm without draining away, allowing soil diseases to attack the tubers. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water flow away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nu babaoo eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ atutua bulb lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?
