english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects sucking the juice out of the leaves. Spraying an approved crop medicine or neem water clears the insects so new, healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ tso tsofa loo neem nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my young vegetable seedlings falling over and dying right at the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil stays too wet and seeds are planted too close together, allowing fungal rot to attack the thin stems. Spacing your seeds well and avoiding overwatering keeps the stems dry and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji rot lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei bibii lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhe awa.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree suffers from dry weather, lacks nutrients, or is not pollinated by tiny insects. Keeping shade trees on the farm and watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay on to become pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔi efɔɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni awoɔ amɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing many flowers but no tomatoes are showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi tomato ko bɛ lɛ?

english: High heat, lack of water, or giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer can cause tomato flowers to drop before forming fruit. Watering regularly at the base and reducing strong leaf-growing fertilizer during flowering fixes this.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi. Nu yɛ shishigbɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ aba shi.

english: No, planting too close makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce large cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam tubers go through a natural rest period after harvest. Setts cut from the top head of the tuber sprout much faster than setts from the lower tail end, especially if planted in cool soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Tsei ni afo kɛjɛ bulb lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa fe tsei ni afo kɛjɛ bulb lɛ shishigbɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same soil nutrients and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores the soil and reduces pest problems.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaagbai aba shi.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the primary food maize needs to stay green and grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my field yield smaller cassava roots when I plant cassava on the exact same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans restores soil health and nutrients.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the dry season sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni hulu lɛ miitso yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and tender roots that dry out easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding leaves them with weak stems and little energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking spreads the leaves out in the sun and lifts them off the damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking gbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ eshwaa hulu lɛ mli ni ewóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves limp to protect the plant from drying out, and they usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava twisting up and showing tiny white bugs underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves are caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mealybugs. They drink the plant's juices and spread viruses that prevent the leaves from growing properly.
ga: Kplukai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsake lɛ baa. Amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela ko ni haaa baai lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil becomes waterlogged, air spaces in the ground fill up with water. Without oxygen to breathe, seeds suffocate and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ ni akɛmuɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to wet. High heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen lɛ. Tsi yibiiwoo naa

english: The small side shoots steal food and water from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one strong sucker to take over, ensuring the main plant produces a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni oshi ŋmeii kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baaye esɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stakes too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their leaves compete for sunlight and their roots fight for water and nutrients in the soil. Giving them proper space allows the root tubers to expand large and healthy underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or pests like fall armyworms are feeding inside the stem. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or controlling pests early restores leaf greenness and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does my farmland dry out so fast even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter or high in sand cannot hold onto moisture. Adding decomposed manure, compost, or dried leaves as mulch covers the surface and traps water in the ground longer for your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ loo ŋã babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egbi ni egbo lɛ afata he akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally feeds the surrounding maize plants while carpet-covering the ground to prevent weed growth.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmãa ko fɔ̃ɔ shi koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: What causes black spots on my cocoa pods, and why do they turn the whole pod black so quickly?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and damp farms. Raindrops splashing on infected pods spread the fungus rapidly to neighboring healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shade babaoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rains to start before putting my seed yam in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam seed pieces need reliable moisture to awaken from dormancy and grow roots. Planting in dry soil causes the seed piece to rot or dry out before it can send up shoots.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛte shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe ni amɛye amɛbua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground past maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛdara lɛ?

english: As a cassava plant grows older than its ideal harvest period, it converts stored soft starches into tough plant fiber, turning the edible tuber woody and difficult to boil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ edara fe ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ Etsɔɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ato lɛ ewoɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ayeɔ, ni ewa akɛ abaahoo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back much faster than my crops right after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni ajie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil for years and shoot up immediately when clearing exposes them to sunlight and rain, while cultivated crops take more time to break seed dormancy and grow roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfoɔ dumɔwui ni ehi shi lɛ amli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops look burnt when I apply chemical fertilizer directly next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer acts like salt, pulling moisture out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them. Fertilizer should always be buried a few inches away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo. Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a coconut seedling is healthy and good to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ mli shweremɔ?

english: Good coconut seedlings have thick stem bases, dark green leaves, strong roots, and sprout early. Choosing strong, certified seedlings helps ensure your trees grow fast and bear good fruit.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ shishitoo ni mli wa. Baai ni tsuɔ, shishifãi ni wa, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni ooohala lɛ baaye abua otsei lɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Where can a farmer get clean, disease-free crop seedlings to start a new farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafoi baanyɛ ana tsei ahe dumɔwui ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ?

english: You can get certified, disease-free seedlings from government agricultural research stations and recognized nurseries, where experts carefully select and raise healthy planting materials for farmers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ni awo he odase, ni hela bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei kɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Nileelɔi baahala nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛduɔ okwaafoi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves on my coconut trees to suddenly turn yellow, dry up, and drop off?
ga: Mɛni haa akokoshi tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: This is often caused by lethal plant sicknesses like Cape St. Paul Wilt Disease, which is carried by tiny insects. The disease destroys the plant's internal system, causing leaves to yellow and the entire tree to die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai ni woɔ mɔ wala he gbeyei tamɔ Cape St. Paul’s wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni yɔɔ kooloi bibii akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop is suffering from a disease or just lacks water and fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli?

english: Nutrient or water shortage usually makes growth slow down or leaves turn pale evenly, while a disease causes sudden yellowing, dark spots, rotting, or dying leaves even when there is enough rain and good soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa blɛoo loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo gbele trukaa baa. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa po.

english: Why do coconut trees in coastal areas seem to die off so quickly when a disease enters the community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni akokootsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔnaa lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛ hela bote akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Coastal environments often have high humidity and winds that allow disease-carrying insects to move easily between farms. When farms plant vulnerable tree varieties close together, diseases spread rapidly across the whole area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔnaa shihilɛi amli hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baanyɛ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ mlɛo. Kɛ́ ŋmɔji du tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, helai gbɛɔ eshwaa jɛmɛ fɛɛ oya.

english: Can a coconut tree recover once it catches a major disease, or must I cut it down?
ga: Kokoo tso lɛ yɛ hela ko ni naa wa waa. Ani abaanyɛ atsa lɛ loo esa akɛ afo lɛ?

english: Once a tree shows severe symptoms of incurable diseases like Cape St. Paul Wilt Disease, it cannot be cured. Cutting down and burning the infected tree immediately stops the disease from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko jie hela ko ni anyɛɛɛ atsa, tamɔ Cape St. Anyɛŋ atsa lɛ kwraa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ashãa lɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some coconut trees survive a disease outbreak while neighboring trees die completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi yeɔ hela lɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Some varieties naturally possess disease resistance, meaning their internal defenses can fight off the infection. Agricultural scientists breed these resistant varieties so farmers can plant trees that survive local outbreaks.
ga: Helai nyɛŋ amɛye henɔi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, mligbɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baanyɛ awuu ashi helai. Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efɔ nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ adu tsei ni yeɔ wala yɛ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: If a disease destroys all the crops on my farm, can I plant the exact same crop on the land right away?
ga: Kɛji hela ko kpata ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ Ani manyɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same susceptible crop immediately is risky because the disease or the insects carrying it may still be around. It is best to wait, clean the land properly, or replant with disease-resistant crop varieties.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni baanyɛ atswa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ ekolɛ helai loo kooloi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ lolo. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni wɔmɛ. Tsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ loo okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ awo najiaŋ

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me if a dangerous crop disease enters my district?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji tsei ahe hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara bote he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers help by identifying the disease early, providing resistant seedlings from research stations, teaching control practices, and connecting farmers with government support programs to protect their livelihoods.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ amɛbuaa kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛyɔseɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ helai ahe lɛ ahemɔ kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔhe lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ okwaafoi kɛ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛbuɔ amɛshihilɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and rot when I plant them in a low swampy area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland or swampy areas hold too much water, which suffocates the roots of crops like maize. Roots need air to breathe, so standing water causes them to rot and leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant my crops on the slope of a hill?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji anɔ?

english: Planting on a hill can be tricky because rain easily washes away the fertile topsoil and fertilizer down the slope. If you farm on a hill, you need to make ridges across the slope to stop water from washing your soil away.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa ejaakɛ nugbɔ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ oya. Kɛji ootsu okwaayeli yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ Ehe miihia ni ofee ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa koni nu akashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: I have a piece of land with a deep hollow in the middle; will my crops grow well in that hollow place?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ ko ni bu ko ni mli kwɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ. Ani midumɔ nii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai ŋã lɛ nɔ?

english: Hollow areas tend to collect and hold water whenever it rains. Unless you plant crops that love water like rice, most regular crops will drown or get fungal diseases in a hollow spot.
ga: He ni ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ nu be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ. Tsei ni afɔɔ naa waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo baagboi yɛ nu mli loo amɛbaaná tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ amɛ ŋmeii amli. Ja odu tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ loo esaaa?

english: Good cocoa land should have deep soil that drains water well so it does not stay soggy, and it shouldn't be on a steep, dry hill where water runs off too fast before roots can drink it.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ehiɛ akafɔ, ni esaaa akɛ ehiɔ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ oya tsɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ nɔ.

english: What kind of crops can I safely plant in a wetland area on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Wetland areas retain moisture throughout the year, which makes them great for water-loving crops like paddy rice, sugarcane, or water-tolerant vegetables, but bad for crops like cassava or cowpea.
ga: Shikpɔji ni nɔ edɔ lɛ toɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ehi kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai ni nyɛɔ nu. Shi ehiii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei.

english: Why does water dry up faster on a hilly farm compared to flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downward due to gravity, so rain moves quickly down hills without soaking deep into the ground. Flat land gives rainwater more time to sink into the soil where roots can reach it.
ga: Nu hoɔ kɛyaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ yaa shi oya ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ náa be babaoo ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when planted in heavy or low-lying land where water stays trapped for days. Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil so water doesn't sit around the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ he ni nu ehi shi gbii babaoo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava. Koni nu akabɔle yitso lɛ he

english: Is a valley bottom a good place to plant crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani jɔɔ lɛ shishi ji he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaadu nii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Yes, valley bottoms are great during the dry season because they naturally hold underground moisture longer than higher land, helping your crops survive when rain is scarce.
ga: Hɛɛ, jɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ faaa.

english: How can I prevent rain from destroying my farm if my land is high up on a hill?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ?

english: You can build ridges or mounds across the hill (contour farming) or plant grass barriers to slow down rainwater so it doesn't wash away your crops and good topsoil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋshɔkei loo ŋshɔkei yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ. (Contour farming) loo jwɛi ni aduɔ akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni akɛbaa nugbɔ nu lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akafite.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rain starts coming early or late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa mra loo sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Instead of planting on the very first rainy day, wait until the soil is consistently wet to about a hand's depth for several days. This ensures the seeds have enough moisture to grow continuously without drying up if the rain pauses.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashɛ aaafee tso kome mli yɛ gbii babaoo mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara ni amɛgbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the water sinks deep into the soil before the sun gets too hot. In the afternoon, hot sun evaporates most of the water before the roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ babaoo feɔ lasu dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because full direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving some forest trees protects the cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni ashi yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaagbɔ.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans in the same farm as my maize help or harm my corn?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: It helps your corn. Beans and cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural food source for the maize while keeping weeds down.
ga: Eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ. Peas kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ jwɛi hu.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will give the plant the food it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground with dried leaves around my crops instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni abaashã amɛ

english: Leaving dried leaves on the soil acts like a blanket that traps moisture, keeps the roots cool in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and turns into free plant food as it rots.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ tsei aniyenii kɛji egbo

english: This is usually Cassava Mosaic Disease, carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. The best fix is to plant certified disease-resistant cassava varieties that can stay healthy even if whiteflies land on them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Tsamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni adu ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmeii yɛŋ po yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop a dark, rotten spot on the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular—switching between very dry and very wet soil prevents the roots from soaking up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa lɛ teŋ tsakemɔ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná calcium jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season, will I get the same large yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: No, saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their special vigor in the second generation, producing uneven plants and smaller cobs. Purchasing fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong plants.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ naa nɔmimaa.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up very small if I leave weeds to grow around the young vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii waa kɛji mishi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that the young yam vine needs to build energy. Without early weed removal, the plant cannot manufacture enough energy to grow big, thick tubers under the ground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ ajieee jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli mra lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans before your maize crop helps bring back the rich green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmei lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmei lɛ mli su ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted when the soil is too hard, rocky, or compacted for the tuber to expand easily underground. Loosening the soil deeply and planting in high, soft mounds allows the tubers to stretch out straight and grow large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ feɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni edaraa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot is caused by excessive water standing around the roots, which allows fungal diseases to attack the crop. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why are my cocoa tree leaves curling up and covered in tiny insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with small insects are being attacked by pests like aphids or mirids, which suck the sap out of young leaves and weaken the tree. Spraying recommended organic neem oil or approved crop protection products controls these insects and protects new leaves.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ miitutua kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mirids, ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem mu ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ loo tso hebuu tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu tsei ahe tsei heei ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly like small tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll up when tiny pests like whiteflies or thrips feed on them, often spreading a leaf-curl virus, especially during dry periods. Keeping the plants well-watered and managing sap-sucking insects helps prevent the leaves from rolling.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ye amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ gbɛɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akashwie shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when watering is irregular, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Watering regularly at the roots and providing shade during extremely hot days helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy and easy for wind to push over. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo poles and planting in deep, rich soil protects them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Feemɔ tso nine ni tsii ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui bibii fioo pɛ?

english: Cowpea plants grow too many leaves instead of flowers when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Cowpeas naturally draw nitrogen from the air, so they need minimal fertilizer and direct sunlight to focus energy on growing pods.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ ama ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my maize cobs only partially filled with seeds at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fã ko pɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Incomplete seed filling happens when hot, dry weather damages the pollen while the maize is flowering, preventing full fertilization. Planting on time with the rains ensures good soil moisture during flowering so the cobs fill up with grains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyimɔ eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ kpata pollen lɛ hiɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ agbe fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ naa kwraa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ be naa kɛ nugbɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui eyi ŋmei lɛ mli obɔ.

english: Why do the small fruits on my orange tree turn brown and drop off before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young citrus fruits drop off early when trees are attacked by fruit flies or suffer from sudden dry spells. Clearing away fallen fruits from around the tree trunk and maintaining steady soil moisture keeps the fruit attached until mature.
ga: Citrus yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso yibii amli ŋmeii tutua tso lɛ loo hɔmɔ ba trukaa. Yibii ni egbee shi lɛ amli gbalamɔ kɛjɛ tsei akutsei ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso yibii lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi ebaada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil, or they are getting too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost will help them turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small worms keep eating the inner leaves of my young corn shoots before the corn grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the central leaves of young corn plants. Checking your fields early in the morning and applying recommended organic or chemical sprays early in their life cycle stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baai amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo mli mra. ni ji amɛshihilɛ mli nibii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my neighbors plant cassava together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ duɔ ŋmei kɛfataa ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together helps you harvest maize quickly in a few months while the cassava grows slowly underneath. This covers the ground to protect the soil from heat and gives you two different crops from one plot.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ehaa okpaa ŋmãa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ aba kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving them steady water and shielding them with light shade during hot afternoons will help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli baa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are receiving too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If tomato plants do not get enough water, their leaves roll up and droop; if they get too much water, the bottom leaves turn yellow and the tomatoes can split open. Keep the soil damp like a squeezed sponge rather than soaked like mud.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni tomatoi lɛ baatswa Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i tamɔ sponji ni shwieɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeefee fɛ̃i tamɔ muji.

english: Why is it risky to plant my cowpeas immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a hot, dry spell before the real rainy season starts. Planting too early causes young seedlings to dry up and die under the hot sun before steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and tiny tubers. Spacing them properly allows each plant to spread its roots and produce large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam vines grow tall with heavy green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni amɛhe baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When yams receive too much nitrogen or lack proper stakes to climb, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Beni sweet potatoes nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo ebɛ nibii ni sa ni baaha ekwɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛma bulbs ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn dark brown and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant during fruit formation, usually brought on by irregular watering. Water your plants regularly and add wood ash or lime to the soil to prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha tso lɛ nu daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii akafee.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce small and uneven corn this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee afi nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specifically bred to yield high results only in their first generation. The seeds collected from that harvest lose their high-yield power, so buying fresh certified hybrid seeds gives you a much better harvest.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ, ebaaha oná kpamɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. Yellowing and curling mean the leaves are losing water faster than the roots can drink, which is why young cocoa needs shade trees or plantains to protect it.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Yellow kɛ curling tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ miifite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛha hebuu lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishɛreɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ashwieɔ? mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away most shoots leaves one or two strong stems that can produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Plantains lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji lɛ ateŋ babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ afee kui wuji ni tsii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni mikɛ niji kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they might rot, allowing them to catch sunshine and breathe.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. Ha ni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ ni emu.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall with dark green leaves but fail to produce big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji aba lɛ?

english: This happens when soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen makes leaves grow big, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to form strong, full cobs.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia tsei koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nourishment from the soil. Groundnuts are legumes, meaning they naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, resting and feeding your soil for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and sticky powder inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center leaves to eat the soft young plant, so inspecting your farm early helps you catch and manage them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ ni okwɛ nɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking, twisting, and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe, ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or whiteflies. As they drink the plant's juice, they damage the leaves and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii, thrips, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruit during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, causing the plant to drop its flowers. Adding mulch around the base and watering deeply keeps the roots cool enough to hold fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Mulching around Root kɛ nu ni mli kwɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: Cassava roots store edible starch, but as the plant gets older, it turns that starch into tough wooden fibers to support its heavy stems, making the tubers hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch ni ayeɔ lɛ toɔ. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa ni ekɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: Why do my stored dried grains get small bugs and turn into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmaa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Weevil insects or their eggs often get onto the grain during drying. If the grain is not dried completely or stored in airtight bags, these insects hatch and multiply, eating the inside of the grain until only powder remains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo amɛwui lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ hela yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni ayeɔ kɛyashiɔ powda pɛ ni eshwɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: My land has heavy clay soil that becomes sticky in the rain and hard when dry. Can I still grow good crops on it?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ, ni ewa kɛji egbi. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ jɛmɛ lolo?

english: Clay soil holds onto water and nutrients very well, making it very fertile, but it needs organic matter like animal manure or compost mixed into it so crop roots can breathe and spread easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii waa Shi esa akɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ atsu nii.Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but then the blossoms just fall off without growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduuu tomato ko?

english: Blossom drop happens when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get steady water, causing stress that makes the plant shed its flowers to survive.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to spring up quickly and grab sunlight and water before your domesticated crops can establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛhe hulu la kɛ nu dani oshia tsei lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: Mixing cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving the cassava plenty of room and time to mature later.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa futu ŋmãa lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa hegbɛ kɛ be babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I harvested this year to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted hybrid seeds, saving them for the next season will result in weak crops and low yields; buying fresh certified seeds gives you stronger crops and more food.
ga: Kɛji odu hybrid dumɔwui Okɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa kɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly start eating my crop leaves as soon as the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ yeli shishi trukaa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: The rain causes crops to sprout fresh, tender leaves, which attracts moths and butterflies to lay eggs that hatch into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural trick plants use to shield themselves from intense sunlight and slow down the loss of moisture through their leaves.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni baa kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do you advise me not to plant tomatoes on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu tomato yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows soil pests and diseases that target tomatoes to build up.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tomato nɔ lɛ aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers so they don't rot underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? Koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally, showing that the plant has finished sending food down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛmaje eyitso lɛ naa.

english: How long does it usually take for a coconut seed to sprout after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most coconut seeds take about four weeks to sprout, depending on the specific variety you plant and whether the soil has enough moisture.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui babaoo heɔ aaafee otsii ejwɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Edamɔ tso henɔ ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Do I need to completely cover the coconut nut with soil when planting it?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, ani esa akɛ oha ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ kwraa?

english: Yes, planting the coconut nut directly into the ground and covering it properly with soil protects it from drying out and helps it sprout successfully.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-coconut tso lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ sũ ha nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he koni ekagbi, ni ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I just leave a coconut on top of the ground, or must it be buried to sprout?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ loo esa akɛ afu amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: It needs to be placed into the soil and covered so that it stays cool and moist enough for the seed inside to germinate and push roots into the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni aha nɔ koni edɔ ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi shishifãi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my crops sprout much faster than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Sprouting time depends heavily on the crop variety you choose. Research-backed or improved varieties are bred to germinate more consistently and quickly.
ga: Be ni tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ damɔ tso henɔ ni ohala lɛ nɔ waa. Henɔi ni niiamlitaomɔ fiɔ sɛɛ loo afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Should I use seeds developed by agricultural researchers instead of taking seeds from old farms?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni maŋɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ?

english: Research varieties are generally better because they are selected for reliable sprouting times, consistent yields, and better resistance to field conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niiamlitaomɔ henɔi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ahalaa amɛ kɛha shweremɔ bei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nibii ni afeɔ daa ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe shihilɛi babaoo

english: How does keeping consistent water in the soil help my young crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Consistent water prevents the soil from drying out, ensuring the planted seeds receive the steady moisture they need to break open and sprout without getting stressed.
ga: Nu ni anáa daa lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Ehaa dumɔwui ni adu lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: How do I know if my plants are getting enough water during the week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ otsi lɛ mli?

english: If your soil remains steadily damp and your plants continue growing smoothly without turning weak or dry, it means they are receiving consistent and adequate water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni otsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔɔɔ loo egbiɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be.

english: What is the proper way to cut mature crops so I do not damage the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei ni eda lɛ koni akafite amɛ?

english: When the yield is fully matured, cut it neatly with sharp tools at the right joint so you harvest cleanly without tearing the stem or harming the main plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nifeemɔ lɛ eshɛ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Feemɔ dɛŋdade ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ninejurɔgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa ni he tse ni ogbalaaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo oyeee tso titri lɛ awui.

english: How can I handle my harvested crop carefully so it stays neat and clean for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe atse kɛha jara nɔ?

english: Collect and cut your harvest gently, avoiding dropping or bruising the produce, and keep it clean and shaded right after harvesting to maintain its quality.
ga: Bua onibii lɛ anaa ni ofolɔ mli blɛoo. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ ni oooshwie shi loo ooofite lɛ he. ni eha ehe atse ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I tell when my crop is completely finished and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A crop is finished and ready for cutting when its fruit reaches full maturity, stops growing in size, and develops the proper firmness or natural yield indicators.
ga: Agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa ni asaa he koni afo kɛji aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃. Kpaa shweremɔ ni ofee shifimɔ ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo he okadii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves lose moisture quickly and burn. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to protect them while their root systems develop during their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpee hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ kɛha hebuu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant moves nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of green leaves, but the tubers underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: When soil has high levels of nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stalk without turning into small tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry out or become sterile, preventing proper fertilization. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally sheds the unpollinated flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my plantain stalk dry up and die after producing just one bundle of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ beni ewo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to flower and produce fruit only once in its lifetime. After the fruit matures, the main stem naturally dies off so that plant energy and nutrients can flow into the young suckers growing around its base.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni aduawai lɛ eda kwraa sɛɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii hoɔ kɛyaa tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ ahe lɛ amli.

english: Why do my ripe cassava tubers rot in the soil if I do not harvest them before heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills all the air gaps around the roots, cutting off oxygen. Without air, root tissues die, making it easy for rot-causing fungi in the wet soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifã lɛ baagbo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why do my tall maize plants easily fall over on the ground after a short rainstorm with heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain softens the topsoil, making it easy for wind to loosen shallow roots. If the plant lacks strong support roots or is planted too shallowly, the heavy top weight pushes the stalk over.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ. Nɔ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baatsi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn even when there is no soil or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural resting phase called dormancy. Once this internal biological clock finishes after a few months, warm temperature and air signal to the yam that it is time to wake up and grow, regardless of whether it is in soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji akɛ agbe nɛkɛ mligbɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli pɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛdara. ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji eyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ebɛ mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viral infections spread by these same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil. When the legumes decay, this trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: What should I do if some of my maize seeds fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If seeds do not sprout within 7 to 10 days, check if the soil was too dry or if pests ate them. You should immediately replant fresh seeds in those empty spots so your whole field grows and matures at the same time.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 10 mli lɛ, kwɛmɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo ŋmeii eye. Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nakai hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ohegbɛi lɛ fɛɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛdara yɛ be kome mli.

english: If cassava fails to yield well on a patch of land this season, can I plant cassava on that same spot next year?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nyɛɛɛ awo yibii kpakpai yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is best to rotate your crops instead of planting cassava in the exact same spot. Planting the same crop repeatedly allows soil pests and diseases to build up, which causes future crops to fail even faster.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni ooodu ŋmei yɛ he kome. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya po.

english: Why do my crop plants sometimes look healthy when small but then fail and die right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ beni amɛji bibii shi amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Crops often fail late in the season if rainfall stops during the flowering or fruiting stage, or if pests attack the roots underground where you cannot see them until the plant dries up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ fɔfɔii loo yibiiwoo be lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni onyɛɛɛ ona kɛyashi tso lɛ baagbi.

english: Why does my neighbor's field yield plenty of crops while mine fails on the very same type of soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ wooo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest usually depend on seed quality, exact planting dates relative to the rains, regular weeding, and applying fertilizer or manure at the correct stage of plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Be pɔtɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ yɔɔ tsakpaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What actually causes crops to grow well and produce a heavy harvest during good seasons?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ bei kpakpai amli lɛ?

english: Crops thrive when they get good quality seeds, steady rainfall during flowering, loose soil that lets roots spread deep, and protection from weeds that steal water and food from the plants.
ga: Tsei shwereɔ kɛji amɛná dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nɛɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings wilt and die under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender roots that cannot pull up enough water to survive intense heat. Providing light shade with palm fronds or spreading dry grass around the base keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers but fail to form any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruit when temperatures get too high, when water is scarce, or when there are no pollinating insects around to transfer pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu faaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he. koni akɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli

english: Why is it bad if I plant all my crop seeds very close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Putting seeds too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin plants that produce very little food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds so they do not fail?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite

english: The best time to plant is immediately after the first major, steady rain when the topsoil is thoroughly wet, ensuring seeds get enough moisture to sprout and build strong roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Is it better to grow different crops together in one plot or plant each crop separately in its own area?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome loo aaadu tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko srɔtoi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ekpokpaa nɔ?

english: Mixing crops like maize and beans protects you because if one crop fails due to weather or pests, the other can still succeed and provide you with food and income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ohe. Ejaakɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, tso kroko hu baanyɛ aye omanye ni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika.

english: Why is it better for me to raise my crop seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery beds protect delicate seeds from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, and pests, allowing seedlings to grow strong roots before facing the open field.
ga: Nursery saatsoi lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow sometimes even after I plant them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are old, damaged by pests, buried too deep for oxygen to reach them, or if the soil gets too hot.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite Afu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ

english: If leaves turn yellow and limp in wet soil, you are overwatering. If leaves curl, dry out, and turn brown at the edges, your crops need more water.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oyɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ, egbi, ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia onibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to harvest more from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak, skinny plants with tiny harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do some young crops need shade trees when they are small but need open sun when mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii komɛi ahe hiaa hulutsoo beni amɛdarako lɛ, shi hulu la babaoo he hiaa amɛ beni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat, while grown plants need full sunlight to produce energy for heavy fruits.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi. Beni tso lɛ miida lɛ, hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia lɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha eyibii ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to trim or cut off some small branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli?

english: Trimming extra branches pushes the plant to spend its energy producing bigger fruits rather than useless leaves, and improves airflow to prevent disease.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni aaafo lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo yibii wuji. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why does my harvest drop if I plant the same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding animal manure or compost to my farm soil actually help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Manure feeds the soil with essential nutrients that act as food for plants, helping them develop deep roots, strong stems, and heavy fruit.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei aniyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even after my crops have grown bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds continually drink the water and steal the fertilizer hidden beneath the soil, while also serving as homes for harmful insects and diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nuɔ nu be fɛɛ be ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ shia kɛha kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking plant sap and spreading disease; removing affected plants early stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ, ebaakpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sun and dry winds because their roots are shallow and leaf cuticles are thin. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees shields them from sunburn and helps the soil retain moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baa lɛ hewolo lɛ mli etse. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.
