english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Excess moisture stays on the pods when air cannot flow freely through overloaded branches.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli oya lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. The plant is moving stored nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to feed newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does swamp rice survive standing water while my maize crop rots and dies if water stays on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi kɛjɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ kɛji nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems and roots that transport oxygen from the leaves down to the roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and drown when soil spaces fill completely with water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ nu.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at a slanted angle instead of standing them straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle allows tubers to grow closer to the soil surface on one side, making them expand bigger and making harvesting much easier without breaking the roots.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ 45 degree ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa cassava shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ yɛ fa kome. Ehaa yitso lɛ daa. Ni ewaaa kwraa akɛ abaakpa ni akumɔɔɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward direct sunlight to produce energy through photosynthesis, which is then stored underground to form large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and the flowers dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and uneven watering causing the plant stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli, ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling to the ground without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too hot, when the air is extremely dry, or when there is insufficient soil moisture to support fruit formation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa shwane loo gbɛkɛ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow, fibrous root systems that struggle to hold heavy bunches of fruit, especially if soil nematodes or stem borers have damaged the roots underground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ aduawai babaoo. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ sũ mli ŋmeii loo stem borers efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field make the soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally fertilizing the soil when the plant dies.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, the air is extremely dry and hot. Cocoa trees shed their leaves to reduce water loss and protect themselves from dying of thirst when there is no rain.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbi ni edɔ waa. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my pepper leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil fungi onto the leaves, and the wet leaves create a warm, moist environment where fungal diseases spread quickly, showing up as dark spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ejieɔ ehe kpo akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs inside the leaf funnels of young maize, and when the caterpillars hatch, they eat the tender inner leaves, damaging the plant's growth.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai amli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Ebaaye mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays waterlogged for too long during heavy rains or when fungal diseases in the soil attack the tubers because water cannot drain away properly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ ejaakɛ nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen in the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to the soil and weather conditions. They act quickly to absorb sunlight, water, and soil food before your planted crops have a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Amɛheɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani otso lɛ naa hegbɛ ni eda.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has run out of food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have thin stems, or turn light green and yellow instead of dark green without any pest damage, the soil is missing key nutrients needed for plant growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ daa blɛoo, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteee lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy stems. If you leave too many suckers growing around one mother tree, their root systems compete and weaken, making the main tree top-heavy and easy to blow down.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsii. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, tso ni ji nyɛ kome Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso titri lɛ tsii ni eshishijee waaa.

english: Why do groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground if the nuts grow underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers get pollinated above ground, but after pollination, the plant grows long stems called pegs that bend down and push themselves into the soil, where the actual groundnuts grow.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni baabɔle ehe ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before it evaporates in the sun, and it allows the leaves to dry off quickly during the day, which stops fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani etsɔɔ hulu la lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ akpa.

english: Why do my local coconut trees take so many years to bear fruit compared to the new hybrid types?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmei tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto ŋmei tsei heei ni akɛwo mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Local coconut varieties like the West African Tall naturally take 6 to 8 years to start producing fruit. Hybrid varieties are specially bred to grow faster and start yielding coconuts in just 3 to 4 years, making them produce much earlier.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi tamɔ West African Tall lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani ebɔi yibiiwoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Atsɔse ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ yaa oya kwraa.

english: What is the difference between planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest and buying certified seed from the store?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ shwapo mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose their strength and vigor over time, producing lower yields and weak plants. Certified seeds are specially bred for high yields, uniform growth, and resistance to common local pests and diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the cleared bush on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter in the topsoil, kills helpful organisms like earthworms, and leaves the soil dry and exposed to erosion, which starves your crops of natural plant food.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náaa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: If previous crops had pale yellow leaves, grew very slowly, or yielded small produce, your soil lacks essential nutrients. Rich, healthy soil is usually dark and produces strong, dark green weeds and vegetation.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewooo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewoɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli kɛ tsei wala.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture to protect young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it wrong to plant my cassava sticks very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough space underground to spread and grow thick. If planted too close together, they compete for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he, ni no baaha amɛná tsei bibii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: How often should I water my newly planted coconut seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-ŋmei tso ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young coconut seedlings need deep watering once or twice a week during dry spells so their roots can establish deep in the ground, keeping the soil around the stem moist without waterlogging the roots.
ga: Nu ni mli kwɔ he miihia ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ohaaa shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to prevent water loss. By curling their leaves, plants reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve moisture inside.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni nu akafite. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ baa shi yɛ ehiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young coconut trees turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves can be a sign of nutrient deficiency, prolonged water stress during hot months, or early attack by pests. It shows the plant is lacking nutrients or moisture to keep all leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Nu mli haomɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baaha ebaa lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my pepper plants, and will it affect my yield?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni ani ebaana minitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by leaf-eating pests like beetles or caterpillars. Damaged leaves cannot catch enough sunlight to make food for the plant, which leads to fewer and smaller pepper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii baa. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efeɔ bibioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that lose moisture quickly under direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade using crops like plantains protects the leaves from scorching and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tamɔ plantains tsu nii ni akɛha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When maize lacks nutrients like nitrogen, its lower leaves turn pale yellow, starting at the leaf tips and moving down the middle. Stunted growth and thin stems are also strong signals that the soil needs fertilizer to help the crop grow properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. Tso lɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hu ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting beans or groundnuts together with cassava helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei fata ŋmei he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, providing free nutrients for crops like cassava growing next to them without wearing out the farmland.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa tsei tamɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko. ni ekɛ nɔ ko baaa okwaayeli hei

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars eating holes through the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh, tender leaves at the growing point of the corn plant. Catching them early and using safe pest control methods prevents them from destroying the crop before it forms corn cobs.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and showing light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curling yellow leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by small flying insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your farm safe from this disease.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kplukai bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds take over, your crops do not get enough nourishment to grow strong or yield good produce.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ waa loo amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need plenty of room underground to expand, as well as access to water and nutrients. Spacing mounds properly ensures the plants do not fight each other for soil resources, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he babaoo koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni anáa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe etswaaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ahe akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without producing any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing their flowers to fall off before pollination can happen. Giving the plants regular water and covering the surrounding soil with dried grass mulch helps keep the roots cool and saves the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollination baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off extra stems and old branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji momoi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases like black pod and allows the tree to focus its energy on growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cowpeas get filled with tiny holes and dust after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ sũ beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs on the seeds, and their young eat the grain from the inside out, leaving powder and holes behind. Drying your cowpeas thoroughly and storing them in airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects and keeps the seeds safe for months.
ga: Kooloo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ewui yɛ dumɔwui anɔ. ni amɛbii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Ashi powda kɛ bu yɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ agbi tsina ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains wash soil nutrients away or if the roots are sitting in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo shishifãi lɛ bote nu babaoo mli.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts before maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize in that same soil later, the maize uses this stored natural food to grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ adebɔɔ mli nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eda ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the earth too quickly. It keeps the plant roots cool, saves water, and prevents weeds from taking over your bed.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ehaa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye otsu lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which then travels down into the ground to grow large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ yitso agbo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomato seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they struggle against each other for air, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants thin and weak, and makes it easy for diseases to spread rapidly from leaf to leaf.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ oya.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying during the hot Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft roots and thin leaves that burn quickly under strong sun and dry wind. They need living shade plants like plantains planted beside them and soil mulch to keep them cool and moist during dry months.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: What is eating the leaves deep inside the heart of my young maize stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji baai ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ lɛ yeli?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed on fresh foliage. Catching them early and spraying targeted control solutions directly into the stalk funnel helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ afɔ stem filter cone lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are under stress, often caused by irregular watering, intense heat, or a lack of basic soil nutrients like calcium and phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots under the ground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cassava is generally ready around 8 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves begin to yellow and drop, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot quickly even when I store it inside a dry room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if the grains still hold moisture inside from the field. Grains must be dried in the sun until they are hard and make a dry rattling sound before being packed into bags.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ emli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni ená gbee ni haa egbiɔ dani akɛwo kotokui amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth, or that heavy rain has logged the field and flooded the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ eyiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli nu.

english: Is it true that planting cowpeas alongside my maize makes the soil better for crops?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpea take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this naturally fertilizes the soil for maize.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases specific to maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What makes my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellowish early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a viral infection spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and lack of water stressing the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ ni kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground mainly due to waterlogging when rainwater sits in the soil for too long without draining, allowing fungal rots to grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni egbo baanyɛ ada.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees drying up from the edges and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Sigatoka, a common fungal leaf disease that reduces the plant's ability to turn sunlight into food, causing smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa fe fɛɛ ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji fungal leaf hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni haa tso ko nyɛmɔ ni ekɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ efeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from temperature extremes, too much or too little water, or an overdose of high-nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nu babaoo loo fioo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why do some cocoa flowers drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi komɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they do not get pollinated by tiny insects, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather and lacks enough nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my yam seed setts fail to sprout after I plant them in mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam setts fail to sprout if they were infected with root rot before planting, if planted too deep where there is no air, or if the soil mound is too dry and hot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni egboi lɛ ye amɛnɔ dani adu. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ tsɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than crops, so they steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crop can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How deep should I bury my maize seeds when planting so they grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too deep prevents them from reaching the surface, while planting too shallow leaves them exposed to birds and heat. A good depth for maize is about 3 to 5 centimeters deep so the roots establish firmly while the shoots easily reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni adumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ. He ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa lɛ mli kwɔ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, no hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ama shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ náa hulu la lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving cassava enough space allows the underground tubers to expand fully and produce a large harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni kɛ hulu la ni fa fioo nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmei lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the base of my crop instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures your crop absorbs the nutrients directly before nearby weeds can steal them or rain washes them away from the field.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Dani jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaju amɛ loo nugbɔ baaho amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready and moist enough for me to start planting after the first rain?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni edɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to soften their outer shell and start sprouting. You should wait until the main rains start and the soil stays damp below the surface for a few days, so young roots do not dry out and die.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baabɔi nɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi gbii fioo komɛi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Will using a machine to dig and loosen my soil help my crops grow better than manual clearing?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛfo sũ lɛ mli ni mikɛgbala lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛbaatsu nii?

english: Loosening hard soil allows young plant roots to dig deep easily for water and food. It also improves air and water flow in the ground, helping crops establish a strong root foundation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo ahaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Helps plants have a solid foundation.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant maintain healthy green leaves to make food for its grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni ekɛha dumɔwui lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops look thin and grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni edaa blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni hulu la lɛ mli wa yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it beneficial to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool and prevents valuable soil water from evaporating under the hot sun.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings droop and look lifeless during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In hot sun, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their young roots can pull water from the soil. Water them early in the morning or late evening so roots stay hydrated throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ nu awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to grow cocoa before I spend money buying seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo dani mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, soft soil that lets water drain easily so roots do not rot. If your land stays flooded like a swamp after rain or is full of big rocks, cocoa roots will struggle to grow deep enough to feed the plant.
ga: Kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. Kɛ́ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo tɛi wuji eyi nɔ obɔ. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ.

english: Why are plantain trees usually planted together with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ekome lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are not strong enough to handle full, direct sunlight. Without natural shade trees to block the intense heat, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it, causing them to burn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baatsi adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ naa lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close, their branches fight for sunlight and their roots fight for food in the soil. This competition makes all the trees weak, reduces pod production, and trapped damp air creates a good home for pod diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Niji lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ feɔ shia kpakpa kɛha pod helai.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, act like freeloaders on the main tree. They steal nutrients and water that the tree needs to make flowers and cocoa pods, so removing them keeps the tree focused on producing fruit.
ga: Nakai tsei krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso wulu lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm, or will it hurt my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ? Aloo ebaaye mi cacao tsei lɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots grow very large and pull massive amounts of water and food from the soil, leaving little for young cocoa. Cassava also grows tall fast and can overcrowd young cocoa, so crops like plantains or legumes are better companions.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa waa ni amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fioo pɛ eshwɛ kɛha kookoo ni mli tse lɛ. Cassava hu daa oya ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ cocoa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ atsu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo legumes ji nanemɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small black spots to turn my healthy green cocoa pods completely rotten during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji bibii ni haa mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small water mold that spreads fast when rain drops bounce off wet soil onto low pods. High dampness and dark shade make it spread quickly from pod to pod across your farm.
ga: Nu mli ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ jɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛba ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ haa egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when tiny beneficial insects called midges are not available to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by sudden dry weather and lacks enough nutrients in the soil to support baby pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ gboi. Anyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my cocoa farm so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo kookoo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer at the start of the rainy season when the soil is warm and moist, which allows roots to quickly drink up the nutrients. Avoid applying during heavy downpours that cause water to run across the surface of the land.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce a huge harvest one year, but very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ?

english: A heavy harvest uses up almost all the tree's stored food reserves and soil nutrients. If you do not feed the soil with fertilizer or compost after a big harvest, the tree takes a year off to recover its strength.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni tsii lɛ yeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni ato kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ baahe afi kome dani ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is GMO corn, and how does it behave differently in my farm compared to my local corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji GMO ŋmãa? Ni te esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: GMO corn is modified in a laboratory to resist specific pests or survive dry weather better. While it can produce higher yields under good conditions, you usually cannot save seeds from your harvest to replant next season like you do with traditional corn.
ga: Atsake GMO ŋmãa yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni enyɛ eshi kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ yibii babaoo aba yɛ shihilɛi kpakpai amli moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ onyɛɛɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛ blema ŋmãa atsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do some improved corn seeds produce a big harvest the first time, but give very weak yields if I plant seeds saved from that harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Those are hybrid or specially bred seeds designed for one generation of high performance. Their offspring lose the parents' strength, so you need to buy fresh certified seeds each season to get high yields.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome loo dumɔwui srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi ni afee aha yinɔ pɔtɛɛ ko ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Amɛbii lɛ anaaa amɛfɔlɔi lɛ ahewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli yɛ be fɛɛ mli koni ona yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Does the variety of corn I plant affect how good it is for making local foods like banku and kenkey?
ga: Ani ŋmãa srɔtoi ni miduɔ lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mafee maŋ lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ banku kɛ kenky lɛ he?

english: Yes, corn varieties have different starch levels and hardness. Traditional hard white corn ferments well and yields a smooth texture for banku and kenkey, while some softer or imported varieties may absorb water differently and change the taste or texture.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa henɔi lɛ yɛ starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ bɔ ni ewa ha lɛ srɔtoi. Kusum mli ŋmãa yɛŋ ni wa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa Banku kɛ Kenkey feɔ blɛoo, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa komɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ ni amɛtsake ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Are imported crop varieties and GMO foods safe for my family to eat in our local dishes?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ kɛ GMO niyenii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye wɔmaŋ niyenii?

english: Yes, food crops that pass agricultural safety checks are safe for human consumption. They provide similar energy and nutrients as traditional crops, though their taste, color, or cooking time might differ slightly.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ ni tsɔɔ okwaayeli mli shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kwɛmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii. Amɛhaa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ blema tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ, su loo be ni akɛhooɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔto fioo moŋ.

english: Why do bean crops brought from drier countries like Burkina Faso or Mali grow so well with very little rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛbaajɛ maji ni mli egbi tamɔ Burkina Faso loo Mali lɛ amli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Farmers in drier northern regions plant early-maturing cowpea varieties with deep root systems that search for groundwater. These varieties finish flowering and podding quickly before the rain stops completely.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ hei ni egbi lɛ duɔ tsina ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ kwraa.

english: How can I protect my bean crop from insect attacks while the plants are flowering in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-bean tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean flowers attract pests like pod borers. You can protect your crop by planting early at the start of the rains, spraying with neem-based organic repellents, or choosing pest-resistant bean varieties.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii gbalaa kooloi tamɔ pod borers. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooodu mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ helai ni neem yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔ nɔ. Aloo halamɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: How do I know which bean variety to plant if I want cross-border traders to buy my harvest in bulk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmeii ni esa akɛ madu? Kɛji miisumɔ ni jarayelɔi ni tsɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ ahe minibii babaoo.

english: Bulk traders look for uniform size, bright color, and grain that cooks quickly. It is best to check with local agricultural officers or traders to know whether white, brown, or black-eyed cowpeas are currently most demanded in the market.
ga: Jarayelɔi babaoo taoɔ ŋmaa ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, sui ni mli tse, kɛ ŋmaa ni shwereɔ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo jarayelɔ lɛ koni ona tsina ŋmei yɛŋ, ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni ataoɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ jara nɔ ŋmɛnɛ.

english: Why do grains brought in by regional traders stay free of insects longer than the corn I store in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kpokpaa nɔ jarayelɔi ni kɛ ŋmaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi ni kooloi bɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmaa ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Traders thoroughly dry their grain to very low moisture levels and store them in airtight hermetic bags or treat them with food-safe storage powders that prevent weevils and mold from growing.
ga: Jarayelɔi gĩɔ amɛŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi kwraa. ni akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Aloo okɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ he powda ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ anaa.

english: What causes my harvested beans to develop tiny holes and turn into dust after a few months of storage?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli lɛ baa? ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ

english: This damage is caused by bean weevils, whose eggs are often laid on the pods in the field and hatch during storage. Drying the beans completely and storing them in sealed, airtight containers stops the insects from breeding.
ga: Bean ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmeii lɛ kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafɔ.

english: Why does my soil lose its fertility faster when I plant corn every year compared to when I plant beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi oya kɛ́ midu ŋmãa daa afi fe be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Corn uses up a lot of soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, to grow tall and produce big ears. Beans are legumes, which means they take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, actually helping to restore soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. titri lɛ nitrogen Koni ekwɛ ni eha toi wuji Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important nutrient in the soil, or the soil has too much water around the roots, stopping the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist after a warm rain and when the plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting and again when flowering begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni tsei miida Bei pii lɛ Enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni fɔfɔi jeɔ shishi lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool air the young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii ahi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other to get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and smaller yields than if they had enough space.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: Planting maize on the same soil every season drains the exact same nutrients every year and allows soil pests and diseases that target maize to build up in that farm plot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh leaves inside the whorl of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn rings lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: That damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing funnel of the maize plant and feed on the soft, young leaves before they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which feed on leaf sap and can spread plant viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors; they rapidly drink the water and steal the soil nutrients and sunlight that your main crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii ni he hiaa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without making fruit when temperatures become too high, when the air is extremely dry, or when the soil experiences sudden changes between being very dry and very wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa teŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long after heavy rains, or when damaging soil pests attack the tuber surfaces, letting fungal rot enter.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tutua tuber lɛ hiɛ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbo yɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my maize grow better the next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are natural soil improvers. Their roots pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving behind rich soil food for the maize crop that follows.
ga: Cowpea ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Eshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii baa shi kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often because the plant is not getting steady water to draw nutrients up from the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while hanging on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by tiny fungal organisms that thrive in cool, dark, wet weather when there is too much shade around the cocoa trees.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi bibii kɛbaa Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji hulutsoo be ebɔle ehe. Kakao babaoo tsɔ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to live. When soil stays flooded with water for too long, the roots drown and decay-causing micro-organisms attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni nibii bibii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do my okra leaves get covered in a sticky fluid and curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mli tse ehà mi okra baai lɛ anɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called aphids sit under the leaves and suck out the plant's sap. As they feed, they produce a sticky waste that coats the leaves and attracts soot-like mold.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ taraa baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛfeɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi. No haa baai lɛ ahe ni egbalaa ŋmei ko ni tamɔ sũ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any pepper fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden change in moisture, which causes the plant to protect itself by shedding blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow very tall stems but produce very few leaves and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa shi ewoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants stretch out toward light when they are shaded or planted too closely together, spending all their energy reaching upward instead of making pods.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya la lɛ he kɛji akɛ awo amɛ shade mli loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeefee pod.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out small, bent, and full of rough bumps instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bibii, amɛbɔle amɛhe, ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yams struggle to expand in hard, unplowed soil, and microscopic worms called nematodes in the soil can feed on the skin, causing twisted growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ soil nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aye hewolo lɛ. ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a long time to start growing fast after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi plantain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers must build a strong new root system first before growing leaves, and they delay if the soil lacks moisture or organic compost.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ana shishifã hee ni mli wa dani amɛdu baai. Ni ebaatsɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain usually only wets the surface and is followed by hot dry sun, which dries out the soil and kills newly sprouted seeds. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the roots have steady moisture to establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ oomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: Why does clearing weeds while my crops are still small help them grow so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni migbeɔ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your young crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and water they need without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to break up hard soil and clear large stones before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie sũ ni wa ni ajie tɛi wuji dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to grow long and thick underground. If the soil is too hard or full of rocks, the tubers cannot expand properly and will grow small or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaafee bibioo loo ehiɛ su ni ejaaa

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong heat and direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun and keep the moisture in the air and soil until they are older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhe afee hulu la ni naa wa lɛ, ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow when they are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ lɛ? No ji kuku lolo?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the plantain fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground. When the bunch becomes heavy, the weight pulls the shallow roots out of the soil, so you need to prop the stem up with sturdy wooden poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shwiili lɛ shwiili lɛ shwiili lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tso ni wa afi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers without producing fruit if the weather gets too hot, if the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, or if there is no wind or insects to move pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato baafɔ̃ ni ewooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Aloo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni baaye abua kɛ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on the plant sap and pass a virus from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛjieɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, many pests look for green plants to get moisture, and the heat helps them multiply faster. Rain also physically washes many small insects off the leaves.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, kooloi babaoo kwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ. Ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔɔ bii oya. Nugbɔ hu hoɔ kooloi bibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops produce less food when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil every year and allows soil pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin instead of strong when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are placed too close to one another, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They stretch upward as fast as possible to catch light, which leaves their stems weak, thin, and easily knocked over by rain or wind.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ he waaa, efeɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ enáa enɔ hewalɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl inward during the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a protective response to heat. The plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the harsh sun, which helps it save water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛhaa hulutsoo be lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni hulu la ni naa wa ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei dani midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil later, the maize feeds on this stored natural fertilizer to grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni ato nɛɛ koni eda ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni enyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the open air so they can catch maximum sunlight without getting shaded or infected by soil-borne diseases. More sunlight on the leaves allows the plant to produce more energy, resulting in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akawo amɛmli loo amɛkamɔ amɛ. Hulu la babaoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with organic material, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden plot.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ akafo oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I planted sprout right away while others in the same garden fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ kome mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require even moisture, warmth, and the right planting depth to germinate. Seeds planted too deep, seeds that dried out after planting, or seeds damaged by insects before planting will fail to push through the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni sa, dɔlɛ, kɛ mlibotemɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni adu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui ni gbiɔ yɛ adumɔ sɛɛ Aloo dumɔwui ni kooloi efite dani adu lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to clear weeds while my crops are still small rather than waiting until the weeds get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Weeding early removes competition before the weeds can steal water, light, and nutrients from your small crops. It also saves you time and heavy labor, because young weeds are much easier to clear than deep-rooted, overgrown plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie akaŋshii kɛya dani jwɛi lɛ anyɛ aju nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli. Ehaa be kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa hu baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi bibii lɛ ajiemɔ waaa fe tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed for fruit formation. Protecting the soil moisture helps the plant retain its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai ni anáa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: How can I tell if the cassava stems I saved from last season are healthy enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu?

english: Good cassava stem cuttings should feel firm, not dry or brittle, and have clear, undamaged eye buds along the stem. If you scrape the bark gently with your fingernail and see fresh green underneath, the stem is alive and ready for planting.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ afee nɔ ni wa. Egbi loo egbo ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni efiteee yɛ tso lɛ shishi fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ eniji shwie tso lɛ he blɛoo ni ona su ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains alongside new young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni kookoo dumɔwui heei yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad shade leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and keeping moisture in the soil while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores green color and helps the plant grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help my soil for the next season's maize crop?
ga: Te ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni baa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize that follow.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small, low-yield tubers instead of large roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ shishifãi wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds fail to sprout when I plant them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛdu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply run out of stored energy before their shoots can reach the surface to catch sunlight, causing them to die under the soil before emerging.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji He ni esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, pepper plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Drooping is a temporary defense mechanism to conserve water, and the leaves usually recover once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ tsakemɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains soften and spoil so quickly when collected during midday heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting in high heat increases the internal temperature and chemical activity of the fruit, which speeds up ripening and causes plantains to decay much faster than those harvested during cool mornings.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli wa tsuɔ nii kɛkpaa nii lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ amli dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ oya, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya fe kɛji akpa amɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do worms attack my maize leaves mostly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa baai babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and fresh, soft leaf growth during rainy periods create ideal conditions for pests like armyworms to lay eggs, hatch rapidly, and feed continuously on young crops.
