ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai heei ni daraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworms lɛ koni amɛwo amɛwui. shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii be fɛɛ be

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I cut down all the big trees in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Large shade trees protect young cocoa by filtering sunlight, lowering field temperatures, and keeping humidity in the air and soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa ahi shi

english: Why should I trim off the lower branches and extra shoot growths from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing bottom leaves and extra shoot branches directs energy away from non-essential leaf growth and redirects nutrients straight into producing larger, healthier tomato fruit.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli. ni etsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ ekoŋŋ koni ekɛ tomato yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do flowers drop off my okra plants without growing into okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miishi mi okra tso lɛ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ okra ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Okra plants shed flowers when stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Rosella tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ haaa amɛná haomɔ.

english: Why does my topsoil wash away during heavy rains, and how can I keep my farmland fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii?

english: Heavy rainfall strips away fertile topsoil if the land is left bare or sloped without protection. Planting cover crops, building contour ridges, or farming across slopes holds the soil firmly in place so nutrients remain in your field for your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ kɛji akɛ abuuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo ejɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. dumɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ridge formation Loo okwaayeli ni akɛtsɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and heat. Planting plantains or fast-growing shade trees alongside them provides essential canopy shade and conserves soil moisture while the young cocoa plants establish themselves.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya lɛ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize seeds after the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the very first rain is risky because a dry spell can follow and kill the sprouting seeds. It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist down to a finger's depth after two or three good rains.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ hulutsoo be baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashɛ inchi kome pɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall stems with bushy leaves while producing very small, thin tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa.

english: Why are there holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants, and what is eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ? Ni mɛni ji niyeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide and feed inside the central leaves (funnel) of the plant. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the funnels stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai (cones) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, curling, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings for planting. You can manage it by planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties and removing infected plants early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe ni awo he odase akɛ ooodu ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the plant experiences severe heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent moisture to the soil and applying mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi titri kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the growth stage will help the leaves regain their dark green color and improve yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my pepper crop after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, resilient plants adapted to quickly claim bare soil and open sunlight. Spreading a layer of dry grass or organic mulch around your pepper plants blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi oya ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni mli tse mli oya. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔ ehe. Pepper tsei ni akɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I take a soil sample from my farmland to an officer before I start planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ shikpɔŋ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Testing your soil shows what nutrients your land is missing and whether it is healthy for maize, helping you avoid wasting money on the wrong fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he kɛha ŋmãa loo daabi? Enɛ haaa ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crops planted in sandy soil dry out much faster than those planted in darker soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has larger spaces between its particles, so water runs straight through it quickly, whereas darker soil retains water and nutrients much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ nibii bibii lɛ ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ oya. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry grass help them stay alive during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the soil acts like a blanket that shades the ground from hot sunlight, stopping water from evaporating and keeping the crop roots cool and moist.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni oha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How can sickness spread from my neighbor's farm to my cocoa trees if I do not touch his plants?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela ko agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛya kookoo tso ko nɔ? Kɛji mitaaa ekoo tso lɛ he?

english: Crop diseases can travel through wind, flowing rainwater, or on muddy boots and farm tools that carry contaminated soil from one farm to another.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ nu mli loo yɛ muji atadei kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same spot allows pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to build up in the soil and multiply.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that crops need to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there are no shade trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight; larger shade trees protect them from intense heat until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni edara lɛ haa hulutsoo, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce tiny tubers when I plant the sticks very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots compete for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving less energy to grow large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ babaoo aba ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when rainwater collects and stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe; when water covers the soil for too long, it smothers the roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetables grow slowly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your vegetables.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-vegetables lɛ waa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the heat burns the leaves and dries out the plant before its roots can grow deep into the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Dɔlɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ tso lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: If too many shoots grow from one plantain stump, they all fight for the same water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only the strongest stem, which helps produce much larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli Tso kome pɛ baatswa akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ plantain ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of leaves spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ baai ni baagbee shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up toward the sun to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking keeps the leaves dry and clean, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the crop build bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛha bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛhe atse. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water sits on my field after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay alive. When heavy water stays on the soil without draining, the roots drown from lack of oxygen, allowing rot fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji akɛ muji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plant turn yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen fertilizer. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new green growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This provides free plant food for the maize growing next to it.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and weak near that weed with pinkish-purple flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, also known as witchweed. It is a parasite that connects its roots directly to your maize roots underground, stealing all the water and food before the maize can use it.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji striga. Ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ tsaa oshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni ejuɔ dani akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into a bowl shape on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɛnsi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves on a hot afternoon is a crop's natural way of protecting itself. By curling its leaves, the plant hides part of its surface area from the hot sun to stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehiɛ fã ko teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they face stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients. If the plant feels it does not have enough water or food to support fruit, it drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ kɛha aduawai lɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cabbages stay loose and leafy instead of forming hard round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ etse ehe ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to wrap tightly when the plants get too much shade, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. High heat can also cause the leaves to stay loose rather than fold tightly over the center.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the energy it needs to stay green and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ebɔle he lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewaa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. This acts as a natural food source for nearby maize plants without harming them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni eyeee amɛ awui.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on top of the soil around my vegetables keep them from wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mi-vegetables lɛ akagbo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which shades the soil, keeps ground temperatures cool, and prevents water from evaporating too quickly so the plant roots stay hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my crop seeds sometimes rot in the dirt if I plant them immediately after a single heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa shikome pɛ sɛɛ?

english: A heavy rain can flood the soil and push out all the air pockets, suffocating seeds before they sprout. Waiting until the ground settles and drains slightly gives seeds the balance of air and moisture they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ ajie kɛje kpo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ ni nu fioo ajɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ baaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni ataoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to prune away some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Extra sucker shoots steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main plantain stem. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem produces a big, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ woɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food that builds large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground, where they get full sun and stay safe from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot quickly if I leave them in the ground during a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme drought and hot soil stress the mature cassava plant, making the underground roots lose moisture and become vulnerable to rotting fungi in the earth.
ga: Hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their young flowers before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry winds, or a lack of natural shade and insect pollinators like midges. Maintaining shade trees helps protect the flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. kɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ midges. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars appear in large numbers and chew holes inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo babaoo ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs inside the leaf funnel of maize. Checking plants early and applying organic neem oil mixtures or proper treatments into the leaf whorl helps save the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ organic neem fɔ ni akɛfutu loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there aren't enough insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing leaves room for each plant to grow strong and yield larger crops.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni edara waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them for protection during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Kɛha hebuu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets plant diseases build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. kɛ tsei ahe helai ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my corn leaves and hiding inside the top funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the leaves at the center of the plant to feed safely away from predators.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in heavy soil for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water drain and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl and droop in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu ewo mli?

english: Pepper plants droop during hot hours to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, saving internal moisture until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifee mitso titri lɛ bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and steal soil food, water, and sunlight before your main crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni oju niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my dry soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure adds organic matter that acts like a sponge, holding water in dry soil longer while slowly releasing nutrients that feed crop roots over time.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji fataa he. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the borehole water on my farm is good enough for watering my vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nubu lɛ mli lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: If your water is soft and clean, it is generally good for crops. However, hard water contains high amounts of minerals like calcium that can build up in the soil and prevent your crops from taking in food properly.
ga: Kɛji onu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ehe tse Bei pii lɛ Enɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛlɛ, minerals babaoo yɛ nu ni wa mli, tamɔ calcium, ni baanyɛ abua naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛná niyenii kpakpa.

english: Can using hard well water affect how my crop fertilizers work?
ga: Ani nu bu mli nu ni wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aná bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii eha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, hard water has extra minerals that can lock up fertilizer nutrients, making it harder for your crop roots to absorb the fertilizer you apply.
ga: Hɛɛ, minerals krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɛ nu ni wa mli. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: What is an easy way to tell if river water is safe to spray on my leafy crops?
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ aleɔ kɛji faa mli nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ mi tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Check the water early in the morning for clear color and fresh smell, and ensure it isn't hard or filled with heavy scum, which can block plant leaves and spread rot.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nu lɛ mli leebi kɛji eyɛ su ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa. Ni kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ akafee fɛ̃i loo jwɛi babaoo akayi mli obɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei ahe baai anaa ni egbɛ fitemɔ eshwa.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to test my farm water early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ maka nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Early morning is the best time because oxygen levels in the water are at their lowest point after the night. Testing then gives you the most accurate baseline before sunlight begins to change the water's balance.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baa shi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ sɛɛ. Kaa lɛ haa shishijee nikanemɔ ni ja fe fɛɛ dani hulu la lɛ jeɔ shishi etsakeɔ nu lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Does sunshine help add air and oxygen into my irrigation water?
ga: Ani hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa fataa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, sunshine helps small organisms and tiny green plants living in the water create fresh oxygen during the day, which makes the water healthier for plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la yeɔ ebuaa nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Nu lɛ mli shihilɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛha shishifãi ni aduɔ.

english: Why do my crops and soil seem to need more air during the night than during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo gbɛkɛ fe shwane lɛ?

english: During the day, sunlight allows plants to produce fresh oxygen. At night, when there is no sun, plants and soil microbes only consume oxygen, lowering the available air in the root zone.
ga: Yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni he tse. Gbi gbɛkɛ, beni hulu la bɛ lɛ, Tsei kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ pɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is oxygen in the irrigation water so important for my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ mi nu ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen to breathe and absorb nutrients effectively. Water with low oxygen can cause roots to suffocate, turn black, and rot.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: How does strong sunlight affect the green scum growing in my farm pond?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa jwɛi eŋɔli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The green scum is made of algae, which act like tiny plants. Strong sunlight makes them grow faster and release oxygen into the water during daytime hours.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei bibii feɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi eŋɔli nɛɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛyaa nu lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is the green moss growing on top of my water tank dangerous for my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi nu ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: A small amount of green moss or algae produces oxygen under the sun, but too much can clog your drip pipes and steal oxygen from the water during the night.
ga: Mos loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa hulu lɛ shishi. Shi kɛ́ eshɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ paipi ni hoɔ nu lɛ naa ni eju kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa nu lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do oxygen levels in my fish pond or water storage change from high to low throughout the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen ni yɔɔ loo nubu loo nubu mli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shishi yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oxygen rises high during sunny hours because green algae produce it, but it drops low at night because everything in the water uses up the oxygen while no new air is being made.
ga: Oxygen lɛ fa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ oxygen. Shi ebaa shi gbɛkɛ ejaakɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hee ko bɛ ni abɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when there are no bigger plants grown around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting taller crops like plantains alongside them creates shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the tender young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe Kɛyashi tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many green leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has to its newest top leaves to survive, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my land yield less food when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific nutrients in the dirt. Planting it in the same place every season strips the soil of those nutrients, but rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the land naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akaná nakai niyenii kpakpai lɛ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season drops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell. If you plant too quickly, the seeds will sprout from the temporary wetness and then die when the dry weather returns before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui baaje kpo kɛjɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. ni egbo beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for space, sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Even with heavy rain, the weeds steal the nutrients before your crop's roots can drink them up.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ, shi jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii mli nibii dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize crops mostly during the night and hide during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli babaoo gbɛkɛ ni amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms dislike direct sunlight and extreme daytime heat. They hide inside the leaves or under the soil during the day to stay cool and come out at night or early morning to feed on leaves safely.
ga: Armyworms sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbi mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. ni oje kpo gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa koni oye baai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough steady water. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing it to fall off before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Is it good for my crops if I plant groundnuts in between my cassava rows?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, groundnuts work well with cassava because groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This enriches the ground and gives food to the cassava without taking away its growing space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni ejieee he ni eyɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved in a bag from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku mli kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or damp conditions absorb moisture and rot or lose their life energy over time. Storing seeds in airtight containers in a cool, dry place preserves their ability to germinate strong plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto shihilɛi ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaŋɔ hulutsoo ni amɛgboi loo amɛwala hewalɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool, moist soil it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their dark green color and energy, so when soil runs low, the plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa amɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil richer for the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots decay in the ground, that nitrogen is left behind in the soil to nourish future crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ gboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ashiɔ nakai nitrogen lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps cool the root zone so flowers can form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper crop curling up and puckering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled or twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaf surfaces. Spraying appropriate organic or recommended sprays controls these pests so new leaves grow out healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni etse ehe loo etsɔ ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai fɔji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Enɛ baaha baai heei akwɛ̃, ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does it matter which end of a cassava stick I put into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmei naagbee esa akɛ adu?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the stem buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stem cuttings upside down forces new shoots to waste energy turning around underground, resulting in weaker plants and small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso wulu lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei lɛ afite amɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yitsei bibii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles or stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso loo tso ko ama emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves off the soil and reach direct sunlight. Exposing more leaf surface to sunlight allows the yam plant to make maximum food energy, leading to much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ anɔ hulu la babaoo lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds when my crops are still small seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwu bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, delicate root systems and cannot easily compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Early weeding gives young plants full access to soil nourishment so they can grow strong roots.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ mlɛo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Koni shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look wilted during the middle of the day even if the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce water loss, and it usually recovers automatically once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ajɛɔ tsuiŋ agbeɔ tsei koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize stalks are completely ready to harvest for dry grain storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-abele tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛha ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for dry grain harvest when the outer husks turn completely light brown and dry, the silks turn dark brown, and a small dark black layer forms at the bottom tip of each corn grain kernel.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ akpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Siliki lɛ etsɔ asarasu ni tsuɔ waa. kɛ ŋmei diŋ bibioo ko Feɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishigbɛ naagbee.

english: How many weeks after planting my maize should I apply the first batch of fertilizer?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu ŋmãa lɛ esa akɛ akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ awo mli?

english: You should apply your first fertilizer about three to four weeks after planting. At this early stage, the young shoots have established roots and need extra nutrients to build strong stems and leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii feɔ shishifãi ni amɛbiɔ niyenii krokomɛi koni amɛfee ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why are the roots and stems of my cassava plants turning soft and rotten underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Soft or mushy roots and stems are usually caused by root rot disease, often triggered by water staying too long in the soil. Improving drainage and planting disease-resistant cuttings helps keep the stems and roots firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni egbo lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ehi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and soil moisture, protecting young cocoa seedlings during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hia kɛ sũ mli nu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why should I leave measured space between my plants instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mitsei lɛ anaa moŋ fe ni mabua amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives every plant enough room for its roots to spread and its leaves to catch sunlight. When plants are crowded, they compete for food and produce thin, weak stems.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni baai lɛ hu aná hulu la. Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds three to four weeks after planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal light, water, and nutrients from young crops. Clearing them three to four weeks after planting gives your crop the chance to grow strong leaves without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do insects attack the stems of my young seedlings as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ tutuaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Young shoots and seedlings have soft, tender stems filled with water and sap, making them easy food for insects. Clearing weeds around the farm perimeter early reduces hiding places for these pests.
ga: Tsobii bibii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu kɛ nu eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi bibii baatsɔ niyenii Ejieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Ebaaye ebua ni hei ni kooloi bibii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I test if my soil has the right moisture before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil in your palm. If it forms a loose ball that stays together without dripping water, it is ideal; if water squirts out, it is too wet, and if it crumbles like dust, it is too dry.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko yɛ onine nɔ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni etse ehe ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eja jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu je kpo lɛ Etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ Ni kɛji egbɛ eshwa tamɔ sũ Etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, planted in dry soil, or eaten by soil insects. Planting seeds at a shallow depth about as long as your thumb joint helps them break through the soil easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ Dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ oshishifa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: How do underground root crops like yams gain enough strength to swell into big tubers?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji?

english: Yam tubers grow large by storing energy produced by their green leaves above ground. Keeping the vine leaves healthy and growing in loose, well-drained soil gives tubers space to expand.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ daa kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni baai eŋɔli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ni amɛtoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ wein tso lɛ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ejɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ náa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their sensitive leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil cool and moist. Removing all shade trees exposes young cocoa to extreme heat stress and drying winds, which quickly kills them.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ mli baa. ni gbeɔ amɛ oya lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving too many side shoots (suckers) causes them to steal food and water from the main plant. Pruning them down to just one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nutrients to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil is lacking nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to build strong leaves; when soil runs out of it, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ebaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwie shi lɛ, tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the central leaf whorl of young maize plants to feed on leaves before the corn cob forms, which can destroy the farm if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni eye baai lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ afee. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔ ko kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: How does adding dried poultry manure help my farm crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifã ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure acts as a natural soil food that supplies essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. It also improves the soil's ability to hold water, making roots stronger and helping crops survive short dry spells.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground during the peak rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents the roots from breathing and encourages soil-borne fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking holds the yam leaves up toward the sunlight and off the wet ground. Leaves that get maximum sunlight produce more food, which travels down to make larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akashɛ hulu lɛ he kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Baai ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ waa lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer can cause tomato plants to drop their flowers. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that transmit viruses. These insects feed on leaf sap, causing the leaf tissue to wrinkle and stunt fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni hiɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli nu. Ehaa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my garden crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate before reaching plant roots. Water droplets left on leaves can also heat up and scorch the leaves or trigger fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha baai lɛ adɔ ni eshã amɛ loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Why do some pepper farmers dry their fresh harvest instead of taking it straight to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper okwaafoi komɛi fɔ̃ɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh peppers rot quickly and drop in price when everyone is harvesting at the same time. Drying preserves the pepper, allows you to store it safely for months, and lets you sell when market prices go up.
ga: Pepper heei fiteɔ oya ni ejara baa shi kɛ́ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kpa yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. Ehaa okɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo. Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ nii kɛ́ jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi.

english: What is the benefit of grinding my dried pepper into powder before selling it?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni ashwieɔ mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he?

english: Turning dried pepper into powder is called value addition. It increases your selling price, attracts buyers like restaurants and households who want ready-to-use spices, and extends the shelf life even further.
ga: Atsɛɔ chili ni egbi ni atsakeɔ awoɔ powda mli lɛ akɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛfataa he. Ehaa onihɔɔmɔ jara lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ni agbalaa mɛi ni heɔ nii tamɔ niyelihei kɛ shiabii ni he hiaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii klalo lɛ kɛyaa shĩa lɛ mli kɛyaa shɔŋŋ po.

english: What is the best way to dry my harvested peppers so they do not rot or turn mouldy?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ogbi o-peppers ni okpa lɛ koni ekafite loo ekafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Spread the peppers evenly in a single layer on raised drying nets or clean tarpaulins under direct sunlight. Turn them regularly so air reaches all sides and moisture does not get trapped underneath.
ga: Jaa ŋmeii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okɛto he kome yɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni awo nɔ loo tarp ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsɔɔmɔ lɛ daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ayashɛ he fɛɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ akamɔ shishi.

english: How long does a pepper crop yield after it starts producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔtɔ baawo yibii beni ebɔi yibiiwoo sɛɛ?

english: Once pepper plants begin fruiting, you can harvest them continuously every week for about 6 to 12 weeks or more, depending on how well you water, fertilize, and care for the soil.
ga: Beni pepper tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi Obaanyɛ oya nɔ okpa daa otsi aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 12 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Edamɔ bɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli, ni okwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my peppers are ready to be picked from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peppers lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Peppers are ready to pick when they are firm and have reached full size, turning bright red or deep green depending on the variety market demand. Picking regularly encourages the plant to keep growing new peppers.
ga: Afee klalo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii kɛji amɛwa ni amɛdara. Tsakemɔ kɛya tsuru ni mli tse loo eŋɔli ni mli edɔ nɔ Edamɔ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eya nɔ ekwɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why am I harvesting very few bags of pepper while my neighbour gets several tons from the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpa ŋmɔtɔ kotokui fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ tɔni babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Higher yields depend on proper spacing, adequate water during flowering, using healthy seed varieties, and protecting crops from pests and diseases early in their growth.
ga: Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ damɔ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Should I sell my farm produce fresh right after harvest or process it first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii heei ni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo matsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Selling fresh gives you immediate cash but leaves you at the mercy of daily market prices. Processing gives you flexibility to wait for better prices and earn more profit per kilogram.
ga: Live sales baaha oná shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ekɛ bo woɔ daa gbi jarayeli jara lɛ mɔbɔnalɛ shishi. Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ haa onáa hegbɛ ni omɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni onáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ kilogram kome mli.

english: How should I handle my harvested crops on the farm before sending them to the market?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Sort your crops immediately after picking by removing damaged, diseased, or insect-bitten ones. Clean the healthy ones and pack them in ventilated crates or sacks to avoid crushing them on the way to the market.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ onibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ogbe naa. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni efite, helai, loo kooloi emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe ni okɛwo adekai loo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli koni akakumɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I safely store my pepper powder so it does not lose its strong smell and taste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ pepper powder ato shweshweeshwe? Koni ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akalaaje.

english: Ensure the pepper is completely dry before grinding, then store the powder in clean, airtight plastic containers or sealed bags kept in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsu nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ powda lɛ awo plastic tsinsii loo kotoku ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Do I need expensive machines to start turning my harvested crops into powder?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni jara wa he miihia mi koni mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ atsakemɔ afee powda?

english: No, you do not need expensive machinery to start. You can dry your harvest naturally under the sun and use community grinding mills or small local processing machines to grind it into fine powder.
ga: Dabi, tsɔnei ni jara wa he ehiaaa bo koni onyɛ oje shishi. Obaanyɛ ogbi onibii lɛ yɛ hulu la shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni okɛ akutsoŋ tsɔnei ni akɛshãa nii loo maŋ lɛ mli tsɔnei bibii ni akɛshãa nii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛshã amɛ ni amɛfee powda kpakpa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen early in its life to build strong green leaves for feeding the plant; adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmei yɛ eshihilɛ shishijee mli koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves, or a virus they transmit, which damages the leaves as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ beni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain floods my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess water fills all the empty spaces in the soil, the roots drown and soil fungi quickly invade, turning the soft roots into rotted mush.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyi he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ mli obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii baabote mli oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce much smaller and fewer fruit bunches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms require continuous water to form heavy fruit bunches. During prolonged dry weather, the tree conserves its strength by dropping flowers or delaying fruit formation until rain returns.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tsei hiɛɔ hewalɛ mli kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi loo aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ ni amɛhaa sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the forest trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plantains or shade trees to stay cool and retain moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ plantains loo tsei amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa amɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight and airflow. This extra light energy feeds the underground tuber, while keeping leaves away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo. Nɛkɛ la hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my plantain tree give a small, light bunch when I let all the shoot suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra suckers growing around the main plantain stem steal food, water, and sunlight from the mother tree. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the main stem with full energy to grow a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krɛdɛɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Plantain tso titri lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee aduawai akuu ni tsii.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato bibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often shed their blossoms when the air gets too hot or dry. High heat stresses the plant, preventing pollen from fertilizing the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I see small holes in the center funnel of my maize plant with tiny brownish dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ, muji fioo ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the tender growing center of the maize plant during the day, chewing the soft leaves before they unroll.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oooye dani ojie amɛ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody when I leave them in the ground for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: As a cassava root grows older past its prime harvest age, the soft starch transforms into tough wood fibers (lignin), making the tuber hard, fibrous, and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ eda, ni kpamɔ be ni sa lɛ eho lɛ, Soft starch lɛ tsɔɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa (lignin), ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni wa, ŋmeii, ni ewaa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients out of the root area. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow well at first, but produce much smaller yields when I plant on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating your crops with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains on the same plot as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting the soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my maize, or will they fight each other in the soil?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa afee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaawuu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: You can plant them together if spaced properly because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava takes over the space without losing yields.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome kɛji akɛ okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa lɛ, Cassava baaye jɛmɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ baafite.

english: What is causing small black insects to gather under my cassava leaves and make them curl up?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii diji buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: These insects are pests like aphids that suck liquid from the leaves, weakening the plant and spreading diseases. Spraying the leaves early with neem water or recommended extension sprays controls them before damage spreads.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aphids, ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ lɛ dani nɔ ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are white powdery spots spreading on the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miigbɛ eshwa ŋshɔŋlooi ahe baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called powdery mildew that develops when plants are packed too closely together in humid weather. Spacing your plants and trimming lower leaves lets air flow freely, preventing the fungus from taking hold.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ni baa kɛ́ tsei ebua amɛhe naa tsɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Afoɔ gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from extreme sun heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering during dry spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers splitting open inside the mound before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli gbalaa kɛfeɔ gɔji dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when heavy rains follow a dry spell, causing the inside of the tuber to expand faster than the skin can stretch. Keeping mulch over the mounds keeps soil moisture steady and prevents sudden growth spurts.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo okpɔŋɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa trukaa.

english: How do I know the ground is ready for seed planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best not to plant right after the very first rain because the deep soil underneath is still dry and hot. Waiting until the soil receives two or three good rains ensures there is enough lasting moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo ni edɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa fioo ko koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato nursery seedlings growing tall and thin like threads instead of standing strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo tamɔ kpãai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out thin when they do not receive enough direct sunlight or are overcrowded in the nursery bed. Giving nursery beds full morning sunlight and thinning out extra seedlings encourages thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe bibii kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛyɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ hulu la ba ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ leebi, ni afolɔ dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear my farm field?
