ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for a long time. When you clear the land, sunlight hits the soil directly, which wakes up these hidden seeds and makes them germinate rapidly before your crops can cover the ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Hulu la lɛ baatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baate dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ shi. ni oha ekwɛ̃ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How exactly do weeds harm my yam crops if they are just growing nearby?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi sweet potato tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your yams for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. If you leave them, the weeds will steal the food your yams need, leading to very small tubers at harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ sweet potatoes yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛji oshi lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baaju niyenii ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ. Ewoɔ bulbs bibii waa kɛji akpa.

english: Is it better to burn cleared bushes on my land or leave them to dry on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo maha amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving cleared bushes to rot on the soil creates mulch, which keeps the soil moist in the hot sun and turns into rich natural food for your crops, whereas burning destroys good soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii ni he tse ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo kɛha onibii. yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ sũ mli niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to conserve water when there is no rain. This protects the plant from drying out, and it will quickly sprout fresh leaves once the rainy season begins.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akagbi Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant save water and stay alive during extreme heat.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu la ni shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight without protection. They need shade crops like plantains nearby to filter the light while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpee hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛjie la kɛjɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal space, sunlight, and nutrients, while also making it much easier for you to walk through, remove weeds, and apply fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nyiɛmɔ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Can I rely only on chemical fertilizer to get a good crop yield every year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ koni maná yibii kpakpai afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Fertilizer feeds the plants quickly, but it does not improve the soil structure. Adding organic material like decomposed crop leftovers keeps the soil soft and capable of holding water long-term.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsei ni egboi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebaaha nu ahi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji komɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning extra stems forces the tomato plant to send its energy directly into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, tomato tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni ewo aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Can I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can, but saved seeds often produce weaker plants and lower yields than fresh certified seeds, which are specially bred to fight off local diseases and resist drought.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ. Atsɔse amɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai awuu, ni amɛte shi amɛwo hɔmɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant fewer crops with proper spacing instead of crowding as many as possible on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du tsohi fuu ngɛ ye zugba ɔ nɔ bɔ nɛ ma nyɛ.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting fewer crops with good spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to grow strong, stay healthy, and produce a higher total yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei fioo ni aduɔ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei fɛɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛdalɛ kpakpa. Ha ohe ajɔ bo ni ofee nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ

english: How does planting my crops at the very start of the major rainy season affect their yield?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ saa yibiiwoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting early in the rainy season allows young seeds to take advantage of consistent soil moisture, helping them establish deep roots and strong foliage before any dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛnáa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa dani hɔmɔ be lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so I can sell it for a good market price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer leaves turn brown and dry and the kernels are hard. Harvesting at full maturity prevents grain rot during storage, allowing you to hold and sell your yield when market prices rise.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛgbi ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ ohiɛɔ nibii ni adu lɛ mli ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara nɔ jara tee hiɛ.

english: How long does cassava usually stay in the soil before it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ?

english: Most cassava varieties need 9 to 12 months to mature. Harvesting too early results in small, watery roots, while waiting too long makes the roots woody and unappealing to buyers.
ga: Kasavas babaoo heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ afee bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tamɔ tsei, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ.

english: What can I do to keep my young tomato seedlings from dying right after transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ akagboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience shock when moved. Transplanting them late in the afternoon or on cloudy days protects them from harsh sunlight while watering them immediately helps their roots settle into the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe efee shoo kɛ́ ajie amɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ baaye abua ni eshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing leaves and flowers even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa baai kɛ fɔfɔii feemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Watering keeps plants hydrated, but plants also need food. If the soil lacks compost or fertilizer, the plant runs out of nutrients and stops producing new leaves and flowers.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ haa tso lɛ mli fũuɔ. Shi niyenii hu he miihia tsei. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebaakpa baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei feemɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra side shoots from my tomato plants while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary branches prevents the plant from wasting nutrients on extra leaves, directing all its energy into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers during severe heat or dry conditions as a survival defense, conserving water and energy until rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu wala he Buu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually signs of pest attack or disease, such as mosaic virus, which damages the leaves and prevents the plant from feeding itself.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba, tamɔ mosaic virus, ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ gbɛ koni ekatao niyenii eha ehe.

english: Are improved high-yield crop seeds better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni atsake lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to mature faster, resist local diseases, and give bigger yields, whereas saved seeds tend to lose vigor and yield less with each passing season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛshwere oya. local disease resistance ni amɛwoɔ babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when a seed seller tells me a seed is a 'hybrid'?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui ahɔ̃ɔlɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ dumɔwui ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid seed is created by breeding two specific plant varieties to combine their best traits, like disease resistance and higher yield. They produce strong crops, but you must buy fresh hybrid seeds every season to keep getting those high yields.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni afɔɔ koni akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ afata he. Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa. Shi esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa afi koni oya nɔ owo nakai yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my corn crops perform poorly when I plant seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from previous harvests—especially from hybrid crops—lose their special strength in the second generation. This leads to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields compared to planting certified fresh seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli—titri lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ—fiteɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ he.

english: How can I simple test if the seeds I bought will actually sprout before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Ma fee kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a damp cloth for a few days. If 8 or 9 sprout, your seeds are healthy and high quality for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ.

english: How far away should I plant my corn from my neighbor's farm so my crop quality is not ruined?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ he ni kɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite?

english: You should leave at least 100 meters between your corn and nearby corn fields. Corn pollen travels easily on the wind, so safe distance prevents unwanted pollen from mixing with your crop.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ oshi mitai 100 yɛ o-ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ateŋ. Abɛi pollen lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fãa gbɛ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baatsi pollen ni otaooo lɛ naa koni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akafutu.

english: Why did my yellow corn harvest end up with mixed white grains on the same cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni mikpaa lɛ naagbee kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This happens due to cross-pollination. Wind blew pollen from a nearby white corn field onto your yellow corn flowers, causing different colored grains to form on the same cob.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ krɔs pollination hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa pollen kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmãa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni hiɛ sui srɔtoi jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmei kome mli.

english: Why does wind matter so much when my corn starts producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa waa beni mi-abele lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Corn relies entirely on wind rather than insects to transfer pollen from the tassels at the top of the plant down to the silks on the cobs. Good air movement is necessary for every grain to form properly.
ga: Abele kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ fe kooloi bibii koni ekɛ pollen kɛjɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ tsɔji lɛ amli kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni nyiɛɔ ehe lɛ he miihia koni ŋmaa fɛɛ ŋmaa afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my corn stalks too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small, poorly filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: How do I know whether my farmland is better suited for planting rice or corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔ?

english: Rice grows best in low-lying, wet soils or valleys that hold water, while corn requires well-drained, fertile soil and will rot if left standing in flooded water.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo jɔɔ lɛ mli shikpɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni baa nii. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my corn look healthy and green but still produces very small cobs with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Incomplete cobs are usually caused by poor pollination during hot or dry periods, or a lack of nutrients right at the stage when tassels and silks are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa ji pollination ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ be mli ni tsɔji kɛ siliki lɛ miifee lɛ

english: Why is water so important for my rice plants right when they start to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need consistent water during flowering because drought at this stage causes the flowers to dry up, leaving you with empty husks instead of grain.
ga: Nu he miihia omɔ tsei daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ejaakɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to build small net cages or shade covers over my seedling beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa trellis loo shade shĩa bibioo ko yɛ midumɔwui lɛ asa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young nursery seedlings are very delicate. Shade covers and net cages protect fragile young plants from scorching sunlight, heavy rainfall that can crush them, and hungry birds or insects while they establish roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa kwraa. Shades kɛ mesh cages buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baanyɛ akumɔ jwɛi kɛ okpoi loo kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ beni amɛtswaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is a crop's natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to the burning sun, helping it preserve moisture and survive intense heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When the plant cannot get enough food from the ground, it pulls stored nutrients from its oldest leaves to feed the young growth on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Egbalaa niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it necessary to apply fertilizer to my cassava, or does cassava grow fine without feeding?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofa awo ŋmei mli? Aloo ani ŋmei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii bɛ mli?

english: While cassava can survive in poor soils, it consumes a lot of nutrients to build tubers. Providing balanced soil nutrients ensures your cassava produces large, heavy roots rather than thin, woody ones.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ moŋ, Shi eheɔ niyenii babaoo dani enyɛɔ efeɔ ŋmei. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni okɛaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛɔ shishifãi wuji ni tsii. Moŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ tso.

english: Why does my cowpea crop have plenty of leafy green growth but almost no seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni dumɔwui ŋmɔji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage with few pods often happens when soil has too much nitrogen. Cowpea plants naturally make their own nitrogen, so giving them extra nitrogen causes them to grow leaves instead of flowers and pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Cowpea tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen kroko ha tso lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akwɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: How can I easily test if my soil has enough water for my vegetables without special tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka mi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mi-vegetables lɛ makwɛ mlɛo ni mikɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi tsuuu nii?

english: Push your finger about two inches into the soil near the plant base. If the soil feels cool and damp and sticks to your skin, it has enough water; if it comes away dry and crumbly, the crop needs watering.
ga: Nyɛɛ oniji anɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nu fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji egbi ni egbɔjɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ.

english: How often should I water my pepper plants during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-pepper tso lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Pepper plants prefer deep watering two to three times a week rather than light daily surface sprinklings. Deep watering encourages roots to grow deeper into the ground where soil stays moist longer.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ sumɔɔ nu ni mli kwɔ shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli, moŋ fe nu ni waaa daa gbi. Nu ni mli kwɔ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers fail to form pods when there are not enough natural insect pollinators around, or when the tree suffers from drought stress, excessive sun exposure, or poor soil nutrition.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ faaa. aloo kɛ́ tso ko miipiŋ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ hewɔ. hulu la ni fa tsɔ loo niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain stems fall over so easily right when the bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛtsiimɔ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can snap or pull free under heavy fruit weight, especially if root pests like nematodes or weevils have damaged the root base or if the soil is loose.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ agbo loo ajɛ mli kɛji aduawai lɛ tsiimɔ wa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ shishifãi amli kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo weevils fite shishifãi lɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse.

english: Why are the bottoms of my sweet pepper fruits turning dark brown and rotted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: Dark, sunken spots on the bottom of peppers are caused by blossom-end rot. This condition occurs when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, typically due to irregular watering routines.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni egbo lɛ. Shihilɛ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why should I remove or clear the leftover crop stems and straw after harvesting my rice field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie loo majie ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ni eshwɛ beni akpa ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing or burning old stalks removes pests and plant diseases that hide in leftover crop residues, preventing them from attacking your next batch of crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei akutsei momoi lɛ loo ashã amɛ lɛ, ebaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkatutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why must I dry my rice thoroughly before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi ŋmãa lɛ dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying removes moisture that mold, fungi, and insects need to survive, which protects your stored grain from rotting or spoiling.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii ahi shi lɛ. Enɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite loo amɛkafite.

english: Is it better to plow healthy leftover rice straw back into the soil or remove it completely?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaaku ŋmãa jwɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ajie kwraa?

english: Plowing healthy straw back into the field adds natural organic material and restores soil nutrients, as long as the previous crop did not suffer from serious diseases.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akuɔ sɛɛ ashɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ni ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni hela ni naa wa ko enaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I test a small batch of seeds before planting my main farm to know if they will grow?
ga: Maka dumɔwui akuu bibioo ko makwɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔ titri lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni mana kɛji dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaakwɛ̃?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing a few seeds in a wet paper or cloth for a few days to count how many sprout, showing you the strength of your seed batch.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 2-3 ni akɛwoɔ wolo loo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 koni akɛkane amɛkwɛ̃mɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli wa ha.

english: Why do some rice seedlings grow much faster and stronger in the first few weeks than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Seedlings grow faster when they come from high-quality seeds planted in well-prepared soil, giving them an early lead over weeds and weather stress.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya kɛji amɛjɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ jwɛi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi oya.

english: Why is it important to level my rice field properly before I begin planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ?

english: Leveling the land builds a proper foundation so water spreads evenly across the farm, preventing some plants from drowning while others dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa shishitoo kpakpa baa bɔni afee ni nu lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi shwieɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer rice grains if I plant on it every year without adding manure or fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmaa fioo kɛji midu nɔ daa afi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Rice draws heavy nutrients out of the earth, so planting continuously without replacing those nutrients weakens the soil foundation and lowers future harvests.
ga: Omɔ gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oya nɔ odu nii ni okɛ nakai niyenii lɛ wooo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so the grains do not fall off and waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ shwieee shi ni efiteee?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn a golden-yellow color and the lower stems begin to dry.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔtɔ. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my rice plants right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ beni adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and aggressive, allowing them to quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before young crop seedlings develop deep roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli ni eyɛ basabasa. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ baawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ

english: Why do my young rice plants turn yellow when water sits on the field for too long without moving?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni eshiuuu ehe lɛ?

english: Rice roots need air to breathe; when water stays trapped and stagnant for too long, the roots begin to suffocate and cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers always advise me to plant plantain trees on the same land where I am starting my young cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mibɔi kookoo dumɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can wither easily. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide temporary shade to protect young cocoa seedlings while also providing food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛ shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting too closely causes trees to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak trees that produce fewer pods and spread diseases faster due to poor airflow.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to spray my cocoa trees regularly even when I do not see any visible insects on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu afɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ? Ani onaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Regular spraying helps prevent hidden pests like mirids (capsids) and fungal diseases like black pod before they destroy flowers and pods. Prevention keeps the trees healthy and protects your total harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ mirids (capsids) kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ anaa dani amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔii kɛ pods. Nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ onibii fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by excess humidity, heavy shade, or poor drainage. Clearing weeds and pruning branches helps air circulate and reduces this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal helai ni fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine, shade ni tsii, loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa naagba nɛɛ baa shi.

english: How can government programs like COCOBOD help me manage the costs of running my cocoa farm?
ga: Te nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko tamɔ COCOBOD lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ shika ni mikɛtsuɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he nii lɛ nɔ?

english: COCOBOD and local agricultural extensions offer subsidised farm inputs, free or low-cost cocoa seedlings, mass spraying services, and technical advice to help reduce your expenses and increase yields.
ga: COCOBOD kɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa. Cocoa dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko loo ni jara waaa Mass spraying service kɛ ŋaawoo ni baaye abua ni shika aba shi ni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Can I get assistance or farming advice from extension officers if I choose to farm plantains instead of cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná okwaayeli he yelikɛbuamɔ loo ŋaawoo kɛjɛ extension nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ? Kɛji mihala akɛ makwɛ plantain yɛ kookoo najiaŋ

english: Yes, government agricultural support programs cover major food crops alongside cocoa, providing guidance, improved planting materials, and pest management support to ensure food security.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɔɔ niyenii titrii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe kɛfataa kookoo he. ŋaawoo ni akɛhaa Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ koni niyenii ahi shi.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees when they are growing so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight to reach the trunk where pods grow, improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases, and directs the plant's energy into producing bigger pods rather than extra foliage.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa. ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ baai babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during heavy rains without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Excessive moisture, low sunlight, or insect damage during heavy rain can cause flower drop. Proper field drainage and timely pest control help flowers successfully turn into pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine, hulu la ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: How does clearing weeds around my young plantain and cocoa plants help them grow faster?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cacao dumɔwui kɛ tsei lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: Weeds steal essential water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from young crops. Clearing the base of your plants ensures all available nutrients go directly into growing strong stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli Otso lɛ shishi ni ooojie lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni miida ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods every year even though I care for them the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ lɛ yeɔ nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural productivity declines and disease risk increases. Replacing aging trees with modern, high-yielding seedlings helps restore long-term harvest production.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, nɔ ni ekɛbaa lɛ baa shi, ni helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo baatsake lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmaa lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I dig them up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they get bruised during harvest or if they are stored in warm, poorly ventilated places. Storing them off the ground on raised wooden structures in a shaded, cool barn allows air to circulate and keeps them dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil within just a few days in the market basket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ bafee blɛoo ni efite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛhi jarayeli tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tomatoes give off heat and natural ripening gases after being picked. When squeezed tightly into deep baskets under the sun, heat gets trapped inside, causing them to crush and decay rapidly.
ga: Tomato jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akpɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ shiŋŋ yɛ tsɛnsi ni mli kwɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi lɛ, Dɔlɛ ŋmɛɔ emli. Enɛ haa tsɛnsi lɛ gbáa ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water evaporation when the sun is hottest. Once the evening cool sets in or rain falls, the leaves unroll again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Beni fɛ̃i loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and die off quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need a lot of moisture to sustain all their large leaves. During dry periods, the plant voluntarily drops its older leaves to conserve water for its core stem and fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains he miihia ŋmɔtɔ babaoo koni amɛbaai wuji lɛ ahi shi. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei jɛɔ amɛsuɔmɔ mli amɛshwieɔ baai momoi koni amɛkɛto nu he kɛha aduawai lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience high temperatures, irregular watering, or too much rich fertilizer, which causes the plant to spend its energy growing stems instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mli Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still attached to the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ? Ani ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi lolo?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and deep shade. Clearing tall weeds and trimming shade branches lets air and sunlight reach the pods to prevent this.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Jwɛi kakadaji ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ tsiɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many dark green leaves but producing almost no bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi eshɛɛɛ pea ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing big leaf canopy rather than flowering and bearing pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaabi ni tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii agbo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods baa lɛ

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall and thin without yielding many okra pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ shi ewooo okra babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Okra requires direct sunlight on all sides to branch out and bear fruit. When planted too close together, they shade each other out and stretch upward to fight for light instead of producing yield.
ga: Okra he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ efãi fɛɛ koni enyɛ ewo niji ni ewo yibii. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee amɛhe shade ni amɛbaakpã amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛye la he akaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does my cassava turn tough and woody instead of soft when boiled if I leave it in the farm for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso moŋ fe ni eeefee blɛoo kɛji ahoo lɛ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living storage organs. As the plant gets older, the soft starch gradually converts into tough woody fiber, making the tubers hard and unpalatable.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso mli nibii ni kɛ wala yibii toɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ da lɛ Ashikishaŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baatsake fiofio ni etsɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa Enɛ haa efeɔ tsitsi ni ehiɛ kpaaa nɔ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread along the surface of the soil instead of growing upward like other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ tamɔ tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes are naturally creeping vines. Spreading along the ground allows their stems to touch moist soil, form roots at different points, and produce extra tuberous roots under the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpeɔ. Bɔɔ shishifãi yɛ hei srɔtoi ni obaanyɛ ofee shishifãi krɛdɛɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Can I allow my farm chickens to walk around freely in my young cocoa field?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha ŋmɔ mli kooloi ayashara shi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, allowing chickens to roam in your cocoa farm can help control insect pests and provide rich natural manure through their droppings, though you must monitor them so they do not scratch up fresh seedling roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oŋmɛ kooloi gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ o-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eye kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aha kɛtsɔ amɛmli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okafo dumɔwui heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ moŋ.

english: Is chicken manure good for feeding my growing crops, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo ebaafite loo efiteee?

english: Chicken manure is excellent plant food because it is high in nitrogen, but it must be dried or composted first before applying; fresh manure is too strong and can burn plant roots.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei ji tso niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shi esa akɛ agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani akɛfata he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are developing properly and healthily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa seedlings will display firm green leaves, a strong upright stem, and periodic flushes of new reddish or pale leaves at the top indicating fresh growth.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli wa, eŋɔli. Tso lɛ damɔ shi ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Ni yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, baai tsuru loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ damɔ shi kɛha dalɛ hee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and turning brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight; they require temporary shade from plantain trees or nurse plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei bibii adɛŋ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Is it better to plant cocoa seeds straight into the field or start them in nursery bags first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu kookoo yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɔne mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting cocoa in nursery polybags gives seedlings a strong root system and protection during their weakest stage, leading to higher survival rates when transplanted into the field.
ga: Kookoo ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ poly grow bags mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ hebuu yɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibii babaoo baa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli.

english: What kind of food or nutrients do cocoa trees need to grow strong and bear good fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii loo niyenii kpakpai he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees require nitrogen for leaf and stem growth, phosphorus for root development, and potassium for pod formation and disease resistance, which can be supplied through compost or cocoa fertilizers.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia cacao tsei koni amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adara. Phosphorus kɛha shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ potassium kɛha pod feemɔ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs naturally if the tree lacks proper nutrients, suffers from dry weather stress, or lacks tiny pollinating insects (midges) in the farm environment.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli loo pollinators bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my crops little by little even after I clean the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛmiiba miŋmɔshi nibii amli fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Pests naturally migrate from surrounding bushes or neighboring farms in search of food; continuous weed control and regular field inspection are necessary to keep their populations low.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli loo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ daa he miihia koni gbɔmɛi ayibɔ akafee bibioo.

english: Why is it important for me to prune the tall branches of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ niji kakadaji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach the lower trunk, which reduces humidity and helps prevent pod rot diseases like black pod.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua ni atsĩ pod rot helai tamɔ pod diji lɛ anaa.

english: Can I plant cash crops like cassava right next to my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe?

english: While fast-growing crops like plantain provide helpful shade, competitive crops like cassava draw heavy moisture and nutrients away from cocoa roots and should be spaced far enough apart.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nɛkɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daa oya nɛɛ haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ moŋ, shi tsei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli tamɔ ŋmei lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. ni esa akɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he ko ni sa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, strong sunlight. Taller trees and plantain crops provide essential shade and moisture, keeping the soil cool and protecting the fragile young cocoa leaves from scorching until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ kɛ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I make my cassava plants produce big tuber roots instead of just growing tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava tso lɛ aná bulbs wuji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ baai babaoo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves. Adding balanced potassium-rich organic manure or fertilizer directs the plant's energy down into building thick, heavy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo potassium ni falɛ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and rot at the base after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants suffer from root rot when water collects around their stems. Excessive moisture allows fungal diseases in the soil to attack the roots; planting peppers on raised soil mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ naa shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he amanehulu kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛtso lɛ he. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Consistent watering and mulching the soil to keep it cool helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial microbes in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, this extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: If I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next year, why will my harvest be poor?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to yield high harvests for one season only. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: What happens to my yams if I plant the mounds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potatoes lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ mi-mounds lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting yam mounds too close together forces the vines to compete for sunlight and causes the roots to fight for underground space and nutrients. Giving mounds enough space allows each plant to capture sunlight and produce larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha wain tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Ni enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai amli. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nyɛɔ emɔɔ hulu la ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tight as a self-defense mechanism to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun and prevent water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai fɔ̃ɔ shi shiŋŋ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch becomes large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top weight pulls the plant down, so supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop fork keeps it standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ Muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know that my groundnut crop is mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanut tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up, and when you open sample pods to find that the inside lining of the shell has developed dark brown or black veins around full seeds.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele sample pod ko ni ona akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbɛ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they need to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot under the ground when the soil stays too wet for long periods. Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots and encourages fungal diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ahe helai hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Keeping the field clear of weeds helps reduce these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or sudden changes in water supply, such as a long dry spell followed by heavy watering. This stress causes the plant to abort the flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu egbi ni nu babaoo nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward light to make food through their leaves. Using stakes lifts the foliage high off the ground where it gets plenty of sunlight and air circulation, leading to bigger tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ. Ekɛ tubers wuji yaa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and space. Removing most of them and leaving just one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce a much larger bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ he ko. Kɛ́ ajie amɛteŋ babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves dry up and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds rapidly pull moisture out of both the soil and the plant leaves. Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry spells to protect themselves from losing too much water and drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ ni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why does swamp rice produce better when it stays covered in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo ha nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have adapted to grow in shallow standing water, which keeps the soil consistently hydrated and naturally suffocates ground weeds that would otherwise steal light and nutrients from the rice.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ etsake ehe koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baanyɛ aju la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ omɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the roots and leaves decompose, they leave this natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Abaashi Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ dumɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables stay small when I plant seeds too close together in the bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough resources to grow to its full size.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ha gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli.

english: I have always planted my crops in July because that is when the rains come, so why are my crops failing now even when I plant in July?
ga: Miduɔ yɛ July mli be fɛɛ be ejaakɛ no mli lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite bianɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ July mli moŋ?

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana have shifted over time due to climate change. July rains may now arrive late, end early, or be unpredictable, so relying strictly on traditional calendar months can cause crops to dry up. It is better to check current weather forecasts and soil moisture before planting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ etsake yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Amrɔ nɛɛ July nugbɔ baanyɛ aba sɛɛ mli, eba naagbee mra loo efee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. No hewɔ lɛ, kusum kalanda nyɔji lɛ anɔyeli Gbɛjianɔtoi ni mli wa waa baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be dani odu.

english: What will happen to my seeds if I plant them in dry soil before the rains actually start?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Seeds need water to sprout. If you plant in dry soil, extreme heat and insects can destroy the seeds before it rains, or a light shower might start germination without giving enough moisture to keep the seedling alive.
ga: Nu he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite dumɔwui dani nugbɔ po anɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi lɛ haaa.

english: How do I know the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Dig down about a hand's length into the soil and squeeze a handful of earth. If it forms a ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ aaafee ŋmei tso kome kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo ko ajie mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: An agrochemical seller told me that spraying a specific chemical will keep my crops alive even if it doesn't rain. Is this true?
ga: Mɔ ko ni hɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai komɛi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po. Ani enɛ ji anɔkwale?

english: No chemical can replace water. Plants need soil moisture to drink and absorb nutrients. Spraying chemicals on dry crops during a drought can actually scorch and kill the plants.
ga: Tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ aye nu najiaŋ. Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu koni amɛnu nu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni egbi lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ni egbe amɛ.

english: How can I tell if a chemical seller is giving me genuine advice for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa-kɛ-ŋma jarayelɔ ko miiwo ŋaa yɛ anɔkwale mli yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Chemical sellers are businessmen who want to sell products, so they may recommend chemicals you do not need. It is always safer to confirm chemical advice with your local agricultural extension officer before spending your money.
ga: Mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ tsofai lɛ ji jarayelɔi ni miisumɔ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ nibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa bo aba. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be kɛji akɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ ma tsofai ahe ŋaawoi lɛ anɔ mi dani ofite shika.

english: Why did my crops burn after I applied fertilizer during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsi ni nu bɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil. Without water, the concentrated fertilizer salts sit around the roots and pull moisture out of the plant, causing the leaves to burn and wither.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ

english: Why should I visit the district agriculture office when my family has farmed this land for generations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ? Akɛni miweku lɛ etsu shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nii kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo hewɔ lɛ?

english: While traditional experience is valuable, weather patterns, soil health, and plant diseases have changed over time. Extension officers provide modern, proven methods to help you get better yields under today's changing climate conditions.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema niiashikpamɔi he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ moŋ Shi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ, kɛ tsei ahe helai tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli ni baaye abua bo ni oná yibii kpakpai yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ mli.

english: What kind of free support can I get if I go to the local agriculture office in my area?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni aheee nɔ ko manyɛ maná kɛji mitee okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ?

english: Agriculture offices offer guidance on the best crop varieties for your area, correct fertilizer application, pest and disease management, and accurate weather updates to help you plan your planting season.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ ŋaawoo haa yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Pest kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ja ni baaye abua bo ni oto be ni okɛbaakwɛ nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year even though I do everything the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mifeɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly without adding nutrients or rotating crops wears out the soil and allows pests to build up. Soil needs crop rotation and proper organic or mineral nutrients to stay fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Kɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fataaa he lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ biɔ ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo mineral niyenii koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can spraying weedicide completely replace clearing and preparing my land before planting?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni asaa he dani aduɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Weedicides only kill weeds; they do not loosen tight soil. Clearing and properly tilling the land allows young crop roots to spread easily and absorb water and air efficiently.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi pɛ. Amɛŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your trees are either missing key nutrients from the soil, getting too much or too little water, or suffering from a root disease that prevents them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ooona? Aloo eji shishifã hela ko ni haaa anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: How can I tell if a sick plant on my farm is spreading a disease to other healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbɛ hela amɛmiishwa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli?

english: If you notice similar symptoms—like black spots, wilted leaves, or rotting pods—moving from one plant to nearby plants over time, a contagious disease or pest is likely spreading across your farm.
ga: Kɛji ona okadii ni tamɔ nakai tamɔ ŋmeii diji, baai ni egbee shi, loo ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ, Eshiɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions and spreads through rain splashes to ruin pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ Shade babaoo yɛ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli koni efite ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees planted above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni aná tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat; shade trees act like natural umbrellas to keep the young seedlings cool and protect them from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade koni eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing many flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi anɔkwa fɔfɔi fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop without making pods if there are not enough beneficial insects to pollinate them, or if the tree is too weak and stressed from lack of water or soil nutrients.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ekɛ haomɔ miiha nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Should I completely remove a cocoa tree if its branches start swelling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji eniji lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ?

english: Yes, because swollen branches are a sign of Swollen Shoot disease, a viral infection that cannot be cured; cutting down infected trees prevents the virus from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei niji ni efuu lɛ ji ŋmei hela ni efuu lɛ he okadi. Virus helai ni anyɛɛɛ atsa Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni virus lɛ akagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why is it important for me to prune dead or extra branches from my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji ni egboi loo niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the tree, which keeps leaves dry to stop diseases from growing and directs energy into producing bigger fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ koni helai akakwɛ̃, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni da.

english: Why do weeds around my crop stems make my main plants grow slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ miiha mitso titri lɛ miida blɛoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your crops need, leaving your main plants weak and struggling to produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks the right food for my crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When soil lacks food, your crops will show warning signs like stunted growth, pale leaves, weak stems, or very small harvests, showing they need manure or fertilizer.
ga: Beni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baajie kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii akpo, tamɔ shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ, baai ni mli tse, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo ŋmaa bibioo ko kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops dry up during hot dry spells even if it rains once in a while?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ bei komɛi amli moŋ?

english: Light or rare rains during hot weather do not soak deep enough into the soil to reach root systems, and intense heat causes that moisture to evaporate before plants can drink it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ boteŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or struggling with waterlogged soil. Giving the crop proper fertilizer or manure and ensuring good drainage helps it regain its deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ miiye nitrogen loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ miiwuu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eda waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn roll up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to conserve moisture and prevent water from escaping into the air. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to survive hot afternoon sun.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ehi wala mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my corn produce bigger cobs?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji?

english: Weeds compete directly with your corn for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing them gives your corn full access to all the food in the soil, allowing the cobs to grow large and full.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ehaa o-corn lɛ náa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛyiɔ obɔ kɛ dumɔwui

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly whenever the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Soil without enough organic matter cannot hold moisture for long. Adding compost or leaving dry grass on top of the soil acts like a sponge, keeping water around the roots even when the rains pause.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po sɛɛ.

english: How can I get a good harvest if I only have a small piece of land to plant on?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmaa kpakpa kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni makwɛ nɔ?

english: You do not need a huge farm to produce a lot of food. By using good seed spacing, feeding the soil with manure or fertilizer, and taking proper care of the plants, a small plot can produce a surprisingly heavy yield.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni oná ŋmɔ agbo koni onyɛ oná niyenii babaoo. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ bibioo po baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo ni haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow thin and fall over when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Stalks grow weak and thin if seeds are planted too close together or if the soil lacks nutrients like potassium. Giving plants proper space and feeding the soil strengthens their roots and stalks against high winds.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni oha amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe awa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in my young corn leaves, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are pests like Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves. Checking your fields early and applying appropriate natural or chemical controls quickly keeps them from ruining your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agricultural officer give a better yield than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Specially bred seeds are designed to resist common local pests and diseases while growing bigger crops. Saved grains gradually lose this strength over time and tend to produce smaller harvests.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ amɛ krɛdɛɛi lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ. Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fiofio Hewalɛ nɛɛ laajeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. ni esumɔɔ ni ekɛ nɔ ni faaa aba

english: How do I know my corn is dry enough to store in sacks without it getting spoiled?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotokui amli ni efiteee?

english: Corn is ready for storage when the grains are hard enough that your fingernail cannot dent them, and they make a sharp clicking sound when dropped together. Proper drying prevents mold from ruining your grain.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛtoɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ oniji ahe ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni gbee ni naa wa ko ni tswaa Klikimɔ baajɛ mli aba Beni amɛgbee shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ Gbimɔ ni sa tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite oŋmaa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn into dust after staying in storage for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ sũ beni akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils bore inside stored corn grains to eat them and multiply. Storing your clean, dry corn in airtight bags or treating them with approved grain protectants stops weevils from damaging your harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛye ni amɛshwere. Abele ni he tse ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli loo ni akɛ tsofa ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ he nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and humidity they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is eating holes in my maize leaves and leaving small brown dust inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni eshiɔ sũ fioo ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ? Yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central whorl of maize plants during the day and eats the young leaves, leaving behind frass that looks like sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii, ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This symptom indicates Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting stem cuttings taken from infected plants. Planting certified disease-resistant varieties is the best way to avoid it.
ga: Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ Tsoi srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ he kɛjɛɔ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning soft, black, and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato aduawai eŋɔli lɛ shishi yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ, ni ebote mli lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering where the soil rapidly alternates between very wet and dry.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa teŋ.

english: Why should I put my chemical fertilizer in a circle around the crop instead of right at the main stem?
