ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle he lɛ? Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso wulu lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the main stem can burn plant tissue and damage roots. Placing it a few inches away in a ring allows the outer feeder roots to absorb nutrients safely without damaging the stalk.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋtayaai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee ŋtayaa lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air through their roots and trap it in the soil. This enriches the ground with natural nutrients that feed companion crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei ni fata he tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops even in poor soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii po nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants evolved over centuries to aggressively grab water and nutrients from harsh soils faster than domesticated crop plants, which rely on carefully managed soil conditions.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa nɔ oya fe shia tsei ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my maize yield smaller when I plant my seeds very close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni faaa Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make energy for growing large tubers. Lifting the vines off the damp ground exposes leaves to sunlight while reducing root and leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs wuji ni baa lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shishifãi ahe helai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ hu baa shi.

english: Early rains can be 'false rains' followed by dry spells that scorch fresh seedlings. It is safest to plant after soil is moist down to a hand's depth (about 10–15 cm) and steady seasonal rains have truly established.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ afee ‘nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amale’, ni hulutsoo be ni shãa dumɔwui heei nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii ji beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ tso ko mli (aaafee 10–15 cm) ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa yɛ be mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How many cobs of maize can I expect a single plant to produce?
ga: Abele ŋmeii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ yɛ tso kome mli?

english: Most standard maize varieties in Ghana produce 1 to 2 good cobs per stalk. Trying to force a plant to grow more cobs usually leads to smaller, poorly filled grains because the plant's food is spread too thin.
ga: Abele henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo woɔ ŋmeii kpakpai 1 kɛyashi 2 yɛ tso kome mli. Bei pii lɛ, mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni anyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ehiii ejaakɛ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsɔ.

english: How many seeds should I drop into a single hole when planting maize?
ga: Dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ akɛwo bu kome mli kɛ́ adu ŋmãa?

english: It is best to plant 2 seeds per hole. If both germinate, you can remove the weaker seedling so the remaining plant gets enough nutrients to produce a large, healthy cob.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui 2 yɛ bu kome mli kɛji amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Obaanyɛ ojie dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I take my cassava roots out of the ground without breaking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie ŋmei shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mikuuu shishifãi lɛ?

english: You should soften the soil around the base with a cutlass or hoe after rain, hold the main stem firmly, and pull gently upward so the roots stay intact and do not rot quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei afee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he blɛoo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Mɔmɔ tso titri lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛgbala lɛ blɛoo kɛya ŋwɛi koni shishifãi lɛ akafite ni amɛkagbo oya.

english: Why shouldn't I leave diseased or rotten tomatoes on the plant next to the fine ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ tomato ni hela emɔ lɛ loo ni egbo lɛ yɛ tomato tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Tomato kpakpai?

english: Leaving bad fruit on the plant allows pests and fungal diseases to easily jump to the healthy ones growing next to them, ruining your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi aduawai gbohii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shi kɛyaa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ anɔ. mlɛo Kpata onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do I need to pull out some healthy young plants if they are growing too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji amɛdara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: This process, called thinning, ensures each remaining plant has enough soil space, water, and sunlight to grow strong instead of fighting each other and staying weak.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ thinning lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso ni eshwɛ lɛ náa shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, a hwu ta ngɛ a kpɛti nɛ a ya nɔ nɛ a gbɔjɔ.

english: Should I cut off old, yellowing leaves from my pepper plants or leave them there?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai momo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli loo mashi amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: You should remove old, yellow leaves because they no longer help the plant grow and can easily catch diseases from rain splashes on the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie baai ni egbɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛyeee amɛbuaa tso lɛ ni eda dɔŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ hela oya.

english: Why do some flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they are stressed by high temperatures, lack of water, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or calcium.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster than my cassava after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to local conditions, so they absorb water and soil food much faster than farm crops until the main crops grow big enough to shade them out.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akpã gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. kɛyashi tsei titrii lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly if I pile them together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Piling yams traps heat and moisture, creating a wet environment where decay spreads fast. Storing them on raised wooden racks lets air circulate and keeps them dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni abua naa lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa ni fitemɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Okɛto tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni eha egbi.

english: Why should I separate old harvested crops from newly harvested ones in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala ŋmaa momoi kɛ ŋmaa heei amli yɛ mi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Older crops often carry hidden insect eggs or mold that can quickly move to your fresh harvest if they are kept together in the same space.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni baanyɛ ajie oya kɛya onibii heei lɛ amli kɛji akɛ akɛto he kome yɛ he kome.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for leaf growth. The plant pulls remaining nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, showing that your soil needs compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha dalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii heei anɔ lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. When it gets too hot or dry, the flowers cannot produce pollen properly, so the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollen jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ pollen koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on leaf sap, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Giving the plants adequate moisture and managing insects early keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahaa tsei kɛ kooloi bibii ahe nitsumɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sun and strong winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects tender young cocoa leaves from burning while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmei ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rains fall heavily for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in flat soil, the roots drown and rot; planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛtrɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small, empty cobs, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the surrounding maize crop without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ebuaa naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look weak even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the nourishment in the soil goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ anu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture after the first rainfall for me to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three good rains and moisture goes deep into the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ kpakpa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved in a sack after last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku mli yɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds stored in warm or damp air lose their life quickly or get damaged inside by hidden pests like weevils. Seeds must be dried completely, mixed with clean ash or seed protectant, and kept in sealed, dry containers to stay viable for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato ni akɛto shihilɛi ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ baagboi oya loo amɛbaaná mligbɛ naagbai kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii amli. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa. Okɛ sũ ni he tse loo dumɔwui ahebuu afutu mli. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni egbi ni atsĩ naa mli koni anyɛ adu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have sensitive foliage that scorches easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields the young plants and retains soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my maize crop without spending money on expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can plant attractant trap crops, such as Napier grass, around the perimeter of your field. Pests like stem borers prefer the trap crop over your main crop, drawing them away from your maize.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu trap tsei tamɔ Napier jwɛi yɛ oyale lɛ naa. Kooloi tamɔ stem borers sumɔɔ trap tsei fe otso titri lɛ. Kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy improved hybrid seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and yield more crop. Saved seeds gradually lose these strong traits over successive seasons, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite fiofio Efiteɔ sui nɛɛ kɛ bei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: What key things should I consider before expanding my vegetable farm to a much larger piece of land?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ masusu he dani magbɛ mi-vegeduar ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya he ko ni da kwraa?

english: Before scaling up, test your soil quality, ensure a reliable water source for irrigation during dry periods, and secure market buyers in advance, as larger plots require significantly more labor and initial investment.
ga: dani ooofee lɛ agbo Ha aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ mlihilɛ akwɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni amɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná nɔmimaa yɛ wɔsɛɛ be jarayelihe lɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔji wuji biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo kɛ shishijee shika babaoo.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year even though I plant the same crop each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. Adding compost or rotating crops helps rebuild soil organic matter and restores nutrients.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Consistent moisture and adequate nutrients help the plant hold its blossoms long enough to turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen into the soil through their roots. This enriches the ground naturally, providing essential nutrients for nitrogen-hungry crops like maize in the following season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shika babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tso lɛ ni edaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch prevents sunlight from drying out the ground, stops weeds from sprouting, and slowly decomposes to add extra nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii krokomɛi afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots spread across my pepper plant leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity create ideal conditions for fungal leaf diseases to spread. Spacing plants further apart allows wind to dry the leaves quickly, reducing the risk of fungal outbreaks.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal leaf helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ egbiɔ oya. Tsɔɔmɔ oshara ni yɔɔ fungal helai ni baa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my harvested corn from weevils while storing it at home?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe be mli ni mikɛtoɔ shia lɛ?

english: Drying your corn thoroughly before storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects and prevents mold growth by depriving pests of moisture and oxygen without needing harmful chemicals.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmã jogbaŋŋ dani akɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are new and unfamiliar insects suddenly appearing on my farm and destroying my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi srɔtoi heei baa trukaa lɛ? Adebɔɔ ko ni mileee lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Insects can travel long distances on wind currents, inside imported seeds, or due to changing weather patterns. When a new pest arrives in an area, local crops have no natural resistance to it, and local birds or beneficial insects may not know how to hunt it yet, allowing the pest population to explode quickly.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aya he ko shɔŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa. Yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ loo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Beni tsɛŋemɔ hela hee ko boteɔ jɛmɛ lɛ Kuu lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii hu nyɛɛɛ amɛye nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ekolɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ leee bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛgbeɔ amɛ lolo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why are the standard pest chemicals I buy at the market no longer killing the bugs on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you use the exact same chemical repeatedly, a few bugs survive and pass their immunity on to their offspring. Over time, the whole pest population becomes resistant. To solve this, you need to alternate between different types of pest control methods and rotate chemical groups.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, Kooloi komɛi baahi shi ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni tsiɔ helai anaa lɛ baaha amɛbii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ fɛɛ baafee nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ. Bɔni afee ni otsu naagba nɛɛ he nii Ebaabi ni otsake gbɛi srɔtoi ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ateŋ. kɛ tsofai akui ni tsɔɔ he fɛɛ he

english: Why do pest attacks seem so much worse during specific times of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ mli wa waa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Insects depend heavily on temperature and moisture to reproduce. Warm temperatures and high humidity speed up their egg-laying and hatching cycles, leading to sudden pest population booms during transitional weather periods.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa nɔ waa koni amɛfɔ bii. He ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ fɔɔ kɛ amɛfɔmɔ be lɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ayibɔ yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli.

english: How do crop pests manage to spread so fast from my neighbor's farm to mine?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko agbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛya shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli?

english: Pests can easily travel on wind currents, crawl through untended weeds along field borders, or hitch a ride on shared tools, clothing, and farm animals. Clearing farm boundaries and cleaning tools after use helps block their pathway.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ. Ni oootsɔ jwɛi ni atsako nɔ lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa Aloo okɛ tsɔne aya ni okɛ nibii, atadei, kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi aja. Okwaafoi husui lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛsaa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my crop yields dropping every harvest even though I am doing my farm work the same way as always?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni makpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Farming the same spot repeatedly depletes essential soil nutrients and allows hidden soil diseases or small pests to build up year after year. Plants get weaker over time unless you restore the soil nutrients or rotate different crop families.
ga: Okwaayeli yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Ni enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa afi fɛɛ afi. Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ja okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ tsei awekui srɔtoi tsake.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a lack of rain or from pest attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi?

english: Drought stress usually causes leaves to curl up and turn dry and brown uniformly across the whole plant. Pest damage leaves specific signs behind, such as tiny chewed holes, sticky liquid on leaves, dark spots, or individual branches wilting while the rest looks green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa anaa okadii komɛi, tamɔ buji bibii ni ashɛreɔ, nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ, hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo niji aŋkroaŋkroi ni gboɔ yɛ be mli ni fã ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive pest attacks while others right next to them die completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ wala kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ? yɛ be mli ni kooloi krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ gboi kwraa lɛ?

english: Some crop varieties have natural defenses built into them, such as tougher outer skins, bitter natural sap that bugs dislike, or strong root systems that regenerate quickly after damage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ama awo mli, tamɔ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni mli wa. Latex ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni kooloi sumɔɔɔ. aloo shishifã ni mli wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya kɛji efite

english: Why do export crops like cocoa or cashew sometimes fail to produce fruit even when the market price is high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ tamɔ kookoo loo cashew lɛ wooo yibii yɛ be mli ni jarayeli jara wa po lɛ?

english: High market prices do not protect trees from localized pest attacks, soil exhaustion, or aging branches. Export trees require targeted pruning, shade management, and specific pest treatment at precise stages of flower blooming to set fruit successfully.
ga: Jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ ebuuu tsei ahe kɛjɛ jɛmɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ, loo tsei niji ni egbɔ lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ nɔŋŋ. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii agbɛfaŋ, koni ewo yibii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Can mixing different crops together on one piece of land help protect my farm from pests?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Yes, planting a mix of crops creates a natural barrier. The different smells and leaf shapes confuse pests looking for a single crop, and some secondary plants even attract helpful insects that eat crop-destroying pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii baa. Henumɔi srɔtoi kɛ baai ahe mfonirii futuɔ kooloi ni taoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome lɛ. Ni tsei komɛi ni akɛwoɔ saatso nɔ lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to protect my farm so my family does not face food shortages if a pest invasion happens?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni yɛ ni baabu miŋmɔ lɛ he koni miweku lɛ kɛ niyenii ni faaa akakpe kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko batutua amɛ?

english: You can protect your food supply by growing a mix of different crops instead of just one, inspecting your leaves twice a week to catch pests early, using pest-resistant seed varieties, and keeping healthy soil that gives crops the strength to recover from damage.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu niyenii ni oyɔɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome pɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ obaai lɛ amli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli koni onyɛ omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ mra. Kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ, ni no haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the right type of maize seed to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni sa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different maize varieties are bred for specific conditions, such as drought resistance, pest tolerance, or fast maturity. Choose seeds based on your area's rainfall patterns, soil type, and whether you want an early harvest or grain for long-term storage.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi Atsɔse amɛ kɛha shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ bɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo edalɛ oya Halamɔ dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɛji oosumɔ ni akpa mra loo dumɔwui ni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my recent maize harvest to plant during the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted hybrid seeds, saving and replanting them will lead to smaller cobs and poor yields in the next season. It is best to buy fresh certified seeds each planting season to maintain high quality and strong crop growth.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee bibii ni yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara waa

english: Why do some corn varieties mature in two months while others take up to four months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ.

english: Maize varieties have different maturity lifecycles. Fast-maturing varieties are designed for short rainy seasons so farmers can harvest quickly, while late-maturing varieties take longer to grow but often produce larger cobs and higher yields.
ga: Abele henɔi lɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi ni amɛshwereɔ. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ aha nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ. koni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ akpa oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ. Shi amɛfɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kpojiemɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their deep green color and fuels growth, so applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer or manure can help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants look stunted and pale even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Regular rain is helpful, but crops also need nutrients from the soil to grow tall. Stunted corn usually means the soil lacks key nutrients, is too compacted for roots to expand, or weeds are stealing the water and fertilizer meant for the crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ hu he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi niyenii hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji dwarf lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo jwɛi miiju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing grains or large gaps on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ elaaje loo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when pollination fails while the corn is flowering. Extreme heat, drought, or over-crowded planting can prevent pollen from reaching the silks, leaving empty spaces on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ naa koni ekashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ baa cob lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting maize too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and smaller cobs with low yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibii ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my corn is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn dry and brown, the husks covering the cob turn light brown, and the kernels become hard with a tiny black layer visible at the base of each seed.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Hewolo ni ha tso lɛ he lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni nɔ ko bibioo ko ni yɔɔ diŋ yɔɔ mli. Abaanyɛ ana yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil or get eaten by insects so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ kɛ́ akɛto lɛ?

english: Grain spoils quickly when stored with too much moisture or without pest protection. Corn must be dried thoroughly until kernels are hard, and stored in sealed, airtight bags or treated storage bins to keep insects out.
ga: Ŋmãa fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛbuuu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ naa loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ amli koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: What makes some corn varieties good for roasting fresh while others are better for grinding into flour?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa henɔi komɛi feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa hee ni ashãa? yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi hi kɛha ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛfee ashikishaŋ.

english: Fresh roasting corn has soft, sweet kernels when harvested early, making it pleasant to eat directly. Grain varieties develop dense, hard starch as they dry, making them perfect for milling into fine flour for local dishes like banku and kenkey.
ga: Popcorn hee yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ kɛji akpa mra. Ehaa niyeli feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ŋmãa henɔi lɛ feɔ ashikiŋsha ni mli wa, ni wa be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaatsɔ mli ashikishaŋ kpakpa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ banku kɛ kenkey.

english: What should I do when one of my cocoa trees dies while still standing in my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ eko gbo be mli ni midamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: When a tree dies while standing, it is often due to a root disease or stem borers. You should avoid immediately dragging or burning it until you identify the cause, as moving infected plant material can spread disease to healthy neighboring trees.
ga: Kɛ tso ko gbo beni edamɔ shi Bei pii lɛ, shishifã hela loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Esa akɛ okpa lɛ ni ooogbala loo okɛshã lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛyashi obaanyɛ ona nɔ ni kɛba lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala hela lɛ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it a good idea to cut off all the leaves from a sick crop to make it grow back healthy?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofolɔ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ koni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: No, you should not cut off all the leaves. Leaves act as the crop's kitchen to make food from sunlight. Removing all leaves starves the plant; you should only prune the infected or yellow leaves and leave the healthy ones.
ga: Esaaa akɛ afoɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ ŋtayaa he ni ekɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii yɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ pɛ ni oshi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and produce good corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water settles in the soil for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers safe from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni yitso lɛ akafite

english: Why do agriculture officers tell us not to burn dry bushes on our land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani wɔdu nii lɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil insects, destroys natural nutrients, and leaves the soil dry and exposed to heat. Letting dry plant material rot naturally adds rich organic manure back into your farm soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa Tso mli nibii ni egbi lɛ gbɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What are the benefits of covering the ground around my young seedlings with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ he?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil during dry heat, prevents weeds from sprouting, and slowly rots into fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and cannot endure direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them provides living shade and holds moisture in the ground to keep them alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni tsei lɛ ahi shi.

english: Should I apply fertilizer at the exact same time I plant my crop seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is better to wait two to three weeks after seeds sprout before applying chemical fertilizer. Applying fertilizer directly onto seeds or fresh sprouts can burn tender young roots before they are ready to feed.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui heei loo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii lɛ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaye nii.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before they bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall easily when underground pests called nematodes or stem borers destroy their root system. Using clean planting material and treated suckers prevents pests from weakening the roots.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ akɛ dumɔ nii ni he tse kɛ suckers ni atsa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɔjɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me manage my farm better?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi koni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers are trained government field agents who visit farms to teach farmers safe chemical use, diagnose strange crop diseases, introduce high-yielding seeds, and guide you on proper planting practices.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi ji shikpɔŋkuku mli nitsulɔi ni nɔyeli lɛ etsɔse amɛ. ni baayasara ŋmɔji amli koni etsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ bɔ ni amɛkɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe Kwɛmɔ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Atsɔɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo. ni amɛtsɔɔ nifeemɔi ni akɛduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to mix chemical medicine into water before spraying my crops to kill pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai futuɔ nu mli dani mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ?

english: Mixing crop medicine with water dilutes the chemical so it spreads evenly across your plants without burning the leaves, ensuring the whole farm is protected safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso tsofa futu nu mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ afee mlɛo. Koni oja yɛ otso lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oshãaa baai lɛ. Ha oná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni abuɔ he.

english: Why must I add fresh fertilizer or medicine every time I refill my crop water tank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa hee afata he be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ nu baawo nu tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you replace old water with fresh water, you flush out the existing nutrients and protective chemicals, so you need to re-add them to keep your plants fed and protected.
ga: Kɛji otsake nu momo kɛtee nu kpakpa mli Obaafɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nu afata he ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni abu amɛhe.

english: Is it safe to mix pest medicine and liquid plant food together in the same water container?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ tsei aniyenii ni ji nu baafutu yɛ nu tsinsii kome mli?

english: Some chemicals react badly when mixed together and can harm your crops, so you should always confirm with an extension officer before combining two different products in one water tank.
ga: Tsofai komɛi kɛ amɛhe futu mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ extension official lɛ ama nɔ mi be fɛɛ be dani okɛ nibii srɔtoi enyɔ afata nu tsɛnsi kome he.

english: What happens if I use dirty stream water instead of clean water to mix my farm medicines?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji tsu nii yɛ nu ni mli tse najiaŋ kɛfutu tsofa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mud and dirt in unclean water can react with the crop medicine and weaken its strength, making it less effective at killing pests and preventing plant diseases.
ga: Mu kɛ muji ni yɔɔ nu ni he tseee mli lɛ baanyɛ afee ekome kɛ tso tsofa lɛ ni eha hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbemɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai atsimɔ mli.

english: Why do insects keep gathering around my water storage containers on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa lɛ? Mi nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Open fresh water naturally attracts insects looking to drink and lay eggs, which is why keeping containers covered or adding approved pest treatments is necessary to prevent insect outbreaks.
ga: Nu kpakpa ni agbele naa lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni miisumɔ ni amɛnu nu ni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ kɛbaa amɛnɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni atsĩ tsɛnsii amli loo akɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afata he koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote mli lɛ.

english: What should I do if insects attack my crops just a few months after I started using a new chemical treatment?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmeii batutua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mibɔi tsofa hee ko kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Pests can sometimes build tolerance to a chemical, meaning you may need to switch to a different recommended medicine in your spraying water to control the new insects effectively.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aná tsofai ahe tsuishitoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni otsake kɛya tsofa kroko ni atsɔɔ yɛ nu ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni onyɛ oye kooloo hee lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the insect medicine I added to my water tank is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛwoɔ mi nu tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will notice fewer live insects on your leaves within a few days, and your plant leaves will stop showing fresh chew marks or yellow spots caused by pest damage.
ga: Obaana kooloi bibii ni hiɛ ka fioo yɛ obaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Ni otso lɛ baai lɛ baakpa ŋmɔlɔ he okadii heei loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ kpojiemɔ.

english: Why are extension officers asking us to adopt these new water treatment methods instead of our traditional farming ways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni wɔkɛ nɛkɛ nu he nitsumɔ gbɛ̀i heei nɛɛ atsu nii yɛ blema okwaayeli najiaŋ lɛ?

english: New water-based feeding and pest control methods deliver nutrients and medicine directly to plant roots faster, giving you healthier crops and higher harvest yields compared to traditional practices.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛ gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ akuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa niyenii kɛ tsofai baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto blema nifeemɔi ahe.

english: How long does it usually take to see clear results after starting a new water-based crop treatment?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni kadiɔ mɔ beni aje nu mli tsei ahe tsofafeemɔ hee shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most crops show noticeable improvements in leaf color and growth rate within 3 to 4 months of consistently applying the right water treatments.
ga: Tsei babaoo yɛ hiɛyaa ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe su kɛ amɛdalɛ mli yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akɛ nu ni sa tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why does my crop water change color or smell different when I put fresh medicine inside it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su loo eŋɔɔɔ srɔto kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa hee fata he lɛ?

english: A change in color or mild smell usually means the chemical is dissolving and activating properly in the fresh water so it can protect your crops from disease.
ga: Su ni tsakeɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa shi Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu kpakpa mli. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants start turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the plants recover their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough strength to grow cassava without adding chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okwɛ ŋmei ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Good soil for cassava is dark, crumbly, and drains water easily. If your land naturally grows thick, dark green weeds and water doesn't pool on top after rain, your soil has enough natural fertility for cassava.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni nu lɛ efeee ekome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmei.

english: Why do my crops droop in the middle of the day even when there is moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They curl or droop their leaves to protect themselves from the heat, and they usually bounce back in the evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ loo amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Ni amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This provides natural food to the nearby maize plants, making both crops healthier and improving your harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Ha tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hewalɛ ni oha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to keep shade trees on my land when planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he hiaa mi beni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade trees act like large umbrellas, protecting the young plants from harsh sun and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and mulching around the roots help keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? dani eda

english: Cocoa trees drop small pods (known as cherelle wilt) when the tree doesn't have enough water, light, or nutrients to feed all the pods at once. Pruning excess branches and feeding the soil helps the tree retain its pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ ŋmeii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ Cherelle Wilt) kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, la, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ shikome. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow bent or stunted when the soil underneath them is hard, rocky, or poorly tilled. Yams need deep, soft mounds so the tubers can expand easily downwards without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛ gbɛ.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up into small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii? ni okpa dalɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying wood ash water or organic neem extract helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ nu, tso mli sũ loo neem ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers under the ground are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, cracks appear on the soil around the plant stem, and the plant reaches 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Gbɛjegbɛi jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli, ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow root systems that burn and lose water quickly under full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a moist shelter that protects the young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shãa ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in high humidity and wet soil. Excess moisture on the pods allows the fungus to grow, especially if the cocoa trees are overgrown and air cannot flow freely between branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes inside the leaves of my young maize shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which lays eggs on young maize leaves. Once hatched, the caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves to feed on the tender parts, which stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baai bibii anɔ lɛ. Kɛji amɛfɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to build green leaves. When the soil is starved of nutrients, the plant cannot produce enough energy to make big, healthy maize cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's natural way of saving water during dry weather. By shedding its leaves, the plant stops water from evaporating into the air and keeps itself alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ nu ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When mature cassava is left in soggy or waterlogged soil past its harvest time, soil microbes and excess moisture begin breaking down the tubers, causing soft rot underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei momo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ kɛho ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ he. Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baabɔi ŋmeii lɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by underground pests like weevils or nematodes. Without strong roots anchoring them to the soil, the heavy weight of the growing plantain bunch easily pulls the whole tree down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo nematodes baanyɛ afite. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Plantains kuu ko ni miida lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii waa lɛ baanyɛ agbala tso muu fɛɛ kɛba shi mlɛo.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and become small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or passing a virus to the plant. This damages the leaf tissue and stops the plant from growing healthy leaves and peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsei Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa tso lɛ baa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. This temperature and water stress prevents the flowers from pollinating, so the plant drops them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Temperature kɛ nu mli haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pollination. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to absorb water and surface soil food very quickly. Their seeds wake up instantly after rain and outgrow cultivated crops because they require fewer nutrients to spread quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe esa akɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Dumɔwui teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ ejaakɛ niyenii fioo pɛ he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying when the sun gets very intense during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot endure direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn and roots dry out quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leafy stems above ground, but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves instead of growing large tubers underground. Balancing the soil nutrients helps the plant direct its food downward into the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-pattern indicate that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, showing that fertilizer or compost needs to be applied.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Is it really necessary to stake my yam vines, or can I just let them grow along the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ loo manyɛ maha ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to sunlight so they can make food for tuber growth. Leaves left on the ground get shaded by each other, stay wet longer, and catch fungal diseases from the soil much more easily.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he koni ekɛfee niyenii aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Baai ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Hiɛ shi be kakadaŋŋ Ni ewaaa kwraa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaná bo.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Plantain sɛi wulu lɛ je kpo.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for water and soil nutrients. Pruning down to one main stem and one small successor allows the plant to focus its full energy on producing a single heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso titri kome kɛ seshibii bibii baa. Tso kome haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains kuu kome ni tsii ni ebaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to prune branches from mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ aniji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted growth and opens up the tree canopy, letting sunlight and air pass through. This reduces humidity around the trunk, preventing black pod disease and ensuring nutrients go into pod production.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ nibii ni esaaa ni edaa lɛ, ni egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa black pod hela aba ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ boteɔ pod feemɔ mli.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which also spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents them from stunting the plant and destroying your yield.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli hu Mra be mli ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ nɛkɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee shweremɔ ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why am I seeing small holes and powdery dust inside the stems of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni sũ lɛ yɛ miŋmaa bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by maize stem borers, which are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths and burrow into the stem to feed. Applying targeted treatments inside the plant leaf funnel early controls them before they break the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ baaha anyɛ akudɔ mra. dani tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafo

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers heat stress or irregular watering during hot spells. When conditions become too intense, the plant sheds its flowers to save moisture and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough water for me to sow my maize seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check that the rain has soaked deep enough to moisten the top 10 to 15 centimeters of soil, rather than just wetting the surface. Planting after a shallow rain causes seeds to sprout and then dry up if a short dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni feɔ sɛntimitai 10 kɛyashi 15 lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, moŋ fe ni eeefee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the food they need to turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to stay small and thin even after a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to swell and grow big. If the ground is packed hard or lacks nutrients like potassium, the plant cannot expand its tubers properly.
ga: Kassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛfuu ni amɛdara. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ bulbs jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from losing too much water in heat, or because tiny insects like thrips are sucking sap from the leaf undersides. Watering early in the morning and checking for pests helps keep leaves flat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if wind and insects aren't moving pollen inside the flower. Consistent watering and shade during mid-day heat can help fruit form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii tsiii fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua yɛ enɛ mli.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on land where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for future crops and keeping the land fertile without overusing chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmeii ni ato lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil moist, protects seeds and tubers from hot sun, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into organic fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ Buɔ dumɔwui kɛ bulbs ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Excess moisture during heavy rains creates black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in humid conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and prevent rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: What are the white powdery spots under my papaya leaves, and why are the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni ji powder yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mipapaya baai lɛ ashishi lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Those white spots are small insects called mealybugs. They suck sap from the leaves and drop a sticky substance that grows black mold, which weakens the tree and turns leaves yellow.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off branches from my cocoa trees if I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji kɛji miitao ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning cocoa trees removes unproductive branches so the tree puts its energy into growing healthy pods. It also lets in light and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ kookoo tso lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni daraa waa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu naa la. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When seeds are buried too deep or flooded with water, they get trapped without air and suffocate. Planting seeds at the correct shallow depth and ensuring good drainage prevents rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni amɛmuɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa ni akwɛ koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite.

english: Officer, why are my crops failing even though I am farming on the same land in Ga South that my family used for years?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔshi nii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni miweku lɛ kɛtsu nii afii babaoo lɛ nɔŋŋ miitsu nii moŋ?

english: Continuous farming without replenishing nutrients or allowing the soil to rest wears out the land over time. Applying compost, manure, or organic matter recharges the soil so crops can get the food they need to yield well again.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he loo ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli awo hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a piece of farmland in Accra is good for planting vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ Accra lɛ hi kɛha aduawai akwɛmɔ?

english: Good soil for vegetables is dark, loose enough to crumble easily in your hands, and lets water drain without turning into a long-lasting swamp after heavy rain. Darker soil usually contains rich organic matter from decayed leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ aduawai lɛ aná su ni tsuɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efo mlɛo yɛ enine mli ni eha nu lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebatsɔŋ ŋshɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ baai ni egboi amli baa lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant on my small plot of land near Accra to get a quick harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? Ebɛŋkɛ Accra kɛha nitsumɔ oya

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, hot pepper, garden eggs, and leafy greens like okro or spinach grow quickly within two to three months and have strong demand in local urban markets.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, chili, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli tamɔ okra loo spinach. Ebaada oya yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ni ataoɔ amɛ waa yɛ maŋtiasei lɛ amli jarayeli hei lɛ.

english: Corn leaves curl up to protect themselves and reduce water loss through evaporation during intense heat. It is the plant's natural way of conserving moisture until cooler hours or rainfall.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the stem and green leaves look very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excessive shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and leaves instead of storing food down in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: What causes heavy rain to wash away all the good topsoil on my land, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ kpakpa kɛyaa? yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi naa?

english: Rain washes topsoil away when land is cleared completely bare with no plant roots to hold the soil together. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or making raised ridges across slopes stops water from washing away the fertile layer.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji ajie jɛmɛ ni tsei shishifãi ni hiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔ he lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afeɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekafɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips that damage the flower stem before fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Sir, can land that has been cleared or disturbed by heavy machinery ever grow healthy crops again?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, ani shikpɔŋ ni tsɔnei ni tsii efo nɔ loo egba enaa lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, damaged land can recover, but it needs care. You must break up hardened ground, work plenty of animal manure or compost into the soil, and plant leguminous cover crops to rebuild nutrients and natural life.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ atsake shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ okpãtã hei ni wa lɛ ahiɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni akɛ ŋmeii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni akɛfee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ wala ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn pale yellow and drop after long periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills up all air spaces and suffocates plant roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing food from the soil, causing leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ebaakpa niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ loo ŋmeii ko kwraa baaa.

english: Yellow leaves on lower maize stems usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, a major plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish new leaves, which causes the bottom ones to turn yellow. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get as hard as a brick whenever the rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ brikii be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa gbii fioo lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure, which normally acts like a sponge to keep soil soft and moist. Adding organic compost or spreading dry grass mulch over the soil protects it from the hot sun and keeps it soft for crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo
