english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and dry up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp, and cool conditions. Clearing surrounding weeds and pruning tall tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to dry out moisture, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ebɔle he lɛ kɛ tsei kakadaji ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the tubers and causing fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo kɛya. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What makes the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly into cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is typically caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies by clearing weed patches around your garden prevents them from carrying the virus to your tomato crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Whiteflies nɔyeli kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ Abɔɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaŋɔ hela lɛ kɛya o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, erratic watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and applying organic mulch keeps root temperatures low so flowers can stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ aya shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. Midges breed in moist leaf litter on the farm floor, so leaving a natural blanket of fallen leaves on the ground encourages midges to pollinate your cocoa.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Midges fɔɔ yɛ baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oshi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ewoɔ midges hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo o-cocoa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can easily be destroyed by microscopic worms called nematodes or insect larvae boring into the underground stem base. Staking young trees with wooden poles and using clean planting material keeps the base anchored firmly in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Tsei bibii ni akɛ tsei ŋmɔji woɔ mli kɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishitoo lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my planted yam pieces take several weeks before they start sprouting out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ otsii babaoo dani mi-sweet potatoes ni midu lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam seed pieces go into a natural resting state called dormancy right after harvest. They will remain dormant in the soil until natural inner hormonal changes occur, which are triggered by moist soil conditions and warm temperatures.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli fãi lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Amɛbaakã he amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ mli lɛ baaba. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ latsaa kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger on my farm than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛdara fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive harsh conditions and naturally absorb water and plant food faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from taking away essential sunlight and nutrients from your crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Is it good to leave weeds on the ground after I cut them in my plantain farm, or should I move them away?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ beni mifo amɛ yɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ? Aloo esa akɛ majie amɛ kɛya he kroko?

english: Leaving piles of cut weeds on the ground creates safe hiding places for pests and wild animals. Over time, these pests settle in the cut weeds and end up attacking and damaging your plantain plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ koo mli kooloi lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni afo lɛ amli. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaatutua odumɔwui lɛ ni ekpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: What causes small animals and pests to keep disturbing my plantains every year?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai gbaa mi plantain tsei lɛ anaa daa afi?

english: Pests are usually attracted by uncleared bush and dead crop materials left on the farm. If these materials are not removed, pests build homes there and return season after season to feed on your plantains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieee kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛji ajieee nibii nɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baafee shia yɛ jɛmɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni amɛbaye o-plantains lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds on my farm early instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Ehe miihia mi moŋ akɛ mafo be mli.

english: Clearing weeds early destroys the hiding spots and homes of pests before they can fully establish themselves and multiply, protecting your crops before the main growing season begins.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Efiteɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe kɛ amɛshiai dani amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ. Koni okɛbu onibii ahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: How do leftover cut weeds on my field affect the safety of my plantain crop?
ga: Te jwɛi ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni afo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ashweshweeshwefeemɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Leftover weeds act as a shelter for destructive insects and rodents. As the weeds sit on the soil, animals move in, multiply, and eventually feed on the nearby plantain roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shĩa kɛha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kooloi fãa kɛyaa mli, amɛshwereɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛyeɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi.

english: Why do pest problems on my farm seem to get worse next year even if I weeded this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe naagba lɛ baaya hiɛ waa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mafo jwɛi afi nɛɛ moŋ.

english: If cut weeds are left lying on the field after weeding, pests migrate into those piles and stay there continuously. By the next year, a whole colony of pests will be living on your farm ready to attack new growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛyaa nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛhiɔ jɛmɛ. Yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo baahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaatutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: What should I do with the grass and bush I cut down so it does not harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni mifolɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, eyeee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: It is best to clear the cut grass completely away from the base of your crops or spread it thinly so it dries fast, preventing animals and insects from using it as a permanent shelter.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi ni afo lɛ kɛjɛ otsei lɛ ashishi loo ooogbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he koni egbi oya. Enɛ ji koni kooloi kɛ kooloi akafee amɛshihilɛhe daa.

english: Can proper weed clearing alone reduce the pests attacking my plantains without using chemicals?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mi plantains lɛ anɔ aba shi ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, maintaining good farm sanitation by clearing weeds early and keeping the field free of dense plant trash deprives pests of shelter, naturally reducing pest attacks on your plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ kpakpa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni oookpa mra lɛ nɔ. kɛ he ni tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa odumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do pests hide on my farm even when there are no main crops growing yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ani aduko ŋmɔshi nibii titri ko lolo?

english: Pests can survive during the off-season by living inside dead weeds, soil trash, and uncleared bush left on the farm, waiting for new plantain shoots to grow so they can feed on them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egboi, jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni he tseee ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ ni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ koni amɛye amɛ.

english: How does keeping my field clean help my plantain stems grow strong?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli ni mikwɛɔ koni ehe atse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi plantain tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa?

english: A clean field prevents rodents and burrowing insects from breeding near the plantain bases, ensuring that the plant's root system and stem remain undamaged so the plant can grow strong.
ga: He ko ni mli tse baatsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ bu lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ plantains lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifã kɛ eshishifã lɛ akafite. Koni tsei lɛ adara waa

english: What is the best routine to follow to protect my plantain farm from animal disturbance?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛjianɔtoo ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni baaye nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Clear your farm early before planting, remove or properly manage all cut weeds so animals cannot settle in them, and maintain clear paths around your crop stands throughout the year.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra dani odu, ojie loo okwɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni kooloi akato shia yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni okwɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ nɔ kɛbɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I know if the pest medicine I am spraying actually reaches the highest leaves of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ eshɛ kookoo tso lɛ yiteŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can inspect the upper canopy right after spraying to check if the leaves are wet, or tie special paper strips to the top branches that change color when liquid drops hit them.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yiteŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ efɔ nɔ koni ona kɛji baai lɛ mli edɔ. Aloo okɛ wolo krɛdɛɛ ko akpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni tsakeɔ ehiɛ su kɛji nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tswa tso lɛ nine lɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to spray under the leaves of my vegetable plants and not just on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishi shi jeee yɛ nɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Most insects and plant diseases hide on the underside of leaves to protect themselves from the sun, so spraying underneath ensures the medicine touches and destroys them.
ga: Kplukai kɛ tsei ahe helai babaoo kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsofa lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni efite amɛ.

english: What happens to the chemical medicine on my crops if heavy rain falls right after I finish spraying?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni migbe tsofa lɛ nɔ migbe naa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the liquid medicine off the leaves into the soil before the plant or pests can absorb it, which means the treatment will not work and you may need to reapply.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsofa ni ji nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Is a motorized spraying machine better for my maize field than my regular hand-pump knapsack?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi fe daa nine pɔmp ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛ baagi nɔ?

english: A motorized sprayer covers large fields much faster and breaks liquid into fine droplets that reach deeper into crops, whereas a hand knapsack is slower but allows precise control on smaller farms.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ haa hei wuji ahe oya kwraa ni amɛjaraa nu mli amɛwoɔ nu bibii bibii amli. ni baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli shɔŋŋ Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sɛɛgbɛ kotoku ni akɛ niji woɔ mli lɛ yaa oya shi ehaa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can I mix my insect medicine and my disease medicine together in the same spraying tank to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ afutu yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Some farm chemicals can be mixed safely, but combining incompatible chemicals can cause them to clump, damage your crop leaves, or make both medicines lose their power.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai komɛi afutu shweshweeshwe. Shi tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛfee ekome. efiteɔ tsei ahe baai loo ehaa tsofai enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and burn after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning usually happens when the chemical mix is too strong or when spraying is done during the hot afternoon sun, which stresses and damages the soft leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ashwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baa lɛ shãa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ni efiteɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow even after I spray liquid fertilizer on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: If the sun is too hot or the roots are damaged by poor soil, the plant cannot take in the liquid nutrients through its leaves, causing it to remain weak and yellow.
ga: Kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aná nu mli niyenii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ kã he egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Will using chemical weedkillers near my tomato plants harm their roots under the ground?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ awui?

english: Yes, if weedkillers drift onto tomato stems or soak into shallow soil, they can stunt root growth and stop the plant from taking up water and food.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ hoɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ loo eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fioo. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni amɛtsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why are armyworms still eating my crops even though I sprayed the medicine recommended to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa eshwie nɔ taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant where surface spray might not reach, or they may have become used to that specific chemical if used too many times.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo tsofa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ kɛji amɛkɛtsu nii shii abɔ tsɔ.

english: Does spraying liquid fertilizer directly on plant leaves work faster than putting solid fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Liquid fertilizer sprayed on leaves acts quickly to boost weak plants, but solid fertilizer placed in the soil feeds the plant steadily through its roots over a longer time.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya koni ekanya tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fiofio kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their root systems and leaves are delicate. Leaving big shade trees on the farm protects young cocoa from sunburn and keeps the soil cool and moist during hot periods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and does this mean they are dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ egbo?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and stay alive. The plant is not dead; it rests underground and will grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ejɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ebaajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. When temperatures are too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy until conditions cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the plant is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants need to stay dark green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná su ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year even though I plant on the exact same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaaa ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ.

english: Growing the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baatsake Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnels of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaves to feed. Applying targeted treatments early into the leaf funnel helps control them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofafeemɔ ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli koni eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insect pests early stops the foliage from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni aaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I put four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together creates heavy competition. The crowded roots and leaves fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil food, making every plant weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa. Shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rain and wind hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the surface. Propping up trees that are bearing heavy bunches with bamboo stakes prevents strong winds from uprooting them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Tsei ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii tsei duɔ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie amɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of leafy green branches above ground but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji babaoo ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes yams to put all their energy into leafy growth above ground instead of expanding tubers underground. Staking the vines properly also ensures tubers develop fully.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo ŋmei lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, wain tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important food that plants need to stay green and build leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water from the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nugbɔ babaoo?

english: When tomato plants get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and look droopy even when the ground is damp. Overwatering drowns the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbo, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ehaaa amɛmu ni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally curls and drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and stays alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ, ni egbiɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, long periods without water, or lack of plant nutrients. Dropping flowers helps the plant conserve energy to stay alive during tough conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha amɛhao. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ bɛ Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow large outer leaves but fail to form a tight head in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni mli edɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to close tightly if the weather is too hot or if the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages fast leaf expansion instead of head formation.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ eŋmɛŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ mli alɛɛ oya moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee bulbs.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves instead of pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when tiny flower-feeding insects destroy the delicate buds before pods can form.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii Ni yeɔ fɔfɔii, ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani ŋmeii feɔ.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow so slowly when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their broad leaves shade one another from sunlight, and their roots fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil, slowing down overall growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer cocoa pods when the farm becomes bushy and overgrown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ?

english: Heavy bush growth steals light, water, and nutrients away from cocoa trees. An overgrown farm also traps high humidity, creating an environment where diseases like black pod thrive and destroy young pods.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Gbɛjegbɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu hiɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up on their own before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry up when the underground tuber has finished growing and storing starch. This drying is a normal biological signal that the yam is fully mature and ready for digging.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ blɔfo ni amɛbaagbi kɛji agbe ŋmeii lɛ adumɔ naa ni awo amɛ starch. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji wala yibii ahe okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ eda ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into a fine powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Powder inside stored grain is caused by insects like maize weevils. They bore inside the dry kernels to feed and lay eggs, reducing the solid grain to dust over time.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ powda ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii, ni buɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni egbi mli koni amɛye nii ni amɛwo amɛwui. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni wa lɛ tsɔɔ sũ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil, giving plants essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that help them build strong roots, grow bigger leaves, and produce a higher harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii. Ehaa tsei niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔras, kɛ potasiam. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why do the leaves on my young crops turn yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient they need to grow healthy and green. Applying the right fertilizer provides the food they need to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs fertilizer before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale leaves, or gave a small harvest, your soil is likely low on nutrients and will benefit from fertilizer added before or during planting.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ da blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewooo yibii fioo. Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni obaaná he sɛɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani odu loo yɛ be mli ni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or a shortage of key nutrients in the soil like calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking plant juices or spreading diseases. Using proper crop protection inputs or removing diseased plants early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso mli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni abuɔ he lɛ ahe saji ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants dry up quickly even when we receive a little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo po lɛ?

english: If the soil is hard or lacks organic matter, rain water runs off the surface instead of sinking deep to the roots. Improving soil health helps the ground hold water longer for your crops.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛhaa onibii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant room to produce well.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ haa nitsumɔhe tsu fɛɛ tsu feɔ nibii kpakpai.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are very quick at stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits than my neighbor who uses certified inputs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii fe akutsoŋbii ni kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni awo he odaseyeli tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Smaller fruit size usually means the plant lacked sufficient water or plant food during the fruit-forming stage. Certified seeds combined with proper fertilizer help crops grow larger, heavier produce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii lɛ dalɛ bibioo tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo tso niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso lɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni tsii baa.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest produce weaker crops than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time and can carry diseases from previous seasons. Certified store-bought seeds are specially bred to resist diseases and grow strong, high-yielding plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ shwapoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow all of a sudden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe trukaa ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It is a biological disease rather than a spiritual issue, and planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps protect your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Eji hela ko ni jɛ wala mli fe mumɔŋ naagba. Ni ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Without temporary shade from larger plants like plantains, intense direct sun will scorch the leaves and kill the young seedling.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains lɛ bɛ hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni egbe tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, damp conditions. Pruning dense branches lets air flow through the farm and keeps the pods dry to prevent the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ kɛ he ni ediŋŋ lɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Dense pruning haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ koni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains on the same land where they plant young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade to shield young cocoa plants from harsh sun, while also providing food and quick income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika oya dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Plants need room to breathe and feed. When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: He ko he miihia tsei ni amɛmu ni amɛye nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light yellow even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. While rain provides water, plants still need soil nutrients or organic fertilizer to stay green and produce well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ haa nu moŋ Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lolo koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on land where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmãa tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which restores soil fertility for future crops without needing heavy chemical inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plants with dry leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, keeps the ground moist by slowing down water evaporation and protects plant roots from extreme sun heat.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ he

english: Why do certified seeds from agro-dealers perform better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and diseases and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations and yield less.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less food even if I give the farm enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa ŋmɔ lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than regular crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops, leaving your plants malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu lɛ baaje onibii amli waa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are some cassava varieties better for making fufu while others are best for kokonte?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fufu feemɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi krokomɛi hi fe fɛɛ kɛha Conte cocos lɛ.

english: Different cassava varieties have varying levels of starch and water content. Varieties high in starch and lower in moisture pound smoothly into soft fufu, whereas other varieties dry out better and are ideal for processing into flour for kokonte.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ ashikiŋsha kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Akɛ starch ni fa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni faaa lɛ srɔtoi lɛ shwieɔ fufu ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehi kɛha nitsumɔ ni akɛfeɔ ashikishaŋ kɛha coconte.

english: Why do some raw cassava tubers taste sweet when boiled, while others taste very bitter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi komɛi ni ahoko lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ ahoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Bitterness comes from natural chemical compounds called cyanogenic glucosides. Sweet varieties have very low levels and are safe to boil and eat fresh, while bitter varieties have higher levels and need soaking, fermenting, or drying into flour to safely remove the toxins.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ cyanogenic glucosides lɛ mli baa. Sweet henɔi lɛ amli tsɔi lɛ baa shi waa ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaahoo ni aye ehee. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni mli edɔ lɛ fa babaoo ni ehe miihia ni awo mli, afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo agbi ni afee lɛ powda koni ajie tsofai fɔji lɛ kɛjɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant uses energy stored in its stems to quickly grow fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ etso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai heei oya.

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Too much nitrogen encourages leafy top growth instead of sending energy down to expand the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛha bulb lɛ ada.

english: Why do cut cassava stem sticks stay alive for weeks before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ hiɔ shi otsii babaoo dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems store food reserves, moisture, and dormant buds inside their bark. This allows the cuttings to stay alive in a cool shade until moist soil triggers them to grow roots.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ toɔ niyenii ni ato, fɛ̃i, kɛ ŋmeii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niji lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, shishifãi baakwɛ̃.

english: What causes cassava tubers to turn dark inside just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled from the ground, it undergoes natural rapid spoilage called post-harvest oxidation. Selling or processing the tubers within 24 to 48 hours prevents this internal darkening.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ ni yaa oya ni atsɛɔ lɛ oxidation lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ loo atsu ŋmeii lɛ ahe nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee duŋ yɛ mli.

english: How does planting cassava on raised mounds help the tubers grow bigger than planting on flat soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so roots can expand easily without resistance. Mounding also improves water drainage, preventing soil from getting soggy and rotting the growing tubers.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni efite bulbs ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the cassava roots. Without oxygen, fungal diseases thrive in the wet soil and quickly rot the buried tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Fungal hela lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Will my soil lose its strength if I keep planting cassava on the same land every year?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Yes, cassava absorbs large amounts of soil nutrients, especially potassium. Continuous planting without adding fertilizer, manure, or rotating crops will wear out the soil and reduce future yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. titri lɛ potassium Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebaaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi.

english: How can I turn cassava farming into a profitable business so the youth in my village stop running to the cities?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmei dumɔ afee jarayeli nitsumɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he? Bɔni afee ni oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ akpa foidamɔ kɛmiiya maŋ lɛ mli?

english: Using high-yielding improved cassava varieties, preparing land with tractors, and connecting with processors who buy bulk cassava for starch or flour cuts heavy manual labor and brings reliable, commercial profits.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmei henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tsu nii Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kɛ traktɔ Ni akɛ mɛi ni feɔ ŋmei ni heɔ ŋmei babaoo kɛhaa ashikishaŋ loo ŋmei lɛ abɔ lɛ baaha nitsumɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ jarayeli sɛɛnamɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ aba.

english: Can I use natural plant extracts like neem juice to prevent insect attacks on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli, tamɔ neem nu lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi akatutua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, spraying natural plant extracts like neem acts as a preventive measure that repels insect pests and slows down their breeding without harming the plant or soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli tso mli nibii tamɔ neem ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa amɛbotemɔ baa shi ni eyeee tso lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ awui.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my plantain leaves, and how can I stop them from spreading?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ miije kpo yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa?

english: Dark spots are caused by leaf spot diseases that spread through air and rain; cutting off affected leaves early acts as a preventive step to keep the rest of the plant healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa ji leaf spot hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni ena hela lɛ mra. Enɛ baafee nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa koni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or insect damage, which prevents the flowers from developing into mature pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen or that excessive rain has washed nutrients away from the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural behavior where the tomato plant reduces its leaf surface area to prevent losing too much water during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni tomato tsei baa baa lɛ nɔ shi koni nu ni fa fe nine akafite yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden weather changes that cause stress during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa ni kɛ haomɔ baa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts together with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baafata he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts cover the soil to keep moisture in and naturally fix nitrogen into the earth, which provides essential food for the growing cassava plants.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni ekɛ nitrogen ahi sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmei dumɔ

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees provide shade and conserve moisture needed for the cocoa to survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kookoo ahi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do cassava cuttings need to be planted at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu lɛ jaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slight angle encourages roots to spread out evenly underground, making it easier for tubers to swell and grow large.
ga: Kɛ́ odu o-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot quickly inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize naturally holds moisture inside the grains; if it is bagged before drying fully in the sun, trapped moisture encourages mold and insects to grow.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ awo kotokui amli dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a completely cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse kwraa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as natural shade trees, protecting the young leaves from sunburn and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ tso ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo Buu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves its limited nutrients from older leaves up to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni fa fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil during seasons of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots get waterlogged and suffocated, which attracts bacteria that cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛmuɔ. Enɛ gbalaa helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers but the flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or dry conditions cause heat stress, making tomato plants drop their blossoms to save water and energy. Lack of bees or insects to pollinate the blossoms can also cause them to fall off without fruiting.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Gbalamɔ tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai koni okɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo ni aduawai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients without overcrowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli fe nine. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that builds the tubers underground. Raising the leaves off the wet ground using stakes allows maximum sunlight exposure and prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe babaoo, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing the central leaves of my young maize plants to develop ragged holes filled with sawdust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf funnel of young maize plants to feed. Treating the central shoot with safe, recommended pest controls early protects the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baai amli koni amɛye nii. Tsamɔ teŋ tsei lɛ kɛ shweshweeshwe, tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaawoo mra. Ebuɔ tip ni miida lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking, curling upward, and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf juices and spread plant viruses. Controlling these sucking insects early prevents the leaf curl disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa nu lɛ ni amɛ gbɛɔ muawai yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ chili baa baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi leaf curl hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or palm leaves around the base of my crops help them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter acts as mulch, shielding the soil from direct sun heat. This blanket keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly and helps plant roots stay cool and hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ haaa sũ mli nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛmli edɔ.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops every year if I keep growing the same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating different crops, especially beans or peanuts, helps naturally restore nutrients and keep the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ titri lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, a major food crops need to grow strong. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young top leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃ waa lɛ Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eha hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland help improve the soil for my other crops later?
ga: Kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested and its leaves rot back into the earth, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaa lɛ fiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ. Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the inner leaves of my young maize stalks during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which seek shelter inside the tender stem fold (whorl) where it is moist and safe from direct sunlight and birds. Catching them early by applying organic neem oil solution or recommended sprays inside the leaf folds protects the plant's main growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni naa abobaahe yɛ tsitsii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli (rings) he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ okpoi ahe lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that feed on the sap under the leaves and spread plant viruses. Protecting the plants with insect traps or spraying diluted soapy water or neem extract early stops the insects from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Buu tsei ahe kɛ kooloi bibii ahe tsɔnei loo okɛ samla ni mli ewo nu loo neem mli nu afɔ amɛhe mra. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii akafee babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches start getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains do not produce deep taproots; instead, they have shallow feeder roots that stay near the surface. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, strong winds or soft wet soil can easily pull the roots up. Propping the main trunk with a strong bamboo or wooden fork gives the plant extra support.
ga: Plantains lɛ wooo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ we nɛ a kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ dara waa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye abua lɛ babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines up on sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ miniji lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy, which is then directed down into the ground to swell the yam tuber. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air, preventing leaf rot diseases from the wet ground and stopping weeds from shading them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Tsi baa ni fiteɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ naa. ni ehaa jwɛi tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground if I leave them in the earth during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When rain saturates the soil completely for long periods, air cannot reach the underground tubers, causing root suffocation. This excess water allows wet-rot fungi in the soil to multiply quickly and break down the cassava tubers before harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, sũ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nu ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni efiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes split open along their sides right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden surge of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water rapidly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Tomatoi baatswa kɛji amɛná nu ni fa trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of blossoms, but flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil food, or extreme shade. Preserving moist leaf litter on the farm floor encourages the pollinating midges to breed.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, shi fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo Ni akɛ baa ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why should I wait for regular rain before planting my second season seeds instead of planting right after the first light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa koni madu dumɔwui yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: A single light rain only wets the top layer of dirt, leaving the deeper soil hot and dry. If seeds sprout after light rain, their delicate young roots will run into dry earth below and wither before the next rain falls.
ga: Shawa kome ni mli tse lɛ baaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ Eshishifãi bibii lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagbi dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do some crops like cassava take nearly a whole year to mature while crops like maize take only a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei, heɔ afi lɛ mli be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Crops have different growth cycles based on how they store energy. Maize stores energy in seeds above ground, which happens quickly, while cassava builds up starch in thick underground roots, requiring many months of rainfall and sunlight to grow full tubers.
ga: Tsei yɛ dalɛ bei srɔtoi ni damɔ bɔ ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Abele toɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli, ni ebaa oya. Beni ŋmeii buaa starch naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ. Eheɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo nyɔji babaoo dani yitso ni eyi obɔ baakwɛ̃.

english: If I plant fruit trees like mango or citrus, how many years should I expect to wait before getting a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji midu aduawai tsei tamɔ mango loo ŋmei Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Most fruit trees take about 3 to 5 years to bear their first proper harvest because the plant must first spend its early years building strong roots and branches to support heavy fruits.
ga: Yibii tsei babaoo heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii ni sa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, be he miihia tsei yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni afee shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baaye abua aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do cocoa seedlings need shade from plantain trees when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ adɛŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn and dry out easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants shade and cool air until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ha kookoo tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when water stays on my field for too long after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil becomes waterlogged, the crop roots cannot get oxygen from the air in the soil. Without oxygen, the roots stop working, preventing the plant from drinking water or nutrients, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baakpa nitsumɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkanu nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do crops grow differently if I move my farm from a forest zone to a drier area around Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛji mijie miŋmɔ lɛ kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle Accra lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions have different soil types, humidity, and rainfall levels. Drier coastal regions like Accra have less annual rainfall, so crops need extra water management or crop varieties that handle dry weather well.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, latsaa, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi. Ŋshɔnaa hei ni egbi, tamɔ Accra lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ daa afi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo kroko loo tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear small weeds around my crop plants even when they do not seem to be blocking the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? mi tsei lɛ ahe Kɛji jwɛi lɛ tsiii hulu lɛ naa po.

english: Weeds steal water and valuable plant food directly from the soil using their roots. Even small weeds feed aggressively and can starve your main crops before they get a chance to produce yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi bibii po Eyeɔ niyenii oya ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hɔmɔ aye onibii titri lɛ dani ená hegbɛ ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts on a farm field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize next, it feeds on this extra nitrogen to grow larger and healthier.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa be kroko lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni fa nɛɛ koni eda ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or transmitting viruses. This damages the leaves, causing them to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ ehe ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits when the heat becomes very high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures become too hot, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries up and fails to fertilize the plant. Unfertilized flowers cannot form fruit, so the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ tso lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ tsei duɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do fall armyworms attack my maize, and how can I identify their damage early?
ga: Te cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse nɔ ni efite lɛ mra?

english: Fall armyworms crawl into the central growing tip (the funnel) of young maize plants and eat the soft leaves inside. You can spot their damage early by looking for ragged holes in leaves and powdery, dark droppings inside the funnel.
ga: Roundworms lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋgbɛ (cone) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ ona nɔ ni efite lɛ mra. Taomɔ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ powda yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential plant food, or the soil has too much water sitting in it. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the dirt. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ekpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why does animal manure make my crops grow better than planting in plain dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with rich organic matter and essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. It also helps the soil hold onto moisture longer during dry periods, providing your crops with a steady supply of food and water.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu daa.

english: Why will planting my crop seeds too close together give me a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong stems and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ shi ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people cover the soil around young crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This technique is called mulching. Covering the dirt with dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋaa nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water in flat or clay soil, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I am already giving the farm water and care?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikwɛ nɔ hu?

english: Weeds grow faster than most cultivated crops and aggressively steal water, light, and nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you provide.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa amɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft center of the plant. Checking your field early and putting neem leaf extract or recommended treatments into the leaf funnel can protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni okɛaawo tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that hide under the leaves, combined with stress from hot dry weather. Providing light shade and controlling these insects restores normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛfata he lɛ, nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ mli baa. La ni akɛhaa kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ haa amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can grow big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?
