english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shady, and crowded farms. Pruning extra branches lets in sunlight and air flow, which dries out the farm and protects the cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni hulu enyɔ shi, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni afolɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the soil, and heavy bunches make the tree top-heavy. Supporting the trees with wooden stakes or planting them in protected areas keeps them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni niji ni tsii haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii. Tsei ni akɛ tsei fiɔ sɛɛ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up, shrink, and look yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects and infected stems. Using disease-resistant planting stems from certified sources prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni jɛ hei ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to remove weeds around my yam mounds if the yams grow deep inside the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? mi ŋmeii ni ato lɛ Ni kɛji ŋmeii kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ hu?

english: Even though yam tubers grow underground, the leaves on top need sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to feed those tubers. Weeds steal those resources, resulting in smaller yam tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato tubers lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ, Shi baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he miihia hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni nakai bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi juɔ nakai nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when it gets too hot, when they lack water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Regular morning watering and providing light shade during peak heat helps the fruit set.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ nu bɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni baaha amɛfɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa leebi kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it better to water my pepper farm in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔji amli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb water before the hot sun evaporates it. It also prevents wet leaves from sitting in hot sun or staying wet overnight, which reduces leaf diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo ni amɛkashwieɔ nu nyɔɔŋ kome. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa helai baa shi

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. If crops look pale or grow very slowly despite rain, the soil likely needs organic matter like compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛdaraa blɛoo waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cowpea and bean crops seem to make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea kɛ bean tsei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop planted there.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests and diseases build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops like groundnuts or beans breaks disease cycles and restores the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Enɛ haa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from old leaves up to new ones to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into little cups and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pods?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop most of their flowers because they only keep the number of pods they have enough water, soil nutrients, and energy to support.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa ŋmeii ayibɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛ. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but the flower stems bend down and push into loose soil because the groundnut pod can only develop dark and safe underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ bean pods baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the soil when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess standing water chokes the roots, allowing fungal rots to set in and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ewoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and underfed.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb on instead of crawling on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yams lifts the leaves into the sunlight and air, which helps the leaves make more food to build bigger, heavier tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato lɛ wo tso mli lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I cut away extra young shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots suck away water and food from the main mother plant, causing her to take longer to fruit and produce smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii ni ewoɔ niji bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small roots that burn easily under direct sun. They need shade trees to stay cool and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key food for plants, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to its newer leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do crops grow much better in fields where I previously grew cowpeas or groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni tsutsu lɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plants like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Tsei tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to block the direct sun and keep the air cool while their roots are still small and weak.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa hulu la lɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ darako ni amɛhe waaa lɛ.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward on hot days to reduce the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, which helps the plant save water and stop itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni eba baa lɛ nɔ hulu la shi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for building tubers underground, and keeping leaves off the soil prevents damp rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai baaa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over right when the bunch of fruit starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip the soil deeply, so the heavy weight of a growing bunch can pull the tree down unless you support it with a strong wooden prop.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni tsii baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ kɛba shi. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself from losing water through evaporation, storing its energy safely underground in the roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. ni akɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil because the plant gets stressed and discards the flowers to conserve moisture for its main stem.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is there dark, wet dust inside the central funnel of my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center of the maize plant where it eats the new, soft leaves during the growing season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Ebaaye baai bibii heei. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: Why should I avoid applying dry granular fertilizer when the soil is completely dry and there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ bako lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so root systems can absorb them; applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts that can burn and damage plant roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection because direct, intense sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects the cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe miihia ni abu amɛhe ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ agbi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. This nitrogen acts as a natural food for the maize, making the soil richer without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is soaked in standing water. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before I plant my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams grow downward into the earth and need soft, loose soil to expand into large tubers. Mounds provide deep, loose dirt and allow excess rain to drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji feɔ muji ni mli kwɔ, ni etse ehe. ni oha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli koni ekafite

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii kpakpa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the flowers from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap from new leaves. Spraying early with recommended organic pest controls like neem oil helps protect the foliage and flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ neem fɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, abaabu baai kɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets fluctuating amounts of water. Extreme heat makes the pollen dry out, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu ni tsakeɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell before the main rainy season starts. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then die in the hot, dry soil before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ, ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: When is the best time during the day for me to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool and the soil is moist. Heavy midday heat can burn plant roots and cause the fertilizer to evaporate away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava under the soil is ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months, the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: How do I know when my corn is completely ready for harvesting so I don't pick it too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋɔɔɔ mra tsɔ.

english: Corn is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and the silks at the top become dark brown and brittle. You can also press a kernel with your fingernail; if a clear liquid or black spot at the kernel base appears instead of milky fluid, it is fully mature.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ hu anyɛ kernel lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu ni mli tse loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ je kpo yɛ ŋmei lɛ shishi yɛ nu ni tamɔ mliki lɛ najiaŋ. tsɔɔ akɛ edɔ kwraa

english: What happens if I leave my ripe beans on the farm for too long before picking them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mifolɔ amɛ?

english: If dry bean pods are left on the plant too long under the sun, the pods will pop open on their own and scatter the seeds on the ground. Harvesting on time prevents this loss, known as pod shattering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baatswa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be naa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pod ni ekumɔ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I harvest them early in the morning or during the hot sun?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikpa leebi loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: It is best to harvest early in the morning when the temperature is cool. Harvesting in peak heat causes crops like vegetables and cobs to lose moisture rapidly and spoil faster when packed together.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ŋmaa lɛ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsuɔ nii kɛkpaa nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsɔne mli.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll inward during hot weather to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural defense to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why are my bean plants dropping their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant loses its flowers to protect itself and save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Tsei laajeɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting beans makes the soil better for my next crop of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes, which means they take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the bean roots decay after harvest, they leave behind rich nitrogen food that helps your next corn crop grow strong.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ niyenii babaoo ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ koni eye ebua oŋmei tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Can I plant beans and corn together in the same field without them destroying each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them with proper spacing. Tall corn stalks act as a support structure for climbing beans, while the low bean plants cover the ground to stop weeds and feed nitrogen back into the soil for the corn.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofo amɛ kɛ gbɛ ni sa. Abɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni fiɔ ŋmeii ni akwɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ baa shi ni awoɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni amɛkɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ awo sũ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my young crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very aggressive roots that absorb water and soil food faster than young crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops the sunlight and nutrients they need to grow bigger than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei bibii. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs start growing white mold when I store them in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛtoɔ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when corn cobs are put into storage while still containing too much moisture. Drying your cobs thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard before storing them stops fungus and mold from growing.
ga: Mold daa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Agbiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: What do the powdery tassels at the top of my corn plants actually do for the cobs?
ga: Mɛni kpakpa ashikishaŋ tsɔji ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The tassels produce pollen grains that must fall onto the sticky silks lower down on the plant. Every single grain of corn on a cob grows from one silk that received pollen, so good tasseling leads to full, complete cobs.
ga: Tassels lɛ jieɔ pollen ni esa akɛ egbee siliki ni ŋmɔɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Abɛi mli ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ siliki ni akɛ pollen etsu nii lɛ mli ŋmei kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ brɔshi tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ ayi obɔ ni eye emuu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to block the intense heat and hold moisture in the soil while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: I see my cocoa trees producing many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods. Why is this happening?
ga: Minaa akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces far more flowers than it can feed, so dropping some is normal. However, excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks water, nutrients, or is stressed by hot winds and insects.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ yibii komɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi bibii haoɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing from the base of my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those shoots, called chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk and pods. Removing them keeps the tree strong and allows sunlight and air to flow through, which prevents pod diseases.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akabote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark, and overly wet conditions. Keeping the farm weeded, pruning low branches, and removing affected pods stops the spread.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ low pruning Ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ena naagbai lɛ baaha egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green or yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and lets pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients to the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower and produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo kwraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds take over, your crops are deprived of the essential resources they need to grow and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water prevents oxygen from reaching them in flooded soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it good to cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves and grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture trapped in the earth, and prevents your crops from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. ni otsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are the rains not coming at the exact same time every year like they used to on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaa yɛ be kome mli daa afi tamɔ tsutsu lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Changes in global weather patterns and rising temperatures are shifting the timing of rainy seasons. Farmers can no longer rely purely on traditional calendar months and should instead monitor actual soil moisture and local weather updates before sowing seeds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he kɛ latsaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ miitsake nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ. Okwaafoi nyɛŋ amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ blema kalanda nyɔji anɔ. alone anymore Agbɛnɛ hu, kwɛmɔ ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe saji dani odu dumɔwui.

english: How can modern weather updates tell me the right time to plant my maize when the weather is so unpredictable?
ga: Te Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ Beaŋ Kɔɔyɔŋ He Saji lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ akɛɛ mi be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee aha lɛ?

english: Modern weather services use satellites in the sky to track rain clouds and temperature changes across large areas. Extension officers receive this information to warn farmers about upcoming dry spells or heavy rains so you don't lose your seeds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nitsumɔhei kɛ satelait ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ atatui, nugbɔ kɛ latsaa tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ hei wuji lɛ anɔ. Extension nitsulɔi lɛ nine shɛɔ saji nɛɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbɔ okwaafoi lɛ kɔkɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be loo nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni baa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni okafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, or when the soil lacks organic matter. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing big corncobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves each plant too weak to form proper corncobs. Giving each seed its own space allows it to grow thick and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmãa ŋmeii ni sa. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land yield smaller harvests when I plant cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific diseases build up in the dirt. Rotating cassava with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility and prevents disease.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ Cassava. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings naturally grow under forest canopy shade; their delicate leaves cannot handle harsh direct sunlight, which burns them and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ebaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baashã ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need to be planted with their bud nodes pointing upward toward the sky. If buried upside down or buried too deep in hard soil, the buds cannot reach the sunlight and will rot underground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shishi loo eshɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli tsɔ lɛ, hulu la shɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits rot on the ground if I leave the plants to grow flat on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji mishi tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants resting directly on wet ground are exposed to soil fungi and pests that attack the skin of the fruit. Tying the plants to wooden stakes keeps the tomatoes off the damp dirt, keeps them dry, and allows fresh air to blow through.
ga: Tomato tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ehaa tomatoi lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ, ehaa amɛgbiɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my young corn plants and leaving dark powdery dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibii ni miyeɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing tip of the corn plant. Catching them early by checking your crops weekly allows you to control them using safe bio-pesticides or ash mixes before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ onibii ni okwɛɔ daa otsi lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo sũ ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience high heat stress or sudden water shortage. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive extreme hot weather until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo nu ni faaa trukaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, acting as natural shade umbrellas to protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each plant space allows roots to spread and stalks to grow strong, producing larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hegbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni eshishifã lɛ daa waa. ni kɛ cob ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and make food for the plant.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: How does animal manure actually help my crops grow better than soil alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ pɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil by adding rich food for plant roots and helping the soil hold moisture for longer during dry days, making crops healthier and stronger.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my farm so it is not wasted?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after light rain, early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Avoid applying right before heavy downpours, which wash the fertilizer away before roots can take it in.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. leebi loo shwane Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Enɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect medicine on my crops in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ?

english: Hot sunlight causes crop medicine to evaporate into the air quickly before it can work. The strong heat can also cause the liquid chemical to scorch and burn your crop leaves.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsofai ni ji nu lɛ hu ni eshã otso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the fresh center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai heei ni jɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the soft, growing heart of the maize plant. If left untreated, they can destroy the growing point and ruin your crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei atsuii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ni amɛfite onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Root rot happens when water stays trapped in heavy soil around the roots for too long, or when soil diseases attack. Planting on raised ridges helps excess water drain away to keep roots healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ hela ba. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil food. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy just to stay alive.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiii Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there is enough rainfall for everything on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal more than just water; they suck up the nutrients in the soil, block sunlight, and harbor insects and diseases that spread to your healthy crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nɔ ni fe nu kɛkɛ Amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa, ni amɛji ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe jɛɛhe.

english: When is the best time for me to plant my maize during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli?

english: You should plant right after the first two or three steady rains arrive, usually around April. Planting too early in dry soil causes the seeds to dry up or rot before they can sprout properly.
ga: Esa akɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ, bei pii lɛ yɛ April aaafee. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect its roots underground. Once the rains return, the plant will produce fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Yams require deep, loose, well-drained soil so the tubers can grow long and fat. If your soil is heavy clay or full of rocks, the tubers will remain small or become misshapen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato. Bɔni afee ni yitso lɛ atsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛ fɔ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo loo ebaafee nɔ ni efite.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by root rot or bacterial wilt from standing water. Soil that stays too wet starves the roots of air and encourages diseases that prevent water from climbing up the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaawo helai ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekakwɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How can I stop caterpillars from eating the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms. You can protect your corn by inspecting the centers of the leaf shoots regularly and applying recommended botanical sprays like neem oil or mild insect control early before they spread.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji enɛɛmɛi. Obaanyɛ obu o-abele lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni oookwɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ atsu nii mra. dani egbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds regularly helps keep the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kookoo lɛ mli tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which feeds the maize and improves overall soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking leaf juices and passing on viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem leaf extract stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips kɛ chili baa baa. Emuɔ baa nu ni ekɛ helai baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I keep insects from eating my harvested rice while it is in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Make sure your rice is thoroughly dried under the sun before storing it, and keep it in clean, sealed, airtight bags. Storage pests need air and moisture to survive and multiply.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-rice lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi dani okɛto. ni okɛto vacuum kotoku ko ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii amli lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and struggle to hold the weight of heavy fruit bunches, especially in wet soil. Propping the stems up with sturdy wooden Y-sticks supports the trees until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn brown when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sunshine. They need shade from temporary nurse crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from heat and conserve moisture until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha fɛ̃i ahi mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the hot ground and spreads them out so they can trap more sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa bɔni afee ni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsi ohe kɛba shi koni ofee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I pluck all the leaves off my cassava plants to feed my animals while waiting to harvest the roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso mli lɛ koni mikɛha kooloi niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni akpa shishifãi lɛ?

english: Removing too many leaves stops the cassava tubers from growing bigger. Leaves gather sunlight to feed the root roots below ground, so stripping them early reduces your final harvest size.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai babaoo lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmei shishifã lɛ naa koni ekafee agbo. Baai lɛ buaa hulu la naa koni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant gets stressed by sudden hot dry weather or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm help the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food in the soil. When you harvest them, this natural fertilizer remains in the ground for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni obaakpa Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves. Spraying safe bio-pesticides like neem oil extract kills these insects and stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem fɔ mli nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni agbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ekpa baa ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak with tiny ears when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ toi bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow strong and produce large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ená toi wuji.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops heat from evaporating soil water quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist for a longer time and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do small insects still destroy my harvested maize even after I have sun-dried it properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Insects like maize weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the kernels while the crop is still in the field. To keep dried grain safe, store it in clean, airtight bags or storage hermetic containers that block air and starve pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe Kɛ amɛ awo kotoku ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ anaa lɛ mli.

english: Is relying on rain and prayer enough to get a good cocoa harvest, or do I need specific farming techniques?
ga: Ani nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ sɔlemɔ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛkpaa kookoo kpakpa? Aloo okwaayeli he ŋaa pɔtɛɛ ko he miihia mi?

english: While favorable weather is essential, modern farming practices such as proper pruning, timely weeding, and soil management are necessary to protect crops and ensure a consistently high yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa moŋ, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ Ehe miihia ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akwɛ koni yibii babaoo aba be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my neighboring farmers getting much higher crop yields even though our farms share the same weather and soil type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ amli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Differences in yields usually depend on farm management practices. Farmers who adopt improved techniques like regular pruning, shade management, and pest control harvest far more than those who rely only on traditional methods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi ni kɛ ŋaai ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ tsuɔ nii Shade management kɛ pests control lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ blema gbɛi pɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open, cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or plantains to shield them from intense heat and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does proper plant spacing make my crops grow healthier and produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Spacing plants correctly ensures that every tree receives enough sunlight, air circulation, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, leading to stronger stems and higher fruit production.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during dry spells usually signal water stress or nutrient deficiency. Leaving dry leaves and organic matter around the base of the tree as mulch helps retain soil moisture and protect the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ nu he haomɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crop yields keep dropping every year when I farm on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ mitsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously removes vital nutrients from the soil over time. Replenishing the soil with organic compost or appropriate fertilizer restores its fertility so your crops can produce well again.
ga: Tsei ni miida lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads easily in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning overgrown tree branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm and reduce pod rot.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ, ni ehaa pod ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I spend time picking off diseased cocoa pods if they are already ruined?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛbua kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa kɛji akɛ amɛfite momo?

english: Leaving infected pods on the tree allows fungal spores and insect pests to multiply and spread to your remaining healthy pods. Removing diseased pods early saves the rest of your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaahere onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why does it take a few years for a new cocoa tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii fioo komɛi dani cacao tsei heei jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to establish strong root systems and thick branches to store food and support heavy fruit. Proper care during these early years ensures the tree stays productive for decades.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ niji ni mli tse ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato ni amɛkɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni sa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli Enɛɛmɛi haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they lack water, proper nutrients, or insect pollinators. Keeping the tree well-nourished helps it hold on to more flowers and turn them into mature pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu bɛ mli. Niyenii ni sa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi baa lɛ Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo ni ená fɔfɔi ni eda babaoo.

english: Why do seeds brought from other regions or countries sometimes fail to grow well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ kpokpai loo maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops adapt over time to the specific weather, rainfall pattern, and soil of where they originally came from. If you bring a seed from a different climate, it may struggle with Ghana's heat, rains, or local pests, leading to poor yields or crop failure.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsake amɛhe yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ejɛ mli eba lɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli ba lɛ Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ Ghana lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant seeds I brought back from my travels without asking an officer first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui ni mikɛba kɛjɛ gbɛfaa mli ni mibiii nitsulɔi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds brought from outside can carry hidden pests, fungi, or diseases that do not exist in your area. Planting them can infect your soil and spread dangerous crop diseases to nearby farms.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, ŋmeii, loo helai ni bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ atswa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hela ni ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if a new crop seed will survive in my specific village before I buy a lot of it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baahi shi yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli dani mahe amɛ babaoo?

english: Always check if the new seed was bred for a climate and soil similar to your village, or plant a very small test patch first to observe how it handles your local weather before investing fully.
ga: Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui heei kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔji ni tamɔ okrowa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Aloo du kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko kwraa klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baatsu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nii eha dani okɛ shika awo mli kwraa.

english: Why do my traditional local crops survive bad weather better than the new high-yielding seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ tsei, ni ji mimaŋ tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa mli jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Local traditional crops have spent decades adapting to your area's tough weather, dry spells, and local insects. New high-yielding varieties are designed to produce more, but they often require steady rain, good soil, and extra care to do well.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi ni aduɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ehé afii nyɔŋmai abɔ dani ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, hɔmɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ etsu nii. Afee tsei srɔtoi heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, shikpɔŋ kpakpa, kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛfɔ bii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains start coming late or unexpectedly?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enɛɔ blɛoo loo trukaa lɛ?

english: It is best not to plant after the very first light rain, as the ground can quickly dry out and destroy your seeds. Wait until the rain becomes consistent for a week or two so the soil holds enough water for the seeds to grow strong roots.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ oya. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be otsi kome loo enyɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow during periods of continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When it rains too much without stopping, excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil. This drowns the plant roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ekpaaa Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Can I grow crops that thrive in the northern dry savannah down here in the southern forest zone?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ biɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ koo lɛ kpokpaa ni egbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Not always. Crops from dry northern zones prefer high heat and lower humidity. The heavy rainfall and high humidity of the forest zone can cause these crops to suffer from rot, fungal diseases, or mold.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei ni jɛ kooyigbɛ hei ni nu egbi lɛ sumɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni baa shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei nɛɛ agbɔjɔ, amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ, loo amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does the same maize seed grow tall on my valley land but stay short on my hilltop land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mijɔɔ lɛ mli shi eyɛ kuku yɛ migɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Valley land collects topsoil and rainwater washed down from higher areas, making it rich and moist. Hilltop land loses its water and nutrients quickly through erosion, causing crops there to grow smaller.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ buaa shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anaa. Ehaa efeɔ nii ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look dead in the afternoon heat even though I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛgbooo lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu ewo mli?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Curling their leaves is a natural way for the plant to protect itself from the burning sun and save water until the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing lots of big green leaves above ground but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, it puts all its energy into making leafy branches instead of storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji kɛ baai amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why does cocoa grow well on my neighbor's land but fails on mine in the same district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ shi ekwɛɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and nutrient levels can vary widely even between nearby farms, directly affecting how cocoa roots spread and absorb nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi waa yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ateŋ po. Enɛ saa bɔ ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ jaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛŋɔɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is good for planting cocoa before I invest my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mikɛ shika awo mli?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, well-drained, rich in organic matter, and retains moisture without becoming waterlogged during heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ mlibotemɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Does every farm town in Ghana have soil suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi maji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, cocoa requires specific forest-zone conditions with rich, deep soil. Drier or savannah regions are better suited for crops like cashew, sorghum, or shea.
ga: Dabi, kookoo biɔ koo mli shihilɛi pɔtɛɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii. Hei ni egbi loo savannah lɛ ji hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew ŋmeii, sorghum loo chia.

english: Why do some crops perform completely differently when moved from one region of Ghana to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa nɔ kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ Ghana kpokpaa kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Variations in rainfall patterns, sunlight intensity, local temperatures, and soil composition across Ghana change how crops grow and yield fruit.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulu la ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii amli yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Tsakemɔ bɔ ni tsei daa kɛ amɛwoɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ

english: Why do my crops wither quickly during hot spells while nearby farms stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Differences in soil moisture retention, organic compost levels, and shade cover determine how well soil stays moist during periods of intense heat.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli organic compost level Kɛ shade tsɔɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why should I check how local crops perform in my area before trying a new crop variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ dani maka tso hee ko makwɛ?

english: Local climate conditions and pest populations affect how new varieties adapt. Observing nearby farms reduces the risk of crop failure on your land.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ saa bɔ ni tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ he. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ, ebaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die off soon after I plant them on new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ yɛ he ko hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are vulnerable to extreme heat and transplant shock; they need temporary shade from crops like plantains to survive their early months.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ anɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli.

english: How does shade affect the way my cocoa trees grow and bear fruit?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade protects young trees from scorching sun, but mature trees need a balanced mix of filtered sunlight to flower and produce healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What makes a crop like cocoa profitable for long-term farming in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo feɔ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa is a reliable perennial crop with a structured local purchasing market, providing steady seasonal income for decades when managed with good farming practices.
ga: Cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni yeɔ jara ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa be mli shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai tsu nii.

english: How can I make my farm as successful as the top cocoa farmers in my town?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ aye omanye tamɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Successful farmers achieve high yields by using proper plant spacing, regular weeding, timely pest management, and maintaining adequate soil fertility.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛtsɔ tsei ateŋ gbɛ ni sa ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ be naa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ akwɛmɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaf surfaces burn easily and dry out quickly. Shade trees protect young seedlings from excessive heat and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes a strong root system.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shãa oya ni egbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa.

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move down the center line show that the soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new top growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kaadi ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ naagbee lɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ teŋgbɛ line lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when daytime temperatures get too high or when there is sudden drought stress. The heat and lack of water prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ he haomɔ ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cassava roots thin and woody even though the stems grow very tall with many leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee mlɛo ni amɛfee tamɔ tso lɛ? Mɔ ni tso lɛ sɛɛ kwɔ waa ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water, it spends all its energy growing tall leafy branches instead of storing starch underground. Balanced soil nutrients force the plant to direct its food down into expanding the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmeii baato shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye nii koni amɛshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.
