english: Why do some of my pepper seeds sprout quickly while others in the same bed do not germinate at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ? Yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ, edaaa kwraa?

english: Pepper seeds need consistent soil warmth and continuous moisture near the surface to break dormancy. Seeds planted too deep or in dry soil spots fail to get enough oxygen and water to start growing.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa kɛ nu ni mli edɔ daa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni efo wɔɔhe. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ naaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants curl up and feel sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji ota he lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. As they feed, they excrete a sugary juice called honeydew that coats the leaves and attracts dark mold.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Amɛjieɔ nu ni atsɛɔ lɛ wuo mli nu lɛ kpo. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo baai lɛ amli ni egbala ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold downwards and droop heavily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbee shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold down and droop to protect themselves from intense heat. By reducing the leaf area exposed directly to the sun, the plant slows down water evaporation through its leaves during dry spells.
ga: Akɛ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi tsɔ. Kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does Striga weed grow right next to my maize roots and make the maize turn purple and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miida yɛ mi-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ? Ni eha ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ purple ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Striga seeds lie asleep in the soil until maize roots send out chemical signals. Once awakened, Striga attaches directly to the crop’s roots to steal water and nutrients, starving the maize from underground.
ga: Striga dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ tsofa he okadii. Kɛji Striga te shi lɛ, ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni hɔmɔ aye ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my yam plants yield smaller tubers when I leave the vines to crawl on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ naa bulbs bibii beni mishiɔ wain tso lɛ koni eyafo shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni matswa stake lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to capture maximum sunlight for energy production. When vines crawl on the ground, leaves shade each other, leading to lower energy production and smaller underground tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni emɔ hulu la babaoo ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Beni wain tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni ŋmeii bibii hu baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa beans stay purple and taste bitter instead of turning chocolate brown after drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ purple ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ tsokolate brown beni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Beans remain purple and bitter if they were not fermented long enough under plantain leaves before drying. Proper fermentation generates natural heat that breaks down bitter compounds and turns the bean interior brown.
ga: Beans lɛ baakã he afee purple ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ atswaaa amɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ plantain baai lɛ ashishi dani amɛgbi. Fɛ̃i ni sa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nibii ni mli edɔ lɛ baa ni ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Now that the first rains have fallen, how do I know if my soil has enough moisture for me to start planting seeds?
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eho. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui aje shishi?

english: You can test your soil by squeezing a handful from a few inches below the surface. If it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water or crumbling into dry dust, the soil has ideal moisture for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ sũ ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: What can my husband and I do on our farm to keep water in the soil for longer after it rains?
ga: Mɛni mi kɛ miwu baanyɛ afee yɛ wɔŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering the bare soil around your plants with dried grass, leaves, or crop stalks—a method called mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It slows down water evaporation, keeps the soil cool, and prevents moisture loss.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo tsei ashishifãi shwieɔ tsei ahe - gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ

english: How does adding dried animal manure to my farmland help my crops survive short dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil's ability to absorb rain and hold onto both water and plant nutrients for a long time, giving crops water even when rain stops for a few days.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ nugbɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii fɛɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha tsei lɛ aná nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi po.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant right after the rain to make a quick profit at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni maná sɛɛnamɔ oya yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Short-season vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, okra, and leafy greens grow quickly and can be harvested in 2 to 3 months, allowing you to sell early and generate fast cash.
ga: Aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tomato, pepper, okra kɛ leafy greens lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya ni onáa shika oya.

english: How can planting two different crops together on the same land help my family make more money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miweku lɛ ni ená shika babaoo?

english: Intercropping, such as planting maize and cowpeas together, maximizes your land. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil for the maize, and if one crop experiences bad market prices or pests, you still have the other crop to harvest and sell.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii amli, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ohaa ogbɛhe lɛ feɔ babaoo Cowpeas kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha ŋmãa. Ni kɛji akɛ jarayeli jara ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Oyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants survive dry periods while my vegetable crops wither and die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-vegetable tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that reach water buried far below the surface, and it drops its leaves to conserve water when it is dry. Vegetable plants have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose water rapidly.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. ni ebaashɛre baai koni ekɛbu nu he beni egbi Aduawai tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn light yellow after heavy rains fall on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can flood the ground and drown root systems, preventing plants from absorbing nitrogen from the soil. When nitrogen is lacking, plants pull it from their bottom leaves first, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ atsɔ nu afua ni shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ baajie lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow big leafy green branches but fail to produce fruit or grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ niji kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Crops put all their energy into leaves if the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or lacks phosphorus and potassium. Phosphorus and potassium are the nutrients crops need to produce strong flowers, fruits, and seeds.
ga: Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine loo phosphorus kɛ potassium faaa. Phosphorus kɛ potassium ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi, aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my crop seeds to rot underground instead of sprouting after a very big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpeteŋkpele ko sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as water to sprout. If heavy rain leaves water sitting on the field, the soaked soil blocks air, causing seeds to suffocate and rot before they can grow above ground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu baakã he ahi ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best way for my husband and me to divide farm labor so our crops get watered and cared for properly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mi kɛ miwu baatsɔ nɔ wɔja ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ mli koni wɔdu nii lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni wɔkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Dividing work by time of day works best: one person can focus on early morning planting and weeding when it is cool, while the other handles afternoon tasks like applying mulch or checking plants for pests.
ga: Nitsumɔ mlijaa ni damɔ be nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ: Mɔ kome kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔ nɔ leebi maŋkpa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛji hulu lɛ miitso. yɛ be mli ni ekroko tsuɔ shwane nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I take planting materials or stems from crops that have withered leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ojieɔ tsei ahe nibii loo amɛshishifãi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni amɛbaai lɛ egbo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Withered leaves often mean the parent plant is sick, infested with pests, or dying. Planting stems or suckers from an unhealthy plant transfers those same diseases to your new field, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ. Ayɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui. loo gbomɔ Tso ni bɛ hewalɛ mli lɛ shishifãi loo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baagbɛ hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ eshwa he hee ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: How can I identify a healthy plant to select seeds or suckers from on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mahala dumɔwui loo ŋmeii kɛjɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for strong, upright stems, vibrant green leaves without spots or decay, and firm root systems. Healthy parent plants give your new crops the best chance to grow strong and resist diseases.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni wa ni ja. Baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he loo egbo. kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baaha otso hee lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛŋ emɔ lɛ.

english: If a plant looks fine overall but has a few withered leaves, is it safe to use for propagation?
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ fɛɛ hi jogbaŋŋ shi eyɛ baai komɛi ni egbo lɛ, ani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii kɛgbɛ eshwa?

english: It is safer to avoid plants with withered leaves entirely. Even if part of the plant looks good, disease or insect damage might already be spreading inside the stems and roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai egbo lɛ ahe kwraa. Kɛji tso lɛ fã ko hi jogbaŋŋ po Shi ekolɛ nɔ ni hela loo kooloi bibii efite lɛ egbɛ eshwa tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli momo.

english: What causes the leaves on my crops to wither and dry up even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po?

english: Leaves often wither despite rainfall due to root diseases, soil pests, or fungal infections that damage the roots, preventing the plant from taking up water and nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ yɛ shishifãi ahe hela hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops in the exact same field dry up while the ones next to them stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ gboɔ yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ gboiɔ lɛ? eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo

english: Plants can react differently due to variations in soil diseases, underground root damage from pests, or because weaker planting material was used for those specific plants.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aha hetoo yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ helai sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ loo akɛni akɛ dumɔ nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa nakai tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can severe afternoon heat cause my crop leaves to wither even if the ground is moist?
ga: Ani shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ agbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Yes, high sun heat causes plants to lose moisture from their leaves faster than roots can absorb it, leading to temporary wilting during the hottest part of the day.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to carefully inspect each crop before I choose which ones to harvest or keep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli jogbaŋŋ dani ahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ akpa loo akɛto lɛ?

english: Checking crops individually ensures you only harvest high-quality produce and prevent bad or diseased plants from mixing with healthy ones during storage or replanting.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ona nɔmimaa akɛ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ pɛ. ni etsĩɔ tsei ni ehiii loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafutu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ loo aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: What should I do if I find a few plants in my field with withered leaves while the rest look healthy?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina tsei fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni baai egbo yɛ be mli ni eshwɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: You should carefully pull out and destroy the infected plants away from the field so that pests or diseases do not spread to the surrounding healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ agbala tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ bɔni afee ni tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Does removing withered leaves from a growing plant help it recover?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ajie baai ni egbo kɛjɛ tso ko ni miida lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi?

english: Pruning off withered or diseased leaves helps prevent fungal spores from spreading and allows the plant to direct its energy toward fresh, healthy leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni egbo loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize or cassava turn yellow and wither early before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa loo mi-cassava lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early leaf yellowing and drying usually indicate a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen, attacks by sucking pests like aphids, or prolonged water stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni ŋmeii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids lɛ tutuaa amɛ, loo nu mli haomɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why does cocoa farming require so much continuous effort compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a delicate tree crop that needs constant attention—including regular pruning, shade regulation, and disease management—to prevent yield loss and keep the trees producing healthy pods for years.
ga: Cocoa ji jwɛi tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa. Nɔ ni fata he ji tso ni afoɔ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ tsiɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo.

english: What makes cocoa such a demanding crop to care for throughout the year?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo feɔ tso ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa goes through distinct stages like flowering, pod setting, and flushing, each requiring different handling such as weeding, hand-pesticide spraying, and carefully timed harvesting.
ga: Cocoa tsɔɔ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ tamɔ fɔfɔi, pod kpojiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eko fɛɛ eko biɔ gbɛi srɔtoi ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical to measure when treating my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ masusu beni mikwɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals are manufactured to specific concentrations, so you must always follow recommended unit measurements per water tank to avoid under-treating pests or burning your cocoa leaves with too much chemical.
ga: Afeɔ tsofai yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ onyiɛ susumɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛsusuɔ nu ŋtayaa fɛɛ nu ŋtayaa he lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsaa amɛ fioo tsɔ lɛ. loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛshãa kookoo baai

english: If a spray kills pests on my cocoa trees instantly, does that mean my farm is safe for the rest of the season?
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe yɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Instant effectiveness only kills the insects present at the moment of spraying; it does not protect your trees from new pests hatching or moving in later, so regular monitoring is still required.
ga: Nɔ ni tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Ebuuu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɛɛ kooloi heei ni sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛbaafɔ loo amɛbaabote mli lɛ ahe.No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ mli daa.

english: Can I use the same chemical spray meant for my cocoa trees on my food crops like cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ cacao nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei nɔ?

english: No, cocoa chemicals are formulated specifically for cocoa pests and tree bark; using them on food crops can ruin the crop or make the food unsafe to eat.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ aha kookoo kɛ kooloi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii loo eha niyenii afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: What happens if I apply a chemical to my cocoa trees in rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ cacao tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Rain can wash away the chemical before it has time to work, reducing its effectiveness and wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie tsofai kɛya dani amɛná be ni amɛkɛtsu nii. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ Eji shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ hu ni afiteɔ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black even when the tree trunk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that attacks the pods directly during rainy, humid conditions, requiring specific fungicide sprays to control even if the tree looks strong.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko ni gbeɔ ŋmeii atsu nii kɛkudɔ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ po.

english: How do capsids damage my cocoa trees if I do not spray on time?
ga: Te capsids lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ efite mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieee amɛnɔ yɛ be naa?

english: Capsids suck the sap from young shoots and pods, creating wounds that dry out branches and severely reduce your farm's pod production.
ga: Capsids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ekɛ pilamɔi ni haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gbiɔ ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees growing around them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cocoa tso lɛ aná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun, so shade trees help cool the farm, keep soil moist, and protect cocoa leaves from heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni magbee shi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flower shedding can happen naturally, but heavy loss is often caused by heat stress, water shortages, or insect attack preventing pod development.
ga: Blossom ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ nibii ni laajeɔ waa baa. nu ni faaa loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your crop lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient the plant needs to grow green and leafy. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛfee baai. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during the day even when there is water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root rot present in the soil. These germs block the tiny water pipes inside the stem, so water cannot travel from the roots to the leaves even if the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa. tso lɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ, nu nyɛŋ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems bend down and push themselves into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That is the natural behavior of the groundnut plant. After the flower is pollinated above ground, it forms a peg that grows downward into the soil so the nut can safely swell and mature underground away from sunlight and heat.
ga: Nakai ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni ŋmeii tsei yɔɔ. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Ebaafee peg ni baakwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, he ko ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ bɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry spells, extreme heat, or attack by mirid insects (akate). The tree drops flowers to save its energy and water for survival until conditions improve.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ ahum, latsaa ni naa wa, loo mirid (akate) tutuamɔi kpe. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on leaf sap and spreading viruses. The virus disrupts the plant's normal tissue growth, causing leaves to twist and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Virus lɛ gbalaa tso mli fãji ni yɔɔ daa lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Which way should I plant my cassava cuttings into the soil for them to grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the buds or eye-nodes pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the roots and leaves struggle to sprout in the right direction, resulting in weak plants and lower yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ he yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the hot soil into direct sunlight and increases air movement. Sunlight helps leaves manufacture more food, which flows down to build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmei agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete for nutrients, water, and light. Removing extra suckers leaves 2 or 3 strong stems, ensuring the main plant has enough food to grow a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii 2 loo 3 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa koni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few seed pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ woɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea receives too much water and nitrogen from heavy rains, it focuses all its energy on growing leaves instead of flowering. Heavy rains can also wash away pollen or attract pests that destroy flowers.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nu kɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔi amli muji lɛ loo egbala kooloi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why does paddy rice grow better when it is kept in shallow standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water protects young rice plants from competing weeds and maintains steady moisture needed for root development, allowing the plant to take up nutrients efficiently without drying out.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ buɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ahe. ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ ahi shi daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Groundnuts are unique because after the flower blooms above ground, the stem bends down and buries itself in the soil, where the actual nut develops and matures into a pod underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ tso lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my groundnuts produce empty shells with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells, often called 'pops,' usually happen when the soil lacks calcium or doesn't get enough water while the pods are forming under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘nut ŋmeii’ lɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I use a hoe to weed my groundnut field once the plants start spreading out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi yɛ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ?

english: Once groundnuts spread out, their young seed stems are growing down into the topsoil. Hoeing close to the plant breaks these stems and destroys the pods growing underground.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaakumɔ nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ ni efite tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut plants make the soil healthier for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning their roots work with beneficial soil microbes to capture nitrogen from the air and leave natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I check if my groundnuts underground are fully mature and ready to pull up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ agbala?

english: You can test readiness by opening a few sample pods in your farm; if the inner skin of the shell has turned dark brown or black instead of pale white, the nuts are fully mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka hesaamɔ okwɛ kɛtsɔ pods komɛi ni ooofee yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ edɔ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to dry my freshly dug groundnuts before storing or processing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-peanuts ni mifo ehee lɛ dani mikɛto loo matsu he nii lɛ?

english: Freshly dug groundnuts carry a lot of water in the seeds and shells. Drying them prevents dampness that causes fast mold growth and dangerous toxins like aflatoxins.
ga: Peanuts ni atsa ehee Nu babaoo baahi dumɔwui lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ oya lɛ kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ naa.

english: Why is it much easier to break open groundnut shells after they have dried in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa kwraa akɛ aaagbala ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ amli beni agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Sun drying removes moisture, making the outer shell brittle so it snaps easily, while also shrinking the seed inside slightly so it detaches from the shell walls.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni efo oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo koni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ ahe gbogboi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do groundnuts turn into a smooth paste when ground, while maize turns into dry powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ atsɔ amɛmli lɛ? Beni ŋmãa lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni egbi lɛ

english: Groundnut seeds naturally contain high amounts of natural oil. When crushed or ground, this oil releases and mixes with the solid nut particles to form a rich paste.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmei dumɔwui amli. Kɛji akɛ aaakpã loo aakpã lɛ, ajieɔ mu nɛɛ ni ekɛ nut mli nibii ni wa lɛ futuɔ ni efeɔ nɔ ko ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my stored groundnuts develop a bitter taste over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: A bitter taste in stored groundnuts is caused by mold fungus that grows when nuts are harvested damp, stored with high moisture, or exposed to humid air.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei ni ato lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmei lɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. loo ni akɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli

english: Why is it important to blow away the papery light skin and trash after cracking my groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie woji kɛ jwɛi ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛjɛ mli beni atswa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Removing the light skins and farm trash leaves clean nuts that store longer without attracting insects, yield higher quality paste, and grind much more smoothly.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni he tse ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ŋmeii gbalaaa amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji krim ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to stay healthy. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea near the plant roots early in the season helps keep the leaves green and growing strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni toi lɛ hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crops after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years waiting for light and water. When you clear and turn the soil to plant crops, you bring those buried weed seeds to the surface where warm sunlight and rain trigger them to sprout instantly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, ni emɛɔ la kɛ nu Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni otsake koni okɛdu tsei Ebaabi ni okɛ nakai jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct heat. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leafy shield that keeps the seedlings cool until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni baanyɛ ashã oya ni amɛgbi yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe tsei ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over whenever the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni aduawai akui lɛ baaje shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, so supporting the main stem with a strong, bamboo or wooden fork prop prevents wind from knocking the tree over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Aduawai lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ ji asymmetrical. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni mli wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haaa tso lɛ agbee shi lɛ naa.

english: What causes small holes in my young corn leaves with powdery droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni powder ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a hungry caterpillar that hides inside the center whorl of the corn plant. Applying recommended biopesticides or dropping a small amount of clean sand mixed with wood ash directly into the leaf center early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmei mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii loo ŋã ni mli tse fioo ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ shwie baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot away during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, cool, high-humidity weather. Pruning excess branches and clearing heavy weeds lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to dry out moisture on the pods, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil solution early helps keep these insects off your plants so new leaves can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Neem fɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akaje tso lɛ he koni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil without proper drainage. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off easily, keeping the soil damp without drowning the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ oya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight for making starch, which feeds the growing tuber below. Staking prevents the leaves from resting on hot, wet soil where they can easily rot or get diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ. ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ni baanyɛ afite loo hela aba lɛ oya

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer stress from intense heat or irregular watering. Giving your tomato plants consistent water at the root level and mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool and helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tomato tsei anɔ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen nutrients or are getting too much water around their roots. Applying a balanced fertilizer like NPK or Urea and ensuring excess rainwater drains away helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea atsu nii ni okwɛ koni ajie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves on top look tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, cassava plants put all their energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Loosening the soil before planting and using fertilizers balanced for root growth encourages larger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bulbs lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Providing consistent moisture and light shade during severe heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Ni akɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves shred into ribbons when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbálaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally tear along their side veins during heavy winds as a natural protection mechanism. This reduces wind resistance so the entire plant does not snap or get uprooted.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbálaa yɛ amɛsɛɛ fãji lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, jeee tsei fɛɛ ji tsei ni akumɔ loo ashwie amɛshishifãi.

english: Black spots are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, shaded environments. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe koni hulu la babaoo abote mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is typically caused by a plant virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Spraying with organic neem oil solutions early on and removing badly infected plants helps stop the disease from spreading through your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Akɛ organic neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is my watermelon crop producing plenty of yellow flowers but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants produce separate male and female flowers and rely on insects like bees to carry pollen between them. If insect activity is low or only male flowers have opened so far, fruit will not form immediately.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi fɔfɔi hii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ loo fɔfɔi hii pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are completely ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yams indicate maturity above ground; when the leaves and vines naturally dry up and turn brown at the end of the season, it signals that the tubers underground have stopped growing and reached full size.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee. No ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables soften and spoil so quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops during the hot afternoon sun causes them to lose water rapidly and decay fast. Harvesting early in the cool morning and storing produce in well-ventilated, shaded crates keeps them fresh much longer.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu faaa oya ni efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ leebi maŋkpa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees protect them from burning in the heat and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to survive on their own.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji lɛ haa hulutsoo, amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crop plants need from the soil to grow big leaves and produce good ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai wuji ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi kpakpai.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that hide in the moist center funnel of the plant to eat the young growing leaves before the corn can form ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ toi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but end up with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or get too much leaf-building fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves to reach the sun instead of storing food in underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ ŋmei babaoo wo mli koni ekɛha baai lɛ aya hiɛ. Ebaafite ebe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa ebaai kakadaji lɛ yɛ hulu la mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass stop the ground from drying out so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt, blocking the hot sun from evaporating the water in the ground and keeping the plant roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so roots can drink it in. When put on dry soil, the concentrated chemical sits directly against the roots and burns them.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ oowo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãa amɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain usually wets only the top dirt while the deeper ground stays hot and dry. Planting too early causes seeds to get cooked in the dry soil before steady rainfall actually begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ baakã he adɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ daa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy. Lifting them off the ground on sticks prevents leaves from rotting on wet dirt and helps build bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebɔɔ yitso ni da

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that trap plant food from the air and leave it in the dirt, naturally enriching the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers that drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime weather gets too hot, when plants suffer from irregular watering, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei kɛ nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ he naagbai kpeɔ loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii

english: How do I plant sweet potatoes if I don't have seeds?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adu sweet potato kɛji dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: Sweet potatoes are not grown from traditional seeds. Instead, you plant fresh vine cuttings. You cut healthy stem pieces from an existing plant and bury part of them in the soil so they can sprout roots and produce new tubers.
ga: Jeee kusum naa akɛ aduɔ sweet potato kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli. Mohu ɔ, o duɔ wai tso ehehi nɛ a ngma. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ mli tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ofu efã ko awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii heei.

english: Which part of the vine is best for me to cut and plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ wain tso lɛ fã hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The vine tips or top cuttings (about 20 to 30 centimeters long) are the best to use. They grow much faster and carry fewer pests and diseases compared to the older stem parts near the base.
ga: Wein tso lɛ yitsei loo nɔ ni afolɔ yɛ ŋwɛi (ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30) ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai fioo kwraa fe tsei ni egbɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ.

english: How deep should I bury the vine cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu miwein tso lɛ niji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should plant about half to two-thirds of the vine cutting underground, ensuring at least 3 to 4 nodes (leaf joints) are covered with soil so strong root systems can develop.
ga: Esa akɛ odu wain tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ aaafee fã kɛyashi mlijaa enyɔ mli ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛtsɔ nɔmimaa ni aaakwɛ koni kɛ hoo lɛ, sũ aha nodes 3 kɛyashi 4 (baai lɛ ahe fãi) lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ aná.

english: Are all sweet potato vines the same, or is there a specific type I should plant to get good profit?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei lɛ fɛɛ ji ekome? Aloo ani tso pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ adu koni aná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa?

english: There are different varieties. High-yielding varieties—especially orange-fleshed sweet potatoes—are popular in the market because consumers love their taste and high Vitamin A content, bringing you better profit.
ga: Ayɛ henɔi srɔtoi babaoo. Nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo Titri lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Ehe gbɛi waa yɛ jara nɔ ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo kɛ bɔ ni vitamin A babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: Can I really make good money selling vine-planted crops in local Ghanaian markets?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika kpakpa kɛtsɔ wain tso mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana jarayelihe ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, crops like sweet potato mature quickly within 3 to 4 months and have high market demand for direct food consumption and processing, allowing for fast returns on investment.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes daa oya yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli ni amɛyɛ jarayeli nibii babaoo kɛha niyenii ni ayeɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nitsumɔ. Ehaa shika ni akɛwo mli lɛ baa oya

english: Why do I need to make mounds or ridges before planting crop vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani madu wain tsei lɛ?

english: Making mounds or ridges loosens the soil so the roots can expand easily into large tubers. It also improves drainage so your vines do not rot during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ hu bɔni afee ni owein tsei lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Will my vine cuttings die if I cannot plant them immediately after cutting?
ga: Ani miwein tsei lɛ baagboi kɛji minyɛɛɛ madu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Vines dry out quickly under the sun. If you cannot plant them right away, store them in a cool, shady spot and keep them slightly moist so they remain fresh until you are ready to plant.
ga: Wein tso lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu shishi. Kɛji onyɛɛɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ha ehi he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ni ha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo koni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu.

english: How far apart should I space the vine cuttings on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ miwein tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ abɔ he kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Space your vine cuttings about 30 cm apart along the ridge or mound. This gives each plant enough space and light to form large tubers without competing for soil nutrients.
ga: Shi sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni miihe ashɛ 30 cm yɛ wain niji lɛ ateŋ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa loo gɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: How can I tell if the tubers are growing well under the ground when I only see green leaves on top?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ bulb lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Be ni obaanyɛ ona baai eŋɔli pɛ yɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Aside from healthy leafy growth, you will notice the soil around the base of the plant beginning to crack and swell as the tubers expand beneath the ground.
ga: Kɛfata baai lɛ adalɛ kpakpa he lɛ Obaayɔse shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efuɔ beni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What happens if I put too much nitrogen fertilizer on my vine crop?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miwein tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Too much nitrogen makes the crop grow long, bushy green vines, but it prevents the plant from forming large tubers underground, which reduces your final harvest.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo baaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ wain tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Shi ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: I want to plant oil palm on a sloping piece of land. Is that a good idea, and how will the trees perform?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu mu tso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Ani eji susumɔ kpakpa? Ni te tsei baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palm can grow well on gentle or long slopes because slopes prevent excess water from pooling around the roots. However, on steep slopes, heavy rains can wash away topsoil and fertilizer, so planting trees along the curve of the hill helps hold nutrients in the soil.
ga: Mu tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ etseee loo nɔ ni jɛkɛɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋshɔkei lɛ tsiɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shi, yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: People say the Western Region is great for oil palm. Why does oil palm grow better in some regions of Ghana than others?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei fɔ. Mɛni hewɔ oil palm lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai komɛi anɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need steady rainfall and warm sunshine all year round to produce heavy fruit bunches. Regions like the Western Region have abundant, regular rain and ideal weather conditions, which help the trees produce much more palm fruit than in drier areas.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ he miihia oil palm tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kpokpai tamɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmei yibii babaoo fe hei ni nu bɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is deep enough for planting oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu mu tso?

english: Oil palm trees need deep soil—at least one meter deep—without hard underground rocks. Deep soil allows the roots to spread wide and far down, anchoring the heavy tree firmly against strong winds and reaching moisture underground during dry spells.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. (Kɛ hoo lɛ, eshishi mita kome) ni tɛ ni wa bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ tso ni tsii lɛ ni eeemɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ ni anáa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: How far apart should I space my oil palm seedlings when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo oil palm dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Oil palm trees should be planted about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern. This wide spacing ensures that mature fronds do not block sunshine from neighboring trees, allowing every tree to get maximum sunlight to produce fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni da nɛɛ haa baai ni edara lɛ tsiii hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ koni ewo yibii.

english: Does oil palm require full sunshine to yield well, or can I grow it under the shade of bigger trees?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia mu tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai aloo abaanyɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: Oil palm trees need full, direct sunlight throughout the day to make food and form fruit bunches. Planting them under heavy shade slows down their growth and drastically reduces the amount of fruit they will produce.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛhoo ni amɛfee aduawai akui. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha yibii ni amɛbaawo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Can I plant food crops like maize or groundnuts between my young oil palm trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani abaanyɛ afee yɛ mu tsei bibii ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop with food crops during the first two to three years while the palm trees are still small. This provides quick food and income, provided you keep the food crops a few feet away from the palm tree bases so they do not compete for water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii tsei adu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika oya. He ni okɛ niyenii tso lɛ toɔ he ni kɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: How many years does an oil palm seedling take before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani oil palm dumɔwu ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Most modern hybrid oil palm seedlings start producing their first harvestable fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after being planted in the main field, provided they receive proper fertilizer and care.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid oil palm dumɔwui babaoo baabɔi amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ feemɔ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm turning yellow, and what should I do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsitsi lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the tree is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil. Applying the right palm fertilizer or compost will help the leaves regain their healthy dark green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli ni mli wa.

english: How does waterlogging or standing water affect palm trees on low-lying ground?
ga: Te nu ni damɔ shi loo ni damɔ shi lɛ saa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While palm trees love moisture, sitting in stagnant water for weeks suffocates the root system. This rots the roots, prevents the tree from absorbing nutrients, and eventually causes stunted growth or death.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo moŋ, shi kɛ́ ota nu ni ekã shi otsii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do some of my young palm trees drop their flowers before turning into full fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai ni yeɔ emuu lɛ?

english: Flower dropping is often caused by water stress during intense dry seasons or poor pollination. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and maintaining good farm health helps the flowers develop successfully into heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okwɛ ŋmɔ mli hewalɛ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛye omanye ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa toi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves curl up tightly like tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot periods to reduce water loss from their leaves. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save moisture when the soil is dry or the sun is very strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi loo hulu la lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce small pods that turn black and shrivel on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is typically caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excessive shade. Pruning shade trees, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and the trunk snaps before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miikumɔ dani aduawai lɛ miida lɛ?

english: This issue is often caused by tiny soil pests called nematodes or banana root weevils damaging the root system. Using clean, disease-free suckers and applying wood ash or compost around the base strengthens the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Kɛtsɔ tsei ahe tsei ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli kɛ tso sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but small roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ waa, ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo, shi amɛshishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava has too much nitrogen in the soil, it puts its energy into leaf growth rather than building roots. Planting cassava in balanced soil without excess chemical nitrogen fertilizer encourages bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei yɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baa moŋ fe ni eeefee shishifãi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja nɔ ni tsofa ni ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fataaa he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my yam leaves develop brown spots and dry up before the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Early leaf drying in yam is usually caused by anthracnose, a leaf spot fungal disease. Planting resistant yam varieties and mulching the soil helps keep the foliage healthy until harvest time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ mra yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ Sweet potato henɔi ni nyɛɔ egbɔjɔɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is inconsistent watering. Providing regular watering and light shade during extreme midday heat keeps the blossoms healthy so fruit can form.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new flowers after the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants exhaust their nutrients after the first fruit yield. Adding organic compost or a balanced fertilizer immediately after harvesting gives the plant energy to flower and bear fruit again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ beni amɛwo yibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow heavy green vines but produce very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni tsii shi ewoɔ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fix their own nitrogen in the ground, so if the soil is already very rich, the plant focuses on leafy vine growth instead of pods. They yield better seed pods when planted in average soils.
ga: Tsina ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay open and leafy instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ miigbele ni amɛmiifee baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly when they lack constant soil moisture or are planted too close together. Spacing plants properly and giving them regular water allows the center leaves to roll tightly together.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ atsɔ yitso nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ afee ekome jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I want to buy from a store are genuine and high quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni mahe yɛ shwapo ko mli lɛ ji anɔkwale ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for an official seed certification tag displayed in the store or attached to the bag. Certified seeds are tested and approved by government inspectors to guarantee that they sprout well and yield a healthy harvest.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ahe odaseyeli okadii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ shwapoi amli loo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ kotokui ahe. Nɔyeli mli kwɛlɔi lɛ kaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhaa amɛhe odase koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is a seed certification paper, and why should I care if an agro-dealer has one in their shop?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ahe odaseyeli wolo? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he kɛji okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko yɛ woji yɛ amɛshwapo lɛ mli?

english: A seed certification paper is official proof from crop authorities showing that the dealer is selling real, disease-free seeds. Without it, you might be buying ordinary grain that will not grow well.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe odaseyeli wolo ji odaseyeli ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ko ŋɔɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ jarayelɔ ko miihɔ dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni hela bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, ekolɛ obaahe ŋmaa ni bɛ mlɛo ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do if an agro-dealer tries to sell me crop seeds that don't have any official label or brand on them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛi loo nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ mi?

english: You should insist on seeing properly labeled, sealed packages or ask for proof of certification. Unbranded seeds carry no guarantee that they will germinate or yield a good crop.
ga: Esa akɛ oma nɔ mi akɛ ona nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. aloo bi odaseyeli ni tsɔɔ akɛ Dumɔwui ni akadiko amɛ lɛ bɛ nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it safe for me to buy crop seeds that an agro-dealer measures out of an open bag into a small polythene bag?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ susuɔ he dani ewoɔ plastic kotokui bibii amli lɛ?

english: It is risky because loose seeds lose their strength quickly when exposed to air and moisture. They can also get mixed with old, poor-quality, or damaged seeds.
ga: Oshara yɛ he ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi oya kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Abaanyɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbɔ, ni ehiii loo ni efite afutu mli.

english: Why are factory-sealed seed packets better for my farm than unsealed seed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ fe dumɔwui kotokui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Factory packaging keeps out air, heat, moisture, and pests. This protects the tiny living plant inside the seed so it stays strong and healthy until you plant it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, kɛ kooloi akabote mli. Enɛ buɔ tsei bibii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ahe koni amɛhe awa ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛyashi obaadu amɛ.

english: If I only need a small quantity like 1 kilogram of seeds, how should it be packaged when I buy it?
ga: Kɛji miitao mahe dumɔwui fioo komɛi, tamɔ dumɔwui kilogram 1 lɛ, te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ awo mli?

english: Even small quantities should come in sealed, properly labeled small factory packets rather than hand-tied plastic bags to make sure you are getting genuine, strong seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ nibii bibii po aba yɛ nitsumɔhe wolokpoi bibii ni atsĩ naa ni aŋmala nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ plastic kotokuhi kɛ tsu ní nɛ o kɛ o nine fĩ mɛ konɛ o ná nɔ mi mami kaa o ná dumɔwui kpakpahi nɛ a ngɛ he wami.

english: Can sitting on an open shop shelf in the heat ruin seeds before I even buy and plant them?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mita adeka ni agbele nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite dumɔwui lɛ dani mahe ni madu?

english: Yes, heat and humidity dry out the seeds and slowly kill the living embryo inside, causing them to sprout weakly or fail to grow altogether when planted.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, latsaa kɛ latsaa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni egbeɔ fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiofio. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ fioo loo amɛkwɛɛɛ ekomekomei.

english: Why do some seeds fail to sprout in my field even after I give them good soil and enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ miha lɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were stored poorly, are too old, or were uncertified grain sold as seed. Quality seeds need to be properly preserved to keep the living embryo alive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto jogbaŋŋ, egbɔ tsɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni fɔmɔ kotokui ni baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do certified seeds behave differently in the soil compared to seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baafee amɛnii amɛha tɛŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Certified seeds sprout evenly at the same time, grow into strong seedlings that resist common diseases, and produce much higher yields than saved seeds that lose vigor over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni sa lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be kome mli. Edaa ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow at different speeds and sizes when I buy loose seeds from the open market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ dalɛi srɔtoi amli beni miheɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Market seeds are often a mixed collection of different grain types and ages, whereas certified seeds are uniform, ensuring all your plants sprout, grow, and mature at the exact same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni abua naa ni yɔɔ srɔtoi kɛ afii srɔtoi. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ, amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying when the sun is too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight; they need shade plants like plantains to shelter them until their roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛha amɛhe aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow before the corn matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, causing it to pull existing nutrients from its older leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ haa amɛgbalaa niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do farmers recommend planting cassava and maize together on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground over a year; planting them together gives you two harvests from one plot without them competing for space at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ afi kome mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa onine shɛɔ nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe awo he ko he akaŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce leaf surface area, helping it trap moisture and stop losing water in extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do armyworms keep attacking the very center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Armyworms target the central 'funnel' or growing point of the corn plant because it is soft, rich in tender leaves, and provides a hidden pocket for them to hide from predators.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ‘kone’ loo he ni ŋmãa tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni baai bibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ni buji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ jɛmɛ bɔni afee ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my pepper leaves after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores and bacteria from the soil onto the lower leaves, and the wet surface allows the disease to quickly attack the leaf tissue.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni he ni efɔ lɛ haa helai tutuaa baa lɛ mli fãji oya.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai ni kɛlɛ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer high in nitrogen forces the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the root tubers.
