ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce small bunches when I leave too many of them around one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ bibii bibii lɛ? Beni mishi babaoo yɛ tso kome he lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a single mother plant, they all fight for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in weak plants and tiny fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ Nyɛ tso kome pɛ Amɛbaatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii ni abua naa lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, leaving free fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress, as shedding flowers saves energy so the main plant can stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kpe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni egbee shi lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sun which burns their leaves and dries out root moisture quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates a cool canopy that protects the young trees until they are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ agbi oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa. Kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same spot wears out the specific nutrients that maize relies on and allows soil-borne pests to build up year after year. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome afi fɛɛ afi. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When soil gets waterlogged, crop roots cannot breathe, causing the leaves to turn pale yellow, wilt even though the ground is wet, and sometimes show stem rot at the ground level. Creating drainage channels helps move excess rainwater away from root zones.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Egboɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, tsei lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ he gbɛi ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass help them survive hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, prevents hot sunlight from baking the ground and keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly. It also keeps the roots cool and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaje kpo.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight for space, sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plant stems to grow tall and thin while producing small, thin tubers underground instead of large, heavy ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why are extension officers recommending that I pinch off extra side shoots on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ mi nɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mafo mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Removing side shoots, or suckers, prevents the tomato plant from spending energy on unnecessary branches and extra leaf growth. This allows the plant to focus its nutrients into growing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ, no haaa tomato tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa baa lɛ daa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf whorl. Catching them early is important because if they damage the center growing point of the stalk, the crop will fail to produce proper cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Ehe miihia ni amɔmɔ lɛ mra Ejaakɛ kɛji amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ afee cob ni sa.

english: How do weeds growing near my cowpea plants lower my crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, fertilizer, and groundwater away from your cowpea crops. They can also hide harmful insects that carry plant diseases, resulting in weaker cowpea plants and fewer pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ o-cowpea tsei lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ hu ato. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, cowpea tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnáaa ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent and using balanced fertilizers encourages flowers to stay attached and form healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants from extreme sun until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning purple and failing to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of phosphorus in the soil, which is essential for root development and plant growth. Applying phosphorus-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant recover and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground whenever we get heavy rain for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water logs the soil, cutting off the air supply to the roots and allowing fungal diseases to multiply. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. kɛ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Early morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the heat causes rapid evaporation. Watering during the hot afternoon can shock the plants and cause water drops on leaves to burn under direct sunlight.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa efoɔ oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ he akpokpo ni eha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ashã yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep dropping off without producing fruit. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering, which stops pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps the plants retain their flowers and form fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Enɛ haa pollin lɛ kpaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ muji wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Does staking my yam vines really help the tubers under the ground grow larger?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yes, lifting the yam leaves on stakes allows them to capture maximum sunlight to produce food for the plant. This extra food energy travels down into the ground to feed and expand the yam tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato baai ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha sweet potato tsei lɛ. Niyenii hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eyaye sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni ekwɛ amɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the growing funnel of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tso ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap helps control these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my yield keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to accumulate. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I leave all the suckers growing around my main plantain tree, or should I cut some off?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ loo esa akɛ mafo ekomɛi?

english: You should trim away extra suckers and leave only two or three of different sizes per mat. Having too many suckers causes competition for soil nutrients, leading to smaller, lighter plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii srɔtoi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ yɛ mat kome nɔ. Tsoi ni fa babaoo lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why should I spray my cocoa trees for black pod disease before the rainy season starts instead of waiting until I see infected pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔkɛ tsofa afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ koni wɔjie black pod hela lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi obaana ŋmeii diji ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions. Applying protective fungicide early creates a shield that prevents the fungus from entering the pod; once a pod is infected and rotten, chemical remedies cannot undo the damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Fungicides ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekabote pod lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela emɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni efite lɛ Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu nyɛŋ ajie nɔ ni efite lɛ.

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworms are attacking my maize field before they destroy all my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji Fall Armyworms miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ dani amɛfite mi-ŋmãa fɛɛ?

english: Look closely for tiny ragged holes and saw-dust like droppings in the funnel leaf (the center whorl) of young maize plants. Detecting them at this early stage allows you to treat the crop before the caterpillars reach the growing point and destroy the whole harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ona buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai (middle rings) lɛ amli. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra lɛ, obaanyɛ ohere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I clear all the big trees off my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense heat from full sunlight. Leaving or planting shade crops like plantains provides a canopy that protects young cocoa seedlings from sunburn and keeps moisture in the soil until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa kwraa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ hu kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ fataa he. ni ehiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli waa

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up with yellow patches, and why shouldn't I use cuttings from those plants for my next planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli fãi ni afo lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus living inside the stem tissue. There is no cure once a plant is infected, and using its cuttings guarantees that your new crop will start off sick from day one.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hela ko ni hiɔ fã ni jɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsamɔ ko bɛ kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ tso ko pɛ. Ni kɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onibii heei lɛ baaje hela shishi kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow when they are only a few weeks old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛye otsii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. Applying fertilizer early gives the crop the fuel it needs to build a strong stalk before weeds take over the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná tsofa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛma tso lɛ shishi ni wa dani jwɛi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my pepper plants before the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or dry leaves around your plants is called mulching. It acts as a protective cover that blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil, helping the roots stay cool and moist longer during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I pull out and destroy a tomato plant showing signs of bacterial wilt instead of trying to heal it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato tsei ni jieɔ bacteria wilt he okadii akpo lɛ ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsa lɛ

english: Bacterial wilt travels through soil and water to infect healthy neighboring plants, and there is no chemical cure for an infected plant. Removing and burning the sick plant early stops the disease from spreading throughout your entire farm.
ga: Bacteria wilt lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli koni ekɛ hela aba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni tsofai komɛi bɛ ni akɛtsaa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ amɛshãa mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop produce smaller cobs every year if I keep planting it on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to rebuild. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores vital nitrogen naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly in storage even when they looked healthy when I dug them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ mifo mli lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Small scratches or bruises caused by hoes during digging create open wounds where air, bacteria, and rot fungi can enter after harvest. Careful digging and curing yams in a shaded, well-ventilated spot thickens their skin to keep rots out.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ bibii loo ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmei lɛ kɛbaa yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ pilamɔi ni agbele naa he ni kɔɔyɔɔ, helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo baanyɛ abote mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa sweet potatoes yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekafite.

english: Why is it better to clear weeds when my crops are very small rather than waiting until the weeds grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ agbɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil food from young crops during their crucial early stage. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all available resources so they aren't stunted for the rest of the season.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishijee bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfeee mɛi ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for the plant. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the season helps keep the leaves green and produces bigger corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni dara lɛ aba.

english: I planted tomatoes, but the flowers keep falling off without forming any fruit. What is wrong with them?
ga: Miduɔ tomato Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Giving them steady water at the roots and protecting them from extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ daa ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly whenever weeds grow close around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the food and space they need to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets in sunlight and air, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ tsɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my young corn and hiding inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ ni akɛtee tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your farm regularly and applying recommended control methods early prevents them from destroying the center growing point of the corn.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Etsiɔ ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Too much trapped water starves the cassava tubers of air, encouraging rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni emɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry leaves or grass on the soil around their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi yɛ sũ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry plant material on the ground is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool, traps water in the ground so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for food, water, and light, resulting in weak plants with small crop yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to yield its maximum potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu kɛ la he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eshɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ ewo lɛ he.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to the ground on the exact same day I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbi nɔŋŋ ni midu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the seeds sprout and form young roots that can actually feed on the fertilizer. Applying it too early can burn the seed or cause heavy rain to wash the plant food away before it is used.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi bibii ni baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ loo eha nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ekɛ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ afɔ shi dani akɛtsu nii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they enrich the soil with natural nutrients that feed the maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Planting immediately after the first light rain can be risky because the ground might dry up again. Wait until the soil is moist at least finger-deep (about 5 cm) after a heavy rain so the seeds have enough water to germinate and survive.
ga: Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ fioo sɛɛ Oshara baanyɛ aba ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ekoŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ inchi kome (aafee sɛntimitai enumɔ) yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burnt at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellow and burnt leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are getting too much direct sunlight or lack water. Young cocoa needs shade trees or plantains planted around it to protect it from the harsh sun while its roots establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshãa yɛ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ loo nu efo amɛmli. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛma shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my mature cocoa trees when they are growing so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji komɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach the inner trunk. This prevents black pod disease, keeps the tree healthy, and encourages the plant to direct its energy into producing more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, hela emɔmɔ amɛ, loo ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Koni akɛtsi black pod hela naa Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewaa. ni ewo tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee pods.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green, or produce very small fruits compared to previous years, your soil is losing nutrients and needs compost, manure, or fertilizer to become healthy again.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ekɛ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe Oshikpɔŋ lɛ miifite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge stems and leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing tall green leaves instead of feeding the roots. Avoid applying high-nitrogen fertilizers late in the season so the plant focuses on swelling the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni kɛlɛ ni eŋɔli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ahi ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are there small holes on my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats the heart of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early in the morning and applying recommended organic or chemical treatments into the central leaf funnel helps kill them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei atsui. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is too much fertilizer. Ensuring consistent watering and providing partial shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it bad if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases that love maize to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ekpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops even if I give my crops enough water and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves. They grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants, causing your crops to starve and yield much less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How can I keep my vegetable farm soil moist during the hot dry season without watering all day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni mikɛ nu wooo nɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or straw—a method called mulching—acts as a blanket that blocks the hot sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo jwɛi - gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why should I tie my young mango tree to a wooden stick in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mango tso lɛ fĩ tso kuku ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tying a young mango tree to a sturdy wooden stake keeps it growing straight upward and protects it from being blown over by strong winds while its trunk is still soft.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ mango tso lɛ fĩ tso ni wa ko he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa atswa lɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lolo lɛ.

english: What can I do if my young fruit seedling is bending over instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi tsei bibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ ebɔle shi moŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You can place a strong stake next to the seedling and gently tie the main stem to it so the plant straightens out and grows upright.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso ni wa ama dumɔwu lɛ masɛi ni odu lɛ blɛoo. Kpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he koni tso lɛ ahi shi ja ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I prevent strong winds from knocking over my newly planted fruit trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa aduawai tsei ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ?

english: Drive a wooden stake into the soil near the center of the plant and tie the trunk to it; this anchors the tree and creates a sturdy base during heavy storms.
ga: Tsɔ tso tso ko awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ akpɛtɛ he. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ahi shi ni efee shishitoo ni wa yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: How tight should I tie the material when securing my young tree stem to a support stake?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafi nibii lɛ ahe shi jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ tso bibioo lɛ miikpɛtɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: You should tie it firmly enough to guide the tree upward, but keep it gentle so you do not choke or cut into the growing stem as it thickens.
ga: Esa akɛ okpɛtɛ he jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ewo tso lɛ nɔ. Shi kwɛmɔ ni okɛfi lɛ blɛoo koni ekafo loo ekafo tso ni miida lɛ mli beni egbɔjɔɔ lɛ.

english: Will supporting my young fruit tree with a stake help it grow better in the long run?
ga: Ani mikɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ midumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, supporting a young tree helps build a thick, sturdy base at the bottom, which allows the top of the tree to grow strong branches capable of holding heavy fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii ni ayeɔ abuaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishitoo ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ niji ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ahiɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: At what stage of growth should I put support stakes next to my young fruit trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mikɛ sɛɛfimɔ tso ama mi tso bibioo ni woɔ yibii lɛ masɛi?

english: You should add a support stake early while the stem is still young and flexible, so you can train the tree to grow tall and straight right from the start.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ sɛɛfimɔ tsei afata he mra. be mli ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo Enɛ ji koni onyɛ otsɔse tso lɛ koni ekwɛ ni ehi shi ja kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: Why are the top branches of my young fruit tree drooping toward the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ niji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young stems are often too soft to hold their own weight. Tying the stem to an upright stake lifts the top of the tree so it grows upward toward the sun instead of creeping along the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fĩ tso ko ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does keeping a young tree upright help its trunk become stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ oha otso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli waa?

english: When a stake holds the plant steady, the tree can safely focus its energy on thickening its lower trunk, creating a sturdy foundation for future growth.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ hiɛ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama shishigbɛ tso lɛ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe. Bɔɔ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dalɛ.

english: What is the correct way to place a support stake next to my fruit tree without hurting it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni aaatsɔ nɔ akɛ tso awo mi tso yibii lɛ masɛi ni efiteee tso lɛ?

english: Insert the stake into the soil near the middle of the plant base, taking care not to push through major roots, and then tie the main stem to the stake.
ga: Okɛ tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okabote shishifãi wuji lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, fimɔ tso titri lɛ kɛya tso lɛ he.

english: How can I help a weak, skinny sapling grow into a tall and leafy tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua tso bibioo ko ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ni etsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ baai?

english: Supporting a skinny sapling with a stake and tying it upright gives it the stability it needs to grow upward, strengthen its base, and produce healthier leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso fi tso bibioo lɛ sɛɛ ni okɛfi lɛ shiŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eshwere. Wo shishitoo lɛ hewalɛ ni oha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ŋwɛigbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is infected by a leaf disease. Adding manure or appropriate fertilizer provides the nutrients needed to keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ foliar hela ko emɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: If one of my tomato plants gets black spots on its leaves, why does the disease spread so quickly to the rest of my farm?
ga: Kɛji mi tomato tsei lɛ eko yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ Mɛni hewɔ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa hei krokomɛi? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya

english: Black spots are usually caused by tiny fungal spores or bacteria that easily travel through the wind, splashing rain, or on your hands and tools as you work between plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal spores bibii loo helatsɛmɛi amli helai ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa. No baanyɛ afã yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo oniji kɛ odɛŋdadei anɔ beni otsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ. mlɛo

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly collapse and die right after sprouting out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a soil disease called damping-off, which thrives in overly wet soil with poor drainage and attacks the soft stems of young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ fe nine ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni etutuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach light, which makes their stems thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or small insect pests like thrips that damage the delicate blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even when I give my fields plenty of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them, leaving your main crops underfed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss, helping the plant conserve moisture in its stem and roots to survive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and decay during the period of heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and dense shade create high humidity where black pod fungal disease thrives. Pruning shade trees allows sunlight and wind to dry the cocoa trees and reduce rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Biɛ ji he ni black pod fungus hela lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa kookoo tsei lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers become smaller every time I plant them on the same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ, afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Why are the roots of my plants turning soft and dark brown instead of staying light and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi mlɛo ni amɛfee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soft, dark roots are a sign of root rot, which happens when water collects in the soil without draining away, suffocating the roots and attracting destructive soil fungi.
ga: Shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo lɛ he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any tall plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a natural canopy that shields young cocoa trees from heat and retains soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and food from the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother plant to produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally moves whatever nitrogen it has from older leaves to nourish the fresh, top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me small, thin tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen or water, cassava puts all its energy into growing green stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ, Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei bibii kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do farmers place dry grass on top of the soil around the base of pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under hot weather, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from growing near your pepper roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the center of my young maize plant leaves and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which target the soft inner leaves inside the maize funnel. Hiding inside protects them from daylight heat and birds while giving them constant food.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ amɛte shi amɛwo mli lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa kɛ okpoi ahe. kɛfata niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small wrinkles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. The damage distorts how new leaves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ ni efite lɛ fiteɔ baai heei adalɛ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when heat is too extreme or when the plant does not get enough water. Severe heat stops pollen from fertilizing the flowers, causing the plant to shed them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. ni haa tsei shwieɔ nu

english: Yam vines need to climb high to get maximum sunlight for leaf growth. Lifting vines off the wet ground also protects leaves from soil fungal diseases and leads to bigger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture for me to start planting maize after the first rainy day of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Single short rains only wet the top surface while subsoil stays dry. Soil is ready for planting when you can dig a few inches down, squeeze a handful of moist earth, and it holds together in a soft ball.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kuku kome pɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ kã he egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ be mli ni obaanyɛ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi atsu nii. Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo ko mli. Kɛkɛ ni ebua ehe naa ni etsɔ bɔɔlu.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving select trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides the moisture and shade young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ahala loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be yaa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the season helps keep the leaves green and leads to larger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii agboi aba.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when sticking them in the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, direction matters significantly. You must plant the stem with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky so roots grow down easily and shoots emerge quickly. Planting them upside down weakens or kills the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia waa diɛŋtsɛ. Osumɔɔ ni odu tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni shishifãi lɛ ada oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ebaagbe lɛ.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my crops instead of planting as many seeds as possible together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛjegbɛi wuji yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du duwuhi fuu kɛ pee kake bɔ nɛ o ma nyɛ.

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, which results in thin plants and smaller yields. Giving each crop enough space lets roots spread and leaves absorb enough light to produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni baai lɛ ŋɔɔ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my corn immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell that can dry up seeds before they establish deep roots. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate and grow continuously.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my corn leaves and caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young corn leaves and growing tips. Checking your farm early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni dalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem tso mli nu loo bio-insecticide ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients cause tomato plants to drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch and watering regularly helps flowers set healthy tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee shiŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas improve my farm soil for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant leaves and roots break down in the soil, they release this natural fertilizer, making the ground richer for crops planted next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fã kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo ni tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves into direct sunlight. Leaves use sunlight to produce the food that fills the underground yam tubers; without stakes, leaves stay shaded on the ground and produce much smaller yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: This rot is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and wind into the farm helps dry out dampness and slows down the disease.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ duŋ kɛ nu shihilɛ mli kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I clear away all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under forest trees and need partial shade to protect them from high heat. Without shade trees, intense sunlight causes heat stress, dries out the soil quickly, and reduces the plant's ability to hold onto flowers and form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ashishi yɛ kooi amli ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings grow tall and skinny instead of strong and thick in my nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and grow thin stems when they are planted too close together or under dense shade because they are competing with each other to reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaaná ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi. Ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛshi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers can grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience water stress or lack key nutrients in the soil. The plant drops flowers as a survival mechanism to save energy when it senses poor soil conditions or irregular rainfall.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ loo niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji amɛnu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the lower parts of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen, an essential food for leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baa lɛ mli koni eya nɔ edara.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and covered in hairy roots even when I add plenty of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ yitsɔi ehà nɔ lɛ? He ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ mli

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes yams to put all their energy into growing bushy green vines on top while neglecting the root underground. Yams require balanced nutrition, especially potassium, to expand into clean, heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ biɔ ni sweet potatoes kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni ja he miihia Sweet potatoes. titri lɛ potassium koni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ yitso ni he tse ni tsii

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants curl tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons to reduce their surface area and prevent water from evaporating off the leaf. It is a natural self-defense action to save water until the day cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni akɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebaajɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into thin ribbons when strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split along natural lines when hit by wind to allow the air to pass through easily. This prevents the heavy wind from snapping the main stem or uprooting the whole plant.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ linei yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafo tso lɛ tso lɛ shishi loo ejie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves develop tiny yellow patches and fall off long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? ni amɛgbee shi dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Loss of cassava leaves is often caused by tiny pests like mites feeding on the sap underneath the leaf. When leaves fall early, the plant loses its food factory and cannot grow large tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baa lɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi mra Tso lɛ laajeɔ eniyenii tso lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by soil-borne bacterial diseases or root rot from poor drainage. The disease damages the root tubes, preventing water from traveling up into the stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ shishifã paipi lɛ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when I delay weeding my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa beni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act as competitor plants that drink up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. When weeds crowd around cassava, the crop spends its energy fighting for resources rather than swelling its tubers.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni amɛnuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle ŋmei lɛ he Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛye nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe akaŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Nitrogen moves to the newest growth at the top first, leaving older lower leaves hungry, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen tsiɔ kɛyaa dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana plant cassava and maize together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly over a year. Planting them together maximizes space and food production without the cassava crowding out the maize early on.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ afi mli lɛ, nanemɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ŋmei lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa mra.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are attacking my young corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall cutworms miitutua mi-baby ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Look for ragged holes in the central leaves of young corn and small greenish-brown droppings that look like sawdust inside the plant whorl, which indicates caterpillars are actively feeding inside.
ga: Taomɔ bu ni etse yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai kɛ ŋmãa bibii amli. Su ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miitao niyenii yɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up or droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl or droop their leaves during intense heat to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, helping them conserve water and prevent drying out until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe loo amɛbaagbee shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaaa baa lɛ agbi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato stems are naturally weak and cannot support heavy fruit. Staking keeps fruits off the wet ground to prevent rotting, improves air circulation to fight disease, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii. Staking haa aduawai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛkafite. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛ helai awuu Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing many flowers but dropping them without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects or wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: What causes small cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ani etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning heavy tree canopy lets in sunlight to dry out the pods and prevent infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ eshishifãi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa mɔ nɔ.

english: Seeds buried too deeply exhaust their stored energy reserves before reaching sunlight, leading to weak shoots that die underground or fail to emerge properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the crops I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mito he gbɛjianɔ akɛ makwɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to absorb water and nutrients aggressively from tough soil, allowing them to outcompete cultivated crops if left unchecked.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ sũ mli lɛ waa. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei ni ama shi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if farmland that has been left overgrown for a long time is ready for replanting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ashi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ekoŋŋ?

english: Check for dark, crumbly topsoil rich in decomposed organic matter and clear excessive brush so light can reach the ground, ensuring young crops have enough nutrients and space to thrive.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli ewo duŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni efite eyi mli obɔ, ni eyɛ brɔshi ni mli tse tsɔ ni haaa la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce so much fruit around March at the end of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ March afi lɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees follow natural weather cycles. The intense sunlight during the dry season triggers peak fruit ripening, leading to a major harvest peak around March in southern Ghana.
ga: Mu tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi asɛɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ woɔ aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ babaoo he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni fe fɛɛ baa yɛ March mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my palm fruit before it spoils on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei yibii dani egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You know palm fruit is mature and ready to harvest when the fruit turns a bright reddish-orange and at least 2 to 5 loose fruits drop naturally to the ground beneath the tree.
ga: O le kaa tso yiblii ɔ wa nɛ e pee klaalo kaa e maa kpa ke e ba pee ngmlɛ tso nɛ ngɛ kpɛe. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, aduawai 2 kɛyashi 5 ni egbee shi lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my palm trees give a huge harvest in one season and very little fruit in other months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ewoɔ fioo yɛ nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees go through natural yield cycles. Peak seasons happen when rainfall and sunshine align perfectly, followed by lean rest periods where the tree conserves energy to produce the next crop.
ga: Mu tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko mli. Be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baa be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ kpãa gbee jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji hejɔɔmɔ be fioo ko ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni eya nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do crops seem to rest or stop growing during the major dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii jɔɔ amɛhe loo amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be ni mli wa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the major dry season, plants slow down their growth to conserve moisture and protect themselves from extreme heat until the rainy season returns.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Will the hot dry harmattan weather destroy my oil palm flowers before they turn into fruit?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baafite mi-oil palm fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai?

english: Severe heat can cause some young flowers to dry up, but healthy oil palm trees are tough and can store enough water to keep developing the remaining fruit bunches.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi bibii komɛi agbi. Shi mu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai akui ni eshwɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Does plenty of dry season sunshine affect the quality of oil inside my palm fruits?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ saa fɔ ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, abundant sunlight helps the palm tree produce more carbohydrates through photosynthesis, which increases the oil content and weight of the fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tsei ni amɛfeɔ carbohydrates babaoo kɛtsɔɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Enɛ haa mu ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I help my farm survive the long dry season so my trees don't dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli koni mitsei lɛ akagbi?

english: Covering the soil around the tree roots with dry leaves or cut grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture and protects the roots from harsh heat during the dry months.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni afo lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: What work should I be doing on my palm farm during the months when the trees are not fruiting?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ esa akɛ matsu yɛ mi-palm ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji ni tsei lɛ wooo yibii lɛ amli?

english: During low-fruiting periods, focus on clearing weeds around the base, pruning dead lower fronds, and applying fertilizer so the trees are well-nourished for the upcoming peak season.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Gbalamɔ ojwɛŋmɔ kɛya jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egboi lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpa yɛ shisharamɔ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How many years after planting will a new oil palm tree start yielding fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu mu tso hee lɛ, ebaaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved oil palm varieties start bearing their first small fruit bunches about 3 years after planting, and reach full commercial yield around 6 to 8 years.
ga: Mu tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo aduawai bibii akui. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee afii 3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ ni jarayeli nitsumɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8.

english: Why are some palm trees on my farm bearing fruit faster than other palm trees planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii mra fe ŋmei tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Trees grow at different speeds depending on how much direct sunlight they receive, local soil fertility variations, and how well their roots access underground water.
ga: Tsei daa oya yɛ srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ hulu la ni tso lɛ náa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsakeɔ kɛ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that too much standing water around the roots is suffocating the plant and preventing it from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ lolo ni ebɔle ehe Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa eye nii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the scorching sun to conserve moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does adding compost or animal manure to my field help my crops grow better than relying only on rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Manure and compost act like a sponge in the soil, helping the ground hold water much longer while continuously releasing natural food that strengthens crop roots.
ga: Manɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi jeɔ kpo be fɛɛ be, ni no haa tsei shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my small green cocoa pods turn black and dry out directly on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives during wet, humid weather when shade is too thick and air cannot circulate properly through the cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Shade lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have bright yellow patterns and start curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfoɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. It damages the leaves so they cannot trap sunlight to make big roots underground.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ baai lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛfee shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without ever forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant is stressed by hot dry winds, irregular watering, or a lack of insects like bees to move pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ yashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall wooden stakes beside my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Lifting their vines off the ground allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a rainstorm hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, but tiny worms or weevils in the soil often chew through them, weakening the plant's anchor and making the heavy tree top-heavy.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Shi ŋmei bibioo ko loo ŋmei Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛtsɔ amɛmli amɛye. ehaa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests and crop diseases a permanent place to live and multiply.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops while they are still tiny?
