ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients meant for your plants, causing your crops to become weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my tomatoes splitting open on the plants before I can even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they take up a lot of water very quickly, especially after a dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ kɛji amɛmu nu oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my vegetables crack when a heavy rain falls after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tswaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When plants go without water for a long time, their fruit skins harden. A sudden heavy rain causes the roots to soak up water fast, swelling the inside of the fruit until the hard skin cracks open.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Yibii lɛ ahiɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu oya. Ehaa aduawai lɛ amli shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmei ni wa lɛ fãa.

english: What happens to my fruits if I do not water my crops on a regular schedule?
ga: Mɛni baaba miyibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu haaa mitsei lɛ yɛ be naa?

english: Irregular watering causes uneven fruit growth. Fluctuating between dry soil and soaked soil weakens the skin of the fruit, making it far more likely to split, rot, or develop soft spots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ teŋ tsakemɔ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaagbala, egbo loo ebaaná hei ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops suffer from heavy fruit damage in some years but grow perfectly fine in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite waa yɛ afii komɛi amli shi amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Crops react strongly to unpredictable weather changes like unexpected rainfall, sudden dry spells, or extreme heat. These seasonal climate shifts alter how fast fruits absorb water and mature, leading to higher damage in bad weather years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ he. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo latsaa ni naa wa Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be mli lɛ baatsake bɔ ni aduawai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Ekɛ fitemɔ ni fa babaoo baa yɛ afii ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ehiii yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Is it harmful to harvest my tomatoes quickly when they are still slightly green?
ga: Tomato ni akpaa oya yɛ Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo lolo?

english: Harvesting when tomatoes are just beginning to turn pink (the breaker stage) is actually good for transport. They are firm enough to resist bruising and crushing on the road, and they will naturally ripen safely later.
ga: Kpamɔ be mli ni tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki pɛ kɛkɛ. (Breaking distance) lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha gbɛfaa. Amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛ nɔ lɛ. Ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaafee shweshweeshwe yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I leave freshly picked vegetables sitting in the hot sun on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mashɛɔ aduawai ni ajie ehee lɛ ashwieɔ lɛ? yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Direct sunlight warms up harvested produce, causing it to lose water quickly, wilt, and soften. Keeping harvested crops under cool shade preserves their firmness and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nibii ni akpa lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya, egbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo. Kɛ́ okɛ okpamɔ lɛ to hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi shiŋŋ ni efee ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I stop my harvested tomatoes from getting crushed on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Avoid stacking heavy loads directly on top of soft fruits. Using shallow, rigid wooden or plastic crates instead of deep sacks keeps weight off the bottom layers and prevents the fruits from getting smashed.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni tsii ni okɛaawo aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ plastic loo tso adekai ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni mli wa tsu nii yɛ kotokui ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishigbɛ adeka lɛ mli tsiimɔ aba shi, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ akakumɔ.

english: Why do some of my tomatoes turn soft and spoil so quickly right after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny scratches or micro-cracks created during rough picking allow bacteria and fungi to enter the fruit. Heat and gentle bruising speed up this process, causing the fruit to rot rapidly from the inside.
ga: ŋmɔlɔ bibii loo ŋmɔlɔ bibii ni ba yɛ be mli ni abuaa nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ naa lɛ Enɛ baaha helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii abote aduawai lɛ amli. Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo Ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ.

english: Does packing my harvested vegetables tightly in deep sacks hurt the produce?
ga: Ani aduawai ni akpa lɛ ni akɛaawo kotokui ni mli kwɔ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Yes, deep sacks trap heat and concentrate heavy pressure at the bottom. The weight of the upper crops squeezes and bursts the lower ones, spreading juice and rotting the whole sack quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kotokui ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli ni amɛhaa nɔnyɛɛ ni tsii baa shishigbɛ. Tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ miimɔ tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Egbɛɔ nu eshwaa ni ehaa kotoku lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: How does carrying my crops over rough roads in vehicles destroy the produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tee gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ yɛ tsɔne mli lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Bumping on bad roads causes fruits inside crates or boots to repeatedly slam against each other. This creates internal bruising that softens the skin, making the produce burst open or spoil before reaching the buyer.
ga: Gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ tsɔne ni tswaa lɛ baaha aduawai ni yɔɔ adekai loo bɔɔtu mli lɛ atswa amɛhe shii abɔ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fãji ni haa hewolo lɛ feɔ blɛoo baa. Enɛ haa nibii ni adu lɛ fiteɔ loo egboɔ dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Their young leaves burn easily, so they need shade crops like plantains to shelter them and keep the surrounding air humid while they build strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plants experience extreme heat or dry soil. Keeping the moisture in the soil consistent helps the flowers stay attached long enough to develop into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do insects attack my pepper plants much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, natural bushes dry up, driving hungry insects toward irrigated farm crops for food and water. Regular watering and using natural sprays like neem extract can protect your peppers.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ mli egbi. Tsɔ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ nɔ nu lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nu ni okɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu o-peppers lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light yellow from the middle instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives leaves their green color and fuels growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing maize in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn-specific pests to build up in the field. Swapping maize with beans or cowpeas returns nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper spacing allows every plant to get enough food to yield a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they share the parent plant's food and water, leading to small bunches. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Plantains lɛ baajara niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to support my yam leaves with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji fiɔ sweet potato baai lɛ asɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the shade of the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in soaked soil without oxygen for long periods. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛwo nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain usually wet only the top layer of dirt, which dries out fast under intense sun. Waiting for steady rains ensures the deeper soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. ni gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure replenishes nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Forage corn he miihia koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas and beans have special nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, this leftover nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer away from your crop's roots into drains or streams before the plant has a chance to soak it up, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli kɛyaa nu tsɔji loo faai amli. Dani tsei lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛfɔ lɛ Ehaa shika kɛ nitsumɔ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that filters the sun and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulu la lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on tall poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant, which results in larger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Shishifãi ni afolɔ ashwie shi krokomɛi lɛ baaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ jwɛi lɛ da.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress, which prevents proper pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kpe. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by stress from extreme heat and inconsistent watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when there are weeds around them, even if I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ jwɛi ebɔle mihe lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ.

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni hulu la lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, hwɔ maa ye mɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes waterlogging in the soil, which cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots and creates ideal conditions for rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli ni eha shihilɛ ni sa aba kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles next to my yam vines after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso ŋmɔŋ fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso ko masɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally want to climb to reach sunlight. Staking them with poles lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch sunlight better, which prevents leaf rot and helps the plant produce much larger tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why should I tie my tomato plants to ropes or sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ kpã loo tsei aniji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato stems are weak and bend easily under the weight of heavy fruit. Tying them up with ropes keeps the fruits and leaves off the damp soil, which stops fungal diseases and pests from destroying your crop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfoɔ oya yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ kpã fĩ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai kɛ baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite onibii.

english: How does using a water motor or pump help my dry season crops stay healthy?
ga: Te nu tsɔne loo pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi tsei ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A water motor allows you to move water quickly from a river, well, or stream directly to your crops. This provides consistent watering during the dry season, preventing your crops from wilting or dying due to drought.
ga: Nu tsɔnei haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu yaa oya kɛjɛɔ faa loo ŋshɔ mli. loo ehoɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni afɔɔ nu daa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Tsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo loo amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is getting unequal amounts of water. Adding fertilizer or animal manure feeds the plant so the leaves stay green and build heavy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni falɛ eshɛɛɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or poor nutrients. Keeping the soil damp and feeding the crop helps the plant hold its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni aha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni etsɔɔ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I water my crops on the leaves in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ tsei anɔ nu yɛ tsei ahe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under strong, hot sunshine causes the water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots. Water droplets left on the leaves can also magnify the heat and scorch the delicate crop leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ aya hiɛ ni eshã tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do I plant cassava using stem cuttings instead of planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava grows best from the nodes on mature stems rather than seeds. When stem cuttings are planted in moist soil, roots sprout from the bottom nodes to form tubers, while leaves shoot out from the top nodes.
ga: Cassava daa jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ nodes ni yɔɔ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ moŋ fe dumɔwui. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ baajɛ ŋwɛi fãji lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains over young cocoa acts like an umbrella, keeping the crops cool and moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops produce very small cobs when I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed properly and make large maize ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa ŋmãa toi lɛ daraa

english: Why do weeds in my field make my main crops grow slowly and look yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mi tsei titrii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds regularly ensures all the soil food and water go directly into making your crops strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the crop is hungry for nitrogen—a key plant food—or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava producing huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Cassava uses its extra energy to make leaves when soil has too much nitrogen or when rain is heavy, leaving less energy to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ kroko tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by excessive sun heat or dry conditions, dropping the flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Shĩ fɔfɔii ashwie koni nu akafite ni ohi wala mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry out and curl up when the dry hot wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves curl up to reduce water loss under bright sun and harsh dry air, which is why young cocoa crops need shade trees to protect them.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi lɛ aba shi. Enɛ hewɔ ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ koni ebu amɛhe lɛ.

english: How do I know my yam tubers are fully mature underground when I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Ni minyɛɛɛ mana lɛ?

english: When the yam vines above ground naturally dry out and turn yellow, the crop is signaling that the tubers underground have finished growing.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow very slowly when I leave many of them around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mishiɔ amɛteŋ babaoo yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The main mother plant share water and soil food with all her suckers; having too many attached causes them to fight for food and grow slowly.
ga: Tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ jaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ niyenii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and taller than my planted crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe tsei ni midu lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Local weeds are naturally tougher and adapted to local soil, so they wake up faster with moisture and steal soil food before crops establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ jɛmɛ shikpɔji lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛteɔ shi mra koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛju niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Will planting cowpea together with my maize slow down my maize growth?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Cowpeas actually help maize because they capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as natural food for the maize plant.
ga: Cowpeas yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ

english: Why are some of my maize seeds failing to sprout after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds are like sleeping sleeping babies; they require moisture to wake up and push out roots, so without damp soil they stay asleep or die.
ga: Dumɔwu tamɔ abifao ni ewɔ. Amɛmiitao ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛje kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ bɛ lɛ, amɛbaawɔ loo amɛbaagboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and looking sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on sap and spreading plant sickness, or the plant trying to keep moisture inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo tso lɛ miitao ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli.

english: How can I know if my land has enough richness to support crops before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: You can check your land's richness by looking at its color and feel—dark, soft soil that holds moisture well usually has plenty of nutrients. You can also look at the weed growth; land with thick, healthy wild leaves is often rich and ready for crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii babaoo ehaa kɛtsɔ ehiɛ su kɛ bɔ ni onuɔ he ohaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Obaanyɛ okwɛ jwɛi lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and strong on one part of my land but stay small and weak on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fa kroko mli.

english: Soil richness is not always equal across the whole farm. Some areas may have lost their food nutrients due to water erosion or heavy farming, while other spots retained rich topsoil and moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ nii lɛ jeee nɔ kome be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Hei komɛi baanyɛ afite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi loo okwaayeli ni wa hewɔ. yɛ be mli ni otii krokomɛi Ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli.

english: Why do some foreign seeds I buy fail to grow well on my local land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mimaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds brought in from other countries were created for different weather and soil types. When planted here, they can struggle with our hot sun, local pests, and soil conditions unless given extra fertilizer and care.
ga: Abɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ biɛ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛwu amɛshi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ. jɛmɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi Ja amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ.

english: Is it safer for me to plant traditional local seeds or try new imported crop varieties?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi akɛ madu maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui loo maka dumɔwui heei ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ makwɛ?

english: Local seeds are naturally used to our Ghanaian weather and soil conditions, so they survive easily. Foreign varieties can yield more, but only if your soil is very rich and you can provide the specific food and water they demand.
ga: Akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ewaaa akɛ aaahi shi. Maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo pɛ kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse waa ni obaanyɛ oha amɛ niyenii kɛ nu pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: What happens to the soil richness when I uproot all the wild plants and bushes on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ beni mijie koo mli tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Uprooting all bush clears space for your crop, but it leaves the bare earth exposed to harsh sun and heavy rain. Without leaf cover, the sun dries out the soil quickly and rain can wash away the rich top layer of plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaagbele he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Shi ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ aná hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa. Kɛji baai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ Hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Ni nugbɔ baanyɛ ahoo tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do young crop shoots dry up quickly when I plant them on freshly cleared bare land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare ground absorbs a lot of heat from the sun, which bakes young plant roots. Providing temporary shade or leaving some ground cover keeps the soil cool and preserves water for the young crop journey.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbalaa dɔlɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ha loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi koni tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: How do I know which crop is right for the specific type of soil on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Every crop demands different soil conditions to thrive. Crops like cassava can survive in lighter, poorer soils, while crops like maize and cocoa demand deep, rich soil with plenty of organic matter.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi srɔtoi koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni waaa, ni ehiii kwraa nɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ kookoo Ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why is my crop taking a much longer journey to produce fruit than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: If the land lacks the richness the crop demands, the plant spends all its energy trying to survive instead of growing food. Adding organic manure helps speed up its growth journey.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ niyenii ni amɛaadu lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya.

english: Why should I put manure on the land before putting seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Adding manure feeds the soil before the seed germinates. When the seedling shoots out its first roots, it finds immediate food and moisture, allowing it to start its growth journey strong.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Ebaana niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ehaa ejeɔ shishi waa yɛ edalɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil dry up so fast even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its water quickly when it lacks organic richness. Adding decayed leaves or animal dung helps the soil act like a sponge, holding rain water much longer for your crops to drink.
ga: Nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Too nugbɔ nu kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛnu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: The rainfall pattern seems to have changed lately, so how do I know the exact right time to plant my maize?
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ etsake nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa?

english: Weather patterns in Ghana are changing, making fixed calendar planting dates unreliable. Instead of planting on specific traditional days, wait until you get two or three heavy, soaking rains that thoroughly wet the soil before sowing your seeds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ miitsake. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ kalanda nɔ dumɔ gbii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ kusum gbi lɛ nɔ Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantain shoots alongside my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is fertile enough for a large farm before I spend money clearing it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ agbo ko? Dani abaafite shika koni akɛjie nakai he lɛ

english: Look closely at the plants already growing naturally on the land; rich topsoil usually supports thick vegetation like elephant grass, wild cocoyams, and broad-leaf trees with dark, crumbly soil underneath.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ fiɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi, koo mli kookoo, kɛ tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves start curling up and turning pale when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that multiply quickly during dry and hot periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni baafa oya yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do dark black spots spread over my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives when humidity is high and rainwater stays trapped on wet pods without good airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Fungal helai ni baa kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ. kɛ nugbɔ nu ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat, uneven watering, or getting too much nitrogen fertilizer instead of fruit-bearing nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni anáa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaaná niyenii ni haa tso yibii lɛ yɔɔ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce very small fruits after the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants exhaust their nutrients after the first crop; removing old leaves and adding fresh compost or fertilizer gives the plant new energy to grow bigger peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai momoi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ hee ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and tall with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops crowd each other out and fight for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and poor yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni adu lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them survive during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass creates a protective layer called mulch, which keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil and holds water near the roots much longer.
ga: Mulching ni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ Oŋmɔshinii lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Enɛ haaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni ehaa nu lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Without enough shade from nurse crops like plantains, the intense heat steals moisture from the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and curl to protect themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over whenever a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit. Tiny pests in the soil called nematodes often eat away these roots, weakening the plant's grip on the ground so a light storm can easily push it down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. ŋmeii bibii Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ. Ehaa tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni ahum ni mli wa lɛ anyɛ ashɛre lɛ shi mlɛo.

english: Yellowing along the center line of older maize leaves is a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient that keeps plants green and healthy, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant recover and make big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes into the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the funnel of young maize plants where it is dark and damp. They feed on the soft leaf tissue before the leaves open, which can ruin the whole plant if not treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji dani baai lɛ gbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch full sunlight, which builds the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also protects them from fungal diseases that thrive in moist soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. To save energy, the plant drops its blossoms; keeping the soil consistently watered and mulched helps prevent this heat stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. koni akɛ hewalɛ ato Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi; Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni akafee dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they feed on the leaf juices, they cause the leaf to warp and spread viruses that stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same farm plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop loves and gives pests a permanent home. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsei sumɔɔ ni ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ náa shia ni baahi shi daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does spreading dried leaves and animal manure on my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Dry leaves and animal manure act like food and a water sponge for the soil. As they break down, they release rich plant nutrients and help the soil hold onto rainwater longer during dry weeks.
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛ sponji kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ egbo lɛ, ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii babaoo kpo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to grow strong. The plant is moving the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei miitsi nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves, but produce very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Your soil likely has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. High nitrogen makes the plant put all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to expand the tubers.
ga: Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the dirt. When the plant dies, that stored food stays in the soil for your next crop to use like natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ okɛtsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny, invisible insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. They weaken the plant and stop the leaves from expanding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhaa baai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and hiding inside the plant funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the hot day and feed on the soft, growing parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni oye tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni miida lɛ

english: Why do I need to place tall stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa shwɛmɔ wulu koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight and air. More sunlight helps the leaves make food for bigger tubers under the ground, and keeping leaves off the damp soil prevents leaf rot.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? ni bɔi nibii ni tsii teremɔ

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread out near the surface rather than going deep into the earth. When the soil gets wet and soft, the heavy weight of the fruit bunch pulls the whole plant down unless you prop it up with wooden poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ Yibii ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large forest trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ koo mli cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight and heat. Large shade trees act like natural umbrellas, lowering the temperature and keeping moisture in the soil so the tender cocoa seedlings do not burn.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ehaa hulutsoo lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Heat stresses the flower, preventing it from getting pollinated and turning into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Dɔlɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ Etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee pollination ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same specific nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the soil completely empty of those foods. Planting the same crop also allows pests and soil diseases that love maize to build up on your farm.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ kwraa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli hu.

english: Why do I need to start my tomato seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them directly in my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are very tiny and vulnerable. Starting them in a shaded nursery lets you protect the fragile seedlings from harsh sunlight, heavy rains, and pests until they grow strong roots and are ready for the main field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ obɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha dumɔ titri.

english: Why do my tomato plants get bushy with big green leaves, but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai agboi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Shi ha tomato fioo ko pɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Giving the plants balanced nutrients with phosphorus and potassium encourages them to bloom and set fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to protect itself. Watering regularly and planting during favorable seasons help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. koni obu ohe Nu ni okɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and touch the ground as soon as the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: As tomato fruits grow, they become too heavy for the thin stems to hold up. Using wooden stakes or sticks to tie up the plants keeps them off the wet soil, preventing diseases and rot.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato aduawai lɛ dara lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni tsii tsɔ ni tso bibioo lɛ nyɛŋ atere. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo tsei fĩ tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. It usually happens when watering is uneven, which stops the roots from absorbing calcium from the soil.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my ripe tomatoes cracking open while still attached to the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miigba be mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: Cracking happens when a dry period is suddenly followed by heavy rain or excessive watering. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Kpãmɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ fe nine nyiɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often carried by tiny whiteflies that infect the plant with a virus, or it can be the plant's natural reaction to hot weather to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ yɛ tsei anɔ. Aloo ekolɛ eji bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa koni nu akafite.

english: Which tomato seeds should I choose if I want market women in Ghana to buy my harvest quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ tomato dumɔwui esa akɛ mahala kɛji miisumɔ ni jarayeli yei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ahe minibii lɛ oya?

english: Market women usually prefer firm, thick-skinned tomato varieties (like Cobra or Power Rano) because they stay fresh longer during transport and do not crush easily when packed in wooden crates.
ga: Jarayeli yei sumɔɔ tomato ni mli wa (tamɔ Cobra loo Power Rano) ejaakɛ amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ. Ni efoŋ oya kɛ́ akɛwo tso adeka mli.

english: When is the best stage for me to pick my tomatoes if buyers have to travel long distances to collect them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mahala tomato kɛji ehe bahia ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ aya he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ koni eyajie?

english: Harvest tomatoes when they are at the 'breaker stage,' which is when the fruit turns from light green to slightly pink or orange. They will finish ripening on the journey without becoming soft or squished.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato be mli ni amɛyɔɔ mli ‘Breaker stage’ ji be mli ni aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse mli kɛyaa pinki loo ŋmɔŋ fioo mli. Amɛbaahoo nii yɛ gbɛfaa nɔ ni amɛbaafee blɛoo loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested tomatoes so they do not rot before buyers arrive at my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite dani mɛi ni baahe lɛ abashɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Keep harvested tomatoes in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas off the bare ground, packed loosely in wooden crates lined with leaves. Never leave harvested tomatoes in direct sun.
ga: Kɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. kpo nɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle ehe Yɛ tso adeka ni baai ebɔ he lɛ mli Kaashi tomato ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is the fertilizer we buy in the market manufactured here in Ghana or brought from abroad?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni wɔheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni afee yɛ Ghana biɛ loo akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ?

english: Ghana does not manufacture raw chemical fertilizer from scratch. Most fertilizer components are imported from abroad, and local suppliers simply mix or blend different nutrients together to match local crop and soil needs.
ga: Ghana efeko tsofai ni akɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ maŋsɛɛ. Ni mɛi ni kɛ nibii baa lɛ futuɔ loo amɛfutuɔ niyenii srɔtoi kɛkɛ koni amɛkɛtsu maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔji lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe nii.

english: Why do fertilizer sellers mix different powders together instead of selling just one type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ futuɔ powda henɔi srɔtoi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ eko pɛ lɛ?

english: Different crops and soils need different plant foods like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Sellers blend these separate materials together so your soil gets the specific mix of nutrients required for your crop to grow well.
ga: Tsei kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi biɔ tsei amli niyenii srɔtoi, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium. Nihɔɔlɔi kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi nɛɛ futuɔ amɛhe koni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil actually needs chemical fertilizer before I go and buy any?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Dani oyahe loo oyahe?

english: You can look for signs like pale or yellowing leaves, stunted growth, or declining harvest yields over time. An extension officer can also look at your soil or test a sample to see which nutrients are missing.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao okadii tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ŋmaa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ akwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛka nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛna niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact amount of fertilizer chemical to put on each plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ falɛ pɔtɛɛ?

english: The right amount depends on what your soil lacks and the age of your crop. By examining your soil and crop conditions, an extension worker can tell you the specific measurement needed so you do not waste money or damage the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ afii abɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ akɛɛ bo susumɔi pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni ofite shika loo okɛ nɔ ko aba tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I put too much chemical fertilizer on my crops to make them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Adding too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops, cause leaves to turn brown, and ruin the soil quality. Plants only absorb what they need, so extra chemicals end up hurting the crop and wasting your money.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ni efiteɔ oshika.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when plants are actively growing and the soil is moist. Soil conditions and plant growth stages signal when the crop is ready to absorb nutrients efficiently.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ tsɔɔ be mli ni tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain so it sinks deep into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away from your farm before the crop roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp but heavy downpours are not expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo shi akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ waa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. When a crop lacks nutrients, it starves its older bottom leaves to send the little food it has to the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Egbeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni ekɛ niyenii fioo amaje baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce a great harvest the first year, but the crops get smaller every year after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo nikpamɔ babaoo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bafee bibioo daa afi yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull nutrients out of the earth. If you do not put nutrients back into the soil using manure, compost, or blended fertilizer, the soil gets tired and yields drop.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I use animal manure from my backyard instead of buying chemical fertilizer from town?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure improves the soil structure and holds water well. However, chemical blends provide quick nutrient boosts, so using manure alongside targeted chemical applications often gives the best results.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfataa tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he lɛ haa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the silks turn dry and dark brown, the outer leaves turn straw-colored, and the kernels become hard and show a tiny black mark at their base when scraped.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni siliki lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi su. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii diji bibii. Yɛ shishigbɛ kɛji akɛ ashɛre

english: Does harvesting my crops a bit early affect the final yield and quality?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa mra fioo lɛ baaná naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Harvesting early usually results in lighter overall weight and smaller produce. While some buyers accept younger crops for specific tender textures, waiting until full maturity yields the maximum weight and highest nutrient content.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ mra haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni tsiimɔ waaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi. Shi kɛlɛ, mɛi komɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpɛlɛɔ tsei bibii anɔ yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo titri lɛ hewɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni amɛmɛ kɛyashi amɛdara jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná muji ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from harsh heat. Once the rains return, the plant will produce fresh green leaves and resume normal growth.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat of the day is a natural defensive behavior to slow down water evaporation from the leaves. If the leaves uncurl when temperatures drop in the evening, the plant is simply managing heat stress and is not diseased.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su ko ni haa nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikwɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ pɛ nɔ ni hela bɛ ehe.

english: Why are the small fruits on my pepper plants falling off before maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop usually happens when plants suffer from sudden water shortage, extreme heat, or insect attack. Keeping the soil moist around the root zone and applying mulch helps stress-prone plants hold onto their fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe waa lɛ ni amɛhiɛ aduawai amli.

english: What makes my young garden eggs stay small and turn yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth usually indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or balanced fertilizer provides the nutrients needed to make the leaves green and support growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni amɛdara.

english: How does adding compost or manure benefit my soil compared to chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the crop quickly, but compost improves the soil structure, allows the ground to hold water much longer during heat waves, and continuously feeds beneficial soil life over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni ekɛ niyenii ni hewalɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together to get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough air, light, and nutrients to produce larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa kɔɔyɔɔ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops so quickly compared to older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ oya kɛ akɛto tsei ni edara lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and aggressively suck up sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Young crops have small roots and few leaves, making them easily overwhelmed by weeds if the field is not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ waa. Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baatsɔ jɛmɛ kɛji ajieee jɛmɛ mra.

english: Why do commercial buyers require my vegetables to be harvested on a precise weekly schedule?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ biɔ ni akpa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli daa otsi lɛ?

english: Commercial buyers and restaurants require uniform size, tender texture, and precise quality standards for processing and selling. Following strict harvesting schedules ensures the produce matches these buyer specifications.
ga: Jarayeli he jarayelɔi kɛ niyelihei biɔ ni amɛdalɛ afee ekome. Tekstur ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ su pɔtɛɛ kɛha nitsumɔ kɛ nihɔɔmɔ. Nikpamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ jarayelɔi nɛɛ ahiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛi anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and rolling up during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce water loss through evaporation. Yellowing usually shows that the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen or is struggling to absorb water from dry soil.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ naa, ni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enyɛɛɛ ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: What causes the flowers on my pepper plants to fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni miiha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ aduawai?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips that damage the flower stems.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ tutuamɔi.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even though the leaves above ground grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ? He ni baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa waa yɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or plants are crowded together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and branches instead of sending food down into the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baatsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and small pods during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli

english: During dry, windy harmattan periods, cocoa trees conserve moisture by dropping young pods and blossoms so the main tree can survive until the heavy rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, hulu lɛ enyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu tswaa. Cacao tsei haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ ni naa wa baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds always sprout and grow much faster than my farm crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in soil for years and are naturally wild and tough, allowing them to absorb moisture instantly and outcompete young cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Ni eji adebɔɔ, adebɔɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhoɔ dumɔwui ni edako lɛ anɔ.

english: Why did the leaves of my crops turn brown and dry up after I put fertilizer right at the base of the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are strong concentrated salts. Placing them directly against plant stems pulls moisture out of the root system like salt on fresh meat, causing the crop to burn and wilt.
ga: Fertilizer ji ŋmeii ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli, tamɔ ŋoo ni yɔɔ loo hee nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough to plant vegetable crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds water well without staying flooded, and contains visible organic matter like earthworms and rotting leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni anaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do hybrid crop seeds from the agricultural store give a better harvest than seeds I save from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong growth and disease resistance, but seeds saved from those harvested crops lose their strong genetic traits in the next generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when the leaves and vines on top begin turning yellow and drying, or when a cut test root produces sap that dries clear rather than black.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni kaa shishifãi ni afo lɛ ená nu ni egbi yɛ diŋ najiaŋ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce water loss through evaporation, acting as a natural survival mechanism to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo gbɛ ni buɔ tso lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Is it better to water my crop during the hot afternoon or in the cool morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa loo leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso waa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so roots can absorb moisture before the sun gets strong; watering in afternoon heat causes water to evaporate before reaching the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ atswa tsɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the sun even when the ground still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose moisture faster than roots can suck it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting during the day until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my plants are yellowing because of too much sun or because they are sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo hewɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Heat stress causes plants to wilt in the afternoon and recover by morning, whereas diseases cause yellowing, spots, or rotting that stay visible all day and night.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni amɛhe feɔ shoo leebi, yɛ be mli ni helai haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛgboɔ ni anaa yɛ shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: High heat damages tomato pollen, preventing fertilization and causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ nii anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
