ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when its bottom leaves turn yellow and drop, the stem becomes woody, and the ground around the base begins to crack open.
ga: Akɛɛ Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ tso. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: What signs tell me that my cocoa pods are mature enough to pluck?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii tsɔɔ mi kɛji mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow—and make a hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔtɔ tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ blɛoo

english: Why do my yam tubers crack inside the soil if I leave them unharvested for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tswaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mishi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni akpaaa amɛ?

english: Leaving mature yams in the soil during sudden dry or wet weather changes causes the outer skin to harden and split when the tuber absorbs sudden moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔtɔ ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ baa trukaa lɛ, ebaaha kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ mli awa ni egbɛ eshwa be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ.

english: If the rains stop earlier than expected, how do I know if my maize is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Check the maize grains; if a small dark spot forms at the tip of the grain where it meets the cob, the grain is fully formed and ready to harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ naagbee yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my watermelon vines start dying off right around the time the fruits get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Watermelon plants naturally direct all their water and nutrients into filling the fruit at the end of their lifecycle, causing the leaves and vines to dry out.
ga: Watermelon tsei lɛ heɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ koni amɛkɛwo yibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ haa baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up like tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my newly planted seeds taking so long to sprout in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to wake up and start growing. If the soil is too dry, the seed stays asleep inside its shell so it does not sprout and die from lack of water.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia amɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ka shi yɛ ŋshɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning yellow even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the soil has too much water. Excess water drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa amɛná niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why did the edges of my crop leaves turn brown and dry after I sprayed chemical medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ewo mihe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spraying crop medicine in strong sunlight or using too strong a mixture can burn tender leaves. Always apply crop medicine early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is weak.
ga: Tso tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ loo akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni mli wa tsɔ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu la lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or poor nutrients. The plant sheds flowers to save its strength so it can survive harsh conditions.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why did my maize crop grow tall and green but end up with small or empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni efeɔ eŋɔli shi etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aloo ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: If maize does not get enough water or nutrients when it starts flowering, proper pollination cannot happen. This prevents the grains from filling out on the cob.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ, Pollination ni sa nyɛŋ aba. Bɔni afee ni ŋmaa lɛ akayi ŋmei lɛ mli

english: Why do insects like armyworms attack my young maize plants more than the older ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ fe mi ŋmã tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have soft, tender leaves that are easy for young insects to eat and digest. As plants mature, their leaves become tough and harder for pests to feed on.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni kooloi bibii yeɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewaa kɛhaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai akɛ amɛaaye.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough soil conditions. Their roots spread fast to steal water, light, and fertilizer before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil and grow mold so quickly inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni efoɔ oya yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Harvested corn still holds hidden moisture inside the grain. If bagged before drying completely under the sun, trapped heat and moisture cause mold and rot to destroy the crop.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee ŋmaa lɛ mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ awo kotokui amli dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack from the thick tubers below.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ yitso ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they say a crop variety is 'true to type'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ tso henɔ ko ji ‘According to type’ lɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from last year's harvest give me lower yields than the certified seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni baa shi fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds, especially from hybrid crops, lose their purity and vigor over generations. Certified seeds sold by authorized seed companies are specially produced under strict controls to remain high-yielding and uniform.
ga: dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ titri lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli Ebaafite ehetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ kɛyashi yinɔi babaoo. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni dumɔwui nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa shishi koni aná yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why shouldn't I just buy grains from the local food market to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miheɔ ŋmaa kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Grains in the market are intended for eating, not planting. They often have low germination rates, carry hidden seed-borne diseases, and will not grow into uniform or high-yielding plants compared to certified planting seeds.
ga: Afee ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ koni aye, shi jeee ni adu. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɛ shweremɔ ni baa shi. Helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ. ni edaŋ ni efee tsei ni yɔɔ ekome loo ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: How do seed companies make sure the seeds they sell to farmers will actually produce good crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei lɛ aná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Seed companies get initial pure seeds developed by agricultural researchers. They multiply these under strict isolation standards to ensure the seeds retain their good traits before packaging and selling them to farmers.
ga: Dumɔwui nitsumɔhei lɛ baaná dumɔwui shishijee ni he tse ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ. Amɛfɔɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi nɛɛ yɛ mligbalamɔ he mlai ni mli wa shishi koni amɛkwɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ amɛsu kpakpai lɛ amli dani akɛwo kotoku mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ aha okwaafoi.

english: Why do my neighbor's hybrid maize plants all grow to the exact same height, while my farm has tall and short plants mixed together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa tsei ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei kakadaji kɛ tsei kukuji efutu.

english: Hybrid seeds are carefully bred to have identical genetic makeup, so every plant grows at the same rate and height. Saved or mixed local seeds contain varied genetics, causing uneven growth across the field.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná wala yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ daaa yɛ oyaiyeli kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli. Kuu mli dumɔwui ni ato loo ni akɛfutu mli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do seeds taken from a sweet orange fruit sometimes grow into trees that yield sour oranges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ mli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Tree crops do not always grow 'true to type' from seed because their seeds inherit mixed traits from pollen. To guarantee sweet fruit, farmers must plant grafted seedlings taken from a proven sweet tree stem.
ga: Tsei kɛ tsei miikwɛɛɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ ‘yɛ henɔi lɛ anaa’ kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ náa sui komɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli. Koni okɛma nɔ mi akɛ obaaná aduawai ni ŋɔɔ. Esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ adu dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni ŋɔɔ ni ana he odaseyeli mli.

english: Why do seeds taken from the same tomato fruit produce plants that look different from one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato kome mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni hiɛ yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers can get cross-pollinated by insects carrying pollen from nearby different varieties. This mixes the genetic traits, causing the resulting seeds to grow into plants with different shapes and sizes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ baanyɛ afee cross-pollination kɛtsɔ kooloi ni hiɛ pollen ni jɛ henɔi srɔtoi amli lɛ anɔ. ni bɛŋkɛ Eji fɔmɔ nii ni akɛfee ekome. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ henɔi kɛ dalɛi srɔtoi.

english: Why do some crop varieties handle dry spells in Ghana better than traditional varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ hulutsoo be lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Breeders select specific traits, such as deeper root systems or faster maturity, to create drought-tolerant varieties. These traits help the plant extract deep soil moisture or finish fruiting before the dry season starts.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ ahala amɛ kɛha sui tamɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛdalɛ oya. Koni afee srɔtoi ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ hɔmɔ naa. Sui nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbala nu kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo amɛwoɔ yibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: If I plant two different varieties of maize next to each other, will it affect my crops?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, Ani ebaana miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, wind carries pollen between the two varieties, causing cross-pollination. While this year's harvest may look normal, any seeds saved from that harvest will be mixed and will produce unpredictable plants next season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ pollen yɛ kooloi srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ ateŋ. causing cross pollination Eyɛ mli akɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmaa lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni sa moŋ, Shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ futuɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo tsei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants give smaller yields after I use stems from the same farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ ŋmɔ kome mli tsei lɛ ahe tsei tsu nii afi fɛɛ afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Reusing stems over many seasons allows diseases and viruses to build up inside the plant material. Replacing old stems with clean, certified planting materials restores high yields.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi tsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ, ehaa helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ tsake tsei momo lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: When the soil gets flooded with too much water, plant roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly. The yellowing is a sign of nitrogen deficiency because heavy rain washes nitrogen out of the root zone and waterlogged soil stops roots from feeding.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Yellow ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning gives your crops the moisture they need to survive the heat of the day. Evening watering leaves the leaves and soil damp overnight, which creates an ideal environment for harmful fungi and diseases to grow.
ga: Nu ni oooha onibii lɛ leebi lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the maize while also covering the soil to reduce weed growth.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa saplings dry up and die during the intense dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantain or shade trees to protect them from excessive heat until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo wu.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot daytime temperatures, prolonged dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer that forces the plant to produce leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do cassava leaves curl up and develop light green or yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. It damages the leaf's ability to make food, reducing the size of your tuber harvest.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ. Kɛtsɔ o-tuber ni okpaa lɛ nɔ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep should I bury my yam sets when planting them on ridges?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu sweet potato tsei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ?

english: Yam sets should be planted about 10 to 15 centimeters deep with the cut side facing downwards. Planting at this depth keeps the set cool and moist while allowing sprouts to reach the surface easily.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato kui ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15, ni fã ni afo lɛ akwɛ shi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nɛkɛ shɔŋŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ ni miida lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why does putting too much chemical fertilizer close to my crops burn their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are concentrated salts. When too much is placed directly against roots, it reverses the flow of water, sucking moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the plant to wither and look burnt.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ, nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ, ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can check a few test plants; if the inside of the pods has turned dark brown with visible veins, the crop is mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ okwɛ nitsumɔhei komɛi ni akɛkaa nii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ fãji ni anaa lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop plants to stay small and yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than crops. They aggressively compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your crops and keeping them from reaching full size.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, ni amɛhaa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhaaa amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that create living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. When soil nitrogen is low, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni tso lɛ náa lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni edara lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better and give bigger tubers when I stake them with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that naturally search for sunlight. Lifting their leaves off the ground on sticks allows them to catch more light to make food, while keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni taoɔ hulu la yɛ ebɔɔ su naa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa la babaoo ni amɛkɛhooɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Dropping leaves is how cassava protects itself from drying out. Leaves lose water quickly in hot wind, so shedding them helps the cassava conserve moisture in its roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ni aŋmɛɔ ŋmei lɛ gbɛ koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the field for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. When it gets too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself rather than trying to grow fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu aduawai

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small and light when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets its full share of food and light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal fertilizers and soil nutrients away from your plants' roots. Even with rain, your crops go hungry because the weeds are eating their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi amli waa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ odumɔ nii lɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiye amɛniyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are meant to store soft starch. As the plant gets older, it converts that soft starch into tough, woody fibers to support its own long-term survival, making the tubers hard to cook and eat.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi toɔ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Kɛ tso lɛ da Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ tso tsɔji ni wa. koni eye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaahoo ŋmeii ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl upwards during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on hot days is a tomato plant's way of reducing water loss. By curling inward, the leaf hides part of its surface from the sun and dry air, trapping moisture inside to keep the plant alive.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tomato tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe fã ko teeɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ he. Emɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a canopy that shields cocoa leaves from hot sunlight while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more food from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong roots and yield larger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them grow on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for underground tubers. Lifting vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from soil moisture that causes foliage rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso nɔ lɛ, hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even when the plant above ground has very tall, green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ aŋɔli moŋ, shi.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing big stems and leaves instead of tuber roots. Balanced nutrients encourage energy to flow downward into heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji yɛ shishifãi ahe ŋmeii najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni eho kɛya ŋmeii ni tsii amli.

english: Is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same row as my maize crop?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts with maize helps the soil. Legumes naturally take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt, feeding the maize without extra fertilizer costs.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni akwɛ ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo ŋmãa he nyɔmɔ kroko

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific plant foods from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating crops gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa tsei niyenii komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli fãa?

english: Ragged holes inside the central leaves of maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They feed on young inner leaf tissue, but early treatment with recommended sprays or neem leaf extracts stops them before they ruin the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baa bibioo lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ neem baa mli tsofa loo nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ atsa lɛ mra. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or uneven watering. Consistent watering and keeping the root zone cool helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni ahaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Spreading dry grass (mulching) acts as a blanket over the soil. It protects the roots from harsh heat, stops moisture from evaporating quickly into the air, and blocks weeds from taking root.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekawo shishifãi.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are small and weak, making them easily overwhelmed by weeds. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing water, fertilizer, and light during the plant's most critical growth stage.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye nɔ Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ la yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that the roots are getting too much water. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize leaves turn dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I know if my land is ready and good enough for planting tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tomato ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good soil for tomatoes should crumble easily in your hand and let water sink in without pooling into mud. If the land gets flooded easily, building raised ridges will keep tomato roots healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha tomato lɛ akumɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni eha nu lɛ abote mli ni etsɔko muji. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya lɛ Ŋshɔkpɔi ni kɛlɛ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni tomato shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects eating holes in my cowpea leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Insects like beetles like to feed on fresh foliage. Spraying the leaves early with a natural mixture made from neem leaves or safe recommended products keeps pests away before they destroy the whole farm.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai heei. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛ neem baai loo nɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ fee lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy soil or during very heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil heaps or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the sun is too hot or the soil is too dry. Giving the plants steady water and spreading dry grass around their bases to cool the soil helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Ha tsei lɛ nu daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã amɛhe. Shishitoo ni akɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the yam tubers inside the ground grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when beetles attack the stem base or when the soil gets too hot and dry. Staking the vines off the ground and mulching the base keeps the vine green long enough to feed the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ ŋmeii tutua tsei lɛ ashishi loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi. Kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aha shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni wain tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ bulbs.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good. Beans trap good nutrients from the air and feed the soil, while maize stalks act as strong supports for the climbing bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiɔ ŋmãa wain tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ewa.

english: When is the best time during the hot day for me to water my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best times to water vegetables are early morning or late evening. Watering in the middle of the day makes the water dry up fast in the heat before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ agbi oya yɛ latsaa be mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: How can I tell that my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their skin changes color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange. Picking them at this stage gives high-quality cocoa beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhiɛ tsake su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahalaa mɛi nɛɛ haa anáa kookoo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast before I can carry them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if harvested when fully soft in the hot sun or packed in airtight bags. Picking them when they just start turning orange and placing them in airy wooden crates keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ beni efee blɛoo kwraa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛwo vacuum mli. Kɛ́ okɛto beni amɛje shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwo tso adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough for planting cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui?

english: Cocoa trees grow best in deep, loose, loamy soil that drains water easily while holding onto moisture. If your land floods frequently or is full of heavy clay and rocks, cocoa roots will rot or fail to grow properly.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe nɔ. Amɛhoɔ nu oya yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji nu afua fɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ kɛ tɛi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the farm before putting my cocoa seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu cocoa tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn quickly in strong Ghanaian sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and provide thick leaf canopies that act as shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ Ghana hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young plants are getting hit by too much direct heat from the sun, lack enough water, or are missing key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ eshɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni bɛ

english: How often should I water my young cocoa seedlings when the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ harmatta be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ shishijee mli?

english: During the harmattan, young seedlings should be watered at least two to three times a week early in the morning or late in the evening so heat does not dry out the soil too fast.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Kokoo tso bibioo fɛɛ tso bibioo otsii enyɔ

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil, causing your young seedlings to stay weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting before my cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: If you plant modern hybrid cocoa seedlings, they usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years with good care, whereas older traditional seed types take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid dumɔwui Bei pii lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo ŋmeii ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune some branches off my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie cacao tso ni miida lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can flow through, which prevents fungal diseases and directs the plant's energy into growing larger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmɔji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod on my tree is ripe enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color completely, turning from dark green or reddish-brown to a bright yellow or orange color, and makes a hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ loo tsuru-tsu kɛya ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ ata he fioo

english: What causes black patches to spread across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black patches are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods and trimming extra tree branches keeps the farm dry and stops it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Should I use animal manure or chemical fertilizer on my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Using well-rotted animal manure improves the long-term texture and water retention of your soil, while balanced chemical fertilizers give young plants a fast boost of growth nutrients; combining both gives the best results.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ja lɛ baaye abua tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ fata he lɛ, nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do all my plantain trees seem to produce bunches and mature at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Plantains planted around the same time react to seasonal triggers like the return of rains together. This natural response causes synchronized flowering and fruiting across your farm, leading to a sudden, large harvest all at once.
ga: Plantains ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ tsuɔ be mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ he nii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hetoo nɛɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibii baa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa shikome

english: How can I tell that a plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to harvest before it starts ripening on the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains kuu ko edara ni esa akɛ akpa dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp angular ridges and become round and plump, and the dried flowers at the tips of the fruits fall off easily when touched.
ga: Plantain tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni etsɔ ŋwɛi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anaa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: If my buyers delay in coming to the farm, how long can harvested green plantains stay before they start getting soft and spoiling?
ga: Kɛji mihelɔ lɛ bashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ Be enyiɛ plantains eŋɔli ni akpa lɛ baahi shi dani amɛje shishi amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛfite?

english: Once cut from the plant, green plantains usually stay firm for 3 to 7 days under warm weather before they start ripening. Keeping them in a cool, shaded place with good airflow helps stretch this window before softening begins.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Green plantains lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ gbii 3 kɛyashi 7 yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli dani ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha samflɛ nɛɛ asɛɛ atsɛ dani ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantains turn black and spoil so fast when I stack them tightly together in large bags or under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui wuji amli loo mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains breathe and release heat and ethylene gas. Stacking them tightly traps this heat and gas, which drastically speeds up ripening and rot, while direct sunlight damages the outer skin.
ga: Plantain ni akpa lɛ muɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ethylene gas kpo. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛshwere ni amɛgboi oya kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ.

english: Is there a way I can slow down the ripening of my green plantains if market transport doesn't arrive on time?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mafo plantains eŋɔli lɛ ashweremɔ mli kɛji akɛ jarayeli tsɔne lɛ baaa yɛ be naa?

english: Yes, you can slow down ripening by storing the green bunches in a cool, well-ventilated shade away from any ripe fruits, and avoiding tight sacks so that heat and natural ripening gases can escape.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni oooha amɛhi shi yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛjɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ kotokui ni mli wa lɛ ahe koni hulutsoo kɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ aje kpo.

english: Why does a single plantain tree keep growing so many small shoots around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso kome pɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle eshishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains produce natural underground shoots called suckers to reproduce. If you leave all of them to grow, they will fight with the main mother plant for food and water, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Plantains lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛfɔ bii. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ pɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu, ni no baaha amɛfee kui bibii.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm getting smaller and lighter with each new harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifee bibii lɛ? Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ hee

english: Plantains draw heavy amounts of nutrients like potassium from the soil. Without replenishing the soil with organic manure or proper fertilizers, the depleted soil cannot feed subsequent crop cycles properly.
ga: Plantains jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo, tamɔ potassium kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataaa sũ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni elaaje lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers always advise us to plant plantains when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ wɔdu plantains kɛ́ wɔje kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow rapidly and provide tall, wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas to shade the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during strong rains even when the stem is not broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifã lɛ ekuuu lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread near the topsoil rather than deep taproots. If soil pests like weevils or nematodes damage those shallow roots, the plant loses its anchor and tips over easily under the weight of a heavy bunch.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii loo nematodes lɛ fite nakai shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ afite eshishifã lɛ oya ni efo yɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves have a high water content and broad surface area that loses moisture rapidly in dry weather. The plant intentionally sheds its older outer leaves to conserve water for the main stem and growing bunch.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ plantain baai lɛ amli, ni amɛhiɛ hu da, ni no haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai momo lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu he kɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tsei akui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them creates a living canopy that protects the cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees when planting maize, while my cocoa needs shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei kakadaji kɛji midu ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kookoo he miihia shade?

english: Different crops react differently to sunlight. Maize needs full, direct sunlight all day to make food and grow strong cobs, whereas young cocoa thrives in filtered shade and gets heat stress under open sun.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ hulu la he yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni enyɛ efee niyenii ni ekwɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛkpeɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli yɛ hulu la ni mli tse mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni baai lɛ hu kwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni akɛ muji woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves and center whorl of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baai kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that eat young leaves inside the plant. Inspecting the center of the plants early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii kɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and feel thick during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to reduce water loss through their surface when the air is dry and hot. Providing steady moisture at the root zone prevents the plant from stressing and curling its leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli fũu pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekahao ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops heat from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli koni ekɛtsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: How does planting cassava cuttings too close together affect the tubers underground?
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ Te enaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the roots to fight for underground space and nutrients, resulting in many small, thin roots instead of large, starchy tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to produce food. Lifting the vines off the muddy ground with stakes exposes maximum leaves to sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni atsĩ foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa

english: Why does my land yield smaller maize harvests if I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those exact nutrients and encourages maize diseases to live in the soil. Rotating with cowpeas or groundnuts restores the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite, ni ebaawo ŋmãa helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to block the harsh sun and keep the air moist, the heat scorches their delicate leaves, causing them to dry up and fall.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã ebaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip and moving down the center, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, feemɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnajiaŋ ni oyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to breathe. When the ground stays soaked in water for too long without good drainage, the soil loses oxygen and harmful fungus grows easily, causing the roots to turn soft and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What happens if I don't give my yam vines sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mihaaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. If the vines trail on the hot ground, they catch diseases from the soil and shade each other, leading to small, weak yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛji wain tsei nyiɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ Amɛmɔɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get more harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely actually reduces your total harvest because the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, skinny stalks that produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn and small caterpillars hiding inside the center roll?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ buji ni etse amɛhe ni akɛtee wolokpo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the tender growing center of corn plants. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel during the day to protect themselves from heat and predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off mainly due to extreme heat or irregular watering. When temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, the plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they spread. These insects drink the plant's sap from under the leaves, causing the new growth to warp and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ hee lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni ebɔleɔ ehe.

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain titri lɛ shwereɔ bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be oshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ?

english: The young shoots, called suckers, take water and food directly from the main plant's root system. If you leave too many suckers, they steal the energy the main tree needs to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii bibii. Eheɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Ejuɔ hewalɛ ni tso titri lɛ he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen, leaving the soil tired. Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, helping to restore fertility for the next crop you plant.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii. haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Sir, why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers on the same land where I am planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture so the young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Sir, why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when the heavy rainy season begins?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater flow off easily, keeping the roots dry enough to avoid rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. without draining out Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Kwɛmɔ ni shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or attacks from small insects. Watering the base of the plants regularly during dry spells and checking for pests helps the flowers stay on to produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishi nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Sir, why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni eha tso lɛ edaaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early with organic sprays like neem oil and keeping the plant well-watered stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ helai kɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ neem fɔ kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ tsei lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines onto stakes ensures every leaf catches sunlight while keeping the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baa fɛɛ baa shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Sir, why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when they are already growing big?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi ni amɛdara momo lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to move freely through the cocoa tree canopy. This dries up excess moisture that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to send its energy into making cocoa pods instead of growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light winds right when the fruit is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny worms or stem borers eat away their underground roots, weakening their grip in the soil. Planting clean, pest-free suckers and mounding fresh soil high around the stem base keeps the tree firmly anchored.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo stem borers lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi Aduɔ tsei ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli ni akɛ sũ hee ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ato he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Sir, why is it bad to plant many maize seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ehiii akɛ aaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the young plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do officers recommend that I plant cowpeas or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of natural nutrients from the ground, but leguminous crops like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting cowpeas restores natural soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa e-adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ, mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Cowpeas ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant them late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ toi bibii waa kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady water and sunlight during its early stage. When planted late, the rains often stop before the ears fill up, causing the crop to dry out early and give poor yields.
ga: Nu kɛ hulu la he miihia ŋmãa daa yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpaa dani toi lɛ eyiɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss and protect its roots. When the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: How can I test if the seed maize I bought will grow before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can wrap 10 seeds in a wet cloth for three days. If 8 or 9 sprout, the seeds are healthy and good to plant in your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mama ni mli efɔ awo dumɔwui 10 mli gbii etɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tomatoes grown from improved seeds stay fresh longer after harvest than tomatoes from my saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ fe tomato ni jɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved tomato varieties are bred to have thicker skins and stronger disease resistance, which keeps the fruit firm and fresh for longer after picking.
ga: Atsake tomato henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛhewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by hot, dry weather or a lack of soil nutrients, saving their energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba amɛnaa. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow big green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ pea ŋmɔtɔi fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas put energy into leaves instead of flowers; they need balanced soil to focus on producing pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja he miihia amɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when water sits on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Flooded soil starves roots of air, preventing them from taking up nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and stunts growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ aná shishifãi lɛ. Tsi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why do Fall Armyworm caterpillars destroy my maize crop so quickly without me seeing them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kpata mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ oya ni minaaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the center leaf funnel of the plant, eating the hidden growing point before you notice damage on the outer leaves.
ga: Roundworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni edaa yɛ lɛ dani oyɔseɔ akɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ efite.

english: Why do cocoa tree leaves burn and curl up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛkpãa amɛhe be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees to protect their leaves from hot sun and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when I stack them inside a hot, closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that breathe and release heat; without cool air flowing around them, trapped heat and moisture cause rapid rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni muɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kpo. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɛ mli ni hoɔ kɛbɔleɔ he Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade from companion plants like plantains, the harsh sun burns their delicate leaves and dries them out before their root system can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi yɛ he kome lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Why are my young maize leaves full of small holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Lots kɛ looks chew?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms. These caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender leaves from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Fungi thrive in this damp environment and attack the roots beneath the soil surface.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Fuji lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni etutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism. The pepper plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface exposed to hot sun, preventing the plant from losing too much moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stem without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or the soil goes completely dry, the tomato plant experiences severe heat stress and drops its flowers to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tomato tsei kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ. ni okɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ehi wala mli

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and dark green but produce tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing thick leaves and tall stems instead of building heavy, full cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee tso ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight underground for the same water and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and poor yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets soil pests build up to dangerous levels.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa kɛyashɛ he ko ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over right when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ agboi lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface. As the heavy bunch grows, the tree becomes top-heavy and needs wooden props to stay upright against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ tsei afi sɛɛ koni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ eshi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why are my crops still weak even after I apply fertilizer without removing the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni mijieee jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that swallow the fertilizer and soil water much faster than your crops can, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: How can using a tractor to prepare my land improve my crop yield compared to using a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Tractors break up hard soil deeper and faster than a hoe. This loosens the dirt so plant roots can easily spread out, hold more water, and soak up nutrients for stronger growth.
ga: Traktai tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyaa oya fe shɔvel. Enɛ haa muji lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Ehiɛɔ nu babaoo ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ haa edalɛ waa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an important food crop roots need. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves the roots standing in water for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi taoɔ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.
