english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist before spreading fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can drink it up. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money because the plants cannot swallow dry chemical food.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni eji shika fitemɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ ami tsofa niyenii ni egbi.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant enough room allows its roots and leaves to grow big without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it deep into the dirt through their roots. When the plant finishes growing, that extra food stays behind in the soil for crops like maize to eat later.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni efuɔ amɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe naa lɛ Nakai niyenii ni fa lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa aye sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees or plantain plants block the strong sun and keep the ground cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo hulutsoo tsei ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa naa lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil right around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the sunlight, fertilizer, and space that your crops need to thrive, even if water is plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ he ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu lɛ fa babaoo moŋ

english: Why are small worms eating the inside funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that prefers the soft, tender young leaves hidden inside the corn stem. Destroying them early stops them from killing the main growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Amɛfitemɔ mra Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbe tso lɛ mli hei titri ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get full of tiny holes and brown dust inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils burrow into maize grains that were stored while still holding too much moisture or left unprotected. Drying your maize fully in the sun before storage stops insects from multiplying and spoiling the crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baafo ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii babaoo loo ni ashi ni abuuu he lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo ni amɛkafite tso lɛ.

english: Why should I buy expensive hybrid seeds instead of just re-planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he ni jara wa moŋ fe ni madu tsei ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce plants that grow faster, resist local diseases, and yield much more grain or fruit. Saved seeds lose these special traits over time, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni eha tsei lɛ adara oya. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai babaoo Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why can't I save seeds from my hybrid crop to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid tsei amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The seeds produced by a hybrid crop lose their strong genetic traits in the second generation. If you plant them, the crops will grow unevenly, produce smaller yields, and be more vulnerable to pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ feɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu tsei nɛɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe oshara ni baa lɛ baa shi ni eyaa hiɛ

english: Why do some crop varieties handle long dry spells in Ghana better than traditional varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are developed to grow deeper root systems and conserve water better, allowing them to stay healthy and survive even when rain stops for a few weeks.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo po.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster and greener after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like nutritious food for crops, supplying vital elements like nitrogen and phosphorus that plants need to build strong stems and lush, healthy leaves.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to stay green. Adding the right fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to grow properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso ni he hiaa ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Nuŋtsɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does placing fertilizer right near the plant roots help the crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures the crop can absorb nutrients quickly before rains wash them away or nearby weeds steal them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ni tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya dani nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛyaa loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ juɔ amɛ.

english: Why do young crops need extra plant food early in the season rather than late in their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei niyenii krokomɛi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe sɛɛ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need abundant nutrients during their early weeks to build deep root systems and strong stems, which are necessary to support heavy grains or fruit later on.
ga: Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. koni akɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa Enɛ he miihia koni akɛfi dumɔwui loo aduawai ni tsii sɛɛ mli.

english: Is taking a loan to buy fertilizer and hybrid seeds actually worth the risk for a small farm?
ga: Ani shika ni akɛfaa koni akɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ sa oshara ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ?

english: Using quality seeds and fertilizer together can double or triple your crop harvest, producing enough extra crop to pay off the loan and leave you with a higher net profit.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ekome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii ni okpa lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ loo toi etɛ. Enɛ ha aná ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛwo nyɔmɔ ni awo lɛ. ni eha oná sɛɛnamɔ ni fa fe no

english: Will buying fertilizer guarantee that I double my crop harvest this season?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ baaha miná nɔmimaa akɛ maná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer greatly boosts crop potential, but maximum yields also depend on good rainfall, planting at the right time, and keeping weeds and pests away from the crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa. Shi nibii ni anáa babaoo lɛ hu damɔ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do crops respond much better to fertilizer when I use good seeds instead of old seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui momo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: High-quality seeds grow into vigorous plants with strong root systems that can absorb and utilize nutrients efficiently, whereas weak plants cannot take full advantage of added fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are market buyers asking if I used safe chemicals on my crops before they buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ biɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani miheɔ lɛ?

english: Consumers in Ghana are becoming much more health-conscious and want to eat food that is safe and clean. Crops grown with safe chemical practices and no harmful residues attract higher demand and better market trust.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miikwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni he tse. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli lɛ gbalaa nibii babaoo ni ataoɔ kɛ jarayeli he hekɛnɔfɔɔ kpakpa.

english: How do small insect bites on my vegetables lower the price I get at the market?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni shwieɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ aha amɛjara aba shi yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Insects leave marks, holes, and diseases that make produce look bad and spoil faster. Buyers want attractive, undamaged food, so damaged produce is downgraded and sold for much lower prices.
ga: Kplukai shĩɔ okadii, bu kɛ helai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ fɛo ni efiteɔ oya. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ fɛo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ nibii ni efite lɛ ashishi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi kwraa nɔ.

english: Why do my farm goods spoil when I send them on long trips to coastal cities like Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ mikɛ amɛ tee gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtee ŋshɔnaa maŋ ko tamɔ Accra lɛ?

english: Soft crops break easily during rough transport, and high heat inside packed bags causes rapid rotting. Harvesting early in the morning and using wooden crates with airflow keeps produce fresh during long journeys.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛfaa ni mli wa mli. Ni la ni mli edɔ waa ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ haa efiteɔ oya. Nikpamɔ leebi maŋkpa kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: What causes my fruits to look fine on the farm but arrive soft and bruised at the buyer's shop?
ga: Mɛni haa mi aduawai lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔlɔmɔ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: Fruits continue to ripen and soften after harvest. Harvesting them when they are over-ripe or stacking heavy sacks on top of them causes deep bruising and quick decay during transit.
ga: Yibii lɛ yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛshwere tsɔ loo akɛto kotokui ni tsii amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafite oya yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why does the market price of my crop drop so low during the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests and sells the same crop at the same time, the market gets flooded with food. High supply lowers prices, while selling early or late in the season brings higher profits.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nii kome yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayeli lɛ baayi kɛ niyenii. Nibii ni akɛhaa babaoo lɛ haa nibii ajara baa shi. yɛ be mli ni jarayeli mra loo naagbee yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo baa.

english: Why do some buyers pay higher prices for smaller, cleaner crops than my bigger ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni he tse lɛ jara babaoo fe miŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ?

english: Modern consumers value cleanliness, natural taste, and safety over pure size. Clean, pest-free produce sells faster to conscious consumers, allowing buyers to offer a premium price for them.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jarayelɔi buɔ hetsemɔ akɛ nɔ ni he hiaa waa. adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ fe dalɛ krɔŋŋ Nibii ni he tse, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ hɔ̃ɔ oya kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ haa amɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave rotten or ungathered crops on my farm after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite loo ni akpako yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leftover crop material hosts pests and fungal diseases through the off-season. Cleaning your farm completely prevents these pests from surviving to attack your next planting cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ́ otsumɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi koni amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants stop producing good fruits near the end of their lifecycle if I don't give them extra care?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii kpakpai ni amɛwoɔ beni amɛwala be lɛ naagbee lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ, kɛji mikwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops exhaust the nutrients in the soil as they yield fruit. Without mid-season feeding or proper clearing of old plant parts, the remaining fruits stay small and poor in quality.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ afeee niyenii yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ loo ajieee tso lɛ fãi momoi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ baafee bibioo ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do tiny pests suddenly show up on my crops just when the fruits start getting sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Pests are naturally drawn to high sugar content and soft plant tissues that develop during fruit ripening. Regular field checks allow you to catch and manage them before they destroy the crop value.
ga: Sugar ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ tso mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni baa beni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni okwɛɔ amɛ nɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara.

english: How do I know if my crop is developing a hidden disease before I take it to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ miimɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani mikɛba jara nɔ?

english: Diseased crops often show subtle early signs like yellowing leaf veins, wilting in daytime heat, or tiny dark spots on stems. Checking plants weekly helps you spot infections before they ruin the entire harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ mra be mli okadii ni bɛ faŋŋ tamɔ baai lɛ amli fãji ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be mli lɛ kpo. loo ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ daa otsi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona helai ni baa mɔ nɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is too much direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block excess heat and hold soil moisture while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ haaa dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine aba, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen, which is a key food crop plants need to grow strong. Adding compost or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and regain healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know which way to place my cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the sprouts to grow crooked underground, resulting in weak plants and fewer cassava roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi fioo pɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, exposes them to sunshine, and prevents diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. hulu la lɛ nɔ ni etsi helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before growing into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or a lack of water, which stresses the plant. Giving the soil regular moisture and protecting plants with light shade during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli dɔ waa loo nu bɛ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni abuɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops rainwater from evaporating too fast in the sun, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plants finish growing, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds food crops like maize planted afterward.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa niyenii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni sɛɛ mli lɛ aduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up into small, hard shapes?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii ni wa?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juices from underneath the leaves. Spraying an organic mixture like neem leaf extract or targeted pest control early can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Ebaanyɛ ebu baai ahe

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ buji ni etse amɛhe ni akɛtee amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on young maize leaves inside the center whorl. Checking plants early and applying recommended treatments into the center whorl stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei wuji lɛ ahe nibii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If too many small shoots grow around the main plantain, they fight with the parent plant for food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves just one or two strong stems, which ensures the main plant produces bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ Too much plantain he lɛ Ekɛ nyɛ tso lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a living canopy that protects young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: How do plantain crops reproduce if they do not produce seeds like maize?
ga: Te plantain tsei baafee tɛŋŋ amɛfɔ kɛji amɛwooo dumɔwui, tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds; instead, they grow from underground stem structures called corms. The plant produces small shoots called suckers around its base, which can be dug up and replanted to grow new plantain trees.
ga: Plantains jɛɛɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛ̃ɔ. Mohu ɔ, e daa kɛ je tso tso ko nɛ ngɛ zugba sisi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke rhizome ɔ mi. Tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ suckers ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni abaanyɛ atsa ni adu ekoŋŋ koni akwɛ plantains heei.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and stay green. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting leguminous crops helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots, restoring fertility for the next season without needing costly chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: When is the right time to apply top-dressing fertilizer to my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied between 4 to 8 weeks after planting when the cassava roots are actively establishing and rains are steady enough to dissolve the nutrients into the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 8 teŋ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp environments. Pruning overgrown tree branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the pods and dry out excess moisture.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ́ɔ

english: Why do my maize plant leaves look ragged with big holes eaten out right near the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni eyɛ bu agbo ko ni bɛŋkɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing funnel of the maize plant. Applying approved organic or chemical remedies directly into the plant funnel early in the morning targets the caterpillars effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaatswa ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full light while preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni eŋmɛɔ koni enine ashɛ la fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why can cassava stay buried in the soil for months without spoiling before I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shikpɔŋ nyɔji babaoo ni egbooo dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers are natural underground storage organs. As long as the stems and leaves remain attached and healthy above ground, the tuber stays alive and fresh in the soil until it is dug up.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ baai lɛ baahi shi ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ yibii lɛ baahi shi ni amɛbaafee ehee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi abaakumɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it important to wait for the main rains to establish before planting maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni amɛmɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa dani adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need continuous moisture in the soil to germinate and develop strong initial roots. Planting too early during unpredictable light rains can cause the seeds to germinate and then wither if dry spells return.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishijee shishifãi ni mli wa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli Nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji majik ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist so young cocoa seedlings can survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas in the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil to grow. Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send whatever remaining food it has to the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni ji baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves showing ragged holes with small caterpillars inside the central funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ jieɔ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii akpo lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing point of maize plants. Spraying appropriate neem extracts or recommended insecticides directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Waterlogged soil cuts off air supply to the roots and promotes fungal rot diseases. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so roots remain healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa, ni ehaa ŋmeii fiteɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does a small purple-flowered weed cause my maize plants to turn yellow and stay stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Ani eeha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: That weed is likely Striga, also known as witchweed. It attaches its roots directly to your maize underground, stealing water and nutrients before the maize can use them.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed. Ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani akɛ ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on high sticks instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves into the sunlight so they can make food more efficiently, while also keeping them away from hot ground soil and humidity that spread fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking haa wain tso lɛ baai lɛ naa hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha wain tso lɛ baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for nutrients and water. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often caused by inconsistent watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant transport calcium into developing tomatoes.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa tomato ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when exposed to sudden high heat, dry soil, or nutrient shortages. Mulching around the base keeps the soil cool and moist, encouraging flowers to stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa. Mulching around Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: If I spray chemical pesticides on my cocoa farm, is it safe for my free-roaming chickens to go into the farm?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ baabote ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, many chemicals used to kill farm pests are toxic to birds and animals. Chickens can die or get sick if they eat insects, grass, or spilled seeds that have been sprayed with pesticide.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji tsofai fɔji kɛha okpoi kɛ kooloi. Kooloi baanyɛ agbo loo hela mɔ amɛ kɛji amɛye kooloi bibii, jwɛi loo dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie shi.

english: Can I wash and re-use empty farm chemical containers to hold water or feed for my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni mikɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ koni mikɛto nu loo kooloi aniyenii?

english: Never re-use chemical containers for animals or household use. Poisonous residue stays stuck in the plastic even after washing, which can contaminate water and kill your livestock.
ga: Kaaha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kooloi loo shia nibii amli lɛ miitsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ plastic lɛ mli kɛ́ afɔ he po. Enɛ baanyɛ afite nu lɛ ni egbe okooloi lɛ.

english: How many years does it usually take for a newly planted hybrid cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within two to three years of planting if they receive proper shade, water, and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Kɛji akɛ aha lɛ hulutsoo, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa

english: Why do young cocoa plants die when exposed to full sunlight during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ kwraa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantain trees to protect them from direct sun while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pods?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to shed up to 90 percent of their flowers because the tree cannot support that many pods. However, severe flower drop can also be caused by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect damage.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei ni fa fe oha mlijaa 90 baawo fɔfɔi, ejaakɛ cacao tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmeii babaoo anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hu baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ aba. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop plants turning yellow and failing to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or it is getting too much water or direct sunlight. Adding manure or fertilizer usually helps plants regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ loo hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my young cocoa pods before the pods fully mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ dani ŋmɔji lɛ dara kwraa?

english: Pests like mirids (capsids) bite young pods, leaving dark brown or black sunken spots. If untreated, these bites dry out the pod and cause it to die before maturing.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni ebote mli. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in the first year but give smaller yields by the third year on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season. If you do not add compost, manure, or fertilizer back into the soil, it becomes weak and produces smaller harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I keep my crops alive and green during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔji yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around the base of your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching). This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly in the dry heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it important to ferment cocoa beans for several days after harvesting instead of drying them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atswa kookoo yibii lɛ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Fermentation removes the sticky white pulp, stops the bean from germinating, and develops the rich chocolate flavor inside the bean before drying.
ga: Fermentation jieɔ loo ni wa ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ. Tsi ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ anaa ni oha tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ aba kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli dani egbi.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people say I should cut off some lower branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower or crowded branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree, which prevents moisture build-up that causes black pod disease and encourages higher fruit yields.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ ni baa shi loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai babaoo baa

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots, preventing the plant from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why is it bad to plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and very small ears of corn.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the stems can sprout correctly; planting them upside down delays growth and reduces tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu cassava ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha dalɛ asɛɛ afo ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to clear high soil mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the earth, so loose and raised soil mounds allow the roots to expand easily without hitting hard ground, resulting in larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the land where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmã yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like cowpeas fix nitrogen back into the soil naturally, restoring fertility for future crops.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛsaa nitrogen lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why is it risky to plant seeds immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni he hiaa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The early rain often cools only the surface while the deeper soil remains hot and dry. If a dry spell follows, newly germinated seeds will wither and die before true rains settle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei ahe loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on the sap and spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why should I keep my young tomato seedlings in a shaded nursery before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ awo he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are very delicate and can burn easily in direct sunlight. A shaded nursery acts like a protective care unit where you can give them extra water and attention until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe ni yɔɔ shia lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ he ko ni akwɛɔ gbekɛbii yɛ ni obaanyɛ oha amɛ nu kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: If I find a few sick plants with spots in my cassava field, why is it necessary to remove them from the farm immediately?
ga: Kɛji ona tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Diseased plants carry infections that easily spread to surrounding healthy crops through wind, rain, or insects. Removing and isolating sick plants prevents the illness from spreading and protects the yield of your whole farm.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ji helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo kooloi anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛ amɛ to he kroko lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa, ni ebaabu oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ ahe.

english: My maize leaves are turning pale yellow and look weak; can I bring them back to good health?
ga: Mi-abele baa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Ani manyɛ maha amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, pale yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying the right fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives weak plants the nourishment they need to regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt when I plant them out in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience shock when moved suddenly from a cool nursery to direct sunlight. You need to give them temporary shade, such as planting them next to plantains, until they adapt to full sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakpokpo kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni mli ejɔ mli kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ oha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ ni ooodu yɛ plantain tso ko masɛi, kɛyashi be mli ni ebaatsake ehe ewo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects attack weak crops more than healthy crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Healthy, well-fed plants have natural chemical defenses that resist insects. When a crop becomes weak from hunger or drought, its defenses drop, making it an easy target for pests.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ayeɔ amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni teɔ shi woɔ kooloi. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ loo hɔmɔ mli Buumɔ baa shi Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of crops every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when crops pull out nutrients harvest after harvest without rest. Leaving the land to rest or adding organic matter helps the soil regain its strength so it can produce good yields again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii ni amɛkpa yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛjɔɔɔɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe loo okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ewo yibii kpakpai ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off damaged or sick leaves from my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni efite loo hela emɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Damaged leaves waste the plant's water and energy while harboring diseases. Pruning them off allows the plantain tree to direct all its energy into growing large, healthy bunches of fruit.
ga: Baai ni efite lɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be kome too mli. kɛ helai srɔtoi ni abua naa lɛ Kpojiemɔ lɛ haa plantain lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and fail to produce big ears when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo toi wuji beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they struggle and compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough food to grow full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhe wuɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can my crops recover after wilting during a hot, dry spell if rain finally falls?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ naagbee lɛ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: If the roots are still alive, crops can recover from mild wilting once they get water. Watering allows the plant to pull up moisture, restore internal pressure, and resume healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo lɛ Tsei baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni amɛgboi lɛ mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ekɛ mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni edara ekoŋŋ

english: Why should I replace seedlings that died shortly after planting instead of waiting for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake dumɔwui ni gboi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi be ni baa lɛ mli

english: Replacing dead seedlings early ensures all plants grow at the same pace. This prevents weeds from taking over empty spaces and ensures you harvest the full amount of crops expected from your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni gboi mra lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei fɛɛ daa yɛ oyaiyeli kome mli. Enɛ baatsi jwɛi anaa koni ekahe hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua bo ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong sunlight directly. They require shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism maize uses to protect itself from heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil stays soaked with excess water for too long, it cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing rot and fungal diseases to set in.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers when their leaves receive maximum sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground to catch sunlight better and keeps the leaves dry, preventing soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water shortage. The plant sheds flowers as a survival choice to save energy and moisture for itself rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛhi shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ aha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei

english: Why does my maize field produce big green leaves but small cobs after applying a lot of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa agboi eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli babaoo efata he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Applying high amounts of nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus on growing stems and leaves. Without a proper balance of phosphorus and potassium, the plant lacks the right nutrients needed to develop large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack open on the vines right after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fãa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa trukaa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when there is a sudden abundance of water following a dry patch. The plant drinks up water very quickly, forcing the fruit inside to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi baagbala kɛji nu babaoo ho trukaa kɛtsɔ hei ni egbi lɛ anɔ. Tsei nuɔ nu oya waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli.

english: Why does my plantain tree bear small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hu?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its food into forming a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso nyɛ lɛ ni ekwɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my rows of maize help the maize grow healthier?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, sharing essential nutrients with the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ jaa nɔ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even if I give the field plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa ŋmɔji lɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients and water from the ground much faster than young crops can. They choke your crops underground by stealing the food meant for crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baanyɛ afee. Amɛfiteɔ onibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni tsei akwɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the early rains are settled enough for me to start planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ miibɔi nɛmɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: You should wait until you receive two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light shower is risky because a dry spell can follow and kill the sprouting seeds before they take root.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo pɛ sɛɛ lɛ dumɔ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ asɛɛ ni egbe amɛ dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to trap moisture and protect itself from intense heat. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is simply managing heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miitsu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he nii kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the bigger trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive their first few years because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a cool environment for the young roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa shishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but give me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen from overly rich soil or heavy shade, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing nutrients in their root tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo loo ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to attack my maize field suddenly overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths fly long distances at night and lay hundreds of eggs under crop leaves. When the eggs hatch at the same time, tiny caterpillars feed heavily all at once, making the damage look like it happened in a single night.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmei lɛ foɔ kɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ gbɛkɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai ashishi. Beni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baaye nii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Ehaa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ni efite lɛ ba yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛbaai dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Maintaining constant soil moisture helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my farmland produce less food every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with beans or legumes helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when there is a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants need water to transport nitrogen from the soil up into the leaves. During a drought, the plant moves nitrogen from its lower leaves to keep the upper, younger leaves alive, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkɛ nitrogen lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi kɛ bibii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ egbi kwraa dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines drying up early is usually caused by leaf spot fungi or microscopic worms called nematodes damaging the roots underground, which prevents water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. ni haa nu shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do my sweet potato plants keep spreading vines everywhere without producing big potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ gbɛɔ e-wein tsei lɛ eshwaa he fɛɛ he ni ekwɛɛɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes produce excess vines when the soil is too loose or has too much manure. Trimming excess vine growth helps redirect the plant's energy into expanding the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes baaha wain tsei babaoo aba kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Wein tso ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and thin when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When you plant too many seeds close together, the crops fight for the same space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for roots and leaves to spread out and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant more pepper seedlings on my plot, won't I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu pepper dumɔwui babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo?

english: Not necessarily. Overcrowding your farm causes crops to compete with each other, resulting in weak plants with few or small fruits. Giving plants proper space leads to healthier crops and a higher yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ mɛi eyi oŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ fe nine lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai fioo loo bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How close together can I plant my cassava without stopping the roots from growing big?
ga: Te manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he ni mihaaa shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: If cassava plants are placed too close, the tubers underground won't have enough room to expand. Leaving about one meter between plants gives the roots enough space to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji odu cassava ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ bɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Aaafee mita kome ni ka tsei ateŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants rot when the branches grow very thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: When branches grow too dense, fresh air cannot pass through the crop, trapping heat and moisture inside. Pruning extra leaves lets breeze flow through, keeping the plant dry and reducing diseases.
ga: Kɛji niji lɛ dara tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni emɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ mli Additional leaf pruning koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why should I leave vents or open sides on the roof shelter of my crop nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii loo fãi ni agbele yɛ mi-greenhouse lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: A nursery needs air circulation to prevent hot air from building up inside. Good airflow keeps the seedlings cool and strengthens their stems so they survive when transplanted to the main field.
ga: Greenhouses lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ akabua ehe naa yɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ewajeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ adu amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants during the hottest weeks of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants and causes them to shed flowers to conserve energy and water. Keeping air moving around the farm and keeping soil cool helps plants hold onto their blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni afeɔ lɛ bɔleɔ Fam lɛ he ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my crops in my plastic green shade house get moldy when I close all the sides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plastic shĩa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ miŋa fãi fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Closing all sides traps hot, moist air inside, creating conditions where fungal mold thrives. Leaving top or side openings allows hot air to escape so cool breeze can circulate.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋa lɛ yɛ efãi fɛɛ lɛ, ebaamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa. Ashiɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi loo afãi koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli. koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ anyɛ abɔle he

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh heat from the sun. Tall trees act like huge natural umbrellas, creating a cooler environment and protecting young plants from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry up quickly in the afternoon heat even after I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Direct hot sun heats up bare soil quickly, causing water to evaporate before roots can absorb it. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does leaving dry leaves on top of my farm beds really help my crops stay cool?
ga: Ani baai ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛhi shi fɛ̃i?

english: Yes, leaving dry plant material on top of the soil forms a protective blanket. It blocks direct hot sunlight, keeps the soil cool and moist, and breaks down into natural plant food over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe nibii ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the center or tips of older maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their green color and healthy growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ loo amɛnaagbee nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that damages maize fields across Ghana. They hide in the central funnel of the plant during the daytime and eat leaves at night, but applying recommended pest treatments early in the morning or late evening controls them effectively.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai gbɛkɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and growing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties provided by agricultural extension officers prevents this problem from destroying your yield.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okwaayeli mli nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ duɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni naagba nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly while resting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mijɔɔ mihe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they were cut or bruised during harvest or if stored in a hot, damp area. Storing undamaged yams on raised, airy wooden racks in a shaded barn keeps them dry and extends their shelf life.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Atomɔ ni mli tse ni akɛtoɔ tso adekai ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shade mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa egbiɔ ni ehaa esɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to cocoa seedlings provides living shade umbrellas that keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and humid weather. Pruning heavy shade trees to allow sunlight in, clearing infected pods, and applying fungicide protects the healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la abote mli Afɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when weather gets too hot, water supply is uneven, or there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant set fruits successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and dropping their leaves early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni egbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Stunted pepper plants with falling leaves often suffer from root damage caused by flooded soil or microscopic soil pests. Planting peppers on raised ridges or mounds improves water drainage and helps roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ elaaje lɛ naa shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he amanehulu. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots fight for nutrients and water while their leaves shade each other from sunlight. Following proper plant spacing gives every crop enough room and light to produce full yields.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha yibiiwoo ni fa aba.

english: Why do my crop leaves look wilted even when the ground is full of water after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: When soil stays soaked for too long, roots drown because they cannot get oxygen, making them unable to pump water up to the leaves. Digging drainage furrows helps drain excess rainwater away from root zones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ajie nu awo baai lɛ anɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing cocoa trees with the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Officer, is it harmful if I burn the bush on my land before planting my crops?
ga: Ofisa Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji mishã jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter in the topsoil, kills helpful organisms like earthworms, and dries out the soil. Clearing land without burning allows the plant matter to rot and act as free fertilizer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbo ni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food green leaves need to grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa baai eŋɔli lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating holes in the middle of my maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa teŋ lɛ? Ni powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying approved crop protection treatments directly into the center funnel of the leaves early in the morning or late in the evening helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?
