english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended by the agricultural office is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that produce bigger tubers underground when their leaves get full sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, maximizing sun exposure while preventing rot from damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ amɛtso lɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Na hulu la babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ naa.

english: My tomato plants are producing flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced fertilizer helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper field under the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper ŋmɔji lɛ amli nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Watering during the hottest part of the day causes the water to evaporate quickly before the plant roots can soak it up.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why is my rice crop growing very weakly even though I applied fertilizer on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli yɛ be naa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young rice and steal the fertilizer, light, and water from the soil. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks after planting ensures the rice gets full access to the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmãa, la kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ náa niyenii kpakpa.

english: How do I know the exact time my groundnuts are ready to be harvested from underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and dry up. You can also dig up a sample pod; if the inside of the shell has dark brown markings and the seeds fill out the shell completely, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ pods nɔkwɛmɔnɔ hu atsu nii. Kɛji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water when the heat is high. It is a natural defense mechanism that helps the plant save internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves to survive drought. By dropping leaves, the plant reduces water loss and goes into a resting state, keeping its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli. Kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive a sudden surge of water after a dry spell, the inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso yibii lɛ loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing indicates a nitrogen deficiency. Maize moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support as pods. The tree sheds unpollinated or weak flowers so it can conserve energy to grow healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ ŋmeii amli. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen loo ni bɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and makes their pollen inactive. To save water and energy, the plant drops the unfertilized flowers instead of trying to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ tsuuu nii. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni awoko mli lɛ kpo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I let them crawl on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji miha amɛkplekeshi shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baawo ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight so they can catch maximum light to make food for the tubers underground. Vines left on the ground shade themselves and produce less food.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli bɔni afee ni amɛná la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo.

english: Why does my plantain shoot grow so many extra suckers around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi babaoo ni ebɔle amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally produce suckers to reproduce. However, if you leave all of them, they will fight for nutrients, which leads to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Plantains baawo ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛfɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji oshɛrɛ amɛ fɛɛ oshwie lɛ, Amɛbaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha plantain lɛ afee bibioo.

english: Why do the tips of my rice leaves turn rusty brown when water stays on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Stagnant water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing iron built up in the soil to become toxic to the plant, which turns the leaf tips brown.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dade ni ebua naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni gbeɔ tsei. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when there is no shade around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living canopy cover that protects the tender leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Guiding the vines up stakes lifts the leaves off the ground, allowing them to catch maximum sunlight and preventing fungal diseases from soil splashes.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ tso ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa wain tsei lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shwiemɔ mli baa lɛ anaa

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for the same limited water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil, leaving all of them weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants need to produce chlorophyll, build strong stems, and stay dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni tsei kɛtsu nii koni amɛkɛfee klorofil Feemɔ tso ni mli wa ni ehiɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomatoes with dry grass help them grow better in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomatoi ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with organic material like dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from stealing moisture from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju nu ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Heavy rainfall washes away applied fertilizer before the plant roots can absorb it, wasting your investment and carrying the nutrients off into streams or deep underground out of reach.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. Excess water filling the air pockets in the soil suffocates the roots, allowing bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine ni akɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any pepper fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience sudden stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or overly wet conditions, as a self-defense mechanism to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu hewalɛ he

english: Why do I find small caterpillars hidden inside the rolled leaves at the top of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants because it provides a soft, sheltered place with tender tissue for them to feed away from birds and heat.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eji he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ he ko ni akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli koni amɛkaye nii kɛjɛ okpoi kɛ latsaa lɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in high numbers in your soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ pɛ. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a natural leafy canopy that shields them from scorching heat and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a much bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, crowding seeds causes crops to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small or empty cobs. Giving each seed proper spacing allows individual plants to grow healthy and yield larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni fa babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tso fɛɛ tso adara ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make food and stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛhooɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these plants finish growing, they leave that extra nitrogen in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ dara lɛ Eshiɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do many farmers spread dry grass and fallen leaves around the base of their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo gbɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ? Pepper tso shishi?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plants experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting flowers nearby to attract bees helps fruits form successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ fɔfɔii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni egbala ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting if they are underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants show they are ready when their bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack open from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Yucca tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ bulb ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant garden eggs or tomatoes in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui kɛji midu abɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly in one spot allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil year after year. Rotating with different crops like maize or cassava breaks the life cycle of those pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaafite nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that adapt very quickly to local soil and are aggressive at stealing water, sunlight, and plant food before your cultivated crops can get to them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get those nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake oya kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nakai niyenii lɛ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to withstand local plant diseases, endure dry spells, and produce high and uniform yields, whereas saved seeds weaken over generations and produce smaller crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow strong and green. This often happens when continuous planting exhausts the soil or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ dumɔwui ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the rain to moisten the soil before applying fertilizer to my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ koni ekɛ sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dry soil cannot dissolve fertilizer, which means plant roots cannot drink it in. Placing fertilizer on dry ground can also burn and destroy plant roots; water helps dilute and transport the food safely to the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nyɛŋ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi. Nu haa niyenii mli shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ niyenii yaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli shweshweeshwe.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize help my soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume plants like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why is my cassava growing plenty of tall leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are placed too close together, cassava focuses all its energy on growing top leaves instead of storing food below. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to direct energy down into bigger roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo akɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ he moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishi. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkudɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Does planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Nibii ni miduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ mihe lɛ haa minine shɛɔ nibii babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants and smaller yields. Giving each crop its recommended distance allows every plant to grow full and produce maximum yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akatse tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ aha lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cold, dark, and wet conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches and clearing weeds lets in sunlight and airflow, keeping the farm dry enough to prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and getting twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are often a sign of damage from tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or a reaction to extreme sun heat and drought. Controlling pest insects early and using mulch to cover the soil helps prevent this stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni hiɛ tsei amli helai lɛ efite. aloo nɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli Mra Be mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe Ni kɛji akɛ akɛ mulch tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or pest attacks like thrips. When a plant gets too dry or hot, it intentionally sheds flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ thrips, baatutua tso lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Tsei baajɛ amɛtsui mli amɛfo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines wilt and dry up after heavy floods even when the ground is full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbo ni amɛgbi yɛ nu afua ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu po?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like they need water. When water stays pooled around roots for too long, they drown and rot, leaving the plant unable to pump water up to the vine, which causes it to wilt and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaagbo ni ebaagbo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛyashɛ wain tso lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant on my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Select maiden suckers that have narrow, sword-like leaves and a broad, firm base free of hole marks or rotted spots. Avoid suckers with wide, flat leaves or damaged roots, as they carry pests and disease into your fresh land.
ga: Halamɔ tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse, tamɔ klante kɛ shishi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni bu loo hei ni fiteɔ bɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishifãi ni efite lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kɛyaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly if I leave them in the hot sun on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight drastically raises the internal temperature of tomatoes, which speeds up decay, causes soft spots, and leads to fast water loss. Keeping harvested tomatoes in a cool, shaded area slows down spoilage and keeps them firm for market.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ aya hiɛ waa. ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya lɛ kɛ he ko ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni ehaa nu fiteɔ oya Kɛ́ akɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha efitemɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo ni eye ebua ni tomato lɛ ahi shi koni akɛya jara.

english: Why do my newly transplanted vegetable seedlings wither and die when direct sunlight hits them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender roots that cannot absorb groundwater fast enough to replace the water lost through their leaves in intense heat. Providing temporary shade gives their roots time to establish so they can handle bright sunlight.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛto nu ni laajeɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ha shishifãi lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛma shi bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nii.

english: How can I prevent my harvested plantains from ripening too fast while waiting for buyers in the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain lɛ naa koni akakpa mra tsɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heat and direct sunlight cause plantains to release ethylene gas rapidly, which speeds up softening and spoilage. Keeping harvested bunches under thick shade or covering them with fresh palm fronds keeps them cool and extends their green shelf life.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ethylene gas lɛ jeɔ kpo oya. ni haa efeɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi loo akɛ tsei ahe baai heei ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni eha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my soft fruits like mangoes get rotten by the time the transport truck reaches the city market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ mango lɛ fiteɔ kɛ akɛtee maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Rough transport and heavy stacking squeeze and shake the fruit, causing internal bruising that breaks the skin barrier. Packing fruit gently in rigid crates with soft padding prevents physical damage and keeps decay from setting in.
ga: Gbɛfaa ni mli wa kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ni tsii, ni akɛmiimiɔ kɛ tso yibii lɛ ni akpokpoɔ lɛ kɛ mligbɛ fãji ni fiteɔ hewolo nɔ gbɛtsii nii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai wo adekai ni wa ni akɛ tsɔne ni yɔɔ blɛoo wo mli lɛ amli blɛoo lɛ, ebaatsi gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ naa, ni ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: How should I lay down and pack my yam tubers in a vehicle so they do not break during transit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawɔ ni mikɛ sweet potato ŋmeii awo tsɔne mli? Enɛ ji koni akakumɔ ŋmeii lɛ beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Yam tubers snap easily when stacked loosely or subjected to hard bumps on rough roads. Laying them flat in organized layers on a soft bed of dry grass or straw absorbs vibrations and protects the growing tips from snapping.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe shi loo atswa amɛ waa yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi yɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi saatso ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋhosomɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tsei niji anaagbee lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers go bad within two days after digging them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii 2 mli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava tubers suffer from rapid oxidation and moisture loss because their protective outer skin is damaged. Processing them immediately or storing them buried in moist sawdust blocks air exposure and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, oksideshin kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ yaa oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni buɔ ehe lɛ efite. Kɛ́ atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo akɛto ŋmei ni mli efɔ mli lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he, ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my stored maize to spoil and develop mold inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa mi-nitoohe lɛ mli?

english: Trapped heat combined with remaining moisture creates an ideal environment for fungi and mold to grow on stored grains. Thoroughly drying maize in thin layers until the kernels are hard before storing them in ventilated sacks prevents mold growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baakwɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ nɔ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa bibioo mli. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto kotoku ko mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa beans turn dark and smell bad if I stack them too thick while drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe tsɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Piling cocoa beans too deeply traps moisture and excess heat underneath, causing them to rot rather than dry properly. Spreading beans thinly on raised drying mats allows heat to escape and air to circulate freely for high-quality cocoa.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni ato he shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine yɛ shishi. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbi jogbaŋŋ. Kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ agbɛɛmɔ bibii bibii Nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ haa dɔlɛ jeɔ kpo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa he fɛɛ he koni aná kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my stored crop seeds so hot weather does not spoil them before planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ akafite amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aba?

english: High temperatures weaken the living embryo inside a seed, drastically reducing its ability to sprout. Storing seeds in airtight containers kept in a dark, cool corner of the house protects their vitality until planting time.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Hewalɛ ni dumɔwui yɔɔ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ shia lɛ mli he ko ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi be ni abaadu lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout and emerge from the soil during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ waaa ni ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds require a steady balance of soil moisture and moderate temperatures to trigger germination. If the soil surface becomes baked and overheated by the sun, the tender embryo inside the seed dries out and dies before it can break through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni eha amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulu lɛ shã lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant my crops in a low-lying swampy land where water sits all year round?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ jɛmɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting directly in stagnant wet land can rot plant roots. You need a system that allows you to control when water enters and leaves the field so the crops get moisture without drowning.
ga: Dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ehe miihia ni oná gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni baaha onyɛ okudɔ be mli ni nu boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ koni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkabote nu mli.

english: Why is it important for me to be able to turn my water supply on and off when farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni manyɛ matswa nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni magbe kɛ́ miitsu okwaayeli he nii lɛ?

english: Crops need different amounts of water at different stages of growth. Having full control over water flow prevents overwatering during sensitive periods and ensures plants get water exactly when they need it.
ga: Tsei biɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ bei ni mli wa mli lɛ anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu kɛ́ ehe miihia amɛ

english: Does the time of day I release water onto my farm make a difference to crop growth?
ga: Ani gbi lɛ mli be ni mijieɔ nu kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering during the cooler morning or late afternoon reduces water loss through evaporation caused by the hot sun, allowing roots to soak up more moisture effectively.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ leebi ni mli ejɔ loo shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long can my crops stay submerged in heavy water before they start dying?
ga: Be enyiɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baanyɛ ahi nu kpakpa mli dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi?

english: Most common crops begin to suffer root damage within 24 to 48 hours of standing in unmanaged water because the flooded soil loses air and starves the roots of oxygen.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛdamɔ nu ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: What simple tests or observations should I do on my field before deciding to plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafee kaa loo nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo? Mɛni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpɛɔ miyiŋ akɛ madu?

english: You should observe how water moves across the land after rain, check if the soil holds too much water, and confirm if you can easily drain or direct water where you want it.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni nu tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Ni okwɛ kɛji abaanyɛ ajie nu lɛ oya loo abaanyɛ atsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ kɛya he ni ataoɔ lɛ.

english: Is land that floods during the heavy rainy season good for planting tree crops?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Ani ehi kɛha tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Most tree crops dislike standing water around their stems. If you use land prone to flooding, you must build drainage trenches or raised mounds to protect the young trees.
ga: Tsei babaoo sumɔɔɔ nu ni damɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu afua nyɛɔ eshɛɔ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, Esa akɛ ofee nu homɔ tsɔne loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni okɛbu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to make a field plan before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo dani ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Planning ahead helps you prepare proper drainage channels, position your water sources, and set clear timelines so you do not lose crops to sudden flooding or dry spells.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni ooofee kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni osaa gbɛ ni sa ni nu lɛ baatsɔ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ he ni nu lɛ jɛɔ lɛ ni okɛ be ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ato Bɔni afee ni nu afua loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ akafite onibii.

english: How do earth bunds or raised ridges help me control soil moisture on wet land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Raised ridges keep crop roots safely elevated above standing water while earth bunds allow you to trap or release water as needed, protecting plants from root rot.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ woɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe. yɛ be mli ni gɔji lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ nu loo ojieɔ lɛ bɔ ni he hiaa. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from too much soil water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miina nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When soil has too much water, crop leaves usually turn pale or yellow, growth stops, and the plant stem may feel weak because the submerged roots cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. dalɛ kpaa Ni tsei ahe tsei lɛ baanyɛ anu he akɛ amɛgbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why can't I keep my vegetable crop flooded constantly like a rice field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ anyɛɛɛ nu atsɔ aduawai anɔ be fɛɛ be tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Unlike rice, most vegetables do not have specialized stems that carry air underwater. Continuous flooding suffocates vegetable roots, causing the plants to decay quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ, aduawai babaoo bɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yaa nu shishi. Nu afua ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: What should I do when my maize farm yields much more grain than my family and local buyers can take at once?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni miweku lɛ kɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afee yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Having a surplus is good, but excess grain spoils quickly if left exposed. Drying the grain thoroughly to a low moisture level and storing it in airtight hermetic bags prevents mold and weevils, allowing you to hold the grain safely and sell it later when market prices rise.
ga: Nɔ ni fa fe nine ni ooona lɛ ji nɔ ni hi. Shi ŋmaa ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi ni akɛto vacuum kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli. Ehaa okɛ odumɔwui lɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ jara lɛ nɔ wa.

english: Why do produce buyers sometimes refuse to buy my harvested crops even when they look big to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahe mikpamɔ lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara kɛha mi.

english: Market buyers look at crop quality standards, not just size. They reject crops that have hidden insect holes, high moisture content, or signs of mold, because those issues cause the produce to spoil quickly during transport or storage.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ susuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe mlai ahe. Jeee bɔ ni edara ha lɛ pɛ he ewieɔ. Amɛkpooɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. hulutsoo babaoo loo eyɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela Yɛ nakai naagbai lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛyaa he kroko loo akɛtoɔ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cassava plants turn yellow and start curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves are usually a sign of insect damage or cassava mosaic disease, which prevents the plant from using sunlight to make food, resulting in stunted growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii efite loo yucca mosaic hela. Enɛ tsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkɛ hulu la akafee niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them, causing the plant to conserve energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii haaa tsei lɛ afee pollination Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my yam leaves roll up and look limp during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Yam plants roll up their leaves during hot afternoon hours to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava and maize seeds very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Crowding crops forces them to compete underground for soil nutrients and water, while above ground they block sunlight from one another, causing both crops to grow weak and yield less harvest.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshi akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Beni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do crops like cowpea or groundnut help improve the soil for my next farm season?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha mikwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer for the crops you plant next.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: The soil is ready when the major rainy season begins steadily and the ground stays moist at least a few inches deep, ensuring seeds get enough continuous moisture to sprout without drying out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee klalo beni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi daa lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo, kɛ hoo lɛ, elɛɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do tiny insects appear inside my bagged grain even when I tie the bags tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Koni amɛje kpo yɛ mi dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ amli Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay microscopic eggs inside the grain while it is still in the field. If the grain is not dried well before bagging, those eggs hatch inside the warm bag; using airtight hermetic bags cuts off their oxygen supply so they cannot survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaa mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko dani awo amɛ kotoku mli Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my crops from dying during the hot lean season before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani kpamɔ lɛ aba?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried leaves or straw, known as mulching, holds moisture in the ground and protects roots from severe heat, helping plants survive dry periods until the main rains arrive.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ titri lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow early in the season before making any ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or cannot absorb nutrients due to poor water flow. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early helps the leaves stay dark green and support strong ear development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can watering my vegetable crops during the hot midday sun harm them?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, midday watering causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can absorb it, and hot soil temperatures combined with water can stress the roots. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane.

english: Will my crops give me more food if I plant a lot of seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: No, overcrowding forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow fully and yield much more.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What makes cassava roots grow large and heavy in some fields while staying small and thin in others?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsii yɛ shikpɔji komɛi anɔ, yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ ekrokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil and potassium to expand. Planting in hard, unplowed soil or crowding plants together prevents the roots from swelling into large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ potassium koni amɛshwere. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo adu tsei yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu ni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when air temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Regular watering and light shading can keep flowers attached to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi tamɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the field where I just harvested my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil richness for the next planting cycle.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even when I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting ensures all nutrition goes straight to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they transmit. Spraying early with a gentle soapy water mixture or neem oil helps control these insects before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I store my harvested maize so insects do not destroy it after a bountiful season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii akafite lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize must be dried in the sun until the grains are completely hard before storage. Storing dry grains in sealed airtight bags or mixing them with clean wood ash stops weevils from multiplying and destroying your yield.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa dani abaanyɛ akɛto. Nibii ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli loo akɛ tso sũ ni he tse futuɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafee babaoo ni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same field as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Plantains have big leaves that lose water very fast in severe heat. Yellowing is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss when the soil is dry, but applying mulch around the roots helps retain ground moisture.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba. Saffron ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: How do I harvest cocoyam leaves for nkontomire without killing the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ akpa kookoo baai koni mikɛdu nkontomire ni migbeee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You should only cut the older, outer leaves of the cocoyam plant and leave at least three or four healthy inner leaves so the plant can continue making food and growing tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ asɛɛ baai lɛ pɛ. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shi mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3-4 koni kookoo tso lɛ afee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs heei.

english: Does it matter which direction I bury cassava stem cuttings when planting them in my farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei niji yɛ mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, you should always plant cassava stems with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can sprout easily and grow upright into the sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu o-cassava tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdara shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out in the sunshine. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant makes to grow big yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ náa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil suddenly becomes very dry, causing the plant stress so it drops flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa trukaa lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni egbeeɔ shi koni ebu ehe.

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which prefer feeding on the tender leaves inside the funnel of young maize plants. Catching them early and treating the center of the plant stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji asraafoi akui ni egbee shi. ni sumɔɔ ni eye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ Amɔmɔ amɛ mra ni ekwɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the land where I usually grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã daa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: What is the benefit of covering the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, stops soil water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli beni sũ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. Applying it to dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money because the plant cannot absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ.

english: How long can my young mango trees survive if the rains stop for a few weeks in Northern Ghana?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ mi mango tso lɛ baahi shi?

english: Young mango trees are fairly tough, but extended dry spells lasting around 21 days to a month can severely reduce their survival rate if they are not well established or watered.
ga: Mango tso lɛ mli wa jogbaŋŋ lolo. Shi hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni ji gbii 21 kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome lɛ baanyɛ aha wala yibiiwoo aba shi kwraa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ahaaa amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does a long dry spell of up to two months affect mango seedling survival rates?
ga: Te nyɔji enyɔ hɔmɔ ni baa lɛ saa bɔ ni mango dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi amɛhaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A dry period lasting up to two months drastically reduces seedling survival rates, as the heat and lack of soil moisture cause young trees to dry out completely unless protected.
ga: Be ni hulu enyɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ashihilɛ baa shi kwraa. Yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei bibii baanyɛ agbi kwraa ja abu amɛhe.

english: Why do crops in the transition zone of Ghana suffer when there is a sudden break in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana tsakemɔ he lɛ naa amanehulu kɛ́ amɛkumɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When rain stops for three weeks or more during the growing season, topsoil moisture evaporates quickly, causing crops to wilt because their young roots cannot reach deep groundwater.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ otsii etɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Is it normal for mango trees in Northern Ghana to drop leaves when it doesn't rain for two months?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mango tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji enyɔ?

english: Yes, shedding leaves is a natural survival trick mango trees use to reduce water loss through their foliage during severe dry spells lasting several weeks.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni mango tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni yeɔ otsii babaoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do trees survive dry periods better in the transition zone than in the far northern region of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei yeɔ wala yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsakemɔ he lɛ fe Ghana kooyigbɛ hei lɛ?

english: The transition zone usually has higher humidity and better soil moisture retention than the far north, giving young trees a slightly better chance of enduring long periods without rain.
ga: Tsakemɔ hei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni fa babaoo ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe kooyigbɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa hegbɛ fioo ni amɛdamɔ shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if my irrigation equipment breaks down and spare parts take weeks to arrive?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mi-nu-shwiemɔ nibii lɛ fite ni nɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ he otsii babaoo dani ebashɛ?

english: Waiting weeks for replacement parts during dry periods leaves crops without water for 21 days or more, which can lead to severe crop failure or stunted growth.
ga: Otsii babaoo ni akɛbaamɛ koni akɛtsake nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaná nu gbii 21 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite waa loo amɛdalɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important to fix my farm machinery long before the dry season begins in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa miŋmɔ mli tsɔnei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Spare parts can take a long time to deliver to remote rural areas, and any delay during a dry spell can mean missing the critical window to water crops and save them.
ga: Efãi lɛ baanyɛ ahe be babaoo dani akɛya akrowai ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli. kɛ sɛɛkuu fɛɛ sɛɛkuu Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ enɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ samflɛ ko ni he hiaa waa ni akɛbaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu ni akɛbaahere mɛi awala lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I help my young mango trees survive a 21-day dry spell without rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi mango tso lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ gbii 21 ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: You can place thick grass mulch around the base of the trees and provide temporary artificial shade to trap moisture in the soil and slow down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ awo mli. Ebɔle tsei lɛ ashishi ni eha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ nu ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ atsu nii.

english: Can I plant mango trees in Northern Ghana even though the region gets very dry?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mango tso yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ jɛmɛ egbi waa moŋ?

english: Yes, mangoes are well-suited for Northern Ghana, but you must plan for supplemental watering and protection during their first dry season to ensure good survival rates.
ga: Hɛɛ, mango hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha Ghana Kooyigbɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni oto nu kɛ hebuu kroko he gbɛjianɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ wala yibii kpakpai baahi shi.

english: How do I know if my fruit trees are dying from heat stress or just resting during dry periods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ miigboi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ hewɔ loo amɛmiijɔɔ amɛhe kɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Heat-stressed trees show scorched leaf tips, severe drooping, and stem drying that does not recover even during cooler night hours, signaling that the tree's survival is in danger.
ga: Tsei ni hulutsoo haoɔ amɛ lɛ baaná baai lɛ ashã. shwiemɔ ni mli wa kɛ tsei ni egbi ni nyɛɛɛ atsake yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli po lɛ. Okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ wala yɛ oshara mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Keeping or planting taller trees like plantains or shade trees protects young cocoa from sunburn, cools the soil, and holds moisture in the ground until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantain loo shia tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. sũ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow healthy, dark green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa. baai ni tsuɔ waa

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away off your land before the plant roots have time to drink it. This wastes your money and can contaminate nearby streams without helping your crops grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baatsumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛnu. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaanyɛ efite faai ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ni eyeee ebuaaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts on my land makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has a special natural ability to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving rich natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo amɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up to collect maximum sunlight for growing big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet ground, protecting the plant from fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbua hulu la ni fa babaoo naa kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: If too many shoots grow from the same plantain root, they steal food, water, and light from each other. Removing extra shoots so that only two or three remain allows the main tree to yield big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni jɛɔ plantain kome shishifãi amli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is continuous heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When excessive rainwater stays logged on the farm for too long, it drowns the roots, causing ground fungi and bacteria to attack and rot the cassava.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ nu babaoo buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmei lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or straw, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from intense sun heat, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before growing into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high soil heat, dry weather, or lack of water. Giving the plants consistent water during dry periods helps them keep their flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo he haomɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. nu ni mli egbi loo nu ni faaa Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants and eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets maize. They crawl inside the funnel-shaped center of the plant where leaves are soft to feed, which can severely stunt or kill the maize if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa. Amɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni tamɔ cone, ni yɔɔ baai bibii kɛha niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii waa loo egbe ŋmãa lɛ po kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain standing on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain sits on your farm, it fills all the small air spaces in the soil. Plant roots need air to breathe, and without it, they stop taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which turns the leaves yellow and slows down growth.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, ebaakpa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater gets trapped in the soil, it creates a wet environment where fungi and bacteria thrive, causing the tubers to soften and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall wash away the good soil from my land?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fast-falling rain droplets hit bare soil like small hammers, breaking the soil into loose particles. When water accumulates and flows over your land, it carries away this loose topsoil, which contains the rich nutrients your crops need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ oya lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ hama bibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli agbá bibii bibii. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa ni eho kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse ehe ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo ni he hiaa otsei lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can covering my soil with dry grass or leaves protect my crops from heavy rain damage?
ga: Ani jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite?

english: Yes, putting a layer of dry grass or leaves (mulch) around your crops breaks the heavy impact of falling raindrops, prevents topsoil from washing away, and helps excess water sink into the ground smoothly.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ahe lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli wa lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ naa koni ekaho. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my crops on raised mounds instead of flat ground in rainy areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Planting on raised mounds or ridges lifts the roots above standing water, allowing heavy rain to collect in the lower furrows instead of drowning your plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ woɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ abua naa yɛ shishigbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha tsei lɛ atsɔ nu mli.

english: How do simple channels or ditches help save my farm from rainwater flooding?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni nubu loo nubu bibioo ko ahere miŋmɔ lɛ yiwala kɛjɛ nu afua mli?

english: Ditches act like clear pathways for water. Digging shallow channels around and through your field directs heavy rainwater away from your crops before it can pool up and cause damage.
ga: Nubu tsuɔ nii tamɔ nu gbɛ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ otsa nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni obɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe ni otsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani ebaabɔle ohe ni efite nii.

english: What kind of crops can I grow on land that gets easily flooded during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like rice and cocoyam naturally tolerate high levels of water and flooded soil, whereas crops like peppers, cassava, and maize will quickly rot and die in waterlogged conditions.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ adamɔ nu ni fa babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ chili, cassava kɛ ŋmãa fiteɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can physically wash away pollen, prevent bees from visiting flowers, and cause cold water stress to roots, forcing the plant to drop its flowers before fruits can grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ. Tsi ŋmeii ni baasara fɔfɔi lɛ anaa ni ekɛ haomɔ baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ajie efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewo yibii.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater sweeps across the surface of the soil and washes away loose fertilizer before your crops can absorb it, wasting your money and time.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ofiteɔ shika kɛ be.

english: Why do dark spots and diseases spread quickly on my crop leaves after long periods of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain keeps leaves wet and creates high humidity, which is the perfect environment for plant disease spores to grow and splash from leaf to leaf.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baa. Enɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛshwere kɛjɛ baa kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Why do all my maize plants ripen at the exact same time, making it difficult for me to harvest everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ makpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome.

english: Crops of the same seed variety naturally follow the same biological timeline when planted together under the same weather conditions. To avoid having too much ripe crop at once, you can practice staggered planting by sowing seeds in batches a few weeks apart.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwu kome lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ be kome kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ shihilɛ kome mli. Enɛ ji koni tsei babaoo akakwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli. Obaanyɛ okase dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ he nii kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ kui amli ni otsii fioo komɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop plants produce plenty of leafy green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ miiwo lɛ?

english: Excess green leaves with low fruiting usually happen when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer and lacks phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen encourages leaf expansion, while phosphorus and potassium trigger flowering and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai eŋɔli ni fa fe nine ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni phosphorus loo potassium hu bɛ mli lɛ. Nitrogen haa baa lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium haa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai feɔ lɛ.

english: Vegetable crops drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Supplying steady water during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Aduawai tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain bunches remain small even when the plant stems look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains form small bunches when too many sucker shoots grow around the main plant and steal its water and food. Pruning excess suckers leaves the main stem with enough energy to build larger bunches.
ga: Plantains baabua amɛhe naa amɛfee jwɛi bibii. Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso wulu lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ panicle agbo.

english: Why do market traders offer me lower prices when I harvest a huge amount of produce at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi haa mi jara ni baa shi kɛ́ mikpa nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest abundant crops at the same time, the market becomes flooded with produce. High supply causes crop prices to fall, while selling early or storing crops to sell when supply drops gets you better prices.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Jarayelihe lɛ eyi kɛ nibii ni aduɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi. Yɛ be mli ni ohɔ̃ɔ mra loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii toɔ koni ohɔ̃ɔ beni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ ba shi lɛ haa onine shɛɔ jara kpakpa nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch as they mature, but if left in the soil past their peak maturity, the plant converts that starch into tough structural fibers, making the tubers hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ starch be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishitoo ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ wa ni ewa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when I keep them at home before taking them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto shia dani mikɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fully ripe tomatoes release moisture and natural gases that speed up decay, especially in warm room temperatures. Harvesting tomatoes when they start turning pinkish-orange and storing them in a cool, ventilated place slows down spoilage.
ga: Tomato ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ tsu mli latsaa mli. Tomatoi ni akpaa beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinkish-orange su Ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting and shrinking in my barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that naturally wake up and sprout when the rainy season approaches. The tuber shrinks because it uses its stored moisture and energy to grow sprouts, which should be snapped off early to keep the yam firm.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji bɔɔ nii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Bulbs lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Esa akɛ ajie enɛ kɛjɛ mli mra. Koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ
