english: How can I store my harvested maize at home so that insects do not destroy the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato shia? Bɔni afee ni kooloi akafite dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weevils and insects thrive on damp grain. Sun-drying your harvested maize until the grains are completely hard and storing them in airtight bags or treated storage bins prevents insects from multiplying and destroying your crop.
ga: Weevils kɛ kooloi bibii yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa ni okɛwo vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ŋtayaai ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops dry up and die rapidly as soon as the pods are full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops naturally complete their life cycle once their seeds mature. The plant stops feeding its leaves and directs all remaining nutrients into the seed pods, causing the foliage to dry up for harvest.
ga: Legumes gbeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ naa beni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ. Tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ koni akpa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo afee nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between saving seed from my last harvest and buying certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, withstand dry weather, and produce uniform, high yields. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni fa babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: If I want to try a new hybrid crop variety on my farm, should I plant my entire field with it at once?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni maka tsei heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ akwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani esa akɛ madu jɛmɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: It is always safer to test a new crop variety on a small portion of your land first. This allows you to observe how well it handles your local soil and climate without risking your entire harvest and food supply.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ oooka tso hee ko okwɛ yɛ otso lɛ fã bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ eha. ni okɛ okpamɔ kɛ oniyenii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why should I space my corn seeds far apart instead of putting many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-kooloi lɛ amli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Crops need enough space to drink water, gather sunlight, and feed on soil nutrients. Planting too close forces the crops to fight each other, resulting in tall, thin stalks with tiny, undeveloped ears.
ga: Tsei taoɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛnu nu, amɛbua hulu la naa, ni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe awuu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii ni edarako lɛ baa.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my corn leaves and dark dirt inside the plant funnels?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing center of the maize plant. Spraying safe, recommended pesticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in stages: give a starter dose near the roots about two weeks after sprouting when roots form, and apply a second dose when the plant reaches knee-height to support rapid growth and fruiting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli: Okɛ shishijee nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo shishifãi lɛ ahe aaafee otsi enyɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛnaji ahe lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my maize is fully ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is mature when the leaves and husks turn dry and brown, and the silks at the top turn dark. You can also press a grain with your thumbnail; if it is firm and leaves a small dent without squeezing out milky liquid, it is ready.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ duŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ oshishifã lɛ hu anyɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ewa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni okɛ mliki lɛ shwieee mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and lets pests build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni oha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield even if I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds during the first four to six weeks of growth gives your crops the strength they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop whitish powder and insects after keeping it in storage for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ powda yɛŋ kɛ kooloi bibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects and white mold appear when grain is stored before it is completely dry. Moisture allows mold and weevils to multiply, so drying corn thoroughly on clean tarpaulins until grains are hard before storing them in airtight bags protects your harvest.
ga: Kplukai yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui to dani amɛgbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I invite an agricultural officer to inspect my land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ̃ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko nine koni ebakwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: An agricultural expert inspects your soil, slope, and land condition to guide you on proper row layout and seed spacing. This prevents costly mistakes like poor germination or having to uproot and replant your entire field later.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi baakwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ, ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛ mli koni amɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni sa akɛ ato line kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tɔmɔi ni jara wa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ni ehe baahia ni ajie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How does getting my farm land checked by an expert before planting save me money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani edu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shika akafite?

english: Land assessment ensures you use the right planting methods and seed varieties for your soil type from the start, saving you from wasting expensive seeds, fertilizer, and labor on crops that fail to sprout properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shishijee. Enɛ haaa ofite dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsumɔ ni jara wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my seeds sprout weakly or fail to come up evenly across my farm after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo loo amɛkwɛ̃ɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout evenly if they are buried too deep, planted in overly compacted soil, or lack proper moisture. Getting the right planting depth and soil preparation ensures all seeds get the oxygen and water needed to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ loo hulutsoo ni sa bɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds rot in the ground before they even get the chance to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛná hegbɛ po ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted in poorly drained soil that traps too much water, suffocating the seed. Proper land assessment helps identify drainage problems so you can prepare raised beds or mounds before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua ni ana naagbai ni kɔɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he koni onyɛ osaa osɛɛ loo gɔŋ lɛ dani odu.

english: What causes my young crop sprouts to turn yellow and wither shortly after coming out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Newly emerged sprouts wither if the soil lacks essential nutrients, is too acidic, or harbors hidden soil pests. Checking the soil health beforehand helps you apply the right organic matter or fertilizer to support young growth.
ga: Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ acid tsɔ. aloo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii koni eye ebua gbekɛbii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing so crowded that I have to pull them up and plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle mihe waa aahu akɛ esa akɛ majie amɛ ni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds without measured spacing causes crops to overcrowd, competing for sunlight and soil nutrients. Correctly lining your field before planting eliminates the need to uproot overgrown plants later.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ bɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ fe nine. Atswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fɔ shi jogbaŋŋ dani odu lɛ, no haa ehe ehiaaa ni ojie tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is my neighbor getting a much bigger yield even though we planted the exact same crops at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa nibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ nibii komekomei yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Higher yields depend on proper field alignment, correct seed depth, and optimal spacing, which give each plant maximum light and nutrients. Expert layout advice helps turn identical seeds into a much richer harvest.
ga: Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli ni nɔ kwɔ damɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kpakpa nɔ. dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ ni ja kɛ he ni sa Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii babaoo. He nilelɔi ŋaawoo yeɔ ebuaa ni etsakeɔ dumɔwui ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ ewoɔ dumɔwui ni jara wa.

english: How do I know if my farmland is truly ready and healthy enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu nii?

english: Ready soil is well-aerated, moist but not waterlogged, and rich in organic matter. An extension officer can test your soil texture and fertility to confirm it can support root development before you put seeds in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ shi nu bɛ mli ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ bɔ ni ewoɔ nii ehaa lɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛma nɔ mi akɛ ebaanyɛ eye ebua shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ dani okɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it harmful to uproot young seedlings and replant them in another part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ majie dumɔwui ni mikɛdu ehee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Uprooting damages fragile root hairs and causes severe shock to the plant, which slows down growth or kills the crop entirely. Getting planting right the first time avoids the stress of transplanting.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ yitsɔi ni waaa lɛ, efiteɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ hosoɔ waa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ agbo. Kɛ́ adu nii jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I stop my young crops from drying up right after sprouting during the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkagbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sprouts dry up if planted during false rains or in soil that does not retain moisture well. Expert guidance helps you time your planting with stable rains and use mulching to keep soil moisture high.
ga: Bean sprouts lɛ baagbi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ nyɛɛɛ ahi mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ŋaawoo ni he esa yeɔ ebua bo ni oto dumɔ be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. ni okɛ mulching atsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep getting the same disease year after year even after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Disease pathogens like fungi or viruses can survive deep inside plant tissues, crop leftovers, or the soil. If infected plant parts are not completely cut out and destroyed, the disease will continue to return every season.
ga: Helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ fungi loo virus baanyɛ ahi tso mli fãji, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, loo sũ mli shɔŋŋ kɛji ajieee tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa. Hela lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba daa be.

english: Is it really necessary to cut down my cocoa trees if they are sick but still giving me a few pods?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ he kɛji hela mɔ lɛ shi eyɛ ŋmeii komɛi lolo kɛha mi?

english: Yes, because incurable diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus stay inside the tree forever. Leaving a sick tree alive allows insects to feed on it and spread the virus to all your remaining healthy trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ helai ni anyɛɛɛ atsa tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ baahi tso lɛ mli kɛya naanɔ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ amɛ ni amɛhiɛ kã lɛ haa kooloi bibii yeɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei fɛɛ ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does a crop disease move from my neighbor's farm onto my own land?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko gbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases travel easily through the air on wind currents, through rain splashes, on unwashed farm tools, and by insects like mealybugs that carry infected sap from plant to plant.
ga: Helai tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ nɔ, kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ, yɛ okwaayeli nibii ni afɔɔɔ he, kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛɔ nu ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my soil if I leave diseased plants sitting in my farm for many years?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii babaoo?

english: Leaving infected plants in the ground allows disease-causing fungi and bacteria to build up and remain dormant in the soil for decades, making it unsafe for future young crops.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhiɛɔ shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and dropping off before the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is under stress, which can be caused by root-damaging pests, sap-sucking insects, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ shishi. Kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi, koolooi ni nuɔ nu, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen baanyɛ ekɛ enɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of big green leaves but very few fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi aduawai loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much shade or too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into leafy growth rather than spending energy on flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my plants look like they are wilting even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting during rainy periods usually means the roots have rotted from fungi in waterlogged soil, leaving the plant unable to drink water even though the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ anu nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do agricultural officers want to treat an entire farming community all at once instead of just individual farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ baasumɔ ni amɛkwɛ okwaafoi akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ kome pɛ najiaŋ

english: Pests and diseases do not recognize farm borders. Treating a large, continuous area prevents pests from hiding on untreated neighboring farms and flying straight back onto treated land.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ekpɛlɛɛɛ ŋmɔ mli husui anɔ. He ko ni da ni yaa nɔ lɛ ni aaatsa lɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni asaaa amɛhe lɛ amli. ni efã kɛku esɛɛ kɛya he ni atsa lɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How long will it take for my farm to produce full yields again after a major disease treatment?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe ni miŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ beni mitsa hela titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Recovery time depends on the crop type; while quick crops recover in months, tree crops like cocoa typically take 3 to 5 years after replanting to reach full harvest capacity.
ga: Be ni akɛbaatsa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tee hiɛ oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ be mli ni adu ehee lɛ sɛɛ dani eshɛɔ amɛ nibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee lɛ he.

english: What standard steps can I take on my farm today to protect healthy crops from catching diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɛnɛ koni mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Good farm hygiene is essential—sanitize your pruning tools, clear out fallen infected fruits regularly, and keep weeds low so harmful insects do not have places to hide.
ga: Hetsemɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia. Gbalamɔ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ Jiemɔ aduawai ni egbee shi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa. ni oha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi Bɔni afee ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akaná he ko ni amɛbaahi.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to stay green, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ waa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the afternoon heat is too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects or wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak harvests when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded in one spot, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, spending energy to stretch tall instead of developing strong roots and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abu dumɔwui lɛ anaa yɛ he kome lɛ, Tsei ni Miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die during the sunny afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root parasites that block the plant's internal tubes, stopping water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava curling up with yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ tsɛŋeɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why does my maize stalk snap and break easily before the corn is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya dani ŋmãa lɛ hoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks break when stem borer caterpillars burrow inside the stem to eat, creating hollow tunnels that weaken the plant against wind and weight.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ fãa kɛji stem borers lɛ tsɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ haa tsɔne ko ni mli ewo muji ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under direct hot sun; they need surrounding shade plants like plantains to protect them and keep the air moist until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get black rotten spots on the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of peppers are called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How long must I wait after spraying pest chemicals on my vegetables before picking them to sell?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie aduawai anɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Every crop chemical has a required waiting period after spraying, allowing the chemical to break down naturally so the produce is safe for people to eat.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni amɛkɛbaamɛ yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do my harvested dried maize grains develop holes and white powder after sitting in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ mli bu kɛ powda yɛŋ beni mita mi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Powder and holes in stored grain are caused by tiny weevils that hatch from eggs laid on the crop, eating the inside of the grain if it is not dried properly or treated for storage.
ga: Powda kɛ bu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tsei anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtooo amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves grow very large when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, but the plant requires potassium and soft, loose soil to swell and grow big tubers underground.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ agboi waa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi potassium kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he miihia tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What makes compost or animal manure better for my farm soil than relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ ni mikɛaafɔ̃ nɔ?

english: Organic manure builds up the soil structure and helps it hold water longer during dry spells, whereas chemical fertilizers feed the crop quickly but do not improve the soil itself.
ga: Organic fertilizers lɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ oya lɛ, amɛhaaa sũ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ baafee nɔ ni he baaba sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi?

english: Yes, cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize while covering the ground to stop weeds from growing.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa shwieɔ shi koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow, curled leaves indicate that the maize plant is under severe stress, usually caused by lack of water, a missing nutrient like nitrogen, or damage from fall armyworms.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa tamɔ nitrogen loo fall armyworm fitemɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when the plants do not get enough water, or when bees and other insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmeii

english: Why do weeds always grow back faster than my crops right after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to grow rapidly in poor soil conditions, allowing them to take up water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before young crop seeds can fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: What causes my yam tubers to develop dark, rotten spots while they are still in the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ diji ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by fungal diseases that spread through excess water pooling around the plant roots or from using infected seed yams at planting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ tsei shishifãi ahe loo kɛjɛɔ sweet potato ni hela emɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ mli.

english: It is best to wait until the rains are regular for about two consecutive weeks so the soil retains enough moisture deep down for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa aaafee otsi enyɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do insects attack and destroy my stored maize and beans after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in grains that still contain moisture; thoroughly drying your harvested crops under the sun before storing them prevents insect eggs from hatching.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbala okpamɔ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi dani okɛto lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii akui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: How do I know whether to plant my cassava stems slanting or standing straight up in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji esa akɛ odu o-cassava tso lɛ ni okɛ ohe afɔ shi loo okɛ ohe afɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle (about 45 degrees) helps roots grow deeper and spread out evenly, while planting them straight up often causes tubers to grow too close to the surface where they can easily dry out or get damaged.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa pɛpɛɛpɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ adu amɛ shiŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya loo amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture as much sunlight as possible. The leaves convert that sunlight into food energy, which travels down to build larger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ niyenii hewalɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture to help young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do people spread dry grass or leaves on the ground around the stems of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi amɛshwãa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight, traps moisture so you water less often, stops weeds from growing, and gradually rots to enrich the soil with natural plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli babaoo Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips that spread inward in a V-shape mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will solve this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ V-shape mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: If I plant cowpeas alongside my maize, won't the cowpeas steal food away from the maize?
ga: Kɛ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Ani tsina ŋmãa lɛ juuŋ niyenii kɛjɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: No, cowpeas actually help feed the maize. Cowpeas belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil, acting as a natural food provider for the maize planted next to it.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa niyenii. Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth so much, even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa tsei adalɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ efɔ shi moŋ

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb water, light, and fertilizer faster than your crops can. If weeds are present when you apply fertilizer, they eat the food intended for your crops and crowd them out.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaaye niyenii ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy and dead in the middle of the afternoon heat, but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can drink it up, causing the plant to temporarily limp to protect itself. As the air cools down in the evening, the plant recovers its water balance.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nu ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny chewed holes deep inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl deep into the central growth funnel of young maize plants during the daytime to hide from the sun and eat the soft expanding leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he ni amɛye baai bibii ni miigbɛ amɛshwã lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling up tightly into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Treating the insects early keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ atsa kooloi mra lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the trunks of my coconut trees snapping and breaking off near the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When a tree trunk breaks unexpectedly, it usually means a disease or stem-boring pest has rotted the inside of the wood over time, weakening the stem until it can no longer hold the heavy top head of the coconut tree.
ga: Kɛ tso shishi fã trukaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni efo tso lɛ shishi, ni eha tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni enyɛŋ emɔ ŋmei tso ni tsii lɛ yiteŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my coconut tree is dying from a disease or just suffering from a lack of rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛkɛ miigbe mi-ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: Drought causes leaves to wilt evenly across the farm, and plants recover once rain returns. Disease usually causes specific symptoms like premature fruit drop, blackening stems, or tree trunk rotting, regardless of how much rain falls.
ga: Hɔmɔ lɛ eha baai egbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ni tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa, tamɔ tso yibii ni fiteɔ oya, tsei akutsei ni feɔ diŋ, loo tsei akutsei ni fiteɔ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ waa ha

english: Why are all the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dropping off before the fruits are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Rapid yellowing and frond loss in coconut trees is often caused by Coconut Lethal Yellowing Disease, which is spread by tiny sap-sucking insects that infect the tree's circulatory system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ni gbeɔ mɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai ni fiteɔ oya kɛ amɛhe ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni yeɔ tso lɛ lá ni hoɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: If I pluck off and destroy all the sick-looking coconuts from my tree, will the tree heal itself?
ga: Kɛ́ mifolɔ ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni mikpãtã amɛ fɛɛ hiɛ lɛ, Ani tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsa?

english: Removing sick fruit helps clean the tree, but if the illness is an internal plant disease living inside the sap or trunk, destroying the fruit alone will not cure the underlying infection.
ga: Yibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni etsumɔ tso lɛ he. Shi kɛji hela lɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu loo eshishifã lɛ mli Yibii lɛ akpãtãmɔ pɛ lɛ tsaŋ hela ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: If my crop looks sickly and weak, will adding fertilizer fix the problem and make it healthy again?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu naagba lɛ he nii ni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for healthy growing crops. If a plant is suffering from a disease or root rot, fertilizer will not cure it and can sometimes make the infection worse or waste your money.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni miida jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hela loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ tsaŋ lɛ. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hela lɛ aya hiɛ loo efee shika fitemɔ.

english: Why do my young fruits keep falling off the tree before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibii bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop can be caused by fungal infections, pest damage at the flower stage, or severe plant stress, which causes the tree to shed its load to save its own life.
ga: Fungal hela baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ afite oya. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii amli loo tso lɛ haomɔ ni naa wa Enɛ haa tso lɛ shiɔ ejatsui lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Can a disease from one infected tree spread to the rest of the healthy trees on my farm?
ga: Ani hela ko ni jɛ tso kome ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, many crop diseases spread to healthy neighboring plants through underground root contact, wind-blown spores, insects, or shared farm tools like cutlasses.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ. Spores ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa, kooloi, loo okwaayeli nibii ni akɛjaa tamɔ daggers.

english: What should I do with a coconut tree after it dies from a disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ migbo yɛ ŋmei hela mli?

english: A diseased tree should be completely cut down, removed from the farm, and safely destroyed or burned to prevent insects and fungi from breeding in the dead wood and attacking healthy trees.
ga: Esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa. ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akpãtãa amɛhiɛ loo ashãa amɛ shweshweeshwe koni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii akafee babaoo yɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ anɔ. ni amɛtutua tsei ni he wa

english: Why are the bases of my crops rotting right where the stem enters the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifite yɛ he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting at the soil level is usually caused by waterlogging and soil-borne fungal diseases that thrive when heavy rain sits around the stem; planting on mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ lɛ mli shwiemɔ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops dying while the top leaves still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: While older bottom leaves die naturally over time, rapid loss of lower leaves often means the roots are damaged by soil rot or the plant is lacking essential nutrients from the ground.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni fiteɔ oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ loo akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up so fast when the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ gbii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops lose moisture quickly through their leaves when the sun is strong. Soil with low organic matter cannot hold water for long, causing crop roots to dry out rapidly during dry spells.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil, and if a dry spell follows, the newly germinated seeds will dry out and die.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Which crops can survive better on my farm if the rainy season is very short this year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ afi nɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa kwraa?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpeas, sorghum, and early-maturing maize varieties survive short rainy seasons better because their root systems reach deep water or they complete their growth quickly.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli loo amɛdaraa oya.

english: How can I get a heavy harvest when my land is very small?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmaa babaoo be mli ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: You can increase yield on small land by using high-quality seeds, maintaining proper row spacing so every plant gets enough sun, and adding compost to make the soil richer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ gbɛ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ koni tsei fɛɛ ana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do the crops on the university demonstration farm look stronger than the ones on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ yunivɛsiti nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Demonstration farms follow strict practices such as planting in neat rows with exact spacing, applying nutrients at the right time, and clearing weeds early so crops don't struggle for food.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa sɛɛ, tamɔ dumɔ yɛ toi fɛfɛji kɛ gbɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtao niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant a lot of seeds together in one small space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which makes them stretch upward thin and weak instead of growing strong.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I feed my crops properly if I do not have money to buy store-bought fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shika ni mikɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli hu?

english: You can enrich your soil naturally by making compost from decomposed crop leaves and animal manure, or by rotating crops with groundnuts and beans that naturally drop nitrogen into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ahe baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even when it is raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is pooling around the roots without draining, which stops the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. shishifãi ni nu hoɔɔɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do some of my young crops burn and die when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ tso waa lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose water faster than their roots can drink. Providing light shade or mulching around the base keeps the soil cool and preserves moisture.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the dirt completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is packed too hard, planted too deep for light to reach them, lacking moisture, or eaten by insects before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni la nyɛŋ ashɛ he, ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli, loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight and burn easily. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture so the cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This competition makes all the plants thin and weak, resulting in small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main soil nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and staying tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by microscopic pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap out of tender foliage, which distorts new leaf growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai heei ni daraa lɛ afee nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why do I have to put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the upper leaves gather, the larger the yam tuber grows under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Babaoo ni sweet potato tuber lɛ daa lɛ, babaoo ni ebaada yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly, which stresses the plant and prevents fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the dirt before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil where rainwater collects without draining away. The excess standing water chokes the roots and lets fungal diseases destroy them underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ he ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni efooo kɛyaa lɛ. Nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ kpataa amɛhiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is eating the soft middle part of my corn plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ateŋ fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of young corn plants to feed on new leaves before the cobs appear.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the field surface or drains it too deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji granular fertilizer lɛ ahe loo ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava crop grow so slowly even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cassava tsei lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizer faster than cassava plants can, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baanyɛ afee. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: What does compound fertilizer actually do for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛhaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Compound fertilizer contains a balanced mix of vital nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. It helps cocoa trees develop strong roots, stay green and healthy, and produce larger, heavier pods.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni mli wa. Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ ni oná hewalɛ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii

english: Can I use the same fertilizer meant for my maize crop on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: It is not recommended because different crops need different nutrients. Maize requires high nitrogen for fast leafy growth, while cocoa needs higher potassium and phosphorus to grow strong stems and produce good pods. Using the wrong fertilizer wastes money and won't give you a good harvest.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo he miihia kookoo koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii kpakpai aba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika, ni ebaahaaa oná yibii kpakpai.

english: What happens if I place strong fertilizer right against the trunk of my crop?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem or trunk can burn the plant's skin and roots because the chemical concentration is too high. You should always spread it in a ring around the plant, where the outer feeding roots can reach it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi loo etsitsi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa tsɔ. Esa akɛ ogbɛ eshwa be fɛɛ be kɛya ŋwɛi ŋta ni bɔle tso lɛ he he ni kponɔgbɛ niyenii shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: When is the best time during the season to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time is right after the main rains begin when the soil is moist. Moisture allows the roots to soak up the dissolved nutrients, but applying it during heavy downpours can wash the fertilizer away before the plants can use it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani tsei kɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree is stressed. This can happen from too much harsh sunlight without enough shade trees, lack of rain, or because the plant is starving for essential nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Enɛ baanyɛ aba kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo ni tsei haaa amɛhe hulutsoo bɔ ni sa, nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ, loo akɛni tsei miiye niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil has become weak and needs extra plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná tsei niyenii krokomɛi?

english: Weak soil shows in your crops. If your plants grow slowly, look pale, have thin stems, or give you smaller yields than in past years despite good rainfall, the soil has likely run out of natural nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ onibii amli. Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ daa blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops before feeding the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ dani mikɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow fast. If you don't clear them first, they will drink up the water and eat the fertilizer you applied, leaving very little for your actual crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya. Kɛji okɛjieee mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Amɛbaanu nu lɛ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ kɛha onibii.

english: Will my cocoa trees still give me pods if I cannot afford fertilizer this year?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ lolo kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe ŋmɔtɔ afi nɛɛ?

english: Yes, the trees will still fruit using whatever nutrients are left in the soil, but your harvest will be much smaller and the trees will become weaker and more vulnerable to diseases over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ baaya nɔ ewo yibii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shi nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa. Ni tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling us to prune branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ wɔ kookoo niji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or crowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can flow through the tree. This prevents dampness that breeds diseases like black pod and sends more energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni feɔ diŋ lɛ aba lɛ naa, ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ mli.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Keeping the farm clear of heavy bush and pruning branches lets in sunlight to dry out the farm and reduce the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔ mli koni hulu la aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni helai aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a umbrella-like shade that protects the young trees and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green again and grow strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha baai lɛ afee hewalɛ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil. It traps moisture near the roots, keeps the ground cool, and reduces how often you need to water.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni oha nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi shii abɔ

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves, and why is the plant struggling to grow?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Small caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hide inside the growing tip of the maize plant and feed on the tender leaves. Catching them early and applying organic neem spray or recommended pesticides prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem sprays loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very tiny fruits when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sun, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to catch light and spread its roots, leading to bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená la ni egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to settle in. Rotating with beans or groundnuts resets the soil and brings back rich nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ Rotating kɛ beans loo peanuts baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai aba ekoŋŋ.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and soak deep into the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower. Seeds need continuous moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining small and woody even after growing for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ be babaoo edu amɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand if the soil is too hard and compacted or lacks nutrients like potassium. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges makes it easy for the tubers to swell big and soft.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ ni etsɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if my plants look bigger than the weeds?
ga: Te jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ dara fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves under the ground, stealing the water and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into making your crops yield well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi julɔi Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing non-essential side branches (pruning) prevents the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This directs all the plant's food into producing larger, healthier fruits and improves air movement to stop diseases.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ajiemɔ Pruning (pruning) tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ koni ewo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akpa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct hot sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a umbrella that protects young cocoa until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers turn into small green pods that suddenly turn black and shrivel up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni trukaa lɛ amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded cocoa farms. Pruning overgrown branches to let air and sunlight in helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni edara fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa hela agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves wilt and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry Harmattan winds, the air strips moisture from cocoa leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry soil. Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the tree base helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni akɛaabɔle Tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Will cutting mature branches off my cocoa trees hurt my total harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo tso niji ni edara ni mifoɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches actually increases your yield. It allows sunlight to reach the main trunk where cocoa pods grow and prevents fungal diseases, though you should avoid cutting away too many leafy branches at once.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii helai baaa. Shi esa akɛ okpa tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ ni ofoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their tiny fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani amɛdara?

english: Mango trees drop young fruit when they lack water during dry spells or when fruit flies attack the flowers. Regular watering during flowering and trapping pests keeps the young fruit attached to the branch.
ga: Mango tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji nu bɛ amɛnɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli lɛ baaha aduawai bibii lɛ akpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ he.

english: Why are my harvested mangoes full of worms inside even when the outer skin looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango ni akpa lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ po

english: Fruit flies pierce green mango skins to lay eggs inside. When the eggs hatch into maggots, they eat the fruit from the inside; setting up fruit fly traps and removing fallen rotting fruit breaks this cycle.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii tsɔɔ mango eŋɔli ko hewolo mli koni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ Ebaaye aduawai lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Yibii amli ŋmeii ni amɔmɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ.

english: Why is my mango tree growing lots of fresh leaves but producing no flowers this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ yɛ baai heei babaoo shi fɔfɔi bɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mango trees need a short dry period to trigger flowering. Excess water or continuous heavy rains cause the tree to spend energy growing new leaves instead of setting buds for fruit.
ga: Mango tsei biɔ be kuku ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Nu babaoo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai heei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is running out of nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: When crop leaves turn pale yellow, growth stays unusually short, or leaves turn purple at the tips, your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus that plants need to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ tso baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ, Dalɛ lɛ feɔ kuku yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. loo baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ purple Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally fertilize the soil and feed neighboring crops without chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ niyenii ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my harvested fruits spoil so fast before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting fruit in the heat of the day, rough handling that bruises the skin, or keeping harvested crops in direct sun speeds up decay. Storing them in cool, shaded spots keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Yibii ni akpaa yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ ji gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa ni haa hewolo lɛ fãa loo nibii ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ebaaha fitemɔ aba oya. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool, maintaining soil moisture, and protecting the leaves from burning until the crop is mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines climb naturally to reach sunlight, which the leaves use to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot soil, reducing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to catch enough light to grow large yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Akɛ baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ahaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ náa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ sweet potatoes agboi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, signaling that your soil needs manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei yeɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field this season, why will my maize grow better in that same soil next season?
ga: Kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into strips and roll up tightly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split and roll up as a natural survival defense against heat. By exposing less leaf surface to the direct sun and wind, the plant slows down water evaporation and conserves moisture until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shɛɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by several scorching hot days that dry out the topsoil. Seeds need steady moisture over time to sprout, so planting too early causes the seeds to dry up and die in the hot earth before roots can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they suffer from severe heat or sudden water stress. When the plant feels threatened by harsh weather or dry soil, it drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival instead of feeding fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ trukaa lɛ kpe amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miiwo ehe gbeyei lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala moŋ fe ni eeeye aduawai.

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Moving back and forth between very dry soil and soaked soil prevents the crop from moving calcium to the tips of the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa teŋ ni oooya kɛba lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: How long can I leave my mature cassava tubers in the ground before they spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifã ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani efite?

english: Cassava tubers stay fresh underground for up to a year or more because the living plant continues to feed them. However, if left too long, the tubers turn woody, lose starch quality, or rot if heavy rains soak the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi afi loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ baaya nɔ aha amɛ niyenii, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ. Yitso lɛ baatsɔ tso. Ashikishaŋ kpakpa ni baa shi Loo fitemɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why does my harvested dried maize still get eaten by small insects inside my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-nitoohe lɛ miiye mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Tiny insect eggs or hidden weevils often hitch a ride on the maize straight from the field. If the storage space is warm and not completely sealed or treated, those hidden pests hatch, multiply, and eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni atsĩii naa kwraa loo atsako Nakai kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ, amɛfɔɔ, ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do people always advise me to plant plantains on the same land where I am starting my young cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mije kookoo bibii shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist soil they need to survive their first couple of years.
