ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to heap my soil into high mounds before planting yam, or can I just plant directly on flat ground?
ga: Ehi akɛ oookɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ dani odu ŋmei loo obaanyɛ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to grow large and long without obstruction. Making high soil mounds gives the roots plenty of loose earth to expand in and prevents heavy rain from pooling and rotting the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ama lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala mli, ni ehaaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ afee ekome ni efite bulb lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the key food it needs to build green stems and leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or cowpeas on my land after I finish harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni migbe ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legume crops like beans and cowpeas naturally put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility for your next planting season without costly chemicals.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Fɔmɔ ni akuɔ sɛɛ akɛhaa kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa fataaa he.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants during hot weather without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and dry, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from stress. Watering the plants regularly at the base and providing slight shade helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni egbi Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ ni aha lɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the roots of my crops during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, stopping water from evaporating quickly in the dry wind and keeping the roots cool so young crops stay alive longer between rain or watering.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Why should I measure the distance between my maize seeds instead of scattering them closely together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces them to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with tiny cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce full, large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches and yellow leaves from my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ eggplant mli yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting away unnecessary stems and dead leaves stops the plant from wasting food on parts that do not produce fruit. It also allows air and sunlight to reach the inner branches, encouraging the plant to yield bigger garden eggs.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, efiteee niyenii yɛ hei ni wooo yibii lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hu shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides. Spraying a mixture of neem leaf water or mild soapy water helps clear these pests and lets new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem baa mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ ni akɛbaashwie nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ni eye ebua baa heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready to harvest so they do not get woody or watery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni tso loo nu bɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, typically 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too early results in small roots, while leaving them in the ground too long makes the roots hard, fibrous, and difficult to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii baajɛ mli aba. Shi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tsɔi, ni ebaawa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: What are the main types of pineapples available for me to plant in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii titrii ni miduɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, the main varieties grown are Sugarloaf (often sweet and conical, very popular locally), Smooth Cayenne (large, juicy, with smooth leaves), and MD2 (golden, very sweet, and popular for commercial export).
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, tso titri ni aduɔ ji Sugarloaf (bei pii lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ). Ehe gbɛi waa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli), Smooth Cayenne (ni da, ni mli edɔ ni ehiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ) kɛ MD2 (shika tsuru, ni ŋɔɔ waa ni ehe gbɛi kɛha jarayeli ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ).

english: Why do some of my pineapple plants have smooth leaves while others have spiky edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Different pineapple varieties have distinct physical traits. Varieties like 'Smooth Cayenne' have smooth leaves that make working in the farm easier, while local varieties like 'Sugarloaf' often have sharp, spiky leaf edges.
ga: Esoro pineapple henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ su. Henɔi tamɔ ‘Smooth Cayenne’ lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Sugarloaf’ lɛ fɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which pineapple variety should I plant if I want to sell mostly to local buyers in my town?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ babaoo maha maŋbii ni heɔ nii yɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Local Ghanaian buyers usually prefer the 'Sugarloaf' variety because it is extremely sweet and juicy when eaten fresh, making it very popular for local food markets.
ga: Ghanabii ni heɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ‘Sugarloaf’ henɔ lɛ waa ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni eyɛ nu kɛji aye lɛ ehee. Enɛ haa ehe gbɛi waa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Can I plant the leafy green top of a harvested pineapple fruit to grow a new crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei ni akpa lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ koni makwɛ tso hee?

english: Yes, you can plant the top crown, but using side shoots called 'suckers' or 'slips' from an established plant is better because they grow much faster and produce stronger fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ ŋwɛi akekere lɛ nɔ. Shi ehi akɛ akɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘ŋmeii’ loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni jɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni mli wa.

english: How long will it take from the day I plant my pineapple suckers until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ pineapple tso lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa eyibii lɛ?

english: Pineapples generally take between 12 to 18 months from planting to harvest, depending on the variety planted, soil quality, and the size of the sucker used.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa. Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Can pineapple plants survive on my farm during the long dry season without regular watering?
ga: Ani anana tso ko baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ lɛ nu daa?

english: Yes, pineapple plants are very drought-tolerant because their thick leaves store water, allowing them to withstand dry weather much better than crops like maize or cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, anana tsei baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa naa ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni mli tse lɛ hiɛɔ nu. Enɛ haa amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli babaoo fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo kookoo.

english: Why do pineapples produce smaller fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pineapples are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which prevents the fruits from reaching full size.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu pineapple ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Pineapple shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. ni haa aduawai lɛ shɛɛɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ ji lɛ he

english: Why are my pineapple fruits ripening at different times instead of all together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Pineapples naturally flower and mature based on individual plant size and minor weather shifts; to get a uniform harvest, farmers often use specific growth regulators to encourage all plants to flower at the same time.
ga: Pineapple baawo fɔfɔi ni ebaada yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi fioo ni baa lɛ nɔ. bɔni afee ni aná nibii ni anáa daa lɛ Bei pii lɛ okwaafoi kɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli.

english: How can I tell when a pineapple is fully ripe and ready for picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ko ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A pineapple is ready to harvest when the base skin changes color from dark green to yellow, the fruit gives off a sweet scent, and tapping it produces a dull, solid sound.
ga: Efee klalo akɛ abaakpa pineapple kɛji shishigbɛ lɛ tsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ mli. Yibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ. ni kɛ́ otswa nɔ lɛ, gbee ni mli wa ni mli wa baa.

english: What causes harvested pineapples to soft-rot and spoil quickly after I take them off the field?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ oya beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pineapples spoil quickly if they are harvested overripe, bruised during transportation, or kept in direct hot sunlight, which speeds up internal fermentation and decay.
ga: Pineapple fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ fe nine. Atswa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko loo akɛtoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Enɛ baaha mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aya oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under intense sun because their roots are not deep enough to draw sufficient moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Planting too closely actually reduces your overall harvest. When crops are crowded, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: Why does my soil get hard and baked like brick during the dry season even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni edɔ tamɔ brikii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter such as compost or animal manure. Adding compost improves the soil structure, helping it soak up rain like a sponge and hold moisture longer during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ sponji ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen, which feeds heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ tsei aniyenii ni akɛhaa kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Under severe stress, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa shishi Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cassava uses to preserve water during dry weather. Reduced leaf surface means less water escapes into the air, allowing the underground tuber to remain healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Baai lɛ anɔ ni eba shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ joɔ foi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or a virus they spread. Controlling these pests early using neem oil or recommended sprays stops the leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep, hardy root systems adapted to survive harsh conditions and quickly absorb water and nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures they do not steal essential food from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't rot or get eaten by insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, egboŋ loo kooloi yeŋ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels become hard and glossy. Harvesting too early leaves high moisture that causes mold, while waiting too long leaves it exposed to field pests.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ekpɛɔ Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and soft right on the tree before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani minyɛ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Dark brown, soft cocoa pods are infected by black pod disease, caused by fungi that thrive in cold, wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to flow, keeping pods dry and disease-free.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni darako ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli hela ni ji black pod hela lɛ emɔ amɛ. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni hela akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the field has too much standing water drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure can help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Holes in pepper leaves are typically caused by small insects or caterpillars feeding on them at night. Inspecting under the leaves and spraying a simple mixture of neem leaf extract and water can help drive these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ pepper baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem baa mli nu ni akɛfutuɔ nu kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ashwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to drop off before they can grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering at the root level and providing light shade during peak dry periods can help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it important to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: No hewɔ lɛ nɔ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa seedlings while keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my okra seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ okra dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Giving okra plants enough space ensures that each plant gets full sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients. When planted too close, they fight each other for food, leading to weak stems and fewer pods.
ga: Kɛ́ aha okra he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ Kɛji adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ pods fioo.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce leaves but very few nuts under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ baai shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the soil to form hard, full pods under the earth. If your soil lacks calcium or has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant will spend all its energy growing big top leaves instead of making pods.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa ni eyi obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo eyɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their bottom leaves during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ shishi shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from drought. This is normal behavior, and the plant will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Enɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How do weeds harm my yam tubers if they are not directly touching the yam vine?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ? Kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ,.

english: Weeds have deep roots that secretly steal water, plant nutrients, and space from underground yam tubers. Even if they don't touch the vine, weeds starve your yams, resulting in small, thin tubers.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni juɔ nu yɛ teemɔŋ. tso mli niyenii kɛ he ni jɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yam tubers lɛ mli Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ wain tso lɛ ebɔko po, Shi jwɛi lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the main leaves start turning yellow and falling. If left in the ground too long after maturity, the roots become woody, fibrous, and hard to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji baai titrii lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tsei, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshweremɔ wa.

english: Why do my harvested cowpea seeds turn into powder inside my storage bags after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ powda yɛ mi-nitoo kotoku lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: The powder is caused by small insects called grain weevils that lay eggs inside the beans while in the field or storage. Drying your cowpeas thoroughly in the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight containers keeps these insects from eating your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain moths ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo yɛ he ko ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ powda lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsina ŋmeii egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They require shade trees or fast-growing plants like plantain nearby to shield them from full sunlight until they are strong enough to handle it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu he nii.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up high to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light so the plant can make food and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛhaa la boteɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahoo nii ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so it doesn't evaporate in the sun, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ akaje mli. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Does planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Ani tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives each crop enough space to yield heavily.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Alternating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen back to the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm, drying out the moisture that spreads the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt in the growing tip?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the main shoot of the plant. Catching them early and applying recommended organic sprays or approved treatments keeps them from destroying the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii titrii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack from expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ shishigbɛ yitso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: What happens if I leave my mature maize sitting dry in the field for a long time before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa ni egbɔ lɛ koni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani akpa?

english: Leaving dry maize out on the field exposes it to attack by weevils, birds, and mold from unexpected rain, which reduces the quality and market value of your grain.
ga: Ashiɔ ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Akɛ ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii ni baajɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli baatutua lɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahe sɛɛnamɔ kɛ jarayeli jara aba shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava typically matures between 8 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How long does local maize take from planting to harvest in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa heɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Most early-maturing local maize varieties take about 3 to 4 months to produce dry grain, while late-maturing varieties take around 4 to 5 months depending on the rains.
ga: Native abele henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 5, ni enɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that provide vital shade and hold moisture in the soil to help the cocoa seedlings survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields if I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen. When planted repeatedly on the same plot without resting the soil or applying fertilizer, it drains the soil's nutrients, causing future yields to drop.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akɛ sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ mli. ni haa wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni afee lɛ baa shi

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei beni akpa ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does poultry manure help my vegetable crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure releases key nutrients like nitrogen and organic matter slowly into the soil, improving its ability to hold water and feeding the plants steadily over time.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli fiofio. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and showing small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ bu bibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with small holes are often caused by fall armyworm caterpillars or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Checking under the leaves early helps you spot pests before they ruin the farm.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my pepper plants more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry conditions weaken pepper plants, making them thirsty. Pests like aphids and whiteflies thrive in warm weather and flock to green plants to suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa pepper tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa kumai yeɔ amɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What happens to my yam seed tubers if the field gets flooded during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excess water sitting around yam mounds cuts off air from the soil, causing the planted seed tubers to rot underground before they can spout into stems.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe Atoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei ni adu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to suck up water and nutrients rapidly. Clearing land exposes weed seeds to sunlight, allowing them to germinate much faster than planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii oya. He ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is thirsty and needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai miiye mi-abele lɛ ni nu he miihia lɛ?

english: Maize leaves start to curl up tightly like tubes during the day when they are thirsty. Water them early in the morning so the roots can drink before the hot afternoon sun dries the soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛ́ kumai ye amɛ. Nu leebi koni eha shishifãi lɛ nɔ ko ni amɛnu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: How can I tell if my corn is completely ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is usually ready when the silk threads at the top of the cob turn dark brown and dry, and the leaves wrapped around the cob start changing from green to light brown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cob lɛ jeɔ shishi etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the middle of the day even after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, crops lose water from their leaves faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. This temporary wilting protects the plant, and it usually recovers by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa be kukuoo nɛɛ buɔ tso lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin without giving me big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and plant food. They put all their energy into stretching tall to reach light instead of building fat corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ tsei aniyenii he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ amli koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ ngma nɛ mi ngɛ fɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the crop is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that dry soil is preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni sa.

english: How can I keep the soil around my crops wet for longer when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare ground around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—known as mulching—shades the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the water quickly.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha onibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafee nu oya.

english: Why should I avoid planting corn on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Growing corn in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and attracts crop-specific pests. Rotating corn with beans or groundnuts restores soil natural richness.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni egbalaa ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do worms always attack the tender leaf funnel in the center of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa baa bibioo ni agbeleɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei bibi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant is soft, full of moisture, and sheltered from the sun, making it the easiest place for pests like fall armyworms to feed and hide.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ he ko ni ehiɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ haa efeɔ he ni niyenii kɛ he ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aná yɛ mlɛo fe fɛɛ.

english: What is happening to my crop when the corn plant starts producing tassels at the top?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ?

english: The tassels at the top produce pollen, which falls onto the silks below to form the actual grains on the cob. This shows the plant has finished growing leaves and is now shifting its energy to make food.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ pollen ni gbeeɔ siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ koni efee dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ cob lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ naa. Ni amrɔ nɛɛ eetsake hewalɛ ni ekɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that drink water and absorb fertilizer much faster than your crops. Clearing weeds early leaves all the water and nutrients in the soil for your farm crops to feed on.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eshiɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha oŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni ayeɔ.

english: Cassava grows best in loose, sandy-loam soil that allows water to drain quickly. If water sits on your field for days after raining, the cassava roots will rot under the ground.
ga: Yucca daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni haa nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu hi oŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle properly before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain is risky because if a dry spell follows, the seeds will sprout and dry up in the hot soil. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures young roots stay moist.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ ji oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil, resulting in weak stems and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas between my maize rows?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas between maize rows helps cover the ground to stop weeds from growing, keeps moisture in the soil, and naturally adds plant nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually show that the plant is missing nitrogen nutrients in the soil or that the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed inside the central leaves of young maize plants, especially during dry spells, and need early treatment to prevent crop loss.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ mra Koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, which can also spread plant viruses that stop the crop from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ ashwã tsei amli.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same land where I am planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas to protect the cocoa while it establishes roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ be mli ni efeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to build big tubers underground. Staking holds the foliage high off the damp ground so leaves stay healthy and capture sun efficiently.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the afternoon heat is too high or when the plant gets dry while flowering. Watering regularly early in the morning helps the plants keep their flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ egbi be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I put them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, you should plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upwards towards the sky. Planting them upside down causes delayed sprouting and weaker growth because the new shoots have to twist around to reach the light.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu yucca tsei niji ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo ni ebaaha shweremɔ lɛ afee mlɛo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei heei lɛ abɔle amɛhe. koni ená la

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stalks and results in small cobs or plants that fail to produce cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni no haa ŋmeii bibii loo tsei ni nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmeii kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the center line usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans work with beneficial bacteria in their roots to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots break down, that nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, nitrogen lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam vines are natural climbing plants that need stakes to lift their leaves high into the sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce more energy, which allows the plant to grow large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ nɔ. Baai ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Removing extra shoots, called suckers, stops them from stealing food and water from the main plant. This allows the primary plantain stem to grow strong and produce a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkajuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa plantain tsei titrii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant faces stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist and adding dry grass mulch around the base keeps the roots cool and prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ehe lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly into little cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even though I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: In strong afternoon heat, leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. As long as the soil stays moist, the leaves usually bounce back once the sun goes down and temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do officers keep telling us to buy new improved seeds instead of just planting the seeds I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔhé dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du wuhi nɛ i kpa ngɛ jeha nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred by scientists to give higher yields and resist local pests. Seeds saved from your previous harvest lose these strong traits over generations, resulting in lower yields and weaker plants.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What makes a 'hybrid' crop variety different from the traditional seeds my grandfather planted?
ga: Mɛni haa ‘hybrid’ tso lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mitsɛkwɛ̃ duɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: A hybrid variety is created by carefully crossing two specific parent plants to combine their best traits, like high yield and drought resistance. Traditional seeds reproduce naturally in the field, which can lead to mixed and unpredictable results.
ga: Afeɔ tsofai sɔrɔtoi kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni akɛ amɛsui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ lɛ afata he lɛ nɔ. Akɛ kusum dumɔwui shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔi srɔtoi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ aba.

english: Why do some crop varieties produce huge yields while others under the same care remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shishi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Yield potential is built into the seed's genetics. A high-yielding variety has been selected to convert soil nutrients and water into fruits or grains much more efficiently than standard varieties.
ga: Akɛ yibiiwoo ni baanyɛ aba lɛ ema dumɔwu lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli. Ahalaa henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo koni ekɛtsake shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewo aduawai loo dumɔwui amli jogbaŋŋ fe henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ.

english: How can I know if a new crop variety being promoted is suitable for my specific field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hee ko ni atswaa he adafi lɛ sa kɛha miŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can ask your extension officer about the seed's ideal rainfall, soil requirements, and maturity time, and then try planting a small demonstration patch on your farm before planting your whole land.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi extension officer lɛ nugbɔ ni sa kɛha odumɔwui lɛ he sane. shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa kɛ be ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ kaa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko okwɛ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani odu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: I heard someone say plants have 'mother' and 'father' lines—how can a crop have parents like a human being?
ga: Minu ni mɛi miikɛɛ akɛ tsei yɛ ‘nyɛ’ kɛ ‘tsɛ’ line, no hewɔ lɛ te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii aná fɔlɔi tamɔ adesai?

english: Plants have male and female parts. Plant breeders take pollen from a strong 'father' plant line and use it to pollinate a healthy 'mother' plant line to produce a new seed that carries the best features of both.
ga: Tsei yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ jieɔ muji kɛjɛɔ ‘tsɛ’ tso ko ni wa mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ ‘nyɛ’ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli muji koni ekɛwo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does it take researchers several years to bring a new seed variety to us farmers in the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ niiamlitaolɔi afii babaoo dani amɛjieɔ dumɔwui heei kpo lɛ? Kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Breeders must cross-breed the parent plants, grow multiple generations, and test them across different seasons to ensure the new seeds consistently resist diseases and produce high yields safely.
ga: Esa akɛ mɛi ni fɔɔ tso lɛ afɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ yinɔi babaoo ni oka amɛ okwɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei nyɛɔ helai anaa be fɛɛ be ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo shweshweeshwe.

english: How do scientists make a plant grow faster without losing the good taste our customers like?
ga: Te jeŋ nilelɔi baafee tɛŋŋ amɛha tsei adara oya ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ shãaa afɔle?

english: Breeders carefully select parent plants that already have great taste and combine their seeds with plants that grow fast, testing the offspring until they find one that keeps the good flavor while maturing quickly.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ halaa nyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa momo lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ dumɔwui kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ afata he Ka seshi lɛ okwɛ kɛyashi obaana eko ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ oya.

english: If a seed variety was developed in another country like Nigeria or Mexico, will it actually grow well in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee dumɔwui lɛ yɛ maŋ kroko nɔ, tamɔ Nigeria loo Mexico. Ani ebaada jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, because local Ghanaian researchers take those parent seeds and test or breed them directly in our local soil and climate to ensure they adapt well before releasing them to farmers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli niiamlitaolɔi lɛ ŋɔɔ nakai fɔlɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkaa amɛ amɛkwɛɔ loo amɛfɔɔ amɛ yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji koni ana akɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ajie amɛ aha okwaafoi.

english: Why do research institutions bring crop seeds from outside Ghana instead of only using our local plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niiamlitaomɔ hei kɛ tsei dumɔwui ni jɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ baa lɛ, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei pɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: International research centers store parent plant lines with unique strengths, like extreme drought tolerance, which saves local scientists decades of work when trying to improve our native crops.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ toɔ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ko, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ ahe tsuishitoo. Enɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli jeŋ nilelɔi kɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ tsuɔ nii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛha wɔmaŋ tsei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does a seed variety that grows very well in the forest zone perform poorly when planted in the northern savannah?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ savannah lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops are sensitive to heat, daylight, and rainfall. Varieties bred for humid, rainy forest conditions struggle with the hotter weather and shorter rainy seasons of the savannah unless specifically adapted for it.
ga: Tsei nuɔ dɔlɛ, hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he waa. Esa akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi ni mli efɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ kɛ savannah kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi lɛ akpee. ja atsake lɛ pɔtɛɛ aha lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate stems and broad leaves that burn under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas planted alongside them to block the intense heat and hold moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it good to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ Ani mi-cacao bibioo lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi?

english: While cassava provides good shade, its large roots grow quickly and can fight with young cocoa for water and nutrients in the soil. Plantains are usually better shade partners because their root systems don't choke the cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ yucca haa hulutsoo kpakpa moŋ, shi eshishifãi wuji lɛ daa oya ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kookoo bibii lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Plantains haa hulutsoo kpakpa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsiii kookoo lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low on essential food like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots without draining properly. Adding decayed animal manure or compost around the base of the plant can help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe. shishifãi ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu jogbaŋŋ Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the stalks fight each other for sunshine, soil water, and nutrients. This competition leaves you with tall, weak plants that produce small corn cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa bibii loo ŋmãa ko kwraa.

english: Can I grow cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as a natural food to help your maize grow taller and produce better cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that naturally absorb rainwater and soil nutrients faster than farmed crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing the water and food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures become too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no helpful insects like bees around to move pollen between the flowers to form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ lɛ, koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil can absorb the moisture before the sun gets high. Afternoon sun causes the water to dry up quickly in the heat before the plant's roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ ateshi. Shwane hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ latsaa mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are generally ready for harvest when the green leaves and vines above the ground stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ kwraa

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder after sitting in the barn for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ beni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The powder is caused by tiny insects called grain weevils that bore into the dry maize to eat and lay eggs. Drying your maize thoroughly under the sun and keeping it in sealed, airtight bags stops these bugs from damaging your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths ni shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛye ni amɛwo ŋmãa lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ powda lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-abele lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛwo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn and lose water quickly. Shade trees protect young plants from intense heat and conserve soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to spread their leaves toward the sun. Staking exposes more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and feed the underground tuber so it grows large.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Staking baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant pulls nutrients from older lower leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei lɛ adalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When these plants die or are plowed under, they leave behind natural fertilizer that nourishes the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi loo atswa amɛ buldozer lɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season without dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ni egbooo lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism cassava uses to conserve water during dry spells. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration and rests until the rains return to sprout fresh foliage.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji wala gbɛ ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen inside the flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower is not pollinated successfully, the plant drops it to save energy rather than forming an unhealthy fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ pollination awo mli Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my seeds very close together to fit more into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots compete fiercely for limited soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant proper space allows it to feed well and yield larger fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eye nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, pull water and food away from the mother plant. Removing unnecessary suckers leaves more nutrients for the main tree to produce a heavy, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni he wa ni tsii.

english: If I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest, why do I get a poor crop when I plant them next year?
ga: Kɛji mihere dumɔwui komɛi kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa ni ehiii nɔ beni miduɔ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing specific parent plants to get maximum strength in the first generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities in the next generation, leading to uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni anyɛ ana hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy storms after they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli beni ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top of the tree becomes heavy and wind can easily uproot it unless it is supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii Tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shishi oya. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why am I getting only two or three cocoa pods per tree instead of a full harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ nɔ yɛ tso kome mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Very low pod counts usually happen when the soil lacks essential nutrients or when flowers are not pollinated properly, preventing the tree from supporting more fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pod yibɔ ni baa shi waa lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli loo kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ tso ɔ nyɛ we nɛ e wo yiblii babauu.

english: Why does my cocoa tree need rich soil to produce a lot of pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need essential food and nutrients from the soil to develop flowers into healthy pods; without rich soil, the tree cannot support a heavy harvest.
ga: Niyenii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛná fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: How does adding fertilizer to my farm help my cocoa trees make more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer replaces missing nutrients in the soil, giving the cocoa tree the strength and food it needs to grow abundant pods rather than struggling to produce just a few.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni elaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ofee pods fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ.

english: Can a cocoa tree give a good harvest if the soil has no fertilizer or nutrients?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ sũ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii kpakpai?

english: No, a cocoa tree will struggle in poor soil and will only produce a tiny harvest because it lacks the basic building blocks required to form fruit.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ, ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebɛ shishijee nibii ni he hiaa koni ekɛ yibii aba.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are struggling because of poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: If your cocoa trees produce very few pods despite having flowers, it is a key sign that the soil is out of nutrients and requires fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ fɔfɔi moŋ, no lɛ enɛ ji okadi ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmeii.

english: What is pollination, and why does my cocoa farm need it?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa ni afee pollination lɛ?

english: Pollination happens when tiny insects carry pollen between cocoa flowers. Without this process, cocoa flowers cannot turn into actual cocoa pods.
ga: Pollination baa kɛji kooloi bibii woɔ pollen yɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ gbɛ nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee cocoa ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when they fail to get pollinated by insects, or when the soil lacks the fertilizer and nutrients needed to nourish the developing pod.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: How do small insects help my cocoa trees produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Tiny insects move inside cocoa flowers to transfer pollen, which triggers the tree to start growing pods from those flowers.
ga: Kplukai bibii tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kookoo fɔfɔi amli koni amɛjie pollen. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jeɔ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ashishi.

english: What are the main things a cocoa tree needs to produce an abundant harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa ni cacao tso he hiaa koni enyɛ ekpa nii babaoo?

english: To yield plenty of pods, a cocoa tree needs good pollination for its flowers and plenty of nutrients or fertilizer in the soil to feed the growing fruit.
ga: koni ená pods babaoo Ehe miihia ni Cacao tsei lɛ afee pollin kpakpa ni amɛná niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some cocoa farms get huge yields while neighboring farms get almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Farms with high yields usually have healthier soil with adequate nutrients or fertilizer, along with good insect activity to pollinate the cocoa flowers.
ga: Okwaafoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kooloi bibii ni he esa yɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How does leaving space between my crop plants actually help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishi gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors, leading to stronger roots, healthier leaves, and higher yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni wa Baai lɛ wa. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: What is the difference between row spacing and plant-to-plant spacing when planting crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni akɛtoɔ kɛ tso kɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ teŋ kɛ́ ookwɛ tsei?

english: Row spacing is the distance between two full lines of crops, which gives you path room to walk and farm, while plant-to-plant spacing is the distance between individual seeds or seedlings along the same line.
ga: Row spacing ji gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ateŋ. Enɛ haa onáa gbɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ onyiɛ ni ofee okwaayeli. Yɛ be mli ni tso kɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi loo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ line kome mli lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why is the distance between crop rows usually wider than the distance between plants in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni kã tsei akui ateŋ lɛ da fe gbɛ ni kã tsei ni yɔɔ akui kome mli lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Wider row spaces create clear pathways for farmers to walk, weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest easily without stepping on or damaging the growing crops.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛha okwaafoi ni amɛnyiɛ, amɛjie jwɛi, amɛwo ŋmɔshi nii ni amɛkpa nii. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ shwieee shi loo efiteee

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: If plants are too close, they fight each other for nutrients and light, resulting in tall, thin, weak stems with smaller leaves and much smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛɔ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa, amɛbaai bibii kɛ yibiiwoo fioo kwraa.

english: Why do some farming systems use a smaller distance like 25 centimeters between plants while others use 30 centimeters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi komɛi kɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ sɛntimita 25 tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ateŋ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi kɛ sɛntimita 30 tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Closer spacing like 25 centimeters puts more plants in the field to maximize total yield if the soil is rich, while wider spacing like 30 centimeters gives individual plants more room to grow bigger if nutrients or water are limited.
ga: He ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe, tamɔ sɛntimitai 25 lɛ baaha tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aná yibiiwoo fɛɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni mli kwɔ, tamɔ sɛntimitai 30 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ babaoo ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaa kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nu faaa.

english: How does changing my row spacing from 60 centimeters down to 40 centimeters affect my crop growth?
ga: Te ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni atsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ sɛntimitai 60 kɛyaa sɛntimitai 40 lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Narrowing the rows to 40 centimeters increases the total number of plants on your land and helps the crop canopy cover the ground faster, but leaves narrower paths for walking through the farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi kɛyashɛ sɛntimita 40 lɛ, ebaaha tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. But it will make the path narrower for walking through the farm.

english: How do I know if my crop needs wider spacing or closer spacing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋwɛi ŋta babaoo loo ŋwɛi ŋta babaoo?

english: Smaller or fast-growing crop varieties perform well with closer spacing, whereas taller, leafier, or bushier varieties require wider gaps to avoid shading and crowding each other.
