ga: Tsei bibii loo ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ baai babaoo loo amɛyɛ ŋmɔji babaoo. Gbɛjegbɛi ni da babaoo he miihia koni akafee hulutsoo kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo.

english: Can correct plant spacing help reduce weed growth on my farm?
ga: Ani tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, when crop plants are spaced correctly, their growing leaves shade the bare ground, blocking sunlight and naturally stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Amɛbaai ni miida lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does proper spacing between plants protect my farm from crop diseases?
ga: Te gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaving sufficient space between plants allows air to flow freely, keeping leaves dry and preventing fungal and bacterial diseases from easily jumping from one plant to another.
ga: Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni eha baai lɛ akagbi, ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai akajɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ oya.

english: If I do not have a measuring tape, how can I accurately space my crops during planting?
ga: Kɛji mibɛ tɛi ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: You can cut a stick or rope to your desired distances—such as the length of your hand span or a pre-measured stick—to quickly and consistently measure spaces between rows and plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tso loo kpãa lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni osumɔɔ, tamɔ onine lɛ kɛlɛ loo tso ni asusu momo lɛ. Koni asusu he ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai kɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ oya ni asusu he daa.

english: Why do extension officers want to cut down my cocoa tree when some of its leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ miisumɔ ni amɛfo mi kokoo tsei lɛ? Ani baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli lolo?

english: Even if a cocoa tree still looks somewhat healthy, hidden diseases like swollen shoot virus are already inside it. Cutting it down early prevents the sickness from jumping to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo moŋ. Shi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ bud swelling virus lɛ yɛ mli momo. Ni ooofo mli mra Ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni ji oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: Can a diseased cocoa tree cure itself if I leave it alone and give it good fertilizer?
ga: Ani kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsa ehe kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ekome ni aha lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: No, serious cocoa diseases cannot cure themselves. Leaving an infected tree on your farm allows the disease to spread to nearby healthy trees until your entire farm dies.
ga: Dabi, kookoo hela ni naa wa nyɛŋ atsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ kɛyashi oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo.

english: If I refuse to let officers cut down a sick cocoa tree, what will happen to my farm?
ga: Kɛji mikpoo akɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ baafolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: If a sick tree is left standing, insects and root contact will spread the disease to neighboring healthy trees, eventually killing them and destroying your future harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ hela mɔ tso lɛ, ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kplukai kɛ shishifãi ni taa amɛhe lɛ gbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ amɛ ni efiteɔ owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is getting sick before it completely dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ dani amɛgboi kwraa?

english: Look out for unusual signs such as swollen branches, red veins on young leaves, yellow patterns, or pods growing abnormally small. These signs show the tree is infected before it dries up.
ga: Taomɔ okadii ni yɔɔ srɔto tamɔ tsei niji ni efuu, fãji tsuji ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ tso lɛ dani egbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees suddenly dry up and die after looking healthy for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛye hewalɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees dry up unexpectedly, it usually means a viral disease or pest attack has slowly blocked the flow of water and nutrients inside the trunk over time until the tree collapses.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ gĩ trukaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ etsĩ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ gbee shi lɛ

english: Why do agricultural officers visit my cocoa farm to inspect my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi miiba mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbakwɛ mitsei lɛ?

english: Extension officers inspect farms to spot early signs of dangerous crop diseases before they spread across the whole community and to help you take action to protect your yield.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛna tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ahe okadii mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ. kɛ koni eye ebua bo ni ofee nɔ ko ni okɛbu onibii ahe.

english: What is the work of a cocoa liaison officer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni Cocoa He Gbɛjianɔtolɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ?

english: A liaison officer acts as a bridge between farmers and agricultural services. They help explain why certain steps are needed, assist in getting consent for farm treatments, and ensure farmers get support for replanting.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni kã okwaafoi kɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi ateŋ. Ofainɛ, tsɔɔmɔ nɔ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afee nibii komɛi lɛ mli. Ye obua ni ana hegbɛ kɛha helatsamɔi ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. ni amɛha nɔmimaa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ baaná yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha dumɔwui heei.

english: How does sickness move from one cocoa tree to another across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela ko gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases are commonly spread by tiny insects like mealybugs that travel from sick trees to healthy ones, carrying the virus with them while feeding on the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa. Amɛhiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛyaa amɛhe be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: What should I do immediately if I find a dead cocoa tree on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina kookoo tsei ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should report it to an extension officer right away so they can inspect the surrounding trees to check if disease is spreading nearby and advise you on safe removal.
ga: Esa akɛ abɔ enɛ he amaniɛ aha sɛɛkwɛlɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni anyɛ akwɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. Koni ana kɛji hela ko miigbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi aha bɔ ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings right away in the spot where a diseased tree was cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait and let the ground be cleared and treated properly. Planting immediately near live infected roots can cause the new young seedlings to catch the same disease.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ aba dumɔwui heei anɔ.

english: Why do people plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land instead of separate fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ sɔrɔtoi anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize and cassava grow at different speeds and use soil nutrients at different depths. Maize grows quickly and feeds from the surface soil, while cassava grows slowly and reaches deeper into the ground, allowing you to harvest maize early without stopping the cassava from producing a good yield later.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei daa oya yɛ srɔtoi amli. ni okɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ Abɛi daa oya ni eyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ hiɛ. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, Ehaa okpaa ŋmãa oya ni okpaaa ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no larger shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains around them acts as a living umbrella, keeping the seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even though it has been raining regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to stay green and grow. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks nutrients, the plant cannot feed properly unless you add manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii jogbaŋŋ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and fall over after heavy rain when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ be mli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the farm for too long, it fills up all the air spaces in the soil and drowns the roots. Unable to breathe, the roots rot, which prevents the plant from taking up water and nutrients, causing it to wilt even in wet mud.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛmuɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ yɛ muji ni mli efɔ po mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can get them. If you do not clear the weeds early, your crops will starve while the weeds grow big.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei. Ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land, will I harvest more crop?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ hu? Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: No, planting too closely creates overcrowding. The plants will fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin, weak stems and tiny fruits or very small cobs of corn.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha mɛi ayi obɔ fe nine. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii loo ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of just saving and planting seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mabua dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa ni madu kɛkɛ.

english: Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose their vitality and yield much less over time because of natural cross-breeding in the field. Certified seeds are specially produced to give high yields, grow uniformly, and resist common local diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛfee ekome yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hewɔ. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as sudden hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. The plant drops the flowers to save its strength to survive the bad conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same spot three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over, leaving the soil completely empty. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee efolo kwraa Onibii ni okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii atsake lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the small side shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: The small side shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main plantain stem. By cutting away the extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, the main tree keeps all its energy to grow a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ato ehewalɛ fɛɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ plantains ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no plantain trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and extreme heat. Planting shade crops like plantains creates a living umbrella that shields the young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying before the corn cobs even show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the upper growing leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows signs above ground when mature, such as the main leaves turning yellow and falling off, and cracked soil appearing around the base of the stem where the expanding tubers push the earth upward.
ga: Yucca baajie okadii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpo beni edara lɛ, tamɔ baai titrii ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ je kpo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ, ni yitso ko ni miigbɛ eshwa ni tsiɔ sũ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ he.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry or if the soil lacks steady water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed its blossoms to conserve energy rather than trying to feed fruits it cannot support.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otao yibii ni onyɛɛɛ odamɔ shi lɛ,.

english: Why does my plantain tree shoot up so many small suckers around its base, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally grow suckers from their root systems to multiply. You should cut away most of these shoots, leaving only one or two strong ones, so they do not steal water and soil nutrients away from the main fruiting stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛshwere yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Esa akɛ ofo nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ateŋ babaoo. Ashiɔ tsei 1-2 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ koni amɛkaye nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛ yibiiwoo tso titri lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks keep falling over whenever a strong wind or heavy rain hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni naa wa baatswa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over easily if seeds were planted too close together, which forces the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak as they fight for sunlight. Giving seeds proper spacing creates thicker, stronger stalks with deeper root anchorages.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ koni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe afee mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ́ amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ tsei ni mli tse, ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can catch plenty of direct sunlight to make food. Keeping the vines off the wet ground also protects the leaves from damp soils that cause diseases, resulting in bigger tuber yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛhoo nii. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai baa lɛ he. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baafee babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the underside of leaves. The leaves react to this feeding damage by curling and twisting as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ tsuɔ niyenii ni efiteɔ nɛɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look lifeless in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: During the hottest hours of the day, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil. The leaves droop temporarily to reduce their exposure to the sun, but they normally recover once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni hulu la ni baa lɛ aba shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do I get a smaller maize yield every year if I keep planting on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmãa nɔ daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put essential nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does burning the weeds on my land before planting actually harm my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and essential nutrients like nitrogen that crops need to grow strong. It also kills beneficial insects and soil microbes that break down plant material to keep the soil rich and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahiɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni fiteɔ tsei amli nibii koni sũ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ lɛ hu.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I plant maize on the same field continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it a chance to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black, rot, and shrivel up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ, amɛmiifite, ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches and removing infected pods quickly helps keep air moving and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ amli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, shrinking, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by planting infected stems. You can protect your yield by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn or dry out under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs in its first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha wala. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without growing into any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil is too dry, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady watering during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the sides before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbala kɛmiijɛ sɛɛgbɛ dani eshɛreɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they take in water too fast after a dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to grow faster than the skin can stretch. Keeping soil moisture consistent with regular watering or mulching prevents this.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ kɛji amɛná nu oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my maize is fully mature and dry enough to harvest without spoiling in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni efiteee yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and a small black spot appears at the base of the kernel where it connects to the cob. Drying the harvested grains on a clean tarpaulin until they crack sharply when bitten prevents mold and storage beetles.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpaa gbee yɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛtswaa oya kɛji mɔ ko ŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot usually starts from small cuts or bruises made by farm tools during digging, which allow bacteria and fungi to enter. Storing only undamaged yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn off the ground helps them last for months.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ pilamɔ bibioo ko. loo fãji ni okwaayeli nibii kɛbaa yɛ be mli ni atsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni efiteee pɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I protect my young crops from rotting when the heavy rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ je shishi?

english: Heavy rains can flood soil and rot young roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away, and placing mulch like dry grass around the roots keeps heavy rain from washing the soil away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu afua ni eha shishifãi bibii lɛ agboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekahoo shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and droop during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture out of plant leaves very quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves keeps the ground cool and traps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important food in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or insect pests. Planting shade trees nearby keeps the ground moist and helps flowers stay on the tree to produce pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: What makes my pepper plants shed all their leaves suddenly?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ miiho trukaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed leaves when attacked by tiny pests like mites or when the soil goes from very dry to overly wet. Keeping a steady watering schedule and checking under leaves for pests stops leaf loss.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii tutua amɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa ni akwɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft black patches at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ shishigbɛ dani ahoo?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Watering your garden regularly prevents these dark spots from forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni oooha obɔɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ anaa koni ekafee.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do elders advise planting cassava on mounds instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose earth to swell into large tubers. Planting on mounds gives the roots space to grow thick and keeps excess water from standing around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni etsɔ tsei wuji. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni etsĩ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local soils, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhi kɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my crops before the whole harvest gets ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ miifite?

english: Check your plants early in the morning for small holes in leaves, rolled leaf tips, or sticky residue on stems. Spotting these signs early lets you remove affected parts before pests spread across the entire field.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli leebi kɛji buji bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo nɔ ko ni eshwɛ ni ŋmɛɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shia lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains provides the cool cover and moisture the young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha kookoo bibioo lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground if I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often creates a hot and soggy soil environment without soaking deep enough. Seeds trapped in hot, damp soil can suffocate and rot before they get the steady moisture needed to sprout properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi dani amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Heavy rains or continuous farming without added fertilizer can strip nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Growing the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over, while also allowing crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu baa tsei ni yɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow, they naturally release this extra plant food into the soil for neighboring crops to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛjieɔ tso niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light instead of spending energy on producing fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛshɛ la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants produce tiny underground roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-cassava tsei lɛ miihe shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your cassava. Without enough energy, the cassava plant cannot build up and store food in its roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cassava lɛ mli. Kɛji hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Cassava tsei nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops much more during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry conditions weaken crops because of water stress, making it harder for plants to defend themselves. At the same time, warm weather speeds up how fast insects hatch and multiply.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaabu amɛhe he. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi bibii fɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of wind and insects to pollinate them, preventing the flower from developing into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni baanyɛ afee pollination bɛ. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afeee aduawai.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees if they are growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛji amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning directs the tree's energy into making pods rather than useless branches. It also lets air and light pass through the canopy, which helps stop fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Tso lɛ he ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii yɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la hu tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning yellow in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas next to them creates a canopy that blocks the heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect full-grown cocoa from extreme heat, slow down water evaporation from the soil, and act as windbreakers so heavy storms do not break your crop branches.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo ni eda lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni tsei aniji akakumɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly allows each maize plant to grow thick stalks and produce large, full ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ baaha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa aná ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I grow beans on the same piece of land where I plant my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is very helpful. Beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps your land fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches that waste the tree's energy. It lets sunlight reach the main trunk and improves air movement, which reduces disease and directs all nutrients into making healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni egbo loo ni fa fe nine ni haa tso lɛ he waaa lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients, or lacks tiny insects called midges to pollinate them. Proper shade and keeping the soil moist help flowers stay on the tree to form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Curled and yellowing cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni duɔ ŋmeii tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do black spots spread so quickly across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Weeding regularly and pruning canopy branches lets sunlight in to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la abote mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its color changes completely from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting only ripe pods ensures the beans inside have the right quality for processing.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops if I farm the same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji mitsuɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth as they grow. Farming the same spot continuously exhausts the soil. Allowing land to rest or adding compost restores natural nutrients so future crops grow strong.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Okwaayeli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a seedling in my nursery is healthy enough to plant in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A healthy seedling has smooth, bright green leaves that spread out fully, along with a firm but flexible stem. Plants that look lively and upright early on have the best chance of growing into strong, high-yielding crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ni gbɛ eshwa kwraa. Eyɛ tso ni mli wa shi eyɛ mlɛo Tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ wala mli ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ mra. Eyɛ hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ akɛ ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant young seedlings that already have hard, woody stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni wa momo lɛ?

english: When a seedling's stem hardens while it is still small in the nursery, it means the plant was stunted or stressed. Once a young stem hardens too early, the plant loses its ability to grow vigorously and will fail to thrive after transplanting.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli waɔ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. No tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbɔjɔ loo eyɛ haomɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ tso bibioo lɛ mli wa oya tsɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ eda waa dɔŋŋ, ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What does it mean if my seedling leaves stay crumpled and never open up fully?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeleee kwraa?

english: Leaves that remain crumpled from the time the plant is young indicate that the seedling is suffering from disease, pest damage, or severe lack of nutrients. These plants will not recover well in the main field.
ga: Baai ni egbɔjɔ lolo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela miimɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. loo niyenii ni esaaa ni naa wa Tsei nɛɛ shwereŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do some seedlings in my nursery grow very well while others right next to them stay weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Egbɔjɔ lolo

english: Seedlings can grow unevenly due to small differences in seed quality, uneven watering, local soil pockets, or early pest attacks. Sorting through your nursery to pick only the strong ones ensures your field gets off to a good start.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ ada yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe srɔtofeemɔ fioo hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli muji bu lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shishijee yɛ shishijee bei amli Halamɔ ŋmɔji amli koni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa pɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oniji lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I transplant weak or bad-looking seedlings to my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni tamɔ nɔ ni ehiii lɛ tee miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weak seedlings usually die shortly after transplanting or grow very slowly, wasting your land, labor, and fertilizer. It is much better to discard bad seedlings in the nursery than to care for failing plants in the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ loo amɛdaraa blɛoo waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ, nitsulɔi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii laajeɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshɛrɛ dumɔwui gbohii ashwie tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ fe ni oookwɛ tsei ni efite yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best seedlings when buying or taking plants from a nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ mihe loo mihe tsei kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe?

english: Look closely at the stems and leaves. Pick seedlings with soft, healthy green stems and wide, open leaves, and reject any that have hard stems or wrinkled, distorted leaves.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Halamɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni agbele mli. ni okpoo tsei bibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa loo amɛbaai ni etsilɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: If a seedling has crumpled leaves, can I cut the bad leaves off and plant it anyway?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ Ani manyɛ mafo baai gbohii lɛ ni maya nɔ madu?

english: No, cutting off bad leaves does not fix the problem inside the plant. Crumpled leaves are a sign that the whole seedling is unhealthy, and it will still struggle to grow even if you remove those leaves.
ga: Dabi, baai gbohii ni afolɔ lɛ esaaa naagbai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Baai ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Ni ebaawa lolo akɛ ebaada kɛji ojie nakai baai lɛ po.

english: Why are the young plants I brought from the nursery failing to grow bigger after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛba kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ adara babaoo beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If seedlings had hardened stems or damaged leaf growth before leaving the nursery, they lose their ability to absorb nutrients and expand, causing them to stay small even with good field care.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni edɔ loo amɛbaai lɛ adalɛ efite dani amɛshiɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa efeɔ bibioo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ kpakpa fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does selecting only strong seedlings in the nursery help my final harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni mihalaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ?

english: Strong seedlings establish roots faster, resist diseases better, and grow at the same rate. This creates an even crop canopy in your field, leading to higher overall production at harvest time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baawo shishifãi oya. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni edaa yɛ oyaiyeli kome mli Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: What are the main visual signs that I should discard a seedling before transplanting?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii titrii ni anaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwie dani mikɛwo he kroko?

english: You should discard seedlings that have pale or crumpled leaves that look stuck in their early growth stage, as well as seedlings whose lower stems have turned hard and woody too soon.
ga: Esa akɛ oshɛrɛ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ekpɔtɔ ni tamɔ nɔ ni ekã shi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ oshwie. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji dumɔwui ni amɛshishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei oya tsɔ.

english: Why do I need to measure and place pegs when planting my plantains instead of just digging holes anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu ni mikɛ ŋmeii awo mli kɛ́ midu plantains lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Pegging ensures proper spacing—usually about 10 feet apart—so every plantain tree gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without crowding or competing with nearby crops.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa—bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 10—no hewɔ lɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ eyiŋ loo ekɛ akaŋ akaŋ

english: What is the main benefit of organizing my cocoa and plantain farm in straight lines?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ kookoo kɛ plantain ŋmɔji ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ he?

english: Planting in neat, measured rows makes it much easier to walk through your farm, clear weeds, apply fertilizer, and prune trees without accidentally stepping on or damaging young plants.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ ooonyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, okɛ jwɛi awo mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okɛ tsei bibii lɛ abɔi shi yɛ oshara mli loo ofiteee amɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings from my plantain trees?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ama he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa is typically planted alongside plantains in a structured grid (often 10 feet apart) so the plantain provides nearby shade without its root system immediately smothering the cocoa.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ kookoo yɛ plantains ahe yɛ gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ nɔ. (Bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi 10.) No hewɔ lɛ, plantain lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ tsiii kookoo lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Should I plant my plantain suckers before or at the same time as my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu plantain lɛ dani loo yɛ be kome too mli? kɛ kookoo dumɔwui

english: It is best to plant plantains slightly before or at the same time as cocoa so the plantain leaves grow big enough in time to protect the young cocoa from intense sun during the hot dry season.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantain fioo dani loo yɛ be kome mli kɛ kookoo lɛ bɔni afee ni plantain baai lɛ anyɛ adara yɛ be ni sa mli koni ebu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: When and why will I need to cut down the plantains growing on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be kɛ mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once cocoa trees mature and grow a full canopy, they require direct sunlight to produce well. At that stage, you cut down the plantains so they stop competing with the adult cocoa for light and nutrients.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa ni eshɛ eshishijee he lɛ. Hulu la he miihia amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, ehe baahia ni ofolɔ plantains lɛ koni amɛkpa akaŋshii kɛ cocoa ni eda lɛ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Can I plant coconut trees on the same piece of land alongside my plantain and cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ plantain kɛ kookoo masɛi?

english: Yes, but coconut trees grow very tall and spread wide roots. You must plan their spacing carefully so they do not block all sunlight or rob the soil nutrients needed by your cocoa and plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi akokoo tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ waa ni amɛshishifãi lɛɛ. Esa akɛ oto he ni okɛ ohe baawo mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okatsĩ hulu lɛ naa loo okafite shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni haa kookoo kɛ plantain yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Will plantain trees steal food and water from my cocoa seedlings if they grow close together?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Plantains do consume nutrients, but the sun protection they give young cocoa outweighs the minor competition. Adding organic compost or fertilizer ensures both crops get enough nourishment.
ga: Plantains yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ Shi hulu hebuu ni Mild Cocoa kɛhaa lɛ bɛ nɔ ko kwraa fe akaŋshii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I safely cut down old plantain stems without crushing the young cocoa plants underneath them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ plantain tsei momo lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieee shi?

english: You should cut the plantain stems carefully in small sections and manually direct their fall away from the delicate cocoa plants so the heavy stems don't break the young cocoa branches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo plantain tsei lɛ amli bibii bibii ni okɛ blɛoo ajɛ cacao tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei niji ni tsii lɛ akaha kookoo niji bibii lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do plantain leaves sometimes dry up and turn brown when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kɛ́ adu plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, egbiɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Plantains require strong soil moisture and can get heat-stressed in completely clear, dry ground. Mulching around the roots helps retain moisture and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Plantains biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni ebaanyɛ ena amanehulu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli yɛ hei ni egbi ni hulu lɛ tse. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops start rotting or dropping off after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain creates a damp, wet environment that allows fungal diseases to grow and spread very quickly, especially on delicate parts of the plant like the flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: How does rainy weather make plant diseases spread faster on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nugbɔshiimɔ haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Raindrops splash disease spores from the soil or infected plants onto healthy leaves and flowers, while the moisture helps the disease thrive and multiply.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa helai ni amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why are crop flowers more easily destroyed by disease during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai fiteɔ tsei fɔfɔi oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers are soft and tender compared to leaves, so when moisture stays on them for long periods, rain-loving diseases can easily break into them and cause rot.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ blɛoo kɛ akɛto baai lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ hi fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ Nugbɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ abote mli oya ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba.

english: Why is it important to spray medicine on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Spraying protective medicine (like fungicides) puts a protective shield on your plants that stops damp-weather diseases from attacking and destroying the flowers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa (tamɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii) lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ otsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni helai ni yɔɔ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ akatutua fɔfɔi ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: When is the right time to spray medicine on my flowering crops during the wet season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ mi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You should apply the spray early in the rainy period or immediately after heavy rains start, before damp-weather diseases have a chance to take root and destroy the blossoms.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Dani helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli baa lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛwo shishifãi ni amɛfite fɔfɔi lɛ,

english: Can spraying crop medicine save my plant blossoms from disease damage?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ayiwala kɛjɛ helai ni baafite amɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, using the correct spray kills the harmful fungi and bacteria that thrive in wet conditions, protecting your flowers so they can turn into healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Ye obua ni obu ofɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What type of medicine should I buy to protect my crop flowers from rain-induced rot?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa esa akɛ mahe koni mikɛbu mifɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he?

english: You need a fungicide or chemical spray specifically meant to control fungal blights and rots that attack flowering plants in wet weather.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛkudɔ sɛɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why should I inspect my farm right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Checking your farm right after rain allows you to spot early signs of wet-weather diseases on your plants so you can take action before the infection spreads.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hela eba otsei lɛ anɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ofee nɔ ko dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: What specific signs should I look out for on my plants when rain starts falling heavily?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa?

english: You should check the flowers and leaves for unusual spots, blackening, wilting, or rotting, which are signs that damp-weather diseases are beginning to take over.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli kɛji amɛyɛ he ko ni yɔɔ srɔto, amɛmiiwo duŋ, amɛmiigbo, loo amɛmiigbo. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli helai miibɔi amɛhe shweremɔ.

english: Is it bad for rainwater to stay on my crop leaves and flowers for a long time?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu baahi mitsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, standing water left on plants creates the exact wet conditions that fungal diseases need to grow, thrive, and ruin your upcoming harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi ni ashiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛshwere ni amɛfite onibii ni baa lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants keep turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is too waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right time helps the plant produce green chlorophyll and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tsei amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee klorofil eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to excessive heat, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with organic mulch prevents heat stress and keeps flowers intact.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, ni akɛ organic mulch aha sũ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akatsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early using proper yellow sticky traps or recommended sprays helps protect the plants from getting infected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Control Kɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stems and low yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow large and produce well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they are planted too deep, or if underground insects eat them. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in moist, loose soil ensures good germination.
ga: Bean dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. adu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ŋmei dumɔwui Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni mli ewo muji nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small round holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji tɔmɔ ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ ayeli he?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the Diamondback Moth larvae. Spraying neem oil or an approved insect spray early in the morning kills these caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback moth lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds come up much faster than my crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that adapt quickly and absorb water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the morning or afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water crops early in the morning when the sun is cool, allowing roots to soak up water deeply. Afternoon watering causes quick evaporation in the heat and can scorch warm leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli ejɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ mli shwieɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land needs animal manure before planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia kooloi aŋmei dani madu ŋmei?

english: If your soil is dry, sandy, or yields very small tubers, it lacks organic matter. Adding well-rotted chicken or cow manure enriches the soil structure and helps cassava tubers store more starch and grow bigger.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, ŋã yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ bulbs bibii waa. Etsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina loo tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifã lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmei babaoo mli ni efeɔ agbo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains feel hard when pressed with a fingernail. Harvesting on time prevents mould and insect attacks in the field.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa. ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine ŋmei miimɔ amɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn healthy green so the ears can grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Toi lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants have curled leaves and refuse to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpoo akɛ ebaawo yibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites under the leaves. Spraying them early with neem oil or appropriate crop protection products stops the insects so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo baa mli ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo nibii krokomɛi ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ kpaa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too stressed from high heat or lack of water in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently damp and providing light shade during extremely hot periods keeps the flowers attached so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao fe nine. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akabɔle amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my groundnut crop produce empty shells with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods usually happen when the soil lacks calcium or enough moisture while the pods are filling underground. Adding agricultural lime to the soil before planting helps ensure full, solid nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni afu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli lime wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay small even when the main stem looks tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains need huge amounts of water and soil nutrients right when the flowering stem begins to form inside. If the soil is dry or poor at that moment, the tree stays big but the fruit bunch turns out small.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji fɔfɔii ashishifãi je shishi amɛfee yɛ emli pɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo ehiii yɛ nakai beaŋ Tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi agbo shi aduawai lɛ baaja mli awo kui bibii amli.

english: Why are my yam tubers cracking open underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams crack when heavy rains follow a dry spell, causing the tuber to absorb water suddenly and expand faster than its skin can stretch. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching helps prevent this.
ga: Sweet potatoes tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ nu trukaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do crops in one part of my field grow tall while crops in another part stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ kɛlɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes across a field due to past water flow, shade, or heavy farming that washed away nutrients. Applying organic manure or compost to the weak areas feeds the soil so all your crops grow equally well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su etsake yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, hulutsoo, loo okwaayeli ni tsii ni hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni onibii fɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow well even when I do not add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food for themselves. They actually leave the soil richer for the next crops you plant after them.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my cassava stems?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei?

english: The best time to plant cassava cuttings is right after the first steady rains begin so the soil is soft and wet, allowing roots to sprout quickly before dry periods return.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni edɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛdaraa oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do weeds harm my young cocoa trees so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa trees and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food your cocoa needs to survive. Clearing weeds regularly leaves all the nutrients for your cocoa tree to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa okookoo lɛ koni ehi shi. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni kookoo tso lɛ adara oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which can happen after heavy rains wash nutrients away. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base gives the plants the food they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ efite sɛɛ. Shishitoo lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Crops can only absorb fertilizer through their roots when there is water present. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots and waste your money because the plant cannot drink dry nutrients.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nu yɛ pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ anu niyenii ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of food from the soil, but leguminous crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, making the land fertile again for the next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots and causes them to rot under the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efooo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms that like to feed on the tender young leaves inside the center funnel of corn. Catching them early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem leaf mixture protects the crop before the growing point is destroyed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani he ni amɛdaraa lɛ akpata.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves in your farm because they steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the nourishment they need to produce large harvests.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ ejuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella to shield them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam plants use their vines to lift their leaves up toward the sun to manufacture energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposed to sunlight, which allows the plant to send more food down to build bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ wain tsei woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii babaoo kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil lacks water. Keeping the soil moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
