ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce small fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants are planted too close, their leaves shade each other from sunlight and their roots fight for the same soil food. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light, air, and nourishment to grow big fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tomato ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛha niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plants will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he kɛbɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field where I grow my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for your yams. They also cover the bare ground to keep moisture in the soil and stop weeds from taking over.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ hu nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko, ni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right on the branch during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a small fungus that spreads fast in damp, shaded cocoa farms. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and air in, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ afolɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up with light green and yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting healthy, disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent your crop from getting damaged.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Akɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whiteflies lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Cassava henɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsei lɛ afitemɔ naa.

english: Why are holes appearing in the stalks of my corn with saw-dust coming out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: These holes are made by stem borer caterpillars that eat their way inside the plant stalk, making the corn weak so it breaks easily in strong wind. Planting early in the season and dropping a little clean wood ash into the plant heart helps keep them away.
ga: Buji nɛɛ jɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, efoɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu mra yɛ be lɛ mli ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse fioo ko fata tso lɛ tsui he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa like an umbrella until the cocoa gets strong enough to stand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: What will happen to my crop if I bury maize seeds very deep in the ground when planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: If maize seeds are planted too deep, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil to find light, causing them to emerge weak or rot underground. Planting at a depth equal to the first joint of your finger gives them the best start.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsɔ mli koni ena la lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dumɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ onine klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ haa shishijee ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the flower blossoms dropping off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Adding dry grass or palm leaves around the roots as mulch helps keep the ground cool and moist so the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ afee aduawai.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and collapsing around the trunk before the fruit bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ he dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when tiny microscopic worms called nematodes attack the roots, stopping the plant from taking up water and food. Using clean, healthy suckers treated with hot water before planting keeps the root system strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii kɛtsɔ nu ni mli edɔ nɔ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants producing big wide leaves but refusing to form a hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaaba lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ekpooɔ akɛ ehiɛ yitso ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or experience erratic watering. Balancing your fertilizer and maintaining regular watering encourages the inner leaves to curl tightly into a solid ball.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo ena nu ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ nu awo mli daa lɛ, ebaawo mligbɛ baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Yellowing and burnt tips usually mean the young trees are getting too much direct heat without enough shade crops like plantain or shade trees nearby.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ashã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tso bibioo lɛ etsɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods even begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry conditions, lack of nutrients in the soil, or a shortage of small pollinating insects. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during flowering helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: How do I know if my cocoa pod is turning yellow because it is ripe or because it is diseased?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: A healthy cocoa pod turns uniformly yellow or orange when ripe and feels firm. If a pod shows dark brown or black patches, shrinks, or grows soft powder on it, it is infected with black pod disease and should be safely removed.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo akutu kɛji ekwɛ̃ ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ lɛ, egbɔjɔɔ, loo powda ni yɔɔ blɛoo jeɔ kpo. Etsɔɔ akɛ black pod hela lɛ emɔ pods lɛ. ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many leaves during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during the dry Harmattan season as a natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating through their leaves, helping the tree preserve moisture in its trunk and roots until rain returns.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do crops like cocoa need shade trees while crops like maize need full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he hiaa tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Different crops require different amounts of light. Maize needs direct, intense sunlight to make food for heavy grains, while forest crops like cocoa naturally grow under larger trees that shield them from drying out in high heat.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ la babaoo. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, koo mli tsei tamɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Plants close tiny pores on their leaves during the hottest hours to prevent moisture from escaping into the dry air. As long as the leaves stand back up by evening, this drooping is just a temporary defense against heat.
ga: Tso lɛ tsiɔ bu bibioo lɛ naa. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje kpo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ teɔ shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Nɛkɛ gbee nɛɛ ji be kukuoo mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my trees suddenly burst into heavy flowering right after the first rain following a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifɔlɔ waa trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The long dry spell acts as a signal for the plant to prepare for reproduction. When the first heavy rain arrives, the sudden drink of water triggers the tree to release all its stored energy into a flush of blossoms.
ga: Be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi kɛhaa tso lɛ koni esaa ehe kɛha fɔmɔ. Beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba Nu ni anuɔ trukaa lɛ baaha tso lɛ ajie ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kpo ni etsɔ fɔfɔii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge leaves and stems but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, plants focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy tops. Adding balanced nutrients like potassium encourages the crop to push its energy underground into swelling the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni ja tamɔ potassium fata he lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How does wet weather and continuous rain affect the pods growing directly on my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ saa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Continuous rain creates cold, damp conditions that help fungal spores spread easily across wet cocoa trunks and pods, leading to rot. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through to dry out the pods after rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo tsei kɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ amli oya. lead to decay Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my actual crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi tsei diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with aggressive roots adapted to drink water and take nutrients from the top layer of soil faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing your crop's food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnu nu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: How do I know when my maize field is ready to be harvested by a machine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaatsɔ tsɔne nɔ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for mechanical harvesting when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard with low moisture. If harvested while still wet, the machine can crush the grains instead of shelling them properly.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ kɛ́ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa. Kɛji akɛ akpa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ Tsɔne lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ dumɔwui anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm land need to be cleared of tree stumps and large rocks before using heavy harvesting equipment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmeii kɛ tɛi wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akɛ nibii ni tsii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ?

english: Hidden tree stumps and big rocks can break the metal blades or bend the parts of heavy machinery, causing costly breakdowns and stopping the harvest.
ga: Tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tɛi wuji baanyɛ akumɔ dade ŋmeii loo amɛfo nibii ni tsii. Enɛ haa ŋshɔkei ni jara wa waa baa ni ekpaa ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Heavy rains can wash nutrients deep into the soil away from the roots, so applying fertilizer at the right time helps the plant stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: Why do young cocoa plants die if I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn and dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides shade and retains moisture to protect the young trees until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe wa.

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when they suffer from high heat, uneven watering, or too much fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I space my plantain suckers far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala plantain tsei lɛ amli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Plantains need plenty of sunlight, water, and soil food to produce heavy bunches. When planted too close together, they fight for these resources, resulting in thin stems and small fruit.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la babaoo, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye akaŋ yɛ nibii nɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or if stems are planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and wither when the weather is very humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High humidity and rain create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to spread on leaves. Spacing plants properly and removing lower leaves near the soil improves airflow and keeps the leaves dry.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii helai ni baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: How do armyworms destroy young maize crops so quickly without being easily seen?
ga: Te cutworms lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ efiteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ oya ni anaaa amɛ oya?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants where they eat the softest parts of the leaves during the night, making the damage appear suddenly before you notice the insects.
ga: Asraafoi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ahe ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ gbɛkɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni efite lɛ jeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani oyɔseɔ kooloo lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up right before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn yellow and dry out at the end of the growing season because the plant is transferring all its remaining energy down into the underground tuber, signaling that the yam is mature and ready to dig up.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naagbee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ miijie ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their delicate leaves from burning under direct sunlight while their roots are still developing. Planting shade crops like plantains creates a protective canopy that keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miida lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my maize leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil food or too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nu babaoo hewɔ?

english: If leaves turn yellow starting from the center vein near the bottom of the plant, the soil lacks nitrogen. If the soil is continuously soggy and all leaves look pale and droopy, the roots are suffocating from excess water.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni baai lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does mixing animal manure into my field work better over time than using chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure builds up the physical structure of the soil, helping it hold water and nutrients longer, whereas chemical fertilizer gives quick plant food but does not improve long-term soil health.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã ji nɔ ni feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛjianɔtoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do insect pests multiply so fast on my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi fa oya yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects reproduce much faster in warm, dry weather. Rainy weather naturally washes away many small pests and their eggs, so without rain, pest populations grow rapidly.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwuji lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ baaya hiɛ oya.

english: Why do white spots appear on my pepper leaves after a warm spell following heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warmth combined with high moisture creates the perfect environment for fungal spores to germinate and spread across crop leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo fata he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much nitrogen, the plant sends most of its energy upward into leaf and stem growth instead of storing energy in the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why should I target selling my fresh produce to hotels in places like Takoradi instead of only relying on the open local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo mli akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ nibii heei ni anáa lɛ mahã gbɔiatoohei ni yɔɔ he ko tamɔ Takoradi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei ni agbele naa lɛ pɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Hotels and restaurants require a continuous, reliable supply of fresh produce and often offer stable prices, whereas open markets can become oversaturated with crops, leading to price drops.
ga: Hoteli kɛ niyelihei biɔ ni akɛ nibii heei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ aba be fɛɛ be. ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ jara ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ haa. Yɛ be mli ni jara lɛ naa lɛ, ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaba ni no baaha amɛjara aba shi.

english: Why is it better for me to water my tomato crop early in the morning instead of during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb moisture before hot afternoon sun causes rapid evaporation, preventing heat stress on the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ shi oya. Tsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ naa

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce weaker plants than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ajie midumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli ni woɔ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mlijalɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their original vigor and disease resistance over time, while certified seeds are specifically bred to yield strong plants and higher harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite amɛ shishijee hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni mli wa ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting a maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil through their roots.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense heat and sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them creates temporary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist, acting like a protective canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la shishi. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tso ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baanyɛ aná tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune the extra branches and suckers off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ tsei ni fa fe nine ni jɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting off unwanted suckers and excess branches opens up the tree canopy so light and air can circulate freely. This reduces the dampness that causes black pod disease and ensures the tree directs its nutrients toward producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni ataooo kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaagbele tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ naa. Koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ cocoa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to stay green. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores leaf color and helps the plant grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee fɛo ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the leaf funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf whorl and feeds on tender leaves. Spotting this early allows you to apply safe treatments before the pest destroys the center leaf point of the stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii lɛ. Enɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ nii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slanted angle instead of straight up in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanted angle encourages tubers to develop close to the surface in a cluster, which allows them room to grow larger and makes digging them up during harvest much easier.
ga: Cassava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ woɔ cassava ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ yɛ kui amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa. Ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni atsaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for underground tuber growth. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, exposing maximum leaf area to the sun while preventing damp leaves from rotting on the wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha baa lɛ he lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing mulch around the roots helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni enyɛ etsɔ tomato.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper field early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper ŋmɔji lɛ amli nu leebi loo shwane be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before heat builds up. Watering in the hot afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate quickly before roots can take it up and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada ni eha tso lɛ yibii ni mli edɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas refreshes the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant cover crops like velvet beans or cowpeas on my field when I am letting the land rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ velvet beans loo cowpeas yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be ni miha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ

english: Cover crops shield bare soil from being washed away by heavy rains and pull natural nitrogen out of the air to feed the soil, making the ground rich and ready for your next main crop without buying expensive fertilizers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ. ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni efee klalo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why do we make high mounds or ridges for growing yam instead of planting directly on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand into large, long tubers without resistance. High mounds keep the soil loose, improve drainage so the tubers do not rot in heavy rain, and make harvesting much easier.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii agboi kakadaji ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Gɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ etsɔɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Ani ehe miihia?

english: Yes, it matters a lot. Cassava cuttings must be planted with the buds on the stem pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downward first, which stresses the plant and drastically lowers your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. Aduɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow along the middle instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start in a V-shape from the tip along the center usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen early in its growth to build strong green leaves for big cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ V su kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa yɛ edalɛ shishijee mli koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa aba kɛha ŋmãa wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, they leave this natural plant food behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and dropping during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under full sun and dry winds because their roots cannot absorb soil water fast enough. They drop leaves to avoid drying out completely, which is why temporary shade plants like plantain are needed.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya bɔ ni sa. Amɛshɛrɛɔ baai lɛ amɛshwieɔ koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ana tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that act like large umbrellas, providing the young cocoa trees with the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my fresh tomatoes rotting and turning black at the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ miifite ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: Black, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are usually caused by a condition called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil moisture fluctuates unevenly, preventing the plant roots from absorbing enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato ni shishi edɔ ni ebote mli lɛ baa. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, very dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central growing funnel of the plant. They feed heavily on young leaves and must be controlled early to prevent destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii babaoo ni esa akɛ akudɔ amɛ mra koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and stunted even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops before the crop roots can reach them, starving your crop of what it needs to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani amɛshɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantain around them creates a cool environment, protecting the tender leaves from scorching until the trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa. Buu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the plant's growth helps keep the leaves green and improves yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii yɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer when the ground is dry or after rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is moist after rain. Plant roots can only absorb nutrients that are dissolved in water, and applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop's roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli pɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã.

english: Can I plant cassava using seeds, or do I always have to cut and plant the stems?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli? Aloo esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei lɛ ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be?

english: While cassava produces seeds, planting stem cuttings is standard because they grow much faster and ensure the new plant produces the same high tuber yield as the original plant.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei woɔ dumɔwui lɛ Grafting ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ ejaakɛ edaa oya waa ni ehaa nɔmimaa akɛ tso hee lɛ baawo bulbs ni fa babaoo tamɔ tsutsu tso lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plantain stem for food, water, and sunlight. Removing excess shoots so that only one or two remain ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops when they are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛdarako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal the water, light, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows young crops to establish strong roots without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛmaa shishitoo ni wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to high temperatures or lack of water, which prevents pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowering plants nearby to attract pollinators helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ji hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo nu ni bɛ, ni no haaa pollination aba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ fɔfɔi tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni agbala fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden sticks instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ niji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking allows yam leaves to capture more sunlight to make food for the plant. Leaving vines on the ground exposes leaves to heat and soil diseases, leading to smaller tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la babaoo ni ekɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ baa hulutsoo kɛ sũ mli helai. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the top fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛtee ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest feeding on the growing center of the maize plant. Spraying approved insecticides or organic treatments early prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni edaa lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akafite he ni kooloi lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into white powder and get full of holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ ni eyɛ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils eat through dry grains to feed and lay eggs. Drying your maize properly and storing it in airtight containers or specialized bags starves the insects of air and protects your harvest.
ga: Picker kooloi tamɔ weevils yeɔ ŋmaa ni egbi kɛtsɔɔ niyenii nɔ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaabu onibii ahe.

english: How can I identify a cassava plant in my field without having to dig up the roots to look at them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuuu nii koni mana amɛ?

english: Cassava plants can be easily identified above ground by their distinct leaves, which spread out into finger-like segments resembling an open hand, usually with 3 to 7 distinct lobes on a single leaf stem.
ga: Abaanyɛ ana Yucca tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlɛo kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa fãi ni tamɔ nineshi ni tamɔ nine ni agbele mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi 3 kɛyashi 7 yɛ ŋmeii kome nɔ.

english: Is there a way to tell sweet cassava from bitter cassava just by looking at the leaves or stems?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aleɔ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ kɛtsɔ baai loo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Sweet and bitter cassava look almost identical above ground, so leaf shape alone isn't reliable. Farmers usually tell them apart by stem and leaf stalk colors specific to local varieties, or by knowing the history of the planting stock.
ga: Cassava ni ŋɔɔ kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ fɛɛ tamɔ nɔ kome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ baa lɛ pɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi tsɔɔ amɛmli kɛtsɔ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe su pɔtɛɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he yinɔsane ni ale lɛ nɔ

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lowest leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem starts to crack as the expanding tubers push the earth upward.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko miishɛ edalɛ he beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does the soil crack around the bottom of my cassava stem as the season goes on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli fãa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil cracking at the base of the stem is a normal sign of underground growth. It means the roots are swelling into thick tubers and expanding outward beneath the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli etse yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dalɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: My cassava leaves are dropping off the plant, does this mean my crop is dying?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi?

english: If the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off slowly while the top leaves remain healthy, the plant is simply maturing and transferring its energy into developing underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi fiofio yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛhe wa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miida ni ekɛ hewalɛ miiwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Which direction should the small bumps on a cassava stem cut face when I plant it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ afo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: The small bumps (eyebuds) on the stem cut must always point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow properly and yields will be very low.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii (buds) ni yɔɔ tsei ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ Ewa akɛ eeekwɛ̃ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to save for my next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛto kɛha shweremɔ be ni baa lɛ?

english: Select thick, mature stems from strong, disease-free plants that produced high tuber yields. Use the middle section of the stem, avoiding the soft green top and the dry bottom base.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni mli tse, ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai bɛ mli ni woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli. Okɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishi ni egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do cassava leaves stay high above the ground while the edible part stays hidden underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ be mli ni fãi ni ayeɔ lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: The green leaves above ground capture sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. That food travels down the stem and gets stored in the underground roots as starch, which forms the tubers.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛhaa tsei lɛ niyenii. Niyenii lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli yɛ ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: My cassava plants are developing flowers at the top, will this affect the food growing under the soil?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi. Ani ebaana niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Flowering is a normal growth phase for many cassava varieties. It shows the plant is mature, though root growth will slow down slightly because the plant is dividing energy between seeds and tubers.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni sa kɛha ŋmei srɔtoi babaoo. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, shishifãi lɛ adalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo, ejaakɛ tso lɛ miija ehewalɛ mli yɛ dumɔwu lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ teŋ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow as one straight stem while others branch out widely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni ja ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ niji ni mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Branching depends on the cassava variety and soil fertility. Some varieties naturally branch early to create shade and suppress weeds, while others grow straight up and branch late.
ga: Niji ni baa lɛ damɔ ŋmei henɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Henɔi komɛi shwereɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulutsoo aba ni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi daa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛwoɔ niji blɛoo lɛ.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety introduced in Ghana will grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛba Ghana lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: New crop varieties are tested in different agricultural zones across Ghana to make sure they resist local pests, tolerate weather conditions, and yield well before being recommended to farmers.
ga: Aka tsei srɔtoi heei akwɛ yɛ okwaayeli hei srɔtoi. Ghana fɛɛ Enɛ ji koni ana akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai dani ajieɔ lɛ kpo atsɔɔ okwaafoi

english: What makes a newly introduced seed variety better than the traditional seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui heei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ hi fe blema dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ koni mikakpa lɛ?

english: Newly introduced varieties are usually bred to mature faster, produce higher yields per acre, and withstand dry spells better than older seeds saved over many seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ajie amɛ kpo nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Yibiiwoo ni fa yɛ acre kome mli ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi fe dumɔwui momo ni akɛto bei babaoo.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I plant them at a specific time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Crops rely on specific rainfall and sunlight cycles; planting at the recommended time ensures seeds get enough soil moisture to build strong roots during early growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ hulutsoo be nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ be ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa yɛ amɛdalɛ be mli mra.

english: Why do some seeds fail to sprout even when the soil looks moist and ready for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni esa akɛ adu lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they are old, buried too deep in the soil, damaged by underground pests, or planted when soil temperatures are too high.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ. afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite loo adu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ wa tsɔ.

english: Why does a crop variety that yields very well in another part of Ghana perform poorly on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana fã kroko lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions in Ghana have distinct soil types, temperatures, and rainfall levels, so a seed bred for wet forest zones may not produce well in drier savanna areas.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ekolɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ kɛha kooi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ savannah hei ni egbi lɛ.

english: Is it true that planting the exact same crop on the same land every year weakens the soil?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ?

english: Yes, planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots and preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe. shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ

english: What causes my crops to grow huge, healthy-looking leaves but yield very little grain or fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ baai agboi ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai fioo ko pɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into growing leaves and stems rather than developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm more during certain times of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ bei komɛi amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pest populations surge when weather conditions like warmth and humidity favor breeding, and when young, soft plant tissues are available for them to feed on.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, tamɔ latsaa kɛ latsaa, haa amɛfɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ tso mli fãji bibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛye.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing nutrients before I even plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani madu tsei?

english: You can notice signs from previous harvests like stunted plant growth, low yields, or weed types that thrive in poor soil, or you can request a simple soil test through an extension officer.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona okadii ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli, tamɔ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi, loo jwɛi henɔi ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Aloo obaanyɛ obi ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akwɛ bo yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ. kɛtsɔ hiɛyaa he nitsulɔi anɔ

english: Why do crops grow so tall and green on some pieces of land, while on other lands nearby they remain small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔji komɛi anɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔji krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Land fertility varies based on organic matter, soil depth, and nutrient levels. Rich soil retains moisture and nutrients better, feeding the plant continuously, whereas exhausted or degraded soil lacks the essential food plants need to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ srɔtoi yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite loo efite lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my soil need fertilizer or compost if wild weeds grow easily on my land without any help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii? Akɛni koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Wild weeds have deep, tough root systems adapted to survive on low nutrients, but farm crops are bred to produce high food yields, which requires far more nutrients than untamed soil naturally supplies.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mli. Shi akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ koni niyenii babaoo aba. ni biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why can't I plant as many seeds as possible close together so I can harvest more food from my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce tiny fruits or no harvest at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ loo amɛwoɔ yibii kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants look tall, thin, and weak when I grow them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to produce energy. When planted under deep shade, they stretch unnaturally high trying to reach the light, spending all their energy on height instead of growing strong stems and fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ shishi lɛ Amɛbaashɛ amɛhe kɛya he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛha la. kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa Moŋ lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ tsei kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a sudden dry spell that bakes the topsoil. If young seeds germinate right away, the hot dry ground will scorch their tender roots before the regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa ni haa sũ lɛ yiteŋ sũ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ He ni edɔ, ni egbi lɛ baashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when the dry harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather as a survival mechanism to conserve water. By losing leaves, the plant reduces water evaporation and rests safely underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and look dead during hot afternoons even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni amɛdaraaa lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose moisture faster than roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, but usually bounces back once the evening air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Tsei gboiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi esumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe aku sɛɛ aba kɛji gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my crops rot and die when rain water sits on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like human beings do. Waterlogged soil blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to drown, rot, and fail to feed the plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests a permanent home. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha kooloi bibii lɛ ahi shi daa Rotation ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally aggressive and built for survival, whereas cultivated crops focus their energy on producing edible fruits and seeds, making them less competitive against wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ basabasa ni ama amɛ koni amɛhi shi. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni ayeɔ lɛ ahe nii. Enɛ haaa enyɛ ekɛ koo mli tsei abɔ akaŋ.

english: Why should I plant grafted orange trees instead of planting seeds directly from an orange I ate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmei tso ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmei ni miyeɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafted trees produce sweet fruit much faster, usually within two to three years instead of seven or more. They also grow stronger roots that resist common soil diseases.
ga: Tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ oya kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli yɛ afii kpawo loo nɔ ni fe nakai najiaŋ. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa hu ni teɔ shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra small shoots growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plant. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in bigger and heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie mɛi babaoo lɛ, ebaashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa plantains akui wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off old, yellowing leaves from the bottom of my cocoa and plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo kɛ plantain baai ni egbɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Removing old leaves opens up the crop to sunlight and airflow, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading and allows the plant to send its energy to fresh growth and fruit.
ga: Baai momoi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ yaa dalɛ kɛ aduawai heei amli.

english: Why is it good to cover the ground around my young crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground keeps the soil cool and moist during hot dry periods, stops weeds from taking over, and feeds the soil as the dead leaves rot.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ baai ni egboi lɛ egbo.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my trees by hand instead of burning the whole field with fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ minine ajie jwɛi ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ la baawo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms like earthworms, while damaging the delicate roots of young trees near the surface.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni efiteɔ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hu.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees sometimes drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects to pollinate them, and the tree will also shed flowers if it suffers from lack of shade, water, or proper soil nutrients.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha pollination. Ni tsei hu baafɔ kɛji amɛna amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa, nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing many flowers but no fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palms often produce male flowers instead of fruit-bearing female flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or lack of sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii yɛ fɔfɔi yei najiaŋ kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo hulu la ni bɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during small storms even when the stem looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum bibioo ko mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔne lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by underground pests like root nematodes. Without a strong root anchor, the heavy plant falls easily in wind or rain.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kɛji shishifã ni mli wa bɛ lɛ Tsei ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my citrus tree turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil that cannot drain properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ eta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my cocoa trees instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing lets air move freely through the farm and allows sunlight to reach the lower branches, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading easily.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ akagbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spoil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for a fungal disease called black pod to thrive and spread rapidly across cocoa pods through water droplets.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ. Koni eda ni egbɛ eshwa oya kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ nu mli ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees getting chewed up and covered in tiny bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii bibii haa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids (capsids) feed on soft young leaves and shoots, injecting saliva that destroys plant tissues and damages the health of the tree.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids (capsids) yeɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Shwɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni efiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches, allowing the tree to send its water and nutrients directly into growing larger and healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is my old cocoa tree producing far fewer pods than it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their roots become less effective at drawing nutrients from the soil, causing pod production to naturally decline.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa pod feemɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crop turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why does leaving dry fallen leaves on the ground around my cocoa trees help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as natural mulch that retains soil moisture, suppresses weeds, and breaks down over time to return natural fertilizers back to the soil.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same farm plot as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cassava has strong, spreading roots that aggressively compete with young cocoa trees for soil nutrients and water, which can stunt the cocoa tree's growth.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Amɛkɛ kookoo tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism that helps the tree save moisture by reducing the surface area where water escapes into the dry, windy air.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi he ni nu tsɔɔ mli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni ebaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will supply the needed nitrogen and restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting beans or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow better without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni jara wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to full sunlight and dry winds. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing temporary shade and moisture until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to stand the heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i be kukuoo ko kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Which part of the cassava plant should I cut and plant in the ground to grow new tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ koni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃?

english: Cassava is grown from stem cuttings rather than seeds. You cut mature, healthy stem sticks about 20 to 30 centimeters long and plant them at an angle in moist soil with the leaf buds pointing upwards.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii duɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. Ofoɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni okɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crops too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunshine from reaching one another. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large and yield plenty of food.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa ni ewoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden sticks to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋtayaai ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? koni ekɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ beni edaa lɛ

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tseee kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: How do I know when the soil is ready for planting after the major rains start?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: The soil is ready when rain has soaked deep enough that a handful of soil squeezed in your fist forms a soft ball without dripping wet water. Planting in dry soil causes seeds to dry up, while planting in waterlogged soil rots the seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ shi shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko miimɔ otsitsi mli ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni nu shwieee shi Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your farm early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel will protect your maize.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaabu oŋmã lɛ he.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil. Giving your plants consistent water at their roots and spreading dry grass mulch around the base cools the soil and helps tomatoes form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa ha otsei lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tomatoi lɛ feɔ.

english: How do wild weeds hurt my crops, and when is the best time to clear them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Ni mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ?
