english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops, making them weak. It is best to clear weeds early within the first three to four weeks after planting before they grow larger than your crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ha egbɔjɔ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dani jwɛi lɛ adara fe otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I estimate how much cocoa I will harvest from my farm this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kookoo ni abaakpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate yield by counting healthy, mature pods and growing medium pods across a sample of trees in different parts of your farm, taking into account that some pods may be lost to pests or bad weather before harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibiiwoo lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda lɛ akanemɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ ni ooodu yɛ tsei ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli lɛ nɔ. of your farm Enɛ susuɔ akɛ ŋmeii komɛi baanyɛ afite kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii nɔ dani akpa.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally lose productivity as they age past 20 to 25 years because their root systems become less efficient at taking up soil nutrients, requiring either soil rehabilitation or replanting.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛyibii kɛji amɛye afii 20 kɛyashi 25, ejaakɛ cacao tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ biɔ ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo adu nii heei.

english: What happens to my crop if I leave the bush and weeds to grow tall inside my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi kɛ jwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overgrown weeds compete with your cocoa trees for water and nutrients in the soil, while also trapping excess humidity that creates an ideal environment for diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ kɛ kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, emɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni no haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to prune the extra branches and shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, known as water suckers, waste the tree's food and energy that should instead go toward developing healthy cocoa pods on the main trunk and primary branches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ hu akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ, ni esa akɛ eya ni eyafee kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli wa yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without producing pods due to heat stress, prolonged dry weather, lack of pollination by tiny insects like midges, or missing nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli egbiɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ bɛ pollination. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet, and overly shaded conditions, spreading rapidly from pod to pod through rain splashes.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest a cocoa pod?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A pod is ready for harvest when its skin color fully changes from green to bright yellow, or from dark purple/red to orange-yellow, showing that the beans inside have fully matured.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ ŋmɔŋ/tsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ edara kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up in the sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight; without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa trees too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting trees too closely causes their branches and roots to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin trees with lower pod yields and higher disease risk.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ niji kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashi akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo, ni helai hu baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm's soil is running out of food for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ?

english: Signs of low soil fertility include slow tree growth, pale yellow leaves, smaller pods than usual, and a steady decline in cocoa yield year after year even when rainfall is good.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi lɛ he ji tsei ni daaa blɛoo, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Ni kookoo ni anáa lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi afi fɛɛ afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage helps the leaves stay green and feed the growing corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni wa lɛ adalɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem cutting to ensure it grows well after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should pick mature, healthy stems from the middle portion of a harvested plant and cut them into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long. Avoid using very soft tops or extremely hard base stems, as middle cuts sprout faster and develop stronger root tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tso ni eda ni mli wa kɛjɛ tso ni akpa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ofo mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji sɛntimitai 20 kɛyashi 30. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo waa loo tsei ni wa waa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni afolɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaaná shishifãi ayitsei ni mli wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, dry soil, or nutrient imbalances. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Koni onine ashɛ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Bu bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yeɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended insecticides early in the morning or putting dry sand or ash directly into the leaf funnel can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo akɛ ŋã ni egbi loo sũ fata baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, forms a protective layer over the soil that slows down water evaporation. It keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons, prevents weed growth, and gradually decays into natural compost to enrich the land.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to stick long bamboo poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmei tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on poles so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible to make food for underground tuber growth. Raising the leaves off the damp soil also prevents vine rot and fungal foliage diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ wain tso lɛ mli fitemɔ kɛ fungal baa helai anaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying neem oil solution or suitable pest controls early stops the damage and allows healthy new leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Neem mu mli nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɔ ni efite lɛ ni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Ani tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely actually reduces your yield because the crops compete heavily with each other for light, soil water, and nutrients. Giving plants proper spacing allows every stem to grow strong, build deep roots, and produce larger fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi ejaakɛ tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli waa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ daa waa. bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ yibii wuji baa

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help your maize leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmei baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when we get heavy rains in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni wɔnaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills flat or hard soil, water sits around the roots and starves them of air. This extra wetness allows rot-causing fungi to multiply quickly, so planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ Nu bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, heavily shaded cocoa farms. Clearing weeds and pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and air in to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are there tiny holes all over my pepper leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ?

english: Tiny holes on pepper leaves are usually caused by small insects like beetles or caterpillars feeding on them. Spraying your pepper plants early with natural neem water or recommended crop protection products stops the pests before they weaken the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem nu loo nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ mra. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kpaa dani amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant doesn't get steady water. Covering the soil around the plant with dry grass helps keep the soil moist and cool so the flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my watermelon vines grow so long and leafy, but produce almost no watermelons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi?

english: When watermelon plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into making thick leaves and vines instead of flowers. Giving them fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set fruit instead of just leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ watermelon tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni mli tse kɛ wain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii. Tsei ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii moŋ fe baai kɛkɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight lines with measured spacing instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni asusu gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows gives every single maize plant enough room, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow large cobs. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji akwɛ̃. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do my newly planted plantain suckers take so long to sprout new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tso ni midu ehee lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: If plantain suckers are buried too deep in the soil, the growing tip gets smothered and growth slows down. Planting suckers at the right depth—just up to where the bulb meets the stem—allows root growth to start quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, eshishi ni adu lɛ fiteɔ ni edalɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ni sa—kɛyashi he ni shishi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ—haa shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas on my land after I harvest my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die off early before my yams are big enough?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya dani mi-sweet potato lɛ daa bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when underground pests like beetles or tiny root worms damage the root system, blocking water from reaching the leaves. Staking the vines off the wet ground and treating the seed yams before planting keeps the vines green longer.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi amli lɛ je kpo. Nɔ ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ Haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ atswa wain tsei kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni akwɛ sweet potato nɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni wain tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do coconut trees need so much special attention compared to other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Coconut trees are very sensitive to their water supply. Giving them specific care, especially around how much water they receive, is essential for them to grow healthy and yield well.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ nuɔ nu jɛɛhei ahe waa. Akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ titri yɛ nu abɔ ni amɛnáa lɛ he. Ehe miihia ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the most important thing I need to manage when taking care of my coconut trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni mikwɛɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Water is the main factor requiring your attention. Managing the amount of water your coconut trees receive is critical to keeping them healthy.
ga: Nu ji nɔ titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni okɔɔŋtso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he miihia waa koni oná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Do I need to start watering my coconut trees once the rainy season begins?
ga: Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni aje ŋmei tsei anɔ nu shwiemɔ shishi?

english: Yes, as the rainy season arrives, you must ensure your coconut trees get adequate water so they can take full advantage of the growing period.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ Ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni okɔɔŋtso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ be ni ekɛdaraa lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it possible for me to give too much water to my coconut trees?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mawo mi ŋmei tso lɛ mli nu fe nine?

english: Yes, coconut trees can suffer if they get too much water. You have to be careful not to add extra water when the soil is already soaked.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei baanyɛ apiŋ kɛji amɛná nu babaoo. Esa akɛ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu babaoo akafata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ.

english: Should I still set aside time to water my coconut trees if it rains heavily?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ani esa akɛ maná be lolo koni mikɛwo mi-ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ nu?

english: No, if there is heavy rain, you do not need to set aside a day to water your coconuts because the rain has already provided enough moisture.
ga: Dabi, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni oto gbi ko ni okɛfɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ nu. Ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ eha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa eba.

english: What happens if I water my coconut trees on a day it rained heavily?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ nu wo ŋmei tso ko nɔ yɛ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ?

english: If you water them after a heavy rain, you will end up adding too much water, which can overload the soil and stress the tree's roots.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ Ehe baahia ni okɛ nu babaoo afata he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ afee jatsu fe nine ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii.

english: How should heavy rain change my usual watering routine for coconuts?
ga: Te esa akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsake bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei shwieɔ mi daa lɛ ahaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain replaces your need to manually water. You should pause your watering routine on those days so you don't overwater the crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Esa akɛ okpa nu ni oooha yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ be kukuoo ko. koni akashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu tsɔ

english: Why do I need to monitor the weather carefully when caring for coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ?

english: You need to monitor the weather because coconuts require water during the rainy season, but heavy rainfall means you must stop manual watering to avoid giving them too much.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ asɛɛ ejaakɛ nu he miihia ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okpa nu ni okɛ onine shwieɔ nɔ lɛ koni ekaho.

english: If the rainy season starts but the rainfall is very light, should I still water my coconuts?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ be lɛ je shishi shi nugbɔ lɛ waaa kwraa. Ani ehi lolo akɛ ooofɔ ŋmeii anɔ nu?

english: Yes, when the rainy season arrives, you must ensure the coconuts receive enough water, so if light rain isn't enough, you should supplement it manually.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ Ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni ŋmei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ faaa lɛ, esa akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛfata he.

english: Why does growing coconuts require more careful water management than just letting nature take its course?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ biɔ ni akwɛ nu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni aaaha adebɔɔ afee nɔ ni esumɔɔ lɛ?

english: Coconuts require a careful balance of water; while they need good moisture when the rainy season comes, too much water from combined rain and manual watering can harm them.
ga: Kokooi biɔ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa he miihia amɛ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ moŋ. Shi nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Big trees provide shade, keep the air cool, and help the soil retain moisture so the tender leaves do not dry out and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ Baai bibii lɛ egbiɛɛ ni amɛgboii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dark powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ powda bibii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ? yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant during the day and eats the soft young leaves, leaving behind chewed holes and droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ Amɛshiɔ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop give me smaller cobs if I plant it on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it continuously on the same spot drains those nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tsei yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ama ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits trapped around the roots for too long, waterlogging starves the roots of oxygen and allows fungal rot to spread quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ Nu ni ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ faaa. ni oha ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers dry up and drop off without turning into fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When temperature gets too high, the plant drops these unfertilized flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ nɛɛ ashwieɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing green shoots in the barn even before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yams naturally enter a resting state after harvest. Once this dormant period ends, warm and humid air signals to the tuber that it is time to break sleep and send out shoots using its stored food.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ hejɔɔmɔ nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ yitso lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ajɔɔ ehe. ni ekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into tight wrinkles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck leaf juices and spread plant viruses, causing the growing leaves to twist and wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ehaa baai ni miida lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do groundnut plants make the soil better for crops that I plant after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that partner with helpful bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules, naturally enriching the land with fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start producing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji amɛbɔi shweremɔ yɛ kui wuji amli pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and fibrous trunks rather than deep roots or hardwood. As a heavy bunch grows, the top-heavy weight easily pulls the shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ fiber moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo tsei ni wa. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Muji ni tsii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay green during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass acts as a protective blanket (mulch) that blocks direct sunlight, prevents water from evaporating out of the ground, and keeps the soil cool for the roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. (Mulch) Shade ni jɛɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my maize and leaving ragged holes with small droppings?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ baai ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center shoot (whorl) of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended biological treatments or insecticides into the whorl can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa (ring) lɛ mli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ loop lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant proper space ensures they all grow big, healthy ears of corn instead of many weak, barren stalks.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmãa tso lɛ ni etsɔ agbo ni efee hewalɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbi yɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains alongside new cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive and dry out easily under full sunshine. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that provide natural shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa trees during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall stems with many leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ kɛ baai babaoo, shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen food, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Ensuring your cassava receives direct sunshine helps it store energy below ground to make thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ eniyenii mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-cassava lɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help the maize crop I plant next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural nodes on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored food remains in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants to drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from stress. Mulching the soil around the plant base and watering regularly keeps the roots cool so the flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa pods develop dark spots and turn black when the rainy season becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and dense shade create high moisture, which spreads a fungal disease called Black Pod. Pruning extra shade tree branches and clearing lower cocoa branches lets sunlight and air dry out the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. ni gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ eshwaa Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli babaoo ni ajieɔ kookoo niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbi. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why is it important to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and protects them from soil diseases, allowing the plant to build much larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop's growth even when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that grow faster than crops, so they steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer you give to your plants. Clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures that your crops get all the food instead of the wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: This yellowing is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the maize plant takes nutrients from its older bottom leaves and sends them to the younger top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen lɛ, Abɛi lɛ heɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the base of my crop instead of scattering it all over the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni mikɛbaagbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures the plant can absorb the nutrients directly. Scattering it over the entire field wastes fertilizer because rain washes it away and feeds nearby weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ lɛ ni eyeɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ moŋ fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, drought, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant sheds the flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and lose their tiny green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho lɛ? dani eda

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally produce more young pods than they can feed, so the tree purposely sacrifices surplus pods to focus its limited energy and water on growing the remaining pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye. No hewɔ lɛ tsei tsɔɔ yiŋtoo mli ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ atsu ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ he nii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Heavy, standing rainwater fills all the air gaps in wet soil, suffocating the roots and creating conditions for rot-causing fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli obɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi baa ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in the same field make my maize grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This provides natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger and greener.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that are frequently attacked by soil pests like nematodes and root weevils. When the root system is weakened, the plant cannot support the heavy fruit bunch against strong wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes kɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aye aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of a viral disease carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the leaves, they pass on a virus that stunts the plant's leaves and reduces fruit yields.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Kɛji ŋmeii yɛŋ ye baai Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my tall rice plants bend and fall flat to the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is called lodging. It usually happens when crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the stems to grow tall and weak so they collapse under the weight of the grain heads during rain or wind.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kwɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa aahu akɛ amɛkuɔ shi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ ashishi yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn during storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that enter a temporary resting phase after harvest. Once this dormant phase ends, heat and moisture in the storage barn signal to the tuber that it is time to sprout and grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni boteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ nitsumɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni wɔɔhe be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdu wain tsei heei.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce far fewer fruit bunches than I expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ miiwo aduawai akui fioo kwraa fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm naturally has a relatively low individual bunch yield compared to other crops. To get a high harvest, trees require constant nutrients, proper spacing, and time to mature fully.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, mu tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe. Niyenii kpakpa he miihia tsei daa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ be ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Why do some of my palm nut trees produce bunches with tiny or empty nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aloo dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko?

english: Empty or poorly formed palm nuts usually happen because of poor pollination, prolonged drought, or a lack of key nutrients like potassium in the soil while the flowers are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni ehiii lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting before my palm nut trees start producing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du nii agbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani ŋmei tso lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved high-yielding palm nut varieties usually start bearing fruit between 3 to 4 years after planting in the field, though full yield potential is reached around 7 to 10 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 teŋ beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo ni baanyɛ aba lɛ fɛɛ ji afii 7 kɛyashi 10 moŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to have money saved before I start buying palm nut seedlings to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná shika dani mabɔi dumɔwui ni mikɛbaadu lɛ ahemɔ?

english: Because oil palm takes several years to yield fruit and initial crop yields are low, you need upfront cash to buy quality hybrid seedlings, fertilizers, and cover farm labor costs before the farm becomes profitable.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mu tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii, ni shishijee yibiiwoo lɛ faaa. Shika he miihia bo kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni okɛhe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo dani ŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do palm nut prices change so much throughout the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ palm nut jara srɔtoɔ waa yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Palm nut prices fluctuate due to seasonal yields. During the peak harvest season (February to May), supply is high so prices drop, while during the lean season, low supply drives prices higher.
ga: Palm nut jara tsakeɔ yɛ be mli ni afeɔ lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ kpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ mli (February kɛyashi May) Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa babaoo no hewɔ lɛ jara baa shi. yɛ be mli ni yɛ be mli ni yibiiwoo bɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni baa shi lɛ baaha nibii ajara aya ŋwɛi.

english: What can I do to help my palm nut trees produce heavier bunches?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua mi-palm tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Applying balanced fertilizers rich in potassium and nitrogen, regularly clearing weeds around the base, and keeping the farm well-watered during dry spells will significantly increase bunch weight.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium kɛ nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ni ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm trees turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign of nutrient deficiency, especially nitrogen or potassium, or severe water stress during the dry season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Titri lɛ, nitrogen loo potasium. loo nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How does the dry season affect my palm nut harvest?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa mi-palm nut ŋmaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Lack of water causes the tree to produce fewer flowers and smaller fruit bunches, which lowers your yield several months later when those flowers would have matured into nuts.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo ni ewoɔ aduawai bibii bibii. Enɛ baaha onibii ni obaawo lɛ aba shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ beni nakai fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my palm nut bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa tsei akui?

english: A palm nut bunch is ready for harvest when two to five ripe fruits loosen and fall naturally to the ground, and the fruits turn a deep reddish-orange color.
ga: Nuts kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai enyɔ kɛyashi enumɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli edɔ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize between my young palm nut trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi tsei bibii ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term food crops like maize or cassava is recommended during the first two to three years before the palm tree canopy closes, helping you earn money while waiting for the palms to yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli dani ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ aŋmɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni nibii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or large forest trees to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei wuji amli. Enɛ buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to keep leaves green and healthy. When food is low, the plant steals nitrogen from its old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems so that I get big tubers underground?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana ŋmei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Planting cassava stems about 1 meter apart gives each plant enough space under the ground to grow large tubers without fighting its neighboring plants for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baakwɛ̃. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. This extreme stress forces the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ ni naa wa nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural food (nitrogen) from the air and store it in the soil. When planted with maize, they help feed the maize so it grows stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo ŋmãa lɛ nɔ koni ewa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering bare soil with dry grass (called mulching) works like a blanket that blocks the hot sun, keeps moisture in the dirt so you water less, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to cut wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground on poles helps all the leaves catch maximum sunlight to make food. The more sunlight the leaves get, the bigger the yam tubers grow under the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni sweet potato ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know the rain has soaked the soil enough for me to start planting my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until you get 2 or 3 heavy rains that wet the soil deep down to the length of your hand before planting. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die when the heat returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa 2 loo 3 ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni obaanyɛ dani odu. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: What is eating my young maize leaves and leaving ragged holes full of small dirt particles inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai ni ayeɔ ni mishiɔ buji ni etsilɛ ni muji bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest caterpillar that hides inside the young maize leaves to eat them. Catching them early with appropriate bio-pesticides or neem water helps save your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli koni eye amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ bio-insecticide loo neem nu ni sa lɛ nɔ lɛ baahere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow forces the mother plantain tree to share its water and food with them, resulting in tiny bunches. Leaving only 2 or 3 strong shoots ensures your main tree yields large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo shwere lɛ, ebaanyɛ dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ agba nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ́ oshi tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or banana trees alongside young cocoa provides natural shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo banana tsei kɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer that feeds your maize and helps it produce bigger ears.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ toi wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which attack young maize leaves and stems. Spraying recommended organic or standard pesticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms feed helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni afɔɔ he ŋaa lɛ afɔ shi leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ yeɔ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shaded fields. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the fungus from taking hold.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ amɔ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the roots underneath stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of roots below. Potassium-rich soil or balanced fertilizer encourages larger cassava tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha yucca lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ baaye abua o-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants face heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering at the base of the plant and adding well-rotted manure helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi daa kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Rolling leaves is a natural survival trick maize uses to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and prevents moisture loss during dry conditions.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa ehiɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plants stunted and turning yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water smothers their roots and prevents them from breathing or absorbing nutrients. Watering only when the top layer of soil feels dry allows roots to breathe and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ ayi obɔ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ akamu loo ekaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nu he akɛ egbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops reduce my overall harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the food they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli mra yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly after I put them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get bruised during harvest or are stored in hot, unventilated places. Storing undamaged yams off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn protects them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ to ŋmeii atsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe koni amɛkafite.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive direct sunlight when they are small. Plantains grow quickly and produce wide leaves that shield young cocoa plants from the scorching sun while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the same piece of land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Groundnuts and beans naturally put nitrogen back into the earth through their roots, making the soil fertile again for future crops without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ Nuts Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa tso lɛ amu ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Treating the field for sucking insects helps stop it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ otsu oyale lɛ he nii koni ekɛmu kooloi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat or water stress confuses the plant, so it drops its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully removing topsoil near one stem to inspect the root size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kwraa kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ fiofio ni Ooojie ŋwɛi sũ ni bɛŋkɛ baa lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni ona shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yes, you should leave only 1 to 3 healthy shoots per stand. If too many suckers grow together, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree, resulting in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 kɛyashi 3 pɛ yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji plantains akuu bibioo ko.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy that builds big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji baa. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulu lɛ mli ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my maize seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the actual rainy season begins. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout, only for the hot sun to dry out the soil and kill the young seedlings before the next rain comes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ pɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egbeɔ tsei bibii dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce the final harvest I get from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa naagbee ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds take over, your crops receive less food and light, causing them to grow weak and yield far less fruit or grain.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii kɛ la fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui fioo kwraa.

english: Why does the chemical spray I used last season not seem to kill the caterpillars on my maize field anymore?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ egbeee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Insects can build up resistance to the same spray if it is used repeatedly over time. Rotating between different recommended pest control products prevents pests from adapting to a single medicine.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ akɛtsu nii shii abɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ateŋ tsakemɔ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsake amɛhe amɛwo tsofa kome mli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather. Pruning excess foliage lets sunlight in and lowers humidity, which reduces fungal growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and yellowing leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni o-extension agent lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil has enough moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil often points to root rot or bacterial wilt, which lives in the soil and attacks plant roots. Rotating your crops and avoiding planting peppers in the same bed every year stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ egbo. ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa tsei shishifãi Tsakemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ooodu yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves and stems. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or adding well-decomposed manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ Kɛ́ okɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of big leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baa lɛ dara waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth with small tubers happens when soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Using balanced fertilizers encourages the plant to direct its energy into expanding the root tubers.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yields when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets the resources it needs to grow sturdy and bear heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda be fɛɛ be ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmã lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied twice: first about two weeks after germination to boost root growth, and again when the plants are knee-high to support flowering and cob formation.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ: klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni eshishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ koni eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ aaafee amɛnaji ahe koni amɛye amɛbua fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ.

english: Why are small insects destroying my harvested maize grains inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ mi-nitoohe kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils multiply inside stored crops if the grains were not dried completely before bagging. Thoroughly drying maize under the sun and using airtight storage bags prevents insects from surviving.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani awoɔ kotoku mli lɛ Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to make leaves green, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does planting cassava on the same piece of land every year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth as it grows. Planting it continuously on the same spot wears out the soil, so rotating with crops like cowpeas helps put food back into the land.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, cool weather when humidity is high and trees are planted too closely together.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the center whorl of young maize plants to feed on tender new leaves before they open.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai heei dani amɛgbele.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need shade trees to act as natural sunshades and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants produce tubers underground by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay free from ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even if I put fertilizer near my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your main plants hungry and shaded.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Shi otso titri lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if the rainy season lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely waterlogged for weeks, air cannot reach the roots, causing the underground cassava tubers to drown and rot.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when they lack sufficient water, as a defense mechanism to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. akɛ hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ hewalɛ he

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to start planting my maize after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a few inches below the surface; if it forms a ball without crumbling or leaking excess water, there is enough moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi inchi fioo komɛi. Kɛji akɛ efee bɔɔlu ni efoŋ loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What should I do if a disease completely destroys all the crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela ko kpata ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ kwraa?

english: When a disease wipes out your entire crop, you should clear and destroy all infected plant remains, then let the land rest or rotate to a completely different crop family to break the disease cycle before planting again.
ga: Kɛ hela kpata onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ Esa akɛ ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo etsake ehe kɛya tsei aweku kroko kwraa mli koni ekɛfo hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli dani odu ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I keep using the same chemical spray if pests on my pepper plants are not dying?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ blema lɛ atsu nii kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbooo?

english: No, because using the same chemical continuously makes pests build resistance to it. You should switch to a different class of chemical or consult an extension officer to try natural pest management methods.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Esa akɛ otsake kɛya tsofa kroko nɔ loo okɛ o-extension agent lɛ agba sane koni oka adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ okwɛ.

english: How do I safely restart planting on a field that was previously ruined by a major outbreak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ hela ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ efite lɛ lɛ dumɔ ekoŋŋ shweshweeshwe?

english: Before replanting, clear out all old crop debris, select certified disease-resistant seed varieties, ensure proper soil preparation, and change the type of crop you plant so surviving pests do not have food.
ga: dani adu ekoŋŋ Jiemɔ tsei momo lɛ fɛɛ ni efite lɛ. Halamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsakemɔ tsei srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ akaná niyenii.

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the bottom of maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor watering. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will help restore the plant's green color and growth.
