ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my dying crops are suffering from bad weather or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ eha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miigbo lɛ ená nɔ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ enɔ?

english: Weather damage usually affects all plants across the field evenly at the same time, whereas diseases start in small patches, create spots or discolored patterns on leaves, and spread gradually from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ saa tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he yɛ be kome mli. Beni hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ, ekɛ ŋmeii loo mfonirii ni tsakeɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is typically caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root rot, which clogs the tubes inside the stem that carry water. Sick plants should be removed immediately so the sickness does not spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ paipi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ naa Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp, and shady conditions. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly will protect healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good practice to stop farming on my land for a season if my yield keeps dropping every year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ okwaayeli be kome kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Yes, leaving your land fallow allows the soil time to rest and naturally replenish nutrients while starving out soil-borne pests and diseases that depend on your crops to survive.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ sũ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni damɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground even when the leaves on top look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Cassava roots rot primarily due to excess water trapped in heavy soil or fungal infections in poorly drained land. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the root zone.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and power to support crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Signs of exhausted soil include slow plant growth, stunted stems, pale green or yellowish leaves despite adequate rain, hard crusty soil when dry, and continuously declining harvests every season.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. stunted trunk Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛji egbi. Ni nikpamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for me to clear virgin forest land just to start a new crop farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafo koo ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli koni mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii heei akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing virgin forest removes the natural topsoil protection, causing heavy rains to wash away nutrients quickly and leaving young crops vulnerable to harsh heat and severe soil erosion.
ga: Kooi ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baajɛ mli aba.

english: Why do forest trees keep the soil on my farm damp even when it hasn't rained for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Deep tree roots pull water up from deep underground, while their fallen leaves form a natural blanket on the ground that traps moisture and prevents the sun from drying out the soil.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I avoid burning the bush on my plot before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashãmɔ he dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Hot fires kill beneficial soil insects and organisms, destroy rich organic plant matter, and leave the topsoil hardened, making it harder for plant roots to spread and feed.
ga: La ni mli edɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Efiteɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii. ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli waa Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nakai tsei lɛ

english: When you leave too many suckers (young shoots) around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, which weakens the main plant and reduces bunch size.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha kui lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up from the bottom during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require a lot of water to stay healthy; during dry spells, the plant naturally sheds its lower, older leaves to conserve moisture for the trunk and new growing leaves.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛshishigbɛ kɛ baai ni edara lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha tsei kɛ baai heei ni miida lɛ.

english: What causes my plantain tree to fall over suddenly just when the fruit bunch is getting big?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems; strong winds or root damage from soil pests can easily weaken the base, causing the plant to collapse under the heavy weight of the maturing fruit.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ oya, ni eha tso lɛ akumɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni tsii waa lɛ shishi.

english: How many sucker shoots should I keep on one plantain stand for a good harvest next year?
ga: Esa akɛ makwɛ tsei akutsei enyiɛ nɔ koni maná kpamɔ kpakpa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You should keep a maximum of three stems per stand—the main fruiting plant, one medium follower shoot, and one small shoot—so they do not choke each other out.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ tsei ni fe etɛ toɔ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ, ni tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ, tso ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome fata he, koni amɛkafo amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings essential shade and moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I grow cassava and plantain together on the same piece of land without them affecting each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu cassava kɛ plantain yɛ he kome ni amɛnáaa amɛhe nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, but you must space them wide apart because both crops feed heavily from the upper layer of the soil; planting them too close together makes them fight for the same nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he ejaakɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ nii waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland become poor and produce weak crops after farming it continuously for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ afii etɛ ni mikɛtsu nii daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops remove essential nutrients from the soil every season, so continuous farming without adding compost, animal manure, or letting the land rest exhausts the topsoil completely.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, okwaayeli yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo ahaaa shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ afite sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the hot sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them provides cool shade and holds moisture in the soil until the young cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I keep some big forest trees standing on my farm instead of cutting all of them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ koo mli tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Large forest trees act as windbreaks, keep the farm cool, and drop leaves that rot into natural food for the soil. Keeping some shade trees protects your crops from climate heat and keeps the land fertile for future years.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiimɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ obu o-shade tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Is it okay to let cattle walk and feed on my crop field after harvest?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha tsinayei anyiɛ ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: While cattle manure can enrich the soil, too many heavy animals crush and pack the soil down hard. Stiff, compacted soil makes it very difficult for seeds to germinate and roots to grow in the next planting season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsina ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii moŋ, shi kooloi ni tsii babaoo hu yɛ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ ni shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields now compared to when I first cleared it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa fe beni mijie nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients every time crops are harvested without replacing what was taken. Over years of farming, the soil becomes tired and hungry unless you add organic manure, plant soil-enriching cover crops, or use fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ nɔ ni anáa lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli. Afii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli Shikpɔŋ lɛ he baajɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii.

english: How does dried animal dung help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal dung acts as natural plant food that slowly releases nutrients into the soil. It improves the soil's structure so it can hold onto water longer during dry weather and supports healthy earthworms.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Cassava roots spread widely and drain nutrients and water out of the soil very quickly, which can starve young cocoa seedlings. It is safer to plant plantains or food crops that do not compete as aggressively with cocoa.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu plantains loo niyenii krokomɛi ni kɛ kookoo yeee akaŋ waa.

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the soil. If the soil is loose or waterlogged, or if the plant carries a very heavy bunch of fruits, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ yibii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is typically Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid shade. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm, drying up the moisture that the disease needs to spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni hela agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects like midges to pollinate them before they turn into pods. Extreme hot weather, dry soil, or spraying strong chemicals that kill these helpful insects can cause flowers to drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛwo amɛmli dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ agbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ, ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔii lɛ agbo.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build green leaves, or when excess water stays around the roots and stops them from breathing.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. aloo be mli ni nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ekpaa mumɔ

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or insufficient nutrients in the soil, causing the plant to save its energy instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Ha tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛbaafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Tubers rot when water settles in heavy soil for too long, creating an overly damp environment where soil fungi and bacteria can easily infect and break down the roots.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ fe nine baa. Fungi kɛ muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ hela ni amɛfite shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a canopy that protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to catch daylight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ aba lɛ, esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Will planting beans on the same farm with my maize hurt or help my crop?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baaye mi awui loo ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Planting beans helps your maize because beans pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Beans ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ejaakɛ ŋmãa gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Why do my crops dry up and die if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain usually moistens only the top layer of soil, and hot dry spells often follow immediately; planting too early leaves tender roots stranded in dry soil without deeper groundwater.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔ mra tsɔ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer before your actual crops get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ náa hegbɛ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat hole patterns in the funnel center of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he mfoniri lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the tight center leaves of young maize plants to feed on the soft growing tissues where predators cannot easily reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Many modern commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids whose vigor only lasts for one generation; planting seeds harvested from them results in weaker plants with reduced yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jarayeli dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni wa yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I stop diseases from spreading when I move plantain shoots from my old farm to a new one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ? Beni mijie plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Before moving plantain suckers to a new field, inspect and clean them thoroughly so you do not carry hidden pests, eggs, or diseases from the old farm to clean land.
ga: Dani obaajie plantain tsei lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ hee nɔ Kwɛmɔ ni otsumɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni ehe akahia ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ momo lɛ mli aba koni okɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my new plantain farm getting infested even though the land was completely clean before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ hee lɛ miifite eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse kwraa dani adu lɛ?

english: Pests and diseases are often carried directly into fresh fields on infected planting materials, such as suckers brought from old farms without being checked first.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai Bei pii lɛ, akɛyaa sũ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔ nibii ni hela emɔ mli tamɔ suckers ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli ni akwɛɛɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can pests travel from an old crop field to a new one on my planting suckers?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afã gbɛ kɛjɛ hei ni adu nii yɛ momo lɛ kɛya hei heei yɛ mi-suckers lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, insects and their eggs frequently hide at the base or inside the corm of plantain suckers, easily traveling with you to infect new fields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, kooloi kɛ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi loo amɛmli. ni kɛ bo fãa gbɛ mlɛo koni egbɛ hela eshwa ŋmɔji heei amli

english: What are those small white eggs I sometimes see at the bottom of my plantain suckers?
ga: ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Mɛni ji nɔ ni bei komɛi lɛ minaa yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishi?

english: Those white eggs at the base of the sucker are laid by plantain pests like weevils. If planted, they hatch into grubs that destroy the root base and kill the crop.
ga: Kplukai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ sucker lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ lɛ, amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shishitoo nibii ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I check if a plantain sucker is healthy before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi plantain suckers lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu?

english: Look carefully at the bottom base (corm) of the sucker for small white eggs, dark rot, or holes before planting, selecting only clean and undamaged suckers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ sucker lɛ shishi (fɔmɔ) lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii diji, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dani aduɔ lɛ. Halamɔ suction cups ni he tse ni efiteee pɛ.

english: What should I do if I find insect eggs on the base of my plantain shoots?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina kooloi awui yɛ plantains shishi?

english: Do not plant suckers carrying insect eggs. You should carefully scrape or cut away the infested outer layer of the base, or throw away heavily infected suckers.
ga: Kaadu tsei ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii loo ofo shishitoo ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli. loo shɛrɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ashwie.

english: Should I trim or scrape the base of my plantain suckers before putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-banana tsei lɛ ashishi dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, scraping or paring the outer layer of the sucker's base helps remove hidden pest eggs and damaged tissue so you only plant clean, healthy material.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ajie loo ajie suction base lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛ fãji ni efite lɛ. Bɔni afee ni odu nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ.

english: Where do plantain insects usually lay their eggs on the crop?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni plantain ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui lɛ shwiemɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Plantain pests typically use their rear end to lay eggs at the very base or corm of the sucker near the root area where it is soft and sheltered.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain mli kooloi kɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi loo amɛyitso ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ji he ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: How do small insects manage to get inside my plantain suckers to destroy them?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii abote mi plantain tsei lɛ amli koni amɛfite amɛ?

english: Adult insects lay their eggs on the outside base of the sucker, and once the eggs hatch, the young larvae tunnel directly inside to feed and grow.
ga: Kplukai ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ sucker lɛ kponɔgbɛ shishigbɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Abaafee gbɛ ko ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye nii ni amɛdara.

english: Why are my young plantain plants dying shortly after I transplant them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboi beni mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pest eggs hidden at the base of the transplanted suckers may have hatched, allowing young insects to eat through the main bulb and kill the plant from the inside.
ga: Ekolɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛtee tsei ni adu lɛ ashishi lɛ efo. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ bulb wulu lɛ mli ni amɛgbeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Why are my young mango trees dropping all their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers when they do not get enough water during the dry season or when tiny insects like thrips attack the blossom heads. Giving trees steady water at the base during early flowering and keeping pests away allows the flowers to turn into full mango fruits.
ga: Mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ha tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa ni amɛtsɔ mango.

english: Is it better for me to grow mangoes from seeds or use grafted seedlings?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsɔ dumɔwui anɔ akwɛ mango loo akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Grafted seedlings are much better because they produce sweet fruit in just three to four years, whereas trees grown directly from seeds can take over seven years and might not produce the same good quality fruit as the mother tree.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe nɔ ni fe afii kpawo, ni ekolɛ amɛwooo yibii kpakpai tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some of the inside branches of my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo aduawai tsei lɛ amli niji lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Cutting away crowded inside branches—called pruning—allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the center of the tree. This keeps fungal diseases from building up in the shade and helps the tree put its energy into growing bigger fruit.
ga: Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa shia, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: How can I tell when a mango fruit is ripe enough to harvest without waiting for it to fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mango ko ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mimɛɛɛ ni egbee shi?

english: A mango is ready to pick when the top area near the stem swells up and turns rounded, and the dull green skin starts to lighten or show a hint of yellow or reddish color.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi fã ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ efo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ loo ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsuru fioo.

english: Does burning dry grass and bushes on my farm hurt the soil before I plant?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishãa lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui dani aduɔ nii?

english: Yes, burning damages the soil by killing useful organisms that help plants grow and burning away valuable plant matter that would naturally rot into rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ni egbeɔ lɛ nɔ. ni oshã tsei ni jara wa ni baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ koni eha niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli babaoo aha onibii.

english: Yellow bottom leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow big. Applying animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ yɛ nitrogen he. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense trick to protect themselves from losing too much moisture to the intense sun heat. It means the plants are thirsty and trying to save water.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu akafite.

english: Can I plant groundnuts or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts or beans alongside maize is very beneficial because crops in the bean family take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, naturally feeding the nearby maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ legume weku lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, eyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to leave specific distances between my crop seeds when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ ato he ko kɛji midu lɛ?

english: If seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants will fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, leaving you with thin, weak crops. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: What causes the green leaves on my cassava plants to twist and develop sticky white spots?
ga: Mɛni haa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Twisted cassava leaves with sticky white spots are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or whiteflies. Clearing away heavily infected leaves early stops these insects from spreading across your entire field.
ga: Cassava baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies kɛbaa. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat because their leaves burn easily and the soil dries out too fast. Keeping some tall trees or planting plantains beside them creates shade that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa plants grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai lɛ shãa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei kakadaji akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa.

english: Why shouldn't I let plantain suckers grow too close to my cocoa trees after the cocoa has grown big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ tsɔ beni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ?

english: While plantains help young cocoa, fully grown cocoa trees need all the soil nutrients and space they can get. Old plantain stems will compete with mature cocoa for water and food, which reduces your cocoa pod harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantain yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ cocoa bibii moŋ Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ. Plantain tsei momo kɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa o-cocoa pod ni okpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. Applying fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure gives them the nutrient boost needed to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when the rainy season is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked soil for too long because water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and attracting fungal diseases. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to carry tall wooden stakes to support my yam vines instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo tso kakadaŋŋ ko? koni ekɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha enyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to build large tubers under the ground. Keeping the leaves off the damp soil also protects the plant from fungal diseases that thrive on wet leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right in the center fold of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing point of the maize plant where the leaves are tender. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended treatments before they dig deep into the funnel saves the plant from being destroyed.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa hei ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani otsa ŋshɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap and pass viruses into the plant. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from curling and prevents the plant from being stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni ebaaha tso lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water. When the plant gets stressed by drought or heat, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo latsaa miigba tsei anaa lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my crop yields drop when I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain often moistens the topsoil just enough to trigger seed germination, but it is frequently followed by dry hot days that dry out the soil and kill the young sprout. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for roots to establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso bibioo lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain beside them provides protective shade and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adumɔ yɛ Tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Maize plants turn yellow when they lack essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen, in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfata he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess water fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ feɔ babaoo.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows the leaves to trap maximum sunlight for food production and prevents soil-borne diseases from touching and damaging the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ hiɛɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ etaa baai lɛ ahe ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: How do small caterpillars manage to ruin an entire field of young maize so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii bibii nyɛɔ amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii bibii ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm feed on the tender leaf-funnel at the center of the plant, which destroys the plant's main growing point and stops new leaves from forming.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ hei titri lɛ ni ekpaa baai heei ni baa lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow at once forces the parent plant to share its water and nutrients, resulting in smaller, lighter bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome lɛ, enyɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely, as extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents flower pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal fertilizers and soil minerals away from your crops, blocking sunlight and crowding out your crop's roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: How does mixing compost into my soil help crops survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Compost acts like a sponge in the soil by holding onto water much longer, allowing plant roots to continue drinking even during days without rainfall.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi yaa nɔ amɛnuɔ nu yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why do my crops give me very little harvest even when I plant at the exact same time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting at the same time each year isn't enough if weather patterns shift or if the soil has lost its nutrients over time. Soil needs to be fed with organic manure or fertilizers, and planting schedules may need to adjust to changing rainfall patterns to get a good yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi lɛ faaa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsake loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni atsake be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ mli koni aná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my previous harvest produce less food than when I first bought them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo fe be mli ni mihe lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests, especially hybrid varieties, lose their strength and yield potential over time. Buying fresh, certified seeds from trusted agricultural dealers ensures stronger plants that produce much better harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli Titri lɛ hybrid henɔi Ebaafite ehewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo hegbɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Hemɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase kɛjɛ okwaayeli jalɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can my farmland become tired if I grow the exact same crop on it every season?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli baajɔ kɛji midu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Yes, growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating your crops—such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize—helps restore nutrients naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is healthy enough to give me a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, contains earthworms, and crumbles easily in your hand. Hard, pale, or dry dusty soil lacks organic matter and needs compost or animal manure before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. ni efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ, ni wa, ni mli tse, loo ni egbi lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ehe hiaa ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu.

english: Is it my fault when my crops do not yield well, or could it be caused by changes in the weather?
ga: Ani mihe ejɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo ekolɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ?

english: Low crop yields are often not the farmer's fault alone. Changes in rain patterns, long dry spells, or extreme heat strongly affect crop growth, but practices like mulching and using drought-resistant seeds can help protect your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ jeee okwaafonyo lɛ pɛ tɔmɔ. tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli loo dɔlɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ náa tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ waa. Shi nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: What can I do to keep my crops from dying when the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nibii akagbo beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and helps crops survive longer through dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and looking weak even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is standing in the field and choking the roots. Adding proper fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps plants regain their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛmiimɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many seeds as possible close together so I can get more food from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space to produce a full harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkpaa ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Will putting extra fertilizer on my farm automatically double my crop harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots and damage the soil. Crops only need the right amount and type of fertilizer applied at the correct growth stages to yield well.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ henɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni sa mli pɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do insects attack and destroy my farm more in some years than in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ yɛ afii komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Insects multiply faster during years with specific weather conditions, such as sudden warmth or erratic rains, which create ideal breeding environments. Checking your farm regularly helps catch and treat pest problems before they destroy your harvest.
ga: Kplukai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ afii amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahetoohamɔ mli, tamɔ dɔlɛ trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa. ni haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fɔmɔ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni omɔ ni otsa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture to protect young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on their leaves to produce food for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which exposes them to more sun and prevents rot and soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaha hulu la lɛ ashɛ ehe babaoo. ni atsĩ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete underground for food, water, and space. This causes them to yield small, thin roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to reduce water loss. If the leaves relax again when the temperature cools down in the evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face stress, such as irregular watering, extreme heat, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil consistently moist and treating pests will help the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does one sick cocoa tree with swollen branches cause nearby cocoa trees to get sick as well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ ni eniji efuu lɛ haa cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hu hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen Shoot is a contagious virus spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. These insects crawl from the infected tree to neighboring healthy trees, transferring the disease while feeding.
ga: Swollen shoots ji hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ayeɔ nii

english: How do I know the right time to apply pesticide to my maize field to fight fall armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii koni mikɛwu ashi cutworm?

english: Pesticides work best early in the morning or late in the evening when armyworms come out to feed. You should spray as soon as you notice small pinholes in the young leaves before the worms hide deep inside the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni kooloi lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji ona buji bibii yɛ baai bibii lɛ amli, dani ŋmeii lɛ ayahi tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize plant very tall and dark green, but the corn cobs stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ waa lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo.

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen, which promotes leafy growth, but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are the nutrients the plant needs to build large, full grains.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. ni haa baa lɛ daa Shi ebɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start to rot just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react quickly to air and cut injuries, causing them to spoil within 48 to 72 hours. It is best to harvest cassava only when you have a buyer or are ready to process it immediately.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ pilamɔi. Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaakpa ŋmei kɛji oyɛ mɔ ni baahe loo ofee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn yellow and soft too quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee blɛoo oya tsɔ dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains produce a natural gas that speeds up their own ripening, especially when kept in direct sunlight or warm, packed spaces. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated shade slows down ripening.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshwereɔ oya. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu la tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo he ko ni mli edɔɔ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehoo blɛoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb on stakes or trees instead of spreading on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei kɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ oshwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tuber underground. When you stake them, the leaves catch more sunlight, stay off the hot, damp soil to prevent rotting, and produce much larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji okɛ ohe wo shi lɛ, hulu la babaoo baashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he koni akafite. ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are getting choked by too much water around their roots. Without enough nitrogen in the soil, the leaves lose their green color and cannot make the food needed for the crop to yield well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha niyenii ni he hiaa tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry weather as a survival trick to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops water from escaping into the hot air and protects its roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haaa nu akaje mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ebuɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any pepper fruits grow out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the weather is too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my crops produce very small harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves fight for sunlight above ground. Giving each plant proper distance allows it to feed well and grow full-sized fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dried grass help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mulching around Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ jwɛi yeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass—called mulching—acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool, prevents the sun from quickly drying out soil water, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I actually planted in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally built to survive harsh conditions and quickly steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your soil. Clearing weeds early stops them from starving your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hɔmɔ akaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why are small insects chewing holes in my vegetable leaves, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaves act as tiny food factories for your plants by catching sunlight. When insects eat and damage the leaves, the plant loses its ability to feed itself, causing stunted growth and poor fruit quality.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii afeemɔ hei bibii. kɛha otsei lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni emɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi ye ni amɛfite baai lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant yams on the exact same piece of soil every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yams repeatedly in the same soil uses up all the specific food yams need and gives yam pests and diseases a permanent home in your soil. Rotating yams with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients and cleans the soil.
ga: Sweet potato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni sweet potato lɛ he hiaa lɛ baafite. ni oye obua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhelai lɛ ahi shi daa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: How can I tell if the seed yams I stored from my last harvest are still healthy enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu?

english: Healthy seed yams should feel firm to the touch, be free from soft rot spots, and have clean skin with no insect damage. Rotten or overly dried seeds will fail to sprout or produce weak plants.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛji mɔ ko ta he. Ebɛ he ko ni efite ni eyɛ hewolo ni he tse ni kooloi efiteee Dumɔwui ni egbo loo egbi tsɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛwo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off before the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can mean your trees lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or they are infected with a disease like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. When infected, the tree loses its leaves because the disease blocks food and water from flowing through the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hela ko, tamɔ cocoa bud virus lɛ emɔ lɛ. Kɛji hela lɛ mɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ hela lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛ nu naa koni ekatsɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: How does crop disease travel from my neighbor's farm to my cocoa trees?
ga: Te tsei ahe helai yaa kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa diseases can spread through tiny insects like mealybugs carrying viruses, wind blowing fungal spores across farms, contaminated pruning cutlasses, or workers brushing against infected pods as they walk through fields.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛ hela lɛ nɔ agbɛ ashwã kookoo hela lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa fungal spores yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii ni mli ewo muji loo nitsulɔi ni miifɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe beni amɛnyiɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down trees with Swollen Shoot disease instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifo tsei ni ŋmeii efuu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsofa ko kɛkɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease is caused by a virus living deep inside the tree's sap system. Because there is no chemical spray that can kill a virus inside a living plant, cutting down the infected tree is the only way to stop it from spreading to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Cocoa bloat hela lɛ jɛɔ muawai ko ni hiɔ tso lɛ nu mli shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ agbe helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ bɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: The heavy rain creates high humidity, which helps a fungal disease called Black Pod thrive. Raindrops splash fungal spores from wet soil and infected branches directly onto healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ daa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: If I take over an old, bushy cocoa farm that has been abandoned for many years, can I make the old trees yield again?
ga: Kɛji miŋɔ kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni ashi ni ehi shi afii babaoo lɛ. Ani manyɛ maná cacao tsei momo lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Very old or neglected cocoa trees often harbor hidden diseases and produce very low yields. In most cases, it is better to clear the old trees, clear the land, and replant with new, fast-growing, disease-resistant varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni egbɔ waa loo aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei momoi lɛ, ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni akɛ tsei heei ni daa oya, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods every year even though the trees keep growing larger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yaa nɔ edaa moŋ?

english: As trees grow bigger, they use up more soil nutrients just to maintain their frame. Without added fertilizer or manure, the tired soil cannot supply enough energy for the tree to produce pods.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da Amɛkɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when they are growing just fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into the tree canopy. Good airflow reduces humidity that causes pod diseases and helps the tree focus its strength on bearing pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ shishi. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa pod ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to sprout and the outer shell to rot. Overripe pods attract pests and fungal diseases that quickly infect nearby healthy green pods.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa pods eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it good to keep large forest trees inside my cocoa farm, or will they steal water from my crops?
ga: Ehi akɛ makwɛ koo mli tsei wuji yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aloo amɛbaaju nu kɛjɛ midumɔ nii lɛ amli?

english: A mix of tall shade trees protects young cocoa from direct sun heat and keeps moisture in the soil. However, too much heavy shade keeps the farm damp and invites fungal rot, so shade trees must be properly managed and thinned out.
ga: Tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo be babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akwɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni afee amɛ bibii.

english: Why do weeds harm my young cocoa plants so much faster than my fully grown trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ oya fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and compete heavily with weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Mature cocoa trees have deep root systems and dense leaves that block out sunlight, naturally keeping weeds under control.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kakao tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ hiɔ adebɔɔ mli kudɔmɔ shishi

english: Is it better to leave the outer husk on my harvested maize or remove it immediately?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ nɔ loo majie amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Leaving the husk on acts as a natural shield that protects the grains from insects, dust, and excess moisture, allowing the cobs to dry gradually without spoiling.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ ŋmaa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii, sũ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni egbiɔ fiofio. ni efiteee

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil so quickly if I put it in a room right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ mikɛwo tsu lɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn holds a lot of internal moisture. If it is stored in an enclosed space without proper air circulation and drying, mold and weevils rapidly destroy the cobs.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ emli. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni atswa he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni egbi lɛ, Mold kɛ weevils fiteɔ ŋmei lɛ oya.

english: Why do extension officers advise building raised shelves or wooden racks to store maize cobs instead of putting them on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ama shĩai ni awó nɔ loo tso shĩai ni akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ato mli moŋ fe ni akɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Keeping maize on raised shelves allows air to circulate underneath, prevents dampness from rising off the soil, and makes it harder for rats and crawling pests to reach the grain.
ga: Abɛi ni akɛtoɔ shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni shwereɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: How long can I safely store dried maize before it loses its quality or gets damaged by pests?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ato shweshweeshwe dani ehi jogbaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite lɛ?

english: If maize is thoroughly dried, kept off the ground, and stored in a well-ventilated or airtight container, it can stay good for six months to over a year.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa Ha ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli jogbaŋŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Abɛi baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi afi.

english: Can I store my harvested grains in plastic bags without them rotting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ awo plastic kotokui amli ni amɛfiteee?

english: Yes, but only if the grain is completely dry first. Double plastic bags or airtight hermetic bags kill pests by depriving them of oxygen, but any leftover moisture inside will cause the grain to mold.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbi kwraa klɛŋklɛŋ pɛ. Plastic kotokui ni akɛwo mli shii enyɔ loo vacuum kotokui baagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes my stored bag of corn to become warm or hot when I touch it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmã kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli dɔɔ loo edɔɔ kɛ mita he?

english: Heat in a storage bag is caused by excess moisture. High humidity allows fungi and insects to breathe and multiply quickly, producing internal heat that ruins the grain.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii muɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Enɛ haa mligbɛ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves and husks of my maize turn brown and dry up while the plant is still standing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: As maize reaches full maturity, the plant naturally stops drawing water and transfers all remaining energy to harden the seeds, causing the husks and leaves to dry out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha dumɔwui lɛ awa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔji kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why do weevils appear inside my stored maize cobs even when I don't see any bugs on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay microscopic eggs inside the maize kernels while the cobs are still growing on the farm. Once harvested and brought into a warm storage space, those eggs hatch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpa ni akɛwo he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ.

english: Why does my maize turn moldy even after I dry it under the sun for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ mli ewo muji eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: Sun drying removes water from the surface, but if the center of the cob or grain is still wet, that hidden water escapes inside the storage container and creates mold.
ga: Hulu ni egbiɔ lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ loo ŋmaa lɛ mli efɔ lolo lɛ Nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baajo foi kɛya ŋmei ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmei aba.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my harvested crop husks directly on the bare ground to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Bare ground transfers dampness and soil fungi into the crop, inviting termites and rot, whereas drying on mats or elevated platforms keeps the crop clean and dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ nine. Yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ tsɔne loo he ko ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe atse ni egbi.

english: Planting maize with about 75 centimeters between rows and 30 centimeters between seeds gives each plant enough room to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding out neighboring plants.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 75 kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 30 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ ehe wooo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli

english: Why do my corn plants bend over and fall when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Corn plants fall easily when their roots are weak or shallow, which often happens if you do not heap extra soil around the base of the stems (hilling) as the plant gets taller.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ okɛ sũ etooo tso lɛ shishi (yɛ gɔŋ ko mli) beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green, often caused by poor soil or heavy rains washing nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up like tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn leaves roll up in extreme heat to save moisture by reducing the leaf surface exposed to the sun; it is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni amɛ bu fũu kɛtsɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la baa shi lɛ nɔ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves and leaving green waste inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ jwɛi eŋɔli yɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of the plant and eat the leaves, requiring early scouting and treatment before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Esa akɛ akwɛ mli ni atsa lɛ mra. dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why do tiny insects bore holes into my harvested maize while it is in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored maize if the grains are not dried completely before storage or if the storage area is not clean and sealed against pests.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. aloo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ he tseee ni atsĩ naa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli

english: Can I put fresh manure from my chicken farm directly onto my growing crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ mikooloi aŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is very strong and releases heat and chemicals that can burn crop roots; it must be allowed to dry and decompose (compost) for a few weeks before putting it on your plants.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ kpo. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi ni egbo (compost) otsii fioo komɛi dani adu.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I wait too long to remove weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mijie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need, so leaving them in the field starves your crop and reduces your final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ebaaha naagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it good to plant cassava in the same farm where I have planted my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?
