english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to take over the field later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida fiofio lɛ koni amɛye ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know that my corn is completely ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is fully mature when the outer green husks turn completely brown and dry, and the silky threads at the top of the cob turn dark brown.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa ni ji eŋɔli lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa kwraa ni egbi. ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize once the rain begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You need to wait until the rain wets the soil deep enough—usually after two or three heavy rains—so the seed has enough moisture to grow fully without drying up if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ—koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why should I measure exact distances between my cassava stems instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he pɔtɛɛ ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting with proper spacing ensures that each crop gets enough space underground to spread its roots and form large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for soil nutrients and sunlight.
ga: Dumɔ ni akɛ he ni sa shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa ni efee ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la

english: Why do my tomato plants have plenty of big green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stem branches instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei aniji. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen, so the plant is pulling leftover food from its old leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha nɔ hee ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, sucking out the plant's water and spreading plant sicknesses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Pods shrivel and turn black when there is too much moisture and dark shade in the farm, which creates fungal diseases, or when the tree is carrying more pods than its roots can feed.
ga: Pods lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Aloo kɛ́ tso ko hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and replant seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties lose their strength and yield potential after the first harvest, meaning seeds saved from that harvest will produce weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni baahi shi yɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato pile lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mulching keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, holds in moisture, and prevents weeds from growing around the crop.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it necessary to remove weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak root systems and cannot win the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during their early growth stage.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ awuu koni ená hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground, so when the bunch gets heavy, the top weight easily pulls the whole root system out of wet, soft soil unless you support it with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ nine lɛ tsii lɛ, tsiimɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baajie shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and build food. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Legume plants like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they release this natural plant food into the soil, feeding the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the tall trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Tall shade trees or plantains act as umbrellas that protect the cocoa until it grows strong roots and tough leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out in the sunshine to make food for the root tubers underneath. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. When a heavy fruit bunch grows, the top becomes heavy and strong winds can push the tree over unless it is propped up with a sturdy wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ da lɛ Yiteŋ lɛ mli wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa tso lɛ shi ja tso ni wa ko fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot underground when too much rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the ground for days, water fills all the soil spaces and suffocates the roots, causing bacteria and fungi to rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Nu eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, putting heat stress on the plant. Regular watering at the root level and slight shade during hot afternoons help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem water or safe insect treatment stops them from damaging new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooofɔ neem nu nɔ loo ojie kooloi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baai heei lɛ.

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool shade. Pruning excess leaves and weeds allows air and sunlight to dry the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Baai kɛ jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my crops stay tiny and slow-growing whenever weeds grow close around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya be mli ni jwɛi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's nutrients so they can grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛnyɛ amɛdara oya

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, cool weather. Removing infected pods early and cutting back overgrown branches allows air and sunlight in, which helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Kɛ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the stems and branches on my cocoa tree to swell up and look deformed?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi cacao tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ miifu ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ehiii?

english: This swelling is caused by the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread between trees by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because there is no cure once a tree is infected, removing the sick tree stops the virus from spreading to neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Fuumɔ nɛɛ jɛ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ahe. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, tsamɔ ko bɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do small insects cause my young cocoa pods to turn brown and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mi-kookoo bibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Insects like capsid bugs bite into young pods to feed on their juices, leaving dark spots that turn into dead wounds. Spraying approved insecticides at the right time of year protects the young pods so they can grow to full size.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ capsids lɛ ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛye nu lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni tsɔɔ pilamɔi ni egboi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow better under big shade trees instead of direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be agbo shishi moŋ fe hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally belong under forest canopies. Direct sunlight scorches young leaves and dries out the soil, while shade trees keep the soil moist, cool the farm down, and protect the crop from strong dry winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anaa kookoo tsei yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he

english: Trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by excessive heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Maintaining reasonable shade and keeping soil healthy ensures the flowers stay on the tree long enough to turn into pods.
ga: Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha ni shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh green shoots growing from the base of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots, known as water suckers, steal water and food away from the main tree. Removing them ensures all the tree's strength goes into flowering and growing big cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei wuji amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha cacao tso lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efɔ fɔfɔi ni eda ni etsɔ cacao ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce far fewer pods now than it did fifteen years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past twenty years, their roots become less effective at absorbing nutrients and their branches become worn out. Pruning old wood, feeding the soil, or gradually replanting with fresh seedlings helps restore high yields.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye fe afii 20 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni eniji lɛ fiteɔ. Niji ni egbɔ ni ooofolɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii, loo dumɔwui heei ni ooodu blɛoo lɛ baaye abua ni yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan air pulls moisture out of the leaves faster than roots can drink from dry soil, causing stress. Leaving natural mulch on the soil surface helps trap groundwater so the leaves stay green longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. kɛ haomɔ baa Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block light from each other. Spacing them correctly gives each tree enough room and resources to produce abundant pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ baai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does clearing weeds around my trees actually help my cocoa yield more pods?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi-cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi-cacao pod lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for water, light, and soil fertilizer. Clearing them leaves all the nourishment in the ground for the cocoa roots, allowing the trees to grow faster and produce more fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo shishifãi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide tall, broad leaves that create necessary shade and hold moisture for the young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water, which prevents the roots from taking up food properly. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. Kompost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a cassava stem cutting is good enough to plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose thick, healthy stems from mature plants that are at least eight months old, free from insect damage or disease, and cut them into pieces with at least 4 to 6 raised buds (nodes).
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji kpaanyɔ lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa. Ebɛ kooloi loo helai ni fiteɔ nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni awó nɔ (nodes) lɛ afo mli bibii.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot take in enough calcium from the soil, which is usually caused by irregular watering or dry soil spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in your field. Switching to beans or peanuts helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eye ebua ni tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aba oŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje tsei afeemɔ shishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady and moisten the top layer of soil deeply, rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can cause seeds to sprout and then dry out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi.

english: How do groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for future crops?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot, when the soil suffers from a lack of water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ náa baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to build raised mounds of earth to plant my yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni madu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and well-drained soil so their large tubers can expand easily underground without rotting from trapped water or standing rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia atomo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii wuji baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni nu ni emɔ amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteee.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young crops slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi babaoo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your young crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, effectively stealing the essential food and resources your crop needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nibii ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ tsei ni wa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I stop using chemical weedkillers on my cocoa farm, how do I keep the weeds from choking my cocoa trees?
ga: Kɛji mikpa tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi ni yeɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa?

english: Weeds can be controlled naturally by clearing them manually using cutlasses or hoes, and by maintaining proper shade trees that reduce the light weeds need to grow rapidly.
ga: Abaanyɛ akudɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛ niji jieɔ kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni haa jwɛi ni he hiaa la lɛ baa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds affect the growth and health of my cocoa trees if left unchecked?
ga: Te jwɛi baaná mi-cacao tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees, which can stunt the trees' growth and significantly lower their pod production.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni eha pod ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Does using chemical weedkillers damage the soil where my cocoa trees grow?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Frequent use of harsh weedkilling chemicals can kill beneficial soil organisms and lower soil fertility over time, making it harder for cocoa roots to absorb natural nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Will my cocoa trees still grow healthy pods if I do not give them chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ lolo kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haaa lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, cocoa trees can produce healthy pods without chemical fertilizers if you nourish the soil with natural organic material like decomposed cocoa pod husks, compost, and leaf litter.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei baanyɛ awo cocoa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsuuu nii. Kɛji okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kookoo tsei ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ baai amli jwɛi ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii,

english: How can I protect my cocoa crops from pests if I do not use chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can manage pests naturally by regularly pruning your trees to improve airflow, removing diseased pods quickly, and encouraging beneficial insects that feed on cocoa pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ otsei lɛ ni oookpa daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. ni ewo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ kookoo mli kooloi lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: How can I feed my cocoa crops naturally without spending money on artificial chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu cacao tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee lɛ ahe?

english: You can feed your soil by leaving fallen cocoa leaves to rot around the base of the trees and adding composted organic waste, which naturally recycles nutrients back into the root zone.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni oooshi amɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afata he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What does it mean to have organic cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ aaaná kookoo tso ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli?

english: Organic cocoa means your crops are grown naturally without any synthetic fertilizers, chemical weedkillers, or artificial pesticides, resulting in pure and chemical-free cocoa beans.
ga: Organic cocoa tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ tsuuu nii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofai ni akɛfee ni gbeɔ kooloi Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ŋmeii ni he tse ni tsofai bɛ mli.

english: Why are buyers interested in cocoa that is grown without any chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ kookoo ni aduɔ ni tsofai bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many chocolate manufacturers and international consumers prefer chemical-free cocoa because it is healthier, safer to consume, and environmentally friendly, often fetching a better market price.
ga: Mɛi babaoo ni feɔ tsokolate kɛ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ kookoo ni tsofai bɛ mli lɛ ejaakɛ ehaa mɔ he waa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee Bei pii lɛ, amɛhaa jarayeli jara ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why does farming cocoa without chemicals require more farm workers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsofai bɛ mli ni akɛduɔ kookoo lɛ biɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi babaoo lɛ?

english: Without chemical weedkillers or automated sprays, tasks like weed clearing, pruning, and composting must be done by hand, which takes more physical time and labor to keep the farm clean.
ga: Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ bɛ. pruning Ni esa akɛ akɛ niji afee ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ biɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse.

english: How does avoiding chemicals change the daily workload on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni mitsiɔ mihe kɛjɛɔ he lɛ tsakeɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ ni mitsuɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Instead of periodic chemical spraying, your daily routine shifts to regular physical tasks like manual weeding, farm sanitation, compost preparation, and constant monitoring for pests.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofɔ tsofai anɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, Odaa nifeemɔi lɛ baatsake kɛya gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ anɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ Kompost he saamɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ daa

english: I bought NPK fertilizer and applied it to my farm, but my crops are still not growing well. What could be wrong?
ga: Mihe NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo. Mɛni sane nɛ?

english: Even if you apply NPK fertilizer, crops cannot absorb it if the soil is missing small essential nutrients like zinc or boron. Under a rule called the 'Law of the Minimum,' crop growth is limited by whatever essential nutrient is missing most.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɛji akɛ niyenii bibii ni he hiaa tamɔ zinc loo boron bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘minimum rule’ lɛ shishi lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Can missing small elements in the ground stop my NPK fertilizer from working?
ga: Ani nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi mi NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekatsu nii?

english: Yes. If trace elements like boron or zinc are completely missing from your soil, your crops will not be able to absorb the NPK fertilizer you added, making it look like the fertilizer isn't working.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji nibii tamɔ boron loo zinc bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛfataa he lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: How do I know if the NPK fertilizer I bought for my farm is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If you apply NPK to the soil and see no improvement in your crops, it does not automatically mean the fertilizer is bad. It often means your soil lacks other trace minerals like zinc or boron that the crop needs to absorb the NPK.
ga: Kɛji okɛ NPK wo shikpɔŋ nɔ ni ona akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa hiɛ. Enɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite kɛjɛ ehe. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ mineral krokomɛi tamɔ zinc loo boron ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛjie NPK lɛ.

english: Why is giving NPK fertilizer alone sometimes not enough for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ faaa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: NPK provides primary nutrients, but plants also need trace nutrients like zinc and boron. Without these extra elements present in the soil, the plant cannot absorb or use the NPK properly.
ga: NPK haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa waa. Shi tsei hu he miihia niyenii bibii tamɔ zinc kɛ boron. Kɛji nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ NPK loo amɛkɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is this 'Law of the Minimum' that people talk about when feeding crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘mlai ni baa shi fe fɛɛ’ ni gbɔmɛi wieɔ he kɛ́ amɛmiiye ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The Law of the Minimum means that crop growth is controlled by the scarcest nutrient available. If even one minor nutrient like zinc or boron is missing from the soil, the plant cannot absorb the major nutrients like NPK.
ga: Mla ni baa shi fe fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii ni anaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kudɔɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji niyenii bibii tamɔ zinc loo boron bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei hu nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ NPK lɛ.

english: If my crops are not taking up nutrients from the ground, what is stopping them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mitsei lɛ naaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hu? Mɛni baatsi amɛnaa?

english: Crops are often stopped from absorbing soil nutrients when key micro-nutrients, such as boron or zinc, are absent from the soil, preventing the uptake of applied fertilizers like NPK.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kpaɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he nitsumɔ kɛji niyenii bibii ni he hiaa tamɔ boron loo zinc lɛ laaje kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ NPK lɛ aná.

english: My neighbor used NPK and got good crop results, but when I used the same NPK on my field nothing happened. Why?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ NPK tsuɔ nii ni enáa yibii kpakpai. Shi kɛ mikɛ NPK lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baaa. Maaba?

english: Soil composition varies from field to field. Your land might be lacking specific elements like zinc or boron that your neighbor's soil has, which prevents your crops from absorbing the NPK fertilizer.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Ekolɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ zinc loo boron bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does NPK fertilizer need to mix with other things in the soil before crops can feed on it?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii afutu nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani adu tsei?

english: NPK needs to interact with a balanced soil environment. If the soil lacks trace elements like zinc or boron when the NPK touches it, the crops simply will not be able to take in the NPK.
ga: Ehe miihia ni NPK kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ zinc loo boron faaa beni NPK kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ajie NPK kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ.

english: Could my soil be missing something small that makes my expensive fertilizer useless?
ga: Ani ekolɛ nɔ ko fioo ko bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaha mi-ŋmei ni jara wa lɛ afee nɔ ni he ehiaaa?

english: Yes, missing tiny amounts of essential micro-nutrients like boron or zinc can completely prevent your crops from taking up major fertilizers like NPK.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii bibii ni he hiaa tamɔ boron loo zinc lɛ faaa yɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa kwraa koni amɛkaná shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK.

english: What happens to NPK fertilizer when it touches soil that lacks essential minerals like zinc?
ga: Mɛni baa NPK ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ zinc bɛ mli lɛ kpe?

english: When NPK touches soil that is missing zinc or boron, the crops are unable to absorb the NPK, leaving the nutrients unusable in the ground despite your effort to fertilize.
ga: Kɛji NPK kɛ shikpɔŋ ni zinc loo boron bɛ mli lɛ kpe Nibii ni adu lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ NPK, ni no baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. Kɛji obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ fɔ awo mli po.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantains near my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo ni ehaa amɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry up when they receive too much direct sunlight or lack enough moisture in the soil, which happens when there is insufficient shade on the farm.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani pods lɛ feɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they do not have enough water or nutrients to support them all, or if there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi anɔ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ready for me to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ mafolɔ?

english: You can tell cocoa pods are ready when their color changes completely; pods that were green turn yellow, and pods that were reddish or purple turn bright orange-yellow.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ehiɛ su tsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔlii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni pods ni tsuɔ loo purple lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ.

english: How does cutting off unnecessary branches help my trees bear more cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the tree, which prevents diseases and ensures the tree sends its strength into growing pods rather than useless leaves.
ga: Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly through water droplets in cool, wet weather, especially on overcrowded farms with little airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why are white insects covered with ants clinging to my cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni miiho yɛ mikookoo tsei kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The white creatures are mealybugs that suck sap from your cocoa tree. Ants farm these mealybugs for sweet liquid and help spread them, which can transfer damaging viruses to your trees.
ga: Adebɔɔ yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmeii ni nuɔ cacao tsei amli nu lɛ. Ants kwɛɔ nɛkɛ mealybugs nɛɛ anɔ kɛha nu ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni fiteɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã otsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are the branches and stems of my cocoa trees swelling up in some places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei aniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Swelling on stems and roots is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus disease, an infection spread by mealybugs that weakens the tree and eventually causes it to die if not managed.
ga: Fuumɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow even when the farm gets enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Leaves turn pale yellow when the soil runs out of essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when excessive rain waterlogs the soil and prevents roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaye nii.

english: What can I put on the ground to keep my soil wet when the dry Harmattan winds start?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves, grass, or plant remains around the base of your trees—known as mulching—covers the dirt and stops the sun and dry winds from evaporating soil moisture.
ga: Okɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo tso ni eshwɛ lɛ afɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ he. Koni akɛ muji ato ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akagbi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow better when I use a tractor to plow the land instead of using a traditional hand hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ trakta tsu nii kɛtsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii yɛ blema ŋmãa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tractor plowing loosens the soil much deeper than a hand hoe. Loose soil allows roots to easily grow deep, reach buried moisture, and absorb more nutrients needed for healthy crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Nine ni ashɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni afu lɛ nɔ ni anáa niyenii babaoo ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers underground if I do not soften the hard dry soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee sũ ni egbi ni wa lɛ blɛoo dani midu hu?

english: Hard soil acts like a wall that prevents cassava roots from expanding. Softening the soil allows tubers to swell freely into large, bulky roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni tsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ blɛoo lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi wuji yɛ heyeli mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow weak and tall without producing much fruit when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ shɔŋŋ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plant spends all its energy growing tall to reach light instead of producing pepper fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná la moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do weeds affect the size of my yam tubers while they are growing in the soil?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Weeds steal the soil food and water that the yam vines need. Without enough food, the yam leaves cannot produce energy to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni sweet potato wain tsei he hiaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Sweet potato baai lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl down and dry up during the hot dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Hot sun and dry wind make tomato leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it. The leaves curl up to reduce their surface area and save moisture from escaping.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first brief rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kuku ko sɛɛ? Klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: The first rain often only wet the top layer of dry soil. Seeds absorb that small moisture and start sprouting, but die quickly because the dry deep soil underneath starves them of continuous water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa nu fioo ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Shi amɛgboiɔ oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ haa nu bɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the tips when the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaf tips usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stem fibers and green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my next season's maize crop grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil to feed the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto eshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa tree blossoms fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is under stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack, causing the tree to abort young flowers to save its own life.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ shiɔ efɔfɔi bibii lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: How do I know that my rice crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting without losing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mifiteee dumɔwui?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 percent of the field turns a golden straw color and the grains feel hard when bitten. Harvesting too late causes the dry grains to drop onto the ground.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni omɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 etsɔ jwɛi ni ji shika tsuru lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ amɛ Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and make food; adding fertilizer or compost early in the season prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce huge green leaves above ground but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves instead of food. Balancing the soil with fertilizers rich in potassium encourages the plant to store energy in its root tubers instead.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji yɛ niyenii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or lack of pollination by beneficial insects. Keeping shade trees in your farm helps maintain humidity so the flowers stay healthy and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni haaa tso lɛ afee nɔ ko lɛ hewɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eefite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black, rotting bottoms on tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium into the growing fruit.
ga: Tomato shishi ni fiteɔ ni ji diŋ lɛ jɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves to manufacture food. Lifting the vines off the damp ground also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases, leading to much bigger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo, ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akamɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow very thin and weak when I plant seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures every individual plant gets enough resources to grow thick stems and heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and roll up during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The hot, dry Harmattan winds pull water out of plantain leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the dry ground. Covering the soil around the base with dry mulch helps lock in moisture so the plant stays green longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting when heavy rains fall right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to breathe as they sprout, but heavy rain fills all air pockets with water. Waterlogged soil smothers the seed, allowing soil fungi to rot it before the shoot reaches sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli eyiɔ kɛ nu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When these roots decay, they leave natural fertilizer in the ground that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why are holes appearing on my pepper leaves overnight when I cannot see any pests during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji je kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ? Be mli ni minaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like caterpillars and armyworms, hide under soil or dry leaves during the hot day to protect themselves and come out to eat your crops at night. Inspecting plants late in the evening helps you spot and control these nocturnal insects.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ asraafoi awuiyelɔi. Ehiɛɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ baai ni egbi mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye ŋmɔshi nibii gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei amli gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ gbɛkɛ nɛɛ ni oye amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii wuji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their roots are small and cannot absorb water fast enough. Planting shade plants like plantains nearby creates a protective umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is under stress from lack of water, missing key soil nutrients, or when there are no tiny insects like midges present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ teŋgbɛ nibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp weather. It spreads fast when cocoa trees are crowded and sunlight cannot reach the trunk to dry off the moisture.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa tree when I want it to yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi? Be ni miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Trimming removes old or weak branches so sunlight and air can flow through the canopy. This prevents diseases and forces the tree to send its water and food into producing healthy pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabi ni akɛ baai krokomɛi afata he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but leaves me with tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its energy into leaf growth instead of roots when the soil has too much nitrogen or when the soil is packed too tightly for the tubers to expand easily.
ga: Cassava haa hewalɛ kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, this acts as natural plant food that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops drop or curl their leaves to save water. Curling reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping moisture from escaping out into the dry air.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi loo amɛfoɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ oyitsɔi shwie shi lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ oyitsɔi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that drink the water and eat the plant food in the soil faster than your crops can, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the ground to be moist before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Putting fertilizer on dry ground leaves it unusable and can even burn the roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii, ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive stems and leaves that cannot handle full tropical sun. Planting food crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides natural shade umbrellas and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii tsei tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young upper growth, showing that fertilizer or organic compost needs to be added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with organic mulch traps moisture in the dirt during hot dry spells, prevents weeds from taking over, and keeps the root area cool so the crop can continue feeding.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ aye niyenii

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or tomato on the exact same spot on my farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop family in the same place every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like beans or maize breaks this pest cycle and restores soil health.
ga: Weku kome mli tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ tsei ahe helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants along with dark dirt left inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ diŋ ni eshwɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft stem tissue inside the funnel. Early detection and applying targeted biological control or safe spray when the worms are small prevents total crop destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii beni ŋmeii lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa koni akpa?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when their leaves begin turning yellow and shedding, and cracks start appearing in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers expand underground, usually around 8 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce foods that travel down the stem to grow large, healthy tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Small sucker shoots compete with the main plantain stem for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the parent plant receives maximum energy to produce large fruit bunches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii Amɛkɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the early rain at the start of the year is enough for planting maize, or if it is just a false rain?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ loo eji amale nugbɔ kɛkɛ?

english: A single rainfall can wet the top surface while leaving the deeper soil bone dry. You should dig down into the soil to check if moisture has soaked at least hand-depth deep before planting seeds to avoid losing seeds to dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli wui ni mli kwɔ lɛ agbiɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii ni okwɛ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ebote tso lɛ mli dani odu dumɔwui. Enɛ ji koni akafite dumɔwui kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: When is the best time of day to apply liquid fertilizer or spray to my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli loo mikɛ nu awo mli?

english: The best time is early morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. Applying sprays under hot midday sun causes rapid evaporation and can scorch tender leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ hulu la shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai bibii.

english: Why should I get my farm's soil tested before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Testing your soil shows you exactly what nutrients are missing in your land. It prevents you from wasting money buying the wrong fertilizers and helps you feed your crops only what they need to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaaa ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa nɔ, ni ehaa okɛ nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa onibii lɛ haa koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well even when I use the same fertilizer I used last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ?

english: Soil gets tired and loses different nutrients after every harvest. Using the same fertilizer every year without checking the soil condition can cause an imbalance where your soil lacks certain key plant foods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii daa afi ni okwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee nɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ he ni hɔmɔ yeɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tsei amli niyenii komɛi ahe lɛ.

english: Healthy soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and has earthworms. If your soil turns hard like clay or dries out very fast, it needs organic matter or soil treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli tseɔ, efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ loo egbiɔ oya waa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ahe miihia.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much fertilizer on the land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops, cause leaves to turn brown, and ruin your harvest. It also wastes your money and can make the soil too salty for future planting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni efiteɔ onifeemɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ shika hu, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ kɛha nibii ni aduɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: If I put fertilizer on my crops, does that guarantee I will get a big harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ Ani abaaha mi nɔmimaa akɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer gives plants food, but good yields also require adequate water, proper weeding, protection from pests, and planting at the right time. Fertilizer alone cannot save crops if other field conditions are poor.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii. Shi nibii kpakpai ni afeɔ lɛ he miihia nu ni fa lolo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ Hebuu kɛ dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Gbɛjianɔtoo pɛ nyɛŋ ahere ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji shihilɛi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ehiii.

english: Why does heavy rain seem to ruin the fertilizer I just put on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ fite ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away fertilizer from the top layer of soil before the roots have time to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but heavy downpours are not expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛnu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cool. Applying fertilizer during the hottest part of the day can stress the plants and scorch their roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha eshishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plant is hungry for nitrogen, getting too much or too little water, or suffering from root damage. A quick soil or plant check helps identify which nutrient is missing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia otso lɛ. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ooona? loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ enaa enɔ hewalɛ Shikpɔŋ loo tso lɛ mli kwɛmɔ oya baaye abua ni ana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni elaaje.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the cobs remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋshɔŋloo lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: This happens when your soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. The plant uses all its energy to grow leaves instead of making big, full cobs.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii wuji ni baai eyi mli obɔ.

english: How can I know if my crops are weak because of a disease or because the soil lacks food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Nutrient shortages usually cause gradual color changes like yellowing across whole rows of crops, while diseases often cause spots, sudden wilting, or rotting patches that spread quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ fiofio, tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ helai srɔtoi haa ŋmɔtɔ baa trukaa loo egboɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Without stakes, leaves stay shaded on the ground, leading to much smaller yam yields.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: No, planting maize too close causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and tiny, underdeveloped cobs.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. ni afeee lɛ lolo lɛ

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient from the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant build food and turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni efee niyenii ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my garden vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering bare soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out water in the dirt, keeps weeds from invading, and protects topsoil from washing away in heavy rains.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally form their pods underground. After pollination, the stems bend downward to push the growing seed pegs into soft soil where the groundnuts can safely swell and mature.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. after pollination Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi koni ekɛtsi dumɔwu ni miida lɛ ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli he ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra young suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal food and water away from the main mother stem. Pruning them away leaves only one strong sucker, ensuring the main plant yields a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afo baai lɛ, ebaaha tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Enɛ ji koni tso titri lɛ aná plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the underside of leaves and sucking out sap. Spraying with organic neem oil or approved pest spray controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting in the dirt before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater sits in the ground for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy water to drain away so tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa muji lɛ shwieɔ shi. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and die when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Keeping fast-growing shade crops like plantain or taller shade trees protects the cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ to he lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together in the row, will I harvest more corn?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant nutrients. This competition leads to thin stems and small or empty cobs, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it necessary to lift my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ awoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which encourages larger, healthier yam tubers to grow underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread viruses. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa? Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed on the tender young leaves inside the central growing point of the maize plant, which can stunt crop growth if left untreated.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which stem parts should I select when preparing cassava cuttings for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mahala beni miisaa ŋmei niji kɛha dumɔ?

english: The best stem cuttings come from the middle section of mature, healthy cassava plants. Stems that are too soft, young, or taken from diseased plants will not sprout strong roots or high-yielding stems.
