ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni afolɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ Eji bibii tsɔ lolo Loo ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ shishifãi ni wa loo ŋmeii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baakwɛɛɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one parent plantain tree drains water and nutrients away from the main stem. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures larger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Dumɔwu kome pɛ he lɛ baaha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shwiili.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any tomatoes during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and stay alive, rather than spending resources on producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛwo yibii

english: How does spreading dry grass over the soil around my crops help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a protective blanket (mulch). It slows down water evaporation from the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents unwanted weeds from taking root.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. (Mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I avoid placing chemical fertilizer right next to the main stem of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ atso titri lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against plant stems can cause severe chemical burns to tender roots and stems. Fertilizer should be placed a short distance away in a ring or line where feeder roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ashã shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ waa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai amli yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛɛɛ fioo. ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides the cool environment and moisture the young cocoa needs until its roots grow deep enough to handle heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa cocoa tsei lɛ aba. Kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ dɔlɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key food soil gives to crops. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its oldest leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just like they need water. When water stays trapped in flat or heavy soil for too long, it drowns the roots and causes rot, which is why planting on raised ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi ni eha amɛgboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same spot empties the soil of those nutrients and lets pests build up in the dirt, whereas switching to crops like groundnuts or beans restores food back to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tsei yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or a sudden lack of water. The plant drops the flowers to save its own energy and survive the stress instead of trying to feed new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ aduawai heei aba

english: What is causing the inner leaves of my young maize plants to be eaten up overnight with small droppings left inside?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome? Mɛni eshwɛ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the center funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on the tender young leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Does leaving grass and weeds around my crops really stop my yams from growing big underground?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baatsi mi-sweet potato lɛ naa diɛŋtsɛ koni ekakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji?

english: Yes, because weeds grow fast and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your yams. When weeds take the soil's food, the yam plant does not have enough energy to expand its roots into big tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Beni jwɛi ba koni amɛbaye niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ eshishifãi lɛ ni etsɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Lifting the vines up on tall sticks allows all the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and stay away from damp soil diseases, leading to much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Enɛ haa sweet potato ni da kwraa baa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce very small heads or pods, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough food to produce high yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bulbs loo pods bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the certified seeds I buy from the agro-dealer grow better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred in laboratories for strong growth, disease resistance, and high yields. Seeds saved from past harvests naturally lose these special strengths over time and produce weaker plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa, helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛi krokomɛi nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Keeping bigger shade trees or planting plantains provides a cool canopy that traps moisture and protects the young plants while they establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni miida loo plantains ni miida lɛ baaha shade ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe beni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the stems of my pepper plants help them survive hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji Pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a shield over the earth. It prevents the hot sun from evaporating soil water quickly and keeps the roots cool so the plant stays hydrated.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he tsɔne Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Giving the soil well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores this essential nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every season if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efo tso helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young cassava bushes even if the cassava is already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? mi ŋmei tso lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi momo moŋ, shi.

english: Weeds steal invisible resources underground by drinking up soil water and fertilizer that your cassava needs. Clearing weeds ensures all soil moisture and food go into growing bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni anaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why does my yam crop need a tall wooden stake to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni enine ashɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to process energy for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf decay and allows the plant to send maximum energy down into developing huge tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ bulbs agboi amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. When conditions are too hot or dry, the plant sheds its blossoms to conserve water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole bush?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava signals maturity when its bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, the main stem turns woody and gray, and the soil at the base of the stem starts cracking as swollen tubers push upward.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ mli ŋmei ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the maize seeds harvested from my farm for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Grown hybrid seeds lose their strength and uniformity in the next generation. Planting saved seeds often results in small cobs, weaker stems, and lower yields compared to planting fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni adu lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ haa dumɔwui bibii, ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛmɔ he.

english: Why is it harmful to apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry during the Harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil moisture for roots to absorb it safely. Placing dry fertilizer in dry soil under hot sun concentrates heavy salts around roots, which burns and destroys them.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no baashã ni egbe amɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily get scorched by the hot Ghanaian sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide thick leaf shade, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ amɛ awo Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli tse. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads quickly during heavy rains and damp weather. Clearing weeds and trimming crowded branches lets sunlight and air flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli wa lɛ afolɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and rolling up during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and rolling leaves are a plant's natural defense against heat and lack of water. When it gets too dry, the plant rolls its leaves tightly to trap moisture and prevent itself from losing water.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he. Kɛji egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu akafite.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Nitrogen makes the stem and leaves grow big, but potassium is what tells the plant to build thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa. Shi potassium ji nɔ ni kɛɔ tsei koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops instead of just leaving them to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, quickly sucking up the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing them gives your main crops all the resources they need to give you a big harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛmuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei titrii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa bo koni amɛná ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Will I harvest more corn if I put three or four seeds together in one planting hole?
ga: Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ fata ŋmãa bu kome mli?

english: No, putting too many seeds in one hole causes them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Instead of getting many big cobs, you will end up with thin, weak stalks that produce very small or no cobs at all.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Yɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, egbeɔ naa kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii ko kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant maize seeds from my last harvest instead of buying new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, heɔ dumɔwui ehei ni awo he odase.

english: Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose their power in the next generation, producing weaker plants and far less grain. Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases and yield much more food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without making any peppers when it gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When weather gets too hot, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and stay alive. Giving your farm light shade or extra water during dry peaks helps the plants keep their flowers and form peppers.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo loo nu kroko ni fata he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my watermelon vines producing many flowers, but only a few of them turn into watermelons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ watermelon?

english: Watermelon vines have male and female flowers on the same plant. Only female flowers grow into fruits after bees carry pollen to them from male flowers. If there are no bees to pollinate, the flowers drop off without making fruit.
ga: Watermelon wain tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ tso kome nɔ. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai beni ŋmeii kɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli lɛ baha amɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii ni baawo pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaaku kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees still dropping flowers even after I spent money to spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo yɛ be mli ni mifite shika ni mikɛ tsofai shwie amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Chemicals only kill targeted pests or diseases, but cocoa trees will still drop flowers if they are suffering from lack of water, bad soil nutrients, or excessive heat stress.
ga: Tsofai gbeɔ kooloo loo hela ni akɛ ehiɛ fɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Shi cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ lolo kɛji nu faaa yɛ amɛmli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine

english: Can spraying too much chemical on my cocoa farm actually reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical or mixing it incorrectly can burn the leaves and flowers of the cocoa tree, causing damage that reduces the number of pods the tree can produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛfutuɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã cacao tso lɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔii. Enɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa ni haa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Does it matter what time of day I spray pesticides on my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, spraying during the cool early morning or late afternoon works best because high sun heat can cause the chemical to dry up too quickly or burn the wet plant leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulu lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ agbi oya tsɔ loo eshã tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in farms that have too much shade, high humidity, and poor air movement during rainy periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ amli.

english: What causes tiny, dry, burnt-looking patches on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shãa he okadii bibii baa? No tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni eshã yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: These dry patches are caused by mirid insects (capsids) that suck the sap out of young shoots and pods, damaging the plant tissues and preventing normal pod growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hei ni egbi nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Efiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni etsĩɔ pod lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings look yellow and stunted in their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have small roots and soft leaves that get scorched easily by direct sunlight; they need shade from plants like plantains to keep them cool while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Why is my old cocoa farm producing fewer pods now than it used to five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, they continuously drain nutrients from the soil, and without added organic matter or nutrients, the soil becomes tired and unable to support high pod production.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ eda Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni kɛji akɛ nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua ni afee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my farm actually needs fertilizer before I go and buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ? Dani ebaayahe loo oyahe

english: Look at the leaves and growth—pale yellow leaves and small, weak shoots are common signs of nutrient starvation, but an extension officer can test your soil to tell you the exact nutrient missing.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ—baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii bibii. Eji niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ he okadi. Shi extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ koni ekɛɛ bo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods after I trim off some of their branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mifolɔ eniji komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: If you prune too heavily, the tree loses the leaves it needs to capture sunlight and make food, forcing it to spend energy growing new leaves instead of making pods.
ga: Kɛji ofo tsei babaoo Tsei lɛ laajeɔ baai ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsu nii kɛye niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai heei moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii.

english: Why do mature cocoa trees grow better when there are large shade trees scattered around the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Large shade trees shield cocoa trees from direct sun heat, help the ground hold moisture during dry seasons, and drop dead leaves that decompose into natural food for the cocoa roots.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni okɛ baai ni egboi, ni fiteɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha kookoo shishifãi lɛ ashwie.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and resume growing tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow in a V-pattern from the tips inward, and the stalks look pale green and thin rather than dark green and robust.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why are my young tomato flowers falling off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi bibii lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when daytime temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing lush leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Feemɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to wilt and die even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by fungal or bacterial root rot. Excess water smothers the roots so they cannot breathe or take up nutrients, causing the plant to collapse from the roots up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu loo amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ha tso lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Rotating maize with cowpeas restores lost nutrients naturally, breaks pest cycles, and improves soil health for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Gbalamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees curling up and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Brown, curling leaves on cocoa trees are typically caused by intense direct sunlight from a lack of shade canopy trees, or by sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids) feeding on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni jɛɔ cacao tso lɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni yeɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I keep weeds from choking my young yam vines after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbe sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ anaa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering your yam mounds with a layer of dry straw or grass mulch smothers emerging weeds, retains soil moisture, and keeps the soil cool, allowing yam shoots to grow without weed competition.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ha sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi ni miiba lɛ akabote mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow. If soil pests like nematodes or stem borers weaken the root system, the tree cannot support the weight of heavy fruit bunches during strong winds and easily gets uprooted.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers Haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: What makes cassava roots turn woody and hard to cook instead of soft?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi feɔ tso ni ehoomɔ wa moŋ fe ni eeefee blɛoo?

english: Cassava roots become woody when left in the ground past their ideal harvest window, or when the crop experiences prolonged drought stress that causes the plant to store tough fiber in the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he. aloo kɛ́ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ toɔ tsɔji ni wa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my garden eggs develop dark, sunken rotten spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni egboi yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the blossom end of garden eggs (eggplants) are caused by blossom-end rot, a condition triggered by calcium deficiency in the fruit, usually resulting from irregular watering habits.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii (eggplant) fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ diŋ lɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ mli. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build green leaves, or that heavy rain has waterlogged the soil and drowned the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on sap and spread viruses, causing the young leaves to deform as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ehaa baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings suddenly rot at the base and fall over flat in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni aduɔ lɛ Mine lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called 'damping-off,' which happens when nursery soil stays too wet and crowded, creating an environment where ground fungi attack the soft stems of tender seedlings.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fungal hela kɛ enɛ baa. ‘Damping’, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium, which prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo calcium ni faaa Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing broad leaves but failing to form a tight round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather becomes too hot, if they don't get consistent water, or if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth cycle.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ baafee ekome kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni anáaa daa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, offering the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the suckers that sprout around my main plantain tree to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantains titrii lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ.

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, which results in smaller, weaker bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall stems with lots of green leaves but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing tall stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of sending nutrients down to expand the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I place dry granular fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ji granular fertilizer lɛ woɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem concentrates harsh salts on the plant's skin, which causes 'fertilizer burn' and damages the roots and stem base.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya tso lɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa ‘ŋmei shãa’ ni efiteɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to full sunlight for photosynthesis and keeps the foliage off the moist ground, reducing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa kɛha fotosintɛsis. Ni otsĩ sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni no haa tsei ahe helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient needed for leafy growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost near the base helps the plant regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fata shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni efee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during intense heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from burning. If the leaves unfold again in the evening, it is just normal heat response, but if they stay curled, it could mean insect pests or a virus.
ga: Ha ebɔle ehe yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji hetoo ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛkɛ kɛha dɔlɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lolo Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ.

english: Why is it wrong to drop fertilizer right next to the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tsei ashishi lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer placed directly against the plant stem can burn and damage the stem tissue. It should be placed a few centimeters away in a small ring or hole where the roots can safely reach and absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko loo bu ko mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he ni amɛŋɔ nu lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get steady water and nutrients. Supplying consistent water at the roots and providing shade during extreme sun helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ enine shɛɛɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ nɔ daa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava leaves dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and keep its underground tubers alive. Once the rains start again, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the main leaves start turning yellow and dry up. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown spots or linings, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Maize seeds should be buried about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (roughly up to your first finger joint). Planting too deep starves the seedling of energy before it reaches the surface, while planting too shallow leaves it vulnerable to heat and birds.
ga: Esa akɛ afu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee kɛyashi oklɛŋklɛŋ tsitsi lɛ nɔ). Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ akafee dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛyashɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo kɛ okpoi nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ oya.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with crops like beans or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Even with plenty of rain, your crops will starve if weeds are competing for the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii po baaye hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes to appear in the leaves of my young cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-kaaba tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on them. Inspecting under the leaves early in the morning and using proper pest management practices will stop them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather. Keeping your farm clear of weeds, pruning excess branches to let sunlight in, and applying approved cocoa spraying chemicals helps control it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Ni oookwɛ ni jwɛi akafee oŋmɔ lɛ Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la abote mli Ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: What causes small brown spots on my young cocoa shoots and leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa? Yɛ mi kookoo bibii lɛ ahe tsei kɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: These spots are typically caused by mirids (also known as capsids), which are tiny insects that suck the sap out of young shoots and pods. Spraying with recommended insecticides during their peak season helps prevent severe damage to your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwie nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees curl up and turn brown during the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Planting shade plants like plantain or temporary shade trees around them protects them from heat stress until their leaves mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli yɛ he fɛɛ he. Tso lɛ baabu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Dropping leaves is a defense mechanism trees use to conserve water during dry weather. You can help your trees survive by leaving organic mulch on the soil surface to hold moisture and retaining permanent shade trees on the farm.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Obaanyɛ oye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fail to form pods if the tree lacks moisture, if pollination insects are absent, or if the tree lacks nutrients. Maintaining soil moisture and avoiding indiscriminate chemical spraying helps pollinating midges do their job.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee pods kɛji tso lɛ mli nu bɛ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ajieee hiɛaŋkwɛmɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why do coffee berries on the same branch ripen at different times instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ tso nine kome nɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni amɛshwereɔ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Coffee trees produce flowers in response to different rainfall events, causing berries to develop in waves. Because of this natural pattern, berries mature at different rates and must be harvested selectively when they turn bright red.
ga: Kɔfi tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi ahetoohamɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ayibii lɛ feɔ ŋshɔkei. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, tsei ayibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. ni esa akɛ ahala amɛ kɛji amɛtsɔ tsuru ni mli tse.

english: Why is it important to cut off the extra branches and water shoots growing from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ nu mli ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra branches and vertical water shoots steal nutrients and water from the main tree without producing good pods. Removing them allows air and light into the canopy and directs energy toward flower and pod growth.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ nu mli ŋmeii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kpakpai. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli ni ehaa hewalɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is clearing weeds with a cutlass around young cocoa roots safer than spraying chemical weedkillers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ dade baajie jwɛi ni bɔle kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ fe tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers can easily drift onto the soft green stem and shallow roots of young cocoa plants and stunt their growth. Careful clearing with a cutlass removes competing weeds without damaging the young tree.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ. ni ji kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛdalɛ kpaa mlɛo oya Kɛ akɛ dagger shwie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni efiteee tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce many leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: A tree with lush leaves but few pods may have an imbalance of nutrients, such as too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium, which are needed specifically for flowering and fruiting.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo. ni fɔsfɔs loo potasium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. ni he hiaa titri kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo

english: Can I grow coffee and cocoa together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu kɔfe kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, but they require proper spacing because coffee needs more sunlight, whereas cocoa prefers shade. Planting them too close together causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, lowering the yield of both crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulu la babaoo he miihia kɔfi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Cocoa sumɔɔ hulutsoo be. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yibii lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer even if the soil on my farm already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Soil holds natural food for plants, but every crop you grow draws out those nutrients to build its leaves and fruits. Fertilizer puts back essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so your crops do not starve over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ gbalaa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ koni ekɛfee baai kɛ aduawai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ akaye onibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow leafy and green. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the crop the food it needs to turn green and make energy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa ni efeɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my farm at one time hurt my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, applying too much chemical fertilizer can 'burn' the roots and stem of the plant. Excess fertilizer draws moisture out of the root zone, causing the leaves to dry up and scorching the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ‘ashã’ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni fa fe nine lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshãa tso lɛ.

english: How does animal manure differ from the bag chemical fertilizer I buy at the store?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ kotoku lɛ he?

english: Bag fertilizer provides a quick burst of concentrated food directly to the crops for fast growth, while animal manure feeds the soil slowly over time and helps the soil hold onto rainwater better.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ ajaa niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ oya kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi aŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii fiofio. Beni be hoɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I just leave them growing in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji miha ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops weak, stunted, and unable to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: If I spray weedicide on my land, how do I keep it from killing my food crops along with the weeds?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekagbe mi niyenii tsei lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Different weedicides target different plant types. Some only kill broad-leaved weeds while leaving grass-like crops safe, but for general weedicides, you must direct the spray carefully only at the weeds and avoid letting the liquid touch your crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei srɔtoi anɔ. Mɛi komɛi gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo pɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ tsei ni tamɔ jwɛi lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shi kɛha tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ pɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu lɛ ni oooha eshɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Is it better to spray weedicide when the weeds are small or wait until they grow big?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ darako loo ooomɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: It is much easier and cheaper to spray weeds when they are small because their leaves absorb the chemical quickly and die easily. Big weeds have strong roots and have already stolen food from your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ beni amɛji bibii lɛ waaa kwraa ni ejara hu waaa ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ tsofai lɛ oya ni amɛgboiɔ oya. Jwɛi wuji yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛmiiju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli momo.

english: Why do crops planted on a newly cleared bush farm still benefit from fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koo mli ŋmɔji heei ni agbele naa lɛ amli lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛ lolo lɛ?

english: A newly cleared farm has basic nutrients, but young seedlings need an extra, easily accessible boost of food early on to build strong roots quickly before harsh weather or pests arrive.
ga: Okwaafoi heei ni ajie lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Shi tsei bibii hu he miihia niyenii ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he mlɛo mra. koni etswa shishifãi ni wa oya dani kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aba

english: Should I place fertilizer right at the base of the crop's stem or a short distance away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi loo mikɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: You should place fertilizer a small distance away from the stem in a ring or hole near the leaves' edges. Placing strong chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can scorch the outer skin of the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo, yɛ ring loo bu ko ni bɛŋkɛ baa lɛ naa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ ashã.

english: What will happen to the fertilizer I apply if a very heavy rain falls right after?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away powdered or granular fertilizer before the crop roots have time to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but not right before a heavy rainstorm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee powda loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛnu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee dani ahum ni naa wa ko baatswa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the first rains start falling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Do not plant with the very first light rain because the soil is still hot and dry underneath. Wait until the soil receives two or three steady, heavy rains so there is enough deep moisture for the seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ shishi. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if I delay planting them after the rainy season has already started?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ fo?

english: If you plant late, your crops will miss the peak rainfall period and may suffer from dry spells later in their growth stage, which results in stunted growth and very small yields.
ga: Kɛji odu sɛɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ bei amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna hɔmɔ shihilɛi yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to receive my seeds and fertilizers before the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ana dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Having your inputs ready early allows you to plant at the exact moment the soil moisture is right. If your inputs arrive late, you lose valuable days of rain, and your crops will not have enough time to mature fully.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfeɔ nii lɛ ahe saamɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei yɛ bei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Kɛji osaji lɛ bashɛ sɛɛ Obaafite nugbɔ ni jara wa gbii babaoo. Ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my young plants if I apply fertilizer long after planting instead of on schedule?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo amɛmli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ yɛ be ni ato lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ najiaŋ?

english: Applying fertilizer too late means your plants miss the early stage when they need nutrients most to build strong stems and roots, leading to weak plants that cannot produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ shɛɛɛ shishijee be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ awo yibii kpakpai lɛ baa.

english: How long does it usually take from the day I plant maize until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Most standard maize varieties in Ghana take between 90 to 120 days (3 to 4 months) to fully grow and mature for harvest, depending on whether you plant early-maturing or late-maturing seed types.
ga: Abele henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 (nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) dani amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra loo dumɔwui ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some crops take many months to harvest while others are ready in just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi aheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkpaa nii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ klalo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different natural growth speeds; short-term crops like leafy vegetables focus their energy on fast leaf growth, while long-term crops like cassava or cocoa spend months building strong roots and stems before producing yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai ni baa yɔɔ mli lɛ maa baa dalɛ oya nɔ mi. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei loo kookoo Eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa baa dani ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my crops to mature much slower than the time written on the seed package?
ga: Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida yɛ sɛɛ mli kwraa fe nɔ ni aŋma yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Poor soil fertility, unexpected dry periods, pest attacks, or planting in poor sunlight can slow down a crop's natural growth rate, forcing it to take longer to reach harvest time.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii hulutsoo be ni akpaaa gbɛ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuamɔ Loo hulutsoo be ni ehiii mli ni edaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ dalɛ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani akpaa nii.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die even though it rained just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very shallow roots. If the top layer of soil dries out quickly under hot sun during a break in the rains, the roots cannot reach deeper soil water, causing the young plants to wilt.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ Shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ nu he yɛ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baagbi.

english: How can I check if my farm soil has enough water for planting my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaakwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Dig down about hand-depth into the soil and squeeze a handful; if it forms a moist ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil has ideal moisture for planting.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee tso tso ko ni mli kwɔ ni okɛ nine kome ajie mli. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu shwieee shi Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster in some months of the rainy season compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ be nyɔji komɛi amli kɛ akɛto ekrokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Crops grow fastest during periods where there is a good balance of frequent rain and bright sunlight, allowing the leaves to make maximum food while the roots receive constant water.
ga: Tsei daa oya yɛ nugbɔ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa be mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kwraa yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ naa nu daa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield small harvests when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete directly for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, preventing any of the plants from reaching their full strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ edaŋ kwraa.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees protect fragile seedlings from harsh sun, keep the soil moist, and help them survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Shade tsei buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in sunlight to create energy for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines off the ground also protects the leaves from humidity, damp soil, and crawling pests.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ, kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for green leaves and full corn cob development.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why is it harmful to spread chemical fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafata miŋmɔ lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water so roots can absorb them safely. When applied to dry soil, concentrated chemical salts can scorch and burn the crop's roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni amɛshã amɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This feeding pattern is caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl deep inside the growing center of the maize plant where the leaves are tender.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei ni baa bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ niyenii yeli nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rain floods my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to drown and allowing fungal decay to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Okɛ shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli ni oha ŋmeii lɛ akumɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal food and water from the main mother plant. Pruning away weaker suckers ensures that the main stem gets enough energy to bear large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any tomatoes start growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save moisture rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo aduawai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores soil nutrients so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by excessive heat stress. Shielding young plants and managing pests early keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni fe nine mli Dumɔwui ahebuu kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from severe heat, long dry spells, or lack of shade. Maintaining shade trees on your farm helps keep the air cool and humid so flowers can set into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa miimɔ amɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo hulutsoo ni bɛ hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps heavy rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: What makes dark, soft soil better for my crops than hard red soil?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii fe shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa?

english: Dark soil is rich in organic matter like decayed leaves and manure, which holds moisture and plant food much better than hard, dry clay or sandy soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ.

english: It is best to plant after the soil gets two or three good, soaking rains. Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to scorch and fail to sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ kpakpa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need full sunlight on their leaves to feed the growing yam tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa ni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni eye ebua sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when carrying full fruit bunches. Removing excess shoots and propping the trunk with wooden poles stops them from tipping over.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛtsii kɛji aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the inner leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of the plant. Checking the middle whorl of leaves early and applying appropriate controls keeps them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ. Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster in my field than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients quickly. Weeding early in the season gives your main crops room to grow before weeds take over.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ daa dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: How many farming seasons should I expect if my farm is in the Greater Accra or coastal region?
ga: Okwaayeli be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ Greater Accra loo ŋshɔnaa kpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: The coastal belt and Greater Accra experience two rainy seasons each year, which allows farmers in these areas to plan for two main cropping periods.
ga: Ŋshɔnaa kɛ Accra yɛ nugbɔ bei enyɔ daa afi. Enɛ haa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei nɛɛ toɔ gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii enyɔ.

english: Can I successfully grow and harvest mangoes in the coastal region of Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ mango ni makpa yɛ Ghana ŋshɔnaa hei lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Yes, mangoes grow very well in the coastal region and Greater Accra because the weather and seasonal cycles in these areas support healthy fruit development.
ga: Hɛɛ, mango kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei kɛ Greater Accra, ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ be mli nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ hei nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to change my planting schedule if I move my farming operations from the South to northern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake midumɔ be lɛ kɛji mijie miŋmɔshi nitsumɔ lɛ kɛjɛ Ghana Anaigbɛ kɛtee Kooyigbɛ?

english: Farming conditions and rainfall patterns differ by region in Ghana, so your planting timing in the North must match its specific seasonal weather rather than the two-season climate of the coastal South.
ga: Okwaayeli shihilɛi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi yɛ srɔtoi yɛ Ghana kpokpai anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ be ni okɛduɔ nii yɛ Kooyigbɛ lɛ kɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baa lɛ akpã gbee. Nɔ ni fe bei enyɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ South Coast lɛ

english: What is a fire belt, and why do I need one on my farm in northern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji la bɛlɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná la tsɔne yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A fire belt is a cleared strip of land around your farm that stops bushfires from reaching your crops, which is critical during the intense dry weather in the northern regions.
ga: La linei ji hei ni agbele yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa koo mli la shɛɛɛ onibii ahe. Enɛ he hiaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ hei lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time of year to clear a fire belt around my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie la ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The right time to make a fire belt depends on your specific location and when the hot, dry weather sets in for your region, usually right before the risk of bushfires becomes high.
ga: Be ni sa ni okɛbaatswa la tsɔne lɛ damɔ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli dani koo mli la he oshara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What should I do when I notice the weather on my farm is getting very hot?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miyɔse akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miije shishi edɔ waa?

english: When temperatures rise high, you must closely observe your crops and soil to decide on protective measures like mulching, shade management, or building fire breaks to prevent heat damage.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni okpɛ oyiŋ yɛ gbɛi ni oootsɔ nɔ otsi hela naa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, hulutsoo be mlikwɛmɔ. aloo la he gbɛtsii nii ni afee koni hulutsoo akafite nii.

english: Why is it important for me to study the weather patterns in my specific district instead of following general advice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makase bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yaa nɔ ehaa yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ fe ŋaawoo ni akɛhaa mɛi fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weather conditions like heat and rainfall vary greatly depending on where your farm is located in Ghana, so understanding your local climate helps you make the right decisions for your crops at the right time.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ baasoro amɛhe waa yɛ he ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ onu kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpɛɔ yiŋ ni ja yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does sudden hot weather affect the way I should manage my land?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ saa bɔ ni mikwɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mihaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Very hot weather dries out crops and soil quickly, requiring you to inspect your farm daily and adjust your protective farm practices before moisture loss or fire threats harm your field.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi. ni otsake oŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni okɛbuɔ ohe lɛ mli. Dani ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi loo la he gbeyeishemɔ baawo oyale lɛ he gbeyei lɛ,.

english: Do fruit trees like mangoes need different weather conditions compared to seasonal grains?
ga: Ani tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango lɛ biɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi fe ŋmaa ni anáa yɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Yes, perennial fruit trees like mangoes rely on specific regional climate patterns and seasonal shifts, such as those in the coastal belt, to flower and bear fruit properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mango lɛ damɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ kpokpaa pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ kɛ be mli tsakemɔi, tamɔ yɛ ŋshɔnaa kpokpai anɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What precautions should I take on my farm during dry and hot spells in the northern region?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Kooyigbɛ?

english: During hot spells in the North, you should focus on protecting your field by clearing fire belts to prevent wildfire destruction and monitoring your soil to protect crops from intense heat.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama oyale lɛ hebuu nɔ kɛtsɔ la linei ni oootsi koni koo mli la akafite nii lɛ nɔ. Ni okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing that the crop needs fertilizer or rich compost.
