ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded farms during rainy periods. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in air and sunlight helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ amli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava stems keep growing tall with plenty of leaves without producing big roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛnáaa shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are crowded together, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of tubers. Proper plant spacing and balanced nutrients force the plant to feed its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai anɔ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aye amɛshishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are suffering from insect attacks or from a soil disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii etutua mi-tomato tsei lɛ loo hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ yɛ amɛmli?

english: Insects usually leave visible holes, bite marks, or sticky webs on leaves, whereas soil diseases cause the entire plant to wilt suddenly during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi shĩɔ bu ni anaa, ŋmeii okadii, loo ŋmeii ni kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in dry weather is a natural defense for the plant to reduce water loss, but it can also be caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ tsei ahe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my bean plants without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Bean flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture drops during flowering. Heat causes stress to the crop, making it shed blossoms to save energy for survival.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Dɔlɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around my young crop roots early instead of waiting until the weeds grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara lɛ,.

english: Young crops compete directly with weeds for water, sunlight, and food. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil nutrients they need to establish strong roots early on.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa mra.

english: What actually happens to my crop when I spray liquid nutrients on the leaves instead of putting fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Leaves have tiny microscopic pores that can absorb liquid nutrients directly, giving the crop a fast energy boost, especially when dry soil prevents roots from drinking up nutrients.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Ehaa tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ oya Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkanu niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need stakes to climb instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally reach upward for maximum sunlight to produce energy. Lifting vines off the ground on stakes keeps leaves dry, reduces fungal infections, and helps the plant grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa yitsei wuji

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted under big wild trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big trees block direct sunlight and steal water and soil nutrients with their deep roots. Plantains require full sunlight and moist, rich soil to grow fast and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni amɛkɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hulu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii lɛ he miihia plantains koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo jwɛi wuji.

english: Why do some crops take up to two years before I can harvest any food from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ afii enyɔ dani manyɛ makpa niyenii lɛ?

english: Long-term crops like cassava or plantain spend their first year building strong root systems and sturdy stems. This preparation phase allows them to store enough energy to produce heavy tubers or large fruit bunches in the second year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei loo plantain lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ dani ekɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa baa. Nɛkɛ hesaamɔ gbɛ nɛɛ haa amɛtoɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ yitsei ni tsii loo aduawai akui wuji yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crops growing tall green leaves, but I am not seeing any fruit or food on them yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi minako aduawai loo niyenii ko lolo?

english: Plants grow in stages. Leaves are like tiny food factories that collect sunlight to build up energy; once the plant has enough energy stored, it uses it to form flowers, pods, or subterranean tubers.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Baai lɛ tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ hei bibii. ni buaa hulu la naa koni ekɛfee hewalɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa Abaakɛfee fɔfɔi, ŋmeii, loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my crop is still healthy even if I don't see any harvestable yield after many months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo? Eyɛ mli akɛ minako nibii ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni eho lɛ eko moŋ.

english: Look for new shoot growth, firm stems, and bright leaves. As long as the plant is producing healthy foliage and showing no signs of pest damage, it is actively developing underground roots or preparing to flower.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii heei ni eda. Tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni kpɛɔ, kɛji tso lɛ woɔ tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite tso lɛ. Ekɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hu miitsu nii loo eesaa ehe koni ewo fɔfɔi.

english: If my farm gave me a very poor yield last year, can I still plant on that same soil this season?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli hu? Ani manyɛ madu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lolo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, but poor yields usually mean the soil has run out of plant food. Resting the land, adding animal manure, or planting legumes like cowpeas restores vital nutrients so your new crops can thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni ehiii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔ, okɛ kooloi ashishifã afata he. Aloo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni otsei heei lɛ anyɛ ashwere.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant the exact same crop on it every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: The same crop pulls the exact same nutrients out of the soil continuously, leaving it weak. It also gives pests and diseases that prefer that crop a permanent place to live and multiply.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ha egbɔjɔ Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tamɔ tsei lɛ hu naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why do my crops wither so fast when the rain stops for just a few weeks in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo ko pɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Young crops have shallow roots that can only reach topsoil moisture, which dries out quickly under the hot sun. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves traps moisture and protects young roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ he. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops seem to stop growing during the hazy Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ Harmattan be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need bright sunlight and warm air to make their food. The dust clouds and dry winds of the Harmattan block sunlight and cause the plant to conserve water by slowing down growth temporarily.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Harmattan sũ atatui kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa tsei buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛhaa amɛyaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my cassava plants from dying during long periods without rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmeii tsei lɛ akagboi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds some leaves during dry spells to save water while keeping its deep root alive. Planting early in the rainy season ensures the root goes deep enough to survive dry conditions.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant quick crops like maize together with slow crops like cassava on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. The quick crop yields early food for your family while the slow crop matures, making efficient use of your space without harming either plant if spaced correctly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Nibii ni aduɔ mra lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni oyeee tsei lɛ awui kɛji akɛ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did my maize sprout nicely at first but then turn yellow and stop growing after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishijee lɛ mi-ŋma lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shi no sɛɛ lɛ etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that heavy rains flooded the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my maize when the rains become unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ?

english: Instead of planting immediately after the very first rain, wait until the soil remains consistently moist for a few days, or follow rainfall predictions provided by local agricultural officers to avoid seeds drying up in the ground.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi. loo nyiɛmɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ etsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly even when rain fell just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses moisture fast when direct sunlight bakes the ground; adding organic matter like compost or leaving crop residues on the farm helps the soil hold water like a sponge for longer periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli tamɔ sponji be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects; planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and deep shade; clearing weeds and pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli kɛ tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates heavily, preventing the plant from setting fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, tso ɔ nyɛ we nɛ e wo yiblii saminya.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller yields every year even when I clear and burn the brush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Enɛ ji yɛ anɔkwale ni eji akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ ni mishã amɛ dani midu lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Burning farm brush destroys essential organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the soil, leaving the land poorer over time instead of fertile.
ga: Okwaafoi tsei ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy, deep root systems and are naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients rapidly, which is why clearing them early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. ni amɛtsake amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the maize seeds I harvested from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: How can I estimate how much maize I will harvest before the season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni makpa dani be lɛ aba naagbee lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can predict yield by counting the average number of healthy cobs on plants across a small sample area of your field and multiplying that by your total planted area.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ yibiiwoo kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he bibioo ko mli lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ enɛ abɔ he ni odu nii yɛ lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How can I keep my harvested yam tubers from rotting before I can sell them at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani mikɛ amɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yams rot quickly if exposed to heat and moisture; storing them off the ground in a well-ventilated, shaded yam barn protects them and preserves their market value.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe ni eha amɛ jara ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving some large trees or planting plantains beside them provides shade and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure to the soil helps restore their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, which smothers the roots. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to erect tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall sticks so their leaves can spread out in the air to catch sunlight, which the plant uses to make food for growing large tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground to avoid disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná niji kakadaji koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa baai lɛ hu jɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: How does mixing dead leaves and animal manure into my soil help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Dead leaves and manure decay into rich plant food that improves soil texture. This natural fertilizer holds water like a sponge, helping your crop roots get food and stay hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the young centers of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hide in the deep center whorl of young maize plants to feed on new leaves. Early detection and applying appropriate pesticides late in the day target them effectively.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛye baai heei. Tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anaa mra ni akɛtsuɔ nii Gbi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ kooloi anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting at the right time prevents stress and allows fruits to form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akahao haomɔ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni aduawai aba.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Removing most suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ tsei bibii lɛ, juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room to feed and grow thick, healthy stems.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the wet rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Black Pod rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions. Pruning dark leaves and branches allows sunlight and wind into the farm to dry off the pods and keep the fungus away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hei ni efɔ fe nine. Niji kɛ baai ni tsuɔ diŋ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can make big, full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee ŋmãa agboi.

english: What is making small holes in my young corn leaves and leaving powdery brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the young corn stalk to eat delicate leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments or neem oil protects your crop from severe loss.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nibii ni baafite waa lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from new leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents your plants from getting stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the ground around the plants with dry grass (mulch) helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (Mulch) awo tso lɛ he koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight and hot winds because their leaves burn easily. Leaving tall shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains around them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the air cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small suckers grow around my main plantain tree at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ he shikome lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain tree, they fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight, resulting in tiny fruit bunches. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one main tree and one or two young shoots ensures bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ hulu la he, ni no haa aduawai bibii feɔ akui. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome loo enyɔ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden stakes to climb, or can I let the vines crawl on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato dumɔ lɛ biɔ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo manyɛ mashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to feed the tubers growing underground. Letting vines trail on hot ground reduces tuber size and exposes leaves to soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfi bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ baa shi, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant groundnuts or beans between our main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as free fertilizer for nearby crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: How do weeds stop my crops from producing well even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ midumɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal the soil food, water, and sunlight your plants need to grow strong. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ejuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting since they grow under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. You can also dig carefully around one plant to check if the roots have grown thick before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome he hu koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start planting after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ odu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain of the season because it might be a false start followed by a long dry spell. Wait until you get two or three steady rains within a week so the soil becomes deep wet enough to sustain germinating seeds.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ekolɛ ebaafee amale shishijee ni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eye ebua dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What should I do to protect my crops if the rain stops for weeks right after I have planted?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii komɛi yɛ be mli ni midu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When an unexpected dry spell occurs after planting, apply mulch like dry grass or leaves around the bases of your young plants. This keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture, giving the roots enough dampness to survive until the rains return.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ni akpaaa gbɛ ba yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai, abɔle tsei bibii lɛ ashishi koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat and drought. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops precious water from evaporating out of the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Tsei haa amɛhiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and look weak after several days of continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots. Heavy rains also wash essential nutrients away from the root zone, causing the crop to lose its healthy green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe su kpakpa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: What is the best time of day to manually water my nursery crops when the rains are late?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ niji baafɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ nu beni nugbɔ lɛ eba sɛɛ?

english: Water your nursery early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the moisture to evaporate into the air before the plant roots have a chance to drink it.
ga: Okɛ nu awo o-nursery lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ mli nu lɛ babaoo atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛnu.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and the soil moist during dry months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How deep should I plant my seeds when the ground is dry on top?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Plant your seeds slightly deeper, around 3 to 5 centimeters down, to place them in the moist soil layer beneath the dried surface. If you plant too shallow, the hot sun will dry out the seed before it sprouts.
ga: Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ mli fioo, aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, koni okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shishi. Kɛji odu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass on my farm soil help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a protective blanket over the earth. It stops the sun from baking the soil directly, retains moisture longer, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi kɛ onibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Why is cassava able to survive long dry periods better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food in its thick underground roots and can drop its leaves during dry periods to save energy. Maize has shallower roots and thin leaves, making it far more vulnerable to drying out quickly.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai ashwie shi yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii. Eyɛ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaagbi ŋmãa oya.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry, hot Harmattan winds dry out the delicate stems and flowers of vegetable plants. Without enough air moisture, the plant drops its blossoms to save water, preventing fruits from forming.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa aduawai tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛhere nu. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Why do my crops keep getting smaller and weaker every year even though I plant on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibii ni migbɔjɔ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains essential nutrients from the soil over time. Without resting the land, rotating crops, or adding organic compost, the exhausted soil cannot give new crops the food they need to thrive.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ hejɔɔmɔ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ loo akɛ organic compost fata he Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei heei niyenii.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting a crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When harvested, they leave this vital nutrient behind in the soil, naturally fertilizing it for heavy-feeding plants like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I leave dry grass and crop leaves spread on top of my soil instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai ni egbɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, or mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, holds in water during hot days, and slowly rots into nutrient-rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds very close together so that I can fit more plants in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, root space, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in thin, weak stems and tiny ears of corn instead of large healthy harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shishifãi ahe he, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii baa. Mohu ɔ, o náa níhi fuu nɛ haa nɔ he wami.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are starving for nitrogen, a key building block for healthy leaf growth. It can also happen when roots are drowned in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji nɔ ko ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up rotting right inside the soil before I even dig them up for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po koni makpa lɛ?

english: Rotting underground is usually caused by water collecting around the roots due to poor drainage, combined with soil fungi or tiny pests like nematodes that enter bruised or wounded tubers during heavy rain seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa. shishifãi ni jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ Akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ nematodes ni boteɔ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ loo epila lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ fataa he.

english: What is causing small holes in the center whorls of my maize plants and making the leaves look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on young corn. Once hatched, the tiny caterpillars burrow into the center leaves where it is soft and moist, eating the crop from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ, he ni amɛyɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ye ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ

english: Why do my seeds often fail to grow if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season usually only wets the surface and leaves the soil hot underneath. If steady rains do not follow immediately, the intense heat and dry soil below will scorch and kill the newly germinated seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli dɔɔ pɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ eyaaa nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baashã ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my cassava crops so much during the first three months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava grows slowly in its first few months and cannot produce enough canopy shade to block weeds. During this early stage, weeds quickly steal the moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer that the cassava roots desperately need to grow.
ga: Cassava daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa baaa. Yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry Harmattan winds to save water. Planting shade trees around your farm and covering the base of the cocoa trees with dried leaves keeps the soil moist and protects the plant.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni okɛ baai ni egbi aha kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. Adding dry grass or straw around the base of your plants keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe and will rot if they sit in trapped water for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni ebaagbo kɛji eta nu ni ato mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, decomposed manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color and helps them grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni efite loo nitrogen nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara waa ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave behind rich soil that helps future crops grow better.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when they start producing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji amɛbɔi shweremɔ yɛ kui wuji amli pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot easily hold up heavy fruit bunches during high winds. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden fork keeps the plant standing upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds so frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ehe bahiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and food that your yam needs to grow. Keeping the mounds clean ensures that all the soil nutrients go directly into making your yam tubers bigger.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ oha ŋtayaa lɛ he tse lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni eha o-sweet potato tubers lɛ afee wuji.

english: Extreme sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil food stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to protect themselves. Regular watering and proper feeding keep flowers attached so tomatoes can grow.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ehe bahiaa ni amɛshi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ koni tomatoi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get full of tiny holes once the plants begin to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be tsei jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi?

english: Insects are naturally attracted to cowpea plants when flowers appear because the blossoms are rich in sweet food. Checking your plants regularly and using safe controls early prevents bugs from damaging the crop.
ga: Kɛ fɔfɔi je kpo lɛ, kooloi sumɔɔ tsina tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ niyenii ni ŋɔɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing small, wrinkled peppers instead of big smooth ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo pepper bibii ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper agbo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need a steady supply of water while fruits are forming. If the soil gets too dry, the plant cannot pump enough water into the peppers, leaving them small and shriveled.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa awo ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egboɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that cannot handle full daylight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees to protect them from heat stress until their roots and canopy fully establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baagbe naa.

english: What is causing small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central whorl of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells to conserve water. The plant goes dormant to protect its underground roots, and it will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Tsei yaa wɔɔ koni amɛbu amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Ni ebaakwɛ̃ baai heei kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain stem, they compete for nutrients and water. Pruning extra suckers and leaving only one strong daughter sucker ensures the main plant gets enough energy to yield large bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he ni ashi nine bibioo kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my farmland yield a good harvest the first year but produce weak crops if I plant maize on it again the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi kɛji midu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ wo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a large amount of soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil; rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Titri lɛ nitrogen, ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture and shade. Pruning dense branches to let in sunlight and air helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers but dropping them without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi no sɛɛ lɛ egbeeɔ shi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flower drop often happens due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages the plant to grow leaves instead of holding onto its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ baai moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Can I plant cassava directly under my mature cocoa trees, or will it harm the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaaye kookoo awui loo ebaayeee lɛ awui?

english: Cassava has aggressive roots that compete heavily for water and nutrients, and mature cocoa needs open space beneath its canopy. It is better to plant cassava at the field borders rather than under established cocoa.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Ni kookoo ni eda lɛ he miihia he ko ni agbele yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi. Kasava ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ ko naa lɛ hi fe kookoo ni aaadu yɛ he ni gbɛ yɔɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put stakes for my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves toward sunlight so the plant can make food efficiently to grow larger tubers, while keeping foliage off wet soil reduces fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ bulbs wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough water after the first rain to safely plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Wait until the rain leaves moisture at least palm-deep in the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if a dry stretch follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashi kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tso tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because it burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Big trees or plantains provide living shade that cools the ground and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ eshãa amɛbaai lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Kookoo dumɔwui bibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the middle outward when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing leaves. This happens when the soil is worn out from continuous planting or when heavy rains wash the nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive and healthy. When water sits in the field for too long, the soil gets waterlogged, suffocating the roots so they drown and begin to decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, sũ lɛ mli woɔ nu, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebote nu lɛ mli ni ebɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to use wooden sticks to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to catch energy and send food down to grow big tubers. Raising the vines on stakes also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and crawling insect damage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii amaje shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, drought, or sudden hot winds. To save water and energy, the plant drops its flowers instead of spending resources trying to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ trukaa hao amɛ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling tightly upward into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up either to protect themselves from losing water in hot, dry weather or because tiny insects like whiteflies have bitten them and passed on a leaf curl sickness that stunts the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ ŋmɔɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛ leaf curl hela ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ haa amɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the bunch of plantains gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛmiitsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out near the surface of the soil. When the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, it makes the plant top-heavy, causing wind or wet, soft soil to pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ebaaha ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a plant family that traps nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into plant food inside small nodules on their roots. When the cowpea plant dies and decays, that nitrogen stays in the ground to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsina tsei gboi ni amɛfite lɛ, Nakai nitrogen lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why can swamp rice grow directly in standing water while my corn dies if it stays in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ gboɔ kɛji ehi nu mli lɛ?

english: Swamp rice has special hollow tubes inside its stems and roots that pump air down from above the water line to its roots. Corn plants do not have these internal air pipes, so their roots drown without oxygen when submerged.
ga: Swamp rice yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni mli ewo muji yɛ etso lɛ mli kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ amɛmli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ mli kɛ́ amɛbote nu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my garden eggs look droopy and dead in the hot afternoon but look fresh and standing again in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani oookwɛ ehee ni odamɔ shi ekoŋŋ leebi maŋkpa?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it out of the dry soil, causing them to wilt to conserve moisture. During the cool night, the roots catch up on drinking water, plumping the stems back up by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baakpɛtɛ nu ni anuɔ lɛ he ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ niji heei leebi.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip, the crop is lacking nitrogen. Maize moves whatever nitrogen it has from old bottom leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ naagbee lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my maize produce smaller yields when I plant it on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients faster than the soil can replenish them, while allowing pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to build up in the land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaya nɔ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing huge green leaves but failing to produce seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on growing tall leafy stems instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when we get heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot from soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant hold onto water during extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni hulu la ni shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before producing any small fruits during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When tomato plants experience heat stress and drought, they drop their flowers to save water and energy for basic survival rather than fruit growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ, Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ aduawai

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees protect young cocoa from sunburn, keep humidity high, and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and collapse around the stem before the fruit bunch fully grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ he dani ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: This is a sign of root damage caused by pests like nematodes or wilt disease, which block the plant from drinking water and carrying nutrients up the main stem.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ nematodes loo wilt lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ anu nu ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do crops growing close to muddy mining water or washed-out runoff stay small and develop burnt leaf edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni hoɔ ni ehoɔ lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛshãa amɛbaai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Muddy sediment and chemicals in polluted runoff block soil oxygen and poison crop roots, preventing them from taking up clean water and essential food.
ga: Muji ni mli ewo muji kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni efiteɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnu nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops show twisted leaves after I spray weed killer on a windy day near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ baa lɛ etsake beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie shi yɛ gbi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fine droplets of chemical weed killers can float through the air on wind currents and land on nearby crop leaves, causing damage even if you did not spray them directly.
ga: Tsofa bibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ nɔ ni amɛyagbee tsei ahe baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieee nɔ tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that create living shade and keep soil moist, helping cocoa seedlings survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants produce green leaves and grow strong, so yellowing means the maize needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa, no hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that burrows into the center whorl of maize plants. They feed on tender leaves, which weakens the plant and severely reduces yield if not treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni boteɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi waa kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots enough room to expand into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. When soil moisture changes drastically or temperatures spike, the plant sheds blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield in their first generation. If you harvest and replant those seeds, the second-generation crops lose their vigor, growing unevenly and producing much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ hewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa

english: Why do my stored cowpeas end up full of small holes and dusty powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by tiny insects called cowpea weevils that lay eggs on the seeds. The larvae burrow inside and eat the grain, which can be prevented by thoroughly drying the beans and storing them in airtight containers.
ga: Kooloi bibii kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ cowpea moth lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Lalabii lɛ shwieɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to clear my weed foliage without burning it off with fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaagbe jwɛi ni la bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning farm weeds destroys organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms. Leaving cleared plants to rot or using them as mulch protects the soil from heat, holds water, and returns valuable nutrients to the earth.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi loo akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does Striga weed keep stunt-growing my sorghum even when I keep weeding it out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ edaa yɛ mi-sorghum lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches underground to crop roots before it even grows above the surface. By the time you see its purple flowers and pull it out, it has already stolen water and nutrients directly from the crop's root system.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyaa tsei ashishifãi anɔ dani enyɛɔ edaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Beni onaa fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ojieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and turn dry during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by fungal diseases like blight, which thrive in cool, damp weather. Rain splashes fungus spores from the soil onto lower leaves, where moisture allows the disease to infect and dry out the foliage.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli kɛ enɛ baa. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ fɛ̃i nɛɛ kɛ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ baa, ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up and turning yellow during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize gets too hot, its leaves curl to hold onto water and protect itself from drying out. If leaves turn yellow, it means heat stress is making it hard for the plant to take up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the middle of the day even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Extreme heat makes leaves lose moisture faster than roots can pull up water. Giving crops proper spacing so air flows between them helps cool the plants down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu. Tsɔsemɔ tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ, ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔɔ.

english: Why do my young citrus trees drop their flowers before turning into fruit in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fruit trees drop flowers when they get overheated or water-stressed to save energy and survive. Providing afternoon shade or mulching around the roots helps cool the soil.
ga: Yibii tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ loo nu mli hewalɛ ni fe nine mli koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ shwane mli hulutsoo be loo sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: What happens to my soil if I grow cassava on the same land every single year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Overworking the land without letting it rest exhausts the nutrients in the soil, leading to tired land that produces smaller tubers each season.
ga: Kɛ́ otsu amɛ nii fe nine ni ohaaa amɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Enɛ haa hei ni egbi ni woɔ bulbs bibii yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How does placing dry leaves around the base of my plantain suckers help them grow better?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te dumɔwui ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves creates mulch, which keeps the soil cool, traps moisture, and stops the sun from overheating the root system.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ adɔ fe nine kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out much smaller this harvest than last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ miifee nɔ ni baa shi kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Yams need rich soil to build large roots. If the soil is overworked without adding manure or crop rotation, the plant lacks the energy needed to form big tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ efee shishifãi wuji. Kɛji akɛ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii fe nine ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Why did the tips of my cocoa leaves turn brown after I sprayed chemical fertilizer on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using fertilizer that is not suited for your crop or mixing it too strong acts like bad fuel, burning the leaves and stressing the plant instead of helping it.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaaa onibii lɛ tsu nii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa tsɔ futu mli lɛ, ebaatsu nakai nɔŋŋ. Fuel ni ehiii, baai shãa ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ.

english: Can I mix cheap market chemicals together to spray my cowpea farm when pests attack?
ga: Ani manyɛ afutu tsofai ni jara waaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ekomɛi koni mikɛshwie mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ batutua mi?

english: Mixing unapproved or incorrect chemicals can damage your crops. Always use standard products recommended specifically for cowpeas to avoid harming plant leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni ejaaa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee kɛha tsina ŋmei lɛ atsu nii koni akaye tso lɛ baai lɛ awui.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stay small and fail to form tight heads in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛfeee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cabbage prefers cooler conditions. High heat causes the plant to mature too early without forming tight heads unless provided with adequate shade and airflow.
ga: Cabbage sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni ekɛ bulb lɛ ebɔko amɛhe. Ja hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my vegetable beds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them allows air to circulate around your vegetables, keeping them healthy and cool.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ afɔ aduawai ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔleɔ amɛhe, ni ehaa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛhe jɔɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time of year my mangoes will be ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ni mango baafee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: In Ghana, mangoes generally have two harvest periods: the major season between May and July, and a minor season from December to January, depending on your region's rainfall patterns.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, mango lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei enyɔ: be titri ni akɛkpaa lɛ ji kɛjɛ May kɛyashi July. kɛ be bibioo ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ December kɛyashi January. Edamɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that a mango on my tree is ripe and ready to pick without cutting it open?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ mango ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni afolɔ?

english: Look at the top of the fruit near the stem; a ripe mango fills out and becomes rounded at the shoulders. The skin usually shifts from dark green to a lighter yellow or orange shade, and it gives off a sweet aroma.
ga: Kwɛmɔ aduawai lɛ yiteŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ eyi obɔ ni eyɛ kokroo yɛ etsitsi nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hewolo lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu. ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ

english: If I pick a green, hard mango from my tree, will it still turn soft and sweet in my house?
ga: Kɛ okɛ mango ni mli wa ni ji eŋɔli ba shia lɛ, ani ebaaŋɔɔ lolo?
