english: If the mango reached full size on the tree before picking, it will ripen fine at room temperature. But if you harvest it too early while it is still immature, it will stay sour, shrink, or spoil instead of ripening.
ga: Kɛji akɛ mango ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he dani ajieɔ Mango lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shĩa mli latsaa mli. Shi kɛji okpa lɛ mra tsɔ, yɛ be mli ni eshɛko lolo lɛ, Ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo, ebaagbɔjɔ, loo ebaafite yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaahoo lɛ.

english: What causes black, sunken spots on my mango fruits while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi mangoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is a common fungal disease called Anthracnose. It spreads during wet weather and attacks the skin of the fruit, causing dark spots that expand and rot the mango as it ripens.
ga: Enɛ ji hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose. Egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ, ni etutuaa aduawai ahewolo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii diji ni mli lɛɛɔ ni egboɔ beni mango lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my mango tree turning black as if someone spread charcoal dust on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango baai lɛ efee ediŋŋ tamɔ mɔ ko kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ ewo nɔ lɛ?

english: This black coating is called sooty mold. It is a fungus that grows on the sticky liquid left behind by small sap-sucking insects like mealybugs; getting rid of the insects will clear up the black leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tsɔne diŋ nɛɛ akɛ rasutti. Eji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni mli tse nɔ. Baai ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs lɛ shĩɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ajie kooloi bibii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee diŋŋ.

english: Why do all the flowers fall off my mango tree before any fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers usually fall off because of fungal diseases like powdery mildew during damp weather, or because the tree does not have enough water and nutrients to support fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew hewɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my small green mangoes dropping off the tree long before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Trees shed excess fruit when they suffer from water shortages, lack nutrients in the soil, or when tiny fruit fly pests attack the small fruits early on.
ga: Tsei baawo yibii ni fa fe nine kɛ́ amɛna nu ni faaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni aduawai bibii shwieɔ shi Tutuaa aduawai bibii mra.

english: Why should I cut off some of the branches inside my mango tree canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts. This lowers moisture levels that spread plant diseases and helps the tree put energy into growing larger fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli tseɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Does heavy rainfall while my tree is blooming harm my crop?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ lɛ náa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Yes, heavy rain washes away pollen needed for fruit growth and creates a wet environment that encourages fungal diseases to infect and rot the flowers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ kɛyaa. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What is the best way to store my freshly harvested mangoes so they do not rot before I sell them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ mango ni ajie ehee lɛ toɔ? Ani oookwɛ koni ekafite dani ohɔ̃ɔ?

english: Keep harvested mangoes in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded area using wooden or plastic crates. Do not pile them too high, and keep them out of direct sunlight to stop them from over-ripening and rotting.
ga: Okɛ mango ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo kɛtsɔ tso loo plastic adekai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kaawo nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ tsɔ. ni okɛ ohe akabɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni akahoo fe nine ni akafite.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves produce green food and grow strong.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding lime or compost helps prevent the fruits from spoiling.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni akɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ afite.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense sun heat, dry soil, or pest damage. Providing light shade and regular watering during hot spells helps the plant keep its flowers to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao amɛ. ni haa hulutsoo fioo Ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves looking like they were chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai kɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni atsɔ mli nyɔɔŋ kome mli awo bu bibii amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths. Checking plants early and spraying with neem water or recommended insecticides protects the growing center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: How should I position cassava stem cuttings in the soil when I plant them?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems should be planted slanting at a 45-degree angle or buried horizontally, ensuring the leaf buds point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down prevents them from sprouting roots and leaves properly.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ 45-degree angle loo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ehaaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I plow my farm ridges across a sloped hill instead of straight down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gɔji ni etse amɛhe lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mafo gɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Plowing across the hill creates ridges that act as small dams. This stops heavy rains from washing away your fertile topsoil, seeds, and fertilizer down the slope.
ga: Gɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋshɔkei ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei bibii baa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ, dumɔwui, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil through their roots. This restores soil nutrients naturally for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I use animal manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsu nii?

english: Both help crops, but animal manure improves the soil's structure and water-holding ability over time, while chemical fertilizer provides quick food to plants. Combining compost or manure with small amounts of chemical fertilizer yields the best results.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures all available plant food goes into growing your crops rather than feeding unwanted plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni akɛ tsei niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛdu onibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei ni he ehiaaa amɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani abele lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's life provides the food it needs to stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ tso lɛ shishijee shihilɛ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can draw it up. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money because the crop cannot feed on dry fertilizer.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off, keeping the tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ efooo Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ mli babaoo. ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly together and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Curling tomato leaves are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the plant. Removing affected plants early and keeping flies away prevents the disease from spreading to the rest of your garden.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛ ohe koni helai akagbɛ ashwã obɔɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers right beside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa shoots have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around the base of my pepper plants when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Pepper tso lɛ shishitoo beni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young pepper crops. Clearing them gives your peppers full access to the natural resources they need to grow strong branches.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha o-peppers lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight so the plant can make enough energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also lifts the foliage off damp soil to prevent leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni baa lɛ akafite.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem compete with the mother tree for food and water, making the fruit bunch small. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree bears heavy, marketable fruit.
ga: ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Dumɔwui babaoo ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ baabɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Ha aduawai akuu lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii ni tsii ni abaanyɛ ahé.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant without forming any peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee pepper ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms during extreme heat or drought to conserve water and protect themselves. Covering the ground with dry grass mulch keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ loo nu egbiɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I avoid dropping three or four maize seeds in a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmãa bu kome mli lɛ he?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the stalks to fight each other for root space and soil food. Planting one or two seeds per hill with proper distance ensures every stalk grows thick and yields full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awuu koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ gɔŋ fɛɛ gɔŋ nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the tip and moving inward, usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth and increases plant energy.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa ni amɛyaa mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adara ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ ahewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant retain flowers and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do small insects attack my harvested maize grains inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils grow quickly when grain is bagged while still holding moisture. Drying your maize fully in the sun until it is hard before bagging prevents insect damage during storage.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa dani awo lɛ kotoku mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi fiteɔ nii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I plant the sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots compete underground for space, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, small tubers instead of large ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmei wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my tomato field make the tomatoes grow smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ tomato ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tomato lɛ feɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, light, and water directly from your tomato roots. Removing weeds regularly ensures all available nutrients go into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tomato shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves scorch and dry up after I put strong chemical fertilizer near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ ewo amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer too close to plant stems draws moisture out of the roots, burning the plant. Placing fertilizer a short distance from the stem in proper doses keeps plants safe.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni eshãa tsei lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ shishi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do caterpillars destroy the leaves of my young maize faster during dry sunny periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm thrive and reproduce rapidly in hot, dry conditions when natural predators are fewer. Checking your fields early in the morning helps catch and control them before severe damage happens.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ ji be ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ faaa kwraa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ ni oye nɔ dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil still feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Hot sun causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant wilts to conserve moisture and will recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni amɛbaatsa amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of the seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are too old, stored in hot damp places, or damaged by pests before planting. Using fresh, certified seeds ensures high germination rates.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. Kɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite dani adu Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How do I know if my maize seeds are good enough to sprout properly after I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Good maize seeds swell with soil moisture and sprout shoots within 3 to 5 days. You can test seed viability beforehand by placing ten seeds on wet cloth; if eight or more sprout after a few days, your seed lot is healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Abele dumɔwui kpakpai shwereɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli. Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi aha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui nyɔŋma ni okɛaawo mama ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, ekpaa loo nɔ ni fe nakai baakwɛ̃. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to become steady before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shi dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Planting after the very first light rain can be risky because early dry spells can scorch newly sprouted seeds. Waiting for consistent rain ensures stable soil moisture so your crops establish strong root systems from the beginning.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Osharai baanyɛ aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa mra lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ maa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛjɛɔ shishijee tɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do some farmers in my community plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava maximizes land use and protects your soil. Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, leaving open space and soil nutrients for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: What will happen to my pepper plants if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting peppers too close forces them to compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, producing thin stems and few fruits. Proper spacing lets air flow between plants, which keeps leaves dry and reduces fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Young tomato plants have tender, shallow roots that cannot drink water fast enough during peak heat. Spreading dried grass or leaves as mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and retains water longer.
ga: Tomato tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines climb to lift their leaves high into the sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa bulbs wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why does my plantain plant sprout so many small suckers around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle eshishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants multiply naturally by producing suckers around the parent stem. You should prune away extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones so the main plant keeps enough energy to bear large fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. trunk of parents Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ato hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii akui wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and quickly steal water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong leaves and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or that the roots are waterlogged. Adding organic compost or proper fertilizers helps restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim off the lowest leaves of my tomato plants near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves keeps soil fungi from splashing onto the foliage when it rains. It also encourages the plant to direct its growing energy into producing healthier flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Ewoɔ tsei hu hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when I plant directly without properly clearing and loosening the soil first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛshwieee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Loosening and preparing the soil removes weed competition and breaks up hard earth, allowing young plant roots to spread easily, breath, and absorb water and soil nutrients efficiently from the start.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni asaa he lɛ baajie jwɛi akaŋshii kɛya ni ebaagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo, amɛmuɔ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shishijee.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are growing at the normal speed during their first few months in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida oya bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: In the first month, healthy maize focuses on developing roots and green leaves; by the second and third months, it should rapidly grow tall and start flowering. Slow height growth or pale colors usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛ 3 lɛ, tsei lɛ daraa oya ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up instead of staying green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or damage from sap-sucking pests like whiteflies; applying compost or appropriate fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nɔ ni ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between using chemical fertilizer and using animal manure on my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers provide an immediate food boost to plants for fast growth, while animal manure improves the soil's structure and ability to hold water over a longer period. Using both gives the best long-term yield.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii fataa tsei ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha tsei lɛ ada oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná sɛɛnamɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant many seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduawai bibii loo ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young crop plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when it rained a couple of days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots that cannot reach deeper water stored in the soil. Covering the ground around the stems with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the topsoil cool and wet for longer.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ ni ebua ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually harm the food growing under or above the ground?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink the water and eat the fertilizer meant for your crops, causing your crops to starve and produce poor harvests.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi tsei ni nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni owoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer bags of crop each year even when I do the exact same hard work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ faaa daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa tamɔ tsutsu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do pests attack my crops more heavily during dry spells than during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry conditions weaken plants due to water stress, making them less able to defend themselves, while high heat helps many insect populations multiply much faster.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Ehaa onyɛɛɛ obu ohe he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa yeɔ ebuaa kooloi babaoo ni amɛyi fa oya.

english: Why do some of the seeds I save from my previous harvest fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their vitality if stored in warm or damp conditions, or if they were attacked by tiny insects. Certified fresh seeds stored in cool, dry places have much higher sprout rates.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tutua amɛ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why are traders in my local market refusing to buy my tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ jarayelɔi lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahe mi-tomato lɛ?

english: Local buyers often reject crops that are low quality, soft, or filled with excess water, preferring firmer produce that stays fresh longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ni akɛ nu woɔ mli fe nine. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ ni ooohala akɛ okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tomato traders travel to Burkina Faso or Côte d'Ivoire to buy produce instead of buying from local farmers like me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato jarayelɔi yaa Burkina Faso loo Côte d’Ivoire koni amɛyahe nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaahe kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi tamɔ mi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Traders buy from neighboring countries because the crops grown there often have better firmness, lower water content, and higher market quality compared to over-watered local produce.
ga: Jarayelɔi heɔ nii kɛjɛɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ fɔɔ shifimɔ kpakpa. Nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Ni jarayeli mli nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ kwɔ fe maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii tsɔ lɛ.

english: How can I improve the quality of my crops so that local markets will accept them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ koni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi lɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ?

english: You can improve crop quality by managing your watering properly; avoiding over-watering produces firmer crops with lower water content that market buyers prefer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaha tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu fioo ni jarayelɔi heɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes feel soft and watery inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni nu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you give your crop too much water, the fruit absorbs excess fluid, making it watery, soft, and poor in texture.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu babaoo ha onibii lɛ Yibii lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ehaa efeɔ nu, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does giving my plants too much water affect the final crop?
ga: Te nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ fe nine lɛ saa naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Over-watering forces the crop to store excess water inside the fruit, which lowers its overall quality and reduces its shelf life.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha tso lɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot faster than the ones brought in from neighboring countries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya fe tomato ni akɛjɛɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops grown with excess water contain too much internal fluid, causing them to spoil quickly, while crops grown with controlled watering stay firm and fresh much longer.
ga: Tsei ni akɛ nu babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fitemɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ nu ni akudɔɔ lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbaafee ehee be babaoo.

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually cause them to get sick?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛná hela diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, giving crops too much water stresses their roots and creates damp conditions that easily lead to plant diseases and viral infections.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ tsei ahe helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ baa oya.

english: Why are viral diseases spreading so easily among my tomato crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mitato tsei lɛ anɔ oya lɛ?

english: Crop viruses are very common when fields are over-watered, as excess moisture weakens the plants and allows infections to take root quickly.
ga: Tsei ahe helai fɔɔ baa waa kɛ́ nu ho ŋmɔji amli fe nine. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa hela lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Is it possible to damage my crops by watering them too frequently?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, frequent over-watering fills the fruits with excess water and creates an unhealthy environment that brings on destructive plant viruses.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni oooha aduawai lɛ shii abɔ lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ afee nu tsɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni esaaa ni fɔɔ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plants look unhealthy even though I make sure to give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ tamɔɔɔ nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving 'plenty' of water can actually hurt your plants; over-watering weakens crop health and makes them vulnerable to common viral diseases.
ga: Nu ‘bɔ’ ni oooha lɛ baanyɛ aye otsei lɛ awui. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ fe nine lɛ haa amɛhewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni afɔɔ namɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water or not enough water during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops don't get enough water, their leaves roll up, wilt, or feel dry. When they get too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow and the roots start rotting because waterlogged soil starves them of air.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, baai lɛ baa shwie shi, amɛ baa shwie shi, loo amɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛ egbi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ ejaakɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: Is it better to plant cassava stems upright in the ground or slant them at an angle?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei ni ja loo yɛ koŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant (around 45 degrees) helps roots spread out better and grow deeper, making it easier for the plant to absorb nutrients and produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni efee bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my cabbage leaves, and how can I protect them safely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ kaaba baa nɔ lɛ, ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles eating the crop. You can pick them off by hand in the morning, spray neem leaf extract, or use safe insecticides approved by agricultural extension officers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okɛ onine aŋɔ amɛ leebi. Spray neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii amli oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil evenly watered and adding organic compost helps prevent it.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same soil nutrients and allows specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni amɛshwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the soil for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves toward the sun so they can manufacture food to grow large underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off wet ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aná su ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil at the base of the stem begins to crack from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my crop seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves plants tall, weak, and thin, resulting in much smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why did my maize crops produce very small cobs and dry up early during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize requires steady moisture, especially during the flowering and grain-filling stages. When dry spells hit at these critical times, the plant prioritizes its own survival over crop production, resulting in small cobs or empty grains.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli. Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa yɛ be ni he hiaa waa mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yeɔ hiɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: How can I estimate how much corn my farm will produce before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni miŋmɔ lɛ baawo lɛ he akɔntaa dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can predict harvest size by using proper plant spacing and calculating average plant count, cobs per plant, and kernel rows per cob mid-season. Using certified seeds makes growth uniform, making these yield estimates much more accurate.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ bɔ ni kpamɔ lɛ dalɛ ji kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛ tsei lɛ ayibɔ ni ji mlijaa mlijaa, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso kome mli kɛ dumɔwui ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛdaraa daa. Ha nifeemɔ he akɔntaabuu lɛ afee nɔ ni ja jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my young corn leaves to turn yellow and stop growing before cobs appear?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ dani ŋmei lɛ jeɔ kpo?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or nutrient leaching caused by heavy rainfall. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the plant's growth restores its green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do market prices for corn drop so low immediately after the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Prices fall during harvest because most farmers sell their produce at the exact same time, creating a huge supply in the market. As supply decreases months later, prices go back up.
ga: Jara baa shi yɛ kpamɔ be mli ejaakɛ okwaafoi babaoo hɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii babaoo baa jara nɔ. Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ ba shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I lock in a fixed price for my harvest before I even start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo jara pɔtɛɛ ko kɛha mikpamɔ lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: You can join a local farmers' cooperative or enter into a contract farming agreement with buyers. These arrangements fix a guaranteed price and market for your crop prior to planting, protecting you from market price crashes.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyafata maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko he loo okɛ mɔ ko ni heɔ nii lɛ afee okwaayeli he kpaŋmɔ. Gbɛjianɔtoi nɛɛ haa jara kɛ jara ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha onibii lɛ dani oduɔ. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jarayeli jara ni baa shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested corn grains turn into dust while stored in my shed after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ sũ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-shĩa lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils eat through harvested corn if the moisture level is too high. Drying your maize thoroughly and storing it in airtight, hermetic bags suffocates pests without needing harsh chemicals.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii baaye ŋmaa ni akpa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa tsɔ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: What pest is eating big holes in my corn leaves, and how does it affect my final harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela yeɔ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te ebaasa minaagbee nikpamɔ lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, an invasive caterpillar that destroys the leaf canopy. Without healthy leaves, the plant cannot feed itself, drastically reducing the number and size of ears produced.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ. Kɛji baai ni mli wa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, toi ni afee lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What secondary crop can I plant with my maize so I still harvest something if the rain fails?
ga: Mɛɛ saatso manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa akwɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni manyɛ makpa kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Intercropping maize with drought-tolerant legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts provides a safety net. Legumes survive better in low rainfall and fix nitrogen into the soil, which helps feed the neighboring maize.
ga: Abele ni akɛ ŋmãa ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dumɔ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji shweshweeshwe shihilɛ. Legumes hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ, ni amɛsaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii aha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves over my farm soil help my plants during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with organic material, called mulching, acts like a shield against the sun. It traps moisture in the ground, lowers soil temperature, and keeps crop roots hydrated much longer between rainfalls.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why should I buy packaged hybrid seeds instead of saving seeds from my last corn harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength and yield potential with every generation, leading to uneven growth and lower yields. Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance, uniform cob sizes, and better disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo nyɛmɔ kɛ yinɔ fɛɛ yinɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Akwɛɔ Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Cob lɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ

english: How long can I keep my harvested maize before it starts to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: When properly dried and stored in a cool, dry place or in airtight bags, maize can stay good for 6 to 12 months without spoiling or being damaged by pests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi loo yɛ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Abɛi baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteee loo efiteee.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil within just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled from the ground, it rapidly reacts with air and begins to break down internally. Unlike yams or grains, cassava must be eaten, processed, or properly preserved within 2 to 3 days of harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baatsu nii oya ni ebɔi fitemɔ yɛ emli. Esa akɛ aye ŋmãa, atsu he nii loo akɛto jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmaa he.

english: What actually causes my stored yams to soften and rot inside the room?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ fee blɛoo diɛŋtsɛ ni egbo yɛ tsu lɛ mli?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi and bacteria entering through small cuts or bruises made during harvest. High room temperatures and poor airflow make these micro-organisms grow faster and decay the yam.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni fiteɔ lɛ baa ji ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii anɔ. aloo ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmaa lɛ Tsu mli latsaa ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ daraa oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my stored grains go bad faster here near the coast than in drier regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa fe hei ni egbi lɛ?

english: Coastal areas in Ghana have very high humidity in the air. This damp air sinks into stored crops, creating the wet environment that mold and insects need to destroy your food.
ga: Ŋshɔnaa hei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ boteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii afite oniyenii lɛ baa.

english: Is it better to store my crop yield inside my house or outside under a shade?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baato shia loo kpo nɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi?

english: Storing inside protects crops from unexpected rain and animals, but the room must have good airflow. Leaving crops outside, even under shade, exposes them to morning dew and damp soil that speed up rotting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ kɛ kooloi ahe. Shi esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tsu lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi po Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa leebi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni haa amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why is it important for air to move freely through my crop storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ miŋmɔshi nibii atoohe lɛ mli oya lɛ?

english: Harvested crops 'breathe' and generate heat and moisture. Good airflow carries this trapped heat and dampness away so mold cannot grow on your produce.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ ‘muɔ’ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ shwereee yɛ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I avoid leaving my harvested crops sitting at the edge of my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ he ni mahã ehi ŋmɔ lɛ naa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Leaving crops on the edge of the field exposes them directly to soil dampness, sudden rain, and wild animals. This damages the skin of the crop and invites pests before you even bring them home.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ ko naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa, kɛ koo mli kooloi baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewolo ni efɔ̃ɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ nine dani okɛ amɛ po baa shia.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn is dry enough to store safely for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can test corn by pressing your fingernail into a grain; if it leaves no dent, or if the grain makes a sharp cracking sound when you bite it, it is dry enough for long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onineshi ni ooonyɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii komɛi bɛ mli Aloo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ gbee ni naa wa waa kɛji akɛ amɛye amɛhe lɛ, no lɛ amɛgbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to stack my sacks of food by the roadside while waiting for transport?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooshi niyenii kotokui yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he beni omɛɛɔ tsɔne lɛ?

english: If you place bags directly on the damp ground by the road, moisture will soak into the bottom sacks and spoil the crop. Always rest your bags on wooden planks or tarpaulins to keep them dry.
ga: Kɛ okɛ kotoku lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Fɛ̃i baabote kotoku lɛ shishi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ kotoku lɛ awo tso loo tarpaulin nɔ koni ekagbi.

english: How does heavy rainfall close to harvest time affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain right before harvest fills the crops with extra water. This makes grains sprout on the stalk or rots tubers in the soil, drastically shortening how long they will last after you harvest them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ haa nu ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei loo bulbs anɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa be ni dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ beni okpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning yellow and staying small instead of growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing young plants usually lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or are being choked by weeds. Adding a small amount of nitrogen-rich fertilizer early on gives young crops the strength to grow deep roots and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo jwɛi haa amɛhe feɔ shoo. Nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fioo ni akɛbaafata he mra. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa akwɛ̃.

english: Moving seedlings causes transplant shock because their delicate roots get damaged or dry out in the bright sun. Planting late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps seedlings settle smoothly into their new soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ efite loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my cassava crops even when I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ? He ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients before young crops like cassava can establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Dani tsei bibii tamɔ ŋmei baaná shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ,.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges for pollination, and the tree requires sufficient water and soil nutrients to mature those flowers into pods; if the tree is stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛfeɔ pollination. Ni tsei he miihia nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni nakai fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji tso lɛ miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller yam tubers after planting on the same piece of land for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops extract nutrients from the soil every season. Continuous farming without adding organic manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest exhausts the soil nutrients needed to grow heavy tubers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli, loo aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulbs ni tsii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat combined with low soil moisture causes heat stress, forcing pepper plants to drop leaves to conserve water. Adding mulch around the plant base keeps the root zone cool and moist.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo fataa he lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees roll up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up to reduce their surface area and prevent water from evaporating into the hot air. Browning occurs when the roots cannot find enough water in the dry ground to keep the large leaves alive.
ga: Akɛ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Browning baa kɛji shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ koni ekɛkwɛ baai wuji anɔ.

english: Why should I leave space between my tomato plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes too close causes them to compete for sunlight and air, creating a humid environment where fungal diseases can easily spread from leaf to leaf.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ baa kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are worms eating holes in my maize leaves before the corn ears even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele baa lɛ mli dani toi lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm prefer soft, young leaves because they are easy to feed on. Inspecting the crops early allows you to apply safe pest control before the growing center of the plant is destroyed.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ sumɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ejaakɛ amɛyemɔ waaa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ shweshweeshwe dani tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my yam leaves developing dark spots and drying up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by fungal diseases like anthracnose, which thrive and spread when heavy rains leave standing moisture on the leaves for long periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ahe tsɔi ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so it gets a good price at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni aná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too early gives you small, watery roots, while leaving it too long in the soil turns the roots woody, which buyers will reject.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi ohe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ tsei, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in storage before I can take them to the market to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ fite yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani mikɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when bruised during harvest or stored in hot, unventilated places. Digging tubers out gently without scratching the skin and storing them in a cool, raised, shaded yam barn keeps them fresh for months until market prices improve.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Okɛ yitso lɛ atsu nii blɛoo. ni ekɛ ehewolo lɛ shwieee nɔ ni ekɛtoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni awo nɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni ehi shi ehee nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi jara nɔ jara baaya hiɛ.

english: What makes improved seed varieties different from the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, withstand dry spells, and produce much higher yields per acre. While saved seeds are free, improved seeds grow uniformly and yield the consistent produce required by institutional buyers like schools.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe ehiaaa moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni nitsumɔhei ni heɔ nii tamɔ skul lɛ biɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why is it bad to plant my maize very close together if I want a bigger yield from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo kɛji miitao yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed properly, leading to bigger cobs and better quality crops instead of many weak, barren stalks.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbi yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which plants need to build strong green leaves. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life restores their strength and boosts ear production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha toi lɛ afee babaoo.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches your soil to feed your maize crop while giving you an extra food crop to sell.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛye ebua o-ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ ehaa bo niyenii tsei krɛdɛɛi ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are holes appearing in my tomato fruits before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Holes in tomatoes are caused by fruit borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on flowers and young fruits. Applying early organic or recommended safe sprays during the flowering stage prevents these pests so your produce stays clean and sellable.
ga: Fruit borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii anɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa tomato mli. Organic sprays ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe Loo ni ajieɔ yi yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahi shi ni ehe atse ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when rain is falling heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops so they can grow quickly and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without making any peppers during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause pepper plants stress, forcing them to drop flowers to survive. Mulching around the base with dry grass keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant hold its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ pepper tsei lɛ. Anyɛɔ mɔ nɔ koni eshi fɔfɔi koni enyɛ ehi shi Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my maize spoil so quickly after harvest when I stack it up in my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ beni mitoɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when it is stored with too much moisture or without airflow, creating ideal conditions for mold and insects. Drying cobs thoroughly in the sun until the grains are rock-hard before storing protects your harvest so you can sell it gradually.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baafee shiŋŋ dani okɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe koni onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ fiofio.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is too hard for my young plants to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If you try to press your palm into the ground and the soil does not yield easily, it is too hard and compacted. Hard soil makes it difficult for delicate young roots to penetrate the earth and absorb nutrients, so it needs to be loosened or properly watered before planting.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ onine awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ mlɛo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie loo awo nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Why does the earth on my farm crack when it dries out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli fãa kɛ́ egbi lɛ?

english: When heavy or clay-rich soil loses its water under the hot sun, it shrinks and forms visible surface cracks. Watering the soil helps it expand again and settles the earth so that plant roots are not left exposed to dry air.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsii loo eyɛ sũ waa lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fĩɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ akabote kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli.

english: How does hard ground affect the growth of my new crops?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard ground acts like a wall that stops roots from spreading out deep into the dirt. When roots cannot spread, the plant stays small, struggles to absorb water, and can easily dry up and die.
ga: Nɔ ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo, ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã Tso lɛ baafee bibioo. Ewa akɛ eeeŋɔ nu ni ebaanyɛ egbi ni egbo oya

english: What should I do if the soil around my young crop feels very tough and dry?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ fã? Mi dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa waa ni amɛgbi?

english: You should thoroughly water the area around the plant and allow a few days for the moisture to soak deep inside. This softens the hard earth, opens up small spaces in the soil, and allows the roots to grow without stress.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ. tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abote mli shɔŋŋ gbii fioo komɛi. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. Egbeleɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do I need to pour water on my newly set plants after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei heei ni mito shishi lɛ nu yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pouring water after setting plants allows the loose dirt to compact slightly and close air pockets. This helps the plant and the soil settle together tightly so the roots stay firmly anchored and hydrated.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli beni okɛ tso lɛ eto shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha muji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: What does it mean when someone says the soil needs to 'settle' around my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ehe miihia ni ‘akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi’ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ shishi?

english: Settling happens when water washes away extra air pockets in freshly dug earth, causing the soil particles to sink slightly and hug the roots tightly. This ensures the plant doesn't wobble or dry out at the root level.
ga: Sedimentation baa kɛji nu ho kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ hee ni atsa lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe waa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akakpokpo loo ekagbi yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: How do I know when my newly planted seedlings need water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nu he miihia midumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: You can check by pressing your hand into the top layer of dirt near the crop. If the surface feels hard, dry, and unyielding, it is time to give the soil a good soak so it softens up.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ onine ni oootsi kɛya muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ he akɛ ewa, egbi, ni ebɛ gbɔfeemɔ Be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli koni efee blɛoo.

english: Is it better to water my crops lightly every day or give them a deep soaking every few days?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo mawo amɛ nu ni mli kwɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Giving the soil a deep soak every few days is usually better than light daily sprinkling. Deep watering softens hard soil below the surface, allowing water to reach deep roots and encouraging the soil to settle properly around the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha etsɔ nu ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be Bei pii lɛ gbii fioo komɛi hi fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi fioo daa gbi. Nu ni mli kwɔ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa nu shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɔ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why does the ground sink a little bit around my plant after I water it for the first time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani mitso lɛ efo fioo beni mikɛ nu wo enɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you add water, it forces out loose air trapped in freshly dug soil. The dirt particles collapse together and sink slightly, which creates a stable, firm environment for the plant roots.
ga: Kɛ okɛ nu fata he Ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekã shikpɔŋ ni atsa ehee lɛ mli lɛ. Muji bibii lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagbee shi fioo. ni haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: How long should I wait after preparing hard soil before I expect my young plant to adjust?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ beni misaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ sɛɛ dani makpa gbɛ akɛ tsei bibii lɛ baashɛ shi?

english: After watering hard soil, you should give it about two to three days for the moisture to evenly spread and crack open tight soil pockets. This resting period allows the soil to soften so the plant roots can settle smoothly.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ oha lɛ aaafee gbii 2-3 koni nu lɛ aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni efo shikpɔŋ kotokui ni mli wa lɛ fɛɛ mli. Hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods hanging unnaturally low and looking weak on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Certain viral diseases weaken the cocoa tree's branches and stems, causing the pods to droop abnormally or hang low before eventually spoiling.
ga: Helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ haa kookoo tsei aniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo amɛfoɔ shi dani naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa tree is infected with a virus instead of just lacking nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ hela ko emɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛyeee niyenii ni sa?

english: Nutrient shortages usually cause pale leaves across the whole farm, whereas a virus often produces distinct physical signs like strangely drooping pods, swollen shoots, or spotty leaves on specific trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ, ŋmeii ni efuu loo baai ni etse yɛ tsei komɛi anɔ.

english: Does a crop virus live inside the cocoa tree itself or just on the outside of the leaves?
ga: Ani tsei amli helai hiɔ cacao tso lɛ mli loo amɛhiɔ baai lɛ asɛɛ kɛkɛ?

english: A virus lives and multiplies inside the living tissues of the tree, moving through its internal systems and causing long-term damage to the plant's health.
ga: Virus lɛ hiɔ shi ni efɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. ni tsɔɔ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni ekɛ be kakadaŋŋ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ.

english: Can diseases jump from wild forest trees near my farm into my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani hela ko baanyɛ ajɛ koo mli tsei ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atswa kɛya kookoo tsei anɔ?
