english: Yes, many forest trees act as natural host plants for crop viruses, and sap-sucking insects can easily carry these viruses from wild trees into your cocoa farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli tsei babaoo tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hei kɛha tsei amli helai. Ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ koo mli tsei amli kɛba o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: If I remove all sick cocoa trees, can the virus still survive on my land?
ga: Kɛji mijie kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ, Ani hela lɛ baahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: Yes, the virus can survive inside other plant species, weeds, or non-cocoa trees surrounding your field even after the infected cocoa trees are gone.
ga: Hɛɛ, hela lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsei krokomɛi, jwɛi, loo cacao tsei ni bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ anɔ, kɛji akɛ cacao tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ etee po.

english: How does a disease move from an infected tree to a healthy one across my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela ajɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases often spread through small insects that feed on an infected plant's sap and then move to a healthy plant, transferring the virus as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. ni yeɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Are there other crops or plants that can hold cocoa diseases without looking sick?
ga: Ayɛ tsei loo tsei krokomɛi. Ani abaanyɛ ajie kookoo kɛjɛ he ko ni hela mɔɔɔ bo?

english: Yes, certain wild plants and alternate tree species can carry cocoa viruses internally without showing visible symptoms, acting as silent reservoirs for disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli kɛ tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ kookoo hela lɛ ashwã amɛmli ni amɛjieee okadi ko ni anaa kpo. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ he ni helai toɔ dioo

english: Why do extension officers advise us to clear surrounding wild bush near cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔjie koo ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ? He ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko?

english: Clearing wild bush around your farm boundaries removes alternate host plants that harbor crop viruses and harmful insects, reducing the risk of disease spread.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei bibii ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsei ni ji enyɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Can the shade trees I plant inside my cocoa farm harbor diseases that harm cocoa?
ga: Ani tsei ni miduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai ni yeɔ kookoo lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Some specific shade tree species can host the same viruses that attack cocoa trees, so it is important to only plant recommended, safe shade tree varieties.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ hela ni tutuaa cacao tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni adu tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ adu pɛ.

english: Why does cocoa disease keep coming back even after I plant fresh, healthy cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo hela lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa ekoŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: If wild host plants or infected trees nearby are not cleared, insects will continue to carry the virus from those plants directly onto your new, healthy seedlings.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieee tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, Kooloi baaya nɔ ajie helai kɛjɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli kɛya odumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What does phosphorus actually do inside my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni fɔsfɔs feɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mi-cacao lɛ mli?

english: Phosphorus works like a power battery for your cocoa trees. It helps the plant build strong roots, produce flowers, and convert sunlight and soil nutrients into the food it needs to grow healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Fosforo tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewalɛ batiri kɛhaa o-koko tsei lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do my cocoa trees turn nutrients from the ground into food for making pods?
ga: Te mi cacao tsei lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛtsakeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii koni amɛfee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees drink dissolved soil nutrients through their roots. Using sunlight through their leaves, the tree processes these nutrients internally to manufacture the energy and food required to grow stems, leaves, and pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei nuɔ sũ mli niyenii ni mli edɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛtsu niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ahe nii yɛ amɛmli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ ashishifãi, baai, kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Will giving my cocoa trees extra fertilizer always lead to a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baaha amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be?

english: No, adding too much fertilizer can actually harm your cocoa. Just like a person becoming sick from overeating, excessive nutrients can overwhelm the tree, preventing it from properly using the nutrients to make food.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye o-cocoa lɛ awui. Nakai eji yɛ mɛi ni hela mɔɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ fe nine lɛ he. Niyenii babaoo baanyɛ aye tso lɛ nɔ kunim. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛfee niyenii.

english: What happens if there is too much phosphorus in my cocoa farm's soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs fa babaoo yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When soil phosphorus levels become too high, the cocoa tree may absorb it, but it will not be able to process or consume it to make food. The excess nutrient gets trapped inside without benefiting the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ Cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ Shi anyɛɛɛ atsu he nii loo aye ni akɛfee niyenii. Niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ mli ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he kɛhaaa tso lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees still showing poor growth even after I added fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Sometimes soil conditions or excessive nutrient levels prevent the cocoa tree from using the fertilizer. The plant may take the nutrients inside, but if it cannot digest or process them into usable food, the tree will still struggle to grow.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii. Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli loo afee lɛ niyenii ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii Tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ lolo koni eda.

english: Why do some farmers spray liquid fertilizer directly on cocoa leaves instead of putting it on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ kookoo baa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Spraying liquid fertilizer on leaves allows the cocoa tree to absorb nutrients directly through its foliage. This is helpful when the soil is too dry or when the roots are unable to take up nutrients from the ground efficiently.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can cocoa leaves absorb fertilizer sprayed on them, or does fertilizer only work through the roots?
ga: Ani kookoo baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwie amɛnɔ lɛ? Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ shishifãi lɛ pɛ anɔ amɛtsu nii?

english: Cocoa leaves have tiny openings that can take in liquid nutrients directly when sprayed. While roots are the main way plants feed, leaf spraying acts as a quick, direct way to deliver nutrients straight into the tree.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu mli niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ Eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi ji tsei lɛ aniyenii titri moŋ, Shi baai lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ oya, ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ haa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: When should I choose to spray nutrients on my cocoa leaves rather than applying solid fertilizer to the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mahala akɛ makɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baashwie kookoo baai anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaf spraying is best when you need to give your trees a quick boost or when the soil conditions prevent the roots from absorbing nutrients properly. It feeds the plant directly through the leaves without relying on soil uptake.
ga: Foliage ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ oosumɔ ni oha otso lɛ aya hiɛ oya. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a plant has taken in fertilizer but cannot 'use' it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ awoɔ tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii shi ‘akɛtsuuu nii’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: This means the plant's roots absorbed the nutrient into its internal system, but due to nutrient imbalance or plant stress, the tree cannot process that nutrient into usable energy or food to grow.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛyaa mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Shi yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejaaa loo tsei ahe haomɔ hewɔ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nakai niyenii lɛ he nii ni efee hewalɛ loo niyenii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii kɛhaa dalɛ.

english: How can I avoid wasting money on too much fertilizer for my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shika babaoo ni mikɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: You can avoid waste by applying only the recommended amounts of fertilizer for your soil. Applying too much leads to high nutrient levels that the cocoa tree cannot consume, wasting your money without increasing your yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa fitemɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni cacao tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shika fiteɔ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn because direct heat dries them out faster than their roots can take up water. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside young cocoa trees protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and turn yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ?

english: This curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant stem varieties and removing infected plants from the field early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tso yibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the plant's growing center. Checking your maize early and applying recommended pest control measures before the worms grow big prevents heavy crop damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ amli. Abɛi mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii koni akɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa dani ŋmeii lɛ adara lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds in a single hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant groundnuts together on the same land with my cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cassava lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts and cassava grow very well together. Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil to feed the cassava, while also spreading across the ground to keep weeds away.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbɛɔ ashwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant during the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their strength and yield potential in the next generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season ensures higher yields, uniform growth, and better resistance to diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba. dalɛ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know if my farm soil lacks nutrients before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops had pale yellowish leaves, thin stems, or produced very small yields, your soil is low on nutrients. Adding compost, animal manure, or the right balance of fertilizer before planting restores soil fertility.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tsei bibii, loo nibii fioo pɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with aggressive roots adapted to grab water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting stops them from starving your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ akaye otsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plants face extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I keep insects from destroying my stored maize after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils thrive in moist air and loose storage. Drying your maize completely until it is hard and storing it in airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates any pests naturally without needing heavy chemicals.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ fioo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii akabote mli. Suffocate yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are not yet deep enough to draw sufficient groundwater. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains around them keeps the surrounding air humid and shelters the leaves from sun scorch.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall green leaves but produce very small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ baa ni kɛlɛ shi eyɛ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize requires high amounts of nutrients like nitrogen and adequate field spacing to develop full cobs. If seeds are planted too close together or the soil lacks nutrients, the plant consumes its energy growing leaves rather than filling out the corn cobs.
ga: Niyenii nibii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛ ni sa koni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii baafata he.

english: Waterlogged soil deprives roots of oxygen, creating ideal conditions for fungal rots to develop. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away naturally, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal rot lɛ shweremɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into tight rolls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Applying targeted organic treatments like neem oil extracts early on helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ tamɔ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Continuous planting of the same crop rapidly depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite oya. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Rotate corn kɛ legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shi.

english: Tomato plants often shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent water at the base of the plant and maintaining soil moisture helps the plant retain flowers and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shishigbɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are caterpillars eating deep holes into the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a common sign of Fall Armyworm attack, a destructive pest that feeds inside the growing central funnel of young maize plants. Early inspection and applying recommended biological or chemical controls directly into the plant funnel stops the damage.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akudɔɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baakpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on top of the soil help my vegetables grow better during warm periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch like dry grass keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi ni haa nɔ lɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: How can I tell if my land is fertile enough before I sow my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Healthy soil is dark, rich in organic material, soft to dig, and supports vigorous wild grass growth. If past crops showed pale yellow leaves or weak growth, the soil is likely depleted and will benefit from compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo, efoɔ blɛoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa koo mli jwɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ be ko ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ebaaná ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight and strong winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or keeping shade trees keeps the soil moist and creates a cool climate that protects young seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo hulutsoo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do extension agents tell me to plant cover crops on land I am leaving to rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu cover crops yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mishi kɛha hejɔɔmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving land bare leaves topsoil vulnerable to being washed away by heavy rain. Cover crops act like a protective blanket on the soil, preventing erosion, stopping weeds from taking over, and restoring nutrients naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ yɛ oshara mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho. Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from growing well even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal sunlight, root space, and soil fertilizer meant for your plants, starving the crop even if water is available.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ejuɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ waa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the plant has matured?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food needed to make leaves dark green and healthy, or that heavy rains have washed those nutrients deep below the reach of the roots.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my young plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem burns the plant's delicate skin and tender roots, which can stunt or kill the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee shoo loo egbe lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small and misshapen when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni efiteɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, well-loosened soil to expand underground. When planted in hard or compacted ground, the roots cannot push through easily, resulting in thin, woody tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa yitso ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ tso baa.

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow and die when water stays sitting on the land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air underground just as leaves need air above ground. When water sits continuously on the land, it drowns the roots, causing them to rot and fail to absorb nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi. Taakɛ baai he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop in the middle of hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during hot afternoons is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to trap moisture and protect itself from losing too much water to the heat; it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves suddenly have ragged holes and small powdery grains in the middle of the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni akɛ powda fee lɛ trukaa lɛ? Yɛ funnel lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Ragged holes and tiny droppings inside the central funnel of maize are signs of Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender leaves inside before they emerge.
ga: Buu ni elaaje kɛ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli niyenii dani amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ he okadii yɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and thin leaves that lose water very quickly under strong heat. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to shield them from excessive heat while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but it drops a large majority naturally because it only has enough water and nutrients to support a limited number of full-sized pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ yɔɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi ni dalɛ fa babaoo lɛ ayibɔ fioo ko.

english: Continuous moisture and high humidity during heavy rains allow fungal spores, known as Black Pod disease, to multiply and spread quickly across the wet surface of the pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni ji fungal spores, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ black pod hela lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of green leaves but very few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi cocoa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: When cocoa trees receive excessive nitrogen or develop too many unwanted shoots, the tree sends all its energy into growing leaves instead of forming flowers and pods. Pruning helps direct food back into fruit production.
ga: Beni cacao tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni ataooo lɛ. Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Pruning haa niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai afeemɔ mli.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or dark red to a clear yellow or orange. Tapping the pod also produces a hollow sound, showing that the inner beans have separated from the outer husk wall.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. Pod lɛ ni oootswa lɛ hu haa gbee ni mli ewo muji baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi ŋmei lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ mli egbala kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei gbogbo lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to heap my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans, destroys the seed germ, breaks down the surrounding sugary pulp, and develops the essential chocolate flavor precursors needed before drying.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ. efiteɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ Efiteɔ loo ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. ni amɛfee tsokolate mli ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa lɛ dani amɛgbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a major harvest late in the year and a smaller harvest a few months later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ, ni nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow Ghana's rainfall patterns. The main crop develops during the major rainy season when moisture is abundant, while the smaller light crop corresponds to the minor rains.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyiɛɔ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii titrii ni aduɔ lɛ daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli beni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ kpãa gbee.

english: How can I tell if my soil is running out of nutrients for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ niyenii ni haa cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ?

english: Nutrient shortages show on the tree leaves. If leaves turn yellow between veins, stay small, or drop early, the soil lacks key nutrients needed to feed the cocoa tree.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ateŋ, amɛtee nɔ amɛhi shi bibii, loo amɛgbee shi oya lɛ, no lɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa ni baaye abua cacao tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do mirid pests attack the soft new shoots and young pods of my cocoa trees instead of old branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mirid ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ moŋ fe tsei lɛ aniji momo lɛ?

english: Young shoots and growing pods have tender skin and high sap content, making it easy for insects like mirids to pierce the surface and suck out plant juices.
ga: Tsobii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ yɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ashwishwɛi baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Why do my dried cocoa beans absorb moisture and turn moldy inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa nitoohe lɛ?

english: Dried cocoa beans easily draw moisture out of humid air if stored directly on floors or kept in unventilated rooms, creating conditions for mold to grow.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli oya kɛji akɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli baanyɛ atsɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that easily lose water under harsh sunlight. Without enough shade trees or soil moisture during the dry season, the plant drops its leaves to protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baashi baai lɛ yɛ esɛɛ koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra stems growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fata he lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra stems, called suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest stem, which will produce a much larger and healthier bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie amɛteŋ babaoo lɛ, tso lɛ yitso ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi, ni no baaha plantains akuu ko ni da kwraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a major pest in Ghana. They hide in the central funnel of the maize plant where the new leaves grow, eating the plant from the inside out unless controlled early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa yɛ Ghana Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni baa heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni ayeɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo nɔ ja akudɔ mra

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground if I do not harvest them before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots store starch, but when heavy rains soak the soil for long periods, the roots absorb too much water and air cannot reach them, causing fungal rot to set in quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ toɔ starch. Shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu babaoo tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the damp ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Maximum sunlight helps the leaves make food, which flows down to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the growing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and is then soaked suddenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, etsɔ nu trukaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves and spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the crop.
ga: Koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni amɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same plot three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases specific to maize to multiply in the ground, resulting in smaller yields each season.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener when I mix dry chicken manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and organic matter, which acts like food for both the soil microbes and the plants, helping crops build strong stems and deep green leaves.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei amli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often leaves the ground warm and wet, but if a dry spell follows immediately, the seeds start to sprout and then die in the hot, drying soil. It is better to wait until the rainy season settles fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔɔ. Shi kɛji hɔmɔ ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli aba shi kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot hold much water. Direct, intense sunlight causes them to lose moisture faster than their roots can drink from the soil, which makes them wilt without shade.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops perform worse when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for water and nutrients, while their branches block sunlight from reaching one another above ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛniji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some types of land make crops grow fast while other land keeps them small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔji srɔtoi komɛi haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu haa amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Different types of soil hold different amounts of water and plant food. Deep, dark soil holds moisture and nutrients well, while sandy or stony soil loses water quickly and lacks the food crops need to grow big.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ toɔ nu kɛ tsei ahe niyenii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, nu fiteɔ oya, ni niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and yield very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are strong plants that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops weak and unable to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during dry weather as a natural way to save water. Less leaves mean the tree loses less moisture to the dry air while water in the soil is scarce.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Baai fioo pɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli yɛ be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry for nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn yellow instead of healthy green, their growth slows down, and they produce smaller or fewer fruits than expected.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ najiaŋ. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ekɛ yibii bibii loo bibii baa fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if the tree does not get enough nutrients or water, or if tiny beneficial insects are not present in the farm to transfer pollen between the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ?

english: Pruning removes extra branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the whole tree. This prevents diseases and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Heavy rain creates damp and humid conditions that help a fungal disease called Black Pod spread rapidly across your crop through water drops and high air moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ onibii fɛɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny insects causing the fresh shoots on my cocoa branches to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miigbi ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids suck the sweet sap from young branches and inject a liquid that damages the plant tissue, causing the fresh leaves and shoots to dry up and die.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids nuɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ amli nu ni amɛwoɔ nu ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ amli fãji lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai kɛ ŋmeii heei gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because intense sunlight dries out their tender leaves and burns the soil. Keeping taller shade trees like plantains or forest hardwoods creates a cooler, moist environment that protects cocoa seedlings in their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni wa lɛ akwɛmɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and overly bushy conditions during heavy rains. Pruning extra branches and weeding regularly allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, keeping the fungus away.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni jwɛi babaoo yɔɔ fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe ni ojie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha tsei lɛ agbi. ni eha ŋmei lɛ ayaje mli

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow strong and green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will restore their green color and improve crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii feɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot of the corn plant. Inspecting your field early and spraying with recommended organic insecticides or neem extracts can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Which way am I supposed to plant cassava stem cuttings into the ground so they grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the stem cutting to find the small buds or 'eyes'—they must point upwards toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down causes shoots to struggle, delays growth, and results in a lower yield of tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni baatsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kasava ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baaha ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ agbo. ehaa shweremɔ baa shi ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tuber yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the soil for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more food they make, which flows down to grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni niyenii ni ofeɔ lɛ fa lɛ, babaoo ni niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekwɛ̃ɔ yam tsei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil moist with regular watering and adding mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool, helping flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. shishitoo koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into small rolls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by viruses they spread. Spraying with neem leaf solution or insecticidal soap helps control these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baa heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why should I leave dry grass and leaves on my farm soil instead of burning them after clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ beni mijie amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving plant remains on the soil as mulch keeps the ground moist during dry spells, prevents rain from washing away fertile topsoil, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ, ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Too many sucker shoots compete with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to leave only two or three strong shoots per plant allows the main tree to devote its energy to growing large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni eshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ yɛ tso kome mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni shwereɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomato seedlings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and a smaller harvest. Proper spacing gives each plant room to breathe and feed.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni ekɛmuɔ ni eyeɔ nii.

english: Why do I need to push wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Lifting the leaves off the ground with sticks allows them to catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating crops like maize with legumes like groundnuts helps restore the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛtsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dry grass and crop leaves spread on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai ni gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, blocks weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to fully settle before planting my corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Corn seeds require a steady, continuous supply of water right after planting to germinate and grow strong roots. Planting during a false start to the rains can cause seeds to dry up and die.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ejaaa mli Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning dense branches lets air and sunlight in to dry out the pods and prevent infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baaa amɛnɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves with caterpillars tucked inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai ni ŋmeii lɛ efo mli yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars feed inside the funnel of the maize plant where they are protected, so early detection and target spraying are crucial.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ gbɛi lɛ amli he ni abuɔ he yɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli nibii ni anaa kɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia waa

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow with tiny white flies buzzing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ lɛ? ni fãa kɛbɔleɔ he

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava cuttings stops the virus from destroying your crop.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ cassava niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I bother testing my soil if I can already judge its quality just by looking at it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ manyɛ makojo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ lɛ,.

english: Looking at soil only shows its surface color and texture, but it hides vital details like invisible nutrient levels and acidity. A simple soil test tells you exactly what plant food is missing so you do not waste money buying the wrong fertilizers.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ etsɔɔ su, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Shi ekɛ saji ni he hiaa tamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni anaaa kɛ acidity teeɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Ebaakɛɛ bo nɔ tuuntu ni niyenii tso lɛ bɛ. Bɔni afee ni okafite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa.

english: How does getting my land tested help me harvest more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa niyenii babaoo?

english: Soil testing acts like a health checkup for your farm. It tells you the exact health of your land so you can feed your crops precisely what they need, leading to bigger yields and healthier plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewalɛnamɔ he kwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ bo bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha pɔtɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ aha onibii lɛ. Ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Can the types of wild weeds growing on my land tell me if the soil is good for farming?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi henɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ mi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, certain weeds thrive only in poor or acidic soil, while others grow in fertile ground. Observing wild weeds gives you a quick visual clue about your land, though a soil test is still needed for exact details.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ lɛ, koo mli jwɛi ni okwɛɔ lɛ haa onáa susumɔ ko ni mli wa. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ lolo koni ana nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli moŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant them on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating different crops or letting the land rest helps keep the soil rich and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Aloo ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the rich top layer of my soil seem to wash away to the side after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo kɛtee sɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains easily wash away loose, bare topsoil down slopes or to the edges of your field. Planting grass borders or keeping organic mulch on the ground helps trap the soil and keep rich nutrients in place.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ. Ekɛ ehe baa shi yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ loo oyale lɛ naa oya ni ebɛ atade. Jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ husui amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do plants at the bottom of my sloped farm grow bigger than the ones at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni etse ehe lɛ shishi lɛ miida fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes rich topsoil and dissolved plant food down from the higher ground and deposits them at the bottom. This leaves the top area nutrient-poor while the bottom land stays rich and moist.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebuaa naa yɛ shishigbɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ he ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni he ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your crops are missing essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu

english: How do I know if my land has become too tired to support crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: Signs of tired soil include stunted crop growth, pale leaves, stems that break easily, and soil that hardens like concrete after rain. Adding manure or compost helps bring exhausted land back to life.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ ahe ji tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, baai ni tsuɔ, tsei ni fãa oya, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbo lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wala baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to buy fertilizer without knowing what my land actually needs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mileee nɔ ni he hiaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Buying fertilizer without testing your soil is like taking medicine without knowing your illness. Using the wrong fertilizer can waste your money, burn your crops, or make your soil too sour for plants to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛkaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛɔ lɛ, etamɔ tsofa ni oooye ni oleee akɛ hela mɔ bo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ofite shika, eshã oŋmɔshi nibii, loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acid tsɔ ni tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: How can women farmers in our community get help to check their land before planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aye abua yei okwaafoi ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛdu nii?

english: Agricultural extension officers provide advice and soil testing services to all farmers, including women. You can invite an officer to visit your farm, take soil samples, and guide you on the best crops for your land.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ ŋaawoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa nitsumɔi haa okwaafoi fɛɛ, ni yei fata he. Obaanyɛ ofɔ̃ onukpai nine koni amɛbasara ŋmɔ lɛ. Bua shikpɔŋ he nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa ni otsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce many flowers but very few actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi kookoo ŋmɔji diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated—either by tiny insects or manually by hand—to turn into pods. If pollination does not happen, the flowers simply dry up and drop off without forming any cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii loo nine awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ, bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni kookoo ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does it help my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination is a technique where you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small brush or forceps. It ensures that almost every flower develops into a full cocoa pod, dramatically increasing your yield.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni otsɔɔ nɔ okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni jɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh bibioo loo pliers nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi daa kɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ. Ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How many bags of cocoa can I reasonably harvest from my farm if I use good farm practices?
ga: Cocoa kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi kpakpai tsu nii?

english: While a standard farm might only yield around 5 bags per acre with minimal care, using improved methods like hand pollination, proper pruning, and pest control can increase your harvest up to 25 or 30 bags per acre.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ po baanyɛ aha aaafee kotokui 5 yɛ acre kome mli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsake nɔ tamɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashɛ kotokui 25 loo 30 yɛ acre kome mli.

english: When is the best time of day for me to pollinate my cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: The best time for pollination is in the early morning when flowers are fresh and fully open, and before the sun becomes too hot, which can dry out the pollen and reduce success rates.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha pollination ji leebi maŋkpa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ni dani hulu lɛ baadɔ tsɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ agbi ni eha omanyeyeli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some of my small, young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: Young pods often shrivel due to fungal infections like black pod disease, insect attacks, or nutritional stress. Regular spraying, proper shade control, and removing infected pods help protect the surviving ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ black pod hela, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, loo niyenii mli haomɔ hewɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe.

english: Now that cocoa prices are high, what basic activities should I focus on to get maximum harvest this season?
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ, kookoo jara wa waa. Mɛɛ shishijee nitsumɔi esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ koni maná nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: To get the highest harvest when prices are favorable, focus on timely weeding, pruning to let in light, applying fertilizer, spraying against pests, and doing hand pollination to boost pod numbers.
ga: Bɔni afee ni aná nibii ni afee lɛ babaoo fe fɛɛ yɛ jara ni sa nɔ. Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama jwɛi ni ooojie yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ. Afoɔ tsei lɛ koni akɛwo kane mli, akɛwo mli, ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni akɛ niji woɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ ayi afa.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches from my cocoa trees make them produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ haa amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree canopy, which stimulates flower production, prevents humidity-loving diseases, and allows flowers to receive better pollination.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. ni haa fɔfɔi feɔ fɛ̃i Tsĩɔ helai ni sumɔɔ fɛ̃i lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Will adding fertilizer to my farm automatically prevent cocoa flowers from falling off?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsi kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni baafite lɛ naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential nutrients that make the tree stronger, but flower retention also depends on adequate water, reduced shade stress, and active pollination to turn those flowers into pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ waa. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ hu damɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ pollination mli baa lɛ shi koni otsɔ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ afee pods

english: What causes my cocoa trees to shed their flowers during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: During dry spells, cocoa trees drop flowers to conserve water and survive heat stress. Maintaining temporary shade crops like plantains and keeping moisture in the soil helps trees hold onto their flowers.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be harvested for maximum bean weight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa kɛha dumɔwui ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: A pod is ready when its skin changes color completely—usually turning bright yellow for green pods or orange for red pods. Harvesting pods when fully ripe ensures maximum bean size and weight per bag.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo beni hewolo lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. loo orange kɛha red pods Pods lɛ ni akpaa kɛji ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ elɛɛmɔ kɛ etsitsinɔnii ni fe fɛɛ yɛ kotoku kome mli.

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, while traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from direct, harsh sunlight and retain soil moisture. Planting shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to support cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ cacao tsei anɔ?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, well-drained, fertile loamy soils that can retain moisture without becoming waterlogged during heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. kɛ babaoo ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ nu baaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantains on the same farm as my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first few years, you can plant plantains, cassava, or legumes between cocoa rows to get food and income while providing shade to the cocoa, as long as you do not overcrowd them.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ odu plantains, cassava loo legumes yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ateŋ koni eha niyenii kɛ shika kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ŋmɔlɔ aha kookoo lɛ. Shii abɔ ni okɛ amɛ eyiŋ obɔ fe nine lɛ.

english: Is it safe to cut off branches from my cocoa tree, or will it damage the plant?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ majie mi cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii? Aloo ebaafite tso lɛ loo efiteee?

english: Pruning unproductive shoots and dead branches helps the tree direct its energy into pod production, improves airflow, and allows sunlight to reduce fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni wooo yibii ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha hulu la lɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ aba shi

english: How often should I clear weeds around my young cocoa plants?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo?

english: Weeding should be done 3 to 4 times a year, especially during the rainy season, to prevent weeds from choking young trees and stealing nutrients from the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ ji koni jwɛi akaye tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by high humidity and poor ventilation. Clearing weeds, pruning excess leaves, and removing infected pods helps control it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii mli baa. weeding Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects. Natural flower drop is normal, but severe loss can be caused by extreme heat, dry soil, or pest attacks.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni elaaje waa aba.

english: What happens to cocoa trees when the dry Harmattan season lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ?

english: Extended dry weather causes cocoa trees to drop leaves, shed young pods, and dry up. Mulching the soil and keeping mature shade trees help retain ground moisture during dry months.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ baai shwieɔ shi, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe pods change color—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow—and they produce a hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su Pods ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Pods tsuru loo purple tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. ni kɛ́ ata he fioo lɛ Gbee ko ni mli ewo muji baaje kpo.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees just dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by tiny insects or by hand to form pods. Unpollinated flowers cannot turn into fruit, so the tree naturally sheds them after a day or two to save energy.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. loo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ koni akɛfolɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ sɛɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What is cocoa hand pollination, and why are extension officers encouraging us to do it?
ga: Mɛni ji nine ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔfee enɛ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination involves manually transferring pollen from one cocoa flower to another using simple tools. It ensures that far more flowers get fertilized compared to relying on wild insects alone, leading to significantly higher pod yields.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ajieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi babaoo woɔ fɔmɔ mli kɛ akɛto koo mli kooloi bibii pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa pod yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the thick trunk of the tree instead of on the thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei niji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a trunk-flowering plant. Growth cushions on the main trunk and thick branches are designed to support the heavy weight of mature cocoa pods, which would break smaller outer branches.
ga: Cocoa ji fɔfɔi tso ni yɔɔ tso. Afee kushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ koni ekɛfi kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha kponɔgbɛ niji bibii lɛ akumɔ.

english: Does rain affect how cocoa flowers get pollinated on my farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ saa kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, heavy rains can wash away pollen and stop the tiny midges that pollinate cocoa from flying. Doing hand pollination on dry mornings gives flowers the best chance to form healthy pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi kooloi bibii ni daraa lɛ anaa. No haa kookoo lɛ feɔ pollinate bɔni afee ni enyɛŋ efã. Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli yɛ leebi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why did my cocoa farm produce a high yield last year, but this year the trees look tired with fewer pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ? Shi afi nɛɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: A very large harvest drains nutrients from cocoa trees. Without adequate fertilizer, proper pruning, and pollination support early in the new season, trees take longer to recover, leading to lower yields the following year.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa wuji lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ be hee lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tso lɛ baahe be babaoo dani ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are some of my small, young cocoa pods turning shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree has too many young pods to feed with its available nutrients and water, causing it to discard the surplus so remaining pods can mature.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Cherel’s Wilt. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ. Ha ni ekɛ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ashwie koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why is it important to assist with pollination early in the year instead of waiting for later months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aye abua yɛ pollination he yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni ooomɛ sɛɛ mli nyɔji lɛ?

english: Starting early in the season aligns pod development with peak rain patterns, giving pods plenty of water and time to grow full and healthy before dry weather sets in.
