ga: Shishijee mra yɛ be lɛ mli baaha pod lɛ shweremɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ afee ekome. Ha pods lɛ aná nu babaoo. ni ená be ni ekɛda jogbaŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Are the tiny insects I see flying around my cocoa flowers harmful pests that I should spray?
ga: Kplukai bibii ni mina ni amɛmiiho kɛmiibɔle he lɛ Ani kookoo fɔfɔi ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ?

english: Most tiny flies around flowers are beneficial midges responsible for natural pollination. Chemical sprays during flowering can kill these helpful insects, reducing natural pod formation.
ga: Fɛ̃i bibii ebɔle he fɛɛ. Fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ, kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. ni ebaa adebɔɔ mli pod feemɔ shi

english: How does trimming extra branches off my cocoa trees help increase my harvest?
ga: Te niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach the flower cushions on the main trunk. This keeps flower cushions healthy, reduces fungal diseases, and promotes higher pod production.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii akushɛi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees before the flowering period starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-koko tso lɛ mli nu dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilization gives cocoa trees the necessary nutrients right when they need extra energy to form strong flowers, hold onto developing pods, and resist natural pod wilt.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ haa enáa niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa ni ená hewalɛ kroko koni ekɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa aba lɛ. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ pods ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the maize I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local soil and climate, so they sprout aggressively. They steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your planted crops, which need extra care to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli. ni biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛha akaŋshii

english: How does weed killer actually kill the weeds without hurting my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Most chemical weed sprays work by blocking specific growth processes inside green leaves so the weed starves and dies. Once in the ground, these chemicals break down over time into harmless substances.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ dalɛ ni amɛtsiɔ yɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ. be mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsofai nɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛfeɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why is it a waste of money if I spray weed chemical right before a big rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi dani nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the weed leaves before the plant has time to absorb it. The chemical gets diluted and carried away in rainwater, so the weeds survive and your money is wasted.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ jwɛi baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ amɛ. Akɛ tsofai lɛ woɔ nu mli ni akɛyaa nugbɔ nu mli. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi ni eji shikafitemɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow when weeds grow tall around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, a main plant food. Tall weeds absorb the soil nutrients first, leaving your crops hungry and unable to stay healthy and green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ otso lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do I need to put fresh inputs and fertilizer into the soil every time I start a new planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull natural nutrients out of the ground. Adding inputs before the new season refills the soil bank so your new seeds have enough energy to grow strong roots.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ saji fata he dani be hee lɛ shɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔ lɛ ayi obɔ ekoŋŋ koni eha odumɔwui heei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: What actually happens to my cassava roots under the ground if I don't weed the farm early?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwieee miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya?

english: Cassava needs open soil and plenty of water to expand its tubers. If weeds choke the farm early on, their roots block the soil and steal moisture, causing your cassava roots to stay small and thin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ nu babaoo he miihia cassava koni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei jwɛi lɛ mra Amɛshishifãi lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why does planting my crops in neat, well-spaced lines help control weeds later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ fɛo ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Properly spaced crops grow broad leaves that shade the soil between rows. Because weeds need direct sunlight to germinate and grow, the shade from your crops naturally stops weed growth.
ga: Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and holes after keeping them for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powder kɛ bu yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay hidden eggs in the grain. When they hatch, the young insects eat the food stored inside the grain seed, leaving behind empty shells and fine dust.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛteeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii yeɔ niyenii ni akɛto dumɔwui amli. Eshiɔ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ sũ bibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do harvested vegetables like peppers spoil so quickly if I leave them in the heat after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni akpa tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ la mli beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once picked, crops stop receiving water from the plant but keep breathing and losing moisture. High heat speeds up rotting because bacteria and fungi multiply much faster in warm air.
ga: Kɛji abua naa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ shi eyaa nɔ emuɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha egbo oya ejaakɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested beans get mouldy if I store them before drying them completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikɛto dani egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Mould and fungus need dampness to live and spread. If beans still have water inside when you store them, fungus grows quickly and rots the harvest, but proper sun-drying removes that moisture.
ga: Mold kɛ mildew he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji nu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lolo beni okɛtoɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Shi kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that cannot absorb enough water to withstand direct heat. They need temporary shade, like plantain trees, to shield them from sun scorch until they are established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaatswa amɛhe shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the plant needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the field where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally restores soil fertility, making it richer for heavy feeders like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain creates standing water around cassava roots, it starves the tubers of oxygen and encourages fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away easily.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. cassava root Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebaawo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit shows up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress from dry soil or extreme heat. Giving plants regular water at the root area keeps them calm so the flowers can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oshwie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha efee dioo. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ tomato.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the young inner leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa lɛ baai bibii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer the tender growth in the center funnel of young maize plants. Inspecting fields early and applying targeted controls into the plant funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Kwɛmɔ he lɛ mra ni akɛ targeted control awo dumɔwui lɛ amli. Ekpaa nakai hei lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from under the leaf. Spraying appropriate insecticides or insecticidal soap helps stop leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa baai lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why does my extension worker tell me to pinch off extra stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots (suckers) stops the plant from wasting energy on leaves and channels nutrients directly into producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ (ŋmeii) lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ koni ekɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai ni tsii je kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the soil, making heavy bunches pull the whole plant down in strong winds. Supporting the main stem with bamboo or wooden props prevents the plant from snapping.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fioo. Enɛ haa tso niji ni tsii gbalaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛbaa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow very thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to food so they can grow thick stalks and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ adu tsei ni mli tse ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do weeds actually prevent my cocoa trees from bearing good fruits?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for essential nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. When weeds surround your trees, they steal the food the cocoa needs to produce flowers and grow healthy pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kookoo koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help increase my harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Regular weeding opens up the farm floor, allows air to circulate, reduces hiding places for destructive pests, and ensures that all water and nutrients go directly into feeding your crop instead of wild grass.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baagbele ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli Ehaa hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Ni ekwɛɔ koni nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ koo mli jwɛi najiaŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees covered in green leaves, but I cannot see any cocoa pods growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ he baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi minaaa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni miida.

english: A tree can look green while still lacking the specific nutrients or light needed to fruit. Over-shading, lack of soil nutrients, or unmanaged weeds can cause cocoa trees to put energy into leaf growth instead of producing pods.
ga: Tso ko baanyɛ afee tamɔ eŋɔli shi loloolo lɛ, ebɛ niyenii loo la ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii. Shading babaoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo, jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers are delicate and drop easily if the tree experiences dry spells, lack of insect pollination, or stress caused by excessive weeds and dense shade.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ. Kplukai ni bɛ loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jwɛi babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa kɛbaa.

english: How long after planting should I expect my young cocoa trees to start giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ? Ani esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaje shishi amɛha mi ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing their first fruits within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties may take 4 to 5 years under proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ ashishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I easily estimate the size of my farm if I do not have measuring tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ da ha lɛ he mlɛo? Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe

english: You can estimate your farm size by pacing it out using consistent strides (roughly one meter per big step) or by counting the standard planting rows prepared during land clearing.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ onaji ni oooha ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ. (aaafee mita kome yɛ step agbo fɛɛ step agbo mli) loo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni asaa he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ be mli lɛ akanemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to prune my cocoa trees instead of just letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahã eda yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches so the tree does not waste food on useless growth. It allows sunlight to reach the trunk and encourages more flowering.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite niyenii kɛtsɔ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo he hewalɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp, and unweeded farms. Keeping the farm well-weeded and pruned lowers humidity and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi jogbaŋŋ ni ofo mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are getting too much direct sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ?

english: When cocoa trees receive too much sun, their leaves look scorched or turn yellow and brown at the edges. Young cocoa needs shade plants, like plantains, to shield them from intense heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: What signs show that my cocoa trees are not getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Common signs include pale yellow leaves, slow growth, small or misshapen pods, and trees shedding their leaves early even when rain is plentiful.
ga: Okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ji baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. slow growth Pods bibii loo ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli Ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po.

english: If I only have a small cup of a new seed variety, how can I turn it into enough seeds to plant my whole farm?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi bibioo ko mli pɛ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ enɛ nɔ mafee dumɔwui ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃?

english: You can plant that small quantity in a small, well-cared-for nursery or multiplication plot. When those plants mature, you harvest all their seeds to plant a much larger field in the next season, rapidly multiplying your initial seed supply.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bibii bibii yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ nakai tsei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Obaakpa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni okɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni da kwraa mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oshishijee dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why is it safer for me to test a new crop variety on a small plot first instead of planting my entire farm with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maka tsei srɔtoi heei aka yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Testing on a small plot lets you see how the new crop responds to your local soil, rainfall, and pests without risking your entire livelihood if the crop does not perform well.
ga: Kaa ni ooofee yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ haa onaa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Ni okɛ oshihilɛ fɛɛ awo oshara mli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to make food and grow green; adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni efee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I cut down all the large trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large trees provide essential shade and keep the air cool; without them, the young cocoa seedlings lose moisture quickly and burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kɛ́ amɛbɛ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛshãa.

english: Why does my farmland produce less harvest every year even though I plant at the same time and with the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be kome mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Growing the same crop in the same soil year after year drains specific nutrients from the ground. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts helps restore life and nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wala kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, won't I harvest more cassava roots from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ mafo ŋmei shishifãi babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin roots. Giving plants proper space allows each root to grow large and healthy.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã ni edaa ni ewaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die right after a heavy rain during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water and cannot drain away quickly, the roots choke from lack of air. Heat also encourages soil fungal diseases to enter flooded roots, causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ eho kɛje kpo oya. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ hu woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbote shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my neighbor get bigger maize cobs than me even though our farms are right next to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni da fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ mi moŋ?

english: Bigger cobs usually result from using high-yielding certified seeds, planting at the correct spacing, and applying nutrients at the right time in the plant's life, rather than just having good soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli baa ji ŋmeii wuji. Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ tso lɛ wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛkɛ

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that webworms and weevils do not destroy it before I sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Bɔni afee ni wɛb ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite lɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Insects need moisture and air to thrive inside stored grain. Drying your maize until it is completely hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags stops insects from multiplying and destroying your grain.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia kooloi koni amɛdara yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni okɛwo vacuum kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo ni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why should I consult an agricultural extension officer instead of just farming the way my parents taught me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oyabi okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ko? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu okwaayeli tamɔ bɔ ni ofɔlɔi tsɔɔ bo lɛ?

english: While traditional methods are helpful, extension officers bring modern scientific knowledge about changing rainfall patterns, new crop diseases, and improved seed varieties that can significantly increase your harvest and income.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema gbɛi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ moŋ Shi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ hu kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jeŋ nilee ni kɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni tsakeɔ, tsei ahe helai heei, kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake ni baanyɛ aha okpamɔ kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ baa.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick the cassava stem into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ okɛ ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you must plant the stem cutting with the buds or leaf nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting it upside down forces the shoots to grow downward before turning up, which wastes energy, weakens the plant, and reduces root yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni odu tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ni ŋmeii loo baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baafite hewalɛ. ha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi

english: Yam vines need support to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil also prevents rotting and allows the plant to send more food down to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni amɛkɛkwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field with no tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch and dry out under direct, hot sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates cooler, moist air and shields the seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔŋ mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo aba. ni obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my soil produce less maize when I plant it on the same farm plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously draws the exact same nutrients out of the earth every season. Without resting the land or planting legumes like beans to restore the soil, the ground becomes exhausted and cannot support a good harvest.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haaa hejɔɔmɔ loo oduŋ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua nikpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves and stem growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Multiple shoots compete with the mother tree for groundwater, light, and soil nutrients. Trimming away excess shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, directing all the plant's food into growing a thick stem and large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why is my garden egg plant growing big green leaves but dropping all its flowers before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ woɔ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Heat stress or lack of nutrients like phosphorus can also cause blossoms to fall off prematurely.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo oya.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of new leaves. Treating the crops with neem oil or appropriate sprays destroys the insects so healthy, flat leaves can grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi bibii lɛ ahiɛ bɔni afee ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato roots receive uneven amounts of water, making it difficult for the plant to absorb calcium. Maintaining consistent watering habits keeps the fruit healthy and firm.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tomato shishifãi lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my field when the crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, making it hard for them to fight off fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early ensures the main crop gets all the nourishment it needs during its critical start.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ekwɛɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ eshishijee bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there are no big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct hot sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly before their root systems are strong enough to survive full sun exposure.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya dani shishifãi lɛ ahe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Leaving too many young shoots causes them to fight with the main tree for water and nutrients, which results in smaller plantain bunches and weaker stems.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji egbɛ eshwã ni ŋmeii bibii ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the tender leaves and central growing point of maize plants, which can severely reduce yields if not controlled.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often triggered by irregular watering while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell which direction is up when I am burying cassava stems in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ afu ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni eyaa ŋwɛi?

english: Look closely at the leaf nodes or small bumps along the stem where leaves used to grow; those small buds should always point upward toward the sky when planted.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be kɛ́ adu.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to produce large underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often shed their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, lack of water, or a sudden dry spell during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo amɛhe egbi trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make my farm soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehi aha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely absorb it; putting fertilizer in dry soil concentrates the salts and burns the roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ekome ni eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I dig up all my yams from the farm at once after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Yams stay fresh longer when kept underground in the moist soil. If you dig up thousands of tubers at once without having buyers ready, they can dry out, rot, or get heat damage before you can use or sell them.
ga: Sweet potatoes baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛji otsi ŋmeii akpei abɔ shikome ni osaaa mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ. Nakai tsɔnei lɛ baanyɛ agbi, amɛgboi loo la ni tsoɔ lɛ baafite amɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully ready to be dug out of the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are usually ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up, showing that the plant has finished feeding energy into the tuber underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ naa.

english: What is the safest way to dig up yams so I don't break or cut the tubers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsa sweet potatoes lɛ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni aaanyɛ? Bɔni afee ni okafolɔ loo ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Carefully loosen the soil around the edge of the mound using a digging tool rather than striking directly into the middle. Uncut yams stay healthy much longer than wounded ones.
ga: Okɛ dɛŋdade ko ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛjie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle gɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔko lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmeii ni epila.

english: What causes my yam leaves to look twisted or yellowish, and is it a viral disease?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Ni ani eji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli?

english: Twisted or mosaic patterns on leaves are often caused by yam viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like aphids. These viruses weaken the plant and cause it to grow smaller tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato helai ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mfoniri ni etsake loo mosaic ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: How can I prevent plant diseases from spreading from one yam mound to another?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ahe helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kɛjɛ ŋmeii akuu kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: You can stop diseases by planting healthy, disease-free seed yams, removing infected plants from the farm quickly, and cleaning your farm tools regularly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa hela kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe tsemɔ daa

english: Why do my yams start rotting fast after I dig them up with cuts on their skin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo lɛ ni pilamɔ ko yɔɔ ehewolo nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When farm tools cut or scratch the skin of a yam, germs and fungi enter through the open wound. Smooth, uninjured yams can last for months in a cool, ventilated barn.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔ mli nibii ŋmɔ loo amɛfo sweet potato hewolo lɛ, helai kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ amli. Atomɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni pilaaa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli.

english: Can yams rot if I leave them in the ground for too long instead of harvesting them?
ga: Ani ŋmeii baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ni abaakpa?

english: While soil acts as natural storage during the dry season, leaving yams buried once heavy rains return will cause them to sprout again or rot from excess water.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ, Shi kɛ́ oshi o-sweet potatoes lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ loo amɛgboi kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli.

english: Does harvesting yams bit by bit affect how fresh they taste when cooked?
ga: Ani sweet potatoes ni akpaa yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ saa bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo ha kɛ́ ahoo amɛ?

english: Harvesting yams in batches ensures you always bring fresh, moist tubers to the kitchen or market, preventing them from drying out or changing texture in storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni oookpa yɛ kui amli lɛ haa okɛ tubers heei ni mli efɔ baa shĩa loo jara nɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekagbi loo etsake bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How can a single farmer manage harvesting a large field of thousands of yams?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafonyo kome pɛ anyɛ akpa rai akpei abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ mli?

english: Large farms are best managed by harvesting in small batches over time or by organizing communal farm labor with neighbors to share the heavy digging workload.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔji wuji anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ kɛ akutsoŋbii koni amɛja jatsu ni ji ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time to bring in hired labor to help me dig my yams?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aŋɔ nitsulɔi ni baaye abua ni atsa ŋmeii?

english: It is best to bring in extra help when the soil is dry enough to work easily but before it becomes baked too hard, allowing your team to dig tubers cleanly without damage.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobi yelikɛbuamɔ kroko beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii shi dani ebaashã waa tsɔ. Enɛ baaha okuu lɛ anyɛ atsa ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my new young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops produce very small yields when I plant seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to build large fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee aduawai wuji loo bulbs.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do wild weeds growing around my farm actually harm the growth of my crops?
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te miŋmɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops, effectively starving them and providing shelter for destructive crop pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Hɔmɔ ni yeɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ. ni amɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahi.

english: Why do my pepper crop leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a natural survival trick where plants shrink their leaf surface area to prevent water from evaporating into the air too quickly.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akaho oya tsɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before fruits can even grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or watering is irregular, as extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents flowers from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I have to construct wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy needed to develop large tubers underground while preventing ground rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills air spaces in the soil with water, which smothers the cassava roots by cutting off air and encouraging soil-dwelling fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ teeɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants look chewed up with small brown waste inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing stem of the maize plant to feed on fresh foliage, slowing down the plant's growth.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes twisting and puckering into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and puckered leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread leaf curl viruses, preventing normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsilɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Koni akɛtsi tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves stay dark green so the plant can grow strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the tops of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Checking the middle funnel of the corn plant early and applying organic neem extract or recommended control measures stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ekpaa ŋmãa lɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass (mulching) keeps the root area cool and moist.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ naa piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha tsei lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce a big harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants get dark spots and wither during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rain splashes soil containing fungal spores onto the lower leaves, causing leaf blight. Plucking off the lowest leaves and keeping the soil covered with mulch reduces splash-back and disease.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. kɛ blight hela baa Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni sɛɛkuu kɛ helai aba shi.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly and look weak when there are weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ jwɛi ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal food, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting gives your crops all the resources they need to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do some crops like plantain produce food continuously while my cocoa tree only bears fruit during specific months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ niyenii be fɛɛ be lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji komɛi pɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees rely on seasonal changes in rainfall and temperature to flower and set pods all at once, whereas crops like plantains produce new stems continuously, allowing harvests throughout the year if watered properly.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ be mli tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii shikome. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii heei be fɛɛ be. Abaanyɛ akpa lɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ awo nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant cassava, why can I leave it in the ground for months without harvesting, but my vegetables spoil in a few days?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa Mɛni hewɔ mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni mikpaaa ŋmãa? Shi ani mi-vegetables lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli?

english: Cassava is a root crop that uses the soil as natural storage, keeping the tubers fresh underground until you dig them up. Vegetables are soft above-ground fruits and leaves containing high water, making them rot quickly once ripe.
ga: Cassava ji tuber ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe. Ha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi obaatsa amɛ. Aduawai ji aduawai kɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Egboɔ oya kɛji aho lɛ.

english: How long does a rubber tree take before it yields latex, and why can't I harvest it as quickly as maize?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani rɔbɔt tsei feɔ latɛs? Ni mɛni hewɔ akpaaa lɛ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rubber trees are deep-rooted woody perennials that need about six to seven years to mature and develop thick bark capable of producing latex, while maize is a fast-growing annual crop that completes its whole life cycle in just three to four months.
ga: Rɔba tsei ji tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛheɔ afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni mli tse ni baanyɛ afee ŋmeii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ji tso ko ni daa afi daa afi ni gbeɔ ewala be fɛɛ naa yɛ nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa trees require expensive spraying for diseases while cassava grows easily without spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ he hiaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo ni akɛ tsofa shwieee nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are sweet and delicate, making them easy targets for pests like mirids and fungi like black pod. Cassava leaves and roots contain natural bitter compounds that naturally repel most insects and diseases, saving you money on chemicals.
ga: Cocoa pods lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai babaoo yɛ cassava baai kɛ shishifãi amli. ni haa shika baa shi yɛ tsofai ahe

english: Why do my maize plants need fresh fertilizer every planting season while fruit trees don't need it as often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa ŋmãa hee daa be mli ni mi aduawai tsei lɛ he ehiaaa lɛ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Maize has shallow roots that quickly drain nutrients from the topsoil during its short life. Tree crops have deep root systems that reach far underground to collect stored nutrients and water over many years.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ ewala be kukuoo lɛ mli. Tsei yɛ shishifãi ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛbua niyenii kɛ nu ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do broad-leaf crops like sweet potato help me save money on clearing weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ sweet potatoes lɛ baaha mikɛ shika akafite yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines spread fast across the ground and produce wide leaves that create thick shade, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds so they cannot sprout.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up or dry out during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains drop or fold their large leaves during dry weather as a self-defense mechanism to prevent water from evaporating, helping the main stem survive until rain returns.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai wuji lɛ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off during high heat without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress that damages flower pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo haomɔ ni fiteɔ pollen lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have natural bacteria in their roots, which take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, enriching the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii Koni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What crop features should I look for if I want a farm that gives me regular income without high expenses on inputs?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ matao kɛji miitao ŋmɔ ni haa shika daa ni nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo babaoo bɛ mli?

english: Look for hardy perennial crops like cassava or papaya that adapt well to local soil, resist local pests naturally, and produce food continuously rather than requiring fresh seeds and clearing every few months.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni wa, ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei loo papaya. ni kɛ ehe kpãa shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Adebɔɔ naa lɛ, enyɛɔ eshiɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni amɛfee niyenii daa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ dumɔwui heei baatsu nii ni amɛjie amɛ daa nyɔji fioo.

english: What does it actually mean when someone says a crop is grown organically?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ?

english: A crop is organic when it is grown naturally without using manufactured chemical fertilizers, weedkillers, or synthetic pest sprays. Farmers use natural plant food like animal manure and pest deterrents like neem leaf extracts to keep the soil and food healthy.
ga: Abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ amɛji nɔ ni wala bɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai ni afee ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuuu nii. tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofa ni akɛfee nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi Okwaafoi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem baa mli nu tsuɔ nii. Koni shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Can I use crushed neem leaves to protect my vegetable crops from insect pests instead of bought chemicals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai?

english: Yes, neem leaves contain a natural bitter chemical that deters insects from eating your crop and disrupts their growth. Boiling or soaking crushed neem leaves in water creates a natural spray that repels pests without leaving harmful chemical residues on your produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa yɛ neem baai lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye onibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Neem baai ni atswa lɛ ni oooshã loo okɛwo nu mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi ni eshiuuu tsofa ko ni eshwɛ yɛ onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Will adding chicken manure to my field work as well as chemical fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Ani mikɛ tsina ŋmei baafata miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ he, ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baafata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Yes, chicken manure provides rich nutrients like nitrogen that feed crops naturally. While chemical fertilizers feed plants instantly, manure releases its nutrients slowly over time and improves the soil's ability to hold water during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo tamɔ nitrogen, ni ji nɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ, shi Manure jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiofio. Beni be hoɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up into little tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water to the air. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the sun goes down and the air cools off.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green growth. When food in the soil is low, the plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Beni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil. Even with heavy rain, your crops remain small because the surrounding weeds are consuming most of the plant food first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibioo yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ahewɔ. Abaaye tsei niyenii babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do cocoa farmers plant plantain suckers on the same plot with new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cassava and maize together on one piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is ready to harvest in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes up to a year. Planting them together allows you to harvest maize early without interrupting the cassava, making full use of your land and rain season.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni ekɛ afi tsuɔ nii lɛ. Hefatalɔi dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa oya ni ogbalaaa ŋmãa lɛ naa. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do pests attack my cowpea farm mostly after the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo beni tsei lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: The flowers and young pods of cowpea produce a sweet scent and high protein content that attract insects like pod borers. The pests gather during flowering because it is the easiest time for them to find soft food for themselves and their young.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ he ŋɔɔ ni protein babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ pod borers. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ejaakɛ be nɛɛ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha amɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii ni mli jɔ amɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ amɛbii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots, or when the soil stays waterlogged for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe. aloo be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why does my maize produce small cobs with missing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: Maize needs good wind and enough water for pollen from the top flowers (tassels) to fall onto the silks of the cobs. If the plants are too crowded, or if they suffer from dry weather during flowering, pollination fails, leaving empty spots on the cob.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa koni eha pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ (tassels) lɛ amli lɛ abagbee ŋmãa siliki lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ enaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Polin lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ko baa yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating my stored maize grains after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni ato lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply quickly when grains are stored with too much moisture or kept in open containers. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags or clean, sealed drums starves the pests of air and prevents them from breeding.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo oya kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo awo tsɛnsii ni agbele mli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto vacuum bag loo bin ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafɔ bii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Keeping weeds under control and spraying with natural neem oil solutions can help protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot from the bottom while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛmiidara yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rotting at the bottom of a tomato fruit, called blossom end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil. This is usually caused by irregular watering rather than a disease, so keeping the soil consistently moist prevents it.
ga: Rot ni yɔɔ tomato aduawai lɛ shishi Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be moŋ fe hela. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Why does my yam vine dry up and turn brown before the harvest season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn brown and dry up early, it is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose. Planting disease-free seed tubers and avoiding planting yams in the same piece of land every year helps keep the crop healthy.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi oya Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Dumɔwui ni helai bɛ mli ni aduɔ kɛ sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to plant my crop seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them across the farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows makes it much easier to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your field. It also ensures that every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to a better harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni abaanyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ekwɛɔ hu koni tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛ nikpamɔ kpakpa baa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my cassava plants when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi cassava tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Young cassava plants have short roots and cannot fight against fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Weeding early gives the cassava roots space to grow big and strong without competition.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɛ kukuji ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off the stem without producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects called flower thrips. Protecting the crop from pests during the flowering period ensures the blossoms turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tutua tsei lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fɔfɔi thrips. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to grow healthy vegetables without buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds water well, feels soft and crumbly in your hand, and contains living earthworms. Mixing decomposed plant waste or dry animal manure into your soil adds natural fertility without relying heavily on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ekɛ nu toɔ jogbaŋŋ Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nine mli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka yɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni egbo loo kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ebɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central growing part of the maize plant (the whorl) and feed on young leaves, which can reduce your harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ fã ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant does not get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering during hot weather, causing the lower cell tissue of the fruit to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛnaa nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ mli fãa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from heat. The plant is not dead; it is simply conserving energy until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eji hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba kɛkɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they lack enough water or nutrients to feed full pods. Additionally, flowers only turn into pods if they are pollinated by tiny insects called midges.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛfɔfɔi lɛ. Fɔfɔi hu feɔ pods kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ wo amɛ pollen.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural nitrogen fertilizer behind for heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: Signs of low-nutrient soil include pale or yellowish leaves on previous crops, weak stems, very slow plant growth, and smaller harvest yields compared to previous years.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ he ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ anɔ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ tsei ni daaa blɛoo waa. ni kpamɔ lɛ hu faaa kɛ akɛto afi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra young stems growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain lɛ baai lɛ

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces the main stem to share its water and nutrients. Keeping only 2 or 3 healthy suckers ensures the main plant grows a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and stake my yam vines on wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking holds the vines up off the hot ground, giving them sunlight while protecting them from leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tso lɛ ni aaawo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Koni eha amɛ hulu la kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ekɛtsi foliary helai anaa.

english: How does spreading dry grass on the soil around my crops help them grow?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?
