english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool, reduces water evaporation, and prevents weed seeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane mli?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plant can drink before the hot afternoon sun hits. It also allows wet leaves to dry quickly during the day, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ anu nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa baa ni efɔ lɛ hu ni egbiɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but producing almost no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko kwraa bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of flowering. Balancing the fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my sorghum leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is sorghum's natural way of saving water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and wind, keeping moisture inside so it can survive dry spells.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmãa tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why does my rice look pale and weak even though the field is completely full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ? Ani nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ?

english: Even though rice loves water, crop roots still need air to breathe. If water remains too deep without draining periodically, the roots suffocate and cannot absorb nutrients properly from the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi tso shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ lolo koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ ni ajieee nu lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when the plant feels stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or damage from insects like thrips. To protect itself, the plant drops flowers it cannot afford to feed.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni anyɛɛɛ aye nɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers grow above ground, but the nuts form deep inside the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: Groundnut plants have a unique growth habit where, after yellow flowers are pollinated, they grow long stalks called pegs that push themselves down into the soil to safely form peanuts underground.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ dalɛ su krɛdɛɛ ko. Beni ekɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the same line?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ line kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on all their leaves to manufacture food. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes keeps them exposed to the sun and protects them from soil rot, resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai wuji.

english: I found small round lumps attached to the roots of my soybean plants—is this a disease that will damage my farm?
ga: Miyana ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ kokroo. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ soybean shishifãi lɛ ahe Ani hela ni baakpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ nɛ?

english: Those lumps are called root nodules and are actually a sign of a healthy crop. Friendly soil bacteria live in those nodules, capturing nitrogen gas from the air to fertilize the soybean plant naturally.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ shishifãi ni diɛŋtsɛ Eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he okadi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ hiɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli. Emɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha soybean tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my onion plants making large green leaves above ground but failing to form fat bulbs under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi enyɛɛɛ efee fat bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Onions shift their energy from growing leaves to building bulbs based on daylight length and age. Applying fertilizer too late in the season forces the plant to keep making leaves instead of swelling into bulbs.
ga: Sabolai tsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ dalɛ mli kɛyaa bulb feemɔ mli yɛ hulu la lɛ sɛɛtsɛmɔ kɛ ewala shihilɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aya nɔ awo baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefu ni etsɔ bulb.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow when I plant them in a open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade trees or plantains to protect them from scorching sun while their root systems develop during the first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess dampness and shade. Weeding your field and pruning leafy branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ shade mli fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older leaves to nourish the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot lets soil pests and diseases build up over time. Rotating crops starves out these pests and prevents the soil from running out of specific nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ baaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ, ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii komɛi ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and slender but produce small yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of putting energy into growing fruits, they stretch upward to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii Moŋ lɛ, ekpã mli koni eshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches if I leave all the suckers growing around the main stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Ni kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he hu?

english: Suckers act like extra mouths feeding from the main root system. Removing most suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the mother plant to send all its energy into making a large fruit bunch.
ga: Suckers lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabu krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso nyɛ lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates cassava roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil. Without air, the roots die and easily rot due to fungal infection.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ gboiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot days.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants face heat stress, water shortages, or improper nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni faaa loo niyenii ni esaaa Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops when there is plenty of rainwater for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even with enough rain, weeds steal essential soil nutrients and root space from your crops. They also attract insects and plant diseases that can spread to your crops.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ, Jwɛi hu juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Egbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii amli lɛ hu.

english: Officer, why do my young cocoa plants burn and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a natural canopy that protects young cocoa trees from excessive heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni ŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ baa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Officer, why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to grow up on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ? Koni eda yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight to make food, which grows bigger tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhoɔ nii yɛ nɔ. Tubers lɛ baadara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Officer, why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry, when temperatures become extremely high, or if there is too much chemical nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying organic compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛji tsofa ni ji nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ organic compost afata he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ? Be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen fertilizer or sitting in waterlogged soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top leaves to keep growing, so feeding the soil helps restore full color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Officer, why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken rotten spots at the bottom while they are still on the plant?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It often happens when watering is uneven—either too dry or flooded—preventing the plant's roots from pulling up calcium from the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Ekolɛ edɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Etsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Officer, why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Cowpea plants produce their own nitrogen in the soil. If you add extra nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow big green leaves instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Officer, why do my fresh peppers rot and spoil so quickly after I pack them into sacks for market?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi chili heei lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvested peppers generate heat and sweat. When packed tightly in unventilated plastic sacks, trapped moisture creates bacteria that causes fast rotting. Using breathable wooden crates or net sacks keeps them dry and cool.
ga: Pepper ni akpa lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa baa. Kɛ akɛwo plastic kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ feɔ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oya. Kɛ́ okɛ adeka loo mesh kotoku ni haa mumɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehe agbi ni edɔ.

english: Officer, how do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers don't become hard like wood?
ga: Te onukpai lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei koni ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ akafee nɔ ni wa tamɔ tso?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months. If left in the ground too long after maturity, the plant converts its soft starch into tough, woody fibers that make the tubers difficult to cook.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ ashweremɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa

english: Officer, why are my plantain trees easily falling over during light storms even when they have green leaves?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ amɛ moŋ? Mɔ ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and microscopic worms called nematodes often eat away the root system underground. Without strong roots anchoring the base, the heavy plant collapses easily under wind or rain.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shishifã ni mli wa ko bɛ ni hiɛ shishitoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ fiteɔ tsei ni tsii oya.

english: Officer, why do I see small holes chewed into the funnels of my young maize leaves early in the morning?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu bibioo ko? Akɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ funnel lɛ shwieɔ shi leebi.

english: This damage is caused by young armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft, inner leaves of the maize plant. Inspecting early and applying natural neem oil or targeted pesticide directly into the leaf funnel controls them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ baawo baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye amɛnɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive the heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when temperatures get too high or when the plants do not get enough water. It can also happen if insects like bees are not visiting the flowers to pollinate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa fɔfɔi amli koni amɛyawo amɛmli.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient plants need for green leaf growth. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy dark green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ diŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Will my land get tired if I plant cassava on the same farm every year?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi?

english: Yes, cassava feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest will exhaust the soil and yield smaller tubers over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo he ko ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aba yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize is planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stems and small cobs with very few grains.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on high wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight. Staking helps the leaves capture more light to make food, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, shady, and overly humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air flow and removing infected pods helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ, loo hela ko ni kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: How do I know the exact time my fresh maize is ready to harvest for eating?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa hee lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest fresh when the silk threads at the tip of the cob turn dark brown and dry, and pressing a kernel releases a milky fluid rather than clear water.
ga: Efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ŋmãa lɛ ehee beni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ naagbee lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ anyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, nu ni tamɔ mliki jeɔ kpo yɛ nu ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows clear signs when it matures, usually around 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and small cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the plant where the roots are swelling.
ga: Cassava baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni ŋmeii bibii miije kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi he ni shishifãi lɛ miifu lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during intense heat to conserve moisture and protect the plant from drying out. It is a natural coping mechanism, showing that the plant is under heat stress and needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpeeɔ naagbai anaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ latsaa he haomɔ shishi, ni nu he miihia amɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady and using balanced fertilizer helps the plant hold flowers to grow fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni fa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my corn crop turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or root damage from excess water. The plant automatically moves remaining nitrogen from old bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with small ears when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ shi kɛ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress forces the plant to spend its energy stretching upward for light rather than growing thick stalks and big ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛkpãa ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ená la. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ ha nɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tuhi nguahi nɛ a hwɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers heavily right after the first rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to moisture changes. The onset of rain after a dry period signals to the tree that conditions are right to reproduce, triggering a flush of flowers that will turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tsake. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ tsei akɛ shihilɛi lɛ sa kɛha fɔmɔ. Wo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do the outer leaves of my cabbage turn brown and dry at the edges during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry leaf edges, often called tip burn, happen when the plant cannot pull up enough water and calcium fast enough during rapid growth or dry spells, causing the delicate edges of the leaf to dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni egbi loo nɔ ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni shãa Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya loo be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: How does harvesting my maize too early affect the quality of my grain and my sales?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ saa mi ŋmãa lɛ he kɛ jarayeli he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harvesting maize before the grains are fully dry leaves them soft and high in moisture, which leads to mold growth and rotting during storage, reducing the price buyers are willing to pay.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa dani ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it better for me to harvest my tomatoes all at once or in batches if I want to get a good market price?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpa tomatoi lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mafo mli kui kɛji miisumɔ ni maná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting in batches as fruits turn semi-ripe allows you to extend your sales window, prevent damage from overripe fruits rotting in the field, and sell continuously to catch better market prices.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ kui amli beni aduawai lɛ eshɛ fã lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ jarayeli samflɛ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa hiɛ. Tsi nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite yɛ ŋmɔji amli. ni amɛya nɔ amɛhɔ̃ɔ koni amɛná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: If I plant my vegetables at the exact same time as every other farmer in my village, why do I make less money?
ga: Kɛji miduɔ aduawai yɛ be kome mli kɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ shika nɔ?

english: When everyone plants and harvests at the same time, the market gets flooded with crops at once. This oversupply forces prices down, whereas staggering your planting dates helps you sell when crop supply is lower and prices are higher.
ga: Beni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ duɔ nii ni ekpaa nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ Kulɛ jara lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shikome. Nɛkɛ nibii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa jara baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni oootsake lɛ baaye abua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and does this mean my crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry periods to reduce water loss. The plant is not dead; it is simply conserving energy and water while keeping its tubers safe and growing underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eji hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense direct sunlight and hot winds. They need shade trees to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the leaves from burning while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting shoots while they are still lying in my dry barn after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ be mli ni amɛkã mi ŋmɔ ni egbi lɛ mli lolo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally enter a rest period called dormancy after harvest. Once that internal clock finishes after a few months, heat and air humidity signal to the yam that it is time to grow a new vine, even if it hasn't been planted in soil yet.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni nakai mligbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ gbe naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tso hee. Kɛji akɛ aduko lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo po.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like thrips or mites feeding on the leaf undersides, or by a viral disease spread by insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ loo kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekadara bɔ ni sa lɛ mli.

english: Why does that purple-flowered weed keep growing right next to my maize and making the maize turn yellow and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni ji purple lɛ miida yɛ emasɛi lɛ? mi ŋmãa Ni eha ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: That weed is likely Striga, a parasitic plant that attaches its roots to your maize roots underground. It steals water and nutrients directly from the maize plant, especially in poor soils low in nitrogen.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa o-corn shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nitrogen faaa yɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot and smell bad underground when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni wɔnáa nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded or overly wet, oxygen cannot reach the roots. The roots starve for air and drown, creating ideal conditions for fungal and bacterial water-molds in the soil to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu loo edɔ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. This stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to abort the flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afolɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very dark green leaves and standing tall, but the cobs remain very small and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ? Shi ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes maize build lots of leaves and stems, but without enough phosphorus and potassium in the soil, the plant lacks the right nutrients to form full, heavy grain cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ afee baai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Shi kɛji akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaha amɛfee dumɔwui ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why am I advised to cut down the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stool instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain titri lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: Every extra sucker attached to the main plantain stem drinks water and steals food from the mother plant. Removing excess suckers forces the plant to send all its energy into producing one large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi fɛɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Maize leaves roll up inward as a defense mechanism to hide their surface area from the hot sun, reducing the amount of water evaporating from the plant during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛtee ŋwɛigbɛ he lɛ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop producing fruit and dry up when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants require consistent soil moisture and moderate temperatures to form fruit. During the dry season, high heat and dry winds stress the plant, causing flowers to drop off before they can develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: How does a lack of water affect how my vegetable crops grow in the field?
ga: Te nu ni bɛ lɛ saa aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Without enough water, plants cannot pull essential nutrients from the soil. This leads to stunted growth, yellow leaves, early flower loss, and very small or low-quality harvests.
ga: Kɛji nu faaa lɛ Tsei hu nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa edaaa, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni fɔfɔi lɛ hu fiteɔ mra. kɛ ŋmaa bibii loo ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Can too much direct sunlight damage my vegetable crops during the hot months?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, excessive direct sunlight and heat can sunburn fruit surfaces and scorch leaves, making the plants weak and unable to make food efficiently.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã aduawai kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it possible for me to harvest tomatoes every month of the year in Ghana without waiting for the rainy season?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafolɔ tomato daa nyɔŋ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli yɛ Ghana ni mimɛɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, by using irrigation systems to supply water regularly and protective structures like shade nets, you can keep soil conditions ideal for tomatoes to produce fruit continuously all 12 months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu haa daa kɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ shade netting lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ koni tomato aya nɔ awo yibii nyɔji 12.

english: What happens to my soil if I try to farm on the same piece of land continuously for 12 months?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ matsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be nyɔji 12?

english: Farming nonstop consumes soil nutrients quickly and encourages pest buildup. To farm year-round successfully, you need to add organic manure regularly and rotate different crop families.
ga: Okwaayeli ni akpaaa lɛ yeɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ oya ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni eye omanye yɛ okwaayeli mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ organic fertilizer afata he daa ni okɛtsake tsei awekui srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ.

english: How can I keep water in my soil for a longer time when there is no rainfall?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dried grass, leaves, or straw (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from reaching the dirt, which stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo jwɛi (mulching) baaha tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ la oya.

english: Why are the yellow flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛyibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off—a problem called flower drop—when temperatures become too hot during the daytime or when the plant experiences sudden water shortages, preventing pollination.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi - Naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi - be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa nu ni faaa trukaa. Koni akɛtsi pollination naa

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering during dry and hot periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What is a shade house, and how does it help crops grow better than in an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji shade ŋmɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: A shade house is a simple structure covered with mesh netting that filters harsh sunlight, reduces heat stress, and keeps severe pests away, allowing sensitive crops like tomatoes to grow smoothly.
ga: Shade greenhouse ji tsũ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi eha he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni naa wa lɛ anaa Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tomato prices in Ghanaian markets go so high during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato jara wa waa yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Most farmers rely only on rainfall to grow crops. When the rains stop, very few farmers have tomatoes to sell, causing high market demand and low supply, which drives prices up.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ kɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa Okwaafoi lɛ yɛ tomato fioo ko pɛ ni amɛbaahɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ haa jarayeli nibii babaoo taoɔ ni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ hu faaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees or food crops like plantains protect young cocoa from sunburn and help keep the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning black and looking as if fire burned them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This scorching is usually caused by small insects called mirids (or capsids). They suck sap from stems and leaves and inject toxic saliva that leaves dark, burnt-looking spots on the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (loo capsids) lɛ kɛ shãa nɛɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai amli lɛ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi diji lɛ woɔ mli.

english: Why should I prune or cut off extra branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo majie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive shoots (suckers) and opens the canopy to air and sunlight. Sunlight and proper airflow reduce humidity inside the tree, preventing fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii (tsei) ni egbeleɔ tsei lɛ anaa kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Tsi fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ naa

english: Why do many small cocoa flowers drop off my tree without ever growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ mitso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny midges to pollinate them, as well as enough water and plant food. Drought, lack of soil nutrients, or absence of pollinators cause the plant to shed unpollinated or weak flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ gbɔmɔtsei bibii kɛha pollination, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo fɔfɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Overcrowding makes trees compete heavily with each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. It also creates a dark, damp environment where diseases spread quickly, resulting in lower yields per tree.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ hu baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ tso kome mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed new green leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aba.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even if I feed my field with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli po?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than crops. They steal the added fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops before your plants get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. dani otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right before or during a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer off the field or buries it too deep underground before the crop roots can absorb it, wasting your money and nutrient input.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo efuɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa shika kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge tall leaves above ground but very small stems under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ? Shi ani tso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of sending food down into the tubers to grow big roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛya shi kɛya bulb lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dry plant stems on the ground instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi tsei ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry plant matter creates mulch that covers the soil, holding in moisture during hot days and rotting into natural organic food for the next crop cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni amɛgbi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does it take so many years for agricultural researchers to give us new crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi afii babaoo dani amɛha wɔ tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ?

english: Developing a new crop variety usually takes 6 to 8 years because researchers have to grow and test multiple generations of plants across different weather seasons to ensure traits like high yield or disease resistance stay strong and stable before releasing seeds to farmers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi heei ni afeɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 ejaakɛ esa akɛ niiamlitaolɔi akwɛ tsei ayinɔi babaoo ni amɛka amɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli. Enɛ ji koni akwɛ akɛ sui tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo loo helai ni nyɛɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani ajie dumɔwui lɛ aha okwaafoi.

english: Why do hybrid seeds give me a bigger harvest than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing two strong parent plants to combine their best traits for high yield, but if you save seeds from that harvest, the special combination breaks down, resulting in weaker plants and lower yield the following year.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni he wa ni akɛfoɔ mli koni akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afee ekome kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo. Shi kɛji ohere dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do researchers make a crop variety that does not easily get attacked by diseases?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni niiamlitaolɔi afee tsei srɔtoi ni helai bɛ mli?

english: Scientists search for rare plants that naturally survive the disease, then repeatedly cross-breed them with high-yielding crops over many years until they create a new seed that carries both the disease-fighting traits and good yield.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi na tso ko ni anaaa lɛ ni jɛɔ hela naa foi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tsɔ mli shii abɔ. Yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ amɛwo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ sui ni kɛ helai wuɔ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo fɛɛ.

english: What does it mean when you tell me a seed is an 'improved variety'?
ga: Mɛni otsɔɔ beni okɛɛ mi akɛ dumɔwu lɛ ji ‘Improved variety’ lɛ.

english: An improved variety is a seed that plant breeders have spent years selecting and refining so that it grows faster, produces more food, or handles tough weather better than traditional, unselected seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ afii babaoo halaa ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Wo niyenii babaoo loo okɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa akpee naa jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui ni ahalaaa

english: Why do some cassava varieties mature in six months while others take over a year to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different internal genetic clocks; early-maturing types are bred to store starch in their roots quickly, while older, late-maturing varieties spend more time growing stems and leaves before swelling their roots.
ga: Kasava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ mligbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋmɛlɛtswai srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛkɛ starch ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni eda ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛduɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai dani amɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees taking five years to produce pods while hybrid cocoa starts bearing in under three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ he afii enumɔ dani ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ? yɛ be mli ni kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ afii etɛ mli.

english: Hybrid cocoa was developed by plant breeders specifically to mature rapidly and flower early, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties naturally require more years to establish their canopy before producing fruit.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni fee cocoa hybrids lɛ titri kɛha amɛdalɛ oya kɛ fɔfɔi ni baa mra. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do some of my crops survive a long dry period while others wilt and die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties are bred with traits like deeper root systems or leaves that trap moisture, allowing them to pull water from deep underground during dry spells while weaker varieties lose water rapidly.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi koni amɛná sui tamɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety advertised on the radio will actually perform well on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwu hee ko ni atswa he adafi yɛ redio nɔ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crop varieties are developed for specific climates and soil types, so a seed bred for the wet forest zone may not yield well in drier areas unless it was bred to tolerate lower rainfall.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ kɛha kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Ja atsɔse amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ nugbɔ ni baa shi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant the same seed on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same seed drains specific soil nutrients that the crop relies on and allows targeted pests to build up in the soil, which slows plant growth over time.
ga: Dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsei hiɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtaoɔ amɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I make my crops yield bigger fruits just by adding fertilizer, or does it depend on the seed I buy?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii wuji kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ? Aloo edamɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yield depends on both; the seed's breeding sets the limit on how big or plentiful the crop can possibly grow, while fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to reach that full potential.
ga: Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ damɔ nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui afɔmɔ kɛ husu toɔ bɔ ni tso ko baanyɛ adara loo edara aha lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does rain spoil my harvested cocoa beans if I leave them outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ fiteɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Moisture from rain encourages mold and harmful bacteria to grow quickly on wet cocoa beans. This spoils their natural flavor and causes them to fail quality tests at buying centers.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli baa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ kookoo yibii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei lɛ ni ehaa eshɛɛɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he kaa lɛ he yɛ nihɔɔmɔ he lɛ.

english: How many days does it usually take for cocoa beans to dry completely under the sun?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ kwraa yɛ hulu la shishi?

english: Under normal sunny weather, cocoa beans placed on raised bamboo mats usually take about 7 to 10 days to dry down to the safe moisture level required by produce buyers.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Cocoa ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani egbiɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Can I dry my harvested cocoa beans inside my house when it rains heavily outside?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shia mli kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ kpo nɔ?

english: Drying cocoa inside an enclosed room without proper sunlight and strong airflow leads to trapped moisture, which causes mold growth and bad odors instead of proper drying.
ga: Kookoo ni agbiɔ yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã mli ni hulu la ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I check with my hands if my cocoa beans are fully dry and ready to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ minine akwɛ kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Well-dried cocoa beans will make a crisp crackling sound when squeezed together in your hands, and the skin will crack open cleanly without feeling soft or damp.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ okɛ onine ŋmɔ mli. Ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fãa he tse ni enuuu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What happens to the quality of my cocoa beans if I dry them directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji migbi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Drying beans directly on the soil exposes them to dirt, stones, moisture from the earth, and animals, which contaminates the crop and lowers the price buyers will pay.
ga: Beans ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa muji, tɛi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa amɛ. kɛ kooloi srɔtoi Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it bad if my cocoa beans dry too quickly under extreme heat?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mi-kokoo yibii lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa shishi?

english: Yes, drying too fast hardens the outer shell and traps natural acids inside the bean, leaving the cocoa tasting sour and reducing its market value.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ egbi oya tsɔ lɛ, ehaa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli waɔ ni emɔɔ adebɔɔ mli acid ni yɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: High humidity and continuous rain spread Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, wet conditions and attacks cocoa pods if the farm lacks sunshine and airflow.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. ni amɛtutua kookoo ŋmeii kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their leaves when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during severe heat to reduce water loss and protect their main stems, which is why planting tall shade trees helps keep them cool and healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛnáa hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa beans change from purple to dark brown as they dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ purple kɛyaa brown ni mli edɔ kɛji amɛgbi lɛ?

english: As water leaves the beans during drying, oxygen reacts with natural compounds inside them, removing bitterness and turning the beans to their rich brown chocolate color.
ga: Beni nu shĩɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome. Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsokolate ni mli tse.

english: Why do I need to ferment my cocoa beans before taking them to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the seed inside so it cannot sprout, loosens the sweet pulp surrounding the beans, and starts the development of the true chocolate flavor.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gboiɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkakwɛ̃, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔi tsokolate ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ namɔ.

english: Why does my cassava take up to a year to yield while maize is ready in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ afi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stores its energy slowly in thick roots deep underground over 9 to 12 months, whereas maize builds seeds quickly above ground, completing its life cycle in 3 to 4 months.
ga: Cassava toɔ hewalɛ fiofio yɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa woɔ dumɔwui oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaagbe eshihilɛ be lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely and turn brown at the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When yam vines die back, it is the natural signal that the plant has finished moving all its leaves' energy into the underground tuber, meaning the yam is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tso lɛ gboɔ lɛ No ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ etso lɛ baa hewalɛ fɛɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn pale yellow when the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their green color and power to grow heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli, ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to loosen the soil before planting groundnuts instead of planting into hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie sũ lɛ dani adu ŋmeii moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers push themselves back into the soil after pollination to grow nuts, so loose soil makes it easy for the pegs to dive underground and expand.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ pollination sɛɛ koni amɛdu ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛmli baagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward to reduce their exposed surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out under hot sun.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers on my bean plants falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when exposed to sudden drought or severe heat stress because they lack enough water to support developing seeds.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛkɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui adalɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn black and rotten at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when the roots do not get consistent water from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that get scorched under direct sunlight; big trees act as protective umbrellas that shield them and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmeii ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks that produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni egbɔjɔ, ni no haa tsei bibii baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do wild weeds grow and multiply much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ oya fe tsei ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built with strong roots to aggressively snatch up available water, sunlight, and soil food before domesticated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni wa ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni yɔɔ dani tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ shia lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my fertilizer and topsoil after I apply it to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates surface runoff that easily strips away exposed topsoil and plant nutrients. Creating soil ridges across slopes or keeping cover crops on your land slows down the water so it soaks into the ground instead of sweeping your topsoil away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa, ni no jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii lɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ni ooofee yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ afee mlɛo ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I leave dry plant waste on my farm ground instead of burning it before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and leaves the bare earth vulnerable to hot sun and heavy rain. Leaving plant waste to rot naturally enriches the soil with nutrients, keeps moisture in the root zone, and protects topsoil from being washed away.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei amli jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: When roots sit in waterlogged soil for too long, they cannot breathe. Your crops will show yellowing leaves, slow down their growth, or wilt even though the ground is completely wet, eventually causing the stems near the base to rot.
ga: Kɛ shishifãi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔɔ baai ŋmɔŋ. shwieɔ shi loo egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa moŋ Enɛ baaha yɛ naagbee lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Leaf curling during intense heat is a plant's natural coping mechanism to reduce water loss. The leaves roll inward to expose less surface area to the hot sun and trap moisture inside.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛkpeɔ naagbai anaa koni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and touch the ground when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally flexible and become top-heavy as fruit grows. Staking them with sturdy wooden sticks keeps the plants upright, preventing the leaves and fruit from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Etsiɔ baai kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the branches fight each other for sunlight and the roots compete for groundwater and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants that produce very small tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Niji lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ sũ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ bulb bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant tall maize and short pepper together on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kakadaji kɛ ŋmãa kukuji yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping can work well, but you must space the rows carefully. If the maize is too dense, it will block sunlight from reaching the shorter pepper plants, preventing them from flowering and fruiting properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ato ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmãa tsei kukuji lɛ ahe. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw moisture out of plant tissue. Placing it directly against the stem can burn the outer bark and kill the delicate feeding roots nearby.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ ni yeɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing on the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles feeding on the crop. Checking under the leaves early in the morning allows you to catch and manage pests before they destroy the whole leaf area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni eye ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense heat. It is the plant's natural defense to trap moisture inside until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu nii akɛ ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do cassava plants stay green and healthy during dry weather while my other crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi feɔ nakai lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gboɔ?

english: Cassava has very deep roots that reach water far underground, and it stores extra food in its thick tubers. This allows it to withstand long dry spells better than crops with shallow roots.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ amli Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ naa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to reach the light, which leaves them too weak to produce large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do I need to raise my yam vines on wooden stakes instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking gets the leaves off the hot ground and spreads them out to catch sunlight. More sunshine on the leaves gives the plant more energy to build large yams under the earth.
ga: Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la. Hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Flowers usually drop off when the weather is too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. The plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen food. The plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left from the older bottom leaves and sends it to nourish the new green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves curling up and turning sticky during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot and dry conditions attract tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that hide under leaves and suck out the sap. The sticky feeling is liquid left behind by these pests, causing the leaves to curl.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ mli. Henumɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nu ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shĩɔ yɛ sɛɛ. ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do experts tell me not to burn the dry grass on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the natural compost and living microbes that keep the soil fertile. Leaving dry grass to rot into the soil keeps the ground moist, cool, and rich in natural nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that capture food from the air and store it in their roots. When the season ends, that food stays in the soil and feeds the maize planted afterward.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha ŋmãa ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I test if the crop seeds I kept from last harvest are still alive before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo dani midu?

english: Wrap ten seeds in a moist cloth and keep it in a cool place for a few days. If seven or eight sprout, your seeds are strong and ready for field planting.
ga: Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ dumɔwui nyɔŋma he ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛji dumɔwui kpawo loo kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.
