english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops on land that has a lot of rocks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rocky ground prevents crop roots from growing deep to find water and nutrients. The stones also trap heat and do not hold water well, which can cause your crops to dry up and die quickly during hot weather.
ga: Tɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tɛi hu nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ dɔlɛ mli ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya ni amɛgboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant any crop I want anywhere on my farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. ni misumɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, every crop prefers specific soil conditions to do well. Some crops need deep, rich soil, while others can tolerate drier ground. Matching the right crop to the right land ensures a healthy harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsei fɛɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsei komɛi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi baanyɛ akpɛlɛ hei ni nu egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ to he ni sa lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What kind of soil is best if I want to plant root crops like yam or cassava?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei. Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Root crops need soft, deep, and loose soil without big rocks so their tubers can expand freely and grow large under the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi wuji bɛ mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi ŋmɔshi nibii. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some crops grow very well on my neighbor's farm but perform poorly on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even farms right next to each other can have different soil depth, rockiness, or moisture levels. Your neighbor's land might naturally suit that specific crop better than your land does.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. tɛ hewalɛ loo hulutsoo be srɔtoi Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe onɔ̃ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to have my farm land checked by an expert before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani aje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Having someone inspect the land helps you understand the soil depth, water drainage, and nutrient levels early, preventing you from wasting money and labor on a crop that cannot thrive there.
ga: Kɛ́ oha mɔ ko kwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni onu bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha, bɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shishi mra. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will dry out too fast during the farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya tsɔ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli?

english: Land with very sandy or rocky soil drains water extremely fast and dries out quickly, whereas dark soil rich in organic matter holds water much longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo tɛi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli nu hoɔ oya waa ni egbiɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛhaa onibii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is good for planting before I spend money to clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii? Dani obaafite shika ni okɛjie jɛmɛ?

english: You can check the land by digging sample holes in different spots to examine the soil depth, color, and texture. Soft, dark soil with few stones is usually a sign of good land for farming.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ bu ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni oootsu yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ nɔ. Koni akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tɛi fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ji he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli he okadi.

english: What happens to crop roots when the soil under the surface is too hard or full of stones?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ?

english: Hard or stony soil blocks roots from spreading out. This leaves the plant with a weak root system, making it stunted, unable to absorb nutrients, and easy for strong winds to knock over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ. tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa oya

english: If my land has many stones, is there any way I can still use it for farming?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi babaoo Ani gbɛi komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ matsɔ nɔ matsu nii lolo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can remove larger surface stones by hand and add compost to improve the soil, but heavily rocky land is better used for hardy tree crops or grazing rather than food crops that need deep soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ onine ajie tɛi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi hei ni tɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo loo kooloi alɛɛhei ni wa fe niyenii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain alone is not enough if the soil itself is poor or unsuitable. If the land lacks nutrients or is too rocky for roots to feed, the plant will remain weak and yellow despite the water.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo esaaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo tɛi babaoo yɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye lɛ, Tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbɔjɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nu mli po.

english: Why do the seeds I buy from the agricultural store yield more than the seeds I save from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought seeds are often hybrid varieties specially bred for high yield and disease resistance. Seeds saved from harvest lose these superior traits in the next generation, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa hu baa shi.

english: Why are my maize seeds failing to sprout after I planted them in the dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a warm environment and a steady supply of moisture to wake up and germinate. In dry soil, the seed remains dormant or dries out and dies before its root can emerge.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui hiɔ shi ni amɛhiɛɛɛ shi. Aloo egbiɔ ni egboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How does joining two branches together through grafting help my orange tree produce fruit faster?
ga: Te niji enyɔ ni mikɛwoɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-orange tso lɛ ni ewo yibii oya lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Grafting attaches a branch from an already mature, fruit-bearing tree onto a strong young rootstock. Because the branch comes from a mature parent, it tricks the plant into fruiting in two to three years instead of seven.
ga: Grafting kɛ tsei niji ni jɛ tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ fĩɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niji jɛɔ fɔlɔi ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ adɛŋ. no hewɔ lɛ elaka tso lɛ koni ewo yibii yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli yɛ afii kpawo najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow and curled leaves are usually a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings for planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo niji ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my crops die quickly whenever floodwater stays on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nu afua lɛ baahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to survive. When water covers the field for too long, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up air and food, which rots the roots and kills the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni boteɔ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects suddenly attack my crop leaves right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The rain causes crops to flush with tender new leaves, which are rich in food for insects. Warm and moist weather after rain also triggers insect eggs to hatch all at once.
ga: Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa ehei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kooloi aniyenii eyi mli obɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ hu haa kooloi bibii lɛ afɔ̃ shikome.

english: Can I put fresh dung from my chicken coop directly onto my young vegetable crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ tsina shĩa lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry dung produces intense heat and high ammonia levels as it decomposes, which will burn crop roots. It must be composted and left to dry for several weeks before adding it to the soil.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ haa dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ ammonia babaoo baa kɛji efite. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi otsii komɛi dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of specific nutrients like nitrogen out of the ground every season. Planting it continuously empties the soil of these exact nutrients unless you rotate crops or feed the soil.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ niyenii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful microbes in their roots to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the neighboring maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Planting too closely forces plants to fight over limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce smaller fruits and lower overall yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green and strong. Adding compost, poultry manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant will help it recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ wa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔji, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing lots of leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants grow heavy green leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas actually capture their own nitrogen from the air, so they need phosphorus rather than extra nitrogen fertilizers to produce pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ náa baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ fɔsfɔs kroko moŋ fe nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Curled leaves with yellowish mosaic patterns are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. You can protect your farm by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural extension officers.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ mosaic mfoniri ni ji ŋmɔŋ. Eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers instead of producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from small pests like thrips. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and providing shade during extremely hot periods helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips lɛ fite amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny soil pests like nematodes or stem weevils attack their root system, weakening their hold in the ground. Planting clean, treated suckers in fresh soil helps build strong roots that anchor the plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo stem weevils tutua shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi ni wa ni fiɔ tso lɛ shi lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up into the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves produce food for the plant, which makes the underground yam tubers grow much larger and healthier.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings dry up and die shortly after I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings suffer from transplant shock if moved directly into hot sun. Exposing them to outdoor sunlight gradually over a few days before planting and transplanting in the late afternoon helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ transplant shock mli kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Okɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli fiofio yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli dani odu ni okɛ amɛ awo he kroko yɛ shwane mli. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching prevents this.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Cocoa flowers drop if the tree lacks water, faces harsh sunlight, or lacks pollination by tiny midges. Maintaining shade trees on your farm keeps the air humid and creates a suitable home for pollinators.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Hulu la ni naa wa ni okɛkpeɔ loo gbekɛbii bibii lɛ ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ Tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ shia ni sa.

english: How can I tell underground groundnuts are fully ripe and ready for harvesting without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ ni efiteee amɛ?

english: You can check maturity by pulling up one test plant and opening a few pods. If the inside of the shell has dark brown or black veins and the nuts fill out the shell completely, your crop is ready to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tso ko ni akaa lɛ ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmɔtɔi fioo komɛi anɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ amɛ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ amli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo agbɛnɛ akɛ obaakpa.

english: This is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. When maize plants do not get enough nitrogen from the soil, they move whatever nitrogen they have left from the older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the lower leaves to yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpea on my field make the soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with friendly soil bacteria to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant harvested or ploughed back into the soil, that trapped nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akpa tsina tsei lɛ loo aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my pepper farm produce plenty of big green leaves but very few fruits after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-heavy fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into growing stems and leaves instead of flowering. Plants need a balanced mix of nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to trigger flower and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛkwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the ground when rain stays on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves dry out and curl up so fast during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkpãa oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry, dusty Harmattan winds lower the humidity in the air significantly, pulling moisture out of plant leaves faster than the roots can suck up water from the soil, leading to rapid wilting.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i shi jogbaŋŋ. Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oya

english: Why are the leaves on my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings scorching and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ shã ni efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They require temporary shade from fast-growing companion crops like plantains to protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat prevents tomato pollen from fertilizing the flowers properly. When fertilization fails because of high temperatures, the plant drops the unfertilized flowers to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi tomato pollen lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites, thrips, or whiteflies. As these insects feed on the young leaves, they damage the plant tissues or transmit viruses that cause distorted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, thrips, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ Amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji loo amɛhaa helai ni haa tso lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ yaa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous root systems that do not anchor deep into the soil. When the heavy fruit bunch forms, the plant becomes top-heavy, and wet soil combined with strong winds easily pulls the roots out.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni tamɔ fibrous ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ni tsii fee Tso lɛ baaná nɔ ni tsii fe fɛɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli oya.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks for them to yield big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama sweet potato wain tsei anɔ koni maná bulbs agboi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my groundnut plants bend down and dig themselves into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miikoto amɛhe ni amɛmiifo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That is natural for groundnut plants. After the flower blooms and gets pollinated, it grows a stem called a peg that pushes down into the soil so the groundnut pod can grow safely underground.
ga: No ji adebɔɔ naa nɔ kɛha ŋmei tsei. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ efɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: When cassava is ready for harvest, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers swell below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If too many small shoots grow around the main plant, they fight for nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning them leaves only one or two strong suckers, resulting in much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ baajɛ mli aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, plantain jwɛi lɛ ebatsɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight, which helps the tuber beneath the soil grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha tso lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will turn the leaves green and help the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering helps keep the flowers healthy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate organic remedies helps control these pests and restores normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni sa ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it risky to plant my corn seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heat wave or a dry spell. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout but may wither and die before the real, continuous rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do tiny black insects attack my cowpea crop as soon as it begins to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji lɛ tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are aphids, which are attracted to the sweet sap in fresh flower buds. Managing them early protects the buds so your bean plants can form healthy pods.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji aphids. ni ŋmei ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi heei amli nu lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmei tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What is the main difference between a hybrid seed and the local seeds I usually save from my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mifɔɔ buaa naa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing two different strong plant varieties to produce higher yields and resist diseases, while local seeds are traditional seeds saved from previous harvests that are adapted to the area but usually produce lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ srɔtoi enyɔ ni afɔɔ amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, akutsoŋ dumɔwui ji blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why are hybrid seeds often more expensive than the local seeds I get from my neighbors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hybrid dumɔwui lɛ jara wa fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ akutsoŋbii adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds cost more because they require scientific research and careful breeding to create, but they usually reward the farmer with much bigger harvests and stronger plants that justify the initial cost.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ jara wa waa ejaakɛ ebiɔ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ dani anyɛ afee amɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ okwaafoi nyɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da babaoo kɛ tsei ni wa ni haa shishijee shika ni awoɔ lɛ ja.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best not to replant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest because the second generation will lose its special high-yielding traits, resulting in uneven plant growth and lower yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite esubaŋi ni haa yibiiwoo babaoo lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds given by extension officers look different from my local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni onukpai lɛ woɔ he hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ mimaŋ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred with specific genetic traits from parent plants chosen for traits like uniform height, larger fruit, or quicker maturity, making them look and grow differently than local crops.
ga: Akɛ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei ni ahala kɛha sui tamɔ amɛlɛɛmɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ. aduawai wuji loo ni shwereɔ oya Enɛ haa ekwɛɔ ni edaa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I try a new seed variety on a small patch of land before planting my entire farm with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? dani adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu

english: Testing a new crop on a small plot lets you see how it grows in your specific soil and weather without risking your entire season's food or income if it fails.
ga: Kɛ́ oka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko okwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ, ehaa onaa bɔ ni edaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Ni akɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii loo shika ni anáa lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji eshɛɛɛ he.

english: How can I fairly compare a new hybrid crop with my traditional local crop on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ato blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Plant both crop types side-by-side on similar soil, give them the exact same water and fertilizer treatment, and observe which one yields better and handles pests better over the season.
ga: Dumɔ tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ha amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. ni okwɛ tsei ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do if a new crop variety I am testing fails to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tso hee ko ni mikaa mikwɛɔ lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Use the failure as a learning experience to check soil quality, watering, and planting depth, and report the results to your extension officer so they can advise on better suited varieties.
ga: Kɛ shigbeemɔ atsu nii akɛ nikasemɔ niiashikpamɔ ni okɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, nu ni awoɔ, kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ. ni okɛ nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ abɔ o-extension officer lɛ he amaniɛ koni amɛwo ŋaa yɛ srɔtoi ni sa babaoo he.

english: Why do some crop varieties grow faster and yield more food than others on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different plant varieties have different genetics; improved varieties are engineered to absorb soil nutrients and sunlight more efficiently, allowing them to grow faster and produce heavier crops.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ su srɔtoi. Afee tsofai srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ sũ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will be able to survive the weather in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Agricultural extension officers test seed varieties in local regions across the country before recommending them to farmers to ensure they can handle the local rainfall and temperatures.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baaka dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ akutseiaŋ hei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ. dani ejie lɛ kpo etsɔɔ okwaafoi koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why are some new crop varieties better at surviving plant diseases than my local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi yeɔ tsei ahe helai jogbaŋŋ fe mimaŋ tsei lɛ.

english: Scientists breed disease-resistant crops by selecting plants that naturally fight off local diseases, passing that natural protection directly into the new seeds.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni amɛhalaa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ni no sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli hebuu lɛ aha dumɔwu hee lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, keeping the moisture in and protecting the young cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, humid conditions. Rain drips and dense leaves trap water around the pods, allowing the disease to spread rapidly across the tree.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔ nɛɔ ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni no haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: My cocoa tree produces many small flowers, but why do most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers if they are stressed by drought, lack nutrients, or if tiny insects called midge flies do not pollinate the flowers. Only properly pollinated flowers backed by good soil nutrients will form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge ŋmeii lɛ shwieee fɔfɔi anɔ. Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai pɛ ji nɔ ni baafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees swelling up and causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efuu ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by small insects called mealybugs. The virus clogs the channels inside the tree that carry water and food, causing the stem to swell and the tree to slowly die back.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus hela lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ akutso lɛ fuɔ ni fiofio lɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Yellowing down the center of maize leaves means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs from the soil to stay green, make leaves, and build strong stalks.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa teŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hia amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli, amɛbaakwɛ̃, ni amɛma tsei ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves but very thin and small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves on top instead of building thick roots below.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, yucca tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii yɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli tse yɛ shishi.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize make my maize crops grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots break down, they release natural fertilizer into the soil that feeds neighboring maize crops.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shishifãi nɛɛ gbee shi lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why does cutting off extra side branches help my crops produce bigger yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted leaves and branches that steal food and water from the plant. It also lets in fresh air and sunlight, helping the plant focus all its energy on growing healthy fruit or pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ baai kɛ niji ni ataooo ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ gbɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la hu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid applying chemical fertilizer to my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. In dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer stays around the roots and can actually scorch and kill them.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hiɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi ni ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ ni egbe amɛ.

english: Why do tall weeds stunt the growth of my crops even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ naa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act as greedy competitors that steal sunlight, space, and valuable soil nutrients directly from crop roots, leaving your main crop weak and malnourished despite the rain.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi hiɛjoolɔi ni juɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa onibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I stop bushfires from burning my farm during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa koo mli la ni shãa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can create a clear boundary around your farm called a fire belt by clearing all dry grass, brush, and weeds. If a bushfire starts nearby, it stops at the cleared ground because there is no dry plant material left for the fire to burn.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee husu ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ la bɛlt kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji koo mli la yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Atsiɔ la naa yɛ hei ni agbele naa ejaakɛ tsei ni egbi ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baanyɛ aje la shishi.

english: When is the best time for me to clear a fire belt around my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie la ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Clear your fire belt right at the beginning of the dry season before the vegetation becomes completely dry and crisp, so that any sudden or accidental fires will not catch your farm unprepared.
ga: Tsumɔ la tsɔji lɛ ahe mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, dani tsei lɛ agbi kwraa. Enɛ ji koni la ni baa trukaa loo trukaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni asaaa ohe lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How wide should the cleared path around my farm be to keep bushfires away?
ga: Te esa akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni bɔleɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ mli lɛɛ aha tɛŋŋ koni koo mli la akatswa?

english: A fire belt should usually be about 3 to 5 meters wide and completely scraped clear down to the bare dirt so that winds cannot easily blow flames across the path into your crops.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, esa akɛ la tsɔnei lɛ alɛɛmɔ afee aaafee mitai 3 kɛyashi 5 ni atsɔ mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekatswa la ni tsoɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyabote onibii amli oya.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up so quickly during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: When the hot dry season sets in, the intense sun pulls moisture out of the leaves much faster than the roots can drink water from the dry soil, causing the plant to lose strength and wilt.
ga: Kɛji akɛ obote hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plants curl up during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during intense heat as a defense mechanism to hide part of their leaf surface from the sun, which helps them hold onto their remaining internal moisture.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbaai lɛ fã ko ato hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ emli lɛ mli.

english: How does extreme sun and scorching heat kill young trees on my farm?
ga: Kwɛ bɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa miifite tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young crop trees have shallow roots and thin bark. Intense heat bakes the upper soil dry and burns the tender leaves, drying out the young plant completely before its roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ amɛhewolo bibii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to burn cleared weeds and brush on my farm during the harmattan season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ ni mafolɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: No, burning weeds during the dry harmattan period is very dangerous because strong, dry winds can easily carry sparks and turn a small weed fire into an uncontrollable blaze that destroys your entire farm.
ga: Dabi, jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ yɛ oshara waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha la tsoɔ oya. ni otsɔ jwɛi bibii la lɛ Ha etsɔ la ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ. ni baafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What should I do with the bundles of dry brush I clear from my land if I shouldn't burn them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ brɔshi ni egbi ni mijie kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ani esaaa akɛ mishãa lɛ?

english: Instead of burning them, you can pile the brush bundles away from your main crops along the farm edges to rot down slowly into compost, which safely enriches your soil without any fire risk.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ brɔshi ato oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni oshã amɛ fiofio. rotting into compost Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe ni la he oshara ko bɛ he.

english: How can I protect my soil from getting completely dried out by the intense heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around your crop roots with dry leaves or straw, a practice called mulching. This acts like a protective blanket, blocking the harsh sun rays and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi atswa tso lɛ shishifãi. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Will dry leaves left on the ground help my crops when the rains return?
ga: Ani baai ni egboi ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua midumɔ nii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, leaving dry leaves and brush to rot naturally feeds earthworms and soil insects, turning the dry material into rich food that feeds your crops when the rain comes back.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai kɛ tsei bibii ni egboi ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi niyenii. Tsɔmɔmɔ nibii ni egbi lɛ owo niyenii ni jara wa ni baaha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant regain its green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that traps food from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave that natural food behind, making the soil richer for crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ okpa nii lɛ Amɛbaashi nakai adebɔɔ niyenii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal sickness that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments during the rainy season. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight in and removing affected pods immediately helps protect the healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects. Keeping the soil evenly moist and spraying organic neem oil can stop insects and help the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni akɛ organic neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa kooloi ni baa lɛ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii waa loo amɛbɛ ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops all the space and food they need to produce a large harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, drink water and food away from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: As cassava plants get older, they stop storing soft starch in their roots and start forming tough wood fibers. Harvesting your cassava at the right age, usually between 9 and 12 months, keeps the tubers soft and good to eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ da lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛtoɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa. Kasava ni akpaa yɛ afii ni sa mli Bei pii lɛ Enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ koni eye ebua ni eha cassava shishifãi lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ tswaa trukaa kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden flood of water after a dry spell, causing the inside of the fruit to grow faster than its skin can stretch. Watering your plants consistently every day stops the fruits from cracking.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa gbi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ akagbala.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing shoots even when stored inside a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up and try to grow into new plants after a period of rest. Gently snapping off those small white shoots as soon as they appear keeps the yam tuber fresh and heavy for a longer time.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Afolɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Namɛi je kpo blɛoo. Kɛji ejie ehe kpo pɛ kɛkɛ Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from direct sunlight to protect their delicate leaves from burning. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil moist and shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. As long as your soil has moisture, the plants will usually bounce back in the late afternoon when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Tsei hu sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips of lower leaves, it usually means the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted poultry manure gives the plants the strength to stay green and build big ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo toi wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for next season's maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni baa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest and clear the field, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Muawai bibii yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni okpaa ni ojieɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil if heavy rain falls right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water or soggy soil for days, oxygen cannot reach the tubers, causing soil fungi and bacteria to quickly rot the roots underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ha nu lɛ ahi shi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi gbii babaoo. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ oya.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap helps clear these pests so new healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ shishi ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ koni baai heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do paddy rice plants grow so well in flooded water while my other crops drown and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-tsei krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli lɛ?

english: Paddy rice has special hollow tissues inside its stems that act like tiny snorkels, carrying air from above down to its roots under water. Most other crop roots drown because they cannot get oxygen when submerged.
ga: Paddy rice yɛ fã krɛdɛɛ ko ni mli ewo muji yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔne bibioo ko ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shishi kɛyaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei krokomɛi ashishifãi babaoo gboiɔ yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛji amɛbote nu mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when temperatures get too high, water is inconsistent, or the flowers are not being pollinated. Keeping soil moisture steady and encouraging bees—or gently shaking the plant stems—helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmeii ni awoɔ amɛ hewalɛ—loo tsei ashishifãi ni akpokpoɔ blɛoo lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves towards the sun. Staking keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the leaves catch enough sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai ahe helai anaa ni ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small plantain shoots to grow around the main plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Amɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa yɛ tso wulu lɛ he yɛ be kome mli

english: If you leave too many suckers around a single plantain stem, they will steal water, light, and nutrients from each other. Removing extra suckers leaves only the main plant and one follower, which leads to bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ, Amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso titri lɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ eshwɛɔ. ni kɛ mɔ yaa plantain tsei wuji amli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava beside them provides shade and keeps the soil moist, helping the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan dry season, hot dry winds draw moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than roots can drink from the soil. Providing shade trees and mulching the base of the tree retains water in the ground to keep the tree healthy.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow strong leaves. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hia koni baa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why am I finding small holes and dark dirt inside the leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Kɛ muji ni tsuɔ diŋŋ ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the soft inner leaves. Inspecting the crop early and applying appropriate control measures prevents them from destroying the growing center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that feeds the tubers growing under the soil. Staking holds the leaves off the hot ground where they get more sun and prevents diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tsei ahe tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the weather is too hot or when they do not get steady water. Regular watering during flower formation helps the plant hold its flowers so they turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no haa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a disease or by extreme heat and uneven watering. Controlling these insects early keeps the plant foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil's food available for your crops to grow faster and bigger.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ajie amɛhe koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛdara.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my farm so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii koni mikafite nii?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is slightly moist, shortly after rain or watering. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn roots, while applying it during heavy rain can wash the nutrients away before roots absorb them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Nugbɔ loo nu ni awoɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How deep should I bury my seeds in the soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds should not be planted too deep in the ground. If a seed goes way down deep, it will struggle to get air and sunlight energy, causing it to fail to sprout.
ga: Esaaa akɛ aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ tee shɔŋŋ lɛ Ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are some of the crop seeds I planted failing to sprout completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: When seeds are buried too deep underground, they run out of energy before reaching the surface and die beneath the dirt without germinating.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe.

english: If I push my seed deeper into the dirt, will it get more nutrients and grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Ani ebaaná niyenii babaoo ni eda oya?

english: No, pushing a seed deep down actually prevents it from sprouting. Seeds need to be close enough to the top layer of soil so the young shoot can easily break through.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui lɛ ni oootsi kɛya shɔŋŋ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ abote mli mlɛo.

english: How deep should I place my seedlings when moving them from the nursery to the farm field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he ni mli kwɔ ha tɛŋŋ beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When transplanting young plants from the nursery, you must place them deep enough into the soil so that the roots and base are well-supported by the earth.
ga: Kɛji oodu tsei bibii kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ Esa akɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ anyɛ afi sũ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is planting a nursery seedling the same as planting a seed?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, seeds must be planted close to the surface so they can sprout, whereas nursery seedlings already have shoots and need to be planted deeper to stay sturdy.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii momo ni ehe miihia ni adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crops keep falling over whenever strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops fall over in the wind when they are planted too shallowly. Without enough soil buried around their base, the plants do not have strong anchorage.
ga: Nibii ni adu yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni afu yɛ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaamɔ shi.

english: How can I prevent heavy winds from uprooting my newly transplanted crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: To stop the wind from uprooting your crops, make sure you plant the nursery seedlings deep enough into the ground so the soil holds them firmly upright.
ga: Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What makes a transplanted crop fall down even when the stem looks strong?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ko gbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifã lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Even healthy stems will fall down if the root base was planted too high above the soil line, giving the wind enough leverage to knock the plant down.
ga: Tsoi ni wa po baanyɛ agbee shi kɛji akɛ adu shishitoo lɛ nɔ tsɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei lɛ ba.

english: What happens if I plant my nursery seedling too shallow near the surface?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ, ni ebɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ?

english: If a nursery seedling is planted too close to the surface, its roots cannot grip the soil properly, making it easy for rain and wind to pull it out or knock it down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baagbala lɛ loo amɛbaatswa lɛ shi.

english: Can I bury a seed at the same depth that I bury a nursery plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mafu tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: No, nursery plants need deeper planting for physical support, but a seed buried that deep will get trapped underground and will not sprout.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni adu tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni aná gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ. Shi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ baakpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why are grasscutters coming to eat my cassava roots before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔ lɛ ye mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dani mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Grasscutters search for sweet, starchy roots like cassava during dry periods when fresh grass is scarce. Clearing the bushy grass around the perimeter of your farm removes their hiding places and deters them from entering your field.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ taoɔ shishifãi ni ŋɔɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmei be mli, be mli ni jwɛi heei faaa lɛ. Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ baajie amɛhe ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkabote oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I clear away all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight and intense heat. Shade crops like plantains or temporary forest trees act as natural covers, protecting the young plants from sun damage and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the nutrients needed to keep the leaves green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha ŋmeii wuji aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do my harvested yams sprout shoots and become light and soft while sitting in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛmiifee blɛoo beni mita mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that react to heat and humidity by sprouting to grow a new plant, which consumes the starch inside. Keeping your storage barn shaded, cool, and well-ventilated delays sprouting and preserves their weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshwereɔ koni amɛkwɛ tsei heei ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Oshĩa lɛ ni oooha ehi he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ ahi shi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme midday heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects. Providing consistent water during hot dry spells and protecting them from sap-sucking pests keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ yɛ shwane teŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Giving each plant proper distance ensures they grow strong and yield bigger corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops even when the rain is small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally hardier than crop plants and have aggressive root systems that suck up water and nutrients first. Clearing weeds while they are small keeps them from stealing food away from your growing crops.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and filled with insects after I pack it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ kooloi bibii beni mikɛwo kotokui amli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain rots and attracts web-spinning insects if packed while still holding internal moisture from the field. Drying your harvested corn thoroughly on raised mats under direct sun until the kernels are hard prevents mold and insect invasion.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbalaa kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ wɛb lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛfee ekome yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ ŋtayaai ni awó nɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa kɛ kooloi bibii baabote mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farmland make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it inside their roots in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanut tsei gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmei lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat, which causes leaves to burn, dry out, and turn yellow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei adɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my yam vines and tie the vines to wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Dumɔ sweet potato wain tsei ni okɛ wain tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe.

english: Yam vines need sunshine on their leaves to make food; climbing poles raises them above surrounding weeds so they can catch maximum sunlight and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Tso ko ni akwɔɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young maize shoots; early spraying with recommended extension insecticides or using organic neem sprays helps save the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii. Akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo organic neem spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ baaye abua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are my healthy green cocoa pods turning black and rotting directly on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions, which can be controlled by pruning extra foliage, improving airflow, and applying timely fungicides.
ga: Enɛ ji hela ko ni ji black pod ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: What causes my plantain leaves to develop black spots and dry up before the crop is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tsei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is Black Sigatoka, a fungal disease that attacks leaves and reduces the plant's ability to produce energy, requiring the removal of infected leaves to protect the remaining farm.
ga: Enɛ ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tso lɛ baai ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛjieɔ hewalɛ kpo lɛ baa shi. Esa akɛ ajie baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni abu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with big green leaves but leaves me with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground rather than storing food in the root tubers.
