ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do extension agents tell me to plant groundnuts before planting my maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which enriches the earth and feeds heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni ehaa niyenii baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks with small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning allows soil to absorb water before heat causes fast evaporation, and it prevents water droplets on leaves from scorching under hot sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi dani dɔlɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. ni ehaaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but shed most of them before they grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers naturally when they suffer from water stress, sudden severe heat, or lack of nutrients as a way to conserve energy to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni anyɛ ahi shi

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted above them to block the harsh sun and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa ŋmɔlɔ ni adu yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants draw remaining nitrogen from older, bottom leaves to feed new upper growth when the soil runs out of nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and yield less food when I plant them on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating different crops, especially legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, helps naturally refill nutrients in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Titri lɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss through evaporation. The plant enters a resting state to protect its roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe koni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during the hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High temperatures and irregular watering cause heat stress in tomato plants. When stressed by extreme heat, the plant drops its blossoms to save water and energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nyɛ amɛnɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baawo yibii lɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes and dirt inside the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni bɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaf tube of young maize plants and feed on the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ abɛi bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on sap and spread plant viruses, causing leaves to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. fiteɔ baai lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when wind blows before the bunch is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa dani ŋmeii lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be weakened by tiny soil worms (nematodes) or root rot. Damaged roots can no longer support the weight of the heavy plant during strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ amɛ oya. (Nematodes) loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso ni tsii lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting inside shortly after I put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ mligbɛ beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces. Cuts on the skin allow fungi and bacteria to enter the tuber and decay it from within.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Pilamɔi ni yɔɔ hewolo nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helatsɛmɛi boteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops remain stunted even when rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets the full benefit of rainfall and soil nutrition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he sɛɛ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with tiny ears if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ toi bibii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them weak and unable to produce large, healthy maize ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ená baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do we make high mounds of dirt to plant yams instead of planting them directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa sũi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand into large tubers. Mounds make it easy for roots to grow big and protect the tubers from rotting in heavy water.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi. Pile lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ muji lɛ shishi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits in the ground without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that cause rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii helai ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers grow out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to save energy to survive the hot, dry weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why is it important to prune or trim extra shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hia akɛ afo loo afo tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming extra shoots helps the plant direct its water and nutrients into making large, healthy tomatoes instead of growing unnecessary leaves and small branches.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ mli krokomɛi yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛfee tomatoi wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai bibii kɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why is it better to sow my seeds immediately after the first major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rains wake up beneficial organisms in the dry soil, releasing a rush of natural nutrients that give young seedlings a strong and rapid start.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ teɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii oya Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ adara oya ni amɛdara oya.

english: How does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce the final harvest of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mahã akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops, and they often harbor harmful insect pests and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni bei pii lɛ eji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants twisting and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign of a plant virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or a reaction to harsh heat and uneven watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi, loo nɔ ni haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ haa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. It can also happen when the farm gets flooded with water, preventing roots from breathing. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni he hiaa koni afee niyenii ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔ ko mli, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does burning cleared weeds on my farm affect the soil before I plant?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ashãa lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani aduɔ nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While burning leaves ash that gives a quick burst of nutrients, it also destroys organic matter and kills beneficial insects in the soil that hold water and keep the ground healthy for the long term.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ jeɔ kpo oya moŋ, shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hu ni egbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni hiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ hu.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔle ehe waa ni ekpa lɛ shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these insects stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ oye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be eaten by microscopic soil worms called nematodes or banana weevil larvae. When the roots are damaged, the plant cannot hold itself in the ground under the heavy weight of its fruit.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea crops get covered in sticky white spots and tiny bugs during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔi yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: The sticky spots are honeydew left behind by aphids, which are small insects that feed on plant sap during warm weather. They multiply quickly and can ruin flower buds if not controlled early.
ga: He ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni aphids lɛ feɔ. ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni yeɔ tsei amli nu yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite fɔfɔii ashishifãi kɛji akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the green leaves above ground look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava puts energy into growing leafy stems instead of tuber roots if the soil has too much nitrogen or if the plant receives too much rain early on. Balanced nutrients encourage the plant to store food underground.
ga: Yɛ shishifãi amli ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei haa hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ ná nugbɔ babaoo mra mli Niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii akagbee shi.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing plenty of male flowers but no heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo shi ewooo yibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Oil palms produce mostly male flowers when they suffer from water drought or lack potassium in the soil. Proper watering and balance of fertilizers encourage female flowers that turn into fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei babaoo woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛji amɛna hɔmɔ loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi yei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water from the rain or if I need to carry water to them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mawo nu kɛyadu?

english: You can check by digging a few inches into the soil near your crops. If the soil feels dry and crumbles easily in your hand instead of holding together, the root zone lacks moisture and your crops need extra water.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oootsɔ inchi fioo komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ shishifã lɛ mli ni nu kroko he miihia onibii lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables so the water doesn't dry up immediately?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu koni amɛkagbi trukaa?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because the hot sun is not as strong, allowing the soil and roots to absorb the water before it evaporates.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does having too much water on my farm harm my crops just like having no water at all?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nu ko kwraa ni mibɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns crop roots by cutting off air, causing the roots to rot and leaves to turn yellow. Too little water dries the roots out, so balanced soil moisture is necessary for healthy growth.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nu fioo pɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ja lɛ he miihia koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize start curling and turning brown when there is no rain for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during dry spells to reduce the leaf surface exposed to heat and stop water from escaping. If the rain stays away too long, the plant cannot feed itself, causing leaves to dry up and turn brown.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekaje kpo. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat and dry weather become severe, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to conserve energy for survival rather than spending power on growing fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve stored water in its stems and roots. Once the rain returns, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing big fruits during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ aduawai wuji yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The low humidity and dry winds of the harmattan take moisture out of plants quickly, forcing pepper crops to produce smaller fruits to save water and stay alive.
ga: Harmatta hulutsoo be ni baa shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ awo yibii bibii koni amɛnyɛ amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: How does covering the soil around my crop roots with dried grass or leaves help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with organic materials, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops sunlight from evaporating moisture, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops for water.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye nu he akaŋ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them in an open field without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from larger trees or shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Can planting my crops on raised soil mounds or ridges protect them when heavy rains come?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Yes, raised mounds and ridges help drain excess rainwater away from the base of the plant, preventing root rot while keeping enough moisture trapped inside the soil for crop roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, gɔji ni awó nɔ kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the young shoots and small pods on my cocoa trees drying up and turning black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ?

english: This damage is often caused by tiny insects called capsids. They suck sap from the crop's soft stems and pods, injecting harmful saliva that kills the plant tissue and leaves dry, scorched patches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ capsid Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I see so many ants crawling up and down my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho kɛmiijɛ mikokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ants are attracted to sweet honeydew produced by small pests called mealybugs. While the ants might not directly eat the tree, they protect these sap-sucking pests, which can spread harmful crop diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus across your farm.
ga: Akpɔlɔi sumɔɔ wuo ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ feɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii yeee tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ, shi amɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ cocoa bud virus lɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot and turn black during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall and damp conditions allow fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow easily on cocoa trees. The fungus attacks the pod surface, causing it to rot rapidly if protective measures aren't applied early.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ. Fung lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to grow into a fully mature pod ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: After a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated, it usually takes about five to six months for the flower to develop into a mature, ripe pod that is ready to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ omanye jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce a large harvest at one time of the year and a smaller harvest later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli be kome mli, ni ewoɔ ŋmaa fioo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally respond to rainfall and weather patterns. In Ghana, major rains trigger a massive flowering period that leads to the main harvest season around October to February, followed by a smaller mid-crop harvest later.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi babaoo baa. Enɛ haa kpamɔ be titri lɛ baa yɛ October kɛyashi February mli. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akpamɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop small young pods before they can grow into full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he?

english: This is a natural process called 'cherelle wilt.' It happens when the crop does not have enough water or nutrients to support all its pods at once, or when pests attack the young pods early on.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ 'cherelle wilt'. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ shikome. aloo beni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ mra.

english: Why is it important for me to apply protective spraying before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ hebuu nɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi?

english: Applying protective spray early creates a shield on the leaves and pods before rain creates wet conditions. Once damp weather arrives, fungal diseases multiply very fast, making it much harder to stop them if you wait.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ba lɛ, Fungal helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ oookpa kɛji omɛ.

english: How do weeds growing under my cocoa trees slow down crop growth?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ aha tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for moisture, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. They also trap moisture around the base of the cocoa trees, creating humid conditions where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu shwieɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off unnecessary branches help my cocoa trees produce bigger pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning directs the tree's energy and nutrients away from wasteful branches toward growing healthy pods. It also allows sunlight and air to move through the tree canopy, reducing moist air that causes crop decay.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ niji ni efite lɛ amli. kɛmiiya ŋmeii ni wa amamɔ he Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa tsei fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa crops are lacking essential nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa crops lack proper food, their leaves turn pale yellowish instead of deep green, overall tree growth slows down, and the pods produced remain small or poorly shaped.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ baafee blɛoo. ni ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know which type of coconut seedling is best for me to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different coconut varieties behave differently; dwarf varieties mature faster in about 3 to 4 years and are easier to harvest, while traditional tall varieties take up to 7 years to fruit but tend to survive longer and handle harsh weather better.
ga: Kokooi srɔtoi yɛ subaŋ srɔtoi Dwarf henɔi lɛ daa oya yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ekpamɔ waaa. Yɛ be mli ni blema tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii kpawo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, amɛfɔɔ shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some coconut trees producing smaller fruits than the ones my neighbors planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi woɔ yibii bibii fe tsei ni amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit size depends on the specific variety planted as well as soil nutrients; hybrid coconut types are specially bred to produce larger nuts with more water and meat compared to wild or unselected local varieties.
ga: Tso yibii lɛ dalɛ damɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Akwɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji ni nu kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ akɛto koo mli ŋmeii srɔtoi loo maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ahalaaa lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use my coconut harvest to make other foodstuffs besides just selling the fresh juice?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ afee niyenii kroko fe nu ni afee ehee lɛ ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, mature coconut meat can be dried and ground into flour for baking bread and biscuits, pressed into cooking oil, or processed into dried coconut flakes, which allows you to sell value-added products for higher income.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ agbi ŋmei ni edara lɛ loo ni agbɛ lɛ afee ashikishaŋ ni akɛshãa aboloo kɛ biskit. Nyɛɛ mli yɛ fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ mli. loo afee lɛ ŋmei ni egbi Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni jara wa ni onáa shika babaoo.

english: Why are my coconut trees taking so many years before they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Coconuts naturally go through a long growth stage to establish strong roots and trunks before fruiting; tall varieties naturally take 6 to 10 years, whereas modern dwarf varieties begin flowering much sooner.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii tsɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni amɛdaraa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa dani amɛwo yibii. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi mra kwraa.

english: Why do my crop plants drop their young flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops experience intense heat and dry conditions, they drop their flowers to conserve water and survive, rather than spending limited energy trying to develop fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ, ashɛrɛɔ fɔfɔi ashwieɔ koni akɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Is it fine to grow cassava or vegetables in between my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops under young trees makes good use of sunlight and land while the trees are small, giving you early harvests and income until the tree canopy grows full.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii tsei ni akɛfutu mli ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ashishi lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nibii oya ni onáa shika kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ shishi tsɔne lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops growing tall and thin without producing many leaves or branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaa loo niji babaoo bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops stretch out long and thin when they are planted too close together or under heavy shade, as they struggle to reach sunlight needed for strong growth.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my coconut trees turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a natural reaction to old age, but widespread yellowing often signals a lack of plant food like potassium in the soil or an early sign of tree disease.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni baa kɛji mɔ ko eda. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso mli niyenii, tamɔ potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo tso hela he okadii ni tsɔɔ mra

english: Should I trim off the dry brown leaves from my coconut trees or let them fall off naturally?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-coconut tso lɛ nɔ loo mahã amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Removing dead leaves helps keep the tree clean and prevents pests from hiding around the trunk, but you should avoid cutting healthy green leaves because the plant needs them to feed itself.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie baai ni egboi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ he tseɔ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahi shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi, shi esa akɛ okpa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ he miihia amɛ koni eye ehe niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my crop plants are hungry for nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops show hunger through their leaves; yellow leaves usually mean a need for nitrogen, while purplish colors or weak stems point to a lack of phosphorus or other essential soil minerals.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs loo sũ mli nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow and looking weak even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller yields every year even though I plant the same maize every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa abɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be moŋ.

english: Planting the exact same crop every year drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be Afii shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei damɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by hot dry spells, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks. Maintaining moderate shade trees and controlling sap-sucking pests helps the flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni baatutua lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ ná hulutsoo ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall with lots of leaves but give me very few peppers under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to generate enough energy for flowering and fruiting. Too much shade forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves toward the sun instead of producing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ baai ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Yam leaves make food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows all leaves to catch maximum light and keeps them away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa fɛɛ baa naa la babaoo, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ baa.

english: Where do swarms of armyworms come from to eat my young crops overnight?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ jɛ koni amɛbaye miŋmɔshi nii nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Adult moths fly across long distances at night and lay hundreds of hidden eggs under leaves. When these eggs hatch all at once, the hungry caterpillars emerge together, making it look like they appeared out of nowhere.
ga: Kplukai foɔ kɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛtee baai ohai abɔ ashishi. Kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔ amɛhe lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛjeɔ kpo. Ni eha efee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ he ko ni bɛ.

english: Underground root rot happens when water settles in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and causing fungal growth. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii shwereɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes the bottoms of my tomato fruits to turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Black rotten spots on tomato bottoms are caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Water your plants regularly and avoid letting the soil dry out completely during fruiting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha tso lɛ nu daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha egbi kwraa yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ teŋ lɛ he.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce its maximum output.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii babaoo.

english: How do weeds hurt my farm if my crops are already taller than them?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔ lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe amɛ momo?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots underground that steal fertilizer and water before your crop roots can reach them. They also act as hiding places for pests and diseases that can jump onto your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atsɔ onibii anɔ lɛ ahiɛ amɛhe yɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants flowering much earlier this season compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi mra kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli fe afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize plants react to sudden dry spells and hotter temperatures by rushing their growth cycle to produce seeds before dying, which causes early flowering and smaller overall yields.
ga: Abele tsei tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa kɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ he nii kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛfeɔ oya koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgboi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ mra ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan lɛ gbimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water, resting their energy inside the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants have lots of green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer causes pepper plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy leaves instead of producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and crooked instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and well-mounded soil to expand downwards easily; hard or stony soil blocks their movement and forces them to become deformed.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ nyiɛmɔ naa ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly through rain splashes and high humidity, thriving when cocoa trees have excessive shade and poor airflow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do armyworms attack my young maize leaves right after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn baa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fall armyworm eggs hatch rapidly when warm, moist weather begins, and the soft, fresh leaves of young maize provide the ideal food for the emerging caterpillars.
ga: Fall armyworm wɔji fɔɔ oya kɛji dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i je shishi. Ni ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baai bibii ni afee ehee lɛ ji niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni miida.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field help my maize crop grow better afterward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil with nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize need.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow so slowly when I plant them close to large timber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Large trees create heavy shade and their extensive roots compete aggressively for underground water and food, starving nearby plantain suckers.
ga: Tsei wuji feɔ hulutsoo. ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ miiye plantain tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing tomatoes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization so the blossoms wither and fall off without forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why are my old oil palm trees producing far fewer fruit bunches than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso momo lɛ woɔ yibii akui fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As oil palms age beyond 20 to 25 years, their internal transport systems weaken and they direct more energy into maintaining tall trunks rather than producing new fruit clusters.
ga: Kɛ́ mu tsei lɛ ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baa shi. Ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee aduawai akui heei.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the plant helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he Tso lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ su ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Switching to legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I put my fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer placed right on the stem can burn the plant's skin and destroy delicate roots. It is best to place fertilizer a few inches away in a ring or small hole so roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ hewolo ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko loo bu ko mli ni kɛ bo teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks young corn leaves. Catching them early and applying neem seed extract or approved control sprays will protect your farm before they destroy the crop's center.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, wet soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away quickly so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni mli efɔ nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your plants all the resources they need to grow big and produce heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a humid canopy that protects them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ masɛi lɛ ni aduɔ Ehaa hulutsoo be ni mli ewo fɔ ni buɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my tomato seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crowded crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants. Giving tomatoes proper spacing allows good airflow, which prevents leaf diseases and produces bigger fruits.
ga: Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tomatoi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ baa hela naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers dry up and fall off without producing any peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee pepper yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause plants stress, making them shed flowers to save energy to survive. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering during cooler morning hours helps keep roots moist and preserves flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni haoɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei afɔlɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi shwie nɔ ni akɛ nu wo nɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous harvest produce less crop than certified seeds bought from an dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist local pests, handle dry conditions better, and give uniform, higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Etsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni nɔ kwɔ baa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps the plant stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when there is too much rain and water sits in the soil for too long, preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my hot pepper plants curl up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a plant virus. The leaf rolls up as a reaction to the damage caused by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ ni nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ hetoohamɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi efee?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they feel stressed, especially by severe dry weather, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks. The tree sheds its flowers to conserve energy and keep itself alive during difficult conditions.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ mli wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting. As long as they recover by evening, they are safe, but covering the soil with dry grass helps hold moisture longer.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe. Shi jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down, will they still grow well?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei tso lɛ shishi Ani ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Cassava planted upside down will struggle to grow and produce very low yields because the plant buds naturally point upwards to shoot easily. Planting them with the buds facing up ensures fast sprouting and strong root development.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ wa ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ ŋmɔji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ mlɛo. Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋmei lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni shishifãi lɛ hu yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them off the damp soil where diseases can easily rot them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa helai baa. Ebaanyɛ efite oya

english: Why does my plantain plant produce so many suckers, and should I remove some of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie ekomɛi kɛjɛ mli?

english: Plantains produce suckers to multiply, but if too many grow around one stem, they compete for water and plant food. Removing extra suckers and leaving just one or two strong ones ensures your main plant grows larger bunches of fruit.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii kɛha shweremɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛyi fa tsɔ ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ akwɛ yibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over a long time to survive harsh sun, poor soil, and dry spells with no human help. Farm crops are cultivated for food quality rather than toughness, so they need extra care to outgrow weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni adesa yeee ebuaaa amɛ. Aduɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ moŋ fe bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture free nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant roots rot after harvest, that nitrogen remains as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baaya nɔ afee adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Rainfall carries natural nitrogen absorbed from the air and covers the whole field evenly, soaking deep into the soil. Well water lacks these extra airborne nutrients and often only wets the surface layer around the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eboteɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nubu lɛ mli nu lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli, ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fiteɔ. tsei ni efɔ pɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a nutrient maize needs heavily. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ŋmãa waa Kooloo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving tiny dark bits behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the central funnel of the corn plant to feed on tender leaves, leaving their waste (frass) behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛbaa, ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi (sũi) ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing tall, bushy leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together or gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of yellow flowers that fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when too much nitrogen causes the plant to focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why should I remove some of the small plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to compete with the main stem for water and nutrients, resulting in smaller, lighter bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Is it necessary for me to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji awo mli koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food for the plant, while also keeping the vines off damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha wain tso lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ hela akamɔ bo.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally feeding the soil and helping neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa naagbai.

english: Is it better to leave cleared weed bush on my field to rot or to burn it before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbo loo ashã dani adu?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation on the field to rot forms a natural blanket that keeps the soil cool, retains moisture during heatwaves, and returns valuable organic nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Tsei ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛgboi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ fɛ̃i yɛ dɔlɛ be mli ni okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛ wala mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots and washes away the soil food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with big leaves, but the tubers under the ground turn out tiny when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa kɛ́ akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or if cassava is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves towards the sun instead of storing food in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛjie hulu la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off without making pods if the tree is stressed by heat, dry weather, or insect attacks like mirids. Trees also shed extra flowers naturally if they do not have enough water or nutrients to support growing pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ hulu la lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Tso lɛ hu woɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi ni miida lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my maize to look like someone shot holes through them, with green dust inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abɛi lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɔ ko efo bu ni sũ eŋɔli yɔɔ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing leaves of the maize plant and eats the soft tissue before the leaf unfolds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná he ko babaoo?

english: If you plant seeds too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in weak stems, small cobs, and lower total yield.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Kob lɛ ji bibioo. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Too many young shoots take away water and nutrients from the main mother plant, making the main fruit bunch small. Keeping only one or two strong shoots ensures you get a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ baajie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nɔ titri ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná tsei niji ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it forms, usually due to irregular watering where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even when there is enough rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil before your crop roots can reach them, starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good for me to put chemical fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rain washes away the fertilizer before the plant roots can absorb it, wasting your money. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after the rain has stopped.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the young shoots growing around the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing larger fruit bunches more quickly.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii, loo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores leaf health and supports grain development.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baai wuji lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down causes root and leaf buds to grow in unnatural directions, delaying growth and reducing root yield. Always ensure the growth buds point upward toward the sky.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ nɔ. haa dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight for food production. Staking keeps the foliage off the wet ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing maximum light exposure so the plant can form large tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ jɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni enine ashɛ la babaoo nɔ Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume roots decay, this extra nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishifãi fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same field, or will they ruin each other's growth?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafite amɛhe dalɛ?

english: You can safely intercrop them because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly in its early stages. By the time cassava needs more room, the maize will already be harvested.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsake amɛhe shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ be lɛ shɛ lɛ, he ko babaoo he miihia ŋmei. Agbɛnɛ abaakpa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and produce poor harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively absorb water, soil nutrients, and sunlight that your crops need to survive. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your main crops get full access to essential resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ gbalaa nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ oya, ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli mra yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii titrii lɛ náa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages leaf growth over fruit production.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ moŋ fe aduawai ni baa.

english: Why do my crops wither quickly during short dry spells even when the top of the soil looks damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ po.

english: Shallow root systems only draw moisture from the uppermost soil layer, which dries out quickly in hot weather. Deep soil cultivation and mulching encourage plants to grow deeper roots that reach moisture stored lower in the ground.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nu ni mli ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa beans turn black inside the pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black beans usually mean the pod was infected by black pod disease or left on the tree too long after ripening. It is important to separate these bad beans because they spoil the flavor of the healthy ones and reduce the market value of your cocoa crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii diji hela emɔ amɛ loo ni ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni ajie nɛkɛ ŋmeii gbohii nɛɛ amli. Ejaakɛ efiteɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛ jara ni okɛwoɔ o-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa beans look reddish or purple after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ feɔ tsuru loo purple beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Reddish or purple beans mean the cocoa was not fermented long enough or properly. Proper fermentation breaks down the bitter compounds and changes the inner color of the bean to a rich brown, which buyers require.
ga: Beans tsuru loo purple tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo lɛ eshɛko be kakadaŋŋ loo eshɛko bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ afee lɛ fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ nibii ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni etsakeɔ kɔfi lɛ mli su lɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it normal for cocoa beans inside the same pod to have different sizes?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dalɛi srɔtoi yɛ ŋmeii kome mli?

english: Yes, beans inside a single pod naturally grow to slightly different sizes depending on where they sit inside the pod. However, you should sort them during drying so smaller beans do not burn or dry too fast compared to bigger ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ pod kome mli lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛyashɛ dalɛi srɔtoi fioo. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, yɛ he ni dumɔwui lɛ tara yɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ ji koni kɔfi ŋmeii bibii lɛ akashã loo amɛkagbi oya tsɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmeii wuji ahe.
