english: What should I do with the damaged or black beans I pick out during sorting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmeii ni efite loo ŋmeii diji ni mifoɔ yɛ be mli ni mihalaa lɛ?

english: Always discard damaged or diseased beans away from your farm or bury them. Never leave infected beans on your drying mats or farm floor, as they can spread fungal diseases to healthy trees and future harvests.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, shɛrɛmɔ ŋmeii ni efite loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ofu amɛ. Kaashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni agbiɔ loo ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to keep turning and stirring my cocoa beans while they are drying on the tray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ni mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ trati lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stirring cocoa beans regularly ensures that all sides get equal sunlight and air. This prevents mold from growing on damp spots and helps all the beans dry at the same rate.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ, ehaa afãi fɛɛ náa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Why is my work on the drying mat not finished even after the beans look brown on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ agbeee minitsumɔ lɛ naa yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ?

english: Even if the bean skin looks brown, the inside may still hold too much water. You must keep drying and checking them until the inside is thoroughly dry and crisp, otherwise, mold will grow inside the bag during storage.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nut lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ, Shi emli lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo lolo. Esa akɛ ogbi ni okwɛ kɛyashi emli lɛ baagbi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baakwɛ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I try to sell my cocoa beans without drying them completely?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mahɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni migbiko kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwraa?

english: Wet or poorly dried cocoa beans attract mold and produce bad smells. Licensed buying companies in Ghana will either reduce the price significantly or reject your bag completely because wet cocoa spoils during transport.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni efɔ loo egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni ekɛ ŋmeii fɔji baa. Nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ Ghana ni aheɔ nii lɛ baaha jara lɛ aba shi kwraa loo amɛbaakpoo obaagi lɛ kwraa ejaakɛ kookoo ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa beans have a sticky white pulp on them when I open the pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii lɛ yɛ loo yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Be ni migbeleɔ pod lɛ?

english: The sweet white pulp coats the seeds naturally and is essential for fermentation. When you heap the beans, the pulp ferments and generates heat, which kills the germ inside the seed and creates the rich cocoa flavor.
ga: Pulp yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehe hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmeii to he lɛ Loo lɛ baafee marinade ni ekɛ dɔlɛ aba. Enɛ gbeɔ muawai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa kookoo mli ŋɔɔ waa.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color clearly, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Tapping the pod gently also makes a hollow sound because the beans inside separate from the outer shell.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Kɛ́ otswa pod lɛ blɛoo lɛ hu, ehaa gbee ni mli ewo muji baa Enɛ ji akɛ, kɔfi ŋmei lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ mli egbala kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Will my cocoa beans turn bad if I wait too long to harvest ripe pods from the tree?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo yibii lɛ baafite kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa tso lɛ mli yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the seeds inside to start sprouting or rot, turning the beans dark or black and destroying their flavor and value.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ baa. ni efite eŋɔɔmɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa seedlings can survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the food it needs to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or floods the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are there small holes and powdery material on my maize leaves and stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni nibii ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of caterpillar pests like the Fall Armyworm or stem borers. They eat inside the plant leaves and stems, leaving behind powdery waste, which can stunt crop growth if not treated early.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo stem borers lɛ he okadi. Amɛyeɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. kɛtsɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. It stops the plant from growing normally and reduces fruit size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Ebaaha tso lɛ edaaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry weather to save water. The plant is not dead; it goes to sleep to survive the drought and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eyaa wɔɔhe koni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ ebaawo baai heei.

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, which prevents leaf diseases and improves tuber size.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the bunches are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because their roots are shallow or damaged by microscopic worms called nematodes. As the heavy fruit bunch grows, the weak root system can no longer support the weight without bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. Beni aduawai akuu ni mli tse lɛ daa lɛ Kɛji ŋmei nibii ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, shishifã ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ muji lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes 'fertilizer burn,' where the strong chemicals destroy the soft outer bark and shallow roots, which can weaken or kill the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa ‘ŋmɔshi nibii shãa’, he ni tsofai ni mli wa fiteɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so they don't fight for food in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmã dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni mikaye niyenii he akaŋshii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Spacing maize about 75cm between rows and 40cm between plants ensures each plant gets enough water, nutrients, and sunlight to grow strong and produce big cobs.
ga: Aaafee 75 cm yɛ ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ teŋ kɛ 40 cm yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmãa wuji.

english: How do I calculate how many cocoa seedlings I need for my one-acre farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kookoo dumɔwui ayibɔ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: For a standard one-acre cocoa farm using the recommended 3-meter by 3-meter spacing, you will need approximately 435 seedlings to properly cover the field without overcrowding.
ga: Kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 ni akɛ sɛɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto he ni ji mitai 3 x 3 tsuɔ nii lɛ, obaabi aaafee dumɔwui 435 koni ekɛha he lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi babaoo akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which often gets washed deeper into the soil by heavy rains away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ enɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I split my fertilizer application into two parts instead of putting it all at once during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mi-fertilizer ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli enyɔ moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Putting all fertilizer at once is wasteful because young roots cannot absorb it all yet, and rain will wash it away before the crop grows big enough to use it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome lɛ, eji fitemɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ fɛɛ. Ni nugbɔ baaho lɛ dani tsei lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do my young cassava plants lose their leaves when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to make energy and grow big tubers; heavy shade from large trees starves the cassava plant, causing it to drop leaves and yield poorly.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu ni eyi obɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃. Hɔɔ ni mli tse ni jɛ tsei wuji lɛ amli lɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and save water when the heat gets too high.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni ekɛba hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he kɛji latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience dry spells during flowering, which prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pollen lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my maize stems to break and fall over before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa?

english: Stem borers burrow inside maize stalks and weaken them from the inside, or poor root growth from crowded planting makes the tall stems collapse easily under wind.
ga: Stem borers lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Aloo shishifãi ni edako jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji amli lɛ baaha tso ni kɛlɛ lɛ akumɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your crops need to build thick stems and produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are my bean seeds coming out of the ground at different times instead of all together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ekome lɛ?

english: Uneven planting depth or uneven soil moisture causes seeds buried deeper or in drier soil to take longer to absorb water and sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ haa dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth, or that heavy rain has washed the food away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if my land is naturally suited for growing yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Yams need deep, loose, well-drained soil so the tubers can expand easily underground without rotting from trapped water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni nu ni emɔ amɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Too much water fills up the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots and allowing soil fungi to infect and rot them.
ga: Nu babaoo yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná hela ni amɛgboi.

english: Extreme afternoon heat or dry soil causes heat stress in tomato plants, making them drop their blossoms to save water and energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Ha tomatoi lɛ agbo koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages require consistent water and cool, moist conditions to wrap their leaves tightly into firm heads; dry periods or hot sun cause them to stay loose.
ga: Cabbage he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ koni ekɛ baai lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni efee yitso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by the plant curling up to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I seeing white sticky spots on my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛŋ ni shwieɔ mi-kookoo niji anɔ lɛ?

english: Those white spots are usually mealybugs, which feed on cocoa sap and can spread serious diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ nɛɛ ji ŋmeii, ni yeɔ kookoo nu ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni naa wa tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ ashwã.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and have stronger root systems that quickly grab rainwater and soil food before your planted crops can.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ gbalaa nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani tsei ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce fruit when many suckers grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one mother plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from it, delaying fruit production.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. ni haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Young cocoa plants need gentle shade because intense direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a protected environment that keeps the plants cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ni mli jɔ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui ebɔle he. Tsei feɔ shihilɛ ni abuɔ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease known as Black Pod, which spreads quickly in very wet and humid weather. Water droplets splash the fungus from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones, so keeping the farm weeded and pruned helps air flow through and dry out the moisture.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akpɛɔ tsei lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they use to build strong stems and leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛma tsei ahe ni wa kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my maize leaves and powdery dust inside the center leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ni sũ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by a caterpillar called the Fall Armyworm, which burrows into the growing center of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying appropriate control methods into the central leaves stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ koni eye baai heei lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ baa lɛ tsuɔ nii Etsiɔ nakai tsei lɛ anaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of plants that can pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. When these roots decay, they leave behind natural plant food that the nearby maize can feed on.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant, but as the plant gets older, it turns that starch into tough wooden fibers to support its heavy stems. Harvesting cassava at the right age keeps the tubers soft and good for cooking.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ tso lɛ he. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni mli wa koni ekɛfi tso lɛ shishi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ blɛoo ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do I need to spend time tying my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei ahe yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground where leaves might rot, letting them spread out toward the sun to build larger yams.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ekolɛ baai lɛ miifite lɛ. Ha egbɛ eshwa hulu lɛ he koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plants get too stressed by high heat or uneven watering. If the soil goes from very dry to very wet, or if afternoon temperatures stay extremely hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao tsɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa mli Aloo kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ waa lolo. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like an umbrella that shields the soil from hot sun. It prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ niyenii fiofio be mli ni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong and yield larger fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Officer, I only know how to use palm nuts for making soup. What other products can I make from my oil palm tree harvest?
ga: Ofisa, mi pɛ mile bɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii feɔ shwiili. Mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi manyɛ maná kɛjɛ mu tsei ni akpaa lɛ mli?

english: Oil palm nuts are very versatile. Besides making soup base, you can extract red palm oil for cooking, press palm kernel oil from the inner hard seeds for soap and cosmetic making, and use the leftover nut shells and fibers as biofuel for cooking fires.
ga: Oil palm ŋmeii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi waa. Kɛfata shwiili feemɔ he lɛ Obaanyɛ ojie red palm oil hu kɛha niyenii. Akɛ palm kernel fɔ lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni wa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ koni akɛfee samla kɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ. ni okɛ nut ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛ fiber atsu nii akɛ biofuel ni okɛje la shishi.

english: Should I sell my fresh palm nuts immediately after harvest, or is it better to process them into palm oil first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei heei ni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ? Aloo ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafee lɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Processing palm nuts into oil generally yields higher profit margins than selling fresh fruit bunches, but it requires extra labor, water, and processing equipment. If you lack processing facilities, selling fresh fruit bunches directly to local oil mills gives fast cash flow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛfeɔ fɔ lɛ he fe aduawai heei ni abua naa lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ. Shi ebiɔ nitsumɔ, nu, kɛ nibii krokomɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ obɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, tso yibii heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ ahaa mu nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shika baa oya.

english: What is the difference between the red oil from the outer nut flesh and the oil inside the hard seed kernel?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ fɔ tsuru ni jɛɔ ŋmei lɛ kponɔgbɛ loo lɛ mli lɛ kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni wa lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: The outer red pulp yields red palm oil, which is mainly used for traditional cooking and frying. The hard inner kernel seed yields clear palm kernel oil, which has different properties and is heavily used in making soaps, body creams, and industrial products.
ga: Heloo tsuru ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ haa ŋmei fɔ tsuru. Akɛ amɛ tsuɔ nii titri kɛha blema niyenii kɛ shãa. Mligbɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii amli fɔ ni mli tse. Amɛ yɛ nibii srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo yɛ samla, tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ hewolo nɔ, kɛ nitsumɔhei nibii afeemɔ mli.

english: How many years after planting does a young oil palm tree take before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso bibioo ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Improved oil palm seedlings (such as the Tenera variety) usually begin producing their first harvestable fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after being planted in the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tso dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ (tamɔ Tenera tso lɛ) jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my palm nuts have very thick shells with little flesh, while others have thin shells and lots of oil flesh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm nuts lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa waa kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tseee kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa waa lɛ?

english: This depends on the oil palm variety. Wild varieties, known as 'Dura', have thick hard shells and less pulp. Improved hybrid varieties, known as 'Tenera', have thin shells, thick oily pulp, and yield far more palm oil.
ga: Edamɔ oil palm henɔ lɛ nɔ Koo mli tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Dura’ lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli tse, ni wa, ni ŋmei fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Hybrid henɔ ko ni atsake lɛ, ni ale lɛ akɛ ‘Tenera’ lɛ, yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni ejieɔ ŋmei fɔ babaoo.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of palm nuts high up on the tree is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A fruit bunch is ripe when its outer fruits turn a deep orange-red color and at least 5 to 10 loose fruits fall naturally to the ground beneath the tree.
ga: Yibii akuu lɛ ekwɛ̃ beni kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli kwɔ. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, aduawai 5 kɛyashi 10 ni egbee shi lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How many days after harvesting palm fruit bunches do I have before the nuts spoil or lose their oil quality?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ miyɔɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛmli fɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ?

english: Harvested palm nuts begin fermenting within 24 to 48 hours, which increases free fatty acid levels and lowers oil quality. You should boil and process them into oil or sell them to a processor within 2 to 3 days of harvesting.
ga: Palm ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli, ni no haa fatty acid ni bɛ nyɔmɔwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa fɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Esa akɛ okɛwo mli ni okɛfee fɔ loo ohɔ̃ɔ oha mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni okpa lɛ.

english: What is the standard step-by-step process for pounding and extracting red palm oil manually?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ niji tswaa red palm oil ni ajieɔ lɛ?

english: First, boil the fruit bunches to soften the nuts. Next, pound the boiled nuts in a mortar to separate the oily outer pulp from the seeds. Finally, mix the pounded mass with warm water to skim off the floating red oil, and heat the gathered oil to remove any remaining water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, shã aduawai lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, tswaa ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii amli koni ogbala kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ afutu ŋmɔtɔ ni atswa lɛ mli koni ojie mu tsuru ni hoɔ lɛ fɛɛ. ni okɛ mu ni abua naa lɛ awo la mli koni ejie nu ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can oil palm trees yield well in dry areas, or do they require heavy rainfall?
ga: Ani mu tsei baanyɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo amɛbiɔ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Oil palm trees need high amounts of moisture and well-distributed rainfall throughout the year to yield heavy fruit bunches. In dry regions without continuous irrigation, the trees will produce far fewer fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ hei ni nu egbi ni nu shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ Tso lɛ baawo yibii akui fioo ko kwraa.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or cassava between my young oil palm trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when young palm trees are small, you can intercrop the empty spaces with short-season crops like maize, peppers, or legumes to earn income before the palm canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 ni ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa yɛ hei ni mɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ dani ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food for plants, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they spread. Controlling these pests early stops them from damaging the leaves and reducing your pepper yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite baai lɛ ni eha o-pepper yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During very hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it will usually recover when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under intense direct sunlight. Planting them under shade trees or plantain plants protects them from heat and keeps the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi loo akɛ plantain lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi waa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture plenty of sunlight to make food. When vines lie flat on the ground, leaves get shaded and diseased, resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛhoo nii. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai baa amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why will my maize produce smaller ears if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele toi lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to make large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant receives irregular watering, or when pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess rainwater collects in the soil and cannot drain away, creating fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater flow away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ joɔ foi kɛyaa. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil, such as right after a light rain or early in the morning. Applying it on dry soil can burn plant roots, while applying it right before heavy rain can cause the nutrients to wash away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. loo leebi maŋkpa Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Shi kɛ́ okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How can I make sure I apply the right amount of spray to my crops if I cannot read the instructions written on the chemical container?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsu nii? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ makane gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni aŋmala yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ hu?

english: You can ask your local extension officer to show you visual marks, such as using bottle caps or specific cup sizes, to measure the exact amount of chemical for your knapsack sprayer without needing to read the text.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛha okadii ni anaa, tamɔ tɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɔi loo kɔɔpoo dalɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Koni osusu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ osɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okane niŋmaa lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to store empty chemical containers inside my home after using them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baato shĩa lɛ mli beni mikɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even empty containers hold poisonous chemical residues that can seep into your drinking water or food, causing serious health issues for your family.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ atsɔ nu ni onuɔ loo niyenii ni onuɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛnsii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ po amli. Enɛ kɛ helai ni naa wa baa oweku lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do chemical sprays work better when I apply them early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛtsu nii leebi moŋ fe ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot sunlight evaporates the chemical before the plant can absorb it, while strong heat can also burn the leaves when mixed with chemical sprays.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ futu mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and wilt even when there is plenty of rain in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Too much water trapped around roots can suffocate them or cause fungal root rot, which prevents the crop from taking up food and causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni ebɔle shishifãi babaoo he lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ekɛ fungal root rot aba. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aye niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do our traditional methods fail to cure major plant sicknesses when a massive disease outbreak hits the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ blema gbɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsa tsei ahe helai ni naa wa beni helai wuji ni baa ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa lɛ?

english: New diseases are often caused by strange germs or insects brought from other places that traditional remedies cannot kill, requiring specialized treatments or disease-resistant seed varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kɛ helai heei baa. Akɛjɛ hei krokomɛi ni blema tsofafeemɔi nyɛŋ agbe mɔ lɛ. Enɛ biɔ tsamɔ krɛdɛɛ ko loo dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: How does a crop sickness move so quickly from one corner of my farm to destroy the entire field?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela ko aya oya kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome nɔ ni ekpata ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Plant sicknesses are carried by invisible fungal spores or tiny insects that fly through the wind, jump across touching leaves, or attach to your farm tools as you work.
ga: Fungal spores ni anaaa loo kooloi bibii ni foɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni amɛtuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ baai ni kɛ amɛhe kpeɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe helai baa. Aloo okɛ ohe akpɛtɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe beni otsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to cut down and burn a crop that is heavily infected with sickness instead of leaving it to recover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ ni ashã ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ waa lɛ moŋ fe ni aaashi amɛ koni amɛhe awa amɛ?

english: Leaving a severely sick plant in the field turns it into a factory for disease, allowing insects and wind to spread the sickness to all your remaining healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ helai ahe nitsumɔhe. Ha kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ agbɛ hela ashwã onibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds every season instead of planting saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe daa be mli yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength and disease resistance over time, while improved seeds are specially bred to withstand local pests and yield bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers ask us to plant crops in straight lines with precise spacing rather than scattering seeds freely like we used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ biɔ ni wɔdu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ oshwã oya tamɔ tsutsu lɛ,.

english: Planting in straight lines gives every single crop equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed and care for the farm.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land seem to wear out faster when I rely only on chemical fertilizers without adding animal manure or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ miifite oya lɛ? Beni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ahe baai fataaa he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly but does not feed the soil, whereas organic material like manure keeps the soil soft, moist, and naturally fertile for long-term farming.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know how many cabbage plants can fit on my plot of land without crowding them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male cabbage tsei enyiɛ ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyimɔ obɔbɔ fe nine?

english: Proper spacing ensures crops do not fight over soil nutrients and water. Spacing cabbages about 45 to 60 centimeters apart allows you to fit around 14,000 plants per acre while giving each cabbage enough room to form a large, healthy head.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii akayeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kaabaji lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 45 kɛyashi 60, ni no haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei aaafee 14,000 yɛ acre kome mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha kaabii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee yitsei wuji ni mli wa.

english: What happens to my cabbages if I plant the seedlings too close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cabbage lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: Planting too close creates intense competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to remain small, produce weak leaves, and fail to form solid cabbage heads.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa, amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee kaabe yitsei ni wa.

english: Why is it better to grow cabbage seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu cabbage dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cabbage seeds are very small and fragile. Starting them in a controlled nursery bed protects them from harsh weather, heavy rain, and pests until they grow into strong seedlings ready for the main field.
ga: Kaabe dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ aje amɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔji ni akudɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni asaa he kɛha dumɔwui titri.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer or manure to my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-aduawai lɛ amli?

english: Mixing decomposed manure into the soil before planting prepares the land with nutrients. Adding extra fertilizer a few weeks after transplanting gives the plants a boost right when they enter their fastest growing stage.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni eboteɔ eshishijee dalɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water faster through the heat than roots can take it up, causing temporary wilting. As long as the soil remains moist below the surface, the plants usually recover as temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ dɔlɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, Tsei hu sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How long does cabbage usually take from planting the seedlings until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kaabe lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most cabbage varieties take about 2 to 3 months (roughly 70 to 90 days) after transplanting seedlings into the main field to produce firm, mature heads ready for market.
ga: Kaabaji henɔi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 (aaafee gbii 70 kɛyashi 90) yɛ be mli ni adu dumɔwui awo saatso wulu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛwo yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ ni eda ni esa akɛ amɛya jara nɔ.

english: Can I keep growing cabbage on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kaabii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Growing cabbage in the same spot continuously builds up soil diseases and pests that specifically target cabbages. Rotating with crops like corn, beans, or pepper keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kaabeji ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yeɔ kabaji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ aba be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough for growing healthy vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ adumɔ?

english: Good vegetable soil should be dark, rich in organic matter, and loose enough to break apart easily in your hand. It must hold moisture well while allowing excess water to drain so root system doesn't rot.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ aduawai lɛ afee nɔ ni tsuɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni eyɛ mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efo mlɛo yɛ nine mli Esa akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni eeeha eho lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo.

english: How can I organize my farm to keep harvesting and selling vegetables right through the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni maya nɔ akpa aduawai ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: By staggering your planting dates—planting new seedlings every few weeks—and using basic irrigation during dry periods, you can ensure a continuous harvest and steady income throughout the year.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii ni haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe lɛ nɔ—ni aduɔ dumɔwui heei daa otsii fioo komɛi—ni akɛ shishijee nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ nɔmimaa aha nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are being damaged by insects or by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo helai efite mitso lɛ baai lɛ?

english: Insect pests usually leave clear holes, bitten leaf edges, or visible bugs on the plant. Diseases often show up as yellow spots, powdery patches, dark rotting areas, or strange leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai shiɔ bu ni mli tse. Baai lɛ ashishi ni akɔmɔ loo kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, helai jieɔ amɛhe kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eji he ko ni tamɔ powda. He ni egbo ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ loo baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ

english: Yellowing that starts from the bottom leaves usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen. The plant moves the small amount of nitrogen it has up to the younger growing leaves at the top, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means they have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes are harvested and their roots rot, they leave natural nitrogen behind as free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmeii ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily and their shallow roots cannot absorb water fast enough to keep up with the heat. Shade trees shield the young cocoa and keep the air and soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni eshishifãi lɛ hu mli ekɔɔɔ. Enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa Shade tsei buɔ kookoo tsei ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Yam plants produce energy to grow big tubers underground by catching sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all leaves get full sunlight while keeping them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. The damage prevents the leaf from growing evenly, causing it to roll up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Nɔ ni efite lɛ haaa baai lɛ adara pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi shi edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when the plant faces heat stress or irregular watering. Extremely hot weather damages the flower pollen, making it impossible for the plant to fertilize the bloom into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot inside the soil during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to stay alive. When heavy rains flood the soil for long periods, air cannot enter, causing the cassava roots to drown and making it easy for fungal diseases to invade and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli.Okɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji fungal lɛ boteɔ mɔ mli ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one mother plant forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the main stem to grow strong and yield big bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce poor yields even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, space, and sunlight your crops need. Even with good rain, crops remain starved because the weeds absorb most of the food from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ gbalaa amɛ niyenii lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow inside standing water, while maize dies if water sits around it for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa gboɔ kɛji nu ebɔle ehe gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Swamp rice has special internal passages inside its stems and roots that work like tiny air pipes, carrying oxygen down from the air into the flooded roots. Maize lacks these air passages, so its roots suffocate quickly when underwater.
ga: Swamp rice yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ paipi bibioo ko. ni hiɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli Abɛi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu shishi oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their tender leaves from direct scorching sunlight and to retain soil moisture. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that protects the crop until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hidden inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji lɛ? Minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing shoots of maize. Early spraying of recommended biological or chemical insecticides directly into the leaf funnel effectively controls them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Kɛbote baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots underneath stay very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli etsii waa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Staking keeps yam leaves lifted off the damp ground where diseases spread, while spreading the leaves out to catch sunlight, which allows the plant to produce much larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ sweet potato baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, gbɛɛmɔ baai lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my old plantain trees stop bearing big bunches of fruit after two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain momo lɛ kpa aduawai wuji ni ewoɔ yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, plantain plants grow too many sucker shoots around the main stem, creating competition for light, water, and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to keep only two or three per plant restores large bunch sizes.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe. too much main trunk Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi ahe koni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi tso kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kuu lɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when exposed to extreme daytime heat, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients like calcium during the flowering phase.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses spread by these insects that stunt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haaa baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the middle of older maize leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency, signaling that the crop requires nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea.
ga: Yellow jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea.

english: Groundnut plants naturally push their pollinated flowers underground—a process called pegging—so that the actual groundnut pods can safely grow and mature beneath the soil.
ga: Peanut tsei tsiɔ fɔfɔi ni awo mli pollen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fixation. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemicals or watering directly over cowpea plants when they are blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsina tsei anɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ he?

english: Heavy spraying or direct watering on flowers can knock the blooms off the plant and wash away pollen, preventing pods from forming properly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu shwie fɔfɔi anɔ waa loo akɛ nu wo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efeee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide wide leaves that give shade and keep the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow well. It can also happen if there is too much water sitting around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the stem begins to crack open from the swelling tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and produce less harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, your crops do not get enough nutrients to grow big and produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot sunny days and stops the hot sun from drying out the roots of your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha tsei ashishifãi lɛ agbi

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm, which feed on the leaves during cool hours and hide inside the central funnel of the plant during hot hours.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or if the plants do not get enough water. Extremely high temperatures stop the flower from forming fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant beans in the same field where I planted maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting beans after maize restores the soil's strength naturally so future crops grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Eheɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Beans ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim off extra side shoots from my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots allows the tomato plant to direct all its food and energy into growing large, healthy fruits instead of wasting energy on extra stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tomato tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer from the top of the soil before the roots can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving the crops without food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náaa niyenii.

english: My farmland has very hard soil that is difficult to clear and dig, so how will my crops be able to grow roots in it?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa ni ewa akɛ abaajie ni atsa. No hewɔ lɛ, te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ atswa shishifãi yɛ mli?

english: When soil is hard and packed tight, crop roots struggle to push through to find water and food. Adding organic manure, mulching with dry leaves, or plowing the ground softens the soil so roots can spread easily and anchor the plant.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi Loo shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo. Shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛma tso lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant cassava on the exact same plot of land every single year, why do the roots become smaller each time?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops take specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting the same crop repeatedly wears out the soil's strength, so rotating your cassava with crops like beans or groundnuts helps put natural nutrients back into the land.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, akɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ ŋmei. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen or when the soil holds too much trapped water around the roots. Applying organic manure or proper fertilizer restores the leaves to a healthy green color so the plant can make food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo fertilizer ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves when water is scarce as a natural survival trick to prevent losing moisture through the leaves. Once the rains start again, the plant will shoot fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji nu faaa. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin without producing fruit when I plant them under tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make the food required for flowering and fruiting. When shaded by big trees, the plants waste all their energy stretching upward toward the light instead of growing food.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Beni amɛyɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ la ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛkwɛɔ niyenii ni amɛduɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I sow too many seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Spacing seeds out properly gives each plant enough space to grow thick stem branches and yield lots of peppers.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niji ni mli tse baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baa.

english: Why did some of the seeds I planted fail to come up out of the soil after the rain fell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to emerge if they are buried too deep in the soil, eaten by insects, or if heavy rain creates a hard crust on top of the soil that soft shoots cannot break through.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ejeŋ kpo kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ŋmeii yeɔ Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni ŋmeii bibii nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will letting wild weeds grow close to my crops really reduce the amount of harvest I get?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi ni mahã akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like extra hungry plants that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crop. Keeping your farm clean from weeds early on leaves all the soil food for your crops to produce a heavy yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ waa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse kɛjɛ jwɛi amli mra Ebaaha shikpɔŋ niyenii fɛɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when small pests attack the flower stems. Keeping the soil damp around the roots helps the flowers turn into green tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii ahe tsei. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomato eŋɔli.

english: Why do I see tiny insects gathering mostly on the underside of my cowpea leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii lɛ? Abuaa naa babaoo yɛ cowpea baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Insects like aphids hide underneath leaves to shield themselves from hot sunshine and heavy rain while sucking the sweet sap out of the leaves. Checking under leaves regularly helps you catch and stop pests early before they weaken your crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛnuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra ni okpa amɛ. Dani amɛbaagbɔjɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow and refusing to grow tall even though it gets enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpoo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that requires abundant nutrients from the soil to thrive. When the leaves turn yellow, it indicates a lack of nitrogen, meaning the crop needs soil nutrients through fertilizer or organic compost to support its growth.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua amɛdalɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants keep spreading across the soil instead of standing upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miigbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes are naturally vining plants that creep along the ground to form roots at multiple points. This crawling habit helps the plant cover the ground, conserve soil moisture, and produce underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi babaoo. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ su nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii aba

english: Why do my yam shoots need wooden poles to climb instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ he hiaa tso ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally reach upward to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to form large tubers. Without poles, the vines stay on the wet soil where leaves rot and sunlight is restricted.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee tsɔnei wuji. Kɛ́ tso bɛ lɛ, wain tso lɛ baakã he ahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. he ni baai lɛ miifite ni hulu la lɛ faaa yɛ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in low, swampy land while rice thrives in the same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ he ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu kome mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require well-drained soil to breathe and rot quickly in stagnant water. In contrast, swamp rice is adapted to aquatic environments and can channel air to its roots even when submerged.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛfite oya yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ, Peat rice lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehe woɔ nu mli shihilɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni enyɛɔ ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yaa eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ awo lɛ nu mli po.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and light. They require partial shade from companion plants like plantains during their first few years to retain leaf moisture and grow safely.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛha baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my guinea corn survive long dry periods while my maize dries up quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi guinea ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Guinea corn (sorghum) develops deep, extensive root systems that reach subterranean water pockets, while maize has shallower roots that suffer quickly when surface soil dries out.
ga: Guinea ŋmãa (sorghum) lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei lɛ baa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yeɔ amanehulu oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gĩ.

english: Why do my okra leaves and pods cause severe itching when I touch them during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai kɛ mi ŋmeii lɛ haa mihe feɔ mi ŋmɔlɔ waa kɛ́ mita amɛhe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Okra plants grow tiny prickles and hair-like spines on their leaves and fruit stems as a natural physical defense to deter pests and animals from eating them.
ga: Okra tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ yitsɔi ni yɔɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ hebuu ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it unsafe to eat bitter cassava raw directly after harvesting it from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaaye ŋmei ni ahoko lɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Bitter cassava produces natural protective chemicals (cyanogenic glycosides) in its tubers to prevent animals from eating it. Proper processing, soaking, or cooking breaks down these compounds, making it safe for consumption.
ga: Cassava ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he. Amɛyɛ cyanogen glycosides yɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni kooloi akaye ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ, akɛwo nu mli, loo ahoo lɛ, ebaafite nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ. ni haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli

english: Why do insects attack my garden tomato plants much more than my cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa tomato tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have soft leaves and tender stems that attract a wide variety of pests, whereas cassava plants contain bitter compounds in their foliage that naturally repel many common field insects.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ baai bibii kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tsei yɛ nibii ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli ni haa amɛshwieɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does the red witchweed attach itself to my cereal crops and weaken them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witch hazel lɛ kpɛtɛɔ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ lɛ?
