english: Witchweed (Striga) is a parasitic plant that locks its roots onto the roots of cereal crops like maize and sorghum to steal their water and food, causing the host crop to stunt and wither.
ga: Witchweed (Striga) ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe. koni eju nu kɛ niyenii Ehaa tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or spreading well-rotted chicken manure around the plants will quickly feed them and restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baaha amɛ niyenii oya ni eha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yields now than it did when I first cleared the forest five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe beni mijie nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil is like a food bank; every time you harvest crops without adding anything back, you take away its natural food. To make the soil rich again, you can let the land rest for a season, plant leguminous crops like cowpeas, or add compost and animal manure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ niyenii atoohe. Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ nɔ ko fataaa he lɛ Okɛ amɛ adebɔɔ niyenii lɛ miihe. Kɛji oosumɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be kome. Dumɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii loo okɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ŋmeii afata he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal sickness called black pod disease, which spreads fast during wet and humid weather. You can protect your cocoa by pruning overcrowded shade tree branches to let sunlight in and removing all black pods immediately so they don't infect healthy ones.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ obu kookoo he kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe nine lɛ ni ooofo mli koni hulu la babaoo abote mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooojie ŋmeii diji fɛɛ oya koni amɛkamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting covered in tiny white insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava is infested with whiteflies or mealybugs that suck the sap out of the leaves, causing them to curl up and stunt the plant's growth. Spraying the leaves with a simple neem leaf water extract or recommended mild insecticide will help clear them off.
ga: O-cassava lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: What is eating small round holes in my pepper leaves and causing the young plants to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ ni eha tsei bibii lɛ kpa dalɛ.

english: Insects such as beetles or caterpillars are chewing the leaves, which prevents the plant from catching sunlight to make its food. Checking under the leaves in the morning to pick off bugs or applying an approved crop spray will protect your plants.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu la he koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi leebi koni ojie kooloi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ loo okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it good practice to plant plantains on the same land where I am establishing new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily under strong heat. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the cool shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hɔɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ fɛ̃i aha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant beans inside my maize farm at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli yɛ be kome too mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and saves you money on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii, ni ehaa shika ni akɛwoɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering, such as going from very dry soil to heavy flooding. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch made of dry grass will help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyaa nu afua ni mli wa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni egbi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting long shoots in the barn before the rain even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaŋŋ akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ po je shishi lɛ?

english: Yams naturally wake up from their sleep stage when temperatures in the storage area get too warm or humid. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated, shady, and cool delays early sprouting so your seed yams stay strong until planting day.
ga: Sweet potatoes baate shi kɛjɛ amɛwɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, hulutsoo, kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa o-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ mra koni o-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi gbi ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Weed seeds are already buried deep in the dirt and are much tougher than farm seeds, so they wake up immediately when rain touches the soil. Clearing weeds early while they are small prevents them from drinking up all the water and fertilizer meant for your crops.
ga: Afu jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ momo, ni amɛhe wa kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛteɔ shi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Amɛgbekɛbiiashi po baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ akatsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop full of small holes, and why are the plants failing to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm feed on the inner leaves of young maize plants. When the leaves are eaten, the plant loses its ability to capture sunlight and make food, which stunts its growth and reduces your grain harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai lɛ. Kɛji amɛ ye baai lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ adaramɔ baa shi ni ehaa dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: What makes the green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot away during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark conditions. High humidity and rainwater splash the fungus onto the pods, destroying the beans inside before they can ripen.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when the dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi egbi lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself during dry spells. By losing its leaves, the plant slows down water loss so its underground roots can survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Baai ni elaaje lɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ nu ni elaaje lɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt in the soil. The bacteria block the tiny water channels inside the plant's stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves when hot sun demands it most.
ga: Bei pii lɛ muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni egboɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Muawai tsiɔ nu gbɛi bibii anaa. yɛ tso ko shishi Enɛ ji koni nu akashɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or too little direct sunlight, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of shifting energy into making flowers and peppers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fioo pɛ amɛnáa lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami ɔ kɛ peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ chili pepper.

english: Why do my crops give smaller yields when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, their roots fight each other for the same water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block each other from sunlight, leading to thin, weak plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ waa tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my maize plants while they are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ehe miihia ni madu mi-abɛi tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛdarako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete well. Early weeds act like thieves, stealing the fertilizer, moisture, and space the young crop needs during its most critical growth stage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyeee akaŋ jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishijee lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ he ni tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the soil without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akuuu ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves naturally dry up and fall off, the base of the main stem swells, and the soil around the plant begins to show small cracks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ fũuɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa bibii.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing sprouts in the barn even when I haven't planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are living plants resting after harvest. Warm, humid air in the storage barn signals to the yam that its resting period is over and it is time to sprout a new shoot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato lɛ akɛ ehejɔɔmɔ be lɛ eho. Ni be eshɛɛ ni abaakwɛ̃ tsei heei.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly wears out the specific soil nutrients that plant loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Is it bad to clear and uproot all the big trees before I plant my new crops?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ mafo tsei fɛɛ ni edara lɛ ashishi dani madu tso hee?

english: Completely clearing all trees exposes the soil to scorching sun and heavy rain, which washes away topsoil nutrients. Leaving some shade trees keeps the soil cool, retains moisture, and protects young crops from harsh weather.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ aya. Tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni fɛ̃i ahi shi ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe

english: What causes my crop roots to get weak and uproot easily when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni haa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Weak roots usually happen when the soil stays flooded due to poor drainage, causing root rot, or when crops are planted too shallowly. Improving drainage and planting at the correct depth helps roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ baa kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, loo kɛ́ adu tsei yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant trees among our food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ ni wɔkɛ wɔ niyenii ni wɔduɔ lɛ adu tsei lɛ?

english: Trees protect crops from strong winds, provide shade to shade-loving crops like cocoa, and their fallen leaves rot into the soil to act as natural fertilizer.
ga: Tsei buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ehaa tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ feɔ hulutsoo, ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some tree seedlings die shortly after I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi gboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often die from transplant shock, lack of water during the first few weeks, or planting them during the heat of the day instead of early morning or late evening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui gboiɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli, loo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli.

english: Can I grow castor plants together with my regular food crops like cassava and maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ miniyenii ni miduɔ daa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ adu castor ŋmãa?

english: Castor can be grown alongside other crops, but it needs enough space because its wide leaves can block sunlight from smaller crops if planted too close together.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu castor jwɛi lɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe, shi ehe miihia ni aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ejaakɛ ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ naa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: How do I know if a tree seedling is healthy enough to survive after planting it on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi beni midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: A healthy seedling has dark green leaves, a firm stem, and an undamaged root ball, with no visible signs of pests, yellowing, or wilting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni efiteee ni nɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ ko bɛ he.

english: How does keeping trees on my land help keep water in the soil during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Tree roots act like sponges underneath the ground to hold groundwater, while the canopy shades the soil surface to slow down water evaporation.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sponji ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can planting specific trees help recover farm soil that has lost its power to grow crops?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, certain trees like leguminous trees catch nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do farmers plant boundary trees around their farm lands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsei yɛ amɛŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Boundary trees serve as permanent markers to show farm borders, act as windbreaks to protect crops, and prevent soil erosion along the edges of the farm.
ga: Husu tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ okadii ni hiɔ shi daa ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔ husui. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ naa.

english: What should I do if the leaves on my farm trees start turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen, attacks by sap-sucking pests, or overwatering; checking root moisture and applying manure or fertilizer often fixes the issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii tamɔ nitrogen, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni akwɛɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ saa naagba lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil, leaving it tired. Groundnuts and beans put vital nutrients, especially nitrogen, back into the soil naturally, which makes the land fertile again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha etɔ lɛ Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii hiɛɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. titri lɛ nitrogen Ku osɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there small holes chewed into my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the tops of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni mikɛyeɔ nii?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars hide inside the center of the young maize plant (the whorl) and eat the soft growing leaves, which can ruin your crop if not treated early with proper pest control.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. (fã ni ji ring lɛ) ni oye baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ Enɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsaaa mra. Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa nɔ

english: Why do weeds around my cassava cause the roots to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and food from the soil that your cassava needs. When weeds crowd the plant, the cassava cannot make enough strength to store energy underground, resulting in small, thin tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi eyi tsei lɛ amli obɔ lɛ, Cassava nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know when it is safe to sow my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist for a few days straight. Planting after just one early light rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then dry up and die when the sun comes back out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu la lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is it wrong to drop fertilizer right next to the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and can burn the plant's skin and soft roots if it touches them directly. Placing it in a small circle a few inches away allows the roots to safely reach out and drink the food without getting damaged.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ahewolo kɛ amɛshishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo kooyigbɛ bibioo ko mli He ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛnu niyenii ni amɛfiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm, which stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fung ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam mounds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need plenty of room underground to expand into big, healthy yams. If mounds are too close, the plants fight for soil space and nutrients, leaving you with many tiny yams instead of large ones.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he babaoo koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ sweet potato agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji gɔŋ lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔtɔ bibii. Mɛi babaoo moŋ fe agbo kome

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and begin to drop. You can also carefully dig around the base of one test plant to see if the roots have grown thick and full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Kaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mihe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to grow strong, resist local diseases, and produce high yields. Saved seeds from old harvests lose their strength over time and often carry diseases from the previous year.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛdara waa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni bei pii lɛ amɛkɛ helai ni jɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my big stalk crops split open or burst when I cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ ekomɛi amli gbalaa loo amɛkuɔ kɛ mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Thick stalk crops carry high internal moisture and pressure. When hit with a blunt force from a cutlass instead of a sharp, clean cut, the shockwave causes the dense stem to shatter and burst open.
ga: Tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse lɛ yɛ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ. Kɛ akɛ hewalɛ ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ ŋmei mli lɛ tutua lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oya ni he tse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Shock wave lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjaraa.

english: Is using a regular cutlass always the right way to harvest tall, thick crops?
ga: Ani dade ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ ni mli wa?

english: Not always. While cutlasses are common, heavy or thick-stemmed crops can burst or shatter under a rough chop. Using extremely sharp, specialized hand tools or machinery cuts cleanly without destroying the harvest.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, eyɛ mli akɛ dade ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ moŋ. Shi tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse loo amɛtsii lɛ baanyɛ agbala loo amɛgbala kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛtsɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi loo tsɔnei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfolɔ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee nɔ ni akɛfee lɛ.

english: How can I safely cut down thick crop stalks by hand without destroying the harvest if I don't have machines?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ minine afo tsei ahe tsei ni mli tse lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mibɛ tsɔne?

english: Keep your cutlass or blade extremely sharp and slice at a sharp 45-degree angle using a swift sliding motion rather than a heavy downward blunt blow, which prevents the stem from cracking open.
ga: Ha otsɔnei loo otsɔnei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. kɛ slice ni yɔɔ 45 degree ŋwɛigbɛ kɛtsɔ oyaiyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ slam ni wa baatsu nii. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbele.

english: Why is it dangerous to hit a thick crop stalk directly with a blunt knife during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ kakla ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ baatswa tso tso ni mli wa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nikpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: A blunt knife crushes the outer plant fibers instead of slicing them. This crushing force builds tension inside the stalk until it explodes or splits, ruining the crop.
ga: Kakla ni mli tseee lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe tsɔi lɛ asɛɛgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo amɛ mli bibii bibii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etswaa loo efoɔ, ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What makes stalk-type crops act differently from other crops when it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa stem tsei lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe kɛ́ ebashɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ he?

english: Stalk-type crops have solid, fibrous stems designed to hold water and nutrients under pressure. Unlike soft vegetables or grains, improper cutting causes these tightly packed fibers to tear apart violently.
ga: Rod tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni afee koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ato yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afolɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nɛkɛ tsɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe waa nɛɛ shwieɔ shi waa.

english: Why do crop stems feel so hard and brittle when they reach full maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe ejɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As crops mature, their cell walls thicken to support heavy leaves and fruits. This extra strength makes the plant sturdy while growing, but brittle if struck improperly at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Cell gbogboi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛfi baai kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa beni edaa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ebafeɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni esaaa nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why am I losing a large part of my crop yield during harvesting even though the plants grew very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Losses often happen right at harvest due to rough handling. If harvesting tools crush or split the stalks, the edible parts get damaged or exposed to quick rot before they can reach the market.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni laajeɔ lɛ baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli yɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ dɛŋdade lɛ fã loo ejara tso lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii lɛ fãi lɛ fiteɔ oya loo egboɔ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Does it really matter if my crop stalks crack or split a little bit while I am cutting them?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji mitso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli gbala loo ejara fioo beni mifo lɛ?

english: Yes, it matters a lot. Cracks and burst wounds expose the inside of the crop to dirty air, bacteria, and insects, causing rapid spoilage and lowering the selling price.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. Gbɛjegbɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ewo muji, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii baa tso lɛ mli, ni no haa efiteɔ oya ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does bad harvesting technique cause me to lose money at the market?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmaakpamɔ gbɛ̀i ni ehiii lɛ aha mifite shika yɛ jara nɔ?

english: When crops burst or shatter during harvest, buyers view them as damaged goods. Damaged crops spoil quickly during transport, forcing you to sell them at a lower price or throw them away.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli gbala loo amɛmli gbala yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baabu nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ nibii ni efite. Nibii ni efite lɛ fiteɔ oya beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. ni nyɛɔ onɔ koni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ loo okɛshɛrɛ ashwie

english: What happens inside a stalk crop when it gets damaged by bad harvesting tools?
ga: Mɛni baa tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nibii ni ehiii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ fite lɛ?

english: Damaging the stalk breaks the internal vessels that hold plant fluids. This causes juice leakage, loss of weight, and creates open sores where destructive rot and fungi can enter.
ga: Kɛ́ akumɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa lá fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni hiɛɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli gbalaa. Enɛ haa nu mli nu lɛ hoɔ, ehaa mɔ he waaa, ni ehaa pilamɔi ni agbele ni baanyɛ agbo ni ŋmeii baanyɛ abote mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do plantains grow so much better in forest areas than in dry, open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni egbi lɛ?

english: Plantains need high humidity, consistent moisture, and soil rich in natural organic matter from decaying leaves, which forest environments naturally provide.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulutsoo ni fa babaoo. hulutsoo ni tamɔ amɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ ni koo lɛ mli shihilɛ lɛ kɛhaa lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves scorch and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose moisture quickly under direct heat; in forest settings, taller trees break strong winds and provide partial shade to protect them.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ, tsei kakadaji tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow plantains successfully outside of forest regions in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ kooi amli hei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ asɛɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: It is difficult because outside forest zones, rainfall is lower and soils dry out faster, requiring heavy irrigation, mulching, and windbreaks to keep the plants alive.
ga: Enɛ wa ejaakɛ yɛ koo lɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baa shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Eheɔ nu ni mli wa, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is forest soil naturally more fertile for crops than open grassland soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli shikpɔji lɛ ji hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi shikpɔji ni agbele naa lɛ?

english: Forest soil is covered in fallen leaves and decomposing trees that break down into rich organic material, which holds water and nutrients better than exposed soils.
ga: Koo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ baai ni egbee shi kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ ni fiteɔ kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe sũ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ.

english: Is there any government program in Ghana that helps me get farm inputs at a cheaper price?
ga: Ani nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ?

english: Yes, initiatives like Planting for Food and Jobs (PFJ) provide registered farmers with government-subsidized seeds and fertilizers through local agricultural extension offices.
ga: Hɛɛ, nifeemɔi tamɔ Okwaayeli kɛha Niyenii kɛ Nitsumɔi (PFJ) haa okwaafoi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni maŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I get access to subsidized fertilizer for my crop farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can register with your local district agricultural office or a recognized farmer group to buy government-supported fertilizer from authorized local agro-dealers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ loo okwaafoi akuu ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli koni oyahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni nɔyeli fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why does the government subsidize fertilizer for food crop farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa mɛi ni duɔ niyenii lɛ?

english: The government reduces fertilizer costs so that smallholder farmers can afford to nourish their crops, increase yields, and boost the country's overall food security.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ baa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo shi bɔni afee ni okwaafoi bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ amɛŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ, amɛha amɛŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ, ni amɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What actually happens to my crops when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that plant roots absorb to build stronger stems, green leaves, and healthier crop yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni tso shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn dark green and grow lots of leaves after I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ baai babaoo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain nitrogen, which stimulates chlorophyll production—the green chemical plants use to capture sunlight and make food for rapid leaf and stem growth.
ga: Nitrogen yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. ni haa chlorophyll lɛ feɔ lɛ Enɛ ji tsofa ko ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii koni baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adara oya.

english: Will applying subsidized fertilizer automatically guarantee a huge crop harvest for me?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shika mli lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer gives plants necessary nutrients, but a big harvest also requires good weed control, pest management, and sufficient rain or water during the growing season.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ. Shi ŋmaakpamɔ babaoo hu biɔ ni akudɔ jwɛi jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the nutrients it needs to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ waa Kooloi ŋmãa loo nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water and soil nutrients. Mulching the soil around the plant keeps it cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached to produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni amɛwo tomato.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying a neem oil solution early protects the leaves so the plant can grow healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tsei amli. Neem fɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land, giving your cassava extra nutrients without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-cassava lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the main leaves start to turn yellow and drop off. Harvesting too early results in small roots, while waiting too long makes the roots tough, woody, and hard to cook.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tamɔ tsei, ni ewa akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I use a specialized harvesting hook instead of a cutlass to collect my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋtayaa krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛtswaa ŋtayaa atsu nii moŋ fe ŋtayaa ni akɛkpaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Using a cutlass can easily wound the tree bark where future flowers grow, reducing your crop yield for the next season. A sharp cocoa hook cuts the stem cleanly without damaging the trunk or bruising the seeds inside.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ŋmɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ yibii ni wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kookoo ŋmei ni mli wa lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee tso lɛ loo efiteee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot fast if they are picked fully soft or packed tightly in wooden crates where heat builds up. Picking them when they just turn light orange and keeping them in ventilated baskets under the shade stops bruising and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Tomato baafite oya kɛji akɛ akɛto blɛoo loo akɛwo tso adekai amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni dɔlɛ baanyɛ abua naa yɛ lɛ. Kpãa kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli yɛ hulutsoo shishi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔlɔ naa ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my freshly dug cassava spoil after only two days out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni atsa ehee lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni ejɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava roots spoil rapidly once exposed to air because of natural breakdown processes. To prevent total loss, cassava should be processed into gari, kokonte, or high-quality flour within 48 hours of harvest so it can be stored for months.
ga: Kasava shishifãi heei fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ bɔ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛhaa lɛ hewɔ. Bɔni afee ni akafite kwraa lɛ, esa akɛ afee Cassava lɛ Gari, Kokonte loo ashikiŋsha ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. koni anyɛ akɛto nyɔji babaoo

english: How can I protect my dried maize from being eaten by insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni egbi lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive when grain has remaining moisture and open air. Drying your maize until the kernels are very hard and storing them in sealed hermetic bags starves insects of oxygen and protects your harvest without using harmful chemical sprays.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmaa lɛ mli nu eshwɛ lolo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbele. Kɛ́ ogbala o-ŋmãa lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do traders offer me lower prices for my plantains compared to imported or neatly packaged ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi kɛ mi plantains lɛ jara baa shi kɛ akɛto plantains ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ loo ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli fɛfɛo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Traders pay less when produce shows dark bruises, cuts, or uneven ripening caused by rough handling during harvest and transport. Careful handling, sorting your plantains by size, and keeping them unbruised makes them look high quality and fetches higher market prices.
ga: Jarayelɔi woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji nibii ni amɛdu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejaaa yɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kpamɔɔ kɛ tsɔne kudɔmɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛji akɛ ato plantains lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ baaa lɛ, ebaana nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cut bushes and grass when clearing my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni afolɔ beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients in the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms like earthworms. Leaving cleared plant material to decay naturally feeds the soil and keeps it moist for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I clear my farm land before the first major rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ midumɔi lɛ amli dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba?

english: Clearing early allows you to sow seeds right at the start of the rainy season, ensuring your crops catch the initial nutrient-rich rains for strong root establishment.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ naa nugbɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ shishijee mli koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and weak with small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce large, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee toi wuji ni wa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm cause my cassava crops to yield smaller roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light from your cassava plants before the roots can absorb them, depriving the tubers of the food they need to expand.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ o-cassava tsei lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young plantain plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, acting like a blanket that shades the soil, keeps moisture from evaporating in the heat, and prevents weed growth around young roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi bibii ahe lɛ naa

english: Why does growing groundnuts on my farmland make my maize grow stronger in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa waa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil, providing free natural nitrogen fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. koni okɛ nitrogen ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to plant cover crops on unused land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cover crops protect exposed soil from heavy rains and hot sun, stopping soil erosion while adding rich organic matter back into the earth.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ekpaa shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off before developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when pepper plants experience stress, usually caused by sudden heat waves, dry soil conditions, or too much water logged at the roots.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na haomɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are receiving too much harsh sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: Crops suffering from sun stress will usually have pale or yellowing leaves, scorched leaf tips, or leaves that curl tightly inward during the hottest part of the afternoon to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. Akɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ shãa. Aloo, baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do my crops grow lush green leaves but produce no fruits when I apply a lot of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizers high in nitrogen causes plants to direct all their energy into growing foliage and leaves rather than developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ tsei ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Officer, how do I know the best time of year to start planting my crops?
ga: Nitsulɔi Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Crops need a reliable supply of water to establish strong roots. Planting at the start of the rainy season ensures young crops get enough soil moisture to survive and grow during their initial months.
ga: Nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops that are less than a year old need much more care than older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeko afi kome lɛ he hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops have shallow roots and soft stems, making them very vulnerable to weed competition and lack of nutrients. Older plants have deep roots and thicker stems that can handle tough conditions much better.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi baabɔ akaŋ, ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpai. Tsei ni edara lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ adamɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are growing properly for their age?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ kɛha amɛafii lɛ?

english: A healthy young crop should show continuous leaf growth and a strong central stem within a few months of planting. If growth stalls or leaves turn yellow, the crop usually needs nutrient support or relief from weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná baai ni yaa nɔ amɛdara kɛ teŋgbɛ tso ni mli wa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dalɛ lɛ egbɔjɔ loo baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii he hiaa niyenii kpakpa loo jwɛi ahe yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer or agrochemicals directly at the base of the plant instead of spraying everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo agrochemicals awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛshwieɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Applying chemicals directly at the base places the nutrients right where the main root system can absorb them, while preventing nearby weeds from stealing the treatment.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi he ko ni shishifã titri lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju tsofa lɛ.

english: Is it good practice to apply chemical treatments to my crop's base right after it rains?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ tsofai baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, damp soil helps the crop absorb nutrients much faster. Rain softens the earth and dissolves the chemical so the roots can drink it up easily without burning the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa tsofai shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãaa tsei lɛ.

english: Will heavy rain wash away the chemical I put around my crop's stem?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho tsofai ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: A sudden downpour can wash away surface chemicals, but applying treatment to already moist soil right after gentle rain helps the chemical sink directly into the root zone safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai ni yɔɔ nibii anɔ lɛ. Shi ni akɛ tsofa lɛ baatsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ momo lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ abote shishifã lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Should I weed my farm before or after I apply treatment to the base of my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofa lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli loo beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Applying treatment to the base of the crop first ensures the crop gets immediate protection and nutrients, and clearing the surrounding weeds right after prevents them from recovering and competing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ buɔ ehe amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehaa enáa niyenii kpakpai. kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkahe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛkaye akaŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it easier to clear weeds when the ground is wet from recent rain or when it is dry?
ga: Ani ewaaa akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ hewɔ? Enɛ loo be mli ni egbiɔ?

english: Weeding after rain is much better because wet soil is soft, allowing you to pull weeds out easily by their roots so they do not quickly grow back.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my crops right after the rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds in the soil are tough and react instantly to moisture. Because weeds grow aggressively, they will choke young crops for sunlight and soil water unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Amɛbaahã ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná hulu la kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ja ojie amɛ oya.

english: How does recent rainfall affect the way the soil feeds my young crops?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ Te enɛ saa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain acts as a transporter in the soil, breaking down minerals and organic matter so that root hairs can easily suck up water and essential plant food.
ga: Nugbɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ nibii yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Efoɔ mineral kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ oya.

english: Can I plant cocoa seeds directly in my main farm, or must I use a nursery first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yibii yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting cocoa seeds in a nursery protects the fragile young plants from harsh direct sunlight, pests, and heavy rain. Once the seedlings are strong and healthy after a few months, they stand a much better chance of surviving when transplanted to your main farm.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he, ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Amɛbaaná hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kwraa akɛ amɛbaahi shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are receiving too much direct sunlight without enough shade, or the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Adding shade plants like plantains and using gentle fertilizer can help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains fata he, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli jɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in wet, humid weather. You can manage it by removing affected pods quickly and trimming tree branches so air and light can pass through to dry out the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. ni amɛfolɔ tsei koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ mli koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli akagbi.

english: Pruning extra or dead branches allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which lowers humidity and reduces disease. It also helps the tree direct its nutrients into growing bigger and healthier pods rather than useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi ni helai hu baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni enáa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds thrive on the abundant water and warmth brought by the rains. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your cocoa trees.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nu ni mli eyi kɛ latsaa ni nugbɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Additionally, if the tree feels stressed from dry weather or low nutrients, it drops extra flowers to save its strength.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ pollin lɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni faaa lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛha ehewalɛ ahi shi.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the flowers on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy downpours can physically knock fragile cocoa flowers off the tree and discourage the tiny insects needed to pollinate them, leading to fewer pods forming during very rainy periods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ agbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. ni enijiaŋ jeɔ wui yɛ kooloi bibii ni he hiaa kɛha pollination lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa pods fioo pɛ baa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods look much smaller than the pods on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii kwraa fe ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pod size depends on the cocoa variety you plant, the quality of soil nutrients, adequate water, and proper shade control. Planting high-yielding hybrid varieties and keeping the soil nourished with fertilizer will produce larger pods.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dalɛ damɔ kookoo srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlihilɛ Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Hybrids ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color as they ripen, shifting from green to a bright yellow, or from dark purple to an orange-yellow. If you gently tap a ripe pod, it will sound hollow inside.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ purple ni mli edɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ-orange nɔ. Kɛ́ ota pod ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he fioo lɛ, gbee ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees producing fewer pods than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural vigor declines, and the soil around them becomes drained of nutrients. Applying recommended fertilizers, pruning properly, or gradually replanting old sections will help restore high yields.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Kookoo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii Nibii ni egbɔ lɛ ni aaafo mli jogbaŋŋ loo ni aku sɛɛ adu fiofio lɛ baaye abua ni aná yibii babaoo.

english: Why do entire cocoa trees need to be cut down when only a few branches look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni niji fioo komɛi pɛ bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus spread throughout the sap system of the tree. Even if only one branch shows symptoms, the virus is already inside the whole tree and will spread to neighboring healthy trees via mealybug insects unless the entire tree is removed.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ gbɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ tso nine kome pɛ jie hela lɛ he okadi kpo po Shi no mli lɛ, hela lɛ yɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli momo. ni ebaagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ji mealybugs lɛ anɔ. Ja ajie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What causes cocoa leaves to show red veins and swollen stems?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii tsuru kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu?

english: Red veins and swollen shoots are key signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called mealybugs that weakens the tree and eventually stops it from producing pods.
ga: Vɛji tsuji kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo lɛ efuu. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ekpaa ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during heavy rains and humid weather, especially when there is too much dense shade or poor air flow around the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant new cocoa seedlings on land where diseased trees were just cut down?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, it is safe to replant as long as the old infected roots and stumps are completely removed and destroyed, and you plant improved, disease-tolerant cocoa hybrid seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, kɛji ajie shishifãi kɛ tsei akutsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Ni oduɔ hybrid cocoa dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantains on my farm right after my old cocoa trees are cleared?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ajie kookoo tsei momoi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantain immediately after clearing is recommended because they provide necessary temporary shade for new cocoa seedlings while giving you food and income while waiting for the cocoa to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛji ajie ŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ haa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait for new cocoa seedlings to start producing pods after replanting?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting if properly cared for, compared to older traditional varieties which took 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect themselves from drought. Keeping permanent shade trees on your farm helps cool the environment and reduce this leaf loss.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo baahi shi daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Cocoa trees produce many more flowers than they can support. Flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or if the tree is stressed by lack of water and nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii shwieee amɛ nɔ, loo kɛji akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees planted above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sun. Shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young plants from high heat and strong winds while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Protect young plants from extreme heat and strong winds. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough for planting fresh cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo hee?

english: Healthy cocoa soil is deep, dark, crumbles easily in your hand, drains water well without turning into standing mud, and has a top layer rich in decayed leaf litter.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni efeee muji. Ni ŋwɛi fã ko yɛ ni baai ni miigboi eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to keep its new upper growth alive. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores color and helps produce bigger cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmei wuji.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special leaves and roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume plants finish growing, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as free, natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and act like small babies that burn easily under full sun. Shade trees protect cocoa from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool, and prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly during dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Yam plants rely on sunlight to generate the energy needed to form big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight while keeping the leaves dry and safe from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni helai baaa amɛnɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink the amount of leaf surface directly exposed to hot sunlight. This is a survival trick to stop water from escaping through their leaves when the day gets too dry and hot.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa yiwalaheremɔ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ́ gbi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen dries out and cannot fertilize the flowers. Because the flowers cannot make seeds, the plant drops them to conserve its water and energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Tsei kɛwoɔ mli koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their roots fight underground for water and plant food, while their broad leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. This competition steals energy away from forming fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantain ŋmeii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu ni amɛdu niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ aduawai akui afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do weed seeds sprout so much faster than my crop seeds right after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weed seeds are tough and naturally adapted to wake up and grow with even a tiny amount of moisture. Crop seeds are more delicate and usually need steady moisture and clean soil to sprout properly.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui wa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ waaa kwraa ni bei pii lɛ ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ahi nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and watery if I do not harvest them before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rains soak the ground, mature cassava plants drink too much water, causing the firm starch in the roots to break down into excess water. Harvesting before severe rains keeps the roots firm and good for cooking.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Cassava tsei ni egbɔ lɛ nuɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ fãa ni etsɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine. Nikpamɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ waa ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right in the middle before they are ready for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ teŋgbɛ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaahɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages split open when a long dry period is followed by sudden heavy watering or rainfall. The inside of the cabbage drinks up water rapidly and grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch, causing the head to burst.
ga: Kaabaji mli gbalaa kɛji nu ni mli wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa nyiɛ sɛɛ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ. Kaaba lɛ mli nuɔ nu lɛ oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe, ni no haa eyitso lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food it needs to grow strong. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my soil help my crops survive when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the dirt. It holds onto rainwater long after the rain stops, keeping moisture near the plant roots so your crops stay green and fed during short dry spells.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce very little fruit when I use a lot of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits. Balanced feeding ensures the plant knows when to stop growing leaves and start fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eleɔ be ni esa akɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants protect themselves from stress by dropping their flowers because they cannot support new fruit. Providing light shade or mulching the soil keeps the plant cool enough to hold its blossoms.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ haomɔ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii heei. ni haa hulutsoo be fioo Aloo, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward like small cups during the midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing water too fast in the heat. It shrinks the area exposed to hot sunlight, acting as a natural defense against drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ebaagbɔjɔ yɛ hei ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ yɛ lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ hewolo lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rainstorms even when they have big bunches growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni jwɛi wuji yɔɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread near the surface rather than going deep. When the soil becomes heavy with water and the fruit bunch gets heavy, weak roots can easily pull out of the soft ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shɔŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni aduawai akui lɛ hu eyi lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli oya.

english: Officer, why do very small cocoa pods on my tree shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Ofisa, mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɛkɛ? Ani mitsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the cocoa tree discards extra pods it cannot support, or by fungal infections like black pod disease that attack young pods in damp, shady conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela ni tutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground allows them to catch more sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground, while keeping the leaves dry and away from soil diseases that thrive in damp ground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field this season make the soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have special tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that stored food remains in the dirt to feed the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ bɔɔt bibii. Krɛdɛɛ yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If I cut cassava stems to plant, why must I plant them with the bud nodes pointing upward into the sky?
ga: Kɛji ofo ŋmei tso ni odu lɛ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ odu lɛ ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi?
