english: Cassava stem nodes have small buds that sprout outward and upward toward light. If planted upside down, the shoots must bend around to grow upward, using up energy and resulting in weaker plants and lower yield.
ga: Yucca tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni eda. Ehaa ekɛ hewalɛ fioo tsuɔ nii Ehaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow and curling leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Feeding the soil with well-rotted manure and inspecting under the leaves early helps stop the damage before it spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm miitutua lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɔ ni efite lɛ dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the plants grow tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ baai babaoo moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or not enough potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storage roots below. Adding wood ash or balanced compost restores potassium, encouraging bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ ahi shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni potassium lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: What causes black spots on my pepper fruits, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ nɔ lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Black spots on peppers are often caused by fungal diseases that spread when rain splashes dirty water from the ground onto the plant. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass (mulching) prevents splashback and stops the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ ha nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi (mulching) ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed from inconsistent watering or extreme heat. Giving your plants a steady amount of water at the root level—rather than soaking them heavily after long dry spells—helps them keep their flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ amɛshishifã lɛ he daa Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nu egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I prune off some of the middle branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning thick middle branches allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree. This dries out extra dampness inside the canopy, preventing black pod disease from taking hold and allowing the tree to put more energy into pods.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekamɔ tso lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ pod lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if I give my field enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔji lɛ amli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops underground by stealing nutrients, space, and fertilizer from the soil. Even with plenty of water, your main crop will stay weak because the weeds are consuming the plant food first.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baagbɔjɔ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the dirt. Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally extracts nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, restoring field fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture to start planting my seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grab a handful of soil from a few inches down and squeeze it into a ball; if it holds its shape comfortably without leaking water or immediately crumbling apart, the ground has just enough moisture to safely germinate your seeds.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ sũ ni akɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛ inchi fioo komɛi kɛba shi ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Nu lɛ shwieee loo efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize is dry enough to store without it spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni efiteee?

english: Grains are ready for storage when they feel glassy hard and cannot be easily dented with a fingernail or tooth. Storing thoroughly dried maize in clean bags elevated off the floor stops mold and keep insect pests from ruining your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛtoɔ kɛ́ enu he akɛ ewa tamɔ glase ni ekɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii shwieee shi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ wo kotokui ni he tse ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmãa akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and wither when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantains protect them from hot sun and help keep moisture in the soil while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, leading to weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa nii fioo.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree lacks enough water or soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny beneficial insects in the area to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo bɛ jɛmɛ ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk of the tree instead of on the thin leafy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods grow on the main trunk and thick branches because they are heavy and require strong structural support so they do not break the branches as they mature.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛbiɔ tsɔne ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ eda kwraa lɛ, etswaaa niji.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow if I plant them at the start of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady soil moisture to break open, sprout, and grow roots. Planting at the start of the dry season leaves young seedlings without water, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha nu akashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create damp, humid conditions that allow black pod disease, a fungal infection, to thrive and spread quickly across cocoa pods if sunlight and air cannot reach the tree.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ekɛ black pod hela baa Fungal infection Edaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he

english: Will cutting off weak or unnecessary branches from my cocoa tree hurt its growth?
ga: Ani niji bibii loo niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha eda?

english: No, pruning off weak or dead branches actually helps the tree by directing its energy to healthy branches and improving air movement, which keeps the tree healthy and reduces disease.
ga: Dabi, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm to harvest food while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ teŋ koni makpa niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava is aggressive and consumes too much water, nutrients, and light away from young cocoa plants, which can choke or stunt the growth of your young cocoa trees.
ga: Cassava lɛ mli wa ni eŋɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la babaoo kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo etsĩ enaa koni ekada.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal fertilizers and natural soil nutrients before your main crops have a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Dani otsei titrii lɛ baaná hegbɛ amɛye amɛ,.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has run out of food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Soil is low in nutrients when crop leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, and plants remain small or grow very slowly even when receiving enough rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa kɛ́ tsei ahe baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii loo amɛdaraa blɛoo waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. When there is not enough fertilizer or compost in the soil, the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil and helps the maize grow bigger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni edara ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know which way to insert a cassava stem cutting into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tsei ni esa akɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ oodu?

english: Look closely at the stem cutting for small raised bumps called nodes where the leaves used to grow. The tiny buds on these nodes should always point upward toward the sky so the stems can grow properly above ground while roots develop below.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ nodes he ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall grass and weeds away from the base of my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with young cocoa plants for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them away ensures the young cocoa gets enough nourishment to grow strong roots and reduces hiding places for harmful field pests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ, ni ehaa hei ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to long wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the energy required to produce large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high into the air and keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which also prevents foliage diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieee shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai hu anaa.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown sawdust-like waste inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls deep into the funnel (center) of the young maize plant during the cooler hours of the day to eat the soft leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ a-funnel (teŋgbɛ) lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tiny tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ amɛhe bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or whiteflies. As these insects feed on the underside of young leaves, they drain the plant's sap and can pass on viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi. Ehaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ eshwã.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees keep snapping at the ground and falling over during windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily weakened underground by microscopic worms called nematodes or root-boring insects. Once the roots are damaged, the plant cannot hold up the heavy weight of its leaves and fruit bunch.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ baai kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping all their flowers without growing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers if they experience water stress, lack of shade, or severe insect attacks from pests like capsids. It also happens when the tree is still too young to carry the heavy load of growing full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛna nu mli haomɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids tutuamɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ hu baa mli beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etere ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ahe haomɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning dark, soft, and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi eŋɔli lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the developing fruit. It is usually caused by irregular watering during dry spells rather than an infectious disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ moŋ fe hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow and curling up inside my greenhouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing usually happen when plants are under stress from excess heat or infected by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Good ventilation lowers the temperature inside the greenhouse, and fine insect netting keeps pest insects out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ latsaa ni fe nine mli. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baaye abua ni eha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Ni ŋmeii kpakpai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: What is the benefit of growing my vegetables inside a greenhouse instead of directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: A greenhouse acts as a protective house that shields crops from heavy downpours, scorching sun, and insect pests. This controlled environment helps crops like tomatoes and sweet peppers grow faster, produce higher yields, and stay healthy with fewer chemical sprays.
ga: Greenhouses tsuɔ nii akɛ shia ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ bell peppers ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. shweremɔ oya Ha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekwɛ hewalɛ kpakpa nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofai fioo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and maintains humidity, creating a protective canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha hulutsoo aya nɔ. Feemɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning purple at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is lacking phosphorus in the soil. Phosphorus helps plants build strong roots and transfer energy, so applying a balanced fertilizer high in phosphorus early in the season will turn the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fosfɔs yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛhaa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce a lot of bushy leaves, but when I harvest, the tubers are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɔɔ baai babaoo shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from the soil, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of tubers. To get big tubers, the crop needs potassium, which tells the plant to store energy underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. koni ená yitso agbo Tsei he miihia potassium. ni kɛɔ tsei akɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get too hot or experience sudden drought stress. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo ena hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni eha hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makudɔ sweet potato wain tso ko koni ekwɔ tso nine ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to capture light and make food for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum sunlight to grow large yams.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha bulb lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, so watering your crops on a consistent schedule helps the roots draw calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbala calcium kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes inside the center funnel of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in the central leaf funnel (whorl) are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender young leaves inside. Checking your field early and applying targeted treatments into the whorl will stop them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli (whorl) lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look wilted in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, and it will naturally recover once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni ebaahe ejɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving some tall trees helps protect them while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashi amɛdamɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ.

english: Should I cut down all the large forest trees on my land before planting my cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: No, you should leave some large, beneficial forest trees to provide shade. Cocoa trees naturally thrive under a partial canopy, which keeps the farm cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi tsei wuji ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo. Cocoa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Planting cocoa too closely causes the trees to fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin trees that produce fewer pods and are more prone to diseases like black pod due to poor air movement.
ga: Cocoa ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛmli ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni amɛyaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same plot where I am growing new cocoa plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kokoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava very close to young cocoa because cassava feeds aggressively, taking away vital nutrients and water that the young cocoa needs to grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibioo kwraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei yeɔ niyenii waa. Ejieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra branches and suckers from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji bibii kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Removing extra branches and suckers, known as pruning, helps the tree direct its nutrients toward producing healthy cocoa pods rather than wasting energy on useless stem growth.
ga: Niji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pruning. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni oookwɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: How do weeds affect the growth of my cocoa plants when they are still young?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from young cocoa plants, which slows down their growth and creates a hiding place for pests that can damage the crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni amɛfee hei ni kooloi ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist, allowing the roots to easily absorb nutrients for growth and pod production.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.
